jobs.title: Regional Vice President RVP Equipment Finance Sales
jobs.description:
A career as a Regional Vice-President (RVP), Equipment Finance Sales, Western Canada at National Bank is an opportunity to lead the regional Vendor Sales and Direct Sales channels as one coordinated sales organization. 
In this role, you will establish and execute the regional growth strategy, strengthen relationships with equipment vendors and business clients, and lead teams accountable for profitable origination, client acquisition and portfolio development. 
You will work closely with Commercial Banking & 1859 and Equipment Finance partners to deliver sound financing solutions while managing credit, operational and regulatory risk within the Bank's established frameworks.

Your role:

Define and execute an integrated regional strategy for Vendor Sales and Direct Sales, translating business priorities into clear market coverage, growth plans and performance expectations.
Lead the achievement of regional revenue, volume, profitability, client acquisition, vendor relationship and referral objectives across both sales channels.
Guide leaders and sales professionals in developing new business, deepening vendor and client relationships, and building a balanced pipeline across equipment sectors, client segments and geographic markets.
Create clear accountability through business plans, budgets, forecasts, activity measures and performance reporting, and take timely action when results or market conditions require adjustment.
Promote disciplined pricing and deal structuring, balancing growth, client value and return expectations within delegated authorities and established approval processes.
Maintain a strong market presence by being active in the field with clients, vendors, centres of influence and regional partners, while working closely with other market leaders to identify growth opportunities, strengthen referral networks and represent Equipment Finance consistently across the assigned region.
Work in partnership with Credit, Operations, Risk and other internal specialists to support efficient execution, appropriate risk management and a consistent client and partner experience from origination through funding.
Strengthen collaboration between Vendor Sales, Direct Sales and Commercial Banking by developing referral routines, clarifying accountabilities and connecting clients to broader Bank capabilities when appropriate.
Build and maintain senior relationships with important vendors, clients, centres of influence and industry stakeholders, and represent National Bank Equipment Finance in the regional marketplace.
Lead, coach and develop regional sales leaders and team members, establishing a high-performance, inclusive and accountable culture focused on client outcomes, collaboration and sustainable growth.
Lead change initiatives affecting the regional sales model, including process, technology, coverage, talent and operating-model improvements.
Manage the region's sales resources and expenses within approved budgets and ensure adherence to Bank policies, conduct expectations, compliance requirements and risk controls.

Your team:

You are part of the Equipment Finance and Commercial Banking leadership network and collaborate closely with colleagues in Credit, Operations, Risk, Product, Finance, Human Resources and other specialized groups. The role provides leadership across the Vendor Sales and Direct Sales teams in its assigned region.
This role can be based in either Edmonton, Calgary, Vancouver or Winnipeg.

Required skills:

Bachelor's degree in business, finance, commerce or a related field, or equivalent combination of education and senior leadership experience.
Extensive experience in commercial sales, business development and people leadership within equipment finance, commercial lending, leasing or a related financial services environment.
Demonstrated ability to lead multiple sales channels or teams and translate strategy into measurable regional results.
Strong knowledge of commercial credit, equipment finance structures, pricing, portfolio economics and risk-management expectations.
Previous experience in Equipment Finance, including direct exposure to equipment lending, leasing, vendor programs or related financing structures.
Proven ability to build senior relationships, negotiate complex opportunities and influence across business lines and functional teams.
Experience establishing sales plans, budgets, forecasts, performance measures and accountability routines.
Strong leadership, coaching, talent-development and change-management capabilities.
Proven ability to motivate and lead high-performing teams, develop talent and build leadership capability through coaching, feedback and clear performance expectations.
Strong presence working with senior leadership, with the ability to present, influence and translate complex business information into clear, compelling stories for varied audiences.
Sound judgment, executive communication skills and the ability to make timely decisions in a complex, evolving environment.
Ability to travel within the assigned region and occasionally elsewhere in Canada, as business needs require.
For the Quebec and Atlantic Canada role, proficiency in French and English is required to support stakeholders in both languages.

Languages: English
Required skills: Business Alignment, Critical Thinking, Data-Driven Decision-Making, Decision Making, Diversity & Inclusion, Emotional Intelligence, Innovation Management, Learning Agility, Managerial Courage, Mobilization, Partner Development, Resiliency, Risk Management, Strategic Vision, Strategy Execution, Stress Management

Your benefits

In addition to competitive compensation, upon hiring you’ll be eligible for a wide range of flexible benefits to help promote your wellbeing and that of your family such as:

* Health and wellness program, including many options
* Flexible group insurance
* Generous pension plan
* Employee Share Ownership Plan
* Employee and family assistance program
* Preferential banking services
* Involvement in community initiatives
* Telemedicine service
* Virtual sleep clinic

We have an offer that keeps up with trends as well as your needs and those of your family.

Our dynamic work environments and cutting-edge collaboration tools foster a positive employee experience. We value employees’ ideas. Whether through our surveys or programs, regular feedback and ongoing communication are encouraged.

Making a bold move in a people-first environment

We’re a bank on a human scale that stands out for its courage, entrepreneurial culture, and passion for people. Our mission is to have a positive impact on people’s lives. Our core values of partnership, agility, and empowerment inspire us, and inclusion is central to our commitments. We aim, wherever possible, to provide a barrier-free and accessible environment to all employees.

jobs.title: Director, Corporate Risk Information Management
jobs.description:
You are as unique as your background, experience and point of view. Here, you’ll be encouraged, empowered and challenged to be your best self. You'll work with dynamic colleagues - experts in their fields - who are eager to share their knowledge with you. Your leaders will inspire and help you reach your potential and soar to new heights. Every day, you'll have new and exciting opportunities to make life brighter for our Clients - who are at the heart of everything we do.

At Sun Life, we're driven by our Purpose: helping our Clients achieve lifetime financial security and live healthier lives. Our values shape how we work: caring, authentic, bold, inspiring, and impactful.

When you join Sun Life, you'll work with passionate colleagues and empowering leaders who support your growth and celebrate your contributions, so you can make a meaningful difference in our Clients' lives.

Discover how you can make a difference in the lives of individuals, families and communities around the world.

Job Description:

About The Role

Reporting to the Assistant Vice President, Emerging Risk Management & Strategic Risk Initiatives, the Director, Corporate Risk Information Management is accountable for the oversight of the information management, records management, and data governance policy requirements and underlying programs across Corporate Risk, which includes Enterprise & Operational Risk Management, Insurance & Financial Risk Management, Investment & Credit Risk Management, and the Corporate and DBTS Business Group Risk Office teams. The Director sets direction, maintains the framework and methodology, and holds Information Stewards, Records Officers, Records Custodians, Data Custodians and Risk Office teams accountable so that information assets are properly classified, protected, retained, disposed of, and governed in alignment with the Enterprise Information Management Policy, regulatory expectations, and business needs. The Director leads continuous improvement of the program, including enhancements to tools, and strengthens program governance, effectiveness, and efficiency.

The Director is the accountable owner for structured and non-structured business records and information assets within Corporate Risk, in line with the Enterprise Information Management Policy.

The role holds the Records Steward, Records Officer, Data Governance Operational Lead, and Non-Structured Data Information Stewardship accountabilities for Corporate Risk, reflecting the centralized operating model of the function. It provides integrated oversight of information lifecycle management, repository governance, data quality, metadata, reporting, and information risk management, and ensures consistent execution of records and information management requirements across Corporate Risk.

What You'll Be Doing

Lead information governance, risk, and compliance

Serve as the accountable lead for Non-Structured Information Management governance for Corporate Risk.
Maintain the Corporate Risk information management framework, operating guidelines, and standards, aligned to the Enterprise Information Management Policy, and oversee adherence to policy and related control expectations.
Provide guidance and advice to Business Group Risk Office teams and business leaders when judgement or clarification is required on information governance obligations, risks, and implementation requirements. Provide advice into strategic decisions and program improvements.
On a quarterly basis, independently evaluate the Corporate Risk information management risk profile, including Key Performance Indicators (KPIs) and Key Risk Indicators (KRIs), and report results, material non-compliance, and significant issues to senior management and the Operational Risk and Compliance Committee (ORCC) in a timely manner.
Oversee and coordinate Corporate Risk's response to Risk Control Self Assessments, audits, compliance reviews, and regulatory examinations, and oversee related issue remediation activities related to information management.
Prepare an annual report to senior management and ORCC on the status of the information management, records management, and data governance program.
Establish, maintain, and continually enhance the oversight and monitoring frameworks for the program.
Monitor and benchmark Corporate Risk information management practices against industry standards, regulatory expectations, and best practices, and assess complex information risk issues to guide solution recommendations.
Develop and own the short- and mid-term strategy and roadmap for information management, records management, and data governance in Corporate Risk, aligned to enterprise and Business Group strategy, and provide significant input to Corporate Risk's strategic and long-term plans.
Set program roll out objectives and plan and prioritize program resources, milestones, and dependencies across Corporate Risk.

Records and information lifecycle management

Direct and oversee records management activities, including records classification, retention, legal holds, disposition, and remediation planning.
Perform and oversee Records Officer responsibilities for Corporate Risk, retaining accountability for consistent execution of records management requirements, guidance, monitoring, and issue follow-up.
Oversee Records Impact Assessments (RIAs) and Records Management Risk Reviews when new or changed processes, systems, repositories, vendors, or operating models may affect the creation, storage, access, retention, transfer, or disposition of Corporate Risk business records, and provide guidance on complex or high-risk cases.
Oversee the maintenance of records and repository inventories and ensure ownership and stewardship assignments remain current.
Determine how Corporate Risk business records are identified, classified, captured, stored, protected, retained, and disposed of, and hold Records Custodians accountable for applying those determinations.
Make final decisions within Corporate Risk on record designation, retention and disposition, legal hold implementation, and exceptions to records requirements, and escalate only matters that require enterprise policy interpretation or an exception to enterprise policy.

Advance data governance and repository oversight

Provide oversight and approval of Data Governance artifacts and Business Impact Statements prepared by Information Stewards.
Lead data quality, metadata, business glossary, lineage, classification, and critical information inventory practices, including the related standards and methodology.
Monitor and report Data Governance KPIs and oversee remediation of identified issues.
Lead governance of SharePoint, Teams, shared mailboxes, network drives, and other non-structured business repositories.

Enable change and stakeholder engagement

Build strong working relationships with Information Owners, Records Custodians, Information Custodians, Risk Offices, Compliance, Legal, Technology, Data Governance teams, and other relevant teams involved in records and data management to drive execution of key deliverables within the Three Lines of Defense model.
Develop, maintain, and deliver training, communications, and practical guidance to Information Stewards, Records Custodians, Risk Office teams, and other stakeholders to support adoption of information governance practices.
Lead cross-functional discussions to resolve issues, mature governance practices, and embed sustainable ways of working.
Represent Corporate Risk on peer Steering Groups and provide direction on information management matters.
Work closely with Business Group Risk Office teams on the effective roll-out of program changes.
Develop and communicate the vision for information governance in Corporate Risk and build consensus on operating goals aligned with the Risk division.

What You'll Need To Succeed

University degree in Information Management, Data Governance, Records Management, Business Administration, Risk Management, Library Sciences, Information Technology, or a related discipline, and/or relevant certification.
5+ years of risk management, records management, data governance, or information governance experience, with a proven track record of designing and implementing effective programs, controls, and processes, ideally within a major federally regulated financial institution.
Direct experience writing policies and guidelines, and implementing governance frameworks, standards, controls, or enterprise operating procedures.
Demonstrable experience leading cross-functional initiatives, developing strong working relationships, and influencing senior stakeholders in a large, matrixed organization within the Three Lines of Defense model.
Proven experience dealing with complexity and ambiguity, using broad knowledge, keen analysis, and sound professional judgement to arrive at quality decisions.
Working knowledge of Sunlife’s information management, records management, data governance, privacy, compliance, and operational risk practices.
Ability to translate complex policy, risk, records, and data governance requirements into clear business guidance, communications, training, and sustainable operating practices.Strong knowledge of information management, records management, and data governance principles, including information lifecycle management, repository governance, metadata management, information classification, and data quality management, with the ability to assess, measure, and monitor information risk.
Strong knowledge of the information and records management landscape, financial industry leading practices, and regulator expectations.
Exceptional analytical, problem-solving, and decision-making abilities, with keen attention to detail, and experience in risk assessment, control design, compliance monitoring, reporting, and analytics.
Working knowledge of Microsoft 365, SharePoint, Teams, shared mailboxes, network drives, and other collaboration platforms.
Experience implementing, managing, and maintaining a records, information governance, or GRC tool.
Strategic mindset, with the ability to understand business requirements and develop innovative solutions.
Excellent communication, facilitation, influencing, and stakeholder management skills, with the ability to communicate complex concepts to a diverse audience.
Well-developed writing and visual presentation skills to articulate analytic results, options, recommendations, and reporting.
Effective change management and change leadership through impact and influence skills, with governance oversight and a continuous improvement mindset.
Proactive and adaptable mindset, with the ability to thrive in a fast-paced and rapidly evolving organization.

What's in it for you:

Being a member of the Sun Life family, a group of people united by our Purpose: to help Clients and Employees achieve lifetime financial security and live healthier lives.
In 2024, Sun Life ranked among the top 100 most sustainable global corporations by Corporate Knights for the 15th consecutive year, leading Canadian insurers.
We are proud to be on the 2024 Best Workplaces in Canada list by Great Place to Work.
We’re also listed as one of the Best Workplaces for Women and Best Workplaces with Most Trusted Executive Teams.
Our unique Sabbatical Program gives you the opportunity to take up to 6 weeks off, every five years.
Care Days available for self-care or care of others (i.e., family or others you may support) and Sick Days to support your well-being.

The Base Pay range is for the primary location for which the job is posted. It may vary depending on the work location of the successful candidate or other factors. In addition to Base Pay, eligible Sun Life employees participate in various incentive plans, payment under which is discretionary and subject to individual and company performance. Certain sales focused roles have sales incentive plans based on individual or group sales results.

jobs.description:
Job Title

Director, Databricks Consultant - Strategic Solution Architecture

Job Description

We're Concentrix. The intelligent transformation partner. Solution-focused. Tech-powered. Intelligence-fueled.

The global technology and services leader that powers the world’s best brands, today and into the future. We’re solution-focused, tech-powered, intelligence-fueled. With unique data and insights, deep industry expertise, and advanced technology solutions, we’re the intelligent transformation partner that powers a world that works, helping companies become refreshingly simple to work, interact, and transact with. We shape new game-changing careers in over 70 countries, attracting the best talent.

The Concentrix Technical Products and Services team is the driving force behind Concentrix’s transformation, data, and technology services. We integrate world-class digital engineering, creativity, and a deep understanding of human behavior to find and unlock value through tech-powered and intelligence-fueled experiences. We combine human-centered design, powerful data, and strong tech to accelerate transformation at scale. You will be surrounded by the best in the world providing market leading technology and insights to modernize and simplify the customer experience. Within our professional services team, you will deliver strategic consulting, design, advisory services, market research, and contact center analytics that deliver insights to improve outcomes and value for our clients. Hence achieving our vision.

Our game-changers around the world have devoted their careers to ensuring every relationship is exceptional. And we’re proud to be recognized with awards such as "World's Best Workplaces," “Best Companies for Career Growth,” and “Best Company Culture,” year after year.

Join us and be part of this journey towards greater opportunities and brighter futures.

Director, Databricks Consultant - Strategic Solution Architecture

Key Responsibilities

Presales and solutioning

Partner with sales and account teams to run discovery sessions, understand customer objectives, and identify high value Databricks use cases.
Provides team leadership and direction.
Shape solution visions and reference architectures for data, analytics, and AI platforms built on Databricks and cloud services (Azure, AWS, or GCP).
Develop proposals and statements of work, including scope, phases, estimates, risks, and assumptions for Databricks engagements.
Deliver technical presentations, whiteboard sessions, and demos that clearly communicate Databricks capabilities and business value to diverse audiences.
Address technical objections, guide architecture discussions, and build confidence with client architects and executives during the sales cycle.
Drive additional revenue by proactively uncovering opportunities to expand business within current customer base

Architecture and delivery leadership

Lead the design and implementation of secure, scalable Databricks Lakehouse architectures, including Delta Lake, Unity Catalog, and integration with upstream and downstream systems.
Pro-actively define offerings, IP and associated collateral that will resonate with both new/existing customers and help close new business
Oversee the build of batch and streaming data pipelines, notebooks, and Databricks SQL assets using Spark, Python, and SQL, following medallion and other best practice patterns.
Define and enforce engineering standards, including code quality, testing, CI/CD, observability, and operational readiness for Databricks workloads.
Collaborate with project managers and client stakeholders to plan releases, manage dependencies, mitigate risks, and ensure on time, on budget delivery.
Provide hands on technical leadership to data engineers and analysts, reviewing designs and code, and unblocking complex technical issues.

Governance, operations, and adoption

Implement data governance and security practices using Unity Catalog and related tools, including access control, lineage, and compliance aligned policies.
Optimize performance, reliability, and cost of Databricks workloads through cluster tuning, storage strategies, and monitoring.
Drive change management and enablement by creating documentation, runbooks, and training materials, and facilitating knowledge transfer to client teams.
Support production go lives and post olive stabilization, ensuring robust handover to client operations or managed services teams.
Work with specialty sales team and COE Lead to create a plan to engage with and add net new customers to existing portfolio

Required Qualifications .

Excellent communication, stakeholder management, and presentation skills, with the ability to influence technical and nontechnical audiences.
Databricks Professional certification
Demonstrated ability to run workshops, gather requirements, and translate business needs into technical designs and phased roadmaps.
Proven experience leading client facing data or analytics projects in a consulting, professional services, or similar environment.
Extensive hands-on experience designing and delivering data platforms and pipelines on Databricks, including Delta Lake, Jobs/Workflows, and Databricks SQL.
Strong programming skills in at least two of: Python, PySpark, and SQL, with demonstrated ability to build performant batch and streaming solutions.
Solid understanding of cloud services (Azure, AWS, or GCP) relevant to Databricks deployments, such as storage, networking, identity, and DevOps tooling.
Experience implementing data governance, security, and access control in Lakehouse or data platform environments using Unity Catalog or similar tools.

Preferred Qualifications

Experience with largescale data platform migrations or modernizations (e.g., from legacy ETL/warehouse tools to Databricks).

jobs.description:
Requisition ID: 279160

Join a purpose driven winning team, committed to results, in an inclusive and high-performing culture.

Leads and oversees a team within the Data & AI Risk (DAIR), GRM group ensuring the Enterprise Artificial Intelligence (AI) Risk strategies, implementation program and mandated activities are executed / delivered in compliance with the governing regulations, internal policies and procedures, and in support of innovation and business strategy.

Is this role right for you? In this role you will:

Lead and drive a customer focused culture throughout their team to deepen client relationships and leverage broader Bank relationships, systems and knowledge to execute the AI Risk Management Program.
Support the VP, Data & AI Risk in shaping and executing the Enterprise AI Risk strategies.
Design and implement the AI Risk Program including management of AI Risk Management policies, procedures, metrics and processes.
Establish and lead the independent second-line AI risk management oversight and challenge function to support identification, assessment, monitoring and escalations of AI risk in collaboration with other risk partners.
Lead the roll-out and ongoing execution of the AI Risk Management Program among business lines/corporate offices and geographies, which includes but is not limited to the following:
Develop, refine, and enhance the assigned AI risk framework components, policies, procedures, processes, tools, and metrics with the objective to improve the effectiveness and efficiency of the AI risk.
Ensure AI Risk Management policy enforcement and compliance through appropriate governance and oversight mechanisms.
Establish and lead the execution of the 2nd line risk oversight, effective challenge, risk measurement and reporting (NIRAs, RCSA, internal management reports, senior management, and/or Board reports), including identification and escalation of material and emerging risks.
Advise and collaborate with first line business lines, corporate functions, key stakeholders with regards to the AI risk management principles, standards, controls, and best practices, while maintaining effective second-line independence and challenge.
Partner with AI Governance and Model Risk Management functions, Technology, Cybersecurity, Privacy, Legal, Compliance and other key partners with identification, communication and reporting of relevant AI risk priorities, successes, issues, dependencies and regulatory expectations.
Guide and influence various stakeholders across the organization to achieve the goals defined in the DAIR and AI Risk Management strategies and programs, including the responsible adoption of emerging AI technologies.
Support resolution of risk governance and management issues by driving coordination, alignment and timely escalation where required.
Lead AI risk awareness events and training sessions on AI risk management framework, policy, 2nd line of defense processes, metrics and reporting.
Provide oversight on the prioritization and remediation plans for AI risk-related issues: measure, report and monitor key AI risk indicators, identify compliance gaps and risk issues, guide risk impact-focused gap and issue prioritization and creation of action plans to remediate gaps and issues, monitor plan execution, and escalate material or overdue issues in accordance with the Bank's risk governance framework.
Monitor relevant global regulatory developments and assess their potential implications for the Bank's AI risk management framework, controls and risk posture.
Ensure that own and team’s day-to-day activities are conducted in a manner consistent with the Bank’s risk culture and the relevant risk appetite statement and limits. Communicate the Bank’s risk culture and risk appetite statement throughout his/her team.
Develop or contribute to ad-hoc reporting to the Board, risk committees, and senior leadership, including the collection of metrics and reports
Act as a thought leader in AI risk governance, representing the organization in various industry forums and panels
Create an environment in which the team pursues effective and efficient operations within respective areas in accordance with Scotiabank’s Values, its Code of Conduct, and the Global Sales Principles, while ensuring the adequacy, adherence to and effectiveness of day-to-day business controls to meet obligations with respect to operational, compliance, AML/ATF/sanctions and conduct risk.
Build a high-performance environment and implement a people strategy that attracts, retains, develops and motivates their team by fostering an inclusive work environment and using a coaching mindset and behaviours; communicating vison/values/business strategy; and, managing succession and development planning for the team.

Skills

Do you have the skills that will enable you to succeed in this role? - We'd love to work with you if you have:

Minimum 7 years of relevant progressive experience in compliance, risk management, legal or analytics, model or AI governance.
Deep understanding of AI technologies, ML/AI risk management best practices, relevant global laws, regulations, and ethical and risk management standards.
Strong grasp of global and regional AI regulations.
Curious and proactive and agile learner interested in new technology, ML/AI/GenAI/Agentic risk management best practices, trends and developments in data and AI governance.
Experience in leading the development of policies, risk assessments and conducting training programs to establish effective AI risk oversight practice with defined success measures.
Very strong organizational, negotiation, communication, and presentation skills.
Demonstrated experience and skills in collaboration, teamwork, and problem-solving to achieve strategic objectives.
Demonstrated ability to spark innovation and act as a trusted advisor to help teams use AI responsibly.
Degrees in a quantitative field, Business Administration, Computer Science, Data Science or a related discipline an asset.

What's in it for you?

The opportunity to join a forward-thinking and collaborative team, surrounded by innovative thinkers
A rewarding career path with diverse opportunities for professional development
Internal training to support your growth and enhance your skills
An inclusive working environment that encourages creativity, curiosity, and celebrates success!

jobs.title: VP, GWAM Technology Operations & Platforms
jobs.description:
Reporting to the Chief Information Officer, GWAM Technology, and as a member of the GWAM Technology Leadership Team, you will work closely with business and technology executives to align platform investments and operational priorities with enterprise goals, customer outcomes, regulatory requirements and business growth objectives.
This leader will be accountable for the reliability, resilience, security and continuous modernization of the technology platforms that support GWAM's business strategy and digital ambitions.
You will lead a diverse portfolio spanning platform engineering, production operations, cloud platform services, automation, AI enablement and technology infrastructure. A central part of the mandate is to move traditional infrastructure and operations toward a modern platform engineering model built on automation, self service capabilities, developer enablement, operational resilience and AI powered operations.
This leader will consolidate platforms and platform engineering across GWAM Technology. The priority is to modernize the infrastructure environment, drive greater automation and AI enablement, improve operational efficiency, and establish stronger accountability for services and costs.

Position Responsibilities

Set and deliver the strategic roadmap for GWAM Platforms and IT Operations, including governance, prioritization, capacity planning and investment management
Advance a product oriented platform engineering operating model that improves automation, accountability, transparency and delivery effectiveness.
Advance cloud capabilities that support the organization's agentic AI ambitions.
Provide leadership and direction to the existing AVP and broader teams.
Strengthen oversight of GTCS, setting clear expectations around service levels, cost transparency and delivery on behalf of all of GWAM IT.
Ensure the availability, performance and resilience of critical platforms by leading incident reduction, problem management, disaster recovery and operational readiness

The market leader. The premier provider. The best in the business. At Citco, we’ve been the front-runner in our field since our incorporation in 1948 led to the evolution of the asset servicing sector itself. As a product-focused lead within the Data Transformation Office, you will partner with the Transformation Office leadership team to bring structure, governance, and product thinking to our API platform initiative. Drawing on your project governance background and hands-on analytics exposure, you will translate high-level business needs into a clear product roadmap, user stories, and delivery milestones. You will help shape how our APIs are designed, consumed, and evolved — turning a technical asset into a well-managed product that internal teams and clients can depend on.

jobs.title: Director and Technical Lead Data Science & Innovation GEMINI
jobs.description:
GEMINI is Canada’s largest hospital data and analytics network that provides insight into patient care for research and quality improvement. Currently, GEMINI holds granular data on >3 million patient admissions (>10 billion data points) – a population-level laboratory to study and improve hospital care. This deep individual-level data is critical to harness advanced analytic methods such as artificial intelligence and machine learning.

GEMINI uses advanced methods and analytics to extract and standardize data captured in hospital electronic health records. Over 1,000 scientists, clinicians, and students are increasingly using this data. GEMINI currently exists at 40+ Ontario hospitals and supports the Ontario General Medicine Quality Improvement Network, GeMQIN, a provincial network led by Ontario Health to improve care for general medicine hospital patients. In total, GEMINI has been a core dataset on >$300 million of grant funding across 20 institutions.

Building on GEMINI, the Government of Canada has funded the establishment of Vital, a national-scale data platform to enable research and innovation with near real-time hospital data from at least 8 provinces and territories, beginning with Ontario, Alberta and Quebec.

The Technical Lead and Director, GEMINI Data Science and Innovation will lead GEMINI’s efforts in accelerating research and innovation using hospital data by leveraging technology, optimizing processes and streamlining operations, and implementing data governance approaches. The Director will lead the continued growth and successful development of GEMINI’s data and analytics platform. An important part of the work, to be accomplished in partnership with the Technical Lead for Vital, will be to lead the establishment of the capabilities that are required for Ontario’s participation in the new national Vital platform.

The successful candidate will have expertise in data management, a strong technical background, and experience leading a technical team. They will promote a safe and inclusive work environment and lead an agile and cross-functional team that works in data collection and management, reporting, research software, and data analytics. They will work closely with a supportive systems and IT infrastructure team, particularly in the implementation of cybersecurity tools and practices, as well as with a research operations team that is responsible for setting data governance and privacy policies, which the data team implements. They will build strong positive relationships with GEMINI’s internal and external stakeholders including hospital leadership, researchers and government partners. They will participate in the Executive Team of the Unity Health Toronto GEMINI and Vital teams, providing strategic input into organizational direction and management.

Duties And Responsibilities

Provide strategic leadership, set priorities and operational oversight to advance GEMINI’s data and analytics platform.
Promote innovation and lead efforts to develop novel approaches to tackle data challenges.
Manage and advance GEMINI’s established data collection, standardization, and quality control processes, including initiatives to modernize data assets through the implementation of common data models that support scalable research, analytics, and interoperability.
Provide strategic and operational oversight of the GeMQIN reporting program, ensuring the timely delivery of high-quality reports that meet the needs of participating hospitals and support quality improvement initiatives.
Oversee the technical ecosystem that supports research use of GEMINI data, including research-ready databases and analytics tools, ensuring solutions are scalable, maintainable, secure, and aligned with organizational priorities.
Work with the Vital Technical Lead to innovate new methods in hospital data collection to enable near real-time access to data for research and innovation.
Lead the implementation of technology and processes to implement data governance and privacy practices, ensuring regulatory compliance of GEMINI’s data holdings and infrastructure, in partnership with the research operations team.
Work with the IT systems and research operations team to implement cybersecurity technology and practices for handling sensitive health data.
Work with GEMINI’s research team to incorporate new innovations, particularly harnessing Artificial Intelligence, into routine data collection and management processes and into analytical tools.
Work with GEMINI’s research team to support the development and delivery of data products and analytical tools to facilitate efficient, cutting-edge research.
Manage and execute processes that support the continuous improvement of data team operations.
Lead the GEMINI data platform team through a period of transition relating to new methods of data collection and processing and new ways of engaging with the national Vital network.
Provide strategic input into organizational decision-making for GEMINI and Vital that is grounded in data and analytic expertise.
Lead multidisciplinary technical teams across data collection, reporting, data engineering, analytics, data science, and research software development.
Foster a positive work culture that encourages innovation, learning and continuous improvement, supported by the broader Executive Team within GEMINI and Vital and Unity Health Toronto, as well as external expert coaching as needed.
Contribute to strategic decisions about team structure and human resources for the GEMINI data team to optimize team function, aligned with GEMINI’s evolving deliverables, including identifying capacity needs and supporting recruitment and retention of team members.
Provide mentorship, coaching and growth opportunities to a diverse workforce, with a particular focus on technical mentorship, supporting team members to upskill and improve their workflows with AI and rapidly evolving computing technologies.
Work collaboratively with GEMINI leaders and other stakeholders including hospital leadership, researchers and government partners.

Qualifications

Completion of a Master’s degree in Computer Science, Bioinformatics and/or related discipline; PhD an asset
Minimum seven (7) years of experience conducting and leading data-driven initiatives and large-scale projects
Minimum seven (7) years of relevant experience participating in and managing cross-functional teams with the ability to guide teams through complex projects, ambiguity, and change
Minimum seven (7) years of experience across multiple technical domains, including data engineering, data management, data analytics and reporting, data science, artificial intelligence, software development, and data governance
Minimum five (5) years of experience with healthcare data including clinical and operational workflows
Minimum five (5) plus years of experience using project management tools and methodologies
Outstanding analytical and problem-solving skills
Strong experience working with high performance computing environments, complex technical operations and software development principles in an open source framework
Advanced knowledge in data science tools such as R and Python, and relational databases
Familiarity with cloud-based infrastructure, federated analysis and event-driven architecture is an asset
Exceptional organization skills and strong time management experience developing project plans to meet objectives and budgets, adaptable to managing multiple tasks and deadline pressures
Exceptional written and oral communication skills to engage, articulate and conceptualize ideas/issues at all organizational levels with stakeholders
Fully proficient in working independently and self-directed while taking accountability for own actions

Work at CBC/Radio-Canada

At CBC/Radio-Canada, we create content that informs, entertains and connects Canadians on multiple platforms. Our successes and accomplishments are driven by embodying and upholding values, which include creativity, integrity, inclusiveness and relevance.

Do you think you have the ability and drive to keep up with this exciting, ever-changing industry? Whether it be in front of the camera, on air, online or behind the scenes, you would be joining a team that thrives on making connections and telling stories that are important to Canadians.

Unposting Date

2026-11-27 11:59 PM

Behind the scenes, but ahead of the curve: help us develop the next-generation public service media organization.

The Technology & Infrastructure (T&I) team is the backbone and the future-forward arm of CBC/Radio-Canada. Our purpose is to constantly innovate to evolve and maintain the Corporation’s technologies and infrastructure. We are the people that make stuff work. We make connections between media content, systems, people and places. We are the space in between.

A place with purpose. CBC/Radio-Canada has always been a highly regarded pioneer of media technology — not just in Canada, but around the world. Today, we are transforming ourselves into a modern and agile public service media organization. Technology is the driving force, and we are the team making it happen.

This is a hybrid role with a mix of in-office and remote work. Work arrangements will be discussed with hiring managers per departmental guidelines.

Role Vision and Impact

The Senior Director, Information Security and End-User Technology, serves as CBC/Radio-Canada’s Chief Information Security Officer (CISO). A strategic, visionary and collaborative leader, the CISO defines, implements and drives the overarching vision for cybersecurity, risk management and technological resilience across all corporate environments.

The mission of this strategic role is to protect information assets, data, digital heritage, and production and broadcasting infrastructure across all platforms, while ensuring seamless, agile and uninterrupted media operations.
The Senior Director optimally balances rigorous security architecture governance with the flexibility that creative, journalistic and technical teams need to innovate and broadcast without disruption.

Operating at a senior executive level, the CISO regularly briefs and advises the Board of Directors (BoD),
the Audit Committee,
the CBC/Radio-Canada Senior Executive Team (SET)
and the T&I Management Executive Team (MET).

Supported by a team of experienced directors and senior managers overseeing governance, security operations, end-user technology and identity management, the Senior Director serves as the cornerstone of digital trust and strategic transformation for Canada’s public broadcaster.

Key Responsibilities

Strategic Vision, Leadership and Executive Relations

Develop, champion and execute an enterprise-wide cybersecurity strategy aligned with the Corporation’s business mission, risk profile and digital transformation.
Serve as a trusted expert and strategic adviser to the BoD, Audit Committee, SET and MET regarding risk status, security posture and maturity, and required investments.
Foster a “Security by Design” culture and establish security architecture governance frameworks that keep operational and production workflows running smoothly while proactively managing risk.
Anticipate technology trends and lead the secure integration of artificial intelligence (AI/GenAI) and automation into business processes and security defences across the organization.

Securing IT, Cloud, Distribution and Broadcast/Operational Technology (OT) Environments

Define and continuously adapt the security strategy across the entire technology landscape, including corporate IT infrastructure, cloud systems, end-user environments, and critical production, broadcast and network infrastructure.
Ensure the resilience of content acquisition, processing and distribution workflows against threats targeting the media sector and critical infrastructure.

Governance, Risk, Compliance and AI Governance

Oversee the governance function responsible for developing, maintaining and enforcing policies, standards, security architecture principles, exception management and industry frameworks (e.g., NIST, ISO 27001, AI frameworks).
Lead the third-party and partner risk management program (covering vendors and technology contracts) in close collaboration with the Legal Services and Procurement teams.
Co-develop a governance, compliance and ethical framework for the enterprise-wide use of AI and generative AI, assessing specific risks throughout their life cycle.
Ensure strict compliance with applicable laws and regulations (e.g., Quebec’s Law 25, GDPR and sector-specific requirements).
Drive a cybersecurity culture and awareness program focused on lasting behaviour change across the organization.

Defence Operations, SOC and Crisis Management

Oversee the performance and modernization of the Security Operations Centre (SOC), advanced detection tools (SIEM, EDR/XDR, automation) and continuous threat monitoring.
Direct major security incident response operations and lead technology crisis management, from detection to full business recovery.
Oversee regular penetration testing, vulnerability assessments and cyberattack simulation exercises across IT, broadcast and distribution environments.

Identity and End-User Technology

Guide the strategic vision for Identity and Access Management (IAM, PAM) to provide secure, simple and frictionless access for all staff and contractors.
Collaborate closely with the End-User Technology teams to align security with a modern, efficient and intuitive employee experience.

Financial Management and Team Engagement

Plan and optimize the cybersecurity department’s overall budget and partner with internal procurement teams to negotiate major technology contracts.
Inspire, coach and develop a team of directors and senior managers — fostering excellence, innovation and cross-functional collaboration.
Lead with the heart.

Qualifications, Experience And Core Competencies

Education and Certifications

Bachelor’s or master’s degree in computer science, cybersecurity, computer engineering, business administration (IT concentration) or a related field.
At least one recognized executive-level professional certification: CISSP, CISM, CCISO, CISA or CRISC.

Professional Experience

Seven to 10 years of experience managing professional teams or equivalent.
Deep expertise in technology architecture, cloud security, network infrastructure, cryptography, and identity and access management (IAM).
Ability to provide collaborative leadership within the organization to see complex, transformational initiatives through to completion.
Demonstrated skills in planning, organizing and engaging teams.
Proven ability and track record in leading cross-functional teams.
Proven ability to work with cross-functional, agile teams or on projects that have multi-team dependencies.
Ability to distil complex issues into clear, concise presentations and reports.
Expertise in the various technologies typically used by journalists in a newsroom.
Knowledge of business practices, including drafting plans and specifications, contracts, negotiation, finance, and IT management software.
Knowledge of software development and the technology infrastructure required for product delivery.
Knowledge of workflows for content acquisition, management and distribution, with a focus on storytelling.
Innovative approach to technical and operational challenges, paired with sound judgment to protect CBC/Radio-Canada from legal liability and financial loss.
Excellent interpersonal skills, with an ability to engage and influence stakeholders and partners at every level of the organization.
Excellent ability to listen to and communicate with people having different points of view or competing business objectives.
Experience implementing product governance models.
Ability to travel occasionally between Montreal and Toronto.

Balanced relationships.

To create a path with our clients to community wellbeing through meaningful consulting solutions.

Relations: Everything we do is grounded in relationships and showing up in a good way.
Integrity: We deliver exceptional products and services with clarity, transparency and honesty.
Curiosity: We approach our work with curiosity, openness and genuine interest.
Culture: We respect and honour Indigenous ways of knowing and being, such as Inuit Societal Values and the Seven Grandfather teachings.
Humility: We conduct ourselves with respect, kindness and compassion.

NVision Insight Group Inc. is a majority Indigenous-owned consulting company with First Nations, Inuit, Métis and non-Indigenous shareholders, staff, associates, and subcontractors. We have extensive experience working in and with First Nation, Inuit and Métis communities and organizations, governments, corporations, and not-for-profit organizations. With offices in Ottawa, on reserve in Winnipeg, and Iqaluit, and a national team of associates, we provide a comprehensive range of high-quality consulting services across Canada.

NVision provides products and services in three practice areas.
Consulting and Advisory
Lands Studio
Learning and Development

About the Role
Position: Director of Finance & Operations
Supervisor: Board of Directors
Location: Ottawa / Iqaluit / Winnipeg / Remote

Purpose/Summary

The Director of Finance & Operations provides financial and operational leadership for NVision, helping ensure the firm is well managed, financially healthy, and positioned for long-term success. The Director establishes and implements improvements in financial processes and controls, tracking project costs, utilization, and profitability to support informed management decisions. The Director oversees financial planning, budgeting, forecasting, project costing, invoicing and cost recoveries, and profitability, working closely with colleagues to support informed decisions and the financial sustainability of the firm. The Director also leads NVision's Shared Services team, which includes finance, human resources, information technology, and administration. This involves supporting the team, strengthening internal systems and processes, and ensuring people across the firm have the support they need to do their work well. As a member of the Management Circle, the Director works collaboratively with colleagues to support the firm's direction, make thoughtful decisions about resources, and balance financial responsibility with NVision's Indigenous-led values and commitment to People, Purpose, and Profit. jobs.title: Director, Corporate Finance & Corporate Development
jobs.description:
Director, Corporate Finance & Corporate Development

About the Company:

We are hiring for one of Canada's fastest growing technology companies, recognized by Deloitte as the #1 Enterprise Software company in the 2025 North American Technology Fast 500 and ranked #5 in Deloitte Canada's 2024 Technology Fast 50 Companies to Watch.

This is a rare opportunity for an accomplished finance leader to join a high growth Canadian technology company at a pivotal stage of its journey, with a clear path toward a future VP.
We are looking for someone who has been there before. A leader who has helped companies scale, built teams and financial infrastructure, navigated complexity and knows how to evolve a finance function as a business moves into its next chapter.

You will work closely with the CFO, CEO, and colleagues across the leadership team in a highly collaborative environment where finance is a strategic partner to the business.
This is an opportunity to help shape what comes next.

About the Role:

We are seeking a commercially minded and financially sophisticated Director of Corporate Finance & Corporate Development to support the organization’s financial strategy, corporate positioning, and potential strategic transaction opportunities.

Working directly with the CEO and CFO, this individual will help strengthen the company’s financial position, assess business value, and prepare the organization for potential sale, merger, acquisition, or strategic investment opportunities.

The ideal candidate brings experience in corporate finance, financial modelling, business valuation, transaction readiness, and stakeholder relations. This is a strategic leadership position focused on maximizing enterprise value and supporting executive-level decision-making.

Key Responsibilities:

1. Corporate Finance & Strategic Planning

Work closely with the CEO and CFO to assess the company’s financial position and long-term strategy.
Review financial performance, profitability, cash flow, and operational efficiency.
Develop financial models, forecasts, valuations, and strategic financial assessments.
Identify opportunities to improve business value and financial performance.
Provide financial insights and recommendations to executive leadership.

2. Corporate Development & Transaction Readiness

Lead corporate preparation for potential sale, merger, acquisition, or strategic investment.
Assess business valuation, enterprise value, and potential transaction structures.
Coordinate financial due diligence and organize corporate and financial documentation.
Review historical financial performance, liabilities, business risks, and growth opportunities.
Prepare confidential information memorandums, investor presentations, and transaction materials.
Coordinate with external accountants, lawyers, financial advisors, and other transaction professionals.

3. Corporate Relations & Stakeholder Management

Establish and maintain relationships with investment groups, corporate executives, financial institutions, potential acquirers, and strategic stakeholders.
Participate in strategic discussions and meetings relating to corporate transactions.
Support negotiations and evaluate potential transaction terms.
Maintain confidentiality throughout all corporate development and transaction-related activities.

4. Executive & Financial Reporting

Provide regular financial and strategic updates to the CEO and CFO.
Prepare executive-level reports, financial presentations, and valuation assessments.
Support decision-making through financial analysis and commercial insights.
Ensure financial information is accurate, organized, and transaction-ready.

5. M&A, Acquisitions & Financing

Support the evaluation of potential acquisitions, mergers, and strategic investments, from target screening through close
Build acquisition models, including standalone target valuation, merger/pro forma financials, accretion/dilution analysis, synergy estimates, and integration cost assumptions.
Perform valuation analysis using DCF, comparable companies, and precedent transactions.
Assist with financial due diligence: quality of earnings review, working capital analysis, net debt and debt-like items, and revenue and customer retention analysis.
Analyze and help structure transaction financing, including the mix of cash on hand, debt, seller notes, earn-outs, and equity issuance, and model the impact on leverage, covenants, liquidity, and returns.
Prepare materials for the executive team, board, lenders, and investors, and coordinate with legal, accounting, tax, and external advisors.
Support post-acquisition integration, including purchase price allocation inputs, consolidation into budgets and forecasts, and tracking of synergy and deal-thesis performance.

Qualifications & Experience

Bachelor’s degree in Finance, Accounting, Business Administration, or Economics.
MBA, CFA, CPA, or other relevant financial designation considered an asset.
5–8+ years of experience in corporate finance, investment banking, M&A, transaction advisory, financial strategy, or a related field.
Demonstrated experience with financial modelling, business valuations, and due diligence.
Strong understanding of mergers, acquisitions, and corporate transaction processes.
Experience preparing businesses for investment, acquisition, or sale.
Excellent financial analysis, negotiation, and executive communication skills.
Ability to work directly with senior leadership and manage confidential financial information.
Experience with M&A transactions, due diligence, or corporate development (or investment banking or transaction advisory).
Familiarity with debt and equity financing structures, covenant modelling, and capital structure analysis.

Ideal Candidate:

The successful candidate is strategic, analytical, commercially aware, and comfortable operating at an executive level. They understand how businesses are evaluated by potential buyers and investors and can identify opportunities to strengthen financial performance and maximize enterprise value.

This individual must be comfortable working in a dynamic environment, taking ownership of strategic financial initiatives, and advising executive leadership on important corporate decisions.

What We Offer:

Direct exposure to executive leadership and strategic decision-making.
An opportunity to influence corporate strategy and business valuation.
A collaborative, growth-oriented working environment.
Competitive compensation based on experience.

Director, Technical Operations (Platform)

Job Type:
Permanent Full Time

Location:
Hybrid - Toronto, Ontario

Reporting to:
Chief Technology Officer

Salary
: $160,000 – $190,000 CAD

Job Purpose

The Director, Technology Operations owns the operational health of the platforms Goway sells and services travel on: our reservations platform, the infrastructure it runs on, the supplier, air and distribution integrations it depends on, and the automation and data pipelines built around it.

This is a practice-building role. You will define and own Goway's technical operations discipline: service levels, incident management, change control, observability and operational readiness, and you will make them the standard across our technology organisation. You will work alongside other Technology leaders. You will own the technology operations of our platform. You will have the CTO's mandate and backing to build the practice.

What will be your key responsibilities?

Reliability and service management

Define, publish and report service levels and service-level objectives for revenue-critical services, starting with quoting, booking, payment and traveller servicing.
Own incident management end to end: severity definitions, escalation, incident command, communication during an incident, and post-incident review with corrective actions.
Own RCA and problem management.
Own change and release management as a company standard, balancing delivery throughput against change failure rate.
Build observability sufficient to detect degradation.
Own disaster recovery and business continuity for platform services, tested and documented on a stated cadence.

Integration and supplier platform operations

Monitoring of integration paths, error and failure-rate thresholds, and defined fallback behaviour when a partner degrades.
Maintain a dependency map of the external platforms our revenue-generating flows rely on, with assessed operational risk and mitigation for each.
Own operational readiness for new integrations and new product lines entering the platform.
Own the operational reliability of automation and data pipelines in production.

Platform and cloud operations

Day-to-day operation of the AWS and managed hosting infrastructure serving our platform estate: environments, provisioning, patching and lifecycle management.
Own hosting cost governance: visibility by service, a unit-cost measure, and an annual optimisation target.
Lead capacity planning against forecast booking and travel volumes.
Reduce manual, repeatable operational work through automation.
Address seasonal capacity planning, change freezes and enhanced coverage aligned to our booking and departure peaks and to new product launches.

Vendors, partners and compliance

Platform, hosting and integration partner relationships: SLA definition, enforcement and structured performance review.
Reduce single points of dependency, whether on a vendor or an individual.
Partner with security on vulnerability management, patch compliance, access control and audit readiness.

Practice leadership and stakeholder engagement

Build and maintain a multi-year technical operations roadmap aligned to Goway's growth plans.
Report operational performance, risk and investment needs to the CTO and executive team in business terms.

What are we looking for?

Required

8 or more years in platform operations, technical operations, infrastructure or site reliability engineering, including 5 or more years in a lead or leadership capacity.
Demonstrated accountability for the availability and performance of a revenue-critical transactional platform.
Evidence of having built operational practice where little existed: SLOs, incident management, change control and observability introduced from the ground up, with measurable improvement to show for it.
Hands-on depth in AWS, including cost management and multi-environment operation.
Substantial experience operating and governing third-party platforms and integrations, including holding vendors to service levels.
Ability to set standards and drive adoption across teams.
Ability to communicate operational risk and performance.

Preferred

Experience stabilising and operationalising new systems.
Infrastructure-as-code and container orchestration experience.
AWS Certified DevOps Engineer (Professional), or AWS Certified CloudOps Engineer (Associate). Solutions Architect certifications are welcome, but less relevant to this role than the operations-focused ones.
Bachelor's degree in computer science, information technology, engineering or equivalent practical experience.

What can you expect from Goway?

Imagine working for a company where your career feels like an adventure. At Goway, you’ll join a global community that supports one another:
We offer a competitive salary accompanied by performance incentives, and we place real importance on time away from work, such as paid personal days for when life calls for them and your birthday off each year.
Our commitment to professional growth means you’ll have access to continuous learning and industry-leading training that keeps you at the forefront of travel innovation.
You’ll enjoy generous paid time off, including [three] weeks of vacation, [six] personal days, and a dedicated day off to celebrate your birthday.
Travel is in our DNA, so you’ll enjoy exclusive perks and discounts on worldwide getaways.
Since we operate across Toronto, Vancouver, Los Angeles, Manila, Sydney, and beyond, you’ll collaborate across cultures and shape a career path that reflects your ambitions.
Goway is an equal-opportunity employer. We celebrate differences and are committed to fostering an inclusive workplace for everyone. We appreciate every applicant’s interest. Please be advised that only those selected for an interview will be contacted.

How To Apply

If this role feels like your next step, click "Apply Now" to create your profile, upload your CV, and share a few details about yourself. Our talent team reviews every application, and if your experience aligns with our needs, we will reach out to set up the next step.

AI Screening Disclosure

To help us fairly and efficiently review applications, we use an automated screening process to assess responses to pre-determined questions. This initial step ensures all candidates are evaluated consistently. Qualified applicants will be reviewed by our recruitment team for further consideration.

Additional Notes

Goway Travel Ltd will retain applications, notifications, and records related to this posting for three years, reflecting our commitment to fair and equitable hiring practices.

Recruitment Scams & Fraud Warning

Please be aware of any suspicious emails or WhatsApp activity from individuals pretending to be recruiters or senior personnel at Goway Travel. We will never ask you to install an app during the recruitment process. If you receive a message of this nature, please ignore it and report it to Goway.

About Goway

Founded in Toronto in 1970 by Australian economist Bruce Hodge, Goway has evolved from a one-person dream into a family-owned global leader in tailor-made travel. With our headquarters in Toronto and hubs in Vancouver, Los Angeles, Sydney, and Manila, our team of over 800 talented employees designs travel experiences in more than 115 countries across all seven continents. We’re united by a passion for travel and are committed to doing the right thing: supporting diversity, equity, inclusion, and sustainable tourism that enriches local communities. Whether working remotely or side by side in one of our offices, we operate as one forward-thinking team, transforming wanderlust into life-changing adventures for our fellow Globetrotters. Discover more at goway.com.

Job Description

The Director, Strategy and Business Development, will be responsible for contributing to growing Seaspan Shipyards business by leading and implementing business strategies for new or growing markets. Interfacing with Seaspan’s senior leadership team, this role will lead and support a range of strategic plans and initiatives including broad new business strategies, transformational initiatives, strategic initiatives and complex captures.

Key to this role will be a strategic approach to understanding the breadth and complexity of our customer’s needs and developing strategies and solutions to meet those needs – both technical and non-technical. Working as part of the broader multi-disciplinary Seaspan team, this role will include direct leadership of strategic initiative teams collaborative interfaces to many other departments and teams within Seaspan. An important aspect of this role will be the development of business cases for our strategic initiatives including how they will generate long-term returns for Seaspan.

Note: This position qualifies for an optional hybrid work schedule after 90 days of onsite work and onboarding. Employee will be subject to the terms of the Flexible Work Policy Agreement.

What You'll Do

Drive future growth for the company through disciplined but creative strategy and business development.
Lead development and implementation of new business strategies targeting new or growing markets.
Lead implementation of strategic initiatives
Provide oversight, guidance and support to capture leads and their capture and proposal teams.
Lead activities to find and develop opportunities both with new potential customers and with existing customers.
Maintain key business development contacts with current and potential customers.
Build and lead capture teams and proposal teams as required for each approved opportunity.
Identify growth opportunities within international markets and work with the wider Seaspan organization to develop competitive export offerings.
Represent and advocate on behalf of Seaspan Shipyards at conferences, trades shows, and other industry events.
Interface with other departments and teams in the Seaspan organization to achieve objectives in a manner aligned with overall Seaspan priorities, strategies and processes.
Strong communication skills (verbal and written) with customers, partners, suppliers and within Seaspan.

What You'll Bring

10+ years of professional industry experience advancing complex new business development strategies and bid proposals in the shipbuilding industry or in a complex defence, aerospace or systems development, manufacturing or construction industry.
University degree in a relevant area preferred.
Proven track record of developing business strategies and then leading the implementation.
Experience leading and closing complex opportunities with contract values over $10M and ideally over $50M.
Broad understanding of technical, programmatic, financial and commercial aspects of complex deals.
Experience with forming and maintaining strategic industry partnerships and supplier arrangements as part of an overall strategy.
This job is both strategic and tactical, and requires substantial leadership in market/customer strategy and opportunity capture.
Multi-faceted leadership skills applicable to direct leadership roles and influential leadership roles.
Ability to work in a highly flexible and fluid environment and maintain calm and rational thinking and reasoning at all times.
Demonstrated ability to communicate with a variety of stakeholders and the ability to respond to stakeholder needs strategically and tactfully.
Exceptional interpersonal skills, superior oral and written capabilities, including the ability to build professional relationships with government and industry partners.
Skilled at advocacy, influence, and persuasion, with the able to convince others to act on information or recommendations based on compelling logic or common best interests.
Knowledge of complex government markets.
Strong knowledge and expertise with Microsoft Office (PowerPoint, Word, Project and Excel).
Self-starter with good organizational skills who can work both independently and as a member of a team.

Why you'll love working here

This is a full-time, permanent position. With multiple operations and long-term projects, Seaspan employees enjoy job stability as we look ahead to build ships for decades to come.
In addition to an annual bonus and pension plan matching, this role provides you a very competitive salary in line with the successful candidate’s experience.
We also provide a best-in-class health and wellness benefits package for this position, including such things as full health care (e.g. unlimited physiotherapy), dental, vision, life insurance, medical leave coverage, parental leave coverage, wellness/fitness reimbursement for memberships or registration fees, and an Employee Family Assistance Program (EFAP).
This position qualifies for an optional hybrid work schedule.
Parking is included and to assist those that are using transit, we operate a complimentary shuttle bus Monday through Friday with various pick up and drop off points around North Vancouver.

The estimated salary for this position is $180,000 - $220,000. In determining final salary, Seaspan considers many factors including the successful Candidate’s skills and experience as well as position location and internal equity. The final base salary offer will be at the Company’s sole discretion and presented as part of a competitive total compensation package.

Seaspan Shipyards is one of North America’s most modern shipyards and unique in its ability to provide a complete range of services including new construction, conversion, refit, repair and life-cycle maintenance work for Canada’s Coast Guard and Navy as well as commercial vessels including cruise-ships and deep-sea vessels. Seaspan Shipyards operations include Vancouver Shipyards, Vancouver Drydock and Victoria Shipyards.

who we are

We owe our success to our innovative product, emphasis on stores, commitment to our people, and the incredible connections we make in every community we're in. Global Product Technology (GPT) delivers the platforms and capabilities that power lululemon’s product lifecycle – from 2D/3D design and development to merchandising, sourcing, assortment planning, master data management, and go to market. The role

They must thrive in fast-paced environments, be able to manage through ambiguity and complexity, commission charters and empower teams to create and simplify processes, and simultaneously support a growing global organization. This role requires excellent communication, organizational skills, and the ability to drive ideas from concept to execution. Maturity, curiosity, creative problem solving, and team leadership are all essential for success in this role.

Manage resources, oversee financial interests, and implement essential policies, practices, and processes.
Evident leadership skills, a proven track record of building strong teams, setting high performance standards, challenging people to excel and eliciting their sustained high performance.
Excellent verbal and written communication skills is essential.
Drive world-class engineering solutions that are reliable, observable, secure, compliant, and highly available.
Blend deep technical expertise with visionary leadership, to guide a globally dispersed engineering team that drives platform and solution modernization with advanced AI capabilities such as LLMs, vector retrieval, computer vision, and intelligent agents.

Translate lululemon’s merchandising and planning vision into a multi-year solution realization strategy.
Leverage AI and ML solutions to drive measurable impact across planning capabilities that include attributes generation, demand forecasting, allocation optimization, store clustering, etc.
Translate complex AI/ML architectures into clear narratives for executive stakeholders.
Champion transparency, inclusion, and ethics as core enablers of innovation.
Develop future-ready leaders capable of balancing technical depth and business acumen to drive meaningful growth.

Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in computer science, or related field.
5+ years of engineering leadership and delivery experience.
5+ years in retail, merchandise planning and allocations, or related field is a bonus.
Demonstrated experience in managing large budgets.
Demonstrated experience translating business strategy into technology and engineering roadmaps.
Demonstrated experience in data-heavy planning systems such as Anaplan, Oracle RPAS, etc.
Expert proficiency in programming languages (eg: Python, Java), and relevant libraries/frameworks (TensorFlow, PyTorch, scikit-learn, etc.).
Deep understanding of machine learning, NLP, computer vision, and generative AI techniques.
Able to produce documentation such as narratives and root cause analysis providing actionable insights.
Hands on experience with cloud platforms (AWS, GCP, Azure), and MLOps tools.
Strong knowledge of data engineering concepts and big data.
Continuous learning mindset that stays on the leading edge of applied ML, LLM’s and NLP advancements.
Exceptional communication and storytelling skills for executive audiences.
PhD/Master’s in computer science, applied mathematics, statistics is a bonus.

must haves

Acknowledge the presence of choice in every moment and take personal responsibility for your life.
Possess an entrepreneurial spirit and continuously innovate to achieve great results.
Communicate with honesty and kindness and create the space for others to do the same.
Lead with courage, knowing the possibility of greatness is bigger than the fear of failure.
Foster connection by putting people first and building trusting relationships.
Integrate fun and joy as a way of being and working, aka doesn’t take yourself too seriously.
