jobs.description:
About YPO

YPO is a global leadership community of over 35,000 chief executives from more than 140 countries. YPO brings together extraordinary leaders who are committed to becoming better leaders and better people. The organization provides a platform for the leaders to connect, learn, and grow through shared experiences, rich learning programs, and meaningful relationships. Members benefit from a supportive community that fosters personal, business, family and community growth.

Supporting these members is a world-class management team of more than 450 associates, spanning over 25 countries. Our organization is based in Dallas, Texas, with many associates working virtually and outside of the United States. Together, our team of global associates works to create a truly Only-in-YPO experience for our members

Position Details

This is a remote work-from-home position.
Although this position is remote, candidates must reside in British Columbia, Ontario, Alberta or Nova Scotia
as YPO is not an employer in other Canadian provinces.

Work Hours:
Candidates must be flexible to accommodate time zones of international stakeholders when necessary.

POSITION PURPOSE

YPO is seeking a Senior Director of Technology Operations and Security to lead enterprise IT operations, cybersecurity, business continuity, and technology vendor management, ensuring a secure, reliable, resilient, and cost-effective technology environment.

This leader is accountable for the technology services that enable YPO associates to operate effectively, including corporate infrastructure, enterprise IT services, end-user technology, access management, and IT support. The role also leads YPO's enterprise cybersecurity program, establishing policies, standards, and controls that protect organizational and member data across YPO's technology environment.

Working closely with Engineering, Risk and Compliance, Finance, and other departments, the Senior Director strengthens operational resilience, improves the associate technology experience, manages technology risks, and drives disciplined oversight of technology vendors and investments. The role must enable and accelerate AI adoption across YPO by establishing the secure technology environment, governance, and operational capabilities needed to deploy and scale AI solutions. Partners with departments to remove technical barriers, simplify access to approved AI tools, and empower associates to leverage AI effectively and responsibly.

PRIMARY RESPONSIBILITIES

Enterprise IT Operations and Infrastructure

Ensure YPO associates have secure, reliable technology and responsive support to perform their jobs effectively.
Lead enterprise IT operations, including corporate infrastructure, end-user technology, IT support, and administration of assigned enterprise systems.
Oversee technology onboarding, role changes, and offboarding to ensure associates and contractors receive appropriate system access and timely removal of access.
Partner with HR, Contracts, and department leaders to improve technology provisioning, deprovisioning, and access management processes.
Establish standards for device management, software deployment, identity administration, and IT service delivery.
Ensure corporate devices and IT-managed systems are appropriately configured, maintained, secured, and supported.
Leverage AI and automation to streamline IT support, proactively identify issues, and reduce manual administrative work.
Use operational data and service metrics to continuously improve IT performance, efficiency, response times, resolutions times, and associate experience.
Ensure enterprise technology services, support processes, and deployment standards are designed to operate effectively across YPO’s global locations, including differing connectivity, time-zone, language, regulatory, and local support requirements.

Business Continuity and Operational Resilience

Minimize disruptions to YPO's internal operations and ensure critical corporate technology services can recover quickly from outages and other incidents.
Develop and maintain business continuity and disaster recovery plans for corporate IT infrastructure, enterprise IT services, and other technology systems within the team's operational responsibility.
Identify critical internal technology services, dependencies, and risks that could disrupt associate productivity or organizational operations.
Coordinate regular disaster recovery testing, incident simulations, and continuity exercises to validate operational readiness.
undefined
Partner with Engineering and other system owners to identify shared dependencies, coordinate recovery procedures, and address risks that span multiple technology functions.
Report material continuity risks, recovery readiness, and remediation progress to Technology leadership.

Cybersecurity and Technology Risk Management

Protect YPO's organizational and member data by establishing and maintaining effective enterprise security policies, controls, and risk management practices.
Lead YPO's enterprise information security program, including cybersecurity operations, identity and access management, vulnerability management, security monitoring, and data protection.
Oversee enterprise security monitoring, threat detection, security incident response, investigation, and remediation coordination.
Partners with Engineering, Product, Data, Legal, and Risk and Compliance to ensure security and privacy requirements are incorporated into technology solutions and operations.
Oversee the evaluation and implementation of appropriate cybersecurity frameworks, third-party technology security assessments, audits, and certifications.
Build a strong security culture through associate awareness, training, and clear accountability for protecting YPO systems and data.
Maintain visibility into material cybersecurity risks and regularly report security posture, incidents, and remediation progress to leadership.

Technology Vendor and Financial Management

Establish disciplined oversight of YPO's technology vendors, software portfolio, and investments to reduce unnecessary spending, duplication, and operational risk.
Lead enterprise technology vendor management, including software governance, vendor performance, contract oversight, license management, and cost optimization.
Oversee the centralized software intake and evaluation process to ensure new technology investments meet business needs, security requirements, and financial expectations.
Drive software portfolio rationalization by identifying opportunities to consolidate redundant tools, eliminate underutilized licenses, and simplify YPO's technology ecosystem.
Partner with Finance and department leaders to improve technology budgeting, cost allocation, forecasting, and financial accountability.
Use data, AI, and automation to improve visibility into technology spending, license utilization, vendor performance, and cost-saving opportunities.

People Leadership and Strategic Oversight

Build a high-performing technology operations organization that balances security, reliability, service quality, and financial discipline.
Lead, coach, and develop managers and associates across enterprise IT operations, cybersecurity, and technology vendor management.
Translate organizational priorities into a clear technology operations strategy, roadmap, and measurable performance objectives.
Establish accountability, service standards, operating procedures, and performance metrics across all areas of responsibility.
Manage assigned technology operations budgets, resources, and vendor investments to ensure effective allocation and financial stewardship.
Partner with Engineering and Product leadership to align security standards, operational dependencies, and technology governance requirements.
Collaborate with department leaders to understand organizational needs, identify operational risks, and prioritize improvements that deliver value.
Foster a culture of continuous improvement, cross-functional collaboration, ownership, and proactive problem-solving.
Identify opportunities to leverage AI, automation, and emerging technologies to improve efficiency, strengthen controls, and enhance service delivery.
Communicate technology performance, risks, investment needs, and operational priorities clearly to executive leadership and other stakeholders.

SKILLS

Enterprise IT Operations and Resilience

Strong understanding of enterprise IT infrastructure, corporate networks, identity management, end-user technology, and IT service management.
Knowledge of business continuity, disaster recovery, operational resilience, and technology risk management.
Ability to coordinate effectively with Engineering and other system owners on shared infrastructure, security requirements, and operational dependencies.

Cybersecurity and Risk

Strong knowledge of information security, cybersecurity operations, identity and access management, data protection, and incident response.
Understanding of relevant security frameworks, regulatory requirements, and industry best practices.
Ability to translate security and compliance requirements into practical, business-friendly processes.
Ability to assess and mitigate enterprise technology, vendor, and AI-related security risks.

Technology and Financial Management

Strong technology portfolio, vendor, contract, budget, and license management skills.
Ability to evaluate technology investments, assess vendor performance, and identify opportunities to consolidate tools and reduce costs.
Strong financial acumen, including technology budgeting, forecasting, cost optimization, and investment prioritization.
Ability to establish governance processes that balance organizational needs, operational efficiency, and risk.

AI, Automation, and Continuous Improvement

Identify opportunities to leverage AI, automation, and emerging technologies to improve efficiency, strengthen controls, and enhance service delivery.
Ability to identify, prioritize, and implement automation opportunities that improve service quality, efficiency, and scalability.
Familiarity with AI-related security, governance, and operational considerations.

Leadership and Collaboration

Strong people leadership skills, including coaching, talent development, performance management, and organizational planning.
Ability to lead multiple technology disciplines while balancing strategic priorities and day-to-day operational needs.
Strong cross-functional collaboration and stakeholder management skills.
Ability to communicate complex technology risks, trade-offs, and recommendations clearly to nontechnical audiences.
Strong analytical thinking, sound judgment, and a proactive approach to identifying and resolving problems.
Ability to lead organizational change, establish accountability, and drive measurable operational improvements.

EXPERIENCE/BACKGROUND

10+ years of progressive experience in enterprise IT operations, cybersecurity, technology infrastructure, or related technology leadership roles.
8+ years of experience leading technical teams, including experience managing managers or multiple technology functions.
Demonstrated experience overseeing enterprise IT operations, corporate infrastructure, cybersecurity, and end-user technology support.
Experience leading cybersecurity programs, managing technology risks, and supporting security assessments, audits, or compliance initiatives.
Experience consolidating technology platforms, improving license utilization, and delivering measurable technology cost savings.
Experience partnering with Engineering and other technology teams to establish security requirements, manage shared risks, and coordinate operational responsibilities.
Experience leading distributed teams and deploying, scaling, and supporting technology operations across multiple countries, geographies, and time zones, with an understanding of the operational, cultural, connectivity, and support requireme

ôle

Responsible for annual and semi-annual financial and regulatory reporting and audit cycles for ATBIM’s investment products.
Oversees the Investment Fund Finance team and all day to day fund accounting, valuations, performance and reporting requirements.
Oversee all tax compliance for ATB Funds, including year-end and ad-hoc distribution process, liaise with fund administrator, external tax advisors, accounting and operations teams.

Management and oversight of ATBIM’s third party service providers (custodian, administrators, auditors), monitoring service level agreements and accuracy of deliverables and adherence to all regulatory standards
Participate in strategic initiatives and projects including product development and launch, implementation of tools and technology to enhance ATBIM’s investment management capabilities
Leads the Investment Fund Finance team through performance planning and assessment, coaching, developmental planning and resolution of escalated issues to ensure effective performance of the team
Collaborate internally with ATBIM leadership team and ATB Financial teams (Finance, Internal Assurance, Third Party Risk Management, Legal, etc).

CPA or equivalent professional designation required
10-15+ years of progressive experience in the investment industry

Progressive leadership experience with the ability to motivate, coach and develop a high performing team

Highly developed problem solving skills and professional judgment in handling complex or unexpected situations objectively by assessing situations, identifying and weighing alternative options, and making data-driven recommendations to solve problems.

The Senior Director, Governance & Execution Oversight, Global Risk Intelligence and Technology (GRIT) is responsible for driving execution discipline, governance effectiveness, adoption management, and value realization across Global Risk transformation initiatives in AI, Data and Technology. The role serves as a key partner in Global Risk Technology and Intelligence governance, translating strategic priorities into executable workstreams while ensuring governance decisions result in measurable business outcomes.

This position will oversee intake and prioritization processes, establish operating frameworks and governance disciplines, and define the metrics and reporting needed to measure adoption, benefits realization, capacity utilization, and portfolio performance.

The role acts as a critical link between strategy, governance, execution, and sustained business value realization across the Global Risk portfolio.

Key Responsibilities

Transformation Governance & Strategic Execution

Partner with senior leaders to translate approved priorities into executable workstream plans.
Establish and maintain governance processes supporting prioritization, intake, qualification, approval, and execution oversight.
Drive accountability and follow-through on decisions arising from governance forums.
Coordinate cross-functional stakeholders to ensure alignment of delivery plans, dependencies, milestones, and outcomes.
Monitor execution progress and escalate delivery risks, constraints, or resource challenges.

Portfolio Management & Prioritization

Support development and administration of portfolio intake, assessment, and prioritization frameworks.
Evaluate transformation opportunities against strategic objectives, capacity constraints, risk considerations, and value criteria.
Facilitate portfolio planning processes and support leadership decision-making.
Maintain visibility into transformation demand, delivery capacity, investment priorities, and execution status.
Develop and implement portfolio reporting and performance management practices.

Adoption & Value Realization

Define and implement measurement frameworks for technology, automation, AI, and Data transformation initiatives.
Establish and report on key performance indicators measuring adoption, utilization, business outcomes, benefits realization, and operational effectiveness.
Develop methodologies for measuring product value, customer value, business impact, and sustained adoption.
Monitor trends and identify opportunities to improve user adoption and business outcomes.
Partner with product owners, business stakeholders, and transformation leaders to address adoption barriers and optimize value realization.

Operating Model & Process Excellence

Design and formalize governance operating models supporting transformation management and execution oversight.
Develop and maintain RASCIs, Standard Operating Procedures, playbooks, operating frameworks, qualification frameworks, intake processes, and governance documentation.
Establish repeatable and scalable operating practices across transformation portfolios.
Drive continuous improvement initiatives that improve governance effectiveness and execution efficiency.

Reporting, Insights & Performance Management

Establish and execute recurring reporting cycles covering adoption performance, benefits realization, capacity utilization, portfolio performance, transformation progress, and product value realization.
Develop dashboards, scorecards, and management reporting for executive audiences.
Generate actionable insights supporting portfolio optimization and strategic decision-making.
Track and communicate transformation outcomes to senior leadership.

Stakeholder & Executive Engagement

Build strong relationships with executives, product owners, transformation leads, and business stakeholders.
Support leadership decision-making through structured governance, analysis, and reporting.
Facilitate alignment across teams involved in transformation delivery and adoption activities.
Present recommendations, portfolio insights, and performance updates to leadership forums.
Promote a culture of accountability, adoption, continuous improvement, and outcomes-based delivery.

Qualifications

Education

University degree in Business, Finance, Risk Management, Information Technology, Organizational Change, or a related field.
Professional certifications such as CPA, PMP, Agile, Prosci, Lean Six Sigma, CBAP, or equivalent are considered an asset.

Experience

8+ years of progressive experience supporting large-scale business transformation, strategic execution, portfolio governance, program management, organizational effectiveness, or technology adoption initiatives.
Experience working with executive governance forums and senior leadership teams.
Experience developing performance reporting, operational metrics, dashboards, and value realization frameworks.
Experience driving cross-functional initiatives across complex organizations.
Financial services, risk management, compliance, governance, or transformation office experience preferred.

Join our team to engage in continuous learning and skill development in a supportive environment. Experience the best of both worlds with our hybrid work environment, where you spend three days a week in the office, connecting, collaborating, and enjoying quality time with your amazing colleagues! Our Values: Be better; we strive for improvement in everything we do. Be accountable; we foster clarity and are empowered to act responsibly. Accountable for enterprise strategy, standards, and guardrails across security platform and infrastructure engineering, with a direct mandate to mature Threat Intelligence and DevSecOps as day to day operating capabilities. Shapes policy enforcement, resolves systemic constraints across multiple teams, and influences senior stakeholders on investment, resilience, and risk trade\-offs, translating enterprise considerations into actionable governance aligned to Technology standards.

1\. Enterprise Strategy, Standards, and Guardrails


* Define and evolve enterprise platform and infrastructure standards spanning tooling, pipelines, shared services, automation, resilience, recoverability, and observability, and drive adoption across portfolios.
* Serve as trusted advisor on the highest\-complexity platform, infrastructure, and operational resilience issues across multiple teams.

2\. Threat Intelligence Enablement


* Own the enterprise standards for threat intelligence collection, enrichment, and dissemination so that intel drives compensating control recommendations for operators.
* Translate threat intelligence into prioritized, evidence\-based guardrails and detection requirements across the security ecosystem.

3\. DevSecOps and Secure Delivery


* Sponsor policy\-as\-code, automation, and knowledge automation practices so security controls are codified, machine\-testable, and enforced within pipelines.
* Define safe automation and CI/CD enablement patterns that embed security guardrails into build, test, deploy, and operate workflows.

4\. Systemic Constraint Resolution


* Resolve systemic platform and infrastructure constraints impacting delivery speed, reliability, security, capacity, stability, or recoverability across multiple teams.

5\. Resilience, Incident, and Operational Readiness


* Drive observability, resilience, and incident learning at enterprise scale, including telemetry, alerting, capacity, and DR readiness, to improve service maturity.

6\. Influence, Investment, and Escalation Governance


* Influence roadmap and investment decisions with evidence\-based trade\-offs on capability, risk, resilience, cost, and scalability.
* Determine when initiatives require escalation due to enterprise or regulatory impact and ensure consistent engagement with architecture and risk forums.
* Partner with senior stakeholders to align priorities and sequencing when constraints materially impact outcomes.

7\. AI\-Enabled Practices


* Shape and sponsor AI\-enabled platform and infrastructure strategy, including automation, predictive monitoring, and policy\-as\-code, aligned to security and governance.

8\. People and Capability Uplift


* Mentor senior ICs and strengthen capability uplift through communities of practice and standards forums.

9\. Continuous Improvement


* Identify recurring friction and enable durable fixes across the platform and infrastructure ecosystem.
  

**Qualifications**


* Post\-secondary education in Technology or related field, or equivalent practical experience.
* Extensive progressive experience delivering enterprise platform and infrastructure services and enablement.
* Proven influence on standards, governance alignment, and risk\-informed decisions across multiple teams.
* Demonstrated leadership\-by\-influence with senior stakeholders and governance forums.
* Deep expertise in automation, CI/CD enablement, observability, recoverability, and secure operations.
* Ability to shape AI\-enabled strategy and guardrails at scale.
* Demonstrated depth in Threat Intelligence and DevSecOps as core operating disciplines.

The Director balances speed, innovation and employee empowerment with security, privacy, risk, operational resilience and supportability, ensuring employee\-led technology adoption remains practical, governed and sustainable.

  

**Key Accountabilities**


* Lead the pod vision, strategy, roadmap and priorities for Citizen Development and Employee Technology Experience, ensuring alignment to enterprise objectives, portfolio priorities and measurable business outcomes.
* Operate and launch and then continuously improve the Citizen Development operating model, including scope, intake, prioritization, decision rights, solution classification, lifecycle oversight, support model, escalation paths and value measurement.
* Enable governed adoption of Microsoft Copilot, Power Automate and approved low\-code/no\-code capabilities, with clear boundaries between employee\-led solutions and work requiring business\-led or technology\-led delivery.
* Maintain practical guardrails for safe innovation, including solution registration, ownership, risk tiering, control gates, security review, privacy considerations and operational supportability.
* Identify employee technology friction across corporate and advisor communities and sponsor practical improvements that improve productivity, adoption, service experience and confidence in technology.
* Lead employee technology communications, TechTalks, digital learning content, short video learning, tech tips, onboarding support and awareness campaigns that make technology easier to understand and adopt.
* Manage and refine the pod backlog, making informed trade\-offs across value, risk, cost, capacity, quality, employee experience, technical sustainability and operational impact.
* Coordinate agile planning, backlog refinement, sprint execution, reviews and retrospectives to maintain delivery discipline, transparency and momentum.
* Provide day\-to\-day leadership, coaching and feedback to pod team members; partner with Product and Delivery Chapters on standards, capability development, staffing and best practices.

Our Company Background & Culture

UPP is the first pension plan of its kind in Ontario’s university sector, proudly serving over 46,000 members across six universities and nineteen sector organizations. Our purpose is to bring greater retirement peace of mind to the university sector by investing with integrity and serving members with care. As a sector-wide plan designed for growth, our doors are open to all Ontario universities.

We’re a team of progressive thinkers and agile doers operating within a fast-paced culture of collaboration and respect. We believe in bringing smart and capable people together to create, solve, and grow with a clear shared vision and values of integrity, inclusivity, ingenuity, and impact.

We’ve Built And Nurtured a Culture That Is Intentionally Welcoming And Purposefully Rooted In Equity, Diversity, Inclusion, And Reconciliation (EDI&R). We Believe Diverse Teams, Perspectives, And Lived Experiences Contribute To Better Decisions And a Better Workplace. As UPP Celebrates Its Fifth Anniversary, We’re Proud To Be Recognized For Our Efforts

2026 Greater Toronto’s Top 100 Employers
2026 Canadian HR Award for Excellence in Diversity, Equity, Inclusion & Belonging

Join us in building a bright future for our members, our organization, and each other.

THE ROLE

The Associate Director, Pension Planning & Performance Reporting (15-Month Contract) is accountable for leading the development and delivery of Pension Services reporting and analytics, ensuring leaders are equipped with accurate, timely, and actionable data and insights to support operational and strategic planning and decision-making.

This role translates data, analytics, and industry intelligence into insights that inform pension service delivery, experience design, and operational planning. The role supports organizational planning, prioritization, and performance management by providing scenario modeling, forecasting, and reporting that links outcomes to strategic objectives.

Reporting to the MD, Growth, this role provides the operational planning support and analytical foundation that enables leadership decisions across Growth and Enabling Services, Experience and Specialized Operations. This role also compiles Pension Services data for benchmarking studies and surveys in which UPP participates.

A core focus of the role is strengthening Pension Services’ ability to use data responsibly and effectively, ensuring reporting, forecasting, and analytics capabilities align with UPP’s data governance and AI frameworks while enhancing member and employer value.

This role is based in downtown Toronto under a hybrid work policy, allowing employees the flexibility to work remotely and in-office (min two days per week in-office).

This job posting is for an existing vacancy and is open to Independent Contractors

Note

Target Start Date: First week of January
This role is open to independent contractors paid hourly, if preferred

Specific Accountabilities

The Associate Director, Pension Planning & Performance Reporting will have responsibility for but not limited to the following:

Lead the development and delivery of UPP’s Pension Services reporting and analytics.
Translate data, analytics, and industry intelligence into insights and strategies and lead monthly discussions with the Pension Services leadership team and partners to identify areas of concern, risk and/or opportunity
Provide the analytical foundation for pension service delivery, experience design, and operational planning, equipping leaders with the data required to make evidence-based decisions.
Support the MD, Growth in the analysis, research and execution of the pension operational strategy, delivering insights and reporting (to the Pension Services Committee, Board and Joint Sponsors).
Support organizational planning and prioritization by providing scenario modeling, forecasting, and performance reporting that links outcomes to strategic objectives. Lead monthly and quarterly scorecard reporting development and communication.
Work with UPP Data teams to identify data, reporting, and BI infrastructure requirements and solutions.
Collaborate with Pension Services teams and partners to ensure data and analytics inform growth initiatives and business-as-usual operations.
Ensure Pension Services leverages data and analytics capabilities responsibly and in alignment with UPP’s data governance and AI frameworks.
Drive a culture of continuous improvement and curiosity by empowering teams to use data and analytics to enhance member and employer value.

Qualifications & Experience

Bachelor’s degree required; postgraduate degree is an asset.
Minimum 8-10 years of progressive experience in data analytics, business intelligence, reporting, or pension administration within a regulated environment.
Demonstrated experience developing and communicating performance reporting, forecasting models, and scenario analysis.
Strong understanding of Canadian pension administration and service delivery operations.
Experience working with BI tools and data platforms.
Proficiency in data analysis, reporting, and dashboard development.
Experience supporting executive-level decision-making with structured analytics.
Knowledge of data governance frameworks and regulatory requirements related to pension reporting.
Strong written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to present complex findings clearly.
Programming or querying experience (e.g., SQL, Python) is an asset.

ATTRIBUTES

Analytical and structured thinker with strong attention to detail and accuracy.
Curious and insight-driven, with a continuous improvement mindset.
Clear communicator capable of translating complex data into practical insights.
Collaborative and cross-functional in approach.
Comfortable operating in ambiguous environments.
Responsible and disciplined in handling sensitive and regulated data.
Focused on enabling informed decision-making and operational transparency.

Do work that matters.
We are duty-bound to serve our members’ interests, and it’s a responsibility we don’t take lightly. That’s why we’ve ingrained sustainability in our work from day one—to ensure our members have a resilient future to retire into, both today and for generations to come.

Grow every day.

About Innocap

Innocap is the leading Dedicated Managed Account Platform (DMAP) globally, providing institutional allocators with a superior way to structure, access, and oversee their alternative investments. With over US$135 billion on the platform and more than 570 employees across the globe, we are transforming how allocators access and manage alternative investments.

Powered by our people, processes and purpose‑built technology, Innocap is seeking forward-thinking individuals to join us on our exciting journey. At Innocap, you won't just manage what’s here today. You’ll build what comes next. Here, careers are about building, not maintaining.

We give our people the freedom to think boldly, move quickly, and create real impact with less red tape. Driven by transformation, trust and collaboration, we never settle for the status quo and are constantly finding better ways to serve our clients and actively shape the future of the investment industry.

At Innocap, your work makes a difference every day – and helps build what’s next for our clients, the industry, and your career.

Because the future doesn’t build itself. We do.

About The Role

As Global Head of Cloud Platform Engineering, reporting to the Chief Technology Officer, you will own Innocap’s cloud runtime, developer platform, SRE practices, observability, cloud security guardrails, technology recovery and cloud economics. You will build and lead a high-leverage global engineering function that operates a secure, resilient and economical cloud estate and provides shared capabilities that make engineering teams faster and more effective.

Your mandate will be to provide global leadership, ownership and accountability across the following areas:

Cloud Infrastructure, Runtime and Scaling

The architecture, provisioning, secure connectivity and operational health of Innocap’s cloud infrastructure, primarily Microsoft Azure, including container and compute platforms, managed services, storage, networking and hybrid connectivity.
Capacity forecasting, cloud quotas, workload isolation and headroom, together with secure and scalable runtime foundations and compute orchestration for data and AI platforms, including appropriate identity, access, consumption, telemetry and emergency controls.

Developer Platform and Engineering Enablement

Declarative infrastructure provisioning, reusable CI/CD pipelines, artifact management, environment promotion, deployment validation and rollback, with configuration drift eliminated and exceptions visible and time bound.
Shared source-control and build-platform foundations, repository guardrails, build-agent security, artifact integrity, dependency and secret-scanning integrations, and the lifecycle of non-production and test environments.
Provide documented, reusable and self-service workflows for provisioning, deployment, access, test data and troubleshooting, and measure paved-road adoption, developer satisfaction, provisioning lead time and time saved.

Reliability, Observability, and Technology Recovery

The unified observability stack, telemetry standards and end-to-end service-level visibility; establish and govern SLOs, SLIs and error budgets; and lead major technology incident coordination, blameless postmortems and root-cause closure.
Establish production-readiness standards, named service ownership, sustainable on-call coverage and escalation; maintain an authoritative service inventory, architecture documentation and executable operational runbooks; and reduce alert noise, repeat incidents and operational toil.
Infrastructure backups, immutable recovery capabilities and failover mechanisms aligned with business-agreed RTOs and RPOs; run evidenced restore tests and coordinated technical recovery exercises and validate application and data recovery with domain teams.

Reliability Cloud Security and Audit Readiness

Engineer and operate cloud security guardrails, policy as code, scanning, detection integrations, environment isolation, IAM and RBAC, privileged access, secrets, encryption and key-lifecycle controls in partnership with Cybersecurity.
Automated patching, supported-version maintenance and vulnerability-remediation SLAs across shared platform components; automate continuous control-evidence collection for SOC 2 requirements and institutional client due diligence.

Cloud Economics and Technical Vendors

Cloud FinOps, including cost visibility and allocation, forecasting, budget alerting, commitment discounts, right-sizing, waste elimination and meaningful workload unit costs; serve as technical and operational owner for core cloud, data-platform runtime, observability and managed-service vendors.

Cloud Platform Strategy and Organizational Leadership

Define and execute a rolling platform roadmap aligned with business growth, application modernization and operational risk, including shared platform architecture, investment priorities, technical-debt reduction, supported patterns, versioning, upgrade paths, deprecation and retirement of unsupported infrastructure.
Build and develop a high-performing global engineering team with clear ownership, strong technical leadership, succession and sustainable support coverage; reduce key-person dependency and balance internal capability with managed services and specialist partners.
The function’s operating plan, staffing strategy and budget; make capacity allocation between operations, reliability improvement and roadmap delivery explicit; prevent urgent support from permanently displacing platform development; and report outcomes through a scorecard covering reliability, recovery, delivery stability, developer adoption, operational toil and unit cost.

Primary Qualifications & Skills

10+ years of experience in cloud infrastructure, platform engineering, DevOps or SRE, including 5+ years leading global platform or infrastructure teams in data-intensive, high-availability environments. Financial services, fintech, capital markets or institutional data-platform experience is strongly preferred.
Deep architectural expertise in Microsoft Azure, including AKS, networking, Entra ID/IAM, Key Vault and managed services, with modern infrastructure-as-code and CI/CD practices using tools such as Terraform or Bicep and GitHub or Azure DevOps.
Demonstrated success building reusable self-service platforms, improving developer productivity, establishing production-readiness and on-call practices, and delivering measurable reliability and recovery improvements.
Experience operating distributed data or compute platforms and enterprise observability tooling with disciplined cost and performance governance. Databricks and Datadog experience is an asset; equivalent platform experience is relevant.
Experience with SOC 2 control requirements or comparable assurance frameworks, institutional-grade disaster recovery, change control and auditability.
Proven ability to develop teams, prioritize a roadmap, manage budgets and vendors, translate cloud consumption into unit economics, and make pragmatic build-versus-buy and simplicity-versus-complexity decisions.
A technically credible player-coach who eliminates manual toil, measures outcomes, develops others and enables application teams rather than creating a centralized approval or ticket-taking bottleneck.
Excellent communication and stakeholder-management skills, with the ability to influence engineering leaders and translate technical priorities, risks and economics for business leaders.

jobs.title: Director of Portfolio Finance
jobs.description:
The opportunity

We are building a centralized finance function for our portfolio, and we are looking for the person to lead it. You will give Rhyno greater control over cash, faster and more reliable reporting, and the financial credibility to work with lenders and financing partners from a position of strength.
This role suits someone who is comfortable deep in the numbers and equally comfortable stepping back to tell the partners clearly what they see: where each business stands, what healthy looks like, and how far there is to go.

What you will do

1. Treasury and liquidity

Own rolling 13-week cash flow forecasts across all six companies, refreshed weekly with variance analysis against actuals.
Build the 12 to 24 month liquidity outlook that feeds budgets and planning.
Manage AP prioritization and supplier payment plans and monitor bank accounts and cash daily.
Track available credit and covenant headroom under base and downside cases and flag liquidity risks early.
Manage banking relationships, account structures and intercompany funding across the portfolio.

2. Financial reporting
Accelerate month-end and annual financial reporting across the portfolio.
Improve consolidation, and set a common reporting template, chart of accounts mapping and reporting calendar for every company.
Produce a weekly liquidity view and a monthly reporting package for Rhyno leadership.
Set the cadence and content of financial reporting for board meetings.
Coordinate year-end audits with external auditors.

3. Budgeting and forecasting
Lead the annual budget for each company and for the consolidated portfolio.
Run rolling forecasts and monthly variance analysis and hold company leaders accountable to plan.
Benchmark each company's P&L against a healthy business in its space and set clear targets for where it should be.

4. Operational advisory
Identify cash flow inefficiencies across receivables, payables and inventory, and set working capital targets with each company.
Tie project billing (schedules of billings, progress draws and holdbacks) to cash so invoicing moves on time.
Advise leadership on operational resizing and cost reductions.
Find quick wins across the portfolio in financial systems, operations and management practices.
Strengthen financial controls, including payment approvals, signing authority and fraud prevention.
Step in hands-on when a company is under cash pressure, and coach company finance teams on cash discipline.

5. Lender readiness
Produce accurate, consistent, lender-ready reporting that shows forecasting reliability, financial control and management accountability.
Prepare covenant calculations, borrowing base certificates and lender reporting.
Lead responses to lender and auditor requests.
Support credit renewals, amendments and financing discussions alongside Rhyno leadership.

How success is measured
Weekly cash forecast accuracy within agreed tolerance across the portfolio.
Faster, more reliable month-end and year-end reporting.
Cash released through working capital improvement against target.
No covenant breaches or liquidity surprises.
On-time, credible reporting to the board and lenders.
Continuous improvement in systems and processes across every portfolio finance department, with each company's finance lead supported in driving their own improvements.

What you bring
CPA with 5 to 10+ years of relevant experience.
Background in PE-backed manufacturing, multi-entity finance or corporate restructuring.
Hands-on experience with refinancing, liquidity management and financial reporting.
Strong operational understanding, beyond accounting or FP&A alone.
Experience as a Finance Director, Divisional CFO or Senior Finance Manager in a $50M to $300M manufacturing business, or in a restructuring or advisory practice.
Ability to shift priorities quickly and move with speed, without compromising accuracy or momentum.
Autonomy and confidence to make decisions with the information available and bring strong, clear recommendations to the partners and board.
An owner’s approach to results, with hands-on accountability from building the model to presenting the findings.
A continuous improvement approach, with the curiosity to test the numbers, dig into root causes and bring structure where there isn’t any.
Ability to build trust with company leaders and finance teams through clear, direct communication, high integrity and composure under pressure.

Compensation
Base salary of $160,000 to $190,000, plus performance bonus and benefits.

jobs.title: Vice President Finance
jobs.description:
Vice President of Finance – Canada

Location: Calgary, AB

Company: Hero Canada Foods Inc.

About Hero Canada Foods

Hero Canada Foods is a leading branded food company and part of the international Hero Group, headquartered in Switzerland. In Canada, Hero is known for its successful portfolio of brands including Baby Gourmet, Simply Gourmet, and Goodies. Hero Canada combines local entrepreneurial agility with the scale, expertise, and long-term perspective of an international food group and is investing in systems, processes, commercial capabilities, and organizational maturity to support profitable growth.

Role Summary

Hero Canada Foods is seeking a VP of Finance to lead all finance activities in Canada and serve as a key member of the leadership team. Reporting to the General Manager and partnering closely with Hero Group Finance, the VP Finance provides strategic financial leadership while maintaining a strong connection to the commercial and operational drivers of the business.

The VP Finance supports the General Manager in shaping strategy, setting priorities, evaluating opportunities, and navigating day-to-day operational decisions. The role provides clear financial guidance and constructive challenges while remaining close enough to the work to turn insight into action quickly.

The VP Finance will actively partner with the Commercial Finance Manager on pricing, customer profitability, trade investment, forecasting, and business case development, providing both strategic guidance and direct analytical support as needed. At the same time, they will lead a transactional accounting team consisting of a Senior Accountant, an Accounts Payable Accountant, and an Accounts Receivable Accountant, ensuring accurate reporting, disciplined controls, and reliable execution.

Key Responsibilities

1. Strategic Partner to the General Manager

Act as the General Manager’s trusted finance adviser on business strategy, growth priorities, organizational choices, investments, risks, and operational trade-offs.
Provide practical, fact-based guidance on day-to-day business matters, combining strategic perspective with an understanding of operational detail.
Translate financial and commercial information into clear choices, recommendations, scenarios, and actions for the General Manager and leadership team.
Constructively challenge assumptions and help align local decisions with Hero Canada’s objectives and Hero Group expectations.
Support the development and execution of the Canadian strategy, including profitable growth, margin improvement, cash generation, and operating profit protection.

2. Hands-on Commercial Finance Leadership

Lead and actively support the Commercial Finance Manager, providing coaching, prioritization, technical guidance, and direct practical assistance.
Lead financial analysis related to pricing, customer profitability, trade investment, promotions, and margin optimization, personally reviewing and supporting detailed financial models where appropriate.
Personally review, adjust, and, where required, build or manipulate detailed Excel-based pricing and commercial models rather than operating only at review level.
Partner closely with Sales, Marketing, Supply Chain, and Operations to improve decision quality and visibility of margins, cost drivers, pricing impacts, working capital, and profitability.
Ensure financial analysis is commercially relevant, technically sound, timely, and converted into clear recommendations.

3. Planning, Forecasting & Performance Management

Lead the annual budgeting process, rolling forecasts, performance reviews, and longer-term financial projections.
Connect commercial assumptions, supply chain realities, operating costs, and strategic initiatives into an integrated financial plan.
Monitor business performance, identify emerging gaps and opportunities, and establish corrective measures with accountable business owners.
Prepare clear reporting and decision materials for the General Manager, Canadian leadership team, Board, and Hero Group stakeholders.
Use scenario planning and sensitivity analysis to support decisions under uncertainty.

4. Accounting, Reporting & Transactional Finance Leadership

Lead the Senior Accountant, Accounts Payable Accountant, and Accounts Receivable Accountant, establishing clear ownership, priorities, service standards, and controls.
Oversee monthly, quarterly, and year-end close and ensure timely, accurate, and transparent reporting to local management and Hero Group.
Ensure accurate accounting in accordance with applicable accounting standards and Hero Group reporting requirements.
Maintain a strong internal-control environment across order-to-cash, procure-to-pay, record-to-report, payroll, inventory, and treasury processes.
Remain sufficiently close to transactional workflows to resolve issues, remove bottlenecks, improve quality, and provide hands-on support during peak periods or complex matters.
Drive pragmatic process improvements, automation, clear documentation, and stronger use of systems and data.

5. Cash Flow, Working Capital & Risk Management

Own cash flow planning, liquidity, and working capital performance, with focused management of receivables, payables, inventory, and operating commitments.
Identify and manage financial and operational exposures, including insurance, contracts, customer and supplier risk, and foreign exchange where relevant.
Support capital allocation, funding, and investment decisions with disciplined financial analysis and recommendations.
Serve as the primary financial steward of the Canadian business, ensuring decisions support sustainable value creation and alignment with Hero Group objectives.

6. Compliance, Tax & Governance

Ensure compliance with national, provincial, local, and Hero Group financial requirements.
Coordinate external audit, tax, payroll, benefits, legal, insurance, and advisory partners as required.
Oversee statutory filings, tax compliance, transfer pricing support, corporate governance requirements, and Group reporting obligations.
Ensure appropriate documentation, approval authorities, and segregation-of-duties or compensating controls are maintained.

7. Team Leadership & Capability Building

Build one connected finance team across commercial finance and accounting, balancing business partnership with reliable transaction processing and control.
Build finance talent and organizational capability through coaching, development planning, succession management, and cross-functional business exposure.
Develop the Commercial Finance Manager as a strong business partner while remaining available for detailed technical and modelling support.
Create a working culture that values accuracy, pace, ownership, practical problem-solving, continuous improvement, and constructive challenge.
Provide clear goals, coaching, feedback, succession planning, and development opportunities.

Team Structure

Reports to: General Manager, Hero Canada
Functional connection: Hero Group Finance
Direct leadership over: Commercial Finance Manager; Senior Accountant; Accounts Payable Accountant; Accounts Receivable Accountant

Required Qualifications & Experience

CPA designation strongly preferred.
10+ years of progressive finance and accounting experience, including meaningful senior finance leadership responsibility.
Experience serving as a CFO, VP Finance, Finance Director, or equivalent senior finance leader within a growth-oriented, lean operating environment.
Strong commercial finance experience with demonstrated depth in pricing, customer profitability, trade investment, financial modelling, budgeting, forecasting, and performance management.
Advanced Excel capability and willingness to work directly in detailed models and analyses.
Strong technical foundation in financial reporting, accounting, internal controls, cash flow, working capital, audit, tax, and compliance.
Experience leading both commercially oriented finance professionals and transactional accounting teams.
Experience in an international or cross-border business environment; CPG, food, manufacturing, distribution, or branded consumer products experience preferred.
Experience leading finance process improvements, ERP implementations, reporting enhancements, and finance transformation initiatives.

Key Competencies

Strategic and commercial mindset
Hands-on analytical and problem-solving capability
Influence and stakeholder management
Financial stewardship and risk management
Leadership and talent development
Continuous improvement orientation
Executive communication and presentation skills
High integrity and sound judgment
Financial modelling, analytical, and technical accounting capability

About The Role

Blacksmith Agency runs PPC and SEO for clients across multifamily, B2B and technical verticals. As Director of Digital Marketing you lead that department. The PPC strategist and the SEO strategist report to you and they are the specialists in their channels. Right now nobody owns this function, which is the whole reason this seat is open.

This is a management seat, not a senior individual contributor one.
You will not be building campaigns, and on technical SEO your strategist will know more than you do. That is the arrangement, not a gap. You carry channel strategy and where budget goes as accounts scale. The strategists carry the execution of it, and you carry whether the department delivers.

What You Own

The PPC strategist and the SEO strategist: their quality bar, their development, their reviews, and the call when someone is not going to get there.
The standard the work is held to. What a good audit looks like, what gets checked before work leaves the agency, how an account is reported. You write it and you hold two specialists to it.
Client results across the whole function, including whether our reporting is honest. Nobody here is auditing attribution and GA4 accuracy today.
The escalation when an account is at risk. You diagnose it, you direct the strategist who fixes it, and you are on the call with the client.
Channel strategy and where budget goes as accounts scale.
What we tell sales we can credibly deliver, before it gets sold.
The hiring plan for the department, and first-round interviews for your own team, within about a quarter.

What You Need

Strategists or specialists who have reported to you, where their reviews, their development and the decision when someone was not working out were yours. Managing accounts is not this.
7+ years across paid media and SEO. Owning one channel while sitting beside the other does not count here.
Enough depth in Google Ads, GA4, Search Console, Meta and Microsoft Ads to tell good work from work that merely looks good. That is a lower bar than doing it and a higher bar than reading a report.
One account you turned around that you can talk through: the metric, the figure before, the figure after, and why the change worked. Whose hands were on the keyboard matters far less than whether the diagnosis was yours.
Comfortable being the client-facing owner when an account is underperforming. That call comes to you, not to the strategist.
Agency experience carrying many accounts at once.

Please do not apply if

Nobody has ever reported to you, or you have never owned someone's review or had to performance-manage anyone.
You have only ever run one channel.
All of your experience is in-house on a single brand.
What you actually want is to keep building campaigns yourself. That is not a lesser ambition, it is a different job, and this is not it.

None of these are preferences we bend on. They are how we screen, so applying anyway costs you an hour and gets you a no.

Process

Three conversations, then a decision. A thirty minute screen with our recruiter, a first round with the founder this seat reports to, and a final. No take-home project and no panel interview.

How To Apply

Four fields at the link, then a short 6 minute Predictive Index assessment. Use the same email throughout. No cover letter.

As Director, Digital Infrastructure, the role will lead a national team of technical sales professionals while partnering with some of Canada's most influential organizations in the Data Centre, Telecommunications, Financial Services, and Banking sectors.
This role is ideal for an accomplished sales leader with a strong technical foundation and a passion for developing people, building executive relationships, and influencing complex customer ecosystems. The role will play a pivotal role in positioning Phoenix Contact as the preferred technology partner and manufacturer of choice for critical infrastructure projects across Canada.

POSITION RESPONSIBILITIES

Lead and Develop a High-Performing Team

Lead, coach, and develop a team of 4-6 Digital Infrastructure Specialists located across Canada.

Establish clear objectives, development plans, and performance expectations that drive individual and team success.

Drive Strategic Market Growth

Build executive-level relationships with key customers, consultants, industry stakeholders, and decision-makers.
Identify emerging market opportunities, industry trends, and strategic projects that align with Phoenix Contact's growth objectives.
Position Phoenix Contact as a trusted advisor and preferred partner within targeted accounts.

Influence the Digital Infrastructure Ecosystem

Work closely with customers, their supply chains, and selected technology partners to create preference for Phoenix Contact solutions.
Drive both specification and prescription opportunities by influencing key stakeholders throughout the project lifecycle.
Engage with General Contractors, Consultants, EPCs, OEM Manufacturers, System Integrators, and Panel Builders to increase adoption of our solutions.
Strengthen Phoenix Contact's presence and reputation across the entire Digital Infrastructure value chain.

Align Sales, Distribution, and Marketing Resources

Partner with Field Sales teams to ensure consistent and professional coverage across customer organizations and buying centers.
Collaborate with Regional Distributor Managers to optimize route-to-market strategies and channel engagement.
Work alongside Strategic Marketing to map targeted customers and their associated supply chains, identifying key influencers and growth opportunities.
Coordinate resources across the organization to deliver a seamless customer experience and maximize market impact.

Champion Our Digital Infrastructure Portfolio

Lead the strategic positioning and growth of Phoenix Contact's solutions in:
Power Reliability
Connectivity Devices & Network Infrastructure
Building Automation
Cabinet Efficiency & Industrial Components

By leveraging the full breadth of our portfolio, the role will help customers improve reliability, efficiency, connectivity, and operational performance throughout their critical infrastructure environments.

QUALIFICATION REQUIREMENTS

Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Engineering Technology, Business, or a related discipline.
10+ years of success in technical sales, business development, account management, or market development.
Minimum 5 years of leadership experience managing technical sales or business development teams.
Proven experience within Data Centre, Telecommunications, Financial Services, Banking, Critical Infrastructure, Industrial Automation, or related markets.
Demonstrated ability to influence specifications, develop strategic partnerships, and lead complex solution-based sales initiatives.
Strong understanding of electrical, electronic, connectivity, automation, and infrastructure technologies.

ESSENTIAL JOB REQUIREMENTS

Must have a valid driver’s license
Outstanding communication skills – written, verbal and listening.

Exceptional relationship builder and executive influencer.
Strong communicator capable of engaging both technical and business audiences.
Collaborative leader who thrives in a matrixed, cross-functional environment.
Customer-focused with a track record of delivering sustainable growth.

jobs.title: Director of Finance
jobs.description:
An established organization in the healthcare and community services sector is seeking an experienced Director of Finance
to lead its financial strategy and support an important period of organizational transformation. This opportunity is ideal for a finance leader who enjoys strengthening financial operations, developing efficient systems, and providing strategic guidance to senior leadership.

The successful candidate will play a key role in improving financial reporting, enhancing internal controls, and supporting the organization's long-term financial sustainability.

About the Role
Reporting to senior executive leadership, the Director of Finance will oversee financial planning, budgeting, regulatory compliance, and overall financial performance. The position involves working closely with executive leadership and the Board to provide financial insights, manage organizational risks, and support strategic decision-making.

This role offers the opportunity to lead improvements across the finance function, establish effective financial processes, and guide the implementation of new systems. The successful candidate will provide leadership to the finance team while maintaining a strong focus on financial accountability, operational efficiency, and long-term planning.

What You’ll Do

Lead financial planning, budgeting, forecasting, and reporting activities to support organizational objectives.

Provide strategic financial guidance to executive leadership and the Board, including performance analysis, risk assessments, and recommendations.

Oversee the preparation of annual operating and capital budgets in collaboration with departmental leaders.

Prepare and present financial reports, variance analyses, and management recommendations to support informed decision-making.

Manage government funding, grants, subsidies, and related financial reporting obligations.

Ensure compliance with public sector accounting standards, healthcare regulations, and applicable funding requirements.

Oversee financial controls, policies, and approval processes to maintain accuracy, accountability, and compliance.

Develop long-term financial plans to support capital investments, operational improvements, and resource requirements.

Lead financial transformation initiatives, including improvements to accounting procedures, reporting processes, and financial systems.

Oversee financial management across multiple organizational programs and ensure effective allocation of resources.

Manage external audit relationships and ensure timely completion of financial statements and regulatory reporting.

Collaborate with internal stakeholders to strengthen financial processes and improve operational efficiency.

Provide leadership, coaching, and professional development support to finance team members.

Participate in management discussions and contribute financial perspectives to organizational planning and operational decisions.

Identify opportunities to improve financial sustainability, reporting accuracy, and overall financial performance.

What You Bring

Bachelor's degree in Accounting, Finance, Business Administration, or a related discipline.

CPA designation required.

Approximately 7-10 years of progressive accounting and finance experience, including 3-5 years in a senior leadership or management role.

Strong understanding of financial reporting, budgeting, forecasting, and financial controls.

Working knowledge of Public Sector Accounting Board (PSAB) standards and government-funded financial reporting requirements.

Experience within long-term care, healthcare, public sector, or a similarly regulated environment.

Familiarity with regulatory compliance, government funding, and financial reporting obligations.

Advanced proficiency in Microsoft Excel, including financial analysis, forecasting, and modelling.

Experience with financial management systems, accounting software, and ERP platforms.

Demonstrated ability to lead financial process improvements, systems enhancements, or organizational transformation initiatives.

Strong strategic thinking, analytical, and problem-solving abilities.

Proven leadership experience, with the ability to mentor teams and oversee financial operations.

Excellent communication and stakeholder management skills, including presenting financial information to senior leadership and governing bodies.

Ability to manage competing priorities, meet reporting deadlines, and exercise sound professional judgment.

Bilingual proficiency in English and French is strongly preferred.

Familiarity with Canadian employment standards, tax remittances, and healthcare-related financial regulations is an asset.

Ability to complete a satisfactory Vulnerable Sector Check prior to employment.

Why Join
This is an excellent opportunity to join an established, purpose-driven organization undergoing meaningful financial and operational transformation. The role offers the chance to take ownership of financial strategy, work closely with executive leadership and the Board, and lead initiatives that strengthen reporting, systems, and internal controls. With significant leadership responsibilities and the ability to shape the future direction of the finance function, this position is well-suited to an experienced finance professional who enjoys building efficient processes, driving positive change, and making a lasting impact within the healthcare and community services sector.

jobs.description:
Type de poste :
Permanent Modèle de travail :
Hybride Numéro de demande:

Toronto, ON; Brossard, QC; Burlington, ON; Calgary, AB; Edmonton, AB; Fredericton, NB; Halifax, NS; Kitchener, ON; Laval, QC; Moncton, NB; Montréal, QC; Ottawa, ON; Régina, SK; Saint John, NB; Saskatoon, SK; St. John's, NL; Vancouver, BC; Victoria, BC; Winnipeg, MB; ville de Québec, QC

Notre raison d’être

Chez Deloitte, notre raison d’être est d’avoir une influence marquante. Nous existons pour inspirer et aider nos gens, nos organisations, nos collectivités et nos pays à prospérer en créant un avenir meilleur. Notre travail soutient une société prospère où les gens peuvent s’épanouir et saisir des occasions. Il renforce la confiance des consommateurs et des entreprises, aide les organisations à trouver des moyens créatifs de déployer des capitaux, habilite des institutions sociales et économiques justes, fiables et efficaces, et permet à nos amis, à nos familles et à nos collectivités de profiter de la qualité de vie qui accompagne un avenir durable. Étant le plus grand cabinet de services professionnels détenu et exploité à 100 % par des Canadiens dans notre pays, nous sommes fiers de travailler aux côtés de nos clients pour avoir une influence positive sur tous les Canadiens.

En incarnant notre raison d’être, nous aurons une influence marquante.

Diversifiez votre carrière au sein du Cabinet.
Tirez parti d’avantages souples, proactifs et pratiques qui favorisent une culture de bien-être et la création de liens solides.
Approfondissez vos connaissances grâce au mentorat d’experts et à du coaching au travail.

--

À quoi ressemblera votre journée type

En tant que leader principal(e) d’Oracle EPM Planning (directeur(trice) principal(e)), vous serez responsable des programmes de planification d’entreprise et de transformation de la fonction finance pour façonner des solutions, de la gestion de relations avec des clients et de l’exécution de nombreuses missions.

À ce titre, vous devrez faire ce qui suit :

Superviser simultanément la prestation de bout en bout de l’architecture de solutions et de nombreuses missions Oracle EPM Planning, y compris l’étendue, le plan de travail, la gestion des risques et des problèmes (RAID), la gestion financière, la gestion de la qualité et les résultats globaux de la prestation.
Fournir des conseils sur les stratégies de transformation de la fonction finance et de planification d’entreprise.
Assumer la responsabilité de la conception de la solution et des décisions en matière d’architecture.
Diriger la définition des processus de planification pour l’état futur et des modèles d’exploitation en tirant parti des capacités d’Oracle EPM pour rehausser l’efficacité et les perspectives d’affaires.
Favoriser l’harmonisation entre les finances, les TI et les parties prenantes de la direction pour favoriser des processus décisionnels efficaces et veiller à la réussite des programmes.
Assurer la direction fonctionnelle des solutions Oracle EPM Planning, y compris la gamme complète de modules EPBCS.
Superviser la conception du modèle de planification et l’architecture des solutions (catalyseurs, hypothèses, scénarios, flux des travaux, production de rapports) et s’assurer que les solutions sont adaptables, durables et harmonisées aux objectifs du client.
Veiller à l’exécution de cas d’utilisation de grande qualité sur le plan de la planification, des prévisions et de la gestion du rendement.
Superviser les activités de test et de déploiement, notamment la stratégie de test, le tri des défectuosités, l’état de préparation aux essais d’acceptation par l’utilisateur et la planification du déploiement, afin de s’assurer que les solutions sont adoptées avec succès et créent la valeur commerciale attendue.
Favoriser le développement des affaires en faisant preuve de leadership sur le plan des offres de service, en effectuant des présentations auprès des clients et en assurant la gestion des relations.
Contribuer aux stratégies de mise en marché, à l’élaboration d’offres de service et au leadership d’opinion au sein de l’équipe Oracle EPM.
Diriger et encadrer des équipes de prestation dans le cadre de nombreuses missions, afin de promouvoir une solide discipline d’exécution et leur perfectionnement grâce au coaching, au mentorat et à une rétroaction de qualité.
Contribuer au recrutement, à l’intégration et au développement de capacités au sein de l’équipe Oracle EPM.
Demeurer au courant des nouveautés liées au produit Oracle EPM et intégrer les innovations pertinentes à la prestation de services, en particulier les capacités d’IA/IGR telles que la planification prédictive, Auto Predict et IPM Insights.
Aider les clients à mettre en œuvre des capacités de planification habilitées par l’IA pour améliorer l’exactitude des prévisions, automatiser la création de perspectives et améliorer les processus décisionnels.
Façonner les réflexions de clients sur le rôle de l’IA dans le cadre de la planification d’entreprise, et la création d’un équilibre entre l’innovation et la mise en œuvre de mesures pratiques qui créent de la valeur.

La personne retenue aura l’occasion de faire partie de notre premier cabinet de services-conseils qui travaille à la fine pointe de mises en œuvre d’Oracle Cloud. Vous travaillerez auprès d’une grande variété de clients et jouerez un rôle important dans certaines des mises en œuvre les plus stimulantes à l’échelle mondiale.

Renseignements sur l’équipe

L’équipe adopte et incarne la raison d’être du Cabinet – c’est-à-dire avoir une influence marquante –, tout en vous poussant à vous surpasser, vous-même et votre équipe, afin de trouver des solutions aux problèmes les plus importants de nos clients, de nos gens et de la société.

Veiller au perfectionnement de gens et d’équipes hautement performantes en leur offrant des occasions stimulantes et pertinentes.
Offrir un service à la clientèle exceptionnel en obtenant un rendement élevé, tout en favorisant la collaboration entre les équipes et les régions.
Exercer une influence positive sur les clients, les équipes et les gens en donnant l’exemple et en établissant de solides relations.
Veiller à ce que les gens soient sur la même longueur d’onde et à ce que les priorités soient harmonisées aux objectifs d’affaires des clients et de Deloitte.

Assez parlé de nous, parlons de vous

Vous Avez Le Profil Suivant

Au moins huit années d’expérience dans la prestation de solutions Oracle EPM Planning dans des environnements de consultation ou d’entreprise.
Expérience dans la supervision de programmes de transformation de la fonction finance et de la planification d’entreprise pour améliorer les processus de budgétisation, de prévision et de présentation de l’information.
Expérience éprouvée dans la mise en œuvre de bout en bout d’Oracle EPM Planning tout au long du cycle de vie du projet, des exigences au déploiement et à la stabilisation.
Expérience éprouvée en gestion de missions de grande envergure ou simultanées, ainsi qu’en gestion de l’exécution, des parties prenantes et des aspects financiers des missions.
Excellente expertise fonctionnelle liée aux plateformes Oracle EPM Planning, y compris les systèmes EPBCS, PBCS et Hyperion Planning), et aux modules associés (Workforce, Capital, Project, Strategic Modelling).
Compréhension approfondie des processus de planification et d’analyse financières, y compris la budgétisation, les prévisions, la planification à long terme et la gestion du rendement.
Expérience de la gestion des aspects financiers des projets, de leur étendue et des risques liés aux missions complexes.
Connaissances pratiques des intégrations, de l’architecture des métadonnées et des technologies connexes (p. ex., gestion des données, FDMEE, règles d’affaires Essbase, création de scripts dans Groovy, et IPA REST).
Solides compétences en résolution de problèmes et capacité d’analyser et de résoudre des problèmes d’affaires complexes au moyen d’approches structurées.
Excellentes aptitudes pour la communication et les relations interpersonnelles, capacité de produire du contenu prêt à l’emploi et de communiquer avec les parties prenantes de haut niveau avec assurance.
Compréhension des capacités de planification propulsées par l’IA dans Oracle EPM, telles que Auto Predict et IPM Insights, capacité à les utiliser de manière responsable afin d’améliorer l’exactitude des prévisions et l’efficacité de la planification, et expérience de leur application (ou soutien de l’application).
Baccalauréat en finances, en comptabilité, en technologies de l’information ou dans un domaine connexe; une maîtrise ou un titre professionnel (p. ex., CPA, MBA) est un atout.
Certifications Oracle EPM (p. ex., certification Oracle Cloud EPM) : considérées comme un atout important.

Le bilinguisme en français et en anglais est requis pour ce poste en raison de la nature du rôle ayant des interactions avec les clients et les équipes de projet nationaux et mondiaux.

Rémunération totale

L’échelle salariale pour ce poste est de 105,000 $ à 234,000 $. Certaines personnes peuvent être admissibles à notre programme de prime. Sur le plan salarial, Deloitte se concentre sur l’équité et la compétitivité. Nous établissons régulièrement des comparaisons aux données de référence du marché établies pour divers postes, secteurs, cibles et niveaux. Notre approche est fondée sur l’importance de reconnaître les forces et les contributions uniques de chaque personne et de récompenser celle-ci pour la valeur qu’elle apporte.

La rémunération totale offerte par Deloitte s’étend bien au-delà des programmes traditionnels de rémunération et d’avantages sociaux et est conçue pour reconnaître les contributions des employés, favoriser le mieux-être personnel et soutenir la croissance du Cabinet. En plus de nos jours de congé payés réguliers, quelques exemples incluent : 4 000 $ par an pour les avantages de soutien en santé mentale, un compte de dépenses flexibles de 1 300 $, des fermetures à l'échelle de l'entreprise connues sous le nom de "Jours Deloitte", des journées dédiées à l'apprentissage (connues sous le nom de Jours de Développement et d'Innovation), des arrangements de travail flexibles et une structure de travail hybride.

Notre promesse à nos gens : Deloitte est là où vous pouvez propulsez vos ambitions.

Vous, et plus encore.

Évoluez au sein d’une équipe passionnée et déterminée à apprendre et à développer de nouvelles compétences. Bâtissez votre réseau et faites le plein d’expériences qui vous permettront de vous épanouir et vous mèneront vers la prochaine étape de votre carrière.

Vos chemins nous portent plus loin.

La diversité de vos compétences, perspectives et expériences nous rend meilleurs. Nous voulons que vous vous sentiez comme chez vous, qui que vous soyez et d’où que vous veniez. Nous vous oﬀrons des options de travail ﬂexibles et personnalisées pour répondre à vos besoins, peu importe votre mode de vie.

Devenez le leader que vous désirez être.

Certains dirigent des équipes, d’autres sont au cœur d’un changement de culture, d’autres encore bâtissent une expertise de pointe. Nous soutiendrons votre croissance en tant que leader par l’entremise d’expériences, d’occasions et de défis variés et enrichissants.

Ayez autant de carrières que vous le souhaitez.

Nous sommes en mesure de vous offrir de nouveaux rôles et de nouvelles responsabilités, et de vous aider à vous y préparer. Notre objectif est de conjuguer vos aspirations à vos compétences et à l’excellence de votre savoir-faire. Nous sommes l’endroit pour développer un réseau durable d’amis, de pairs et de mentors.

La balle est dans votre camp

Chez Deloitte, nous avons à cœur de faire des affaires de manière inclusive – cela commence par une diversité parmi les collègues de toutes les compétences! Deloitte encourage tous les candidats qualifiés qui représentent la diversité des collectivités partout au Canada

jobs.title: Senior Director, Enterprise Platforms
jobs.description:

The Senior Director, Enterprise Platforms leads enterprise architecture, client solutioning, and pre-sales strategy for pharmaceutical and life sciences organizations. This role bridges sales opportunity ownership with hands-on technical leadership, shaping complex omnichannel ecosystems that drive measurable business impact. The position partners closely with Sales, Strategy, Medical, Media, and Delivery teams to position technology as a differentiator in multi-million-dollar pursuits while establishing scalable architecture standards.

Establish governance frameworks, architecture standards, and AI-enabled solution patterns while guiding steering committees and mentoring internal architecture teams.

Qualifications

Experience establishing architecture governance processes and reference models within regulated industries.
