jobs.title: Deals Value Creation Analytics Director
jobs.description:
At PwC, our people in deals focus on providing strategic advice and support to clients in areas such as mergers and acquisitions, divestitures, and restructuring. They help clients navigate complex transactions and maximise value in their business deals. Those in deal integration and valuation realisation at PwC will focus on assisting clients in successfully integrating acquisitions and maximising the value of their investments. You will be responsible for conducting valuations, financial analysis, and developing strategies for post-merger integration.

The Opportunity

As a Director in Deals Value Creation Analytics, you'll work as part of a team of problem solvers, helping clients use data, analytics, and AI to solve complex business issues from strategy to execution.

Responsibilities include but are not limited to:

Leading high-profile analytics engagements across sell-side, buy-side, value creation, and performance improvement contexts, translating complex data into clear commercial insights
Helping management teams and investors understand business performance, growth drivers, customer behaviour, pricing, revenue quality, margins, operational efficiency, and value creation opportunities
Bringing together financial, commercial, operational, and technical perspectives to support fact-based decision making
Structuring ambiguous problems, defining analytical workplans, and guiding teams from data discovery through to executive-ready insights and deliverables
Leading business development activities, including opportunity identification, relationship building, proposal development, client pitches, and broader practice growth
Building relationships across PwC to support integrated client solutions, including across Deals, Consulting, Tax, Assurance, and data and AI teams
Supporting the development of the Value Creation Analytics practice, including methodologies, tools, reusable assets, delivery standards, and market-facing propositions
Coaching and developing team members across technical, commercial, financial, and client-facing skills
Most importantly, we need you to become a business partner and strategic advisor to our clients, translating and communicating your analysis to help answer critical commercial questions.

What You’ll Bring

Significant experience in analytics, corporate finance, value creation, management consulting, corporate development, private equity, M&A, or a related field
Experience leading client engagements, managing teams, and delivering high-quality work under tight timelines
Experience supporting transactions, performance improvement, value creation, corporate strategy, finance transformation, or related advisory work
Strong commercial and financial acumen, with the ability to understand business drivers and translate data into practical insights for executives, investors, and management teams
Strong understanding of financial analysis and business case development, including forecasting, scenario analysis, sensitivity analysis, KPI driver trees, and investment case support
Experience contributing to business development, including opportunity identification, proposal development, client pitches, and relationship building
Proven ability to build trusted relationships with clients and internal stakeholders at multiple levels
Experience working with complex data environments and guiding teams through data structuring, transformation, analysis, visualization, and insight development
Working knowledge of modern analytics, cloud data, and AI-enabled delivery tools, with the ability to identify practical use cases for AI, automation, and analytics in client delivery and business operations
Strong executive communication skills, including the ability to explain complex financial, operational, technical, or analytical concepts to non-technical stakeholders
Strong people leadership skills, with a demonstrated ability to coach, mentor, and develop high-performing teams
A collaborative working style and a demonstrated commitment to valuing differences, developing diverse teams, and ensuring diverse perspectives are heard
Ability and willingness to travel up to approximately 20% within Canada and internationally

This newly created role reflects our commitment to growth and delivering distinctive value for our clients and stakeholders.

The salary range for this position is $175,000 - $225,000. The posted salary range represents the expected hiring range for PwC locations in major city centres. Given our national recruiting approach, ranges may vary for positions in other locations. At PwC Canada, base salary is determined by your skills, experience, qualifications and work location. In addition to base salary, eligible employees may have opportunities to participate in variable incentive pay programs which are designed to reward individual and firm-wide achievements. We are committed to offering competitive compensation and adhere to all relevant pay transparency legislation. During the hiring process, our Talent Acquisition team will provide details about our comprehensive total rewards package.

Why you’ll love PwC

We’re inspiring and empowering our people to change the world. Powered by the latest technology, you’ll be a part of diverse teams helping public and private clients build trust and deliver sustained outcomes. This meaningful work, and our continuous development environment, will take your career to the next level. We reward your impact, and support your wellbeing, through a competitive compensation package, inclusive benefits and flexibility programs that will help you thrive in work and life. Learn more about our Application Process and Total Rewards Package at: https://jobs-ca.pwc.com/ca/en/life-at-pwc

Job Description 

 What’s the Opportunity? 
 Newcomers are critical client segment for RBC, with distinct needs across their journey - from preparing to move to Canada, to establishing their financial lives upon arrival, to building deeper financial relationships as they settle and grow.
 As Director, Newcomer Channel Strategy & Operations, you will lead the strategy and evolution of the channels, capabilities and partnership operations required to deliver a differentiated newcomer banking proposition. You will own the "how" behind our newcomer strategy: translating our ambition into intuitive client journeys, scalable capabilities, effective frontline experiences and an ecosystem of services that helps newcomers establish their lives in Canada.
 This is a highly cross-functional role. You will work across Everyday Banking & Client Growth, Product, Digital, Enablement, Advice Centre, Technology, Risk, Compliance, Marketing, and external partners to identify friction, establish priorities, and mobilize the organization around a multi-year newcomer journey.

 What You'll Do 
 Own the End-To-End Newcomer Onboarding Experience 
 Develop and continuously evolve the target experience for newcomers across key moments in their journey - from pre-arrival through onboarding, settlement, and early relationship growth
 Map and assess end-to-end newcomer journeys across digital, assisted, and non-traditional channels
 Identify the highest impact experience gaps, friction points, and capability opportunities
 Define the target state newcomer experience and work cross-functionally to define it into a prioritized roadmap
 Establish clear experience principles and standards that can be applied across products and channels
 Partner with Product and Journey teams to ensure newcomer needs are incorporated into broader enterprise roadmaps rather than addressed solely through segment-specific initiatives
 Own the Pre-Arrival Account Open Capability 
 Own and continuously evolve the end-to-end pre-arrival account open capability, ensuring a seamless accessible and differentiated experience for newcomers establishing their relationship before coming to Canada
 Define the strategic direction and prioritized roadmap for pre-arrival account opening, identifying opportunities to enhance functionality, simplify the client experience and expand acquisition opportunities
 Identify and address capability gaps, client friction points, and operational inefficiencies across the pre-arrival account opening journey, from application and identity verification through account activation and funding
 Partner with Digital, Product, Technology, Business Development, Operations and Risk teams to deliver capability enhancements that balance client experience, business growth, operational scalability and regulatory requirements

 Identify policies or processes creating disproportionate friction for newcomers

 Improve consistency in how newcomer policies are understood and executed across channels  Own the Newcomer Channel Strategy

 Work with distribution leaders to understand frontline friction and execution gaps
 Ensure new capabilities and propositions can be delivered consistently across channels

  Deliver Newcomer Advisor Enablement

 Define the ideal newcomer advisor experience
 Simplify complex policies and product information
 Develop tools and frameworks that support needs-based advice

 Create feedback loops between NCOE and National Office Newcomer Client Segment team to remain aware of key challenges, issues, or escalations.

 Must-have 
 8+ years of experience in strategy, client experience, digital transformation, product management, operations or financial services.
 Proven experience leading complex enterprise initiatives across highly matrixed organizations.
 Demonstrated ability to translate strategic priorities into scalable business capabilities and operational outcomes.
 Strong understanding of client journey design, digital enablement and experience transformation.
 Exceptional stakeholder management and influencing skills across senior leadership teams.
 Experience leading and developing high-performing teams.
 Strong executive communication skills with the ability to simplify complex topics and influence strategic decisions.

 Experience working with partner ecosystems or enterprise implementations.

jobs.title: Director, Technology Product Strategy
jobs.description:
Job Description 

 What is the opportunity? 
 Join our U.S. Technology Strategy and Architecture team as Director, Technology Product Strategy, where you will play a key role in supporting the development and execution of technology strategy across RBC’s U.S. organization.
 Working closely with U.S. Technology Strategy & Architecture leadership, business lines, technology teams, and enterprise architecture, you will help shape the strategic direction of the U.S. technology organization. You will analyze the technology landscape, support strategic planning and investment decisions, and work across business and technology teams to advance key priorities.
 This role provides broad exposure across the U.S. technology organization and an opportunity to work on some of its most important strategic questions. You will combine structured problem solving, technology knowledge, stakeholder management, and executive communication to support senior leaders in making informed technology decisions and advancing the U.S. technology agenda.

 What will you do? 
 Support target-state strategy development:  Partner with Technology Strategy & Architecture leadership to develop and maintain forward-looking U.S. technology strategy and, where required, business-line technology strategies. Gather inputs, assess strategic alternatives, and translate direction into clear target-state objectives, principles, KPIs, and priorities.
 Maintain a view of the technology estate:  Develop and maintain a comprehensive view of the U.S. technology landscape, bringing together information on applications, platforms, infrastructure, capabilities, dependencies, and investments to support strategic planning and decision-making.
 Conduct strategic analyses:  Perform structured, point-in-time analyses of technology opportunities, challenges, and strategic questions. Synthesize quantitative and qualitative information, evaluate alternatives, and develop recommendations for leadership consideration.
 Support strategic alignment:  Work with business and technology stakeholders to assess the alignment of major initiatives, programs, and investments with U.S. technology strategy and enterprise priorities. Identify potential gaps or areas of misalignment and support development of appropriate actions.
 Support roadmap and funding decisions:  Develop analyses and decision materials that help leadership evaluate technology roadmaps, investment priorities, dependencies, trade-offs, and funding requirements.
 Support architecture governance and control:  Partner with Enterprise Architecture and technology teams to facilitate architecture governance activities, track strategic and architectural decisions, identify areas requiring escalation, and support alignment with established architecture principles and target states.
 Coordinate strategic planning activities:  Support recurring strategy, roadmap, portfolio, and governance processes across the U.S. technology organization, ensuring stakeholders have the information and analysis required to make timely decisions.
 Develop executive-level materials:  Translate complex technology topics into concise presentations, recommendations, business cases, and decision materials for senior technology and business leadership.
 Monitor strategic progress:  Develop and maintain KPIs, KRIs, and other measures that provide visibility into progress against technology strategies, roadmaps, strategic initiatives, and architectural objectives.
 Build organizational capability:  Support the development and adoption of frameworks, methodologies, tools, templates, and ways of working that strengthen technology strategy and architecture capabilities across the U.S. organization.
 Facilitate cross-functional collaboration:  Coordinate across business lines, technology teams, architecture, finance, risk, and other stakeholders to gather inputs, resolve issues, and support decisions on cross-cutting technology priorities.
 Identify emerging issues and opportunities:  Analyze trends across the technology estate and external technology landscape to identify potential capability gaps, duplication, architectural constraints, emerging technologies, and opportunities for strategic improvement.

 What do you need to succeed? 
 Must have: 
 Undergraduate degree or equivalent experience in technology, business, engineering, finance, or a related field.
 10+ years of experience across technology strategy, enterprise architecture, technology transformation, management consulting, technology program management, or related disciplines.
 Strong strategic and analytical capabilities, with demonstrated experience structuring ambiguous problems and developing fact-based recommendations.
 Ability to understand complex technology environments and connect technology considerations to broader business and strategic objectives.
 Experience supporting technology strategies, roadmaps, business cases, investment decisions, operating models, or transformation initiatives.
 Strong executive communication skills, including the ability to synthesize complex information into clear presentations and decision materials.
 Strong stakeholder management skills and demonstrated ability to work effectively across business and technology organizations.
 Ability to manage multiple priorities and deliver high-quality work in a complex, matrixed environment.
 Strong understanding of technology and/or the financial services industry.
 Experience using current AI tooling to support research, automate repetitive tasks, analyze large data sets, etc.

 Nice to have: 
 Experience in financial services or another highly regulated industry.
 Experience in a matrix environment, such as a large, publicly traded corporation.

 What’s in it for you? 
 We thrive on the challenge to be our best, progressive thinking to keep growing, and working together to deliver trusted advice to help our clients thrive and communities prosper. We care about each other, reaching our potential, making a difference to our communities, and achieving success that is mutual.
 A comprehensive Total Rewards Program including bonuses and flexible benefits, competitive compensation, commissions, and stock where applicable.
 Leaders who support your development through coaching and managing opportunities.
 Ability to make a difference and lasting impact.
 Work in a dynamic, collaborative, progressive, and high-performing team.
 A world-class training program in financial services.

At PointClickCare, we empower our people to be the architects of a smarter healthcare future; one that is human-first and accelerated by AI to create meaningful and lasting change. Employees harness AI as a catalyst for creativity, productivity, and thoughtful decision-making. By integrating AI tools into our daily workflows, collaboration is enhanced, outcomes are improved, and every team member has the proficiency to maximize their impact. Join us in redefining healthcare — so it doesn’t just survive, it thrives. To learn more about PointClickCare, check out Life at PointClickCare and connect with us on Glassdoor and LinkedIn.

Travel to Office expectations**

For Hybrid Roles
: If this role is Hybrid, there will be an expectation to reside within commutable distance to the office/location specified in the job listing. This will include, but not limited to, weekly/bi-weekly/monthly events in the office with your specific team. This is a requirement for this role.

Team Summary

Our team of five Partner Managers owns the full partner lifecycle, from identifying and prioritizing partners through negotiation, go-to-market planning and execution, and ongoing performance management. As Director, you’ll lead this team while also playing a central role in our data strategy, helping evolve and execute authorized data access pathways for both customers and third-party vendors. This is a high-impact opportunity to shape how our partner ecosystem and data strategy work together as an organizational priority. The role can be performed remotely or from one of our offices, so you can work where you do your best work.

Job Summary

Director, Partnerships & Data Strategy is responsible for developing and maintaining the Partner Powered Solutions strategy, managing the entire life cycle of partner relationships (identification, prioritization, negotiation, GTM planning & execution, and ongoing performance management). The role requires an individual who is a strategic thinker with a demonstrated ability to act individually where required but also lead and improve team efficiency and effectiveness through the creation and continued optimization of process and approach. In addition, the Director leads PointClickCare's Data Strategy, supporting the organizational imperative to evolve and execute authorized data access pathways for both customers and third-party vendors. This requires working closely with Product, Engineering, Sales, Marketing, Corporate Development, Legal and Regulatory to define and execute a Data Strategy roadmap aligned to market needs, voice of customer, and regulatory requirements, while cultivating the third-party vendor relationships and internal enablement needed to bring that roadmap to market.

Key Responsibilities

Lead, grow and manage a partnerships team responsible for identifying, selecting, and finalizing the negotiations and operationalization of commercial agreements for new partners
Formulate and evolve partnership strategy, articulate partnership hypothesis, define and deliver an exceptional exchange of value.
Communicates with partners and internal stakeholders at all stages of the deal process to secure agreement and approvals. Lead negotiation strategy, driving deals to closure. Serve as point of escalation for team members during negotiations and partner onboarding.
Conducts monthly partner reviews, provides financial updates, progress against commitment, margin, revenue growth and risk assessments.
Work closely with internal stakeholders across Product, Engineering, Sales, Marketing, Corporate Development, Legal and Regulatory to define, support and execute the Data Strategy roadmap in alignment with market needs, voice of customer and regulatory requirements.
Establish and operate a consistent intake, evaluation and approval process for customer and third-party data access requests, including criteria, decision rights and turnaround expectations.

Required Skills & Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree or equivalent experience in business, technology, data, or a related field
8+ years of experience in partnerships, business development, product, or data strategy, including 3+ years leading and developing teams
Demonstrated experience managing the full partner lifecycle: identification, prioritization, negotiation, go-to-market planning and execution, and performance management
Experience with healthcare data, interoperability or data access and licensing programs, including working knowledge of the privacy and regulatory frameworks that govern them.
Experience negotiating and structuring complex partner agreements and the ability to influence at the executive level.

Preferred Experience

Excellent communication and interpersonal skills, with the ability to build and maintain relationships.
Excellent written and verbal communication and stakeholder management skills
Experience building and structuring a partner program or ecosystem
Familiarity with data platforms, interoperability frameworks, or marketplace models

jobs.description:
Are you a visionary FP&A leader and designated CPA/CFA looking for a high-impact mandate as the primary strategic co-pilot to executive finance leadership?

Are you energized by the challenge of inheriting a complex, spreadsheet-heavy environment and streamlining them into agile, driver-based planning engines and rolling forecasts?

Do you thrive in large-scale, asset-intensive environments where operational throughput, unit economics, capacity utilization, and capital velocity drive performance?

Can you lead a modern planning evolution, with autonomy, harnessing platforms like Workday Adaptive Planning and Power BI while maintaining rock-solid financial governance, and serve as the vital bridge between long-term strategic models and frontline operational partners?

This is a highly visible leadership role within a premier multi-billion dollar organization. The Director, Corporate FP&A sits at the center of enterprise capital allocation and operational strategy. As the direct right hand to the Executive Director, you will step into a fluid organizational structure to build, optimize, and scale corporate planning, forecasting, and business-partnering processes.

If you are an agile builder, an optimizer, and an articulate business advisor with a track record of tangible corporate FP&A transformation, this is the opportunity you’ve been waiting for!

Why Join This Team?

- Executive Right-Hand & High Visibility: Serve as the strategic co-pilot to the Executive Director, acting as the primary liaison between long-term strategic financial modeling and embedded operational business partners, with frequent exposure to the executive leadership team.
- A True Builder’s Mandate: Inherit a fragmented spreadsheet landscape and enjoy a blank canvas to re-architect the entire planning lifecycle, streamlining 50+ models into automated, scalable planning workflows.
- Autonomous, Hands-Off Leadership: Work with a pragmatic, non-micromanaging leader who trusts the team, values open communication, and gives you complete autonomy to own, shape, and modernize the function.
- Modern Systems Evolution: Drive the evolution of the corporate planning stack, leveraging Oracle Financials, optimizing Workday Adaptive Planning, deploying Power BI executive dashboards, and testing predictive AI applications.

Exceptional Compensation & Total Rewards:

- Base salary between 160-200K
- Performance Bonus: 20% annual target
- Retirement & Pension: Up to 8% employer matching program
- Comprehensive Health & Wellness: 100% employer-sponsored health, dental, and vision coverage effective on Day One
- Industry-Leading Time Off: 4 weeks paid vacation + 5 personal days + Care Days
- Professional Growth: Full sponsorship for executive professional development, conferences, and annual CPA dues.

What You Will Do & Lead:

- Model Rationalization & FP&A Architecture: Take full ownership of the corporate planning ecosystem; audit, streamline, and consolidate over 50 legacy Excel workbooks into - standardized, driver-based planning templates and rolling forecasts.
- Strategic Business Partnering: Partner across high-volume commercial, operational, and capital divisions, translating operational drivers and volume throughput metrics into actionable financial models and strategic advice.
- Systems Modernization & Data Integrity: Maximize the value of enterprise tools—anchoring planning in Workday Adaptive Planning, reporting through Oracle, building executive Power BI dashboards, and laying the groundwork for predictive analytics.
- Capital & Operating Budget Oversight: Guide multi-year budgeting, variance analysis, sensitivity analysis, and scenario modeling across complex multi-million-dollar operational budgets and major capital investment programs.
- Team Leadership & Culture: Lead, mentor, and elevate a high-potential corporate FP&A team, instilling a culture of evidence-based analysis, intellectual curiosity, and proactive business advisory.

Who You Are:

- Designation & Education: Active CPA and/or CFA designation is mandatory; an MBA or Master’s degree in Finance/Business is considered a strong competitive asset.
- Progressive Leadership Experience: 10+ years of progressive corporate finance and FP&A experience, with at least 7+ years successfully managing, mentoring, and scaling corporate finance teams.
- Proven Track Record of FP&A Transformation: Demonstrable, evidence-based achievements taking manual, Excel-heavy environments and successfully standing up structured EPM/planning frameworks (e.g., Workday Adaptive Planning, Anaplan, Prophix, or Hyperion).
- Operational Volume & Driver Expertise: Demonstrated experience modeling complex, asset-heavy, or high-throughput operations (logistics, freight, supply chain, utilities, healthcare, public infrastructure, or large-scale multi-entity corporate environments).
- Advanced Systems & Financial Modeling Acumen: Expert-level financial modeling and Excel skills (Power Query/Pivot), paired with hands-on experience in modern BI tools (Power BI, Tableau) and enterprise ERP platforms (Oracle, SAP).
- Executive Presence & High Autonomy: A poised, articulate communicator who simplifies complex financial narratives for executive audiences, challenges assumptions with data, and thrives with complete end-to-end accountability.

jobs.title: Finance Director
jobs.description:
At Dexter, we manufacture and distribute axles, accessories, and towing components primarily serving the commercial trailer, RV, marine, agriculture, and manufactured housing markets. We’re building products and systems that are rooted in a culture of safety, collaboration, and innovation.

Headquartered in Elkhart, Indiana, Dexter has manufacturing and distribution locations throughout the U.S. and Canada. Employing state-of-the-art robotics, precision welding equipment, and automated machining processes, Dexter has achieved over 65 years of success through a commitment to the principles of superior quality, continuous improvement, and unparalleled customer service.

For more information about our company, access Dexter's web site at www.dextergroup.com.

The Finance Director
is the senior financial leader responsible for overseeing the accounting, financial planning, cost management, internal controls, and operational finance activities for the Heavy Duty Business Unit. This role partners closely with plant managers, operations leadership, supply chain, and corporate finance to improve financial performance, strengthen controls, and support effective business decisions. It also oversees day to day accounting (general ledger, cost, accounts payable, accounts receivable) in the Canadian manufacturing ERP system, leveraging support from the US accounting shared services team as necessary.

The Finance Director is responsible for ensuring the accuracy, integrity, predictability, and timely reporting of financial results across all assigned locations. Key responsibilities include revenue and related expense reporting, comparative financial analysis, and providing meaningful commentary to Plant Managers and Senior Leadership. The role also oversees budgeting, forecasting, capital expenditures, month-end close activities, and the maintenance of strong internal controls. The Finance Director provides financial leadership to plant management while promoting consistent processes, reporting standards, and controls across all supported sites.

Essential Duties And Responsibilities

Partner with the plant management and senior leadership team to drive profitability, production cost optimization and efficiencies with a continuous improvement focus.
Provide timely financial analysis, insights, and recommendations to support manufacturing, staffing, sourcing, pricing, and investment decisions; provide timely and accurate response to requests for accounting information.
Lead, coach, and develop a small accounting team supporting general ledger, cost accounting, accounts payable, accounts receivable, inventory accounting, and related financial processes.
Leverage an accounting shared service function to maximize performance of the team.
Review key account reconciliations, journal entries, financial analyses, and other work prepared by the accounting team to ensure accuracy, completeness, timeliness, and appropriate supporting documentation.
Oversee or coordinate GST/HST compliance and applicable provincial sales taxes. Coordinate with Corporate Tax and external advisors in support of Canadian corporate income-tax compliance.
Monitor changes in Canadian tax and regulatory requirements affecting the business and work with Corporate Finance, Tax, Human Resources, and outside advisors to implement required changes.
Provide financial oversight of Canadian customs and import activities and coordinate with Supply Chain, Corporate Tax/Trade Compliance, customs brokers, and other service providers to ensure accurate and timely accounting for imported goods.
Provide clear explanations of significant financial variances and recommend corrective actions.
Translate operational performance into financial results and clearly communicate key business drivers, risks, and opportunities.
Ensure financial results are accurate, complete, and reported in accordance with company policies and applicable accounting standards.
Analyze actual results compared with budget, forecast, prior year, and operational expectations; identify trends; recommend and drive actions.
Participate as a member of the plant leadership teams and provide financial guidance on operational priorities and strategic initiatives.
Monitor production costs and identify opportunities to improve margins, productivity, and cost control.
Validate financial savings associated with operational improvement projects.
Identify performance gaps and work with plant leadership to establish corrective-action plans.
Prepare annual operating plans (budget) and own monthly forecast.
Maintain, monitor and implement plant internal controls, in compliance with corporate policies, as necessary to ensure reporting integrity, safeguard assets, and identify risks.
Prepare and/or analyze Capital Expense projects with an ROI lens and track actual vs. projected performance.
Ensure compliance with inventory control policies and procedures.
Coordinate annual physical inventories, cycle-counting programs, and inventory reconciliation activities.
Partner with operations and supply chain teams to improve inventory accuracy, reduce working capital, and address unfavorable inventory trends.
Review and approve inventory reserves for excess, obsolete, slow-moving, or damaged materials.
Manage the maintenance and accuracy of standard costs in conjunction with Corporate Cost Accounting including BOMs, routers and purchase standards.
Review bills of material, routings, labor standards, and overhead assumptions for financial accuracy.
Maintain a strong and result-driven relationship with Plant Manager.
Demonstrate excellent written and verbal communication skills and an ability to present complex financial information clearly to non-financial leaders.
Maintain strong attention to detail while maintaining a broad business perspective.
Promote a culture of accountability, continuous improvement, accuracy, and operational partnership.
Attend, as required, quarterly management and other plant and finance meetings.
Coordinate with Corporate Controller on information to complete GAAP financial statements with proposed adjustments.
Support a Continuous Improvement mindset / Lean, Six Sigma activities throughout the organization.
Perform other ad hoc tasks or duties as required or assigned.

Supervisory Responsibilities

Direct report to Chief Financial Officer. Indirect (dotted line) reporting to VP, Heavy Duty Business Unit. Supervisory responsibilities must be carried out in accordance with the organization's policies and applicable laws. The Team

Group Risk Management (GRM) collaborates with businesses as a trusted advisor, facilitating well-informed decisions that support Nasdaq’s strategic objectives. GRM manages and continues to enhance the Enterprise Risk Management, Internal Control, Business Continuity, Crisis Management, and Corporate Insurance frameworks and programs. These programs facilitate the identification, assessment, monitoring, and treatment and reporting of all types of risks, Nasdaq faces.

The Position

GRM is seeking an ERM Director supporting the Anti-Financial Crime Division’s – Verafin business. The position will report to the GRM Head of Expert Functions and will be leading the Enterprise Risk Management initiatives for the Verafin business. Establish effective risk governance including board approved risk policies, risk appetite, and risk committee/forums.

Join a purpose driven winning team, committed to results, in an inclusive and high-performing culture.

Scotiabank's Global Technology Enterprise Platforms (GTEP) provides secure, resilient and efficient technology infrastructure that enable the Bank's business strategy and customer experience. The Strategic Portfolio Office (SPO) supports GTEP leadership through integrated strategy, financial management, performance transparency, portfolio governance and enterprise-wide transformation.

The Director, Financial Performance & Efficiency
is responsible for leading the financial performance management and efficiency agenda across GTEP. The role provides an integrated view of financial results, outlook, productivity and value delivery, enabling leaders to make timely, fact-based decisions and deliver against financial commitments.

The role is accountable for strengthening planning, forecasting, performance reporting and cost governance; identifying and advancing sustainable efficiency opportunities; and translating financial and operational information into clear executive insights. Lead integrated financial planning, forecasting and performance management across GTEP, aligning financial commitments with strategic priorities and delivery plans.
Establish a clear and consistent view of actuals, outlook, variances, risks and opportunities, with defined ownership and actions to close performance gaps.
Develop executive-level reporting and insights that connect financial results with operational drivers, investment choices and business outcomes.
Strengthen financial governance, management routines and decision support to improve predictability, transparency and accountability.

Efficiency & Value Optimization
Define and advance the GTEP efficiency agenda, including sustainable cost reduction, demand management, productivity improvement and reinvestment opportunities.
Identify, assess and prioritize efficiency opportunities using financial, operational and benchmark information; establish baselines, targets, benefits and delivery plans.
Track realized and forecast benefits, challenge delivery gaps and ensure efficiency commitments are supported by credible actions and evidence.
Promote disciplined cost management and value-based decision making across the organization without compromising resilience, risk management or service outcomes.

Support leadership forums, planning cycles and portfolio reviews with decision-ready analysis and clear accountability for follow-through.

Leadership & Stakeholder Management

Influence senior stakeholders to align financial choices, operational priorities and efficiency actions with GTEP and Bank objectives.
Foster a culture of ownership, constructive challenge, collaboration, continuous improvement and measurable value delivery.
Lead, coach and develop a high-performing team with strong capabilities in financial management, analytics, business advisory and executive communication.

Strong financial acumen with the ability to connect financial results to operational drivers, strategic choices and measurable business outcomes.
Advanced analytical and problem-solving skills, with experience translating complex data into clear executive insights and recommendations.
Experience establishing performance measures, financial governance, benefit tracking and management routines that improve accountability and execution.

DIRECTEUR DES FINANCES (CFO)

Life in Green est à la recherche d'une personne qui apporte passion, valeurs, objectifs, intérêts et une forte volonté de réussir dans son environnement de travail.

Cette personne possède un esprit entrepreneurial et aspire à réaliser de grandes choses au sein d'une équipe dynamique. Elle accorde une grande importance à la satisfaction client, est méticuleuse dans son travail et apprécie l'accomplissement de ses tâches. De plus, la capacité à travailler sous pression et de manière autonome, ainsi que de solides compétences en écoute, sont très appréciées par l'entreprise.

Nous offrons un environnement actif, rapide et flexible. L'équipe de Life in Green est petite mais puissante, collaborant avec enthousiasme et trouvant de manière créative des solutions pour faire croître l'entreprise chaque jour, ensemble. Les objectifs sont élevés et l’entreprise a besoin d’un capitaine de navire afin de diriger stratégiquement ce dernier vers l’atteinte de ces objectifs. Chaque membre de l'équipe est essentiel et se soutient mutuellement, appréciant la présence au bureau et le temps passé avec les collègues. Le travail d'équipe est une valeur fondamentale de notre entreprise.

À PROPOS DE NOUS

Fondée en 2009, Life in Green est un fabricant et distributeur de premier plan de produits jetables écologiques. Nous avons connu une expansion rapide depuis nos débuts, avec des employés à Montréal, en Argentine, en Inde et en Chine. Nos produits écoresponsables font sensation à l'échelle mondiale, et nous sommes déterminés à continuer de conquérir de nouveaux marchés. Pour atteindre nos objectifs, nous cherchons activement à agrandir notre équipe à long terme.

Notre mission est d'offrir des produits et des solutions innovants de classe mondiale qui ont un impact positif sur nos clients et leur environnement. La centricité client, l'intégrité, la qualité, l'innovation, la croissance et la durabilité sont des valeurs fondamentales chez Life in Green.

DESCRIPTION DU POSTE

Sous la responsabilité du Président, ce poste consiste à planifier les stratégies financières, réviser les rapports financiers et effectuer la recherche de financement. En tant que CFO, vous devez avoir un souci du détail et d’excellentes aptitudes d’analyse et d’organisation. Vous devez être un communicateur hors-pair et avoir un état d’esprit, une attitude, flexible et réactive.

Vous serez également responsable
de :

Gérer les fusions et acquisitions, ainsi que la gestion des capitaux et l'analyse des risques financiers.
Superviser la budgétisation, les prévisions financières, les ajustements de prix, et la clôture de fin d'année.
Assurer la conformité, la durabilité, et le reporting financier, y compris les indicateurs de performance (KPIs) et les subventions.
Gérer les flux de trésorerie, les comptes payables et recevables, les vérifications de crédit, les assurances, et les relations avec les principaux fournisseurs.
Améliorer les processus opérationnels et la qualité, en supervisant l'automatisation, les systèmes ERP, la production, l'immobilier, et le support opérationnel.
Élaborer et mettre en œuvre des stratégies pour l'expansion du marché, la réduction des coûts, et les négociations de contrats, en gérant également les projets et les droits d'auteur et marques commerciales.

Exigences du poste 
:

Baccalauréat dans un domaine connexe
Ordre des comptables professionnels agréés du Québec (CPA)

· Un minimum de 2 à 5 ans d’expérience dans un poste similaire
· Une expérience en gestion d’équipe représente définitivement un atout
· Expérience avec un système intégré de gestion (ERP), Microsoft Dynamics un atout
· Capacité à collecter, suivre et analyser des données
· Être un leader possédant un bon sens de l’organisation et des responsabilités pour établir les priorités et respecter les échéanciers
· Excellentes compétences en communication – orales et écrites (français et anglais)

 Joignez-vous à Life in Green pour faire partie d'une équipe passionnée par l'innovation, la durabilité et l'impact positif. Postulez dès maintenant et contribuez à notre mission de croissance mondiale tout en faisant une différence significative dans le monde.

 ***************************************************
  CHIEF FINANCING OFFICER (CFO)

Life in Green is looking for an individual who brings passion, values, goals, interests, and a strong desire to succeed within their work environment.

This person possesses an entrepreneurial spirit and strives to achieve great things within a dynamic team. They take great pride in client satisfaction, are meticulous in their work, and appreciate a job well done. Additionally, the ability to work under pressure and autonomously, along with strong listening skills, are highly valued by the company.

We offer an active, fast-paced, and flexible environment. Life in Green's team is small yet powerful, eagerly collaborating and creatively finding solutions to grow the company each day, together. Efforts and determination are recognized and rewarded appropriately. Each team member is crucial and supports one another, enjoying office presence and time spent among colleagues. We have been rapidly expanding since our inception, with employees in Montreal, Argentina, India, and China. Our mission is to offer innovative world-class products and solutions that have a positive impact on our customers and their environment. Customer centricity, integrity, quality, innovation, growth, and sustainability are fundamental values at Life in Green.
Headquartered in Montreal, we market our products in North America and internationally, with national distribution across Canada and the USA.

Reporting to the President, this position involves planning financial strategies, reviewing financial reports and seeking financing. jobs.title: Responsable de l'architecture logicielle | Head of Software Architecture
jobs.description:
À PROPOS DE POWER FACTORS

Power Factors est un fournisseur de logiciels et de solutions qui ouvre la voie à la prochaine génération d'énergie propre grâce à Unity, l'une des suites de gestion d'énergie renouvelable (REMS) les plus complètes et les plus largement déployées sur le marché. Avec plus de 300 GW d'actifs éoliens, solaires et de stockage d'énergie gérés dans le monde entier auprès de plus de 600 clients et 18 000 sites, Power Factors gère 25 % des données mondiales sur les énergies renouvelables.*

La suite Unity REMS de Power Factors soutient l'ensemble de la chaîne de valeur énergétique, de la surveillance et du contrôle à l'analyse des marchés. L'ensemble d'applications ouvertes et axées sur les données de l'entreprise permet aux parties prenantes du secteur des énergies renouvelables de collaborer, d'automatiser les flux de travail critiques et de prendre des décisions plus éclairées afin de maximiser les rendements des actifs. Les parties prenantes bénéficient d'un soutien de bout en bout, incluant des solutions pour le SCADA et le PPC, la surveillance centralisée, la gestion de la performance, la gestion commerciale des actifs et la gestion des services sur le terrain.

Grâce à une expertise approfondie du domaine, des perspectives propulsées par l'IA sont livrées à grande échelle, permettant aux entreprises d'optimiser leurs actifs, de stimuler leur croissance et de prendre des décisions plus éclairées dans un contexte de transition rapide vers l'énergie propre. Power Factors lutte contre les changements climatiques grâce au code.

Hors Chine et Inde

À PROPOS DU POSTE

Power Factors prend de l'ampleur en termes de complexité — davantage de produits, de plateformes, d'acheteurs sophistiqués, et des attentes croissantes quant aux capacités natives en IA dans notre suite de logiciels pour les énergies renouvelables. Dans ce contexte, l'absence d'une vision technique unique et imputable crée un risque réel : des schémas architecturaux divergents selon les secteurs verticaux, des approches incohérentes en matière d'investissement dans les plateformes d'IA et de données, et une dette technique qui s'accumule plus vite qu'elle ne peut être résorbée.

Le rôle de Responsable de l'architecture logicielle existe pour combler cet écart. Il s'agit d'un poste de leadership technique pratique et hautement spécialisé, chargé de définir et d'appliquer les normes d'architecture d'entreprise à l'échelle de l'organisation Produits et Technologie de Power Factors — couvrant les secteurs Plateforme, SCADA, EMS, APM, CloudOps et CAM/FSM/Ops produit — tout en concevant et en prototypant personnellement les problèmes les plus complexes auxquels l'organisation est confrontée, notamment en matière d'introduction de produits basés sur l'IA, d'acquisition de données IoT et d'évolutivité SaaS multitenant.

Ce poste combine la portée stratégique d'un·e architecte d'entreprise et la crédibilité d'un·e bâtisseur·se qui continue d'écrire du code, de réviser des demandes de tirage (pull requests) et d'être à l'aise en tant que personne la plus technique dans la salle.

Relevant directement du ou de la Chef·fe des produits et de la technologie (CPTO), la personne titulaire agit comme tissu connectif entre la stratégie organisationnelle du ou de la CPTO et les décisions techniques quotidiennes prises par les équipes d'ingénierie verticales, en collaborant étroitement avec les responsables des secteurs (Plateforme, SCADA, EMS, APM, CloudOps, CAM/FSM/Ops produit), la gestion de produit et les équipes CloudOps et Sécurité.

Il est important de noter que ce rôle n'est pas un poste purement stratégique ou consultatif éloigné du code, ni un rôle de gestion axé sur les processus et les rapports. La personne titulaire est appelée à demeurer une contributrice technique crédible et active tout au long de son mandat. Ce poste ne comprend pas non plus la responsabilité de la priorisation de la feuille de route produit ou de la stratégie commerciale — ces responsabilités demeurent avec la gestion de produit et le ou la CPTO — mais il façonne directement ce qui est techniquement possible et à quelle vitesse cela peut être livré.

CE QUE VOUS FEREZ

Architecture d'entreprise et conception de systèmes complexes

Définir et maintenir les normes d'architecture d'entreprise, les architectures de référence et les garde-fous techniques de Power Factors pour l'ensemble des secteurs verticaux
Diriger les revues architecturales pour les initiatives majeures, en assurant la cohérence, l'évolutivité et la maintenabilité à long terme
Être responsable de la feuille de route technique pour les capacités de plateforme transversales (plateforme de données, couche d'intégration, identité, observabilité)
Concevoir des systèmes complexes à haute disponibilité où l'exactitude, la latence et l'intégrité des données ont des conséquences opérationnelles et commerciales réelles
Collaborer avec les responsables des secteurs verticaux (SCADA, EMS, APM, Plateforme, CloudOps) pour s'assurer que les décisions architecturales locales s'alignent sur la direction d'entreprise

Leadership technique des équipes

Bâtir et diriger une fonction d'architecture distribuée opérant comme une autorité technique de confiance en Grèce, à Montréal et dans d'autres régions
Encadrer les ingénieur·e·s senior et les responsables en ingénierie en matière de jugement architectural, de conception de systèmes et d'analyse des compromis techniques
Établir et animer des forums de gouvernance architecturale (revues de conception, processus RFC, comités de pilotage technique)
Agir comme point d'escalade technique pour les décisions de conception les plus critiques de l'organisation

Architecture et livraison de produits basés sur l'IA

Concevoir et contribuer personnellement à la construction de capacités de produits basées sur l'IA de bout en bout — de l'acquisition de données et de la sélection de modèles jusqu'au déploiement et à la surveillance
Définir l'approche architecturale de Power Factors pour les produits basés sur les LLM, incluant l'utilisation du Model Context Protocol (MCP), les architectures de récupération et les flux de travail agentiques
Évaluer et sélectionner les LLM de développement et les plateformes d'IA adaptés à l'intégration dans des produits commerciaux
Assurer le pont technique entre REMI et les autres initiatives natives en IA et l'architecture de plateforme globale
Mettre à profit l'expertise en apprentissage automatique et en science des données pour orienter les décisions produit — sélection de modèles, ingénierie des caractéristiques, conception de pipelines de données et pratiques MLOps

Développement pratique

Écrire du code de production, prototyper de nouveaux schémas architecturaux et contribuer directement aux problèmes techniques les plus complexes de l'organisation
Montrer l'exemple en matière de qualité du code, de discipline de test et d'excellence en ingénierie
Rester suffisamment proche du code pour formuler des jugements architecturaux crédibles et actuels, plutôt que de se fier à des rapports de seconde main
Réaliser des implémentations de validation de concept pour réduire les risques liés aux grands paris architecturaux avant l'engagement complet des équipes

Architecture IoT, périphérie et systèmes industriels

Concevoir des systèmes d'acquisition de données IoT évolutifs capables d'ingérer, de normaliser et de traiter des volumes élevés de télémétrie provenant d'actifs d'énergie renouvelable distribués
Définir l'architecture pour les dispositifs de périphérie et les contrôleurs de centrale (PPC), en équilibrant le calcul sur site, les contraintes de latence et la connectivité infonuagique
S'assurer que les approches architecturales tiennent compte de la conformité aux codes du réseau, des exigences de contrôle en temps réel et des réalités opérationnelles des environnements SCADA et EMS
Appliquer la connaissance du domaine des énergies renouvelables et de l'énergie pour orienter les décisions de modélisation des données, d'intégration et de conception des systèmes de contrôle

Architecture infonuagique, SaaS et multitenant

Être responsable de la stratégie d'architecture infonuagique sur GCP et/ou AWS, incluant les postures de coût, de résilience et de sécurité
Faire progresser l'architecture SaaS multitenant de Power Factors pour prendre en charge l'échelle, l'isolation des locataires et la configurabilité sans fragmenter le code
Définir les normes architecturales pour le développement d'applications mobiles là où les produits s'étendent aux cas d'utilisation sur le terrain et en opérations
Évaluer les décisions de construction ou d'achat et de consolidation de plateformes à travers la pile technologique

Productivité de l'ingénierie et développement assisté par l'IA

Identifier, évaluer et déployer des outils de développement IA qui permettent une amélioration de la productivité de 3 à 4 fois au sein des équipes d'ingénierie
Définir les meilleures pratiques pour la programmation, les tests et la revue de code assistés par l'IA, en équilibrant vitesse, qualité et sécurité
Collaborer avec la direction de l'ingénierie pour mesurer et communiquer les gains de productivité issus de l'adoption des outils d'IA

Indicateurs de succès

Nombre de capacités de produits basées sur l'IA conçues et mises en production par année
Gains de productivité mesurés (vélocité, délai de cycle) attribuables au déploiement des outils de développement IA
Réduction des incohérences architecturales entre secteurs verticaux et des investissements de plateforme dupliqués
Métriques de fiabilité et de performance des systèmes critiques d'entreprise et transactionnels
Taux d'adoption des normes architecturales et des conceptions de référence à travers les équipes d'ingénierie
Rétroaction qualitative à 360° des responsables en ingénierie sur l'efficacité du leadership technique

CE QUE VOUS DEVEZ APPORTER

15 à 20 ans d'expérience progressive en génie logiciel, avec une part importante consacrée à l'architecture et aux rôles de leadership technique
Expérience démontrée dans la conception de systèmes à grande échelle et haute complexité avec des enjeux opérationnels importants
Capacité avérée à diriger et à encadrer des ingénieur·e·s et des architectes senior au sein d'équipes distribuées
Expérience dans la conception de systèmes transactionnels ou de trading à haut débit et haute intégrité où l'exactitude et la performance sont non négociables
Bilan avéré dans la conception et la mise en production de produits basés sur l'IA de bout en bout, du concept au lancement en production
Approche pratique du développement : un·e architecte qui code encore et qui prend un réel plaisir à construire, et pas seulement à concevoir
Expérience avec des systèmes qui ingèrent et traitent de grands volumes de télémétrie provenant d'actifs physiques distribués
Familiarité avec les architectures informatiques de périphérie et les systèmes de contrôle industriels, incluant les dispositifs de périphérie et les contrôleurs de centrale (PPC)
Expérience directe dans les logiciels pour les énergies renouvelables ou le secteur énergétique au sens large (fortement souhaitée)
Solides connaissances pratiques en apprentissage automatique et en science des données, suffisantes pour prendre des décisions architecturales et de plateforme éclairées
Expérience pratique avec le Model Context Protocol (MCP), les LLM de développement et la création de fonctionnalités produit basées sur les LLM
Expérience approfondie avec GCP et/ou AWS à un niveau architectural
Expérience dans la sélection et le déploiement d'outils de développement IA qui augmentent de façon significative la productivité des équipes d'ingénierie
Expérience avancée dans la conception et l'évolution d'applications SaaS multitenantes
Connaissance pratique de l'architecture et de la livraison d'applications mobiles, suffisante pour guider les équipes qui développent des expériences mobiles

jobs.description:
**Application deadline:** November 26, 2026 at 12:00 PM EST

**Join the EDC Team!**


At EDC, we support Canadian businesses to succeed globally. We provide the financial tools and expertise they need to explore new markets, reduce risks, all towards the goal of making Canada and the world better through trade.


**Position:** Director, Structured and Project Finance \- Digital Industries and Advanced Manufacturing

**Employment Type:** Permanent

**Compensation Details:** Director, Underwriter 22: Salaries typically range from $178,118 to $237,490 annually, based on qualifications and experiences, plus a performance\-based incentive.


**Location:**

* Export Development Canada operates under a hybrid work model. As of September 2026, our in\-office requirement has increased to three days per week and will be implemented gradually through a phased approach based on employee location. (subject to change).
* This role is expected to be based at EDC’s Headquarters in Ottawa. Candidates located near EDC’s Toronto or Montreal offices will also be considered.
* Relocation assistance to Ottawa will be made available for candidates who meet the eligibility criteria.

*Internal Employees, please consult the ServiceNow article entitled Internal movements – what you need to know.*

**About EDC:**


At Export Development Canada (EDC), we empower Canadian businesses to succeed globally. As a financial Crown corporation, we offer innovative financial solutions and expert insights to help businesses explore new markets, mitigate risks, and achieve growth.

**Why Join EDC?**

* Comprehensive Benefits: EDC offers a competitive compensation \& benefits package, work\-life balance, \& the opportunity to help make Canada and the world better through trade.
* Work\-Life Balance: EDC offers a competitive compensation package \& work\-life balance. We have hybrid work options, 4 weeks paid vacation, a corporate closure period, summer early Friday’s \& no meeting Fridays.
* Professional Development: Take advantage of our continuous learning opportunities, including training programs, workshops and language training.
* Inclusive Culture: Be part of a diverse and inclusive workplace that champions employment equity \& values diversity of ideas, strengths, \& backgrounds to succeed.
* Wellness Programs: Access to wellness initiatives, mental health support, and fitness programs to keep you healthy and happy.
* Community Engagement: Participate in volunteer opportunities and give back to the community through our various social responsibility programs.

**Team\& Job Overview**  

  

EDC's Structured and Project Finance Group is one of Canada’s largest internationally focused project finance teams and is a significant player in the global M\&A, project, and infrastructure space. Since its establishment in 1995, the Group has closed over 700 transactions globally, accounting for financings in excess of US$60 billion. Over the years, EDC’s Structured and Project Finance team has built a significant portfolio across different industries, like mining and metals, infrastructure, telecommunications, energy, renewables, and clean technology.


Structured and Project Finance is a specialized field of finance, in which financing decisions are based upon project\-specific cash flow and assets. Generally speaking, these transactions tend to be large and complex. Counterparties to EDC's Structured and Project Finance transactions include top\-tier Canadian and international sponsors, exporters, law firms and international Project Finance and investment banks.
  

  

The Director of Structured and Project Finance is responsible for the **Digital Industries and Advanced Manufacturing sector** and people leadership of a team of 5\-9 professionals, overall strategic direction and operations of the In\-focused teams. The subsectors covered under Infrastructure includes Digital (Telecom, Data Centers, Space etc) and Advanced Manufacturing across different sub\-sectors including Defense and Security . The ideal candidate has proven leadership skills, agility, strong work ethic, and is results oriented.  

  

**What you will be doing:**

* Provide leadership to a Team of product specialists.
* Role model key EDC leadership principles, focused on developing a culture of performance, empowerment, achievement and team spirit;
* Set the strategic direction and key priorities in respect of where Structured and Project financings can have the greatest impacts for Canada, including a focused plan around target subsectors, buyers, customers and markets and how to deploy structured financings optimally
* In collaboration with our Business Development Groups, set a proactive business development and corporate representation plan to support execution of strategic goals and promote the knowledge, network and professionalism of EDC Structured and Project Finance with relevant stakeholders
* Utilize leadership skills and business knowledge to provide effective oversight on complex, high risk financing transactions, ensuring that the structures are appropriate and commercially sound, presentations and submissions are professional and of the highest standard, and authorizations are fully complied with according to EDC’s risk management framework
* Champion initiatives which foster continuous improvements in the delivery of our financing solutions, as well as furthers other relevant EDC priorities and strategies.
* Responsible for building a high\-performance environment and implementing a people strategy that attracts, retains and develops their team by fostering an inclusive work environment.
* Direct the performance management and skill/career development of assigned staff to ensure adequate capacity and capability to meets organizational needs.

**What we are looking for:**

* MBA or equivalent graduate degree in business, finance, economics, or a related discipline
* Minimum of 8\-10 years of experience working with project finance or similar

jobs.title: Director, Digital Marketing & Web Experience
jobs.description:
At Varicent, We’re Not Just Transforming The Sales Performance Management (SPM) Market—we’re Redefining How Organizations Achieve Revenue Success. Our Cutting-edge SaaS Solutions Empower Revenue Leaders Globally To Design Smarter Go-to-market Strategies, Maximize Seller Performance, And Unlock Untapped Potential. Varicent Stands At The Forefront Of Innovation, Celebrated As a Market Leader In The 2025 Forrester Wave Report For SPM, 2023 Ventana Research Revenue Performance Management (RPM) Value Index, Gartner Peer Insights, 2024 Gartner SPM Market Guide, And G2. Our Solutions Are Trusted By a Diverse Range Of Global Industry Leaders Like T-Mobile, ServiceNow, Wawanesa Bank, Shaw Industries, Moody's, Stryker And Hundreds More. Here’s Why You’ll Thrive At Varicent

Innovate with Purpose: Build impactful solutions for customers worldwide.
Join Excellence: Work in a diverse, collaborative, and innovative team.
Shape the Future: Lead in redefining revenue optimization.
Grow Together: Unlock your potential in a supportive environment.

Join us at Varicent—where your talent and ambition meet limitless opportunities for success!

The Opportunity

We’re looking for a Director, Digital Marketing & Web Experience
to lead how Varicent attracts, engages, and converts buyers across our digital ecosystem.

This is a high-impact leadership role for someone who loves connecting strategy with execution. You’ll own our digital growth strategy across paid media, web experience, SEO/AEO/GEO, conversion optimization, and performance measurement
, with a clear focus on generating pipeline and supporting revenue growth.

You’ll have the opportunity to shape the function — leading a Senior Manager of Digital Marketing and Senior Web Developer
, partnering with specialized agencies, and working closely with senior leaders across Marketing, Sales, Revenue Operations, Product Marketing, Content, Creative, and Finance.

We’re looking for someone who is comfortable setting the vision while staying close enough to the work to know what’s performing, what isn’t, and where we should move next.

What You’ll Do

Own Our Digital Growth Strategy

Set the strategy and roadmap across paid media, website experience, SEO/AEO/GEO, conversion optimization, and digital acquisition.
Connect digital investments directly to business goals, including pipeline, revenue, customer acquisition, and brand growth.
Identify new opportunities across buyer behavior, emerging channels, AI-powered search, personalization, and digital experiences.
Bring together teams, agencies, technology, and data around clear priorities and measurable outcomes.

Turn Our Website Into a Growth Engine

Own the strategy for Varicent.com as a key demand generation, storytelling, and conversion platform.
Partner closely with our Senior Web Developer to evolve the website experience, UX, navigation, performance, accessibility, and conversion paths.
Use analytics, behavioral insights, A/B testing, and experimentation to continuously improve the buyer journey.
Lead major web initiatives such as redesigns, personalization, CMS improvements, and other digital experience programs.

Drive Digital Acquisition & Discoverability

Lead our paid media strategy across search, social, retargeting, ABM, programmatic, and other digital channels.
Own channel mix, budget allocation, forecasting, and optimization based on performance.
Shape Varicent’s approach to SEO, AEO, and GEO, helping buyers discover us across both traditional and AI-powered search experiences.
Partner with Demand Generation, Product Marketing, and Content to translate campaigns into effective digital experiences.

Make Data Actionable

Define how we measure digital performance across traffic, engagement, conversion, opportunities, pipeline, and ROI.
Partner with Marketing Operations and Revenue Operations to strengthen tracking, attribution, lead flow, and reporting.
Turn performance data into clear recommendations on where to optimize, experiment, and invest.
Build a culture of testing and continuous improvement across channels, audiences, creative, and web experiences.

Lead & Build

Lead and develop a Senior Manager of Digital Marketing and Senior Web Developer, alongside our paid media and SEO/AEO/GEO agency partners.
Create clear priorities and operating rhythms that allow the team to move quickly without sacrificing quality.
Own digital marketing and web budgets, agency relationships, tools, and investments.
Serve as a trusted digital strategy partner to the SVP of Marketing and broader Marketing leadership team.
Help shape how the digital and web function evolves as Varicent grows.

What You’ll Bring

We’re looking for a digital leader who has operated in a B2B SaaS, technology, enterprise software, or similarly complex sales environment
and understands how digital experiences translate into business growth.

You’ll Likely Bring

12+ years of experience across digital marketing, growth, demand generation, performance marketing, or web strategy.
7+ years of people leadership experience, including leading multidisciplinary teams or managers.
Experience owning digital strategy with measurable responsibility for pipeline, revenue, conversion, and customer acquisition.
Deep knowledge of paid media, SEO/SEM, digital acquisition, web strategy, CRO, analytics, and experimentation.
Experience owning or significantly influencing a B2B website and understanding how UX, content, technology, and conversion work together.
Experience managing meaningful digital budgets and making investment decisions based on performance.
Strong analytical instincts and the ability to turn complex data into clear recommendations.
Experience leading agencies and external partners while maintaining strong internal ownership.
The ability to influence senior stakeholders, navigate competing priorities, and connect digital strategy to broader company goals.
Comfort working in a growth-oriented environment where priorities evolve and leaders are expected to both set direction and help move the work forward.
Familiarity with tools such as HubSpot, Google Ads, GA4, Google Tag Manager, Salesforce, LinkedIn Campaign Manager, ABM platforms, experimentation tools, and modern analytics platforms.
An understanding of how AI is changing digital marketing, content discovery, personalization, and the buyer journey.

Nice to Have

Experience with HubSpot CMS, ABM and intent platforms, multi-touch attribution, website personalization, CRO platforms, behavioral analytics, major website redesigns or migrations, and global digital programs
is a plus.

Working knowledge of HTML/CSS and familiarity with accessibility, privacy, Core Web Vitals, and web governance will also help you partner effectively with our web team.

What Success Looks Like

In your first few months, you’ll get to know our digital ecosystem, team, agencies, performance, and buyers; identify where we can improve quickly; and establish clear priorities for digital growth.

From there, you’ll build a multi-quarter roadmap, strengthen how we measure digital contribution to pipeline and revenue, establish a structured experimentation approach, and evolve Varicent’s website into an even stronger growth and conversion engine.

Over time, success will mean better digital experiences, stronger organic visibility, smarter media investment, higher conversion, clearer performance insights, and measurable growth in digital-sourced pipeline
— supported by a team and operating model that can scale with Varicent.

Additional Information

For this role, the estimated annual base salary range is between $138,200.00 - $181,400.00 CAD
. In addition to base salary, our compensation package may include bonuses, commissions for eligible sales roles, and a comprehensive benefits package. The actual base salary will vary based on factors including individual qualifications and market data, as objectively assessed during the interview process.

This posting is for a new vacancy
.

This hiring process utilizes artificial intelligence tools to assist in candidate screening and assessment. Our AI tools are designed to complement — not replace — human decision-making.

Overview Of Benefits

Health & Wellness — Comprehensive medical, dental, and vision coverage tailored to your local needs
Time Off — PTO and public holidays to rest, recharge, and do what matters most
Volunteer Days — Dedicated time to give back and support the communities that matter to you
Ignite Days — Dedicated learning days to support continuous growth, skill development, and professional learning
Financial — Compensation that reflects your market and your value
Retirement — Retirement plans designed to help you build long-term financial security
Tuition Assistance — Invest in your growth with support for continuing education and professional development
Flexibility — Work where you thrive, with remote and hybrid options available across most regions

All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, gender, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, national origin, genetics, disability, age, or veteran status. If you require accommodation at any time during the recruitment process please email accomodations@varicent.com

Varicent is also committed to compliance with all fair employment practices regarding citizenship and immigration status. Location:
Toronto, Canada

up to $250,000, dependent on experience
Employment:
Permanent | Full-time
Industry:
Legal & Professional Services

Ingenio is supporting a leading international law firm with the appointment of a Global Head of Digital Strategy & Transformation
.

This is a senior leadership position reporting directly to the Global Chief Operating Officer, with significant exposure to the Board and wider executive leadership team. The successful candidate will lead the firm's digital transformation strategy, bringing together business applications, data, AI, automation and digital client services to deliver measurable business improvements.

This is not a traditional IT infrastructure or operational technology role. An established CTO is responsible for those areas. The focus of this appointment is on strategy, development, transformation and execution
.

The Opportunity
You will take responsibility for developing and delivering a global digital transformation strategy across legal, corporate and trust services. Working with senior business stakeholders, you will turn commercial and operational challenges into practical technology solutions that improve efficiency, client experience and service delivery.

You'll inherit an established application development team and will be responsible for developing its capabilities as the transformation programme progresses.

Significant projects are already underway, including a major entity-management platform initiative, a broader data management and analytics programme, and opportunities to extend the use of AI and automation across the business.

Key Responsibilities
Develop and deliver a global digital strategy and transformation roadmap aligned with business priorities.
Lead and develop the existing Business Technology and Application Development team.
Own the business applications roadmap, including entity management and client-facing technology solutions.
Oversee the design, development and delivery of new systems, whether built internally, purchased or delivered through external partners.
Drive the data strategy, analytics, reporting and business intelligence agenda.
Identify and implement practical AI and automation opportunities across legal and professional services.

What We're Looking For
We are particularly interested in senior digital transformation and business technology leaders from professional services, legal, fiduciary/corporate services, financial services or similarly complex, regulated environments
