jobs.description:
Position: Head of Enterprise Architecture & Applications

Location: Vaudreuil-Dorion, QC

Flexible Hybrid Work Model: We support collaboration and connection through a hybrid work arrangement requiring a minimum of 3 days per week on-site.

Status: Permanent, full-time (1)

Lead the architecture behind a growing North American business
.

Quadra’s CRM, ERP, transportation, analytics, employee experience, regulatory compliance and AI platforms are core to how we operate across North America.

We are creating the Head of Enterprise Architecture & Applications role to unify these platforms under one architecture and delivery standard. The role leads Quadra Digital’s (QD) Design Authority
pillar alongside Business Authority and Digital Workplace & Infrastructure.

Reporting to our CDIO, this visible, hands-on leader will guide the team, own the budget and investment portfolio, review designs and delivery practices, and partner with business leaders to turn priorities into measurable value.

At Quadra, we put people first so that together, we can reimagine what's possible.

For more than 50 years, Quadra has placed its 650+ employees at the heart of its success across North America. We offer an engaging culture, a collaborative and human environment, and a high level of autonomy and flexibility. Joining Quadra means being part of a professional, innovative and passionate team, within a growing, people-focused organization certified Great Place to Work®. We have also been recognized as one of Canada's Best Managed Companies for over 20 years.

A leader in the distribution of chemicals and ingredients, Quadra continues to grow with a strong commitment to its teams. If you are driven by excellence, you belong here!

Why This Role Matters

Own enterprise architecture, business capability and process architecture, enterprise information architecture and master data governance, and AI-solution architecture and governance across CRM, ERP, transportation, analytics, employee experience and AI, as well as Quadra-critical regulatory platforms (Intelligent SDS Authoring, labelling, product stewardship and compliance).
Lead the platform managers, product owners, delivery squads, project management and QA under one intake and delivery model.
Enforce design, security, testing and release standards to make delivery predictable.
Own the digital budget and investment portfolio with Finance, the CDIO and business leaders.
Measure digital outcomes through revenue, margin, cost, service, working capital and productivity.

What would be your main responsibilities as Head of Enterprise Architecture & Applications?:

Define and govern target architecture across applications, integrations, data, security and AI; approve major designs, configurations, developments and releases.
Directly manage the platform managers, product owners, project management, QA, development and functional specialists—setting priorities, capacity, performance and development expectations.
Own delivery from qualified demand through release and Level 3 support, including application security, published SLAs and clear technical ownership.
Set and enforce delivery standards for requirements, backlogs, acceptance criteria, UAT, Jira, testing and Definition of Done.
Bring the roadmap and enhancement portfolio to the quarterly QD Prioritisation Board and provide technical validation for production changes.
Map business capabilities, processes and applications to align investments, reduce duplication and challenge proposed solutions early.
Evaluate AI and regulatory platforms (e.g., SDS authoring, labelling, product stewardship) against security, compliance, integration, data and business-value requirements.
Own digital opex and capex planning, business-case quality, stage gates and value realization with Finance, Business Authority and the relevant Key Account.
Advise business leaders on roadmap, feasibility, cost and sequencing; lead vendor selection and performance management.
Assess and integrate application landscapes acquired through mergers and acquisitions.

What are the required qualifications and experience to succeed in this role:

15+ years in enterprise/solution architecture, application management or digital delivery, including 5+ years leading specialists or Product Owners.
Bachelor’s degree in information systems, computer science, software or industrial engineering, or equivalent experience.
Proven design-authority experience across multiple platforms, including solution, integration and release approvals.
Hands-on experience with at least two of: Salesforce, Oracle JD Edwards E1 or similar ERP, Oracle OTM/TMS
Strong integration and API architecture experience across ERP, CRM and TMS in cloud or hybrid environments.
Strong business acumen and ability to translate commercial, operational and financial priorities into practical technology decisions.
Strong oral presentation skills: clear, confident communication of complex ideas, analysis outcomes, architectural concepts and design decisions—and their justification—tailored to diverse audiences and stakeholder needs.
Experience governing requirements, backlogs, Jira or Azure DevOps, SDLC controls, change management, segregation of duties and audit/compliance reviews.
Demonstrated creative thinking and ability to challenge stakeholders, defend decisions, bring stakeholders to understand and accept new approaches and deliver measurable business benefits.
Proven experience owning and managing significant technology operating and capital budgets and investment portfolios, in partnership with Finance and business leaders, with accountability for forecasting, prioritization, cost control and value realization.
Advanced written and verbal communication skills in both French and English.
Assets: MuleSoft or similar API integration platform experience; TOGAF, Zachman, AWS/Azure, Microsoft Power Platform, Power BI/Fabric, Agile/SAFe or Scrum certification; distribution, chemicals, supply chain, regulatory/product stewardship or post-acquisition integration experience.

Working Conditions

Permanent, full-time senior leadership role based in Vaudreuil-Dorion, with three full office days per week.
Travel up to 15% across Canada and the United States.
Occasional off-hours involvement for major releases, incidents or critical business events.

You Might Be the Right Person If…

You are a pragmatic, hands-on leader who can review architecture, lead a team and own a budget. You set standards appropriate for a 650-person company, enforce them without becoming a bottleneck, challenge unclear value and hold delivery accountable for measurable results.

We want to meet you!

Here Are Some Of The Perks Of Choosing Quadra

jobs.title: Chief Financial Officer
jobs.description:
Build more than a career – help shape what comes next

The Argus Group of Companies is seeking a Chief Financial Officer (CFO) to join its senior leadership team. This is a key leadership role for an accomplished finance executive who can bring together financial strategy, capital planning, development and investment analysis, and strong financial governance to a dynamic group. Working closely with ownership and the executive team, the CFO will help guide strategic decision-making, strengthen financial performance, and position the organization for continued growth across its portfolio.

More than a real estate company, Argus is a diversified, entrepreneurial group that has been helping shape the Okanagan for more than 50 years. Headquartered in Kelowna, British Columbia, Argus has built an impressive portfolio spanning commercial, residential, industrial and hospitality properties, supported by in-house expertise across hospitality management, development, construction, leasing and property management

What makes Argus particularly compelling is its long-term approach to ownership. Rather than simply developing properties and moving on, the organization invests, develops, operates and manages assets with a view to creating enduring value. That means its leaders have the opportunity to be involved across the full property lifecycle and to see the tangible, lasting impact of the decisions they make.

This is a place where good ideas can move quickly, leaders are close to the decisions that matter, and your work can leave a visible legacy. As Argus looks toward its next phase of growth, it offers something increasingly rare: the chance to join a successful organization and still have a genuine hand in shaping its future

Key Responsibilities

Shape organizational and growth strategy – Serve as a trusted leader and advisor to ownership, bringing financial insight, commercial judgement and constructive challenge to major business and investment decisions
Lead capital and financing strategy – Drive long-term capital planning, financing and refinancing, liquidity management and lender relationships, supported by robust forecasting and scenario modelling to provide clear visibility into cash flow, leverage and capital requirements and optimize the capital structure to support sustainable growth.
Evaluate investments and growth opportunities – Lead the financial assessment of developments, acquisitions and major capital investments, evaluating returns, cash flow, funding requirements, risk and long-term value creation.
Optimize capital deployment – Advise ownership on where and how to deploy capital across new developments, acquisitions, existing assets, property improvements and debt reduction.
Strengthen portfolio performance – Assess asset and business-line performance and work with development and operational leaders to enhance returns, cash generation and long-term portfolio value.
Manage financial and enterprise risk – Maintain a forward-looking view of liquidity, leverage, debt maturities, interest-rate exposure, project risk and market conditions, ensuring appropriate financial governance and controls.
Build trusted financial relationships – Develop strong relationships with banks, lenders, investors and external financial partners, expanding access to capital and supporting future opportunities.
Turn strategy into action – Translate complex financial information into clear, commercially grounded recommendations, combining strategic leadership with a practical, hands-on approach to execution.
Build finance capability for the future – Lead and develop a strong finance team, ensuring the function continues to evolve in step with the increasing scale, complexity and ambitions of the organization.
Help shape what comes next – Take on other strategic priorities and opportunities where financial leadership, commercial judgement and a hands-on approach can add value.

Qualifications & Experience

Bachelor’s degree in business, finance, accounting, commerce, or a related discipline.
Professional accounting designation (CPA), required.
Master of Business Administration (MBA) or other post-graduate considered an asset.
15+ years of progressive experience, including senior financial leadership experience.
Strong experience in real estate development, property management, corporate finance, or related industry, with demonstrated expertise in financing, debt structuring, and lender relationships.
Proven ability to advise ownership and executive leadership on strategic financial decisions.

Skills & Attributes

Curious and Imaginative –
Energized by building, growing, and shaping the future of the group.
Influential and collaborative –
Leads through influence, collaboration, sound judgement, and accountability.
Commercially astute –
Identifies opportunities, solves problems, and creates value.
Entrepreneurial –
Comfortable with calculated risk-taking and decisive action.
Agile and responsive –
Thrives in a low-bureaucracy environment and adapts quickly.

Today, Argus is entering an exciting next chapter. The organization is growth-oriented, entrepreneurial and highly connected to the decisions that shape its future, with opportunities across its existing portfolio as well as new development and investment. For the right person, this is not an opportunity to simply fill a seat in a large corporate structure. In this highly collaborative and entrepreneurial environment, it is an opportunity to have a voice, roll up your sleeves, work closely with ownership and help influence what comes next.

If you’re ready to be part of a successful, growing group of companies, we want to hear from you. Qualified individuals are asked to submit a resume and cover letter citing “CFO – Argus Group of Companies.” in the subject line. Applications will be reviewed as received and the posting will remain open until a suitable shortlist of qualified candidates has been established
. Early applications are encouraged. We appreciate all expressed interest in this position; however, only candidates selected for interview will be contacted. No phone calls please.

Compensation will be commensurate with the successful candidate’s level of education, knowledge, and experience pertaining to the role; however, it is expected that the salary range will be between $225,000 - $300,000
.

We are committed to fostering an inclusive and respectful workplace that values diverse perspectives and experiences. We welcome and encourage applications from all qualified individuals and are committed to providing equal employment opportunities without discrimination on any ground protected under applicable human rights legislation. All qualified individuals are encouraged to apply; however, preference may be given to Canadian citizens and permanent residents of Canada.

Reporting to the Chief Trust Officer you will partner across Autodesk to influence platform investments and product strategy. Le titulaire de ce poste est chargé de définir les fonctionnalités fiables dont les clients d'Autodesk ont besoin et d'expliquer leur importance, en collaboration avec les équipes chargées des produits et des plateformes qui déterminent la manière dont ces fonctionnalités sont mises en œuvre. Nous recherchons un directeur de la gestion des produits expérimenté pour diriger la stratégie produit relative aux expériences de confiance au sein de l’écosystème de plateformes d’Autodesk. La confiance est le fondement de chaque expérience client et de chaque flux de travail basé sur l’IA que nous proposons. Le titulaire de ce poste définira la vision, la stratégie et les priorités concernant les fonctionnalités de confiance attendues par les clients et travaillera en partenariat avec les équipes chargées des produits et des plateformes afin de garantir que ces fonctionnalités soient mises en œuvre de manière cohérente dans l’ensemble des produits Autodesk. Sous la responsabilité du directeur de la confiance (Chief Trust Officer), vous travaillerez en collaboration avec l’ensemble d’Autodesk pour orienter les investissements dans les plateformes et la stratégie produit. Vous traduirez l’évolution des attentes des clients, des exigences réglementaires et des tendances concurrentielles en investissements dans les plateformes qui renforceront la différenciation d’Autodesk. Il s’agit d’un poste de direction hautement collaboratif et transversal, exigeant une influence exceptionnelle, une réflexion stratégique et une capacité d’exécution au sein d’une organisation mondiale.

Nous sommes ouverts aux candidatures à distance provenant des États-Unis et du Canada.

Assurer la coordination entre les équipes Produit, Ingénierie, Sécurité, Confidentialité, Juridique, Conformité, Réussite client et la direction générale concernant les priorités en matière de confiance et les investissements dans la feuille de route
Évaluer en permanence l’évolution du paysage de la sécurité, de la confidentialité, de la résilience et de l’IA afin d’identifier les opportunités stratégiques et les besoins émergents des clients
Représenter la stratégie de confiance d’Autodesk auprès des clients professionnels, des partenaires stratégiques et des forums sectoriels

jobs.title: Director, GTM Planning & Compensation
jobs.description:
Clio is the global leader in legal AI technology, empowering legal professionals and law firms of every size to work smarter, faster, and more securely.

We are transforming the legal experience for all by bettering the lives of legal professionals while increasing access to justice.

Summary:

Revenue Operations is a strategic growth engine at Clio, accountable for optimizing how we acquire, expand, and retain revenue globally. We partner with Sales, Channel, Marketing, Customer Success, Finance, Legal, and Customer Support to design scalable GTM systems, align incentives to company strategy, and enable predictable, durable growth. The Revenue Operations team provides executive level insights, drives cross-functional decision making, and continuously improves GTM effectiveness through data, systems, and process excellence across North America, EMEA, and APAC.

We are seeking a Director of GTM Planning and Compensation
to own and evolve Clio’s global GTM planning, territory design, and incentive compensation functions as a core lever of growth, performance, and behavior change. This role is available to candidates in Vancouver, Calgary, or Toronto, or remotely across Canada (excluding Québec) and the US.

This role is responsible for translating company and GTM strategy into capacity plans, territories, quotas, and incentive design that drives the right outcomes across Sales, Channel, and Customer Success. You will operate as a strategic advisor to GTM and Finance leadership, balancing competitiveness, simplicity, scalability, and financial discipline.

You will lead capacity planning, territory design and maintenance, and incentive compensation planning, governance, and administration globally, oversee compensation systems and analytics, and build a high-performing sales planning function that scales with Clio’s rapid expansion. Your work will directly influence revenue predictability, seller behavior, retention, and long-term growth.

What you’ll work on:

GTM Planning, Capacity & Quotas

Leading GTM capacity planning and quota-setting, translating growth targets into coverage, headcount, and productivity plans across Sales and CS.
Developing and evolving quota-setting methodologies, ensuring targets are grounded in market opportunity, historical performance, and productivity expectations.
Partnering with Finance and GTM leadership to model capacity needs, ramp assumptions, productivity, and hiring requirements for annual and long-range planning, including scenario models that show the tradeoffs between headcount, coverage, quotas, productivity, compensation, and revenue before decisions are made.
Establishing planning frameworks and analytics to monitor capacity, quota attainment, and productivity and inform in-year adjustments.
Owning quota exceptions, relief policies, and disputes, balancing consistency with practical business judgment.

Compensation Strategy & Plan Design

Owning and evolving Clio's global GTM compensation and rewards strategy spanning SMB and Enterprise segments, partnering with Sales, Channel, and CS leadership to ensure alignment with company objectives, GTM motions, and growth stages.
Leading the design, modeling, and optimization of Sales and CS compensation plans, pay mix, quotas, accelerators, SPIFFs, and performance levers that drive desired behaviors, improve productivity, and support multi-year growth.
Partnering with Finance and Sales/CS Ops to model plan effectiveness, risk, and ROI, leading quarterly and annual compensation effectiveness reviews (attainment distribution, cost of sale, capacity utilization), and ensuring plans support revenue predictability, margin targets, and financial planning.
Developing and delivering clear, compelling compensation education and enablement programs for leaders, managers, and individual contributors, translating complex compensation concepts into simple, actionable narratives that build trust across GTM teams.

Compensation Administration & Systems

Ensuring accurate, timely, and compliant compensation processing in partnership with Payroll, Finance, HR, Legal, and RevOps.
Establishing and maintaining compensation governance, principles, and decision frameworks to ensure consistency, fairness, and scalability.
Owning compensation communications, including plan documentation, guidelines, timelines, and appeals processes.
Leading the refinement, governance, and continuous improvement of Clio's compensation and commission system (Forma.ai), driving automation, self-service, and operational excellence across regions.
Championing automation, self-service, and AI capabilities across planning and compensation to improve accuracy, scalability, and stakeholder experience.

Leadership & Team Development

Leading, coaching, and developing high-performing GTM planning and compensation teams, fostering accountability, strategic thinking, and continuous improvement.
Building scalable processes and operating rhythms, including the cross-functional planning calendar with Finance, HR, and GTM leadership, that enable the team to move from transactional execution to strategic impact.
Supporting change management for new plans, territories, tools, and policies across regions.
Serving as a role model for cross-functional partnership, ownership, and results-driven leadership.

What you bring:

8+ years of experience in SaaS or technology, with direct ownership of capacity planning, territory, quota, and compensation design.
Demonstrated ability to operate as a strategic advisor to senior GTM and Finance leaders.
Excellent executive-level communication skills, both written and verbal.
Experience leading and developing teams, with a focus on coaching and accountability.
High integrity, sound judgment, and comfort handling sensitive information.
Ability to thrive in ambiguity, make high-quality decisions with incomplete data, and drive outcomes in a fast-paced environment.
Action oriented, ownership driven mindset with a strong bias toward impact and results.
Proven ability to develop presentations with strong visual storytelling.
Advanced Excel skills.
Experience in translating measurements into recommendations, and connecting multiple data sources and building dashboards in data visualization tools (CRMA, Looker, Tableau, Google Sheets).
Knowledge of statistical modeling techniques.

jobs.description:
Scribd, Inc. is on a mission to advance human understanding. Our four products — Scribd®, Slideshare®, Everand™, and Fable — help billions of people across the globe move beyond access and into insight, application, and expertise.

Culture at Scribd, Inc.

We support a culture where our employees can be real and be bold; where we debate and commit as we embrace plot twists; and where every employee is empowered to take action as we prioritize the customer.

We believe the best work happens when individual flexibility is balanced with meaningful community connection. Scribd Flex empowers employees to choose the workstyle and location that support their best performance, while committing to intentional in-person moments that strengthen collaboration and culture. Occasional in-person attendance is required for all Scribd, Inc. employees, regardless of location.

So what are we looking for in new team members? At Scribd, Inc., we hire for “GRIT.” Traditionally defined as the intersection of passion and perseverance toward long-term goals, GRIT reflects the mindset we expect from every employee. For us, it also serves as a practical framework for how we work: setting and achieving Goals, delivering Results within your role, contributing Innovative ideas and solutions, and strengthening the broader Team through collaboration and attitude.

This posting reflects an approved, open position within the organization.

The Team

Data & Analytics is building the DNA of an AI native Scribd, Inc. Bringing together Analytics Engineering, Data Science, and Data Analytics, D&A partners across product, technology, content, and the business to scale intelligence, advance understanding, shape strategy, and turn insight into lasting growth across our four brand portfolio.

Making this ambition real at scale starts with Analytics Engineering. The team transforms fragmented data, inconsistent definitions, and dispersed analytical knowledge into trusted, reusable, production quality data foundations and products that enable intelligence to scale across the company.

In partnership with Engineering, Analytics Engineers ensure critical data is captured, centralized, documented, secured, and governed. The team builds canonical datasets, shared metrics, and semantic layers, together with the quality, observability, lineage, and evaluation systems that make these assets trustworthy. On top of this foundation, Analytics Engineers develop AI agents and analytical tools that bring reliable intelligence directly into the decisions and workflows of teams across the company.

The Role

We’re hiring for a Director, Analytics Engineering to own scaling data for an AI native Scribd, Inc. You will build, scale, and lead a high performing Analytics Engineering team, turning strong individual contributors into a cohesive and highly effective team. This requires more than hiring and developing exceptional talent. It means establishing an operating model that creates structure without unnecessary bureaucracy, fostering culture and community that balances local priorities with the broader success of the company, and creating the technical foundations and standards of excellence that enable everyone to do their best work.

Your leadership philosophy is grounded in service. A leader’s role is to provide clarity, create context, remove obstacles, and help others succeed. You will strengthen team dynamics, ensure great work is recognized, create meaningful career pathways, and help individuals navigate obstacles and opportunities throughout their careers. Durable teams are built by distributing ownership, developing leaders, and creating an environment where people feel trusted, supported, and accountable.

Your pragmatic approach keeps the organization moving forward. Rather than waiting for an ideal end state, you will think in sequences and ask, “What is the right next version?” Communication happens early and often because transparency, thoughtful feedback, and visible decision making build trust and help teams move with confidence.

Your strong strategic judgment is paired with enough proximity to the work to guide technical decisions credibly. You will connect analytics engineering investments to company priorities, communicate tradeoffs clearly to senior leaders, and contribute thoughtfully to decisions about data modeling, architecture, governance, quality, tooling, and developer experience.

The transformation happening through AI is an opportunity to expand what talented teams can accomplish. Agentic coding, AI assisted development and analysis, and automated workflows can increase human judgment, creativity, and impact rather than replace them. You approach these technologies with curiosity and pragmatism, applying them where they create clear and measurable value.

Above all, leadership is about building people and strengthening the discipline they share. Success is reflected in a team that grows more capable, confident, connected, and effective because of your leadership.

The Essentials

10+ years of experience in analytics engineering, data engineering, business intelligence engineering or a related discipline, including 5+ years leading and developing technical teams
Proven track record of building, scaling, and leading high performing teams, turning strong individual contributors into cohesive and highly effective teams that are valued as strategic partners
Depth in building governed, canonical data models and semantic layers, giving core business concepts one authoritative, discoverable definition instead of letting teams reconcile competing sources
Experience designing the data quality, observability, documentation, governance, access control, privacy, lineage, and evaluation systems that ensure data and AI products are reliable, explainable, trustworthy, and safe to operate at scale
Advanced SQL skills and production experience with modern data stack, including AWS, Databricks, Airbyte, Fivetran, Looker, or comparable platforms
Demonstrated ability to lead cross functional data initiatives from strategy through production adoption and measurable business impact
Strong judgment in balancing immediate stakeholder needs with long term investments in reusable data products, platform health, and technical debt reduction
Excellent written and verbal communication with technical teams, business stakeholders, and senior executives

The Nice to Haves

Advanced Python
Experience leading data cleanup efforts and implementing role based access controls and data retention policies to improve data quality, security, and governance
Experience designing and building canonical data models and semantic layers that support financial analysis at scale
Experience leading on call rotations, coordinating incident response, resolving production issues, and driving follow up improvements that strengthen system reliability

jobs.title: Head of Finance
jobs.description:
**The Opportunity**
-------------------


Gastronomous is hiring its first full\-time Head of Finance, an executive role spanning finance and operations. You will sit at the executive table, report to the CEO, attend our quarterly board meetings, and build the financial backbone of a robotics company in the middle of a major scale\-up.


This role keeps the books, and goes far beyond them. You will be a leader and a champion of our growth: shaping pricing, steering the finances of our operation, raising capital and helping take us into new countries. The role is built to grow into CFO after our Series A.

**Head of Finance** · Oakville, Ontario (on\-site) · Full\-time, permanent

**About Gastronomous**
----------------------


We are building the “Kitchen of the Future (https://youtu.be/DFROAGdIar4?si\=9mDdiQYygplqu5KF)” for quick\-service restaurants. We design, engineer and manufacture AI\-powered kitchen automation: ChronoGrill™, an autonomous open\-flame grill; Ghost, automated beverage pouring; and Gastroverse, our IoT cloud platform that monitors every machine in the field.


**How we work.** We are a no\-nonsense team of passionate, execution\-driven people. Our ability to deliver, not just dream, sets us apart: inside and outside the company, we do what we say we will do. Our people are trusted to act independently, make practical decisions and move fast. We build the future one deployment at a time.

**How fast we are growing.** The last 12 to 16 months changed the shape of the company:

* **Purchase orders signed with major brands**, moving us from pilots to rollout
* **A new office in La Mirada, California** to support US deployments; most of our customers are in the US, across many states
* **Our own ERP**, built in\-house to run parts, BOMs, inventory, work orders and purchasing


The next 12 to 16 months are bigger: scale across North America, sign new major accounts, enter new markets, secure new financing, and build an organization that can grow quickly and efficiently. We are about 35 people, mostly technical, headquartered in Oakville, Ontario.

**Why This Role**
-----------------

* **A seat at the executive table.** You report to the CEO, work directly with our founders, and help set company direction, not just report on it.
* **In the boardroom.** You attend our quarterly board meetings and present the numbers, the plan and the trade\-offs to our directors and investors.
* **Champion our growth.** Every new account, market and financing round runs through your numbers. You will see your work show up in deals signed and machines deployed.
* **Breadth few finance roles offer.** Two countries and counting, manufacturing, equipment, service and software revenue, government funding and venture fundraising, all in one seat.
* **Build it from the ground up.** Our finance function, pricing model, financial controls and new\-market playbook are yours to design. There is no inherited bureaucracy to work around.
* **A path to CFO.** This role is designed to grow into CFO after the Series A.
* **A team behind you.** You start with a full\-time bookkeeper and build the team as the company grows.

**What You Will Own**
---------------------


Your work falls into two halves of roughly equal weight. You run an efficient close, so you have real time for the decisions that grow the company.

### ***1\. Lead the finance function***


You will set up our systems and processes and do much of the work yourself, making sure every entry, filing and payment is right.

* **Close and reporting.** Lead the month\-end close for our Canadian parent and US subsidiary, including consolidation and intercompany reconciliation. Deliver timely financial statements and management reports to leadership and the board.
* **Year\-end.** Lead year\-end for both our Canadian and US entities: the year\-end close, the audit or review engagement, and corporate tax returns, working with our external accountants.
* **Budget and forecasts.** Own the annual budget and rolling forecasts, track performance against plan, and report the metrics leadership and the board run the company on: margins, unit economics and cash runway.
* **Revenue and billing.** Own revenue recognition across equipment, service and software contracts. Set customer payment terms and manage deposits and milestone billing.
* **Accounts receivable.** Own all of A/R across both entities: invoicing, customer credit and collections, so cash comes in on time.
* **Tax, audit and compliance.** Manage Canadian and US compliance, including HST/GST, US sales tax, corporate filings and transfer pricing, working with our external advisors.
* **Payroll and benefits.** Set up and run payroll in Canada and the US, including Records of Employment (ROEs). Administer our employee benefits programs, from enrolments and changes to provider relationships, keeping both accurate, compliant and cost\-effective.
* **SR\&ED and government funding.** Assist with preparing our SR\&ED claims, from tracking eligible costs to filing. Find, apply for, claim and report on grants and funding programs.
* **Systems and day\-to\-day accounting.** Set up our accounting systems, internal controls and policies. Work hands\-on with our bookkeeper on A/P, journal entries, reconciliations and expenses until each process runs cleanly.

### ***2\. Drive the financial side of our operations***

* **Pricing and margins.** Evaluate product and service pricing, build landed costing from bills of materials, contract\-manufacturer quotes, freight and duties, and track margins.
* **Inventory and systems.** Own inventory accounting and valuation, and keep our in\-house ERP and QuickBooks reconciled so every cost and margin can be trusted.
* **US operations.** Own the budget for our US office and work with its team to run it efficiently.
* **Cash and financing.** Manage cash flow, working capital, banking relationships and USD/CAD exposure. Secure external financing, including inventory financing.

Job Description

Rakuten Kobo brings the best reading experience to millions of readers worldwide. We operate ebook and audiobook storefronts across dozens of markets, build our own eReaders and reading apps, and run a content and technology platform that few companies of our size can match.

Here at Rakuten Kobo Inc. we offer a casual working start-up environment and a group of friendly and talented individuals. Our employees rank us highly in terms of commitment to work/life balance. We realize that for our people to be innovative, creative and passionate they need to feel valued and supported. We believe in rewarding all our employees with competitive salaries, performance based annual bonuses, stock options and training opportunities.

If you’re looking for a company that inspires passion, personal, and professional growth – join Kobo and come help us on our mission of making reading lives better.

The Role

You will lead the architecture function for all of Kobo's products and services, reporting to the CTO and leading a team of four domain architects covering commerce and discovery, purchasing and reading services, eReader platforms, and data engineering.

This is a VP-level leadership role exercised through architecture, not through P&L. You hold decision authority over Kobo's technology architecture — but your leverage comes from setting direction, defining the decision frameworks others use, and making the org better at making good calls without you in the

room. You stay close to the code through design reviews and architecture forums.

The Landscape You'll Shape

Our third-generation ecommerce, ad-tech, marketing automation, and personalization platform, powering storefronts in over 40 geos
Reading experience on iOS and Android apps, on the desktop Webreader, and our eReader devices
A rich content catalog and data model powering search, discovery, and syndication with retail partners

What You'll Do

Lead, grow, and develop the architecture team — four domain architects with coverage across our major technology areas, with hiring authority as the function grows
Run the architecture guild and practice forums. The guild is how architectural change is communicated to the broader engineering org; the practice forums are where major architectural changes and questions get surfaced and stress-tested with our principal and staﬀ engineers and architects.
Grow both into the venue where Kobo's biggest technical decisions are made
Identify gaps in our software ecosystem and drive the roadmap that closes them, in partnership with the CTO
Define the decision rubrics and frameworks that let engineering teams make sound architectural calls autonomously — your influence should scale far beyond your calendar
Champion pragmatic, incremental architecture: reduce complexity, improve velocity and reliability, and keep tactical delivery and long-term evolution moving together

The architecture guild and practice forums are thriving — well-attended, respected, and the de facto venue where big architectural decisions are communicated and debated
The flagship cross-functional initiatives are advancing or delivered, with architecture playing a visible, decisive role
There is a living, prioritized view of gaps in our software ecosystem, with a roadmap the CTO and R&D leadership team buy into

The Skillset

We are not screening for a specific technology checklist. What's essential:

10+ years building and architecting software, including senior leadership experience (Architect /Principal / Director level) in software development organizations

Experience in ecommerce or ad-tech platforms operating at significant scale, in both real-time and asynchronous workflows

Breadth across both client platforms and backend services

The Perks

Subsidized in-office lunches
Four extended long weekends in the summer
Full benefits starting from your first day
Paid Volunteer days, unlimited sick days, and 3% RRSP matching
Work From Anywhere Program for up to 3 months (90 days)
Lifestyle spending account

Dog friendly office

Rakuten Kobo Inc. is the world’s digital bookseller created by and for booklovers. Owned by Tokyo-based Rakuten Group, Inc. and headquartered in Toronto, Rakuten Kobo’s millions of worldwide users can read anytime, anywhere, and on any device. Are you looking for a leadership role where you can shape how an organization operates, manages risk, and achieves excellence? Can you see yourself driving enterprise-wide governance, performance, and continuous improvement initiatives that support safe, secure, and efficient operations? If you answered yes, this may be the job for you. Apply today
! Our Chalk River location is looking for a Director, Governance and Controls
to provide strategic leadership for CNL's management system, governance frameworks, safeguards management, nuclear material accountability, human performance, and organizational effectiveness programs.

What you will be doing!

Leadership and Strategic Direction
Developing and implementing the strategic vision, objectives and performance expectations for the Governance and Controls organization.
Establishing long-term plans supporting corporate objectives and operational priorities.
Providing leadership for enterprise-wide Governance and Controls initiatives.
Promoting a culture of accountability, continuous learning, and operational discipline.

Management Systems and Compliance

jobs.title: Global Head of Corporate Finance, General Account
jobs.description:
The Head of Corporate Finance is a senior investment leadership role accountable for leading Manulife’s global investment-grade corporate lending activities for the General Account. The role oversees approximately US$163 billion in investments, representing one of the General Account’s largest dedicated investment portfolios.

The Head of Corporate Finance is responsible for delivering strong, sustainable investment performance by identifying attractive relative value across public and private corporate credit markets, maintaining disciplined underwriting and risk management, and deploying capital effectively across Manulife’s global insurance businesses.

Key drivers of the outperformance of our investment program have been our direct contact and relationships with borrowers, our integrated global investment origination model across North America, Europe, Latin America, and Asia Pacific, and our very close partnership with our portfolio managers and credit officers to drive balanced innovation that best fits different Manulife portfolios.

The role leads a global team of approximately 70 lending professionals across Toronto, Boston and London, with an additional 15 lending professionals in Asia operating through a dotted-line relationship.

This leader is also a senior contributor to the broader General Account strategy and investment governance, bringing deep corporate credit expertise, market insight and leadership to enterprise investment decisions.

Position Responsibilities

Market Engagement, Investment Strategy & Performance

Empower your lending officers and teams to be leaders in the marketplace, engaging directly with borrowers and prospective borrowers and peers to understand well the market for investment grade lending and identify emerging sectors and borrowers where we can obtain better risk return in our lending.

Lead the global Corporate Finance investment strategy for an approximately US$163 billion investment-grade lending portfolio supporting the General Account.
Drive sustainable investment performance and attractive risk-adjusted returns for Manulife policyholders and shareholders.
Identify relative value across a highly diversified portfolio encompassing approximately 2,000 corporate borrowers.
Oversee investment activity across both public bonds and private placements, with the portfolio currently comprising approximately 70% public and 30% private investments.
Maintain a strong understanding of industries, companies and market dynamics to inform investment decisions and portfolio positioning.

Global Capital Deployment

Lead corporate lending activity across multiple currencies, including USD, CAD, EUR, GBP, AUD and CHF.
Optimize investment opportunities across Manulife’s global balance sheets, including Manulife Canada, Manulife Asia and John Hancock.
Partner closely with portfolio management teams to align corporate credit origination and investment activity with liability characteristics, portfolio requirements and business priorities.

Credit & Risk Leadership

Maintain disciplined investment underwriting and risk selection across a large and diversified corporate credit portfolio.
Work collaboratively with credit officers and portfolio managers to evaluate credit risk and identify attractive risk-return opportunities.
Bring industry expertise and judgment to complex investment decisions.
Contribute senior investment expertise to broader General Account investment decisions and governance.

Leadership & Talent

Lead a geographically dispersed global Corporate Finance organization across North America, Europe and Asia.
Build a high-performing investment culture characterized by strong judgment, accountability, collaboration, transparency and respect.
Develop leadership and investment capability across the organization and create a strong pipeline of future investment leaders.
Establish clear priorities while empowering senior leaders and investment professionals to operate effectively within their areas of responsibility.

Strategic Leadership

Serve as a senior member of the General Account Leadership Team and General Account Investment Committee.
Contribute to the development of the General Account's broader investment strategy and priorities.
Help identify and evaluate new investment capabilities, markets and opportunities where the General Account can generate differentiated value.
Represent Corporate Finance and the General Account with key internal stakeholders and external market participants.

Key Stakeholder Relationships

The Head Of Corporate Finance Works Closely With

General Account leadership
Portfolio Management
Credit
Investment Risk
Manulife Canada, Manulife Asia and John Hancock
Private Markets and other investment teams
Senior Finance and enterprise leadership
External borrowers, issuers, intermediaries and other market participants.
Success requires balancing strong independent investment judgment with the ability to operate collaboratively across investment disciplines, geographies and business units.

Required Qualifications

Deep expertise in corporate credit and investment-grade lending, ideally across both public and private markets.
Demonstrated experience leading a large and complex investment portfolio.
Strong understanding of credit underwriting, relative-value assessment, portfolio construction and risk management.
Experience operating across global markets and multiple currencies.
Strong commercial and investment judgment, including the ability to make effective decisions in complex or changing market environments.
Demonstrated ability to lead, develop and inspire senior investment professionals across multiple locations.
Strong executive presence and the ability to communicate complex investment matters clearly to senior leadership and investment governance forums.
Ability to collaborate effectively with portfolio managers, credit professionals and other investment teams while maintaining appropriate independence of judgment.
A track record of innovation and continuous improvement within an investment organization.

jobs.title: Director Supply Chain Strategy
jobs.description:
As the global leader in high-speed connectivity, Ciena builds the critical infrastructure powering the AI era. We’re a technology company shaping the future of networking, guided by innovation, integrity, and collaboration. Through development opportunities, meaningful work, and flexibility, Ciena supports growth and well-being—on and off the job. Connect with a career that matters.

The Director, Global Supply Chain Strategy & Architecture
is responsible for defining the long-term strategy and future-state architecture of the global Supply Chain organization.

This leader will translate business growth objectives, product strategy, customer requirements, market dynamics, and external supply-chain trends into an integrated global supply chain strategy and future-state design. The role will define the strategic choices required across the supply chain network, manufacturing and partner ecosystem, capacity, resilience, inventory positioning, and critical capabilities
to ensure the Supply Chain is positioned to scale, respond, and perform as the business evolves.

The Director will serve as the architect and integrator of the end-to-end supply chain
, connecting functional strategies into a cohesive future-state direction, identifying structural and capability requirements, developing strategic scenarios, and establishing the multi-year roadmap required to prepare Supply Chain for future business needs.

Key Responsibilities

Global Supply Chain Strategy
Lead the development and ongoing evolution of the global, multi-year Supply Chain strategy, aligned with the corporate strategy and growth objectives.
Translate business, product, market, and customer strategies into implications for the future supply chain.
Define the strategic choices required across areas such as global footprint, capacity, sourcing, manufacturing, inventory, logistics, supply assurance, resilience, and partner strategy.
Identify the capabilities required to enable the supply chain to scale effectively while maintaining agility, competitiveness, and customer responsiveness.
Maintain an external perspective on geopolitical developments, industry trends, supply-market dynamics, manufacturing models, and emerging supply-chain practices.
Physical Strategic Roadmap & Prioritization
Develop and maintain an integrated 3-5 year Supply Chain strategic roadmap, translating strategy into clear priorities and strategic initiatives.
Establish the strategic rationale and expected business outcomes associated with major supply-chain investments.
Identify dependencies and trade-offs across major strategic initiatives and recommend priorities
Ensure functional strategies connect to a common end-to-end direction rather than developing independently.
Partner with functional leaders to translate the global strategy into actionable priorities within their respective organizations.
Facilitate leadership discussions and strategy sessions focused on major supply-chain choices and priorities.
Establish a regular cadence for reviewing the Supply Chain strategy, external assumptions, strategic risks, and progress against priorities.
Ensure strategic decisions are translated into clear ownership and accountability across the Supply Chain organization.
Supply Chain Network & Ecosystem Strategy
Develop strategic perspectives on the global supply-chain footprint and ecosystem required to support future growth.
Assess long-term requirements for manufacturing capacity, geographic diversification, supplier ecosystem, contract manufacturing, distribution, and logistics networks.
Evaluate strategic make/buy/partner considerations and recommend the appropriate operating model for different elements of the supply chain.
Incorporate geopolitical, concentration, continuity, capacity, cost, and customer considerations into global network decisions.
Partner with functional leaders to develop strategies that strengthen supply assurance and reduce structural supply-chain risk.
Strategic Capacity & Scale Readiness
Assess the supply chain's ability to support future revenue, product, volume, and customer requirements.
Identify structural constraints that could limit the company's ability to scale.
Develop strategic scenarios for different growth, demand, supply, and geopolitical conditions.
Identify where additional capacity, capability, supplier diversification, inventory, or ecosystem investment may be required.
Establish a forward-looking view of supply-chain readiness and bring recommended actions and trade-offs to senior leadership.
Strategic Business & Financial Analysis
Develop fact-based recommendations for complex supply-chain decisions, clearly articulating options, trade-offs, risks, investment requirements, and expected business outcomes.
Develop business cases for significant strategic supply-chain investments and decisions.
Partner with Finance to assess the financial implications of alternative supply-chain strategies.
Balance service, growth, resilience, inventory, working capital, cost, and investment considerations when developing strategic recommendations.
Establish measures that demonstrate whether the supply-chain strategy is delivering the intended business outcomes.
Enterprise & Cross-Functional Alignment
Build strong partnerships across Product Line Management (PLM), R&D, Finance, Sales Operations, and other Enterprise functions.
Connect product roadmaps, business growth plans, financial objectives, and customer requirements to future supply-chain requirements.
Ensure Supply Chain implications are incorporated early into major business and product decisions.

Outside the Scope of This Role

This Role Does Not Own

Digital supply-chain strategy or technology implementation
Process transformation and process redesign
Supply-chain systems implementation
Automation or AI deployment
Transformation program management
Day-to-day functional or operational execution

The Must Haves

Bachelor’s degree in supply chain, Operations, Engineering, Business, Finance, or a related discipline.
Significant progressive experience in global supply chain, operations, strategy, or a related leadership role.
Broad end-to-end understanding of supply-chain disciplines including planning, sourcing, manufacturing, inventory, logistics, supplier management, and supply assurance.
Demonstrated ability to develop long-term strategy and translate complex business requirements into clear strategic priorities.
Experience within a complex global manufacturing environment, ideally technology, telecommunications, electronics, semiconductor, or a related sector.
Experience evaluating supply-chain networks, manufacturing strategies, capacity requirements, outsourcing models, and/or global supply ecosystems.
Strong business and financial acumen with experience developing investment recommendations and evaluating strategic trade-offs.
Exceptional executive communication skills and demonstrated ability to influence senior stakeholders across organizational boundaries.

Nice To Have

MBA or advanced degree in Supply Chain, Operations, Engineering, Finance, or related discipline.
Experience working within an outsourced or contract-manufacturing operating model.
Experience supporting periods of significant business growth or structural change.
Experience with scenario planning, network strategy, supply-chain risk, and global capacity strategy.

Leadership Competencies

Enterprise Thinking: Optimizes decisions for the end-to-end business rather than individual functions.
Strategic Foresight: Anticipates future business requirements and their implications for the supply chain.
Commercial Acumen: Connects supply-chain choices directly to growth, customers and financial outcomes.
Structured Problem Solving: Brings clarity and fact-based thinking to ambiguous strategic issues.
Influence & Alignment: Builds commitment across functions and senior leaders.
Executive Presence: Communicates complex strategic issues simply and confidently.
Decision Orientation: Moves strategy beyond analysis into clear choices, priorities, and accountability.

Pay Ranges

The salary range for this role in Ottawa, Canada is $144, 900 - $231, 500

The salary range for this role in the eastern-USA is $158, 800 - $253, 600

The Role

Practice Leadership & Strategy

Define the direction and growth strategy for the data practice
Build and maintain a compelling service offering that reflects market demand and client need
Work closely with senior leadership to align practice goals with broader business objectives
Contribute to thought leadership, proposals, and business development activity

Delivery

Maintain hands-on involvement where needed — reviewing delivery approaches, unblocking teams, and ensuring quality
Establish and embed delivery standards, methodologies, and best practices across the practice
Identify and manage risks before they become problems

Stakeholder Management

Act as the senior point of contact for key clients, building trusted advisor relationships at C-suite and director level
Lead client engagement from scoping through to delivery and beyond
Navigate complex stakeholder environments with clarity and confidence
Ensure client satisfaction drives repeat business and referrals

People & Team

Lead, mentor, and grow a team of consultants, engineers, and architects

About You

A proven track record delivering complex software or data projects, ideally within a consulting or professional services environment

Marketing

About The Role

Blacksmith Agency runs PPC and SEO for clients across multifamily, B2B and technical verticals. As Director of Digital Marketing you lead that department. The PPC strategist and the SEO strategist report to you and they are the specialists in their channels. Right now nobody owns this function, which is the whole reason this seat is open.

This is a management seat, not a senior individual contributor one.
You will not be building campaigns, and on technical SEO your strategist will know more than you do. That is the arrangement, not a gap. You carry channel strategy and where budget goes as accounts scale. The strategists carry the execution of it, and you carry whether the department delivers.

What You Own

The PPC strategist and the SEO strategist: their quality bar, their development, their reviews, and the call when someone is not going to get there.
The standard the work is held to. What a good audit looks like, what gets checked before work leaves the agency, how an account is reported. You write it and you hold two specialists to it.
Client results across the whole function, including whether our reporting is honest. Nobody here is auditing attribution and GA4 accuracy today.
The escalation when an account is at risk. You diagnose it, you direct the strategist who fixes it, and you are on the call with the client.
Channel strategy and where budget goes as accounts scale.
What we tell sales we can credibly deliver, before it gets sold.
The hiring plan for the department, and first-round interviews for your own team, within about a quarter.

What You Need

Strategists or specialists who have reported to you, where their reviews, their development and the decision when someone was not working out were yours. Managing accounts is not this.
7+ years across paid media and SEO. Owning one channel while sitting beside the other does not count here.
Enough depth in Google Ads, GA4, Search Console, Meta and Microsoft Ads to tell good work from work that merely looks good. That is a lower bar than doing it and a higher bar than reading a report.
One account you turned around that you can talk through: the metric, the figure before, the figure after, and why the change worked. Whose hands were on the keyboard matters far less than whether the diagnosis was yours.
Comfortable being the client-facing owner when an account is underperforming. That call comes to you, not to the strategist.
Agency experience carrying many accounts at once.

Please do not apply if

Nobody has ever reported to you, or you have never owned someone's review or had to performance-manage anyone.
You have only ever run one channel.
All of your experience is in-house on a single brand.
What you actually want is to keep building campaigns yourself. That is not a lesser ambition, it is a different job, and this is not it.

None of these are preferences we bend on. They are how we screen, so applying anyway costs you an hour and gets you a no.

Process

Three conversations, then a decision. A thirty minute screen with our recruiter, a first round with the founder this seat reports to, and a final. No take-home project and no panel interview.

How To Apply

Four fields at the link, then a short 6 minute Predictive Index assessment. Use the same email throughout. No cover letter.

Reporting to the Connected Vehicle Engineering Director, the Head of E/E Architecture is the primary technical and strategic leader responsible for defining, evolving, and governing the next-generation Electrical/Electronic (E/E) systems and Software-Defined Vehicle (SDV) platform across all BRP product lines.

In an environment where software and electronic architectures are core strategic differentiators for BRP products, you will lead the transition from legacy, flat distributed networks to a multi-product, domain-based central compute architecture. In collaboration with software, systems, integration, validation, cybersecurity, and product line teams, as well as global technology suppliers, you will shape BRP’s multi-year technological roadmap and build a world-class architecture and software engineering organization.

YOU’LL HAVE THE OPPORTUNITY TO

Define and execute the transition to a more centralized E/E architecture, integrating Infotainment, Connectivity, and ADAS using Service-Oriented Architecture (SOA) and Software-Defined Vehicle (SDV) principles.
Lead top-level platform design for next-generation vehicle E/E architectures, defining hardware topology, high-speed vehicle networks (Automotive Ethernet, TSN, CAN-FD), power wake-up/sleep strategies, and SOA service boundaries.
Drive vehicle-to-cloud and mobile ecosystem architectures to deliver reliable connectivity features in off-grid environments using smartphone proxying, local caching, and automated wireless handshakes.
Direct and enforce BRP’s 3-tier E/E Architecture Governance Model across all product lines using objective trade-off evaluation tools to eliminate technical debt and maximize component reuse.
Function as the technical lead and final approver for cybersecurity and functional safety, ensuring vehicle architectures comply with UN R155, CRA, ISO/SAE 21434, and ISO 26262 standards.
Lead the adoption of Model-Based Systems Engineering (MBSE) methodologies (Capella/SysML) and manage the New Technology Roadmap (NTR) for Connected Vehicle R&D in partnership with BRP’s CTA.

A bachelor's or master's degree in Computer Science, Electrical Engineering, Mechatronics, Computer Engineering, Software Engineering, or a related discipline.
10–15+ years of progressive engineering experience in automotive, powersports, off-highway, or aerospace E/E system design, with at least 5+ years in a technical leadership or managerial role.
A proven track record of delivering mass-production E/E architectures, central compute platforms, or complex embedded software systems from concept to vehicle launch.
Deep expertise in Software-Defined Vehicles (SDV), domain and zonal compute topologies, centralized compute SoCs (e.g., NXP, Qualcomm, Telechips), and hypervisor/virtualization technologies.
Strong proficiency in vehicle networking protocols (Automotive Ethernet, TSN, SOME/IP, DDS, CAN/CAN-FD, LIN, UDS).
Excellent executive communication and influencing skills, with the ability to synthesize complex multi-domain technical concepts into clear proposals for executive leadership.
Demonstrated change management capabilities and strategic business acumen to align independent business units around shared platform architectures while balancing technical innovation against BOM cost and development speed.

Assets

Knowledge of AUTOSAR (Classic & Adaptive), POSIX RTOS (QNX/Linux), C/C++, Python, and modern embedded software development practices.
Direct experience with requirement management tools (Polarion, DOORS), MBSE tools (Capella, SysML), and RFLP frameworks.
Familiarity with automotive standards, including ISO 26262 (Functional Safety), ISO/SAE 21434, UN R155/R156, and ASPICE delivery frameworks.
Experience evaluating and structuring supplier partnerships in global markets, particularly in Asia or EV/automotive ecosystems.
Demonstrated expertise in architecting hybrid connectivity solutions for powersports, off-highway, or automotive applications, leveraging mobile proxy mechanisms for off-grid navigation and deferred over-the-air updates.

Role Description

As the Director, Insights & Measurement
, you will be the primary analytical mind and strategic architect behind our advanced media attribution, experimentation, and business science methodologies. This role is designed for a heavyweight statistician and media measurement expert who thrives on solving the "what worked and why" for major brands.

While you will collaborate closely with our dedicated internal Data Engineering and Infrastructure teams—who build and maintain our cloud pipelines—you will own the frameworks, model designs, and causal inference methodologies. You will act as a senior leader, serving as the crucial bridge who translates complex statistical outputs (like MMM, MTA, and lift studies) into high-level strategic narratives and multi-million-dollar budget optimization recommendations for modern CMOs and CFOs.

Core Focus: 70% Attribution Methodology & Experimental Design; 30% Client Consulting, Narrative Strategy & Team Mentorship.

Advanced Attribution & Econometric Modeling

Methodology Ownership: Lead the theoretical design, validation of custom Marketing Mix Models (MMM), Multi-Touch Attribution (MTA), and customer Path-to-Conversion frameworks.
Unified Measurement Strategy: Champion a "Unified Measurement" approach, combining macro-level MMM econometric trends with micro-level digital attribution signals to give clients a singular source of truth.
Advanced Feature Engineering & Design: Determine the data requirements, adstock transformations, and saturation curve variables needed for accurate modelling, directing data engineers on how to prepare these schemas.

Experimentation & Causal Inference

Testing Frameworks: Architect randomized control trials (RCTs), matched-market tests, and geo-lift studies to establish true incrementality and validate marketing models.
Model Calibration: Use test-and-learn results and lift studies to continuously calibrate and ground MMM/MTA models, stripping out correlation and proving true causal media ROI.

Client Consulting & Strategic Storytelling

Strategic Translation: Turn highly complex mathematical outputs, coefficient shifts, and statistical variances into clear, visual, and highly compelling business recommendations.
Budget Optimization: Guide clients on optimal media mix scenarios, flighting strategies, and cross-channel budget reallocations based on model predictions.
New Business & Growth: Serve as the measurement subject matter expert during high-profile agency pitches, articulating our advanced attribution capabilities to prospective client stakeholders.
Team Mentorship: Direct and mentor a growing team of media analysts and marketing scientists, cultivating deep methodological expertise and client-ready presentation skills.

jobs.description:
**Company:** Rwandan Canadian Healing Centre (RCHC)

**Location:** Toronto, Ontario

**Job Type:** Part\-time

**Schedule:** Approximately 4 hours per week

**Work Arrangement:** To be confirmed

**Reports To:** Executive Director

About the Rwandan Canadian Healing Centre

The Rwandan Canadian Healing Centre (RCHC) is a nonprofit organization dedicated to supporting newcomers and refugees through transitional housing, employment assistance, community programs, and initiatives that promote stability, inclusion, and independence.

Our organization is committed to responsible financial management, transparency, and accountability to ensure that our resources effectively support the individuals and communities we serve.

Position Overview

RCHC is seeking an experienced, detail\-oriented, and highly organized **Finance Director** to oversee the organization's financial operations, bookkeeping, financial reporting, budgeting, payroll, and regulatory compliance.

The successful candidate will play an important role in maintaining accurate financial records, strengthening internal controls, improving financial processes, and supporting informed organizational decision\-making.

Working closely with the Executive Director, Board of Directors, Program Manager, and other team members, the Finance Director will help ensure responsible stewardship of organizational resources and the long\-term financial sustainability of RCHC.

This position is ideal for a finance or accounting professional who demonstrates strong technical expertise, sound judgment, independence, and an interest in contributing to a mission\-driven nonprofit organization.

Key Responsibilities

**1\. Financial Reporting and Budget Management**

* Prepare accurate and timely financial reports for the Executive Director, Board of Directors, and relevant program leads.
* Monitor organizational revenue, expenditures, cash flow, and overall financial performance.
* Develop and maintain annual organizational budgets in collaboration with leadership.
* Prepare financial forecasts and identify potential financial risks, needs, and opportunities.
* Compile annual financial information and reports for funders, donors, auditors, and other stakeholders.
* Develop and maintain practical financial dashboards and reporting tools where appropriate.
* Provide financial analysis and recommendations to support organizational planning and decision\-making.

**2\. Bookkeeping and Financial Administration**

* Maintain accurate, complete, and organized financial records.
* Record and categorize financial transactions in accordance with established accounting procedures.
* Ensure invoices, receipts, reimbursements, and other financial documentation are properly maintained.
* Initiate, document, and organize payments for approved organizational and program expenses.
* Perform or oversee bank reconciliations and month\-end and year\-end financial processes.
* Maintain and troubleshoot integrations between accounting, banking, payroll, and other financial systems.
* Ensure financial records are properly organized and available for authorized review.

**3\. Banking and Cash Flow Management**

* Oversee organizational bank and investment accounts.
* Monitor account balances, cash flow, and upcoming financial obligations.
* Ensure organizational funds are managed in accordance with approved budgets, internal policies, and funding restrictions.
* Maintain appropriate financial controls and authorization procedures.
* Identify opportunities to improve financial efficiency while maintaining accountability and transparency.
* Support responsible cash management and financial planning.

**4\. Payroll, Tax Filing, and Regulatory Compliance**

* Process payroll and employee expense reimbursements accurately and on time.
* Prepare and issue required employee tax documentation.
* Coordinate annual Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) filings and other applicable nonprofit or charitable reporting requirements.
* Maintain documentation required for financial audits, regulatory filings, and organizational reviews.
* Support compliance with applicable payroll, taxation, funding, and financial reporting requirements.
* Coordinate with external accountants, auditors, and other financial professionals when required.
* Ensure appropriate confidentiality and security of financial and employee information.

**5\. Financial Systems and Process Improvement**

* Review existing financial procedures and identify opportunities for improvement.
* Develop and maintain efficient, transparent, and practical financial management systems.
* Establish clear procedures for expense tracking, reimbursements, payment approvals, budgeting, and reporting.
* Improve financial documentation and recordkeeping practices.
* Support the integration and effective use of accounting and financial management software.
* Develop scalable financial processes that support RCHC's operational needs and continued growth.

**6\. Financial Leadership and Organizational Collaboration**

* Provide financial guidance and recommendations to the Executive Director and Board of Directors.
* Communicate financial information clearly to individuals without an accounting or finance background.
* Collaborate with program staff to support budget monitoring and responsible expenditure management.
* Contribute financial insight to organizational planning and strategic discussions.
* Support financial accountability across programs and operational activities.
* Promote a culture of transparency, accuracy, and responsible financial stewardship.

Qualifications and Experience

**Required Qualifications**

* Demonstrated professional experience in accounting, bookkeeping, financial management, or nonprofit financial administration.
* Strong working knowledge of QuickBooks or comparable accounting software.
* Experience preparing financial reports, budgets, reconciliations, and financial records.
* Familiarity with payroll processing, CRA

Position Description

We are seeking a Director, Consulting Expert (DCE) – Enterprise Data Modernization Lead (GCP) to provide senior technical, solutioning, and client facing leadership

The DCE will serve as a trusted advisor to the client while helping shape, win, govern, and successfully deliver complex enterprise data initiatives.

This is not a narrow technical specialist or delivery only position. The DCE combines deep enterprise data warehouse and modern data platform expertise with consulting acumen, architecture leadership, commercial awareness, and executive presence. The successful candidate will be equally comfortable discussing business outcomes with senior client stakeholders, shaping and estimating solutions, leading architecture decisions, and engaging in detailed technical discussions with engineering teams.

Your future duties and responsibilities

Serve as a senior client facing advisor for enterprise data warehouse, data engineering, analytics, and data platform modernization initiatives within a complex telecommunications environment.
Translate business objectives and requirements into actionable data strategies, architectures, roadmaps, and solution options.
Lead end to end solution architecture, considering data, applications, integration, cloud, cybersecurity, operations, cost, scalability, and delivery trade offs.
Architect and guide enterprise data solutions on Google Cloud Platform (GCP), including technologies such as BigQuery, Cloud Storage, Dataflow, Dataproc, Pub/Sub, Cloud Composer, Dataplex, Dataform, and Looker.
Provide technical leadership across enterprise data warehousing, data modelling, ETL/ELT, batch and streaming pipelines, data quality, metadata, governance, security, and analytics.
Lead or co lead technical solutioning for strategic pursuits, proposals, RFPs, and account growth opportunities.
Develop and challenge solution scope, architecture, assumptions, estimates, resource models, dependencies, risks, and delivery approaches to ensure solutions are competitive and executable.
Orchestrate SMEs across data, cloud, applications, integration, cybersecurity, infrastructure, and operations to develop cohesive end to end solutions.
Lead or participate in architecture, estimation, proposal, and delivery governance reviews, identifying technical and delivery risks before commitments are made.
Advise on AI/ML and generative AI data readiness, including data quality, accessibility, governance, privacy, security, and responsible adoption.
Maintain sufficient hands on technical depth to challenge designs, validate assumptions, troubleshoot critical issues, and defend architectural decisions.
Mentor architects and technical leads and promote reusable architectures, patterns, accelerators, and solution assets across the team.
Partner with the DCS and broader P&L leadership to strengthen the client relationship, identify growth opportunities, improve solution quality, and develop technical leadership capability within the team.

Required Qualifications To Be Successful In This Role

10+ years of progressively responsible experience in leading enterprise data warehousing, data engineering, analytics, cloud architecture, solution architecture, or related IT consulting disciplines.
Demonstrated experience architecting and delivering complex enterprise data warehouse and modern cloud data platform solutions.
Strong experience with Google Cloud Platform (GCP) and its data and analytics ecosystem, particularly Big Query and associated ingestion, processing, orchestration, governance, and analytics capabilities.
Strong knowledge of enterprise data architecture, data modelling, ETL/ELT, data integration, data quality, metadata, security, governance, and analytics.
Strong SQL skills and working knowledge of modern data engineering technologies and practices such as Python, Git, CI/CD, Infrastructure as Code, APIs, and automated testing/deployment.
Experience with enterprise data technologies such as Snowflake, Databricks, Oracle, SQL Server, Teradata, Informatica, DataStage, dbt, or comparable platforms.
Demonstrated experience leading solution architecture for significant client engagements, proposals, RFPs, or complex technology pursuits.
Experience developing or validating solution estimates, delivery models, assumptions, dependencies, and technical risks.
Strong consulting and executive communication skills, including discovery, problem framing, facilitation, solution development, and client presentations.
Demonstrated ability to lead multidisciplinary technical teams, influence senior stakeholders, and mentor architects and technical leaders.
Working knowledge of AI/ML and generative AI concepts and their implications for enterprise data architecture and governance.

Preferred Qualifications:

Experience delivering data and analytics solutions within the telecommunications industry, with an understanding of large scale, high volume telco data environments and associated business and operational use cases.
Google Cloud certification, particularly Professional Cloud Architect and/or Professional Data Engineer, or equivalent demonstrated expertise.
Experience modernizing large legacy or on premises enterprise data warehouse environments to GCP.
Experience within a large IT consulting, systems integration, managed services, or professional services organization.
Experience supporting large, complex and highly integrated enterprise technology environments.
Commercial awareness encompassing consulting economics, solution costing, delivery risk, and value based solutioning.

Leadership Profile

The successful DCE will be a visible, take charge consulting leader who:

Leads with client and business outcomes rather than technology alone.
Has the executive presence to independently lead senior client conversations.
Takes ownership of ambiguous or difficult solution problems and drives them to resolution.
Retains enough hands on technical depth to challenge and defend important architecture decisions.
Challenges unrealistic estimates, unsupported assumptions, scope gaps, and delivery risks before commitments are made.
Works across organizational and technology boundaries rather than operating as a narrow or isolated SME.
Coaches and develops architects and technical leaders, raising the capability of the broader team.

Measures of Success

Success will be reflected in stronger client relationships, higher quality solutions and estimates, improved pursuit outcomes, reduced delivery risk, successful enterprise data initiatives, and increased technical capability across the team.

The DCE will be recognized by the client, delivery teams, DCS, and broader P&L leadership as a trusted senior advisor who connects telecommunications business outcomes, enterprise data architecture, technology, commercial realities, and delivery feasibility.
