jobs.title: Director, Technology
jobs.description:
The Director, Technology is to ensure that the BC Cancer Foundation has reliable, secure and fit-for-purpose technology services that enable our people to work effectively, strengthen fundraising and donor engagement, and support our 2030 strategic ambitions. The role translates business needs into technology solutions and measurable service improvements, maximizing the value of existing platforms while preparing the Foundation for evolving needs.

Working through a shared-service and vendor-led delivery model, the Director is accountable for dependable technology services, effective provider partnerships, oversight of technology risk. This is a hands-on leadership role: the Director sets the technology roadmap, makes informed trade-offs, resolves issues, delivers improvements and works directly with partners and internal teams to get results.

Reporting to the Senior Vice President, Chief Strategy & Business Intelligence Officer, the Director leads a small team and works closely with business leaders, the Provincial Health Services Authority (PHSA) and technology vendors to ensure technology investments are adopted, secure, cost-effective, and responsive to the Foundation’s priorities.

Key Accountabilities

1. Technology Enablement, Roadmap & Value

Translate BCCF's enterprise technology strategy and organizational priorities into a practical, sequenced roadmap that optimizes existing platforms, enables new capabilities and delivers measurable improvements in productivity, fundraising, donor engagement, and operational effectiveness.
Partner with business leaders to understand pain points and future requirements; identify when to optimize existing tools, improve processes, integrate platforms, or recommend new solutions.
Partner with the data team to ensure a reliable and secure technology platform underpins our reporting and analytics and accessible data and evolving organizational needs.
Evaluate and prioritize technology initiatives based on business value, donor and employee experience, reliability, security, cost, adoption and organizational capacity; define measurable benefits and track results.
Provide technical and commercial advice to enterprise planning, platform decisions, automation and responsible AI adoption, in alignment with enterprise governance.

2. Technology Service Delivery & Operational Excellence

Ensure dependable day-to-day technology services for all our staff. or another vendor.
Lead operational issue resolution and escalation; establish service expectations, reporting, clear ownership and follow-through for incidents, requests, root causes and recurring problems.
Ensure seamless employee onboarding, changes and offboarding, including devices, identity, permissions, licenses, collaboration tools and access to critical business applications.
Continuously improve employee technology experience and operational efficiency through simple processes, fit-for-purpose support, clear documentation and actionable service measures.

3. Strategic Partnerships, Contracts & Service Accountability

Own and strengthen the operational technology partnership with PHSA, defining service scope, accountability, escalation, decision rights, administrative access, and a fit-for-purpose future service model for BCCF.
Manage relationships and performance across key enterprise and SaaS providers, including Blackbaud and other platforms supporting fundraising, finance, and donor engagement.
Negotiate and oversee contracts, service levels, licenses, renewals and vendor roadmaps; hold partners accountable for responsive, secure, timely and cost-effective delivery.
Anticipate dependencies and provider-driven changes, represent BCCF’s needs credibly and secure workable outcomes through collaboration, influence and disciplined follow-up.

4. Technology Risk and Cybersecurity Oversight

Building on BCCF’s current cybersecurity assessment, oversee the operational security measures delivered by PHSA, Blackbaud, and other service providers
Ensure the risks to our technology reliability, and the potential impact of service issues on our business, are understood
Evolve BCCF’s technology risk mitigation approach and our plans to respond to and recover from service disruptions

5. Implementation, Adoption & Future Readiness

Personally lead and coordinate priority technology service improvements and cross-functional implementations, from requirements and vendor coordination through testing, rollout, issue resolution and stabilization.
Partner with the PMO, Data Platforms and Analytics, People and Organization People teams and business owners to manage dependencies, change control, communications, training and adoption so solutions are used effectively.
Maintain a current view of technology capabilities, integrations, licenses, architecture dependencies and replacement horizons; proactively recommend sustainable improvements that reduce complexity and future risk.
Assess emerging technologies and opportunities for secure automation and AI, and translate promising ideas into realistic pilots, business cases, or phased implementation recommendations.

6. Financial Stewardship, Team Leadership & Performance

Manage technology services budgets, assets, software subscriptions and vendor spend with clear forecasting, cost controls and value-for-money decisions.
Lead, coach and develop a small, service-oriented team, clarifying accountability, balancing workloads and building the internal capability needed to manage partners and deliver reliably.
Provide concise reporting to the CSBIO and business leaders on service performance, project delivery, adoption, spend, material risks and decisions required.
Model BCCF’s values — Be Curious, Be Authentic and Be Courageous by embracing innovation, building trusted relationships, communicating transparently, challenging the status quo, proactively addressing risks, and taking ownership of outcomes.

What Success Looks Like

Technology investments and initiatives demonstrate measurable improvements in employee productivity, service effectiveness, technology adoption and organizational value, supported by a realistic, prioritized and financially sustainable roadmap.
Employees and teams can rely on timely, secure and responsive technology support; recurring issues decline, and service satisfaction improves.
PHSA and other providers operate against understood responsibilities, measurable service levels and effective escalation; critical dependencies are proactively managed.
Cybersecurity, privacy, continuity, and third-party risks are visible, assessed and mitigated, with tested plans and no unmanaged critical gaps.

Qualifications

Post-secondary education in technology, information systems, business or an equivalent combination of experience and demonstrated capability.
10+ years of progressive technology experience, including 5+ years leading technology services, teams, vendors or complex delivery.
Proven success leading technology delivery through outsourced, shared-service or SaaS partnerships, with accountability for service performance, contracts and escalations.
Hands-on experience solving operational technology issues, leading implementations and turning business needs into adopted improvements.
Working knowledge of infrastructure, Microsoft 365, identity and access management, enterprise applications, integrations, cybersecurity, privacy and business continuity.
Strong business and financial judgment, including prioritization, business cases, total cost of ownership, vendor negotiations and budget accountability.
Experience with fundraising, CRM or finance systems (e.g., Blackbaud) and healthcare, philanthropy or public-sector partners is an asset.
ITIL, cybersecurity, project or vendor-management credentials are assets but don’t replace proven results.

  Core Competencies

Accountability & Results
— Owns dependable technology service delivery, follows through on commitments, resolves operational issues and delivers measurable service and business improvements.
Collaboration & Influence — Builds trusted relationships across business teams, PHSA and vendors; clarifies needs, negotiates solutions and secures accountability without direct authority.
Judgment & Decision-Making
— Balances reliability, business value, risk, cost and capacity; makes timely, practical decisions, challenges assumptions and escalates material risks with clear recommendations.
Learning, Adaptability, Innovation & Change
— Evaluates emerging technologies, improves existing platforms and leads implementation and adoption through practical change management.
Organizational & Strategic Thinking
— Connects technology investments to BCCF’s 2030 strategy, anticipates future needs and translates direction into achievable roadmaps and priorities.
Leadership & Development
— Leads a capable, service-focused team; sets clear expectations, coaches performance, builds ownership and supports inclusive collaboration and development.

Functional Knowledge & Skills

Technology service delivery — Knowledge of infrastructure, Microsoft 365, enterprise applications, integrations, identity and access management, IT service management and incident resolution.
Vendor, financial and risk stewardship — Manages PHSA/shared-service and SaaS providers, service agreements, budgeting, cybersecurity, privacy, continuity and third-party risk.
Hands-on implementation — Ability to translate needs into requirements, coordinate vendors, troubleshoot barriers, guide testing and rollout, and measure adoption and results.

jobs.title: Head of Applied Science and AI Delivery
jobs.description:
This is your opportunity to join AXIS Capital – a trusted global provider of specialty lines insurance and reinsurance. We stand apart for our outstanding client service, intelligent risk taking and superior risk adjusted returns for our shareholders. We also proudly maintain an entrepreneurial, disciplined and ethical corporate culture. As a member of AXIS, you join a team that is among the best in the industry.

At AXIS, we believe that we are only as strong as our people. We strive to create an inclusive and welcoming culture where employees of all backgrounds and from all walks of life feel comfortable and empowered to be themselves. This means that we bring our whole selves to work.

All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to any protected characteristic, including age, color, disability, ethnicity, gender identity, marital status, national origin, pregnancy, race, religion, sex, sexual orientation, veteran status, or any basis prohibited by the laws that govern its operations.

How does this role contribute to our collective success?

Data, analytics and AI are critical to AXIS’s ability to make confident decisions, identify opportunities, improve efficiency and create sustainable competitive advantage. The Head of Applied Science & AI Delivery leads the development, management and evolution of AXIS’s portfolio of reusable applied science and AI capabilities.

Rather than owning delivery for individual business initiatives, this role provides the shared services, models, frameworks, engineering patterns and specialist expertise that enable and support delivery of high-quality business solutions rapidly, safely and consistently. The role is accountable for creating scalable, governed capabilities that can be adopted across multiple value streams, reducing duplication and accelerating value from analytics and AI.

What will you do in this role?

Set the platform vision and roadmap: Define and communicate the strategy, architecture and investment roadmap for reusable data science and AI capabilities, aligned with AXIS’s business priorities, enterprise technology strategy and Data & Analytics operating model.
Build reusable capabilities: Lead the design and development of shared AI services, analytical models, accelerators, agent frameworks, evaluation frameworks, experimentation environments and common solution components that can be adopted across multiple business-aligned solutions.
Enable business-aligned delivery: Partner closely with the Head of Insights & Analytics and value-stream teams to understand recurring needs, translate them into platform priorities and ensure capabilities are practical, discoverable, well documented and easy to adopt.
Lead experimentation and innovation: Create a controlled environment for exploration of emerging analytics, machine learning, generative AI and agentic capabilities. Convert successful experimentation into supported, repeatable enterprise components where there is clear value.
Establish product and platform management: Manage analytics and AI capabilities as products through their full lifecycle, with clear ownership, roadmaps, service expectations, adoption measures, technical health indicators and plans for continuous improvement or retirement.
Lead technical standards and engineering excellence: Establish consistent patterns for development, testing, deployment, integration, monitoring, observability, version control, documentation and reuse. Ensure capabilities are robust, maintainable and designed for enterprise scale.
Drive responsible and governed AI: Partner with Data & AI Governance, Information Risk Management, Legal, Compliance and Technology teams to embed responsible AI, model risk management, security, privacy and regulatory requirements into platform capabilities by design.
Own evaluation and monitoring frameworks: Ensure reusable approaches are in place to evaluate model and agent quality, performance, reliability, safety and value, and to monitor deployed capabilities throughout their lifecycle.
Advance the technology ecosystem: Work closely with Data Platforms & Engineering and Business Technology Solutions to shape and implement the analytics and AI technology stack, integration patterns and deployment pathways across Azure and Databricks.
Build and lead a high-performing specialist team: Lead and develop a multidisciplinary team of data scientists, applied scientists and AI engineers. Set a high bar for technical and academic rigour while fostering collaboration, inclusion, curiosity and pragmatic delivery.
Manage demand, capacity and investment: Prioritise the platform backlog based on enterprise value, reuse potential, risk reduction and strategic fit. Manage resources, budgets, suppliers and delivery commitments transparently.
Champion adoption and reuse: Promote awareness and effective use of shared capabilities, provide technical enablement to delivery teams and actively identify opportunities to consolidate duplicated solutions or patterns

How This Role Works With Insights & Analytics

The Insights & Analytics teams are aligned to business value streams and are accountable for identifying opportunities, defining priorities, designing solutions for each business need, delivering business-aligned solutions and driving adoption and measurable value. The Analytics & AI Platforms team is accountable for the reusable technical capabilities, frameworks, standards and specialist expertise that enable those teams to deliver at greater speed, quality and scale.

Both teams share accountability for successful end-to-end outcomes. The platform team does not become a central delivery queue for every use case, and business-aligned teams should reuse enterprise capabilities wherever practical rather than creating parallel solutions.

Success Measures / Key Outcomes

Reuse and adoption: Shared analytics and AI capabilities are adopted across multiple value streams, with evidence that reuse is reducing duplicated effort and accelerating delivery.
Speed and scalability: Business-aligned teams can move from opportunity to production more quickly because common services, patterns and deployment pathways are available and reliable.
Quality and reliability: Platform capabilities meet agreed standards for performance, availability, maintainability, documentation, monitoring and support.
Responsible delivery: Analytics and AI capabilities operate within AXIS governance, security, privacy, model risk and responsible AI requirements, with effective controls embedded by design.
Business enablement: Capability investments are demonstrably connected to priority business outcomes and enable solutions that are adopted and deliver measurable value.
Technology modernisation: The portfolio evolves in a controlled way to take advantage of relevant advances in data science, machine learning, generative AI and agentic technology.
Team performance: A highly engaged, inclusive and technically strong team with clear accountabilities, effective development pathways and a culture of collaboration and continuous improvement.
Cost and portfolio discipline: Investment is focused on capabilities with enterprise value and reuse potential, with transparent management of cost, technical debt, suppliers and lifecycle decisions.

About You

We encourage you to bring your own experience and expertise to the table. While there are qualifications and experiences we need you to have, we are open to discussing how your individual knowledge may help you fulfil this role and contribute to our goals.

What You Need To Have

Platform and product leadership: Significant experience defining and delivering a platform, product or reusable capability strategy in a complex organisation, with accountability for roadmaps, prioritisation, adoption and lifecycle management.
Technical leadership: Deep experience in data science, machine learning and AI, including generative AI, with the credibility to set technical direction, challenge design decisions and lead senior specialists.
Insurance or financial services experience: Understanding of the data, analytical, regulatory and risk context of insurance or another highly regulated industry.
Enterprise AI engineering: Strong understanding of how analytical models and AI services are developed, evaluated, deployed, monitored and operated at scale, including modern software engineering and MLOps or LLMOps practices.
Cloud and data platforms: Strong knowledge of Azure AI services and Azure Databricks, together with practical understanding of enterprise data architectures, APIs, deployment pipelines and integration patterns.
Responsible AI and risk: Experience embedding governance, security, privacy, controls and responsible AI practices into the design and operation of analytics and AI capabilities.
Strategic and commercial judgement: Ability to balance innovation, speed, enterprise value, cost, risk and technical sustainability when making platform investment and prioritisation decisions.
Collaborative operating style: Demonstrated success working across business-aligned analytics teams, engineering, architecture, technology, governance and senior stakeholders to deliver shared outcomes without relying solely on direct authority.
People leadership: Proven ability to build, lead and develop multidisciplinary technical teams and create a high-performance, inclusive and learning-oriented culture.
Communication and influence: Excellent communication skills, including the ability to explain complex technical concepts, choices and risks clearly to executives, business leaders and delivery teams.
Delivery leadership: Ability to operate in a fast-paced environment, manage multiple priorities and provide clear direction, resource planning, cost oversight and delivery transparency.

What We Prefer You To Have

Relevant technical background: Advanced technical education or equivalent professional experience in data science, computer science, statistics, engineering or a related field.
Enterprise implementation experience: A track record of building reusable analytics or AI platforms and taking generative AI or agentic capabilities from experimentation into governed enterprise use.
Technical depth: Strong working knowledge of Python, Databricks, foundational models, evaluation techniques, retrieval patterns, agent architectures, deployment pipelines and monitoring approaches.

jobs.title: Director, Machine Learning
jobs.description:
Narvar
is Growing! We're looking for a leader to own the machine learning systems behind post-purchase commerce — identity, fraud, and the intelligence layer that agentic AI runs on.

Hundreds of millions of consumers interact with Narvar every year, across 20B+ orders and 1,300+ retail brands. That data powers three systems: Graphite
, our identity resolution engine that ties fragmented consumer data into a single verified identity across retailers; IRIS
, our fraud and returns-abuse detection engine built on top of it.

You'll own the ML organization behind all of it — the models, the platform they run on, and the people who build them. This is a role for someone who wants a system with real consequences: fraud decisions that move retailer margin, identity resolution that agents make automated decisions on, and an adversary on the other side who adapts every quarter.

For this role, you should be located in Canada and able to work within EST/EDT OR PST hours. We are fully remote.

Day-to-day

Own the ML charter across identity resolution, fraud and abuse detection, risk scoring, and consumer intelligence — strategy, roadmap, and delivery
Build and grow a high-performing, globally distributed team of ML engineers; hire, coach, and develop senior ICs and managers
Set the technical bar for how models get built, evaluated, deployed, and monitored — and hold the org to it
Push identity resolution coverage, precision, and profile classification accuracy against a measured, frozen-holdout baseline — not against vibes
Own IRIS model performance end-to-end: detection rate, false-positive rate, label quality, and the feedback loops that keep both honest as fraud patterns shift
Build the ML platform layer — feature stores, training pipelines, model registry, online serving, drift and performance monitoring — so model velocity isn't bottlenecked on infrastructure
Partner with the AI engineering team so identity and risk signals are first-class inputs to NAVI's agent decisions
Work directly with Product, Engineering, Security, and Customer Success to translate messy retailer problems into ML problems worth solving — and to say no to the ones that aren't
Own build-vs-buy and data-partner decisions (third-party identity data, enrichment providers), including the economics
Communicate model performance, risk, and tradeoffs credibly to executives, retailers, and the board

What We're Looking For

We care more about judgment and ownership
than credentials.

You're Likely a Strong Fit If You

Have 12+ years in engineering with 5+ years managing ML or data teams, including managing managers or senior ICs
Are an engineer at heart — you can still read a training pipeline, review a feature spec, and tell when an eval is measuring the wrong thing
Have shipped ML systems that make consequential automated decisions in production, and have owned them after launch — drift, retraining, incidents, and all
Have deep experience with at least one of: entity resolution / identity graphs, fraud and abuse detection, risk scoring, or anomaly detection at scale
Understand what makes ML different from software: labels are noisy and delayed, systems fail silently, offline metrics lie, and last quarter's model is fighting last quarter's adversary
Have opinions about evaluation — precision/recall tradeoffs on heavily imbalanced data, holdout hygiene, feedback loops where the model's own decisions contaminate future labels
Have built or scaled ML infrastructure: feature pipelines, training orchestration, online model serving with real latency budgets, monitoring and alerting
Are fluent in Python and comfortable in a modern data stack (Spark, Airflow or equivalent, streaming, cloud data warehouses — we run on GCP)
Have hired well, retained well, and can point to engineers whose careers got better on your watch
Excel in a fast-paced environment with a flat structure — you set direction by earning trust, not by mandate
Have a BS/MS in computer science, statistics, or an equivalent background

Bonus points

These Aren't Hard Requirements, But Strong Indicators

You've worked on identity resolution or graph systems against third-party consumer data (credit bureau, telecom, or similar), including the matching logic and confidence scoring underneath
You've operated adversarial ML systems where attackers actively adapt to your detection
You've built real-time inference paths where identity or risk has to be resolved inside a request budget
You've worked in retail, payments, fintech, insurance, or marketplace trust & safety
You've partnered closely with LLM/agent teams and understand how structured ML signals ground agentic decisions
You've navigated privacy, consent, and data-governance constraints on consumer identity data
You've done 0→1 — stood up a function, a platform, or a data partnership from nothing
You use modern tooling (including AI-assisted development workflows) to increase leverage, not outsource thinking

Why ML at Narvar?

Because the data is genuinely rare and the problems are genuinely hard.

The dataset is a moat. Cross-retailer visibility across 20B+ orders means we can see coordinated fraud patterns no single retailer can — a returns abuser hitting five brands looks like a good customer at each one.
The problem is adversarial and unsolved. Returns fraud and policy abuse are growing faster than retail itself, and the counterparty adapts. There is no off-the-shelf answer.
The stakes are measurable. Fraud loss, false-positive cost, identity coverage, resolution rate. Not vanity metrics.
It feeds something bigger. As AI shopping agents enter commerce, every agent will need a trust layer for returns, claims, and delivery promises. Identity and risk are that layer — and you'd own it.
The work is greenfield enough to matter. Real-time resolution, cold-start modeling, historical backfill, new data partnerships — these are decisions still being made, not legacy you inherit.

Why Narvar (from an engineer's perspective)?

Real scale, real customers, real consequences
Startup-level ownership with platform-level impact
Teams that value thinking, judgment, and responsibility
Low ego, high trust, and room to do your best work

We're on a mission to simplify the everyday lives of consumers. Post-purchase is a critical phase of the customer journey. That's why we created Narvar - a platform focused on driving customer loyalty through seamless post-purchase experiences that allow retailers to retain, engage, and delight customers. If you've ever bought something online, there's a good chance you've used our platform!

From the hottest new direct-to-consumer companies to retail’s most renowned brands, Narvar works with GameStop, Neiman Marcus, Sonos, Nike, and 1300+ other brands. With hubs in San Francisco, Atlanta, London, and Bangalore, we've served over 125 million consumers worldwide across 10+ billion interactions, 38 countries, and 55 languages.

Pioneering the post-purchase movement means navigating into the unknown. Our team thrives on this sense of adventure while nurturing a mindset of innovation. We're a home for big hearts and we leave our egos at the door. We work hard but we always make time to celebrate professional wins, baby showers, birthday parties, and everything in between.

We are an equal-opportunity employer and value diversity at our company. We do not discriminate on the basis of race, religion, color, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, or disability status.

The range reflects the minimum and maximum target for new hire salaries for the position across Canada. Within the range, individual compensation packages are based on factors unique to each candidate, including but not limited to, skill set, education and certifications, and work location.

jobs.title: Technology Procurement Leader
jobs.description:
Who we need

Reporting to the CFO, illumin
is hiring a Technology Procurement Lead
to own procurement across illumin, with a primary focus on SaaS, software, technology services, hardware, and other corporate vendors. The role will include procurement responsibilities outside of IT .
You will take ownership of the full procurement lifecycle, driving cost optimization and strong commercial outcomes through strategic sourcing, negotiation, vendor consolidation, licence optimization, and disciplined vendor management. As a hands-on individual contributor, you will partner across the organization to strengthen purchasing decisions, secure favourable commercial terms, identify opportunities to reduce unnecessary spend, and ensure illumin receives maximum value from its vendor relationships.

This is a full-time, hybrid position, working in our Toronto office three days per week.

What you bring:

The procurement experience. You have deep procurement experience, including significant exposure to SaaS, software, technology services, and hardware. You have managed procurement activities across the lifecycle, from sourcing and vendor evaluation through negotiation, contracting, renewals, and ongoing vendor management.

The commercial mindset. You have a proven track record of achieving meaningful cost savings and securing strong commercial terms. You know how to identify opportunities for vendor consolidation, licence optimization, and spend reduction, and you are confident leading negotiations that balance cost, value, and business needs.

The technical aptitude. You can quickly understand software, technology services, licensing models, pricing structures, and market alternatives. You are comfortable researching technologies, vendors, and competitors, analyzing your options, and using those insights to strengthen purchasing decisions and negotiations. Experience with ServiceNow Procurement and Sourcing Operations is an asset.

The judgment and initiative. You bring strong analytical, research, and problem-solving skills and can confidently assess options, make recommendations, and move work forward. You are organized and comfortable managing competing priorities, operating independently, and taking ownership of your deliverables.

The interpersonal skills. You are a clear and confident communicator who can build trusted relationships with senior stakeholders and partners across Finance, IT, Security, Legal, HR, Marketing, and other areas of the business. You can understand different priorities, ask thoughtful questions, advocate for strong commercial outcomes, and bring stakeholders together around procurement decisions.

Compensation

At illumin, we believe compensation should be transparent, fair, and reflective of both experience and impact. The salary range for this role is $120,000–$140,000 plus bonus.

Compensation is determined based on skills, experience, and the scope and complexity of the role. We value open conversations about compensation and are happy to discuss our approach at any stage of the hiring process.

What's in it for you

Ownership and impact. You will own procurement across the organization, with a primary focus on SaaS, software, technology services, hardware, and other corporate vendors. You will have the autonomy to research alternatives, negotiate commercial terms, consolidate vendors, optimize licences, and identify meaningful savings. Your work will directly influence how illumin manages technology investments and vendor spend.

Influence and exposure. Reporting directly to the CFO, you will have visibility into procurement priorities and purchasing decisions across the business. You will partner with Finance, IT, Security, Legal, HR, Marketing, and business leaders, bringing your procurement expertise and commercial perspective to decisions that improve cost efficiency and strengthen the value illumin receives from its vendor relationships.

Professional growth. At illumin, we are dedicated to pushing the boundaries to improve and reach our full potential, both as individuals and as a company. You will deepen your expertise in technology procurement while expanding your exposure across the business. You will also have the opportunity to strengthen procurement policies, workflows, controls, and tools, helping shape a more disciplined and scalable approach to procurement.

How you will make an impact:

Own the procurement lifecycle. You will lead procurement from sourcing and vendor evaluation through negotiation, contracting, renewal, and termination, with a primary focus on SaaS, software, technology services, hardware, and other corporate vendors. You will partner with Finance, IT, Security, Legal, HR, Marketing, and business leaders to understand requirements and make informed purchasing decisions.

Drive cost optimization. You will identify and deliver meaningful savings through negotiation, vendor consolidation, licence optimization, and the elimination of unnecessary spend. You will advocate for illumin’s best interests in vendor discussions, securing strong pricing, terms, and commercial outcomes.

Strengthen purchasing decisions. You will research technologies, pricing models, competitors, and market alternatives to inform procurement decisions and strengthen your position in vendor negotiations. You will bring together market insight, spend data, and business requirements to identify opportunities and ensure illumin is getting the right value from its investments.

Manage vendors and contracts. You will oversee contracts, renewals, and vendor performance, ensuring agreements continue to meet business needs and deliver expected value. You will maintain visibility into upcoming renewals, monitor vendor performance, and proactively identify opportunities to renegotiate, consolidate, or make changes.

Improve procurement processes. You will review and strengthen procurement policies, workflows, controls, reporting, and tools, including ServiceNow. You will help create a more disciplined, efficient, and transparent approach to procurement while supporting effective vendor management across the organization.

Who we are

At illumin, we are transforming the advertising landscape. Our platform offers an integrated space for journey planning, execution, and reporting. It empowers marketers to connect with their audiences in powerful ways through real-time data and easy-to-use visual tools. By seamlessly combining media planning and buying in an intuitive interface, marketers can take complete control of their campaigns, meeting customers wherever they are in the buying journey and maximizing the impact of their ad spend through personalized insights for smarter decision-making.

We are at a pivotal moment, evolving into a product-led company with a team of over 100 skilled professionals and new leadership guiding our path forward. By harnessing the power of data, advancing our AI capabilities, and deeply investing in our people, we are preparing for a future that will redefine what’s possible in journey advertising.

Our work is guided by two beliefs: that the ability to execute is paramount to success and that we are only as good as our people. As we grow and transform, we are looking for team members (illumineers) who share our bias for speed, delivery over perfection, and an entrepreneurial mindset. Joining us now is a chance to be part of our transformation.

What else should you know about us?

We are undergoing a transformative shift. We are embracing change and the opportunities that come with it, empowering every illumineer to innovate, experiment, and bring forward new ideas. Whether accessing new technology, restructuring workflows, or expanding your team, you will have full support if you can make the business case.

We are a broad and diverse team, but we all share a passion for success, a drive to do more, and a love of creating connections. We hire for talent and commitment and provide the guidelines and guidance to elevate skills, knowledge, and abilities across all areas. This is a place where proven methods meet bold ideas, offering opportunities to grow personally and professionally.

To support a healthy work-life balance, we offer a flexible work environment, a meal credit for your in-office days, and a free massage with an RMT in-house every eight weeks. That is in addition to our comprehensive benefits, which include life, AD&D, long-term disability insurance, and coverage for prescriptions, dental, vision, mental health, and professional health services. You will also have access to a workplace advisor, the Vitality Wellness app, and a $300 annual healthcare spending account.

Apply now

If you want to seize the opportunity to impact a company and influence an industry, and you have 70% of what we are looking for, apply now. We can't promise an interview, but we will consider your whole application.

What you can expect from our interview process:

A virtual interview with a Talent Advisor to discuss your interest in the role, your background, and what you are looking for in your next opportunity. The conversation will be recorded using BrightHire, an AI-powered interview platform. More details will be shared when you are invited to interview.

An in-person interview with the COO. This will be an opportunity to discuss illumin’s business priorities, growth strategy, and the role procurement plays in supporting the organization. You will have the opportunity to share how your experience and approach can contribute to strong commercial outcomes and cost optimization, while learning more about the broader business.

A final interview with the Hiring Manager. You will have the opportunity to discuss your experience leading procurement initiatives, managing technology vendors, driving cost savings, and negotiating commercial agreements. You will also learn more about the priorities and expectations of the role and have time to ask any remaining questions.

jobs.description:
With millions of diners, 70,000+ restaurant partners and 25+ years of experience, OpenTable, part of Booking Holdings, Inc. (NASDAQ: BKNG), is an industry leader with a passion for helping restaurants thrive. Our world-class technology empowers restaurants to focus on what matters most – their team, their guests, and their bottom line – while enabling diners to discover and book the perfect restaurant for every occasion.

Every employee at OpenTable has a tangible impact on what we do and how we do it. You’ll also be part of a global team and its portfolio of metasearch brands. Hospitality is all about taking care of others, and it defines our culture.

About The Job

OpenTable is seeking a strategic and operationally-minded Director of FP&A to lead financial planning, forecasting, and analysis for our core operational investments. Located in our Toronto office, this role will have primary ownership over the company’s Operating Expenses (OpEx), Capital Expenditures (CapEx), and Commissions modeling and structures. Reporting to the VP, FP&A, you will act as a key business partner to departmental heads, ensuring disciplined resource allocation, optimization of capital investments, and the implementation of commission plans that align with corporate growth objectives. This posting is for an existing vacancy.

Responsibilities

OpEx Management & Forecasting: Lead the annual budgeting and monthly forecasting processes for global operating expenses. Partner with department heads ( tech, sales, marketing, G&A) to track spend, analyze variances, and identify cost-efficiency opportunities.
CapEx Planning & Governance: Oversee the evaluation, tracking, and prioritization of capital expenditures. Develop robust ROI models for major technology, infrastructure, and facilities investments to guide executive decision-making.
Commissions Oversight: Own the financial oversight of the commission program. Partner with Sales Operations to ensure commission plans are accurate and effective.
Business Partnership: Serve as a trusted financial advisor to operational leadership, translating complex financial data into actionable insights that drive strategic initiatives.
Management Reporting: Deliver clear monthly and quarterly financial review packages focusing on spend efficiency, capital deployment, and incentive plan effectiveness for senior leadership.
Process & Systems Improvement: Continuously scale and automate FP&A processes, particularly around expense tracking and commission calculations, to support organizational growth.

Qualifications

Experience: 7–10 years of progressive experience in corporate finance, FP&A, or strategic finance, with a strong emphasis on expense management, capital budgeting, and sales compensation finance.
Leadership: Demonstrated experience managing professional finance team members and leading cross-functional projects.
Analytical Skills: Advanced financial modeling skills (Excel/Google Sheets) and experience handling large datasets. Proficiency with financial planning tools, ERP software, and commission management platforms (e.g., CaptivateIQ).
Communication: Strong ability to influence and build partnerships with non-finance executives by presenting financial concepts clearly and concisely.
Education: Bachelor’s degree in Finance, Accounting, Economics, or a related quantitative field.

Benefits and Perks

Work from (almost) anywhere for up to 20 days per year
Focus on mental health and well-being:
Company-paid therapy sessions through SpringHealth
Company-paid subscription to Headspace
Annual company-wide week off a year - the whole team fully recharges (and returns without a pile-up of work!)

Paid parental leave
Generous paid vacation + time off for your birthday
Paid volunteer time
Focus on your career growth:
Development Dollars
Leadership development
Access to thousands of on-demand e-learnings

Travel Discounts
Employee Resource Groups
20 days of paid time off
Private health and dental insurance
Life and Disability insurance

The best connections happen face-to-face, whether you’re sitting down to dinner or having coffee with a coworker. That’s why OpenTable has adopted a hybrid workplace model. This role aligns with that approach, with an expectation of coming into the office two days a week—giving employees the best of both worlds: in-person collaboration and flexibility.

We offer a competitive base salary and benefits including: health benefits; flexible spending account; retirement benefits; life insurance; paid time off (including PTO, paid sick leave, medical leave, bereavement leave, floating holidays and paid holidays); and parental leave benefits. This role is eligible to be considered for an annual bonus and equity grant.

Work Environment & Flexibility

At OpenTable, we pride ourselves on fostering a global and dynamic work environment. As a team member with us, you will benefit from a schedule tailored to accommodate a global workforce operating across multiple time zones. While the majority of your responsibilities may align with conventional business hours, there will be instances where you are expected to manage communications - via calls, Slack messages, or emails - outside of regular working hours to effectively collaborate with international colleagues, respond to restaurant partners, and/or address urgent matters. OpenTable will always abide by and consider local laws and regulations.

Inclusion

We’re committed to creating a workplace where everyone feels they belong and can thrive. We know the best ideas come when we bring different voices to the table, so we're building a team as dynamic as the diners and restaurants we serve—and fostering a culture where everyone feels welcome to be themselves.

jobs.title: Senior Director, Product Management - Agentic Platform (Tax & Trade)
jobs.description:
We are seeking an exceptional Senior Director, Product Management to shape the future of the Agentic Platform for Tax and Trade, one of Thomson Reuters’ most strategically important AI-first product portfolios, spanning ONESOURCE and our Transactional Compliance, Tax and Trade products.

Join the Transactional Compliance Product team as we build the next generation of AI-first, agentic experiences for tax, trade, and compliance professionals. We are looking for a curious, commercially astute, and technically fluent product leader who thrives on turning complex customer problems, market opportunities, and technology shifts into elegant, scalable, and commercially successful solutions.

Job Description

In this pivotal leadership role, you will own the Agentic Platform for the Tax and Trade portfolio: the shared foundation that product teams across ONESOURCE use to build, orchestrate, govern, and scale AI agents. You will define the platform’s product vision and strategy, set its roadmap and standards, and deliver the shared capabilities that let our product lines move faster and more safely in the agentic era, in service of our vision to meet customers at the intersection of commerce and compliance.

You will partner closely with Product-line VP's, treating each product line as a primary customer of the platform, and aligning on priorities, dependencies, and shared investments across the portfolio. You will also partner with Engineering, TR Labs, Data, Security, Compliance, Design, Product Marketing, Sales, and Commercial teams.

This role requires a proven product leader with a track record of delivering AI, agentic, automation, workflow, or platform products at scale in B2B SaaS. You will bring strong commercial judgment, deep customer orientation, and technical credibility with engineering and AI/ML teams, along with the ability to influence and align senior stakeholders across a matrixed global organization.

Scope

You will report to the Head of Product Management for Tax and Trade and sit on the product line leadership team.

Key Responsibilities

Platform Vision & Strategy

Define and evangelize a long-term vision and strategy for the Agentic Platform, aligned with Thomson Reuters’ broader AI, product, and business strategy.
Own the platform roadmap, covering orchestration, agent memory, tool and integration frameworks (including MCP), identity and permissions, and governance, balancing near-term product line needs with long-term differentiation.
Establish clear plans for functional and agentic AI across a broad ecosystem of technologies and partners.
Sponsor market research, competitive analysis, and customer discovery to identify unmet needs and opportunities for differentiation.

Cross-Portfolio Alignment & Delivery

Establish a single platform roadmap and dependency model, with shared priorities that balance platform investment against each product line’s commitments.
Partner with product-line VPs to understand their needs, set shared priorities, and resolve trade-offs, working to align interests and implement scalable solutions.
Treat the platform as a product: define the developer experience, APIs, and service levels for product teams building agents on it.
Establish agent evaluation and quality standards (accuracy, explainability, safety, and regression testing) that product teams adopt as release gates.
Own unit economics for agentic workloads, including token consumption, cost to serve, and consumption-based pricing and packaging, in partnership with product-line VPs and Finance.
Establish governance and human-in-the-loop controls for regulated tax, trade, and compliance workflows, ensuring experiences are trusted, explainable, secure, and reliable.
Define success metrics covering platform adoption, reliability, developer satisfaction, cost efficiency, and business impact, and use them to guide investment decisions.

Leadership & Influence

Build, lead, and mentor the platform product management team, fostering accountability, customer obsession, and commercial discipline.
Socialize and align senior stakeholders to platform strategy and roadmap, and evangelize the vision across the organization.
Be a recognized thought leader inside and outside the organization, writing, blogging, and speaking at events on agentic platforms and AI in tax, trade, and compliance.

Required Qualifications

Curious and innovative, with an obsession for customers’ problems and needs, and a drive to solve them in unique ways.
Agile, with a strong sense of urgency and comfort leading in fast-paced, ambiguous environments. You are unafraid of failure and learn quickly from setbacks.
An effective communicator who projects confidence and communicates concisely and clearly to executives, peers, customers, and partners.
Experience: 10+ years of product management experience, including 5+ years in a senior leadership role managing platform, multiple product lines, or teams in B2B SaaS, workflow, data, AI, or enterprise software.
Working fluency with agent tooling and protocols such as MCP, model evaluation, data quality, and LLM cost drivers, along with responsible AI considerations.
Hands-on, daily user of frontier AI tools, with a current, practical understanding of what agentic systems can and cannot do, and comfortable prototyping with agentic tools.
Strong commercial acumen, with a track record of driving measurable outcomes through monetization, packaging, pricing, adoption, and retention.

jobs.title: Director of Platform Engineering
jobs.description:
Blackpoint Cyber is the leading provider of world-class cybersecurity threat hunting, detection and remediation technology. Founded by former National Security Agency (NSA) cyber operations experts who applied their learnings to bring national security-grade technology solutions to commercial customers around the world, Blackpoint Cyber is in hyper-growth mode, fueled by a recent $190m series C round.

Company Culture

At Blackpoint Cyber, we value high-quality execution, ownership, and strong morals. Our principles are never tested, and we are proud to always do right by our customers. We are an energetic and collaborative team that maintains a high-performance culture and enables growth by overcoming challenges in the modern cyber threat landscape. If you are a driven professional with a passion for learning and contributing at a high level, Blackpoint Cyber welcomes you.

Position Overview

Blackpoint Cyber is seeking a strategic and visionary Director of Platform Engineering to lead the development and execution of its Unified Security Posture data platform, which powers the company’s data-centric cybersecurity solutions. This leader will serve as the single-threaded owner for the roadmap and operations of the cloud-based platform, including vendor integrations, developer and data tooling, identity, authentication, tenant management, and other core services.

This role will drive vision and execution across multiple engineering teams, working cross-functionally with internal stakeholders, product leaders, and site reliability engineering partners. The Director of Platform Engineering will translate business and technical needs into clear strategies, oversee roadmap execution and service quality, and build a high-performing organization through strong hiring, mentorship, and technical leadership. As a highly visible leader, this person will also help establish company-wide operational excellence practices for instrumentation, incident response, root cause analysis, and remediation.

Key Responsibilities

Define and drive the platform roadmap aligned with product and business goals.
Partner across the Product organization and SRE team to ensure platform security, reliability, and scalability.
Lead the development of the data pipeline, integrating with Blackpoint’s endpoint agent and vendor data, including storage, tiered access, and query capabilities.
Deliver platform services and public APIs supporting core functions such as tenant management, identity, and role-based access control.
Lead platform tooling and APIs that accelerate AI/ML and business intelligence initiatives.
Oversee developer productivity tooling, including CI/CD systems.
Define the long-term vision for the data platform by implementing best practices in data architecture, modeling, and governance, while staying current on emerging technologies and trends.
Build strong relationships with internal stakeholders and partners.
Foster excellence in platform reliability, scalability, security, and software quality.
Hire, develop, and grow a high-caliber team of platform and data engineers, scaling the team and organizational structure as needed.
Drive the adoption of AI across the development lifecycle (AI DLC) to increase engineering productivity, accelerate delivery, improve software quality, and enable teams to build and deliver high-quality products more efficiently

Qualifications

15+ years of experience in software development, preferably in cybersecurity, including at least 5 years of people management experience leading multiple teams.
Proven experience leading a Platform Engineering function at the Director level.
5+ years of experience working with large-scale AWS cloud solutions and technologies such as Postgres, Elastic, Redis, streaming data platforms, and ETL processes.
Hands-on experience architecting and building complex data platforms and service integrations.
Deep knowledge of CI/CD, production deployment at scale, and data pipeline orchestration.
Demonstrated ability to drive high-impact initiatives and long-term strategic goals.
Strong leadership, communication, and cross-functional collaboration skills.
B.S. or M.S. in Computer Science, Engineering, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience.

Why Join Blackpoint Cyber

If you are passionate about cybersecurity and have a proven track record of leading and managing software engineering teams, we encourage you to apply for this exciting opportunity. Blackpoint Cyber offers competitive compensation, comprehensive benefits, and a dynamic work environment where you can make a real impact in the field of cybersecurity.

Blackpoint Cyber welcomes and encourages applications from qualified individuals of all races, colors, religions, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, national origin, age, marital status, or any other legally protected status. We are committed to equality of opportunity in all aspects of employment.

For eligible employees in the US, Blackpoint offers competitive Health, Vision, Dental, and Life Insurance plans, a robust 401k plan, Discretionary Time Off, and other minor perks. International employees receive competitive benefits in accordance with local market standards and applicable country requirements.

Blackpoint believes all employees should share in the company’s success – equity participation is available to employees globally, with program details varying by location and employment structure.

Nova Scotia is rich in natural resources - including biodiversity, forests, geological resources, provincial parks and the land we manage. The Department of Natural Resources is responsible for the development, management, conversation and protection of forest, mineral, parks and wildlife resources and the administration of the province's crown land. Together, we are working with Nova Scotians to build a better future through sustainable natural resource management as we all benefit from the natural health and wealth of the province.

About Our Opportunity

As Director, Strategic Policy and Planning, you provide leadership in facilitating appropriate linkages between policy, program and delivery structures, and developing new inclusive approaches which will generate greater collective knowledge and enhance capacity for integrated, collaborative policy planning, legislative and regulatory development.

In addition, you provide strategic direction and oversight for the research, design, planning, implementation, monitoring and evaluation of department strategies and initiatives.

Further, you are responsible for directing a team of policy professionals, including maintaining appropriate relationships with central agencies (ECO, OSE, FTB), and directing and ensuring the quality of DNR and DOE submissions to Executive Council.

Primary Accountabilities

Lead and develop an effective, coordinated strategic planning infrastructure with associated policy, planning and regulatory management processes, change management, standards and guidelines for DNR/DOE.
Lead policy/planning initiatives, with an emphasis on those related to key natural resource and energy strategies.
Provide broad oversight for environmental scanning and analyses to monitor trends, identify gaps and risks in internal planning activities and to inform and stimulate discussion about future strategic directions and opportunities that might affect policy and planning decisions.
Provide oversight for the development and coordination of legislative planning and response during the Legislative Sessions of the House.
Oversee and directs the development of departmental Memos to Executive Council, R&Rs, legislative requests, Briefing Books, and all Committee appearances for DNR and DOE.
Provide a planned approach to increase internal capacity and build and sustain required skill sets of the team to meet current and future needs, ensuring the policy and planning team are properly resourced, motivated, empowered and have access to opportunities for growth and development.

You are an innovative policy leader with an educational background in policy development and administration (e.g. Public Administration) and have progressive senior leadership experience in a related field.

The opportunity

Are you motivated by the chance to help ensure all young people in Canada can access mental health support and Feel Out Loud? Kids Help Phone (KHP) is Canada’s Unlock The Hope Youth Charity. We’re the first and Canada's only national 24/7, free, confidential, and multilingual e-mental health service for youth and a global leader in innovation for youth and their well-being.

The Senior Director, Data Governance and Management leads Kids Help Phone’s enterprise data strategy, governance, and management functions, ensuring data is governed, protected, and leveraged as a strategic asset. Reporting to the EVP, Technology & Data, this role is accountable for data governance, quality, stewardship, architecture, analytics governance, lifecycle management, responsible data use, and AI readiness.

Working across leadership, clinical services, research, privacy, legal, and operational teams, the Senior Director establishes enterprise standards, drives the evolution of KHP’s Data Operating Model, and strengthens organizational data capabilities. The role provides strategic leadership on data-related risks, opportunities, and investments, ensuring data practices support organizational goals, innovation, service excellence, and the trust of youth seeking support. It’ll take courage, collaboration, innovation, resilience and trust. If you’re interested in transforming e-mental health solutions with KHP, you can explore this opportunity today!

The responsibilities

Enterprise Data Strategy:

Develop and lead KHP’s enterprise data strategy and multi-year roadmap, aligning data, analytics, and AI capabilities with organizational priorities.

Define the vision for data governance, architecture, quality, accessibility, and responsible AI adoption.

Advise senior leadership on emerging trends, opportunities, risks, and investments related to data and AI.

Enterprise Leadership & Decision Authority:

Serve as the organization’s senior leader for data governance and management.

Establish enterprise data standards, accountability frameworks, and governance requirements.

Provide strategic guidance on data-related risks, investments, priorities, and key organizational decisions.

Resolve complex, cross-functional issues related to data ownership, quality, metrics, and reporting.

Data Governance & Operating Model:

Lead and evolve KHP’s Data Operating Model, governance frameworks, and enterprise-wide adoption.

Establish clear roles, responsibilities, and decision-making processes for data governance and stewardship.

Identify and mitigate emerging data, technology, and AI-related risks.

Drive KHP’s data transformation journey, advancing organizational data maturity and governance capabilities.

Data Ownership & Stewardship:

Lead the enterprise data stewardship program across business and service areas.

Define stewardship practices, training, and accountability expectations.

Resolve cross-functional issues related to data ownership, quality, access, lifecycle management, and reporting.

Data Quality, Metrics & Analytics:

Oversee data quality, reporting, business intelligence, and analytics governance.

Establish standards for critical data elements, business definitions, metrics, and reporting consistency.

Advance data and analytics capabilities to support evidence-based decision-making and innovation.

Oversee internal staff and external vendor support for ongoing development, optimization, and maintenance of data infrastructure and pipelines

Data Sources, Lifecycle & Responsible Use:

Define governance requirements for data sourcing, retention, lifecycle management, and responsible use.

Support governance processes for research, data sharing, analytics, AI-enabled initiatives, and regulatory compliance.

Ensure data practices align with privacy, security, legal, and ethical standards.

Governance, Adoption & Organizational Capability:

Chair enterprise data governance and stewardship forums and drive accountability across the organization.

Monitor adoption of governance practices and report on key risks, outcomes, and performance measures.

Lead stakeholder engagement, communications, and training to strengthen enterprise data literacy and capability.

Provide leadership and oversight for data governance programs, priorities, resources, and investments.

The qualifications

Minimum 12 years of progressively senior experience in data governance, data management, analytics, information management or related enterprise data disciplines, including significant experience in senior leadership roles with enterprise-wide accountability. 

Demonstrated leadership experience overseeing complex data, governance or operating-model transformation programs and leading program or project delivery professionals. 

Demonstrated experience designing or operationalizing a data governance framework, stewardship model, decision-rights model or enterprise data standards. 

Strong understanding of data ownership, stewardship, data definitions, data quality, metadata, lineage, lifecycle and metric governance. 

Experience optimizing and modernizing data architecture to enhance reliability, consistency and availability of data to end users. 

Demonstrated experience leading leaders and multidisciplinary teams, including establishing functional strategy, organizational capabilities, performance expectations and succession plans. 

Experience facilitating cross-functional decisions where business, technology, privacy, legal, risk and operational perspectives must be reconciled. 

Experience advising executives and senior governance bodies on complex data strategy, risk, investment and organizational decisions. 

Experience overseeing significant vendor relationships, technology investments and/or enterprise transformation budgets. 

Strong understanding of modern data platforms, cloud data architecture, analytics and BI ecosystems, including platforms such as Power BI and Databricks, and the governance implications of emerging AI capabilities. 

Ability to convert complex governance, risk and technical requirements into practical roles, standards, workflows and decision tools. 

Strong written communication, facilitation, stakeholder management and executive presentation skills. 

Sound judgement when working with sensitive information, ambiguity and competing organizational priorities. 

University degree in data/information management, computer science, information systems, business, engineering, health informatics or a related discipline, or an equivalent combination of advanced professional experience and education. Graduate-level education is an asset. 

Preferred / Advantageous

Status: Permanent, Full time
Salary: $300-350k base salary, unlimited vacation, bonus and health benefits

Our client is a global insur-tech company focused on embedded insurance and protection solutions. Its technology enables insurers and other businesses to integrate insurance products directly into their existing customer journeys, making it easier to quote, purchase, manage and service coverage through digital channels. The company has built a significant international footprint, with operation in 35 markets across the world. Right now, they are expanding and building a team in Canada.

The Chief Technical Product Officer is responsible for defining and executing the company's product and technology strategy, ensuring our products, platforms, architecture, and engineering capabilities support our long-term business and growth objectives.
This executive will bring together Product, Engineering, Technology, Architecture, Data and AI
under a cohesive strategy, creating clear accountability from product vision through technical execution and delivery.

The CTPO will balance innovation with disciplined execution, ensuring we build scalable, secure, reliable, and commercially successful solutions that solve meaningful customer and partner needs.

Responsibilities:
Own the US product and technology strategy
, translating the US business strategy into a clear product, technology and investment roadmap, with AI embedded throughout.
Own the end-to-end US product portfolio
, from product vision and prioritization through build, launch, adoption and continuous improvement, using AI to accelerate the product lifecycle.
Lead the US technology organization
, including engineering, architecture, platforms, QA/testing and technical delivery, driving an agentic AI-first coding transformation
that fundamentally changes how software is designed, built, tested and delivered.
Create one integrated Product + Tech operating model
, with clear accountability, faster decision-making and materially shorter cycles from idea to production.
Own the US platform and architecture roadmap
, building a scalable, modern architecture that is API- and MCP-enabled
, allowing bolt capabilities, data and services to be readily consumed by both traditional applications and AI agents.
Own technology reliability, security and performance
, increasingly applying AI and automation across testing, observability, release management, incident prevention and remediation.
Build a high-performing, AI-native Product + Tech organization
, including organization design, leadership, talent strategy, location strategy, capabilities and new ways of working.
Own Product + Tech investment and resource allocation
, balancing strategic priorities, platform modernization, AI transformation, technical debt, delivery capacity and operating cost.

The successful CTPO will:
Establish a clear and commercially focused product and technology strategy
.
Create stronger alignment between Product, Engineering, Commercial, Operations, and other functions.
Improve speed, quality, and predictability of product delivery
while maintaining appropriate technology and security standards.
Increase adoption and measurable business impact from product investments.
Simplify the technology landscape and reduce unnecessary complexity and technical debt.
Establish AI and data as meaningful business capabilities rather than standalone initiatives.
Build a strong, accountable leadership team with clear ownership across Product and Technology.

Qualifications:
10+ years in senior Product and/or Technology leadership
, ideally with significant responsibility across both disciplines.
Hands-on understanding of modern AI-enabled software development
, including agentic coding, AI coding agents and AI-assisted SDLC, with experience driving meaningful improvements in engineering productivity.
Strong product management discipline
, with demonstrated ability to set product vision and strategy, understand customer and market needs, make prioritization decisions and manage a product portfolio.
Track record of transforming engineering productivity and ways of working
, including development practices, testing, CI/CD, automation and operating models.
Strong modern architecture background
, particularly APIs, MCP, cloud-native platforms and architectures designed for interaction with AI agents.
Proven team and organizational leadership
, with experience building high-performing Product and Technology teams, developing strong leaders, attracting talent and creating a culture of ownership, pace and accountability.
Strong technical credibility
, able to challenge architecture decisions, understand engineering trade-offs and engage deeply with senior engineers.

Leadership Profile

The ideal candidate is:
Strategic but operational:
Able to establish a long-term vision while maintaining accountability for delivery.
Commercially minded:
Evaluates product and technology decisions through the lens of customer and business value.
Technically credible:
Able to challenge architectural and engineering decisions without needing to be the organization's principal engineer.
Product-led:
Starts with customer and market problems rather than technology solutions.
Data-driven:
Uses measurable outcomes to determine priorities and evaluate success.
Transformational:
Comfortable simplifying organizations, platforms, processes, and portfolios when necessary.
Collaborative:
Builds strong partnerships across Commercial, Operations, Finance, People, and other functions.

jobs.title: Director, Business Intelligence
jobs.description:
At Viral Nation,
we specialize in building social-first ecosystems for brands to connect with the modern consumer journey. Our integrated solutions align strategy, talent, media, and technology with culturally relevant creativity to scale the world’s fastest-growing digital brands. Viral Nation offers a fluid, creative, and growth-oriented environment that will support your ambitions to apply your talents in an open, collaborative, and fast-paced culture. Our ability to stay at the forefront of the industry has fuelled our success and will guide us in paving the path forward. We’re driven to push boundaries and think beyond today to deliver strategies, and we’re just getting started.

While we continuously exceed our goals, we need your help – our success is only as great as our people. Strong performance leads to high expectations, and we must keep raising the bar!

The Director, Business Intelligence will lead enterprise-wide analytics strategy and will be responsible for building and leading a high-performing team of analysts delivering actionable insights across sales forecasting, retail performance, campaign measurement, and influencer/paid/social strategy optimization.

This leader will serve as a strategic thought partner to Sales, Marketing, Brand, eCommerce, Finance, and Executive Leadership, translating data into commercial growth opportunities, driving ROI, and embedding analytics into core business decision-making. The role combines strategic vision, technical depth, cross-functional leadership, and team development.

Responsibilities:

Act as a senior analytics partner to client account, strategy, and service teams by translating client objectives into scalable, best-in-class measurement frameworks that support social-first marketing performance.
Serve as the senior analytics advisor to executive leadership, shaping marketing, retail, and social investment decisions through data-driven insights.
Elevate analytics from reporting to strategic advantage by synthesizing data into clear narratives that inform brand positioning, channel strategy, and enterprise decision-making.
Own end-to-end measurement strategy across paid media, influencer, social, and retail media, ensuring clear linkage between investment and revenue outcomes.
Forecast and quantify incremental revenue and retail lift across eCommerce and offline retail partners by developing predictive models that connect media spend, influencer engagement, and social performance to sales velocity and conversion.
Design and operationalize robust ROI frameworks, including brand lift studies, sales lift studies, incrementality testing, multi-touch attribution, and marketing mix modeling, translating insights into optimized channel mix and budget allocation.
Build scalable measurement systems to evaluate influencer effectiveness, content performance, audience growth, and conversion impact, informing creative strategy and platform optimization.
Identify emerging consumer and digital engagement trends to inform brand strategy, innovation, and go-to-market planning.
Build, lead, and mentor a high-performing analytics team, fostering a culture of analytical rigor, commercial acumen, and executive-ready storytelling.
Design and oversee scalable data collection and reporting infrastructure, including structured databases, automated reporting workflows, dashboards, and standardized presentations.

Qualifications:

Extensive experience in marketing, media, or agency environments, with demonstrated ability to apply analytics and research to drive client strategy and business outcomes.
Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in a relevant field (Social Sciences, Statistics, Data Science, Business Analytics, or related discipline), or equivalent practical experience.
12+ years of progressive experience in research, analytics, and measurement, with a proven track record of leading complex, high-impact initiatives.
Advanced expertise in primary and secondary research methodologies, including brand tracking, brand and communications strategy, brand lift studies, regression analysis, Market Mix Modeling, social listening, and digital and site analytics.
Deep technical proficiency in analytics and BI technologies, including Python and SQL for analysis and data modeling, Google Cloud Platform, BigQuery, and Snowflake for data infrastructure, and BI tools such as Sigma or comparable platforms for scalable reporting and dashboarding.
Demonstrated ability to architect and optimize analytics workflows, data pipelines, and reporting systems that support automation, scalability, and self-serve insights.
Strong executive-level communication and collaboration skills, with the ability to translate complex analytical findings into clear, actionable recommendations for both technical and non-technical stakeholders.
Proven ability to influence cross-functional teams and senior client stakeholders, providing strategic guidance grounded in data, research rigor, and business context.

This role has an annual salary range of $140,000 - $160,000.

This range reflects the full scope and progression of the role, from building capability to operating with sustained impact at a higher level. In addition to base salary, we offer a comprehensive benefits and total rewards package designed to support our team as they grow with us.

Where an offer falls within this range is determined through the interview process. Candidates are benchmarked by the hiring team based on role scope, relevant experience, skill alignment, and expected impact, using consistent and objective criteria.

Compensation Philosophy:

At Viral Nation, compensation is structured, performance-led, and market-aligned. Pay decisions are intentional, based on role requirements, performance, and market alignment by country, and are set to maintain internal pay equity across comparable roles and levels.

Compensation progression is tied to demonstrated performance, expanded scope, and sustained contribution over time, not tenure alone. Employee compensation is reviewed regularly through formal performance reviews and check-ins to ensure alignment with role expectations and impact.

AI in Recruitment:

Viral Nation does not use AI-enabled tools to screen, assess, rank, or select candidates – our hiring teams make all hiring decisions. AI note-taking tools may be used during interviews.

DEI Commitment:

Viral Nation is committed to diversity, equity and inclusion in our agency. Viral Nation welcomes applications from people with visible and non-visible disabilities. Accommodations are available on request for candidates taking part in all aspects of the recruiting and selection process.

A core aspect of this role is to partner closely with cross-functional stakeholders to align business requirements with system capabilities, manage complex integrations across HRIS, finance, time, and third-party platforms, and ensure the successful execution of payroll transformation objectives.

Is this role right for you? In this role, you will:

Lead end-to-end payroll transformation initiatives, including solution design, system configuration, testing, deployment, and stabilization activities.
Drive payroll testing and validation efforts, including user acceptance testing (UAT), parallel payroll runs, reconciliation, and issue resolution to ensure system accuracy and readiness.
Oversee system integration across HR, Finance, time, and third-party platforms to enable seamless data flow and end-to-end payroll processing.
Partner with HR, Technology, Finance, and external vendors to align system requirements, manage dependencies, and deliver transformation outcomes.
Ensure compliance with regulatory, audit, and governance requirements related to payroll processing, data integrity, and financial reporting.
Lead cross-functional workstreams and collaborate with program stakeholders to ensure delivery against timelines, scope, and quality expectations.
Support continuous improvement efforts by identifying opportunities to enhance payroll processes, systems, and overall operational efficiency.
Build and maintain strong relationships across stakeholders, fostering alignment, accountability, and effective communication throughout the transformation lifecycle.
Create an environment that promotes effective and efficient operations, ensuring alignment with Scotiabank’s Values and Code of Conduct, and supporting strong governance and control practices.

Skills

Post-secondary education in Human Resources, Business, Technology, or a related field; relevant SAP or payroll certifications are considered an asset.
Progressive experience in payroll transformation, HR technology implementation, or enterprise system delivery within complex, large-scale environments.
Strong understanding of SAP HCM Payroll and/or SuccessFactors Employee Central Payroll, including system configuration, testing methodologies, and payroll operations.
Demonstrated experience supporting end-to-end payroll implementation, including design, UAT, parallel runs, and post-go-live stabilization.
Experience working across HR, Technology, Finance, and vendor partners, with the ability to translate business requirements into system functionality.
Strong project and program management skills, with the ability to manage multiple priorities and deliver within tight timelines.
Excellent stakeholder management, communication, and influencing skills, with the ability to engage senior leaders and cross-functional teams.
High attention to detail and a strong focus on accuracy, data integrity, and risk mitigation within payroll environments.

Strong leadership capability with a focus on collaboration, accountability, and continuous improvement.
