jobs.description:
Position Description

Artificial Intelligence is reshaping every industry, transforming how organizations operate, innovate, and create value. But organizations aren't looking for more technology. They're looking for trusted advisors who can help them modernize operations, transform how work gets done, and realize measurable business outcomes.

At CGI, we're building on decades of consulting excellence, proven AI capabilities, and global innovation to help clients navigate this transformation. We're looking for a business consulting leader who can help expand that capability while influencing how we continue to bring AI enabled business transformation to market.

As Canada's largest IT and business consulting services firm, and a global leader with more than 400 offices worldwide, CGI combines the entrepreneurial spirit of a local business with the strength, scale, and expertise of a global organization. We call our employees Partners for a reason: 90% are shareholders who take ownership of our success. Here, you'll have the autonomy to influence strategy, the resources to make an impact, and the opportunity to help shape the future of consulting.

Your Role: Lead Transformation. Shape Strategy. Enable Growth.

As a Director Consulting, Business Transformation & AI, you'll serve as a senior business transformation consultant and trusted advisor, helping organizations understand how AI can create practical, measurable business value and realize sustainable value from their AI investments.

Working alongside CGI's Directors of Consulting Services, you'll bring deep expertise in business transformation and AI to strengthen client relationships, shape strategic opportunities, and guide organizations through complex transformation initiatives. Rather than owning client accounts, you'll complement our account leaders by helping clients develop transformation strategies, modernize business processes, and accelerate responsible AI adoption.

You'll also help shape the continued evolution of CGI's Business Transformation & AI consulting capabilities across the Atlantic Business Unit. Building on CGI's established consulting practice, global AI expertise, and proven client success, you'll have the opportunity to influence our strategy, evolve consulting offerings, strengthen our market presence, and help define how we continue delivering AI enabled transformation for our clients.

You'll collaborate closely with CGI's technical AI specialists, architects, and delivery teams, serving as the bridge between client business objectives and successful implementation.

If you're passionate about business transformation, executive advisory services, emerging technologies, and helping organizations prepare for what's next, we'd love to hear from you.

Your future duties and responsibilities

Client Leadership & Strategic Advisory

Serve as a trusted advisor to client stakeholders, business leaders, technology leaders, and executives on business transformation, AI adoption, and digital modernization.
Lead executive workshops that help organizations define transformation priorities, AI strategies, investment roadmaps, and measurable business outcomes.
Advise clients on operating model redesign, organizational change, Responsible AI, governance, and workforce transformation.
Build trusted relationships with key client stakeholders, decision makers, and influencers, strengthening CGI's position as a trusted transformation partner.

Opportunity Shaping & Business Development

Provide business transformation and AI expertise that strengthens client relationships and shapes strategic opportunities.
Support executive presentations, discovery workshops, proposals, business cases, and transformation roadmaps.
Collaborate across CGI consulting, engineering, cloud, cybersecurity, data, and account and delivery teams to recommend and shape integrated client solutions.
Bring innovative thinking, market insight, and consulting expertise to strategic pursuits and client engagements.

Practice Leadership & Thought Leadership

Help shape and evolve CGI's Business Transformation & AI consulting capabilities across the Atlantic Business Unit.

jobs.description:
BoomerangFX

Location:
Mississauga, Ontario — on-site, five days per week
Reports to:
Chief Executive Officer

Mandatory Experience

A Canadian CPA designation and hands-on experience leading finance and operations for a PE-backed SaaS company scaling ARR from $5 million to $50 million.

Why Join BoomerangFX?

BoomerangFX is a global healthcare technology company bringing SaaS, artificial intelligence and digital marketing together to help private-pay healthcare practices operate and grow. Recognized through Deloitte’s Technology Fast 500 program, we are building technology that simplifies practice management, strengthens patient engagement and helps healthcare businesses reach more people.
With operations in the United States, Canada, the United Kingdom, Australia and India
, we are scaling internationally and working at the forefront of AI in healthcare. Our teams collaborate across countries and disciplines to turn new ideas into products and services that make a practical difference for customers.

Joining BoomerangFX is an opportunity to build your career alongside a growing global business. You will have meaningful responsibility, exposure to international markets and the opportunity to contribute ideas, develop your skills and see the impact of your work. We welcome people who take ownership, move quickly and want to help build what comes next.

The Role

Reporting to the CEO, you will lead financial management and general operations with strong financial acumen, commercial judgment and a practical approach to execution
.

You will oversee the Controller and Accountant
while taking responsibility for talent acquisition, human resources, vendor negotiations and corporate infrastructure
. You must be comfortable reviewing the detail, challenging assumptions and resolving issues personally while building an accountable team.

Financial Leadership and Accounting Oversight

Directly oversee the Controller and Accountant, setting clear expectations for accuracy, reporting deadlines, financial controls and accountability. Review their work and provide hands-on guidance on complex issues.
Own the quality and timeliness of monthly, quarterly and annual financial reporting. Review financial statements, balance-sheet reconciliations, management reports and material accounting judgments.
Oversee billing, subscription revenue recognition, deferred revenue, collections, accounts payable, payroll and intercompany reporting. Maintain clear controls over approvals, payments and financial records.
Coordinate external accountants, auditors and tax advisers, and strengthen accounting policies and controls as the company scales.

Financial Performance and Cash Management

Lead annual budgeting, rolling forecasts, financial modelling and variance analysis. Challenge assumptions and translate financial results into clear recommendations for the CEO and department leaders.
Own a rolling 13-week cash-flow forecast and longer-term liquidity projections. Improve collections, working capital, spending discipline and visibility into financial commitments.
Analyze profitability by product, service and market. Use SaaS metrics, including ARR, retention, churn, gross margin, customer acquisition cost and payback, to evaluate performance and investment decisions.
Assess hiring plans, pricing, operating costs and major expenditures against expected returns. Drive measurable improvements in margins, productivity and progress toward sustainable profitability.

Talent Acquisition and Human Resources

Oversee talent acquisition and human resources, including internal staff and external providers. Align recruitment priorities and headcount plans with approved budgets and business needs.
Oversee recruitment execution, agency relationships, hiring timelines, onboarding and workforce planning. Hold hiring managers accountable for clear requirements, timely decisions and hiring outcomes.
Oversee HR administration, employee records, compensation and benefits coordination, performance-review processes, employee relations and offboarding, working with qualified advisers where required.

Vendor Negotiations and Corporate Infrastructure

Lead vendor negotiations and oversee procurement, contracts and renewals. Secure commercially sound pricing, payment terms and service commitments, and hold providers accountable for delivery.
Oversee corporate infrastructure, including offices, facilities, equipment, business systems and outsourced services. Ensure these resources support reliable daily operations and future growth.
Work with technology leaders on corporate IT providers, software licences, infrastructure spending and business continuity arrangements. Improve utilization and eliminate unnecessary or duplicate costs.

Operating Performance and Team Leadership

Establish operating KPIs, management dashboards and regular performance reviews across finance and the functions under your oversight.
Improve workflows, approval processes and reporting through practical automation and stronger data quality. Ensure corrective actions have accountable owners and deadlines.
Lead and develop the finance team and collaborate with Sales, Marketing, Customer Success, Product and Technology leaders to improve execution and resource allocation.

Mandatory Qualifications

CPA designation in good standing in Canada.

At least 5-7 years of progressive finance experience, including hands-on leadership across financial reporting, controllership, budgeting, forecasting, cash management and operating performance.
At least three years of hands-on experience in a fast-paced SaaS business, including leadership of finance and operations for a PE-backed SaaS company scaling ARR from $5 million to $50 million.

Strong financial acumen and commercial judgment: the ability to interrogate financial results, build credible forecasts, evaluate SaaS unit economics and make sound decisions on costs, headcount and investment.
Proven experience directly supervising a Controller and accounting staff, reviewing their work and maintaining high standards for financial accuracy, control and delivery.
Direct experience overseeing talent acquisition, human resources, vendor negotiations and corporate infrastructure, with accountability for operational results.
Advanced financial modelling and Excel or Google Sheets skills, proficiency with accounting and reporting systems, and the ability to explain financial issues clearly to business leaders.
A record of personal ownership and effective execution in an environment with rapidly changing priorities, tight deadlines and limited resources. You must be willing to work on-site in Mississauga five days per week.

Additional Experience We Value

Measurable success improving profitability, cash generation or progress toward break-even.
Experience managing multiple entities, currencies or international operations.
Experience in healthcare technology or a business combining SaaS subscriptions and services.
Experience implementing finance systems, automating reporting or supporting transaction readiness.

Compensation and Benefits

Base salary:
CAD $135,000–$150,000 annually.
Annual target performance bonus:
50% of base salary, based on achievement of agreed performance objectives.
Total target compensation:
CAD $202,500–$225,000 annually.
Performance objectives will reflect measurable outcomes in profitability, cash management, financial reporting and operational execution.
Comprehensive health, dental and vision coverage.
Paid vacation and free on-site parking.
An opportunity to work closely with the CEO and senior leadership and make a measurable contribution to a growing global healthcare technology business.

How to Apply

Submit your résumé with a brief summary of your experience in high-growth software or technology-enabled companies, including two or three measurable financial or operational results you personally delivered.
Shortlisted candidates should be prepared to discuss their experience with financial oversight, operational leadership, strategic planning, and board reporting. CPA credentials, employment experience, and professional references will be verified.

Accessibility Statement

BoomerangFX is an equal opportunity employer committed to diversity and inclusion. We welcome applications from all qualified individuals and are dedicated to accommodating people with disabilities. If you require accommodation at any stage of the application process, please contact recruitment@boomerangfx.com.

jobs.title: Director, Solution Architecture – Information Technology
jobs.description:
Alberta Blue Cross® is an Alberta based organization dedicated to delivering exceptional customer experience and community leadership. We’re committed to providing the best health coverage to over 1.8 million members and take an active role in promoting wellness. We believe in what we do—and place trust in our employees to deliver our vision.

Working at Alberta Blue Cross® means having a career where you’ll be recognized for your contributions. We value diversity, encourage our team members to maintain a healthy work-life balance and provide opportunities for career growth.

Overview

We have an exciting opportunity for a Director of Solution Architecture to lead a team of 10+ Solution Architects at Alberta Blue Cross. Reporting to the Chief Architect, this senior leadership role combines strong people leadership with deep, practical technology solution architecture experience. The Director leads Solution Architecture practice and ensures initiatives have implementable, delivery-ready designs aligned to enterprise architecture direction, approved portfolio target states, and portfolio modernization roadmaps.

The Director translates approved architecture direction into technology solutions that delivery teams can build, integrate, operate, and evolve. The role brings credible technical leadership across applications, integration and APIs, enterprise data, cloud, security, identity, and infrastructure, balancing business outcomes with feasibility, performance, resiliency, privacy, cost, and maintainability. The Director guides complex design decisions and supports architecture through implementation and transition to operations.

Within the proposed Enterprise Architect target-state operating model, Enterprise Architects set enterprise direction and guardrails; Portfolio Architects own portfolio target architectures and modernization roadmaps; and Solution Architects design and guide implementation within those boundaries. The Director of Solution Architecture leads the people, capacity, technical quality, and operating practices of the Solution Architecture team. This role partners closely with Enterprise Architects, the Director of Enterprise Architecture, Domain Architects, and especially Portfolio Architects to connect delivery decisions to enterprise direction and portfolio roadmaps.

Success in this role is achieved by:

Leading, coaching, developing, and aligning a team of 10+ Solution Architects with clear priorities, accountability, and a collaborative technical culture. Most of the Solution Architects are already in place but additional resources may be required depending on demand. These Solution Architects are positioned as generalists who work across various technologies.
Applying deep technology solution architecture experience to produce practical, secure, resilient, and delivery-ready designs for complex initiatives.
Managing architecture demand, team capacity, assignments, and skills development across portfolios and delivery priorities.
Partnering with Portfolio Architects to align solution designs, dependencies, transition states, and technical feasibility with approved portfolio roadmaps.
Collaborating with Enterprise Architects, in their respective specializations, to apply enterprise guardrails, reuse enterprise capabilities and data, and resolve design risks through formal governance.

WHAT YOU WILL DO:

Lead and mature the Solution Architecture practice, including design methods, review practices, documentation, engagement models, and implementation support.
Lead a team of 10+ Solution Architects, including recruitment, onboarding, coaching, development planning, performance management, succession planning, and technical capability development.
Manage solution architecture demand and capacity; assign architects to initiatives with Portfolio Architects and delivery leaders, balancing priorities, complexity, dependencies, and skills.
Provide senior technical leadership for complex solutions across application, integration and API, enterprise data, cloud, security, identity, and infrastructure domains; challenge assumptions and guide design trade-offs.
Establish and monitor solution architecture measures for design readiness, review turnaround, guardrail alignment, reuse, technical risk, and implementation conformance.
Ensure solution designs leverage enterprise data and approved shared platforms, services, reference architectures, and patterns; address data ownership, quality, lineage, access, privacy, and integration with relevant domain specialists.
Oversee initiative-level architecture from discovery and options assessment through design, implementation support, and operational handover, maintaining traceability to business and non-functional requirements.
Partner closely with Portfolio Architects to translate portfolio target architectures, transition states, architecture runway, and modernization roadmaps into implementable solution designs; provide feasibility, dependency, and risk input for roadmap decisions.
Coach Solution Architects in system design, technology evaluation, integration, cloud adoption, secure design, cost trade-offs, and clear communication of technical decisions.
Collaborate with Enterprise Architects, the Director of Enterprise Architecture, and Domain Architects to interpret guardrails, obtain specialist input, and submit proposed patterns or exceptions through established governance.
Identify solution-level technical debt, integration constraints, implementation risks, duplication, and roadmap impacts; agree mitigation actions with portfolio, delivery, and platform stakeholders.
Work with business owners, engineering, delivery, security, privacy, data, platform, infrastructure and operations teams, and vendors to validate feasibility and guide implementation of approved designs.
Maintain transparent architecture decision records and escalate material exceptions, cross-portfolio conflicts, or changes to approved target states and sequencing; do not bypass enterprise or portfolio governance.

POSITION SCOPE

Reports to the Chief Architect and leads the Solution Architecture practice, with people leadership for a team of 10+ Solution Architects.
Provides technical leadership and design assurance for initiatives across business and technology portfolios, from early discovery through implementation and transition to operations.
Owns solution architecture practice methods, team capacity and assignments, design quality, solution-level deliverables, peer reviews, and practice effectiveness reporting.
Provides direct leadership, coaching, prioritization, performance management, and career development for Solution Architects; builds technical depth and leadership capability across the team.
Is accountable for the Solution Architecture capability and design assurance, not enterprise architecture policy, portfolio roadmap ownership, project delivery management, software engineering management, or production operations.

ACCOUNTABILITY BOUNDARIES AND ROLE CLARITY:

The Director of Solution Architecture reports to the Chief Architect and leads the Solution Architecture practice and a team of 10+ Solution Architects. The Director is accountable for people leadership, capacity planning, technical capability, design quality, and consistent solution architecture engagement across portfolios.
Enterprise Architects define enterprise-wide architectural direction, principles, standards, reference architectures, target states, and guardrails. The Director of Enterprise Architecture leads the EA function and its governance and domain architecture capability. The Director of Solution Architecture applies that direction to initiative-level design and contributes delivery insight, reusable patterns, and improvement proposals; the role does not assume enterprise policy ownership or leadership of Domain Architects.
Portfolio Architects own portfolio target architectures, transition states, modernization roadmaps, and architecture runway. The Director of Solution Architecture partners with Portfolio Architects to align architect assignments and solution designs with roadmap priorities and approved sequencing. The team provides technical feasibility, integration, dependency, and implementation feedback that may prompt roadmap changes; ownership of portfolio roadmaps and sequencing remains with Portfolio Architects.
Solution Architects own solution design decisions for assigned initiatives within approved enterprise and portfolio guardrails. They produce and maintain delivery-ready architecture deliverables, guide implementation, and support transition to operations. The Director provides technical coaching, peer review, design assurance, and escalation support without removing the assigned architect’s design accountability. Material exceptions follow formal governance rather than unilateral approval by the Director or Solution Architects.
Enterprise Architects provide specialist design authority and guidance. Delivery and engineering leaders remain accountable for implementation, project execution, and engineering management; platform and operations leaders retain operational accountabilities. This separation connects enterprise direction, portfolio roadmaps, solution design, and delivery while keeping decision rights clear.

KEY ACCOUNTABILITIES:

Lead and mature the Solution Architecture practice as a delivery-enabling capability within the proposed EA operating model.
Own consistent solution design methods, architecture deliverables, peer reviews, and design assurance from discovery through implementation.
Lead and develop a team of 10+ Solution Architects, including recruitment, coaching, performance management, succession planning, and career development.
Manage architecture demand, capacity, assignments, and reporting in partnership with Portfolio Architects, EPMO, and delivery leaders.
Ensure solution designs align to approved enterprise guardrails, portfolio target states, transition states, and roadmap sequencing.
Provide deep technical leadership and constructive challenge on complex application, integration, enterprise data, cloud, security, identity, and infrastructure designs.
Promote reuse of enterprise data, approved services, platforms, and patterns while meeting security, privacy, performance, resilience, operability, and cost requirements.
Make solution-level risks, dependencies, technical debt, and roadmap impacts visible; support mitigation and escalate decisions outside approved design authority.
Coordinate Enterprise, Portfolio, Domain, and Solution Architects with engineering, delivery, platform, operations, and vendor teams to guide implementation without assuming their distinct accountabilities.
Maintain business-to-design traceability, architecture decision records, implementation feedback, and operational handover readiness.
Measure practice effectiveness and improve design readiness, review responsiveness, guardrail alignment, reuse, and implementation conformance.

KEY SUCCESS MEASURES:

Solution designs are delivery-ready, traceable to business and non-functional requirements, and aligned with enterprise guardrails and portfolio target states.
Practice reporting shows design readiness, timely architecture engagement and reviews, implementation conformance, reuse, and transparent technical risk and exception management.
Architecture assignments, capacity plans, role expectations, and development plans support a team of 10+ Solution Architects across portfolio priorities.
Solution decisions support portfolio modernization roadmaps and transition states; feasibility, dependencies, and delivery constraints inform Portfolio Architect roadmap decisions.
Solutions avoid unnecessary duplication and unmanaged technical debt through reuse of enterprise data, platforms, services, and approved patterns.
Business, portfolio, engineering, and delivery stakeholders receive practical solution options, clear trade-offs, and timely design

jobs.title: Director, Finance
jobs.description:
This position is listed on behalf of a partner company, who manages all applications and next steps. Our partner is looking for a Director, Finance based in Canada.

As the first finance leader, you will have the opportunity to build and shape the financial function of a fast-growing company operating at the intersection of aviation, robotics, and autonomous technology. You will take ownership of accounting, financial reporting, budgeting, forecasting, and strategic financial planning. Working closely with executive leadership and department heads, you will translate operational and commercial decisions into clear financial insights that support sustainable growth. You will also play a key role in managing cross-border financial operations across multiple international entities. This position combines strategic leadership with hands-on execution, offering significant autonomy and the opportunity to establish scalable financial processes as the business expands globally.

Accountabilities

Accounting and Financial Reporting: Own monthly, quarterly, and annual financial statements in accordance with US GAAP, ensuring accuracy, consistency, and timely reporting.
Multi-Entity Financial Management: Manage financial consolidation, foreign currency accounting, and intercompany transactions across US, Canadian, and UK entities.
Revenue Recognition and Controls: Oversee revenue recognition processes, accounts payable, and accounts receivable while establishing effective financial controls and reporting procedures.
Tax and Audit Coordination: Coordinate tax compliance, external accounting support, and audit preparation with specialized external advisers.
Budgeting and Financial Planning: Lead the annual budgeting process, maintain rolling forecasts, and develop financial models aligned with business objectives and operational priorities.
Cash Flow Management: Maintain short- and long-term cash forecasts, covering working capital requirements, capital expenditures, and future financing needs.
Business and Commercial Analysis: Evaluate customer economics, deployment costs, pricing strategies, and expansion scenarios to support informed business decisions.
Financial Systems and Automation: Improve accounting and financial planning infrastructure, including ERP selection or implementation, and leverage automation and AI tools to streamline workflows while maintaining appropriate controls.
Financing and Fundraising Support: Evaluate debt and equipment financing opportunities, prepare financial due diligence materials, and support fundraising activities in collaboration with leadership and external advisers.
Strategic Business Partnership: Work closely with department leaders to assess the financial implications of hiring plans, deployment strategies, investments, and other operational decisions.

Requirements

Professional Experience: At least 8 years of progressive experience in accounting and finance, including direct ownership of financial closing processes and reporting within a growing organization.
Professional Qualifications: CPA designation or an equivalent professional accounting qualification, with strong knowledge of US GAAP and ASC 606 revenue recognition standards.
Hands-On Finance Leadership: Experience operating independently within a small finance team or as the primary accounting owner, with the ability to establish processes while personally managing day-to-day execution.
Financial Planning Expertise: Demonstrated experience managing budgets, cash flow forecasts, financial models, and variance analysis, with the ability to translate operational assumptions into financial recommendations.
International Accounting Experience: Strong understanding of multi-entity accounting, cross-border financial operations, US financial reporting, and coordination with external tax advisers.
Technical Skills: Advanced spreadsheet capabilities, familiarity with financial systems, and the ability to improve reporting processes through technology and automation.
Analytical and Strategic Thinking: Strong financial judgment and the ability to evaluate complex business scenarios, identify risks, and provide actionable insights.
Communication and Collaboration: Excellent communication skills and the ability to work effectively with executive leadership, operational teams, and external financial partners.
Autonomy and Ownership: A proactive, detail-oriented approach, with the ability to manage competing priorities and build scalable financial infrastructure in a dynamic environment.

Nice To Have

Experience working in a venture capital-backed company, particularly in robotics, hardware, industrial automation, or logistics.
Familiarity with inventory management, hardware-related financial operations, or Robotics-as-a-Service (RaaS) business models.
Experience selecting, implementing, or optimizing ERP systems and modern financial technology tools.
Previous involvement in equity fundraising, debt facilities, equipment financing, or financial due diligence processes.

Benefits

Competitive annual compensation: CAD $250,000–$300,000.
Leadership opportunity: Build and lead the finance function as the organization's first dedicated finance hire.
Strategic influence: Work directly with executive leadership and contribute to major financial and operational decisions.
International exposure: Oversee financial operations across Canadian, US, and UK entities.
Remote work: Enjoy the flexibility of a remote position based in Canada.
Professional growth: Develop your expertise in a high-growth, venture-backed environment at the intersection of aviation, robotics, and autonomous technology.
Ownership and autonomy: Establish financial processes, systems, and strategies that will support the company's long-term expansion.
Innovation-driven environment: Explore modern financial systems, automation, and AI-powered tools to improve finance operations.

jobs.description:
You are as unique as your background, experience and point of view. Here, you’ll be encouraged, empowered and challenged to be your best self. You'll work with dynamic colleagues - experts in their fields - who are eager to share their knowledge with you. Your leaders will inspire and help you reach your potential and soar to new heights. Every day, you'll have new and exciting opportunities to make life brighter for our Clients - who are at the heart of everything we do.

At Sun Life, we're driven by our Purpose: helping our Clients achieve lifetime financial security and live healthier lives. Our values shape how we work: caring, authentic, bold, inspiring, and impactful.

When you join Sun Life, you'll work with passionate colleagues and empowering leaders who support your growth and celebrate your contributions, so you can make a meaningful difference in our Clients' lives.

Discover how you can make a difference in the lives of individuals, families and communities around the world.

Job Description:

Lead the strategy that differentiates Group Retirement Services (GRS) in the market and connects sponsors and members with its value. As AVP, Market Strategy, Activation, & Communications you will be a key member of the Market Development leadership team, leading the GRS narrative, value proposition and go-to-market strategy. You will unite sponsor and member perspectives into a differentiated market position, strengthening awareness of GRS solutions, including its 2C (individual wealth management) capabilities. In partnership with Corporate Marketing and Communications and member marketing leadership, you will align communications and cross-functional execution while preserving partners’ accountability for member-specific strategy and execution. You will also represent GRS on key marketing strategies and initiatives across Sunlife, advancing growth, retention and member engagement through data-informed decisions and clear measures of business impact and return on investment (ROI).

What will you do?

Set the commercial go-to-market agenda: Translate GRS objectives into a roadmap for priority segments, audiences, competitive positioning, routes to market and growth opportunities. Define strategic trade-offs, recommend resource priorities and secure leadership commitment to coordinated execution.
Lead GRS narrative and proposition communications: Turn strategy and sponsor and member insights into differentiated value propositions and audience-specific messaging. Connect solutions, innovation and credible proof points in a consistent GRS story, validating relevance through market insight and aligning messaging standards with Corporate Marketing and Communications and enterprise requirements.
Establish marketing investment and performance discipline: Link investment priorities to business objectives, expected returns and measurable targets. Assess marketing’s contribution to pipeline and conversion, using ROI analysis and transparent measurement assumptions to recommend where to scale, adjust or discontinue initiatives.
Lead demand generation and commercial alignment: Attract and nurture prospective sponsors and activate consultant and advisor channels. Partner with Business Development on lead qualification, hand-offs, follow-up and feedback, using acquisition and conversion insights to strengthen pipeline contribution without assuming ownership of sales outcomes.
Align enterprise and member-level mandates: Establish shared plans, decision responsibilities and measures with Corporate Marketing and Communications, CXO and member marketing leadership. Integrate the broader member proposition into GRS positioning and sponsor-facing strategy, resolving dependencies while preserving partners’ distinct mandates and ownership of member-specific strategy and execution.
Shape strategic communications and market influence: Set a communications and thought-leadership agenda that reinforces GRS positioning and brings member perspectives into sponsor, consultant and advisor conversations. Guide executive messaging and external communications, aligning events, sponsorships, advertising and digital channels to market opportunities and measuring audience engagement and qualified demand.
Lead cross-functional launch governance: Set readiness criteria for new products, investment solutions and innovations, covering audiences, propositions, channels, commercial enablement and success measures. Align leaders on milestones and dependencies, address gaps and advance launch recommendations through appropriate decision forums. Use post-launch reviews to improve adoption and investment decisions.
Turn market intelligence into action: Assess sponsor needs, member insights, competitor positioning and channel feedback to identify opportunities and proposition gaps. Test strategic assumptions and bring evidence-based recommendations to GRS leadership to inform go-to-market priorities and innovation.
Build an entrepreneurial, accountable team: Lead and develop over 10 marketing and communications professionals, strengthening proposition development, demand generation, analytics and integrated planning. Foster ownership, proactive opportunity identification and disciplined experimentation. Shape priorities with business and enterprise partners while retaining accountability for GRS marketing outcomes and balancing strategic initiatives with ongoing business needs.

What do you need to succeed?

Commercial strategy and prioritization: Translates business objectives and market insight into segment-specific go-to-market plans and demand-generation approaches; makes clear trade-offs and focuses resources on the strongest opportunities
Executive presence and influence: Communicates direction with clarity and conviction, integrates diverse perspectives and exercises sound judgement to build commitment and advance decisions across organizational boundaries
Marketing economics and measurement: Applies investment, lead quality, funnel and ROI analysis to decisions; distinguishes activity from business impact and communicates measurement limitations transparently
Entrepreneurial leadership and ownership: Identifies opportunities, sets priorities and owns results; shapes direction collaboratively, makes timely, evidence-based decisions and adapts through disciplined experimentation.
Enterprise collaboration: Builds trusted partnerships with Corporate Marketing and Communications, CXO, member marketing leadership, Business Development, Legal and other Canadian Business Units, aligning objectives while respecting distinct accountabilities.
Strategic communications and narrative leadership: Translates strategy and audience insights into clear value propositions, persuasive executive communications and a cohesive GRS story, adapting messaging across channels while maintaining enterprise alignment
Market and member insight: Applies knowledge of GRS, the Capital Accumulation Plans (CAP) environment and the end-to-end member experience to strengthen competitive positioning. Uses member insights and evolving marketing practices to shape consumer-facing wealth management strategies that increase awareness, engagement and conversion.
Talent leadership: Attracts, develops and retains marketing talent, builds strategic and analytical capabilities and fosters collaboration, initiative and accountability.
Integrated execution and governance: Establishes effective decision forums, launch-readiness standards and performance reviews; mobilizes leaders to resolve dependencies and deliver coordinated results.
University degree or post-secondary education
10+ years of relevant industry experience, including experience within Group Retirement, Individual Wealth Management, Banking, or related financial services sectors
Experience leading go-to-market strategy, demand generation and marketing investment analysis
Experience developing consumer-facing wealth management marketing strategies informed by member insights
Expertise in strategic communications, value proposition development, market positioning and go-to-market leadership; banking and/or wealth management experience preferred.
Must be able to travel on a regular basis
As this position is posted in several locations, we specify that bilingualism (French, English, both oral and written) is required for Quebec only for the frequent interactions with English and French-speaking colleagues or internal partners across Canada or worldwide.

The Base Pay range is for the primary location for which the job is posted. It may vary depending on the work location of the successful candidate or other factors. In addition to Base Pay, eligible Sun Life employees participate in various incentive plans, payment under which is discretionary and subject to individual and company performance. Certain sales focused roles have sales incentive plans based on individual or group sales results.

Diversity and inclusion have always been at the core of our values at Sun Life. A diverse workforce with wide perspectives and creative ideas benefits our Clients, the communities where we operate and all of us as colleagues. We welcome applications from qualified individuals from all backgrounds.

Persons with disabilities who need accommodation in the application process, or those needing job postings in an alternative format, may e-mail a request to thebrightside@sunlife.com.

We are proud to be a hybrid organization that offers our employees the choice and flexibility to work from both the office and virtually based on the needs of the business, our Clients and you.

We may use artificial intelligence to support candidate sourcing, screening, interview scheduling.

We thank all applicants for showing an interest in this position. Only those selected for an interview will be contacted.

jobs.description:
Requisition ID: 278435

Join a purpose driven winning team, committed to results, in an inclusive and high-performing culture.

Purpose

The Director, Artificial Intelligence Risk Management & Governance
leads the enterprise approach to identifying, assessing, and controlling risks arising from the use of artificial intelligence across the bank. The role defines and operates the AI risk management standard, sets guardrails that allow AI to scale safely, and partners with the business, technology, and the risk and control functions to ensure AI is trusted, explainable, and compliant with Canadian and U.S. regulatory expectations.

Is this role right for you? In this role, you will be involved in:

AI Risk Management Standard

Own the design, maintenance, and continuous improvement of the AI risk management standard, in alignment with Bank policies, including acceptable use and AI ethics requirements.
Align the framework with applicable regulations and industry standards, such as OSFI E-23, U.S. Federal Reserve model risk guidance (SR 11-7), and the NIST AI Risk Management Framework.
Maintain the AI control catalogue and map AI-specific risks to existing risk taxonomy categories, including model, privacy, third-party, cyber, operational, legal, and conduct risk.

AI Intake, Assessment, and Oversight

Lead the AI risk assessment process, including tiering of use cases by risk, Trusted AI assessments, and required mitigations before deployment.
Provide risk-based guidance and approval recommendations for generative AI and other emerging use cases, including conditions for client-facing or external use.
Maintain the enterprise AI inventory and monitor use cases for ongoing compliance, performance, bias, explainability, and drift.
Establish guardrails and restrictions for higher-risk capabilities, such as agentic AI, until governance and controls are in place.

Governance, Reporting, and Regulatory Engagement

Support Data and AI steering groups and governance forums, with clear decision rights and escalation paths.
Produce executive reporting on AI risk exposure, key risk indicators, issues, and remediation progress.
Serve as a primary contact for regulators, internal audit, and second- and third-line functions on AI risk matters.
Track the evolving regulatory and industry landscape and translate changes into practical requirements for the bank.

Partnership and Leadership

Partner with Scotia Intelligence, Harbour, technology, and business lines to embed AI risk controls into delivery and the data lifecycle.
Collaborate with Model Risk, Privacy, Legal, Compliance, Cybersecurity, and Third-Party Risk to ensure consistent, non-duplicative oversight.
Lead and develop a team of AI risk professionals, fostering a culture of accountability, curiosity, and responsible innovation.
Promote AI risk awareness through training, guidance, and clear, business-friendly communication.

Direct Reports
: 4+

Skills

Do you have the skills that will enable you to succeed? We’d love to work with you if you have the following:

10+ years of progressive experience in AI risk, model risk, data risk, technology risk, responsible AI, or a related risk/governance discipline within a complex organization.
7+ years of leadership experience, including experience building, leading, and developing high-performing teams.
Demonstrated experience developing and implementing enterprise AI, model, data, or technology risk management frameworks, standards, controls, and governance processes.
Strong understanding of AI and emerging technology risks, including generative AI, model performance, explainability, bias and fairness, privacy, third-party risk, cybersecurity, and responsible AI considerations.
Knowledge of relevant AI and model risk regulatory requirements and industry frameworks, including OSFI E-23, SR 11-7, NIST AI Risk Management Framework, and evolving AI regulatory expectations.
Proven experience translating regulatory, risk, and technical requirements into practical controls, standards, processes, and guidance that enable responsible business adoption.
Strong strategic and analytical capabilities, with demonstrated experience influencing senior leaders and partnering across business, technology, risk, compliance, legal, privacy, cybersecurity, and other control functions.
Excellent relationship management and communication skills, with the ability to communicate complex AI and risk concepts clearly to technical, business, executive, audit, and regulatory audiences.

About The City Of Markham

The City of Markham is consistently ranked among Canada’s top municipal employers. In 2026, the City received its sixth consecutive Canada’s Best Employers recognition from Forbes and Statista Inc., placing third among municipalities and 15th overall in Government Services. An award-winning municipality, Markham is recognized for its leadership in sustainability, innovative urban planning, and strong fiscal management. Serving a diverse and growing community of more than 370,000 residents, Markham combines rich heritage with a vibrant local economy and offers employees the opportunity to contribute to meaningful, impactful work that helps strengthen the community we serve.

Join us and make a lasting difference!

Job Summary

Reporting to the Commissioner, Infrastructure and Community Services, the Director of Capital Planning and Infrastructure Delivery provides strategic leadership, oversight, and direction for the planning, development, design, procurement, and delivery of the municipality's capital infrastructure program. The Director is responsible for ensuring that municipal infrastructure assets are planned, funded, designed, and delivered in alignment with Council priorities, City design standards, growth forecasts, asset management objectives, legislative requirements, and long-term financial sustainability. The portfolio includes roads, bridges, sidewalks, water, wastewater and stormwater infrastructure, and other public infrastructure assets such as streetlights. This position leads multidisciplinary teams inclusive of the creation of a new Program and Project Management Office while collaborating closely with internal departments, elected officials, developers, regulatory agencies, utility providers, consultants, engineers, project managers, contractors, inspectors, technicians, and community stakeholders to successfully implement the City’s capital program.

Key Duties And Responsibilities

Provides strategic leadership for the City's capital infrastructure planning framework and oversees the development of the 10-year Capital Infrastructure Program.
Leads infrastructure project planning initiatives and establishes investment priorities aligned with municipal strategic plans, growth management objectives, asset management principles, and climate resilience goals.
Ensures site and construction inspections are conducted regularly so that all works adhere to statutory requirements.
Oversee the delivery of the capital infrastructure program, including the project planning, engineering, design, procurement, construction, contract administration, and commissioning of major capital infrastructure projects and programs.
Develops, recommends, and administers the annual and multi-year capital budgets, ensuring projects are delivered safely, efficiently, on schedule, within budget, and in accordance with approved scope and quality standards.
Collaborates with Corporate Asset Management and Financial Services to integrate lifecycle planning, asset condition information, and service levels into capital investment decisions and the capital infrastructure program.
Identifies, secures, and manages funding opportunities, including provincial and federal grants, and supports development charge-related infrastructure planning.
Provides leadership to multidisciplinary teams, fostering a culture of accountability, innovation, collaboration, employee development, and continuous improvement.
Prepares reports, business cases, and recommendations for Council, Committees, and senior leadership, and serves as a trusted advisor on infrastructure priorities and investment decisions.
Serves as the departmental lead in coordination with other City departments to support delivery of the Capital Infrastructure Program.
Represents the City and builds strategic relationships with York Region, regulatory agencies, utility providers, developers, consultants, contractors, and industry associations.
Leads stakeholder and community engagement initiatives related to significant infrastructure investments and projects and provides leadership to contract dispute issues.
Ensures compliance with applicable legislation, municipal policies, engineering standards, procurement requirements, and occupational health and safety obligations.
Other duties as required.

Qualifications

Education: University degree in Civil Engineering, Infrastructure Planning, Construction Management, or a related discipline.
Certifications and licences: Professional Engineer (P.Eng.) designation required.
Experience: Minimum 10 years of progressively responsible leadership experience in infrastructure planning, engineering, capital project delivery, municipal public works, or a related field, preferably within the public sector.
Minimum 5 years of senior leadership experience managing professional, technical, and project delivery teams.
Demonstrated experience leading large, complex capital programs and multimillion-dollar infrastructure projects.
Experience presenting technical and strategic recommendations to Council, senior leadership, and external stakeholders.
Knowledge, Skills and Abilities:
Extensive knowledge of municipal engineering, capital planning, infrastructure delivery, project management and asset management principles.
Strong understanding of municipal finance, capital budgeting, development charge funding, procurement, contract administration, and risk management.
Knowledge of applicable legislation, regulatory requirements, and engineering standards.
Experience with strategic planning, policy development, governance frameworks, and organizational change initiatives.
Exceptional leadership, relationship management, negotiation, and stakeholder engagement skills.
Excellent analytical, decision-making, communication, and presentation abilities.
Proficiency with Microsoft Office / Microsoft 365 applications.
PMP designation, Asset Management Professional (AMP) certification, and municipal experience are considered assets.

Core Behaviours

Service Excellence: Builds a culture that responds efficiently and effectively to current and future customer needs.
Change & Innovation: Champions innovation and change and leads the organization to innovate, improve and evolve using effective change management practices.
Teamwork & Relationship Building: Develops a culture of high-performance teamwork and establishes effective relationships with key strategic stakeholders.
Communication: Communicates effectively in difficult situations, under pressure and with varied audiences; develops a culture of open, respectful communication.
Accountable & Results Oriented: Communicates strategic direction, ensures realistic objectives, aligns efforts and monitors progress; creates a culture that drives ethical behaviour and accountability.
Management & Leadership: Creates an engaged and high-performance culture where diversity is leveraged, continuous learning is supported and future leaders are developed.
Strategic Thinking & Planning: Understands and navigates effectively through complexity; addresses threats and opportunities; demonstrates a long-term outlook and helps to shape the City’s strategic direction.

Core Values

At the City of Markham, our work is guided by a shared set of core values that shape how we serve our community and support one another.

Service Excellence: the consistent delivery of high-quality efficient and customer-centric service that exceeds expectations.
Accountability: our obligation to be responsible and accountable for our actions, decisions and performance.
People-Focused: putting people first.
Trust: the confidence we place in each other to act with integrity and fairness.
Innovation: Investing in each other and the way we deliver our programs and services.

We are looking for candidates who bring these values to life through their actions, decisions, and leadership approach.

Conditions of Employment

As a condition of employment, you will be required to provide a satisfactory Criminal Record and Judicial Matters check

Ability to motivate and influence leaders, physicians and staff at all levels to embrace and take action on transformation initiatives.

We are an 11 person organization headquartered in Cobourg.

We are hiring a Finance and Corporate Support Coordinator. jobs.description:
We are honoured to once again be recognized as one of B.C.’s Top Employers.

If you are looking for an opportunity to contribute your experience, knowledge, and passion in a meaningful way, CLBC is the place for you!

Community Living British Columbia (CLBC) is a Crown corporation responsible for arranging supports and services for adults with developmental disabilities and their families. CLBC staff strive to advance the vision of Communities of belonging, lives with connection.

Term/Status:
Permanent, Full-time

Classification/Salary:
Management Band 6: Position starts at $139,562 to $174,453 annually

Team:
Indigenous Relations

Location:
Vancouver Head Office (hybrid – one day per week in office)

At CLBC, we are committed to fostering a diverse, equitable, inclusive, and accessible workplace. We encourage applications from all people with relevant skills, including women, Indigenous Peoples, persons with disabilities, racialized people, and those who identify as 2SLGBTQ2+IA. For accommodation needs, please contact CLBCPeopleServices@gov.bc.ca at any stage of the hiring process.

Visit our Careers at CLBC page to learn more about working at CLBC, what we offer, and tips for the interview process.

About The Opportunity

We are seeking a strategic, collaborative, and relationship-focused leader to join CLBC as our Director, Indigenous Partnerships and Strategic Transformation.

Reporting to the Vice President, Quality Services and Indigenous Relations, this senior leadership role offers an opportunity to influence how CLBC works in partnership with Indigenous governments, organizations, and communities, while helping shape organizational policies, practices, and services to better reflect Indigenous rights, perspectives, and priorities.

The Director provides provincial leadership in advancing reconciliation, cultural safety, anti-racism, and implementation of the Declaration on the Rights of Indigenous Peoples Act (Declaration Act). Working closely with the Indigenous Advisory Committee, executive leadership, and partners across British Columbia, the Director leads CLBC’s Indigenous partnerships function and supports implementation of the Indigenous Advisory Committee’s Reconciliation Plan.

With responsibility for provincial Indigenous service planning, partnership development, contracting, contract management, funding arrangements, and placements, the Director brings together strategic leadership and practical implementation to strengthen relationships, support Indigenous-led approaches, and advance equitable access to culturally safe services.

This role offers the opportunity to influence meaningful organizational change, strengthen accountability, and contribute to improved services and outcomes for Indigenous adults with developmental disabilities and their families.

Key Responsibilities

Indigenous Partnerships and Service Development

Lead CLBC’s Indigenous Partnerships Strategy, building trusted, reciprocal relationships with First Nations, Métis and Inuit Peoples, Indigenous governments, organizations, and communities throughout British Columbia.
Work in partnership with Indigenous governments, organizations, and communities to support Indigenous-led approaches to service design and delivery, strengthen Indigenous procurement and community capacity, and improve equitable access to culturally safe services.
Oversee provincial Indigenous service planning, contracting, contract management, placements, and partnership agreements, including alternative funding approaches with First Nations that support flexible, community-based service delivery.
Represent CLBC in provincial discussions and initiatives with Indigenous governments, ministries, Crown agencies, and sector partners.

Strategic Transformation, Policy and Performance

Lead organization-wide strategies and initiatives that advance reconciliation, cultural safety, anti-racism, and implementation of the Declaration Act.
Provide expert strategic advice to executive leadership and the Board of Directors, guiding policies, governance frameworks, and organizational change that incorporate Indigenous perspectives into CLBC’s operations and decision-making.
Lead the development and implementation of provincial Indigenous strategies, corporate initiatives, and reconciliation action plans, including the Indigenous Advisory Committee’s Reconciliation Plan.
Establish performance measures and accountability frameworks to monitor progress, identify systemic barriers, and improve equitable access, service quality, and outcomes.

Indigenous Advisory Committee and Executive Governance

Provide strategic leadership and support to CLBC’s Indigenous Advisory Committee in fulfilling its legislative advisory role to the Board of Directors.
Develop strategic reports, briefings, and recommendations for executive leadership, the Board, the Indigenous Advisory Committee, and government.
Collaborate across CLBC and with provincial Indigenous leadership and government partners to advance shared priorities and inform organizational decision-making.

People and Resource Leadership

Lead, coach, and develop a multidisciplinary team, fostering collaboration, accountability, continuous learning, and a respectful working environment.
Oversee significant budgets, contracts, and resources, including an overall budget allocation of approximately $15 million, ensuring effective stewardship and alignment with organizational priorities.
Contribute to organizational planning, risk management, and strategic initiatives that support CLBC’s vision, mission, and values.

What You’ll Bring

Master’s degree in Indigenous Studies, Public Administration, Business Administration, Human Services, Leadership, or a related field. A bachelor’s degree supplemented by significant directly related senior leadership experience may be considered equivalent.
Minimum seven (7) years of progressively senior leadership experience in Indigenous partnerships, reconciliation, public sector administration, organizational transformation, or a related field.
Demonstrated experience developing and implementing strategies, service models, or initiatives in collaboration with Indigenous governments, organizations, and communities.
Experience leading complex organizational or system transformation, including strategic planning, policy development, governance, and organizational change.
Experience leading multidisciplinary teams and managing complex projects, budgets, contracts, or partnership agreements.
Experience working collaboratively across complex environments involving multiple governments, organizations, and community partners.
Extensive knowledge of Indigenous histories, rights, cultures, governance systems, legal traditions, and the distinct perspectives and priorities of First Nations, Métis, and Inuit Peoples in British Columbia.
Extensive knowledge of the Declaration Act, the Truth and Reconciliation Commission of Canada’s Calls to Action, and approaches to advancing reconciliation, cultural safety, and addressing Indigenous-specific racism.
Knowledge of Indigenous engagement, partnership development, government-to-government relationships, and Indigenous-led approaches to service design and decision-making.
Knowledge of public sector governance, strategic planning, policy development, performance measurement, and organizational change management.
Knowledge of the Community Living Authority Act, the developmental disabilities service system in British Columbia, and the network of organizations providing supports and services to adults with developmental disabilities.
Knowledge of trauma-informed, person-centred, culturally safe, and equity-informed approaches to leadership, policy, and service delivery.
Demonstrated ability to establish and maintain effective relationships with Indigenous leaders, government representatives, community organizations, and senior executives.

We recognize that relevant skills and knowledge can be developed through a variety of professional, community, and lived experiences. We encourage applicants to demonstrate how their qualifications and experience align with the requirements of this role.

We’re Also Looking For

A demonstrated commitment to reconciliation, cultural safety, anti-racism, continuous learning, and strengthening relationships with Indigenous Peoples and communities.
A respectful, collaborative, and culturally responsive approach to building trust, navigating different perspectives, and developing meaningful partnerships.
The ability to navigate ambiguity, complexity, and competing priorities while maintaining a clear strategic direction.
A leadership approach that supports collaboration, accountability, staff development, and a positive learning environment.
The ability to communicate complex and sensitive issues clearly and thoughtfully with diverse audiences.
Sound judgment, political acumen, and diplomacy when navigating sensitive matters and competing interests.
The ability to build alignment, influence decisions, and translate strategic priorities into meaningful action and measurable outcomes.
Experience in a public sector organization or similarly complex governance environment is considered an asset.

Benefits:
A rewarding career at CLBC comes with great benefits including

Employer-paid extended health and dental plan
A BC Public Service Pension plan with employer contributions
Generous vacation plus additional personal days
Paid maternity/parental/adoption leave
Life insurance, paid sick days, and, if needed, long-term disability
Wellness supports, including an Employee and Family Assistance Program
Professional development funds and resources to encourage continuous learning and skill development
Access to government discounts on travel, cell phone plans, and more

Additional Info

Pursuant to Section 42 of the BC Human Rights Code, preference may be given to Indigenous candidates who self-identify as First Nations, Métis, or Inuit and possess the required combination of education and experience.
CLBC is committed to equitable compensation. Recognizing that salary negotiation can create barriers for some candidates, we use an objective approach to determining starting salaries that supports equity and fairness.
The successful applicant will be required to complete a criminal record check.
This role requires travel throughout British Columbia, including occasional overnight travel to Indigenous communities, partner organizations, and CLBC offices.
Possession of a valid class 5 Drivers license and a clean Driver’s Abstract

Closing date: November 19, 2026

If your application is shortlisted, you’ll be invited to an interview where you’ll have the opportunity to share more about your experience. Please note that only those selected for an interview will be contacted.

This opportunity is open to applicants who are legally entitled to work in Canada.

Blacksmith Agency

Marketing
Full time
Remote (USA, Canada or South Africa)

About The Role

Blacksmith Agency runs PPC and SEO for clients across multifamily, B2B and technical verticals. As Digital Marketing Director you lead that department. The PPC strategist and the SEO strategist report to you and they are the specialists in their channels. Right now nobody owns this function, which is the whole reason this seat is open.

This is a management seat, not a senior individual contributor one.
You will not be building campaigns, and on technical SEO your strategist will know more than you do. That is the arrangement, not a gap. You carry channel strategy and where budget goes as accounts scale. The strategists carry the execution of it, and you carry whether the department delivers.

What You Own

The PPC strategist and the SEO strategist: their quality bar, their development, their reviews, and the call when someone is not going to get there.
The standard the work is held to. What a good audit looks like, what gets checked before work leaves the agency, how an account is reported. You write it and you hold two specialists to it.
Client results across the whole function, including whether our reporting is honest. Nobody here is auditing attribution and GA4 accuracy today.
The escalation when an account is at risk. You diagnose it, you direct the strategist who fixes it, and you are on the call with the client.
Channel strategy and where budget goes as accounts scale.
What we tell sales we can credibly deliver, before it gets sold.
The hiring plan for the department, and first-round interviews for your own team, within about a quarter.

What You Need

Strategists or specialists who have reported to you, where their reviews, their development and the decision when someone was not working out were yours. Managing accounts is not this.
7+ years across paid media and SEO. Owning one channel while sitting beside the other does not count here.
Enough depth in Google Ads, GA4, Search Console, Meta and Microsoft Ads to tell good work from work that merely looks good. That is a lower bar than doing it and a higher bar than reading a report.
One account you turned around that you can talk through: the metric, the figure before, the figure after, and why the change worked. Whose hands were on the keyboard matters far less than whether the diagnosis was yours.
Comfortable being the client-facing owner when an account is underperforming. That call comes to you, not to the strategist.
Agency experience carrying many accounts at once.

Please do not apply if

Nobody has ever reported to you, or you have never owned someone's review or had to performance-manage anyone.
You have only ever run one channel.
All of your experience is in-house on a single brand.
What you actually want is to keep building campaigns yourself. That is not a lesser ambition, it is a different job, and this is not it.

None of these are preferences we bend on. They are how we screen, so applying anyway costs you an hour and gets you a no.

Process

Three conversations, then a decision. A thirty minute screen with our recruiter, a first round with the founder this seat reports to, and a final. No take-home project and no panel interview.

How To Apply

Four fields at the link, then a short 6 minute Predictive Index assessment. Use the same email throughout. No cover letter.

jobs.description:
About Draganfly

Draganfly Inc. (the “Company”) has been a recognized technology leader within the commercial UAV space for over two decades. We helped establish the commercial market & adoption of multi-rotor helicopters for public safety, agriculture, aerial imaging, & more. As a leader who helped shape the industry, Draganfly’s focus is on the sale of drone products and services, contract engineering & custom integration product development, and health monitoring products and services.

Additional information on our expertise, projects, and culture can be found at https://draganfly.com/

We are looking for a strategic, highly hands-on, execution-focused Director, Enterprise Applications to lead the strategy, transformation, delivery and operation of Draganfly’s core business platforms and processes, including ERP and procurement systems. This is a working leadership role, not a purely strategic or people-management position. The successful candidate will be expected to personally analyze business processes, configure and optimize systems, troubleshoot issues, work with data and integrations, lead implementations, test solutions, and drive projects through completion. While this role will work closely with vendors, consultants and internal teams, the Director must be comfortable rolling up their sleeves and doing the work directly rather than primarily delegating execution to others.

As Draganfly grows across Canada, the US and internationally, this leader will modernize and standardize our application landscape across Draganfly Inc., Draganfly Innovations Inc., Draganfly Innovations USA, Draganfly Defense, USA, and Candrone. The role requires a leader who can partner with senior executives, work with colleagues within each department, drive execution at scale, and be part of a high-performing team.

This is a remote role, but the successful candidate will need to be willing to travel.

Key Responsibilities

Strategy & Transformation

Define and execute the enterprise applications strategy and multi-year roadmap across ERP, finance, procurement and related corporate systems.

Lead transformation initiatives that standardize and simplify business processes, modernize legacy tools and consolidate platforms in the cloud.

Align related application roadmaps with Draganfly’s business priorities, growth plans and multi-entity operating structure.

Delivery & Value

Own delivery of enterprise initiatives from initial requirements through hands-on configuration, testing, implementation and post-launch support.

Define and track measurable outcomes such as facilitating with operations a faster financial close, with finance chart of account updates, new subsidiary uploads, greater AP/AR automation and fewer manual, spreadsheet-dependent processes.

Platform Leadership

Hands on execution of Microsoft Dynamics 365 Business Central and procurement across their full lifecycle, from evaluation and selection of new platforms to ongoing optimization of existing platforms.

Work directly in the systems and with end users to identify issues, determine root causes and implement practical solutions.

Ensure finance platforms support Record-to-Report (R2R) and multi-entity consolidation and reporting, and that HR systems support the Hire-to-Retire (H2R) lifecycle, including payroll, benefits and talent management.

Ensure the platforms support Order-to-Cash (O2C), Procure-to-Pay (P2P), contract visibility and supplier management.

Process Standardization

Partner with Finance, HR, Legal, Procurement, Sales and Supply Chain leaders to define and implement best-practice processes across all entities.

Drive automation and deliver improvements in cycle times, data quality and reporting transparency.

Act as a primary point of contact for process optimization, supporting change management and driving consistency in process standardization.

Architecture & Integration

Define the target-state application architecture and integration patterns across the ERP and dependent data platforms.

Ensure systems are secure, auditable and integrated through scalable APIs and middleware, and guide build-versus-buy decisions.

Governance, Risk & Compliance

Ensure enterprise platforms meet public company financial controls and audit requirements (Canada and US), including COSO Framework, SOX404b protocols, as well as data governance and privacy obligations.

Collaborate closely with IT and Security to ensure compliance with security standards and business continuity planning.

Support export control and trade compliance requirements as required through appropriate system controls, data, and reporting.

Vendor Management

Manage platform vendors, implementation partners and consultants, holding them accountable for delivery performance, cost, and quality.

Leadership

Working manager that can also build and lead a high-performing enterprise applications team, with clear operating models for project delivery, production support and release and change management.

Foster a culture of accountability, cross-functional collaboration, and continuous improvement.

Other duties as assigned.

Who are you really?

A hands-on builder who rolls up their sleeves to configure systems, troubleshoot issues and see projects through to completion, rather than primarily delegating execution

A strategic thinker who can set a multi-year enterprise applications roadmap and standardize processes across multiple entities as Draganfly grows

A strong communicator with executive presence who can translate technical concepts for technical and non-technical audiences and influence the CFO and leaders across Finance, HR, Legal and Operations

Self-driven and dependable, able to manage multiple initiatives independently in a fast-paced, high-growth environment

A vendor and partner manager who holds implementation partners and consultants accountable for delivery, cost and quality

A collaborative team builder who fosters accountability and continuous improvement, and is comfortable working across ERP, HRIS and procurement platforms such as Microsoft Dynamics 365 Business Central

You bring a positive, solutions-oriented mindset, thrive in a role where attention to detail and controls matter, and are willing to travel as needed.

Qualifications

Education & Experience

10+ years in enterprise applications, IT or digital transformation, including 5+ years in leadership roles leading cross-functional teams.

Proven success leading ERP and finance system implementations or transformations, ideally in a multi-entity environment.

Deep experience with ERP platforms (Microsoft Dynamics 365 Business Central), HRIS (e.g. Rippling, Workday) and CLM/procurement platforms.

Track record of delivering complex, multi-year programs with measurable business outcomes.

Strong understanding of finance systems, including general ledger, fixed assets, revenue, consolidation, and reporting.

Strong working knowledge of R2R, P2P, O2C, and H2R processes.

Experience with public company financial controls and audit requirements (Canada and US), awareness of export control and trade compliance, and efficient companywide supply chain management.

Strong understanding of enterprise integration (APIs, middleware), cloud platforms, and data governance principles.

Ability to translate complex business needs into scalable, sustainable technology solutions.

Strong executive presence and the ability to influence the CFO and leaders across HR, Legal, Operations and the wider

Experience building and scaling teams and aligning stakeholders across competing priorities.

Ability and willingness to personally troubleshoot systems, configure workflows, work with data, participate in testing and resolve implementation and production issues. business.

Specializations/Nice to Haves

Experience in manufacturing, aerospace, defence or technology hardware.

Experience modernizing legacy systems into scalable cloud platforms.

Experience with HubSpot CRM and its integration with ERP.
