jobs.title: Chief AI Architect
Director AI Enablement
jobs.description:
**The Opportunity**The Director, AI Enablement is accountable for establishing and advancing Chartwell’s enterprise AI practice. The role exists to help the organization adopt AI safely, practically and at scale by combining strong governance with education, advisory support, and pragmatic implementation guidance.


This is not a pure research or data science leadership role. The Director, AI Enablement governs how AI is introduced into day\-to\-day work, helps departments identify and prioritize valuable AI use cases, and ensures that AI systems are deployed responsibly as they become more multimodal, more connected to enterprise data, and more capable of influencing decisions, workflows, and user behaviour.


The role serves as the organization’s AI expertise\-as\-a\-service function, working across corporate departments, FASTech, Service Management \& Automation, Business Analysis \& Quality Assurance, Data \& Analytics, Privacy, Cybersecurity, and enterprise applications to ensure that AI\-enabled solutions are useful, explainable, governable, and aligned to Chartwell’s operational realities.


**Key Accountabilities*****Enterprise AI Governance***

* Develop, maintain, and evolve Chartwell’s AI governance framework, standards, guardrails, and acceptable\-use practices in alignment with legal, privacy, security, and risk requirements.
* Define practical controls for responsible AI use, including human accountability, override mechanisms, confidence thresholds, auditability, data handling expectations, and documentation standards.
* Lead AI intake and review processes to assess proposed use cases for appropriateness, value, risk, explainability, and organizational readiness.
* Establish approval paths and risk classification for AI initiatives, distinguishing between low\-risk productivity uses, operational decision support, and higher\-risk use cases.
* Partner with Privacy, Cybersecurity, Legal, and enterprise technology leaders to ensure AI\-enabled solutions meet policy, compliance, and audit expectations.

***AI Education and Organizational Readiness***

* Design and deliver role\-based AI education, awareness, and training programs for leaders, practitioners, and end users.
* Create and maintain practical playbooks, templates, examples, and decision guides that help teams use AI effectively and responsibly.
* Promote AI literacy across the organization by translating technical concepts into plain\-language guidance and actionable practices.
* Support leaders in understanding the opportunities and risks of multimodal AI, connected AI, agentic workflows, and AI\-assisted decision support.
* Track adoption, usage patterns, and learning outcomes to refine enablement programs and improve organizational readiness.

***AI Expertise\-as\-a\-Service***

* Provide advisory support to all corporate departments on AI opportunities, use\-case framing, vendor/tool evaluation, and solution options.
* Help teams convert ambiguous problems into clear AI and automation use cases with defined objectives, constraints, risks, and success measures.
* Support business and technology teams during design and implementation by providing practical guidance on model and tool selection, workflow design, prompting patterns, and integration considerations.
* Act as a trusted internal partner who helps departments move from experimentation to controlled, business\-aligned AI adoption.
* Contribute expert guidance to FASTech and other delivery teams so AI\-enabled solutions remain practical, supportable, and aligned with enterprise standards.

***Safeguarding the Organization as AI Evolves***

* Develop guidance and control patterns for AI systems that use text, images, documents, screenshots, voice, and other multimodal inputs or outputs.
* Establish governance for AI systems that are connected to enterprise data sources, documents, communications, applications, and external research tools.
* Assess and mitigate risks related to hallucinations, model drift, privacy invasion, data leakage, bias, impersonation, surveillance, over\-reliance, and unsafe automation.
* Define boundaries for where AI may assist versus where decisions must remain deterministic or human\-owned, especially for safety, compliance, financial approvals, and resident\-impacting decisions.
* Provide guidance on the safe use of AI as an assistant, coach, or decision\-support tool, including controls to prevent manipulation, inappropriate inference, or hidden monitoring behaviours.

***Cross\-Functional Collaboration and Reporting***

* Work closely with FASTech, Service Management \& Automation, Business Analysis \& Quality Assurance, Data \& Analytics, Cybersecurity, enterprise applications, and business leaders to align AI adoption with business priorities.
* Maintain visibility into approved AI use cases, tools, integrations, risks, and realized outcomes across the organization.
* Contribute to executive reporting on AI pipeline, enablement activities, governance findings, adoption levels, and realized value.
* Identify recurring themes, risks, and opportunities across departments and recommend pragmatic improvements to Chartwell’s AI operating model.

**Qualifications*****Education:***

* University degree in Computer Science, Data, Information Systems, Business, Risk, Privacy, or a related discipline; or equivalent combination of education and experience.
* As an alternative to a Computer Science or Data\-focused degree, demonstrated and credible expertise in AI Governance, responsible AI, and enterprise AI enablement will be considered.
* Relevant coursework, certifications, or professional development in AI governance, privacy, risk, responsible AI, or change management are assets.

***Experience:***

* Progressive experience in AI enablement, AI governance, technology advisory, digital transformation, or a related field.
* Demonstrated experience establishing governance, standards, or policy controls for enterprise technology or AI ad

jobs.title: Global Head of Architecture
jobs.description:
**Build the future of AI and data with us**
-------------------------------------------


Datatonic is a leading Google Cloud partner specialising in data and AI. We help organisations design, build and operate production AI systems, from governed data foundations and machine learning platforms to generative AI applications and agentic workflows. Our teams combine Google Cloud, software engineering, machine learning, data engineering and analytics expertise with the consulting skills needed to turn complex business requirements into reliable products.

  

**Your mission**
----------------


As Architecture Lead, you will be a hands\-on Cloud Architect who also leads Datatonic's team of architects. You will design and build cloud, data and application estates yourself, while setting the standards, growing the people and owning the quality of architecture across our client work.


You will split your time between three things: delivering architecture on our most complex engagements, leading and developing a team of architects, and representing Datatonic as a technical authority with clients and in pre\-sales.

 **What you'll do**

  

### **Hands\-on architecture**

* **Target architecture:** Design and lead target architectures across cloud, data and application estates on Google Cloud, covering the platforms and the systems that run on them.
* **Hands\-on build:** Stay close to the code. Prototype, write infrastructure as code, review pull requests and unblock engineering teams on hard technical problems.
* **Systems design:** Own boundaries, failure modes, security, cost, operability and how each design evolves over time.
* **Trade\-off ownership:** Resolve architectural trade\-offs across Platform, Data, Analytics, AI, Software and UX.
* **Delivery governance:** Act as design authority on our most complex engagements, making sure what we ship is secure, reliable and maintainable.

  

### **Leading the architecture team**

* **People leadership:** Line manage and develop a team of architects, including career conversations, performance reviews and growth plans.
* **Mentorship:** Coach architects and discipline leads while leaving delivery ownership with them.
* **Standards and patterns:** Set architecture standards, reference patterns and decision\-record practices used across projects and regions.
* **Capability building:** Grow architecture capability through hiring, training, communities of practice and design reviews.
* **Staffing:** Work with delivery leadership to match architects to engagements.

  

### **Clients and market**

* **Pre\-sales:** Shape solution architecture, estimates and proposals, especially where estate design carries the risk.
* **Client leadership:** Build trusted relationships with senior client stakeholders, from engineering leads to CTOs.
* **Thought leadership:** Help shape service propositions and represent Datatonic as a technical authority at events and with Google Cloud.

  

### **Working with agents**


You will use agents throughout engineering delivery and maintain the agents that support the architecture discipline, including their versioning, evaluation, operation and continuous improvement. This covers agents for option analysis, decision\-record drafts, consistency checks against established patterns, and initial threat and cost assessments.

 **What you'll bring**

* **Cloud architecture depth:** Extensive hands\-on experience designing and building production systems on Google Cloud (or AWS/Azure with a strong interest in GCP).
* **Engineering foundation:** Proven depth in at least one engineering discipline (platform, data, software or ML engineering) at Senior 2 / L5 or above.
* **Demonstrated breadth:** Evidence of systems design across disciplines, including networking, security, IAM, data platforms and application architecture.
* **Hands\-on skills:** Comfortable with infrastructure as code (e.g. Terraform), CI/CD, containers and Kubernetes, and at least one programming language such as Python.
* **Team leadership:** Experience leading, mentoring or line managing engineers or architects, and raising the bar for a whole team.
* **Client leadership:** Client\-facing architecture leadership with senior stakeholders, including pre\-sales and solution shaping.
* **Communication:** Ability to explain complex trade\-offs clearly to technical and non\-technical audiences, in writing and in person.

  

### **Bonus points if you have**

* **Google Cloud certifications:** Professional Cloud Architect or similar.
* **Complex estates:** Experience with multi\-cloud, hybrid or complex integration environments.
* **Architecture methods:** Experience applying formal architecture methods (e.g. TOGAF) in complex delivery environments.
* **AI and data platforms:** Experience architecting ML platforms, generative AI applications or agentic systems in production.
* **Consultancy background:** Experience in a consultancy or professional services environment.

In today’s tech-driven world, CSDS empowers government departments with essential digital solutions to meet Nova Scotians’ expectations.
As a trusted partner across government, we enable departments to fulfill their mandates with secure, user-friendly services. From healthcare and education to public safety, we collaborate to transform how services are designed and delivered.

We don’t just implement technology; we modernize outdated systems and reimagine processes.
Our agile, data-driven approach ensures that digital services are both efficient and adaptable to Nova Scotia’s evolving needs.

Joining CSDS means contributing to work that makes a real difference.
From providing vital tech support to healthcare professionals to strengthening cybersecurity and developing scalable digital platforms, you’ll play a key role in building a more inclusive, responsive government for Nova Scotians.

Together, we’re setting new standards for digital public service, delivering resilient solutions that meet today’s needs—and anticipate tomorrow’s challenges.

About Our Opportunity

Are you a collaborative, forward-looking leader who can turn complex health-system needs into clear digital pathways and better outcomes? You will bring structure to ambiguity, establish trusted relationships, and ensure initiatives receive timely guidance on technical design, architecture review, security and privacy alignment, procurement, operational readiness, and enterprise dependencies. jobs.title: Interim Vice President Finance
jobs.description:
IMMEDIATE INTERIM OPPORTUNITY

Interim Vice President Finance

Reports: EVP Corporate Services & Chief Financial Officer

Duration: 4 - 6 Months

Location: Toronto

Hybrid (2 - 3 Days on-site)

The Opportunity

Our client is a large, complex and highly respected not-for-profit organization that has experienced significant growth and continues to invest in strengthening the capabilities of its finance function. As part of this evolution, the organization has created an Interim Vice President, Finance role for an initial four-to-six-month mandate. This represents an exciting opportunity for an accomplished senior finance executive to provide experienced leadership to a large team while helping to take the finance function to its next level of maturity.

This is not a traditional "keep the lights on" interim assignment. The organization is looking for a senior finance leader who can quickly understand a complex operating environment, provide stability and leadership through transition, and help increase the value that finance brings to organizational decision-making.

A significant focus will be on strengthening data, analytics, management reporting, budgeting and forecasting, while improving the organization's ability to leverage its existing ERP and financial management tools. The goal is to move beyond simply producing financial information toward providing leaders with stronger insight into performance, trends, risks, opportunities and organizational impact.

The Mandate

Reporting to the CFO & Vice President, Corporate Services, the Interim VP Finance will provide leadership across the finance function while partnering closely with senior executives and operational leaders across the organization.

The successful executive will combine strong financial leadership with a practical understanding of how to modernize finance within a large, operationally complex and mission-driven environment.

Key priorities will include:
Lead and engage a large finance team through a period of transition, providing visible leadership, clarity, coaching and direction while maintaining operational continuity.
Assess the current finance operating model, capabilities, processes and priorities, identifying opportunities to enhance the effectiveness and value of the function.
Lead a complex organization-wide budgeting and forecasting process, ensuring appropriate financial discipline while improving the quality of planning, assumptions and scenario analysis.
Strengthen management reporting and financial analytics, ensuring senior leaders have more timely, relevant and actionable information to support decision-making.
Improve the organization's approach to financial metrics, KPIs and performance reporting, creating greater visibility into organizational performance and impact.
Help finance move beyond historical reporting toward a more forward-looking, insight-driven business partnership model.
Maximize the value being generated from the organization's ERP, reporting tools and financial data, identifying opportunities to improve processes, reporting capabilities and management insight without creating unnecessary complexity.
Work closely with operational and functional leaders to better understand their information requirements and strengthen finance's ability to support business decisions.
Review existing financial processes and controls and identify opportunities to improve efficiency, consistency, scalability and accountability.
Provide strategic financial advice and support to the CFO & Vice President, Corporate Services and broader executive leadership team.
Ensure the organization continues to maintain strong financial stewardship, controls, governance and accountability throughout the period of transition.
Build capability within the finance team through coaching, knowledge transfer and the development of stronger analytical and business-partnering skills.
What Success Looks Like
At the conclusion of the assignment, the organization should have:
A stable, engaged and well-led finance team positioned for the next stage of the organization's growth.
A clearer understanding of the capabilities, structure and priorities required within finance going forward.
A more robust and effective budgeting and forecasting process.
Significantly improved management reporting and financial insight.
More meaningful financial and operational metrics supporting executive decision-making.
Greater value being generated from existing ERP, reporting and data capabilities.
Stronger relationships between finance and operational leadership.
A finance function increasingly viewed as a strategic partner to the organization rather than simply a reporting and transactional function.
Clear recommendations for the continued modernization and evolution of finance beyond the interim mandate.

Ideal Background

The successful candidate will be a seasoned, CPA-designated finance executive who has led sizeable finance functions within large, complex organizations.

Ideally, they will bring:
CPA designation is mandatory.
Significant progressive finance leadership experience, ideally including VP Finance, CFO, Deputy CFO or similarly senior responsibilities.
Experience working within a large, complex not-for-profit, healthcare, broader public sector, association, social services or other mission-driven organization.
Demonstrated experience operating in an organization of 1,500+ employees or an environment of comparable scale and complexity.
Experience leading finance teams of approximately 15–20+ professionals, including managers and senior finance professionals.
Strong experience leading teams through transition, growth, modernization or organizational change.
Deep expertise in budgeting, forecasting, financial planning and management reporting within a complex organization.
A track record of improving financial analytics, dashboards, KPIs and decision-support capabilities.
Experience maximizing and improving the use of ERP systems and financial reporting tools, with the ability to focus on business outcomes rather than technology for technology's sake.
Strong understanding of financial governance, controls, reporting and stewardship within environments with multiple stakeholders and competing priorities.
Demonstrated ability to develop finance teams and build stronger FP&A, analytical and business-partnering capability.
The ability to operate comfortably at both a strategic and hands-on level, moving from executive discussions into the detail when required.
Strong communication and stakeholder-management capabilities, with the credibility to influence senior executives and operational leaders across a complex organization.
A pragmatic, collaborative and confident leadership style, with the ability to quickly establish trust and bring calm, experienced leadership during a period of change.
The Leadership Profile
This assignment will particularly suit an executive who has "seen the movie before."
The organization is not looking for someone simply to administer an established finance function. It needs an experienced finance leader who can step into a complex environment, quickly determine what matters, lead a substantial team confidently through transition and identify practical opportunities to make finance better.
The successful executive will bring a combination of financial stewardship, operational leadership, transformation experience and commercial curiosity. They will understand that great
finance organizations do more than report the numbers. They provide the analysis, insight and constructive challenge that allows leaders to make better decisions.
For the right executive, this is an opportunity to make a tangible impact within a large, mission-driven organization and leave the finance function stronger, more insightful and better equipped to support the organization's continued growth.

About the Role

Ottawa Physiotherapy & Sports Clinic is executing a multi-site clinic integration strategy, bringing several independently owned clinics under a unified corporate framework and building the foundational infrastructure to scale over time. We are seeking a hands-on, growth-oriented Director of Finance to unify distributed clinical financial operations, deliver clear visibility on consolidated cash flow and performance to executive leadership, and partner on the execution of our corporate growth strategy.

You will spearhead the financial integration roadmap with direct support from clinic owners and the executive leadership team. This mandate requires working closely with clinic leaders to design workflows that balance local clinic realities with parent-company governance, collaborating tightly with operations management where system changes intersect with clinic workflows.

What You’ll Lead

Finance Operations and Controls:
Oversee accounting, budgeting, forecasting, cash optimization, and financial reporting across all corporate entities. Standardize clinic-level workflows for payments, collections, reconciliations, and internal approvals. Manage relationships with external advisors for year-end preparation, corporate tax compliance, and regulatory reporting.
Systems Integration & Efficiency:
Lead the evaluation, selection, and implementation of a shared corporate finance platforms. Oversee data migration, training, and system adoption. Identify and execute cost and time saving opportunities through centralized vendor purchasing and shared processes.
Change Leadership & Stakeholder Management:
Act as a trusted financial partner to legacy clinic owners. Guide clinic teams through the cultural shift of financial centralization, ensuring clear communication regarding the purpose of new controls, governance, and standardized policies without causing friction in clinical workflows.
Financing, Acquisitions, and Growth:
Partner with executive leadership to plan and model funding future growth. Build financial models, support commercial lender relationships, assess capital needs, conduct financial due diligence on M&A targets, and establish a repeatable playbook for onboarding new acquisitions into the group platform.

What You Bring

15+ years of progressive finance or accounting leadership experience, with a proven track record of managing reporting, cash flow, and financial controls across multiple locations, legal entities, or distributed operating units.
Demonstrated experience leading financial system migrations, cloud ERP implementations, or standardizing fragmented workflows into a centralized shared-services model.
Strong communication and change-management skills, with the ability to translate complex financial concepts into actionable insights for clinical owners and stakeholders, and encourage adoption of new ways of working.
A university degree in accounting, finance, business administration, or a related discipline (or equivalent professional experience).
Experience in clinic practice roll-ups, mergers & acquisitions, or post-acquisition integration, preferably in a private healthcare clinic or multi-site service business, is highly valued. A CPA designation (CA, CMA, CGA) is strongly preferred.

Your First 90 Days

First 30 Days:
Assess each clinic’s legacy accounting software, billing and collections mechanisms, banking structures, and reporting tools. Establish a standardized baseline for localized cash flow, identify immediate operational or compliance risks, and align with leadership on the centralization sequence.
Days 31–60:
Begin centralizing priority finance functions, including corporate cash visibility, vendor payments, and consolidated reporting. Establish a unified corporate chart of accounts, standardized approval processes, and a rigorous month-end close calendar. Define the functional requirements for a shared cloud ERP/finance system and finalize the rollout timeline.
Days 61–90:
Deploy consolidated management reporting, clinic-level performance dashboards, and an agile group cash forecasting model. Begin the phased rollout of the shared finance systems across locations, clearly communicating milestones for completed work. Leverage the financial baseline to collaborate with leadership on a multi-year growth plan, including funding needs and acquisition priorities.

Location and Compensation

Base Salary Range:
$160,000 – $200,000 CAD per annum (commensurate with experience).
Additional Benefits:
Eligibility for a performance bonus tied to corporate and individual growth milestones, along with an opportunity to participate in the company's equity arrangement.
Work Arrangement:
Full-time. Ottawa-based candidates are preferred. Remote flexibility is available, with the expectation of periodic travel to Ottawa (approximately 2–3 days per month during peak initial integration phases, scaling to a quarterly cadence thereafter).

How to Apply

To apply, please forward your résumé to recruitment@optsc.com. Please include a brief summary or example of a multi-site finance integration or systems rollout you previously executed and the operational outcomes achieved.

Artificial Intelligence (AI) Disclosure:

Please note that Ottawa Physiotherapy & Sports Clinic does not utilize automated AI-driven screening or algorithmic ranking software to evaluate applicants for this position. All resumes and applications are reviewed manually by our internal recruitment team.

Accessibility and Accommodations:

Ottawa Physiotherapy & Sports Clinic is an equal opportunity employer committed to creating an inclusive, barrier-free recruitment process and work environment. In accordance with the Accessibility for Ontarians with Disabilities Act (AODA), accommodations are available upon request for individuals taking part in all aspects of the selection process. If you require an accommodation at any stage, please notify us at recruitment@optsc.com and we will work with you to meet your specific requirements.

About The Role:

As the Vice President, Finance & Chief Financial Officer (CFO), you will be a key member of the Executive Leadership team, reporting directly to the President & CEO. You will provide strategic leadership and executive oversight for finance, accounting, business and financial planning, treasury, tax, enterprise risk management, investor relations and procurement, while serving as a trusted advisor to the President & CEO, Board of Directors, and Executive Leadership team.

You will play a critical role in shaping the Corporation’s financial strategy, long-term sustainability, and overall business performance. As the Corporation’s senior financial executive, you will lead the development and execution of financial strategies that support growth across both regulated and competitive businesses, while ensuring sound governance, prudent risk management, disciplined capital allocation, and strong financial stewardship.

The Vice President, Finance & CFO will also play a significant role in evaluating mergers and acquisitions, strategic partnerships, and other significant investment opportunities, providing financial leadership and insight to support the Corporation’s growth strategy.

We are seeking an accomplished and forward-thinking leader with the strategic insight, financial acumen, and executive presence to help guide the Corporation through a period of continued growth and transformation. The successful candidate will be a collaborative and trusted partner who builds strong relationships, influences complex decisions, and leads with integrity, accountability, and a commitment to excellence. You will foster a high-performing, engaged team while advancing a culture of innovation, continuous improvement, and exceptional service to customers, stakeholders, and the communities we serve.

What You Will Do:

Strategic Leadership & Business Performance
:
Partner with the President & CEO, Corporate Development and Executive Leadership team to shape and execute our growth strategy across regulated and competitive businesses.
Provide strategic advice on enterprise strategy, capital deployment, growth, risk and financial implications of major decisions.
Lead financial strategies that support sustainable growth, operational excellence, and long-term value creation.
Align financial plans, resources, funding plans, and performance measures with corporate priorities.
Develop decision frameworks, scenarios, and performance insights that improve the quality and speed of Executive and Board decisions.
Champion accountability, innovation, continuous improvement, and data-driven decision-making.

Growth, M&A, and Competitive Business Development

Lead the financial evaluation of acquisitions, mergers, partnerships, joint ventures, new markets and business opportunities.
Develop transaction and financing structures that balance strategic value, financial returns, tax, regulatory requirements, and overall capital capacity.
Serve as a strategic partner by strengthening business models, pricing, investment governance, performance measures and scalable financial capabilities that support profitable growth.
Co-lead transaction integration and post-investment oversight, including financial systems, controls, cost allocation, synergy tracking and benefits realization, ensuring that approved investments deliver sustainable enterprise value.

Financial Stewardship and Transformation

Provide executive leadership for all finance, accounting and financial planning functions.
Ensure the integrity, accuracy and timeliness of consolidated and operating entity financial reporting, accounting, management information, and external disclosures.
Modernize finance systems, processes, data and analytics to improve efficiency, automation, forecasting accuracy, decision support and the scalability required for business growth and future acquisitions.
Maintain a strong system of internal control, delegated authority, financial policy and assurance that protects the company’s assets and reputation.
Lead enterprise budgeting, forecasting, and performance reporting, providing the President & CEO, Boards and Executive Leadership team with clear, forward-looking insights, and early identification of emerging risks and opportunities.
Support the Corporation’s ESG objectives through financial leadership, performance measurement, reporting, and decision support.

Treasury, Risk Management & Investor Relations:

Lead treasury, financing, liquidity, and capital structure strategies.
Manage effective relationships with municipal shareholders, lenders, rating agencies, and other key financial stakeholders.
Provide executive oversight of the Enterprise Risk Management framework.
Ensure that strategic, financial, transaction and emerging risks are identified, assessed and integrated into capital allocation, business planning, and executive decision making.
Oversee tax planning, compliance, and reporting activities.

Regulatory Affairs:

Advise the President & CEO, Executive Leadership Team and Boards on the financial, strategic and enterprise implications of regulatory policy, emerging requirements and industry developments, identifying opportunities, risks and recommended actions.
Translate regulatory decisions, commitments and emerging policy directions into the financial plans, capital strategy, forecasts, performance measures and risk-management priorities.
Provide executive-level financial leadership for major rate applications, capital funding mechanisms and regulatory initiatives, ensuring that revenue requirements, forecasts, cost allocation, and capital plans are credible, integrated and financially sustainable.
Lead engagement and advocacy with regulators, governments, sector organizations and other stakeholders to advance regulatory frameworks that enable innovation, investments, and improved outcomes for customers and communities.
Partner with General Counsel to integrate and align financial, legal, policy and regulatory perspectives in applications, advocacy, compliance and business development.

Procurement & Supply Chain:

Provide executive leadership and oversight for procurement and supply chain strategy.
Lead the transformation and integration of procurement and supply-chain capabilities, including processes, systems, data, analytics and supplier governance.
Establish procurement policies, controls, authorities, and performance measures and ensure procurement practices support value, transparency, compliance, and prudent risk management.
Promote strategic sourcing, supplier performance management, and continuous improvement.
Partner with business leaders to strengthen commercial decision-making and contract management.

What You Will Bring

Graduate degree in Commerce, Finance, Business, or related discipline, with a CPA designation.
Minimum 10 years of progressive leadership experience in finance or accounting, including at least 5 years in a senior leadership or executive role.
Strong expertise in financial planning, accounting, treasury, capital management, enterprise risk management, and business performance.
Demonstrated experience evaluating or executing mergers, acquisitions, strategic partnerships or significant investment transactions, including financial modelling, due diligence, transaction structuring or integration.

As Head of Platform Engineering, you will build and run that platform: allowing for applications and services to deploy the same way across environments such as Azure, on-prem Red Hat OpenShift, AWS and air-gapped customer sites, with security and compliance built in by design.

You will lead platform teams, translate CBN's vision into the platform roadmap, own technical direction, and stay close to implementation through design reviews, infrastructure-code reviews and complex production troubleshooting.

Key Responsibilities

Platform Architecture and Scale: Set technical direction, review designs and resolve cross-team technical problems across Azure (AKS, hub-and-spoke landing zones) and Kubernetes/OpenShift. Design for national-scale identity services and hundreds of millions of credential verifications annually.
Engineering and Delivery: Work directly with engineers on GitOps, CI/CD and infrastructure automation using Argo CD, Helm, Terraform and JFrog Artifactory. Establish reusable deployment patterns and go-live standards, including secured registries, offline upgrades and signed release bundles verified at air-gapped sites.
Reliability: Diagnose complex production failures alongside engineers and drive lasting fixes. Set SLOs, observability and capacity requirements using OpenTelemetry and visualization tooling; oversee L2/L3 support and problem management, and verify that backups and disaster recovery work.
Security by Design: Embed security gates, SBOMs, image signing, SAST/DAST and automated SOC 2/ISO 27001 evidence into delivery. Own Platform's control responsibilities with Security (patching, hardening, access reviews, backups/DR), identify and close security deviations at scale and support audits.
AI-Enabled Engineering: Support spec-driven development and enhance agents for delivery, change preparation, incident triage, runbook automation, and human approval with audit trails.
Platform Strategy and Adoption: Translate CBN's vision into a practical roadmap. Work with product, engineering and service delivery teams to onboard jurisdictions, reduce bespoke deployments and improve developer experience. Support platform bids and explain investment, capacity, commitments and risk to executives.
Team and Budget Leadership: Hire and develop strong engineers and team leads, allocate staff across DevOps, Infrastructure and DevEx functions, and hold teams accountable for delivery. Own platform spend and vendor contracts, working with Infrastructure & Operations on cost optimisation.

Qualifications

Mandatory Qualifications

Legally eligible to work in Canada
Fluent in English (speak, read, write)
Able to obtain (in a timely manner) and maintain Government of Canada Secret (Level II) security clearance
Able to work evenings, weekends and holidays as required during security incidents and customer go-lives
Able to travel approx. 1-2 weeks/year

Minimum Qualifications

Education: Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Engineering or a related field, or equivalent experience
Experience: 10+ years in infrastructure or software engineering leadership, including 5+ years managing leads or managers across multiple teams.
Operating Record: Demonstrated improvements in production reliability, performance or operating cost. Able to explain the baseline, engineering changes and resulting outcomes.
Recent Hands-On Engineering: Recent experience writing design specifications, implementing infrastructure or deployment automation, and reviewing code and configurations. Able to diagnose complex production failures alongside engineers.
Technical Depth: Deep practical experience in at least two of the following, with sufficient understanding of distributed systems to assess failure modes and architectural trade-offs:
Kubernetes/OpenShift operations (upgrade strategies, networking, secrets management, cluster reliability)
Azure or AWS infrastructure (well-architected frameworks, FinOps/Cost Management, networking, identity, subscription design strategies)
CI/CD and GitOps (Argo CD, Terraform, Helm, Pipeline Implementation)
Reliability engineering (SLOs/Error Budgets, Monitoring Workspaces, Cross-Region Failover, Chaos Engineering)

Platform Delivery and Adoption: Built or substantially modernised a shared platform from design through production adoption, including upgrades, rollback and operational handover. Experience delivering into regulated, government or disconnected environments, with measurable improvements, e.g. DORA metrics, onboarding time or developer satisfaction.
Secure Automation: Implemented controlled, repeatable releases using infrastructure as code and GitOps.
Technical Leadership: Hired and developed strong engineers and leads, and made technical decisions under competing delivery, reliability, security and cost constraints.
AI in Practice: Used AI agents in delivery or operations with human oversight and an audit trail.
Business Accountability: Owned cloud spend and vendor contracts, and explained platform investment, technical trade-offs and risk to product, finance, Security/GRC and executive stakeholders.

Preferred Qualifications

Experience leading or working closely with forward-deployed, solutions or pre-sales engineers, including technical bid and RFP answers
Identity and edge infrastructure: IDP/PAM, PKI, Load Balancing, Zero Trust, CDN/Edge Caching
Policy-as-code and supply-chain security: OPA/Kyverno, SAST/DAST, SBOMs, External Secrets
Microservice and distributed architectures, scalable hub-and-spoke topologies and high-volume data operations

jobs.title: Director of Financial Planning and Analysis
jobs.description:
ABOUT TRINDENT

Trindent Consulting is a global management consulting firm that specializes in technical augmentation in the energy sector, specifically downstream oil & gas and large energy users. We are a profit improvement firm, first and foremost. Trindent Consulting specializes in process engineering & optimization.
Without capital investment we create actionable ways to sustainably increase refinery margins by 2–3%. We’ve helped over 100 clients achieve significant financial benefits that yield between 500–1500% return-on-investment within the 1st year – and we’ve done that without capital investments or software changes of any kind.
Established in 2008, Trindent Consulting has quickly garnered a reputation as a firm that Makes It Happen™. We are ranked as one of Canada’s Fastest-Growing Companies by Canadian Business and GROWTH 500 for 7 years in a row. In September 2026 our 290% 3-Year Revenue Growth was rewarded with being named in Globe & Mail’s 2026 Fastest growing companies in Canada. Trindent Consulting is the 5th fastest growing Professional & Technical Services company in Canada.

Refineries are extraordinarily complex businesses. Trindent specializes in several ultra-high value niches within refineries where tens of millions of dollars in performance improvement may be captured in the short-term. Underpinned by data analytics, industry know-how, and technical experience; Trindent has implemented improvement engagements in over 40 refineries globally.

BUSINESS EXPANSION

Our practice is expanding. As part of this growth, we are building a strong pipeline of experienced professionals to support client engagements. We are gearing up for 20–25% growth and we hope you will join us on this journey!

THE OPPORTUNITY

Trindent Consulting is seeking a Director of Financial Planning & Analysis
to lead the evolution of Finance from a predominantly transactional accounting function into a commercially focused management finance organization.
This is a senior, hands-on leadership role responsible for building the planning, reporting, analytics and decision-support capabilities required to support Trindent’s continued growth. The Director will provide leadership with reliable financial information, actionable commercial insight and clear recommendations that strengthen operational control, improve project profitability, deliver measurable cost savings and enable better delegation of authority.
The successful candidate will establish an integrated view of Trindent’s financial and operational performance, connecting project revenue, consultant labour, utilization, expenses, margin realization, headcount, cash flow and investment decisions. They will work closely with the President, Finance Director, Executive and Leadership Teams, project leaders and functional budget owners to translate company strategy into financial targets, operating plans and accountable actions.

This role requires someone who can operate strategically while remaining close to the detail: building models, challenging assumptions, improving data quality, resolving reporting gaps and explaining financial performance clearly to senior leadership and the Board.

The Director of FP&A will be charged with establishing five foundational management finance capabilities.

1. Project-Based Financial Reporting

Design and implement a standardized Sold vs. Plan vs. Actual
reporting framework for all major assessments and engagements.
Provide clear project-level visibility into:
Contracted and recognized revenue.
Planned and actual consultant labour.
Consultant utilization and resource deployment.
Travel and other project expenses.
Gross margin and margin realization.
Forecast-to-complete and expected final project outcome.
Material financial and operational variance drivers.
Establish consistent project definitions, financial assumptions, data sources, ownership and reporting timelines.
Introduce recurring project financial reviews that identify emerging margin risks, delivery issues, corrective actions and accountable owners.
Ensure project reporting supports stronger engagement governance, resource planning, commercial decision-making and margin management.

2. Executive Management Reporting

Implement a reliable monthly management reporting package for the President, Finance Director, Executive and Leadership Teams.
Provide concise analysis of:
Revenue and project profitability.
Gross margin and operating performance.
Cash flow and working capital.
Budget and forecast variances.
Consultant utilization, headcount and labour cost.
Travel and operational expenditure.
Cost-saving performance.
Key risks, opportunities and required decisions.
Move reporting beyond retrospective results by explaining what happened, why it happened, what is expected next and what action is recommended
.
Clearly distinguish final, provisional, estimated and unavailable information, with named owners and deadlines for resolving material data issues.
Establish a recurring reporting calendar, review cadence and approval process that leadership can rely on.

3. Cost Savings and Expense Optimization

Launch a structured cost-optimization program covering travel, procurement, vendor management and operational spending.
Prioritize opportunities relating to:
Airline and hotel expenditure.
Foreign-exchange and payment fees.
Cancellation and change charges.
Vendor pricing and service levels.
Contract compliance.
Duplicate, avoidable or uncontrolled expenditure.
Quantify business cases, establish financial baselines and maintain a formal savings register.
Distinguish identified, approved, implemented and realized savings to ensure benefits are measurable and verifiable.
Turn cost analysis into practical recommendations on what to renegotiate, consolidate, defer, reduce or stop—without undermining client delivery or sustainable growth.

4. Governance and Financial Controls

Strengthen financial governance through clearer approval authorities, spending controls, vendor oversight, payment controls and project performance reviews.
Introduce vendor scorecards covering cost, service, responsiveness, contract compliance and performance.
Establish recurring financial and operating reviews with clear agendas, decision rights, actions, owners and completion dates.
Improve controls over budget commitments, purchase decisions, project expenditure and forecast changes.
Work closely with Accounting to define a disciplined month-end handover covering required inputs, reconciliation checks, delivery dates, data ownership and escalation routes.
Improve transparency and control while avoiding unnecessary bureaucracy or slowing operational decision-making.

5. Board and Leadership Readiness

Develop Board-ready financial reporting covering:
Overall financial performance.
Project and portfolio profitability.
Revenue, margin and cash-flow trends.
Operational and professional-services KPIs.
Material risks and opportunities.
Cost-optimization performance.
Progress against the Finance transformation roadmap.
Ensure Board and leadership materials are concise, accurate, reconciled and supported by clear analysis.
Maintain models, assumptions and supporting evidence in a due-diligence-ready state.
Provide the President, Finance Director and senior leadership with scenario analysis, recommendations and decision papers that enable confident and timely action.

QUALIFICATIONS

A recognized accounting or finance qualification such as CPA, CA, ACA, ACCA, CIMA, CFA or an equivalent professional designation.

KEY SKILLS & EXPERIENCE

10 years+ business and operational finance track record working for a fast growth services business operating across multiple legal entities, currencies & countries.
Experience in a consulting, professional-services, project-based or people-intensive business connecting project revenue, labour deployment, utilization, expenses, headcount and cash flow.
Experience building
or materially upgrading an FP&A function.
Advanced financial modelling, forecasting, scenario analysis and sensitivity analysis.
Strong project-profitability, margin-analysis variance, trend and root-cause analysis capability.
Strong data reconciliation, model-control and documentation discipline.
Advanced spreadsheet capability and experience working with ERP, planning, reporting or business-intelligence platforms.
Ability to design executive dashboards and communicate financial and operational KPIs clearly.
Strong business-case development, investment evaluation and decision-support capability.
Ability to translate complex financial information into concise, commercially relevant recommendations.

WORK LOCATION & FLEXIBILITY

This position may be based in either Dublin, Ireland or Toronto, Canada.

Trindent Consulting is looking for a FP&A Director who can modernize our financial reporting, provide deep insights and help us Make it Happen
as we grow our global revenues and customer base.

jobs.description:
Toronto or Waterloo, hybrid | Full-time | Reports to the CEO

Compensation: $160,000 to $190,000 CAD base salary

Build the finance function at a fast-growing senior care technology company shipping hardware to 24 countries.

The Company

We went from a lab in Waterloo to 24 countries in five years. Our sensors detect falls and track sleep, health and wellness, with no cameras, wearables or pendants. Families get peace of mind. Older adults keep their independence. Our CTO, Dr. Yihong Qi, holds 680 patents, and the next few hundred get built here.

Why now

We are scaling. One of the largest deals in our history is in delivery, our consumer product launches in January, and we are preparing our next raise. Every one of those runs on numbers leadership can trust: a close that lands on time, a forecast that ties sales to inventory and cash, and books that hold up in diligence. This is the moment to bring in the leader who owns it.

The role

This is the senior finance role at Pontosense. You own the close, the forecast, controls and the numbers behind our next raise, across our entities in Canada and China. You work directly with the CEO and the leadership team, and you are in the room with investors. This is a builder role first and an operator role second. You set up how finance runs here, then you run it.

What You'll Own

A monthly close that is reliable and consolidated across Canada and China, landing by business day 10
A forecast the company actually runs on, with sales, inventory and cash tied together
Product costing that is right: landed cost, COGS and inventory planning for hardware built overseas
The raise: the model, the data room and investor reporting, with you in the room
Annual financials prepared and audited on time, and the relationships with our auditors and tax advisors
Controls that hold up across two countries: approvals, spend and intercompany
A seat at the leadership table

What Year One Looks Like

The books close on time every month, consolidated. The forecast is trusted, and inventory is planned, not guessed. Audited financials are current, and our next raise runs on numbers that hold up in diligence.

How We Work

Build it right, then make it better. People's safety rides on what we ship, so we test hard and never settle for good enough.
Say it as it is. Kind and direct, at every level, including the CEO.
Real impact. There is more room to make a difference here than at a company ten times our size.
Do what you said. Trust is built on follow-through, and we return it with real ownership.
Hard, and worth it. What we build keeps someone's parent safe at home. Rest well, it's part of the job.

This is for you if

You'd rather own a problem than be assigned a task
You want the mission to matter and the pace to be real
You're happy to be the person who just fixes it

This isn't for you if

You want a playbook handed to you
You need a big team before you can move

You'll thrive here if

You are a CPA who started in audit, then grew with a product or technology company, with promotions along the way
You have owned the close and built the model yourself, not just reviewed them
You have run FP&A, not only the close: budgets, forecasts and the model leadership makes decisions on
You have worked with inventory, COGS and supply chain costing. Multi-entity or international consolidation is a strong plus
You have worked with investors, a board or lenders, or are ready to step into that
You explain the numbers plainly to people outside finance, and decide with incomplete information
You are as happy reconciling an account yourself as setting the strategy

You don't need to check every box. If this sounds like you, we'd like to hear from you.

Where this goes

As we raise and scale, this role grows into leading a finance team of your own.

What You Get

A sensor for your parents, on us
Direct access to the leadership team. No layers.
Fair pay, with the opportunity for equity
Impact decides your pay and your path, not tenure
Hybrid in Toronto or Waterloo, remote if that's where you do your best work
Health, dental and vision benefits

The details

Pay: $160,000 to $190,000 CAD base salary
This is a new role, created to grow the team, not a backfill
How we hire: typically an initial interview, a short case, and a final interview in person with our CEO and members of the team. We may adjust this depending on the role
We leverage AI tools in our hiring process, but prioritize human input and manual review

Our Commitment

At Pontosense, we are committed to creating a workplace that is inclusive and accessible to all. We value diversity and believe that everyone deserves an equal opportunity to succeed.

If you have a disability or special need that requires accommodation during the hiring process, please let us know. We will work with you to make the necessary accommodations to ensure a fair and positive experience for all applicants.

We strive to provide accessible communication and technology for our employees and customers and always look for ways to improve. If you have any feedback or suggestions on how we can improve accessibility in our workplace, please don't hesitate to contact us.

We are proud to be an equal opportunity employer and welcome candidates from all backgrounds to apply for open positions at our company.

Top Aces’ dynamic team contributes to delivering on our purpose of training the next generation of combat leaders by living our values of Service, Integrity, Excellence, and Together every day!

Join our team!

Position Summary

The Director of Data Management and Business Intelligence leads the enterprise data function for Top Aces. Reporting to the Chief Information Officer, the Director defines how data is governed, integrated, protected, and used across aviation operations, maintenance and engineering, supply chain, finance, safety, quality, human resources, commercial programs, and executive management.

The role will establish trusted enterprise data products and decision-ready analytics while respecting aviation record integrity, contractual obligations, export controls, data residency, and need-to-know access. A central priority is to improve the quality and usability of data from Ramco and connected systems so that leaders and front-line teams can manage aircraft availability, maintenance execution, material readiness, program performance, and financial results with greater confidence.

Top Aces Business Context

Top Aces provides advanced operational training and aircraft sustainment services to Canada, the United States, NATO members, and allied nations. The company operates globally in a safety-critical and security-sensitive environment that combines flight operations, maintenance and repair, engineering, supply chain, training, and proprietary technology. The data environment therefore requires strong governance across business units, legal entities, jurisdictions, and security domains.

The Director will translate these operating realities into an enterprise data strategy that supports growth, operational readiness, regulatory compliance, and disciplined investment. The role must balance standardization with the access boundaries required for Canadian, U.S., and international programs.

Key Responsibilities

Enterprise Data Strategy and Operating Model

Partner with the CIO to develop and execute a multi-year enterprise data and BI strategy aligned with Top Aces' business strategy, operating model, technology roadmap, and investment priorities.
Create a practical data operating model that defines decision rights, ownership, stewardship, architecture standards, delivery methods, and support responsibilities across corporate and regional teams.
Chair or support the enterprise data governance council and maintain a prioritized roadmap based on operational value, regulatory risk, data quality, and delivery capacity.
Partner with the CIO and U.S. IT and security leadership to establish appropriate data segregation, access controls, and technology control plans for FOCI-related and export-controlled environments, where applicable.

Data Governance Quality and Protection

Establish enterprise policies and standards for data ownership, classification, quality, lineage, retention, archival, residency, access, and acceptable use.
Define authoritative sources and common business terms for critical domains, including aircraft, fleets, components, serialized parts, maintenance programs, work orders, defects, inventory, suppliers, customers, contracts, personnel, and financial dimensions.
Implement data quality controls, issue-management workflows, and scorecards that identify root causes and assign corrective action to accountable data owners.
Work with Cybersecurity, Legal, Export Compliance, Privacy, Quality, and program security personnel to protect personal, proprietary, controlled, and customer information throughout its lifecycle.
Ensure analytics and data-sharing practices comply with applicable contractual clauses, the Canadian Controlled Goods Program, ITAR and EAR requirements, privacy laws, and customer security obligations.

Data Architecture Integration and Platforms

Define the target enterprise data architecture, including ingestion, integration, master and reference data, lakehouse or warehouse services, semantic models, reporting, metadata, and monitoring.
Establish integration patterns and data contracts for Ramco and other enterprise platforms using secure APIs, event-based interfaces, ETL or ELT pipelines, and controlled file exchange where required.
Reduce duplicate datasets and spreadsheet-dependent reporting by creating reusable, governed data products and certified semantic models.
Set engineering standards for observability, reconciliation, change control, testing, performance, resilience, backup, and recovery across the data platform.
Manage the data-platform lifecycle, capacity, licensing, vendor performance, and total cost of ownership, with particular attention to Microsoft Fabric, Azure data services, Power BI, and connected technologies.

Aviation and MRO Data

Lead data remediation and governance for Ramco MRO and ERP, focusing on master data, transactional integrity, usability, reporting structures, and interfaces with finance, supply chain, engineering, and flight operations.
Partner with Maintenance, Engineering, Airworthiness, Quality, Supply Chain, and Operations to improve the completeness and consistency of aircraft configuration, component history, flight hours and cycles, maintenance plans, work packages, defects, technical records, and inventory data.
Preserve the integrity and auditability of approved maintenance and airworthiness records while enabling controlled downstream analytics.
Develop trusted measures for aircraft availability, dispatch reliability, mission-capable status, maintenance schedule compliance, turnaround time, component reliability, inventory availability, and aircraft-on-ground events.
Support data readiness for operational and regulatory audits, customer reporting, contract performance reviews, and fleet-planning decisions.

Business Intelligence and Performance Management

Lead the design and delivery of executive, operational, and functional dashboards using consistent definitions, clear ownership, and traceable data sources.
Build an enterprise performance framework that connects mission delivery, safety, fleet readiness, maintenance, supply chain, program, customer, workforce, and financial measures.
Develop governed self-service analytics so business users can answer routine questions without creating uncontrolled copies of sensitive data.
Improve forecasting and scenario analysis for fleet utilization, maintenance demand, materials, labour capacity, contract delivery, revenue, cash flow, and program profitability.
Maintain a transparent intake and prioritization process for BI requests, balancing regulatory deadlines, operational urgency, enterprise reuse, and expected value.

Advanced Analytics and Artificial Intelligence

Identify and govern analytics and AI use cases such as predictive maintenance, component reliability, inventory optimization, demand forecasting, anomaly detection, and program risk monitoring.
Require documented business ownership, suitable data quality, human oversight, security review, and measurable benefits before analytics or AI solutions move into production.
Coordinate with engineering, operations, and technology teams when operational, training, mission-system, or live and synthetic data may be used, ensuring the work remains within approved classification and authorization boundaries.
Monitor model performance, data drift, access, and business outcomes, and retire solutions that no longer meet operational, security, or financial requirements.

Leadership and Stakeholder Partnership

Build and lead a capable team spanning data governance, architecture, engineering, BI, and analytics; define roles, develop talent, and manage succession for critical skills.
Partner with executives and functional leaders to convert business questions into governed data products, clear measures, and practical decisions.
Create an active network of business data owners and stewards and hold regular reviews of quality, adoption, access, and value realization.
Manage external partners and vendors through clear outcomes, architecture standards, service levels, security requirements, and commercial accountability.
Communicate data risks, progress, tradeoffs, and investment needs to senior leadership in concise business terms.

Education And Experience

Bachelor's degree in computer science, information systems, data engineering, analytics, business, engineering, or a related discipline. A graduate degree or relevant professional certification is an asset.
At least 10 years of progressive experience in data management, analytics, BI, enterprise applications, or data architecture, including at least five years leading teams or major cross-functional programs.
Experience in aerospace, defense, aviation, MRO, or another highly regulated and asset-intensive industry is strongly preferred.
Demonstrated experience improving data quality and reporting in a complex ERP or MRO environment. Direct experience with Ramco is a significant asset; experience with comparable aviation or enterprise platforms is also relevant.
Experience operating across multiple countries, legal entities, or security domains, including Canada and the United States, is preferred.

Technical and Regulatory Knowledge

Strong knowledge of enterprise data architecture, dimensional and semantic modelling, master data management, metadata, data quality, lineage, SQL, APIs, and ETL or ELT integration.
Hands-on understanding of modern cloud data platforms and BI technologies. Experience with Microsoft Fabric, Azure, Power BI, and Microsoft data services is preferred.
Working knowledge of aviation maintenance and supply-chain data, including serialized components, configuration, maintenance planning, technical records, reliability, and inventory transactions.
Familiarity with aviation regulatory and quality environments such as Transport Canada, FAA, EASA, safety management systems, and AS9100 is an asset.
Working knowledge of information classification, access control, auditability, privacy, data residency, the Canadian Controlled Goods Program, ITAR and EAR, CUI safeguards, CMMC, and NIST SP 800-171, as applicable to the role and programs supported.
Ability to obtain and maintain the security clearances, controlled-goods eligibility, and customer or program authorizations required for the position.

Leadership Competencies

Business judgment that connects data investment to safety, mission readiness, contract delivery, customer commitments, and financial performance.
Ability to influence executives, operational leaders, technical specialists, and front-line users without relying solely on formal authority.
Clear written and verbal communication, including the ability to explain data limitations, security constraints, and architectural decisions to non-technical audiences.
Disciplined program leadership, with practical experience managing priorities, budgets, vendors, risks, and organizational change.
Commitment to Top Aces' values of Service, Integrity, Excellence, and Together.
Professional fluency in English is required. French and additional languages us

jobs.title: Director, Technology Delivery and Enablement
jobs.description:
This is a hybrid position, with four days per week in the office and one day remote.

Office Location:
1 Presidents Choice Cir, Brampton, ON L6Y 5S5 (near Hwy. 407 and Mississauga Rd)

Lifemark Health Group (LHG) is a market leader in customized healthcare solutions. With over 20 years of service excellence, LHG is one of the largest, most trusted, and most comprehensive providers in Canada. As a national healthcare company, LHG employs over 5,000 highly trained clinicians, medical experts, and team members in almost 400 locations coast-to-coast and continues to grow both organically as well as through acquisitions. With that growth is a vision to be the most innovative healthcare provider in community rehabilitation, workplace health and wellness, and medical assessment services. Lifemark was acquired by Loblaw Companies on May 10, 2022.

Role Overview:

Lifemark Health Group is hiring a Director, Technology Delivery and Enablement to lead our Application Development Team and advance the modernization of our enterprise application landscape. Reporting to the VP, Engineering and Security Services, you will oversee the development, implementation, modernization, and ongoing reliability of critical business applications supporting Lifemark’s national operations.

In this hands-on technology leadership role, you will lead teams of developers, DevOps engineers, and QA specialists to deliver secure, scalable, and resilient solutions while evolving our engineering practices and technology platforms. You will champion modern approaches including cloud-native architecture, DevSecOps, platform engineering, intelligent automation, and AI-assisted software development, while improving application observability, engineering productivity, and delivery effectiveness.

Working closely with business and technology leaders, you will help shape Lifemark’s application modernization and technology strategy, including the responsible adoption of generative AI and emerging technologies, reduction of technical debt, modernization of legacy platforms, and continued evolution of our Azure ecosystem. You will also collaborate across departments, security and infrastructure teams, architecture, data and analytics, and external technology partners to ensure technology investments deliver measurable business value.

About You:

You are an experienced technology leader with a strong background in software and application development and a track record of leading high-performing technical teams. You combine hands-on technical depth with strong people leadership, delivery discipline, and the ability to translate business needs into secure, scalable technology solutions.

You are comfortable managing multiple concurrent initiatives, guiding application architecture and development practices, building strong cross-functional and vendor relationships, and continuously improving release management, DevOps, monitoring, quality, and reliability. You communicate clearly, develop talent, and stay current with emerging technologies and industry best practices.

Key Responsibilities:

Strategic Leadership and Team Management

Manage the development and maintenance of Lifemark websites and enterprise applications, providing technical leadership, oversight, and execution.
Plan, organize, prioritize, and delegate work assignments; oversee team results for quality, timely delivery, and adherence to policies and procedures.
Attract, mentor, develop, and retain top talent while supporting career development and succession planning.

Architecture, Development and Reliability

Provide guidance on application architecture, UI/UX, database design, and integration with back-end applications.
Maintain high stability, uptime, and reliability of enterprise applications through robust monitoring and QA practices.
Experience leading modern DevSecOps and platform engineering practices, including CI/CD, infrastructure as code, automated testing and security, observability, cloud-native architecture, and AI-assisted software development.

Project Execution and Release Management

Lead and support concurrent initiatives, ensuring alignment with business goals, schedules, and quality standards.
Plan, coordinate, and execute successful software releases using disciplined release management practices.

Vendor and Cross-Functional Collaboration

Manage relationships with third-party agencies and technology vendors to deliver robust and scalable solutions.
Build strong relationships across departments to align technology solutions with business objectives and improve operational efficiency.

Continuous Improvement and Innovation

Research and evaluate emerging technologies to meet business needs and continuously enhance development practices and tools.
Identify opportunities to leverage AI technologies, including machine learning and cognitive services, for automation solutions where appropriate.

What we’re looking for:

Post-secondary education in Computer Science or equivalent experience.
10+ years of software/application development experience, including 3+ years in leadership roles.
Strong understanding of application lifecycle management, system architecture, and development methodologies.
Proficiency in .NET development, relational databases, and cloud platforms; Azure experience is preferred.
Experience managing parallel projects, with strong time-management and organizational skills.
Excellent verbal and written communication skills.
Exceptional project and account management abilities, with a demonstrated ability to establish and meet schedules.
Current knowledge of industry trends and development best practices.
Collaborative mindset with proven team leadership experience.
Strong release management experience, including planning, coordinating, and executing software releases.
Demonstrated success attracting, mentoring, and retaining top talent and supporting career development and succession planning.
Proven record of maintaining high stability, uptime, and reliability of enterprise applications through robust monitoring and QA practices.
Expertise implementing DevOps best practices, including automated pipelines, CI/CD, and infrastructure as code.
Experience evaluating and applying generative AI, large language models, AI agents, machine learning, and intelligent automation to improve business processes, engineering productivity, and customer or employee experiences. Familiarity with responsible AI, security, privacy, and governance considerations is an asset.

What Success Looks like:

Enterprise applications and Lifemark websites are delivered and maintained with strong technical leadership, quality, stability, and reliability.
Development, DevOps, and QA teams are effectively organized, supported, and developed to deliver high-quality outcomes on schedule.
Application architecture, development practices, monitoring, QA, and release management continue to mature and support secure, scalable solutions.
Concurrent initiatives are delivered in alignment with business goals, schedules, and quality standards.
Vendor and cross-functional partnerships effectively support business objectives and operational efficiency.
Emerging technologies and improved development practices are evaluated and adopted where they provide clear business value.

Our Perks:

You will be issued a company laptop, headset and a home office monitor, keyboard, and mouse. After your successful probation period, you will:

Eligibility to earn a STIP (Short-Term Incentive Plan)
Have access to a yearly education re-imbursement fund
Receive 30% discount from Shopper Drug Mart purchases
Contribute to an Employee Stock Ownership Plan (ESOP) with employer matching percentage
Have paid vacation days as well as wellness days
Have a choice to enroll in our Health & Dental Flex Life Benefits (or in lieu contribute to your RRSPs)
Access to employee assistance program
On-site gym, Basketball & Volleyball courts, Ice Rink, Groceries delivered to work via PC Express, Dry-Cleaning services (1 Presidents Choice Circle Office)

Inclusion

We are committed to creating an inclusive environment where people from all backgrounds can thrive. Improving inclusion and equity is a collective responsibility. Lifemark promotes equal employment opportunities for all job applicants, including but not limited to those self-identifying as a member of the employment equity groups: Indigenous peoples, Newcomers to Canada, Women, and Visible minorities.

Accommodation

Accommodations are available on request for all candidates taking part in any aspect of the recruitment and selection process. Email us at Talentatlifemark
