jobs.title: Directeur régional des technologies de l’information - Région de Montréal/Information Technology Regional Director - Montreal
jobs.description:
MDA Space (TSX : MDA) est un partenaire de mission de confiance de l’industrie spatiale mondiale qui crée l’espace entre ce qui est prouvé et ce qui est possible. À titre de pionnier de la robotique, des systèmes satellitaires et du renseignement géospatial, avec une histoire de 55 ans de premières mondiales et de plus de 450 missions, MDA Space est un chef de file mondial dans les domaines des satellites de communication, de l’observation de la Terre et de l’espace, ainsi que de l’infrastructure et l’exploration spatiale. L’équipe de MDA Space, qui compte plus de 4 000 experts du secteur spatial au Canada, aux États-Unis et au Royaume-Uni, possède les connaissances et le savoir-faire nécessaires pour transformer la vision audacieuse du client en une mission réalisable, grâce à une combinaison unique d’expérience, d’excellence technique et d’émerveillement qui fait partie de notre ADN depuis le premier jour. Pour ceux qui rêvent grand et repoussent les limites sur terre et dans les étoiles afin de changer le monde pour le meilleur, nous vous y emmènerons.

Le Rôle

MDA Space connaît une croissance fulgurante, et nous sommes à la recherche d’un dirigeant technologique visionnaire pour piloter l’expérience informatique de plus de 2 000 collaborateurs
répartis entre Montréal, Kirkland, Sainte-Anne-de-Bellevue et d’autres emplacements stratégiques. Vous serez responsable de l’expérience utilisateur de bout en bout, mènerez des projets d’amélioration des services, gérerez les contrats avec les fournisseurs et veillerez au respect des normes ITIL/ITSM, de cybersécurité et de plan de continuité des activités (PCA). Si vous vous épanouissez dans des environnements dynamiques et à fort impact, et que vous aimez transformer des environnements techniques complexes en services fluides et centrés sur l’utilisateur, ce poste vous permettra de propulser votre carrière vers de nouveaux horizons.

Le directeur régional des technologies de l’information (TI), région de Montréal, supervisera la prestation des services informatiques locaux pour l’emplacement de Montréal et les emplacements environnants, en veillant à offrir une expérience employé de qualité, à garantir la fiabilité des opérations et à respecter les normes de MDA Space. À ce titre, il travaillera en collaboration avec les dirigeants locaux, les équipes de TI régionales, les fournisseurs et les intervenants de l’entreprise afin d’améliorer la qualité des services, de soutenir la croissance, de gérer les risques et de s’assurer que les services de TI répondent aux besoins actuels et futurs de l’entreprise.

Principales Responsabilités

Favoriser une excellente expérience des collaborateurs de TI sur les sites relevant de sa responsabilité / entrant dans son champ d’action
Favoriser l’implication des services de TI au sein du site – en veillant à ce que les collaborateurs des TI travaillent comme une seule et même équipe
Diriger les services de TI locaux afin d’offrir une expérience employé homogène et de grande qualité à Montréal et aux emplacements environnants.
Collaborer avec les dirigeants du site et les équipes des TI régionales afin de soutenir la croissance, de résoudre les problèmes et d’améliorer le rendement des services.
Communiquer de manière claire et concrète sur les services des TI, les normes, le rendement et la sensibilisation à la cybersécurité au sein du site.
Surveiller les performances des services locaux, les risques et les plans d’amélioration à l’aide de rapports et de tableaux de bord standardisés.
Veiller à ce que l’infrastructure, les outils et les services locaux respectent les normes de MDA Space et garantissent la continuité des activités.
Servir de point de contact local pour les incidents informatiques, les projets et les problèmes liés aux services, en assurant la coordination avec les équipes concernées pour trouver des solutions.
Soutenir les équipes de production et d’exploitation en garantissant que les services de TI sont fiables, cohérents et alignés sur les priorités de l’entreprise.
Superviser les ressources de TI locales, les services des fournisseurs, les contrats et la mise en œuvre des projets liés aux modifications ou aux extensions des sites.
Veiller au respect des exigences en matière de TI, de sécurité, de gestion des actifs, de la norme SOX et d’assurance qualité.

Direction Et Relations

Établir d’excellentes relations avec les dirigeants locaux, les partenaires commerciaux, les équipes de TI et les fournisseurs afin de garantir que les services répondent aux besoins de l’entreprise.
Diriger, encadrer et soutenir l’équipe des TI locale tout en encourageant la collaboration, la responsabilisation et l’amélioration continue.
Représenter le service des TI au niveau local et aider les employés à comprendre l’assistance, les services et les interlocuteurs à leur disposition.

Priorités

Expérience des employés: Donner l’exemple et donner le ton au sein de la direction des TI en mettant l’accent sur la promotion d’une expérience des employés exceptionnelle à travers l’ensemble des services des TI; diriger et faire évoluer l’infrastructure, les outils et les services de TI du site afin de soutenir le personnel; garantir une prestation de services de grande qualité et une amélioration continue, en accord avec les stratégies mondiales de MDA Space.
Direction d’équipe: constituer, diriger et développer une équipe locale de professionnels des TI qualifiés; être responsable du recrutement et de l’intégration des nouveaux membres de l’équipe, ainsi que de la mise en place de méthodes de travail efficaces.
Gestion technologique: maintenir une compréhension approfondie des technologies et des services de MDA Space; documenter et maintenir l’environnement technique du site afin de garantir que les performances actuelles et futures répondent aux besoins de l’entreprise.
Implication des collaborateurs: Représenter l’équipe technique des TI du site au sein d’une communauté de partenaires et de collaborateurs professionnels; veiller à la cohérence des prestations, conformément aux feuilles de route et aux normes mondiales.
Opérations et conformité: Gérer les contrats et les services des fournisseurs locaux; veiller au respect des normes informatiques, de la sécurité et des exigences de conformité.
Défense des intérêts des utilisateurs finaux: adopter une approche proactive et concrète en matière d’assistance et d’expérience utilisateur; identifier les possibilités d’exploiter les capacités existantes pour obtenir de meilleurs résultats.
Calendrier et lieu: Dans un premier temps, le titulaire du poste aura pour mission de garantir une excellente expérience employé en pilotant divers projets de manière transversale.

Compétences Et Expérience Requises

Passion pour la prestation d’un service d’excellence, en cherchant constamment à améliorer l’expérience utilisateur et à optimiser la performance.
Expérience dans un poste de direction à titre de responsable de services, avec une expérience avérée dans la prise en charge, la gestion et la responsabilité d’un service, d’une plateforme ou d’outils informatiques
Maîtrise parfaite de l’anglais et du français, à l’écrit comme à l’oral.
Expérience avérée dans le secteur de l’industrie ou des services
Expérience avérée dans la prestation et l’exploitation de services
Une compréhension technique approfondie couvrant un large éventail de technologies et de domaines.
Bonnes compétences en communication et en engagement, et expérience avérée dans la gestion des relations professionnelles
Excellentes compétences en matière de collaboration pour gérer les attentes locales et trouver des solutions
Excellentes compétences en matière d’influence, de réseautage et de travail d’équipe
Expérience approfondie dans un environnement normatif, réglementé et conforme
Excellente connaissance pratique de l’ITIL, des outils ITSM ou équivalents
Expérience avérée dans la gestion des fournisseurs locaux, des contrats, des renouvellements et des appels d’offres
Dirigeant et coéquipier : donne l’exemple à l’équipe ou encadre les autres; collaboration efficace avec ses pairs dans toute la région.
Expérience en gestion et en développement d’équipes, dans un environnement de travail ouvert, honnête, responsable et collaboratif.

Compétences Et Expérience Souhaitées

PMP
Six Sigma Ceinture noire
Certification ITIL
Une certification en expérience client serait un atout

Commentaires/Considérations Particulières

Les candidats retenus doivent obtenir et détenir une autorisation de et réussir Secret OTAN
l’évaluation de sécurité pour le Programme des marchandises contrôlées (PMC) et ITAR.

Avantages Sociaux

MDA offre une rémunération et des avantages sociaux compétitifs à ses employés à tous les emplacements. À titre de membre de l’équipe de MDA, vous et vos personnes à charge admissibles pouvez bénéficier d’un régime d’avantages sociaux qui assure un niveau de protection complet grâce à des soins de santé concurrentiels, y compris des régimes d’assurance-maladie complémentaire et de médicaments flexibles, des prestations dentaires et de vision, une protection du revenu en cas d’invalidité, une assurance-vie, des régimes d’épargne-retraite collectifs et un programme d’aide aux employés et aux familles.

Égalité Des Chances

MDA est un employeur qui prône l’égalité des chances, la diversité et l’inclusion. Nous nous engageons à traiter tous les employés et candidats à l’emploi avec respect et dignité. Si vous avez besoin d’une assistance ou d’un accommodement raisonnable en raison d’un handicap pendant le processus de candidature ou de recrutement, n’hésitez pas à nous en informer.

Building the space between proven and possible, MDA Space (TSX:MDA) is a trusted mission partner to the global space industry. A robotics, satellite systems and geointelligence pioneer with a 55-year+ story of world firsts and more than 450 missions, MDA Space is a global leader in communications satellites, Earth and space observation, and space exploration and infrastructure. The MDA Space team of more than 4,000 space experts in Canada, the US and the UK has the knowledge and know-how to turn an audacious customer vision into an achievable mission – bringing to bear a one-of-a-kind mix of experience, engineering excellence and wide-eyed wonder that’s been in our DNA since day one. For those who dream big and push boundaries on the ground and in the stars to change the world for the better, we’ll take you there.

The Role

MDA Space is scaling at warp‑speed, and we need a visionary technology leader to steer the IT experience for 2,000+ colleagues
across Montreal, Kirkland, St‑Anne, and other critical sites. You’ll own the end‑to‑end user experience, drive service‑improvement projects, manage vendor contracts, and ensure compliance with ITIL/ITSM, cyber‑security, and BCP standards. If you thrive in fast‑moving, high‑impact environments, love turning complex technical landscapes into seamless, user‑centric services, this is the role that will accelerate your career to the next orbit

The IT Regional Director – Montreal area will oversee local IT service delivery for the Montreal site and surrounding locations, supporting a strong employee experience, reliable operations, and alignment with MDA Space standards. This role partners with local leaders, regional IT teams, vendors, and business stakeholders to improve service quality, support site growth, manage risks, and ensure IT services meet current and future business needs.

Drive a great IT employee experience for sites accountable for /in scope
Drive IT engagement for site – ensuring IT employees work as OneTeam
Lead local IT services to deliver a consistent, high-quality employee experience across Montreal and surrounding sites.

jobs.title: Director, Strategic Planning, Operations and Administration
jobs.description:
About Toronto Metropolitan

For more than 75 years, Toronto Metropolitan University (formerly known as Ryerson University) has been shaping the next generation of leaders through its uniquely innovative, entrepreneurial and career-focused approach to higher education. Driven by bold leadership, cutting-edge research and a deep commitment to academic excellence, TMU collaborates with students, faculties, staff and partners to push boundaries, reimagine solutions and create meaningful change in an increasingly interconnected world.

For a more in-depth understanding of our vision, core values and ongoing work, please see our academic plan

TMU welcomes those who have demonstrated a commitment to upholding the values of equity, diversity, and inclusion and will assist us in realizing the benefits of embedding these values into the work at every level and in every unit of the university. In addition, to correct the conditions of disadvantage in employment in Canada and to bring lived experiences to the work, we encourage applications from members of equity deserving groups that have been historically disadvantaged and marginalized, including First Nations, Métis and Inuit Peoples in Canada, First Nations Peoples in the United States, racialized people, Black people, persons with disabilities, women, and 2SLGBTQ+ people. Preference will be given to candidates with lived experiences as people from equity deserving groups, as well as experience working with these communities with which the University works every day. Please note that all qualified candidates are encouraged to apply and we welcome newcomers and immigrants to Canada.

In April 2022, the university announced its new name of Toronto Metropolitan University. Learn more about our next chapter.

About The Faculty Of Community Services

The nine Schools within the Faculty of Community Services (FCS) offer professional programs that prepare individuals for addressing the health and social care needs of multiple population groups. Our programs are designed to encourage students to be creative and critical thinkers and effective problem solvers, who can transcend disciplinary boundaries to find lasting solutions to social issues. We prepare our students to navigate an increasingly globalized workplace, characterized by the integration of diverse peoples, cultures, technologies, economies and political processes. We work with multiple accreditation bodies to deliver the highest quality of learning and we promote innovation in practice and research. To learn more about the Faculty of Community Services, visit https://www.torontomu.ca/fcs/ or through our social channels: @FCSTorontoMet on Twitter and FCSTorontoMet on Instagram.

We especially welcome applications from individuals who self-identify as women, Black, Indigenous, racialized persons, persons with disabilities, or members of 2SLGBTQ+ communities, who will be integral towards serving our highly diverse student, faculty, and staff complement. If you identify with any of these equity-deserving groups, we encourage you to self-identify in your cover letter. We are committed to building a culture that recognizes, celebrates, and reflects diversity, and we welcome you to join us.

The Opportunity

We are currently seeking a Director, Strategic Planning, Operations and Administration
to join our team. This role will provide effective strategic leadership of financial planning and management, administration and operations management for the FCS Dean’s Office and Schools within the Faculty. They will collaborate with the Dean and academic leadership of the Faculty during the strategic planning process, supporting and contributing to the development of short- and long-term strategies to execute the vision of the Dean, and to support the University’s strategic goals and priorities, by providing financial, operational and administrative perspectives for academic and non-academic matters.

The successful candidate will lead the effective management and administration of the Faculty’s financial and human resources affairs in an efficient, innovative and professional manner, in accordance with university policies, procedures, applicable collective agreements and Faculty goals and objectives as determined by the Dean. Additionally, they will represent the Dean and the Faculty in long-term financial/human resources/operational planning activities at the University level.

Key Responsibilities

Operational and Academic Strategic Planning: Actively collaborates with the academic leadership and supports the strategic planning process. Participates with the Dean and academic leadership in planning activities, by providing financial and administrative perspectives in operationalizing the Dean’s Academic Plan for the academic and non-academic matters.
Financial Management and Reporting: Provides strategic leadership, direction and oversight to the faculty financial operations team, ensuring robust financial management, governance and consistency across the FCS Dean’s Office and the Faculty as a whole.

jobs.title: Director of Capital, Housing & Infrastructure (Engineering/Planning) - $100K-$150K in Curve Lake, ON!
jobs.description:
Lead capital, housing, and infrastructure delivery for Curve Lake First Nation

Step into a senior leadership role offering a competitive $100,000 to $150,000 annual salary, negotiable based on qualifications, plus excellent benefits!

Build safe, reliable infrastructure and housing for current and future generations

About Curve Lake First Nation

Curve Lake First Nation is an Anishinaabe community with deep roots in this territory, grounded in relationships to land, water, and each other as Curve Lakers. Known historically as Mud Lake, Curve Lake continues as a living, resilient Nation of almost 3,000 members. As part of the Michi Saagiig Anishinaabeg and signatories to the Williams Treaties, the community carries forward its responsibilities, teachings, and governance systems. Curve Lake is a place of strong kinship, cultural continuity, and collective responsibility, where each member contributes to the wellbeing of the Nation. Our community is located just north of the City of Peterborough, Ontario.

Home to trailblazers like Elsie Knott, Canada's first Anishinaabe Kwe O'gimaa, and renowned artisans, our community blends rich history with vibrant culture. More than an employer, we're a community of choice. Join us in preserving traditions, fostering diversity, and contributing to a future where old ways merge seamlessly with progress. Shape the legacy of Curve Lake—a place where heritage meets opportunity.

To learn more about us, please visit: curvelakefirstnation.ca

About the Opportunity

Curve Lake First Nation has an exciting opportunity for a full-time, permanent Director of Capital, Housing and Infrastructure
, based in Curve Lake, Ontario.
This role joins the organization during a period of organizational transition and growth.

Reporting to the Executive Director, you will lead a diverse portfolio that includes:
Capital project delivery
Public works and utilities
Water and wastewater systems
Housing services
Facilities and fleet

This is a hands-on leadership role. You will work alongside project managers, engineers, and contractors, and regularly attend construction and project sites with the project team.

Where We Are Now

The Division is entering an exciting phase of modernization, building toward proactive, well-planned, and data-informed service delivery. You will have the opportunity to shape clear asset management practices, introduce stronger maintenance and recordkeeping systems, and deepen funding partnerships with organizations such as Indigenous Services Canada and CMHC.

Working within a multi-funder and regulated environment, the Director collaborates closely with Chief & Council, senior leadership, staff, community members, and external partners to ensure that capital investments and housing initiatives are effectively planned, delivered, and sustained for current and future generations.

What Success Looks Like

In your first year, success will mean building trust across the Division and with Chief and Council, staff, and community, while bringing greater clarity, accountability, and coordination to the team. You will strengthen staffing and internal capability, improve planning, budgeting, procurement, and reporting practices, and restore compliance with key funding requirements such as FNIIP and CMHC Section 95. Capital projects will be on scope, schedule, and budget.

By the end of year two, you will have transitioned the Division to a preventative maintenance model with structured systems for work orders, asset tracking, and recordkeeping. You will also have established a comprehensive asset management framework and an integrated multi-year capital, infrastructure, and housing plan, and modernized housing administration to support the Nation’s newly approved housing manual.

Your responsibilities include, but are not limited to:
Providing oversight of capital projects from concept through design, construction, and close-out, ensuring schedules stay on track
Coordinating closely with project managers, engineers, architects, and contractors on major projects, including facilities, schools, and water and wastewater infrastructure
Evaluating bids and tenders, and ensuring contracts are followed throughout delivery
Ensuring managers are effectively running public works, roads, and utilities, with activities properly scheduled and completed
Leading capital and operating budgets, and partnering with Finance on funding strategies and grant applications
Ensuring compliance with funder and regulatory requirements, including Indigenous Services Canada, FNIIP, and CMHC Section 95 reporting
Establishing asset management, maintenance, and work order systems to replace informal processes
Providing leadership for housing programs, including development, renewal, waitlist management, and homeownership pathways
Supporting the Nation’s emergency planning, including participating in and helping to staff the Emergency Operations Centre
Leading and mentoring three direct-report managers and their teams

Due to the role's significance, refer to the Director of Capital, Housing & Infrastructure document for a comprehensive overview beyond the listed duties.

More About You

To qualify, you will need a university degree or certification in civil or structural engineering, planning, or a related field,
along with at least 7 years of progressive senior-level experience in municipal or First Nation environments,
including capital planning and project delivery, infrastructure and public works operations, or Indigenous housing.

The following are required:
Hands-on project management experience, with a strong understanding of project methodology from start to finish
Experience working with First Nation funding agencies, and an understanding of their processes and challenges
A valid Class G Driver’s Licence
Ability to attend construction and project sites with the project team
Ability to undergo a criminal background check and vulnerable sector check
Willingness and ability to travel as required

The following skills and experience will be strong assets:
Professional Engineer (P.Eng) designation, or experience as a project engineer
Project Management Professional (PMP), Registered Professional Planner (RPP), or equivalent certification
Experience working in an engineering or construction firm
An understanding of the dynamics of constructing facilities, schools, and other major projects
Experience with Class 3 Water Treatment Plants and Systems
A background in emergency planning or emergency management
Experience with bid evaluation, tendering, and contract management
Knowledge of the Ontario Building Code, the Environmental Protection Act, MECP regulations, and the Occupational Health and Safety Act
Experience working with Chief and Council, a board, or senior administration

As our ideal candidate, you are an outgoing, hands-on leader who is as comfortable on a construction site as you are in a Council meeting. You bring a practical understanding of how major projects come together, from evaluating bids to keeping contractors accountable and schedules on track. You also see the bigger picture: building the systems and team that move the Division from reacting to planning ahead. Just as importantly, you lead with integrity, calm, and a people-centred approach, bringing an awareness of intergenerational trauma and its impact on workplaces and governance, along with a genuine respect for Curve Lake First Nation’s history, culture, and traditions.

Note: Preference will be given to applicants who have First Nation or Indigenous ancestry.

About the Benefits

In exchange for your hard work and dedication, you will receive a highly competitive salary of $100,000 to $150,000
negotiable dependent on experience, along with a great host of benefits, including:
Relocation assistance
Comprehensive Benefits Plan: extended health care, dental, vision, life and long-term disability, etc.
Competitive Pension Plan with up to 7.5% employer matching
40 paid hours for Special/Personal Leave Bereavement Leave
Paid time off for 17 designated days, including National Indigenous Day, Christmas Day, etc.
Generous vacation accrual
Paid sick days
Regular community events such as Pow Wows, Harvesters' Gatherings, Christmas Craft Shows, and more!

Take on a senior leadership role that builds safe, reliable infrastructure and housing for the Curve Lake First Nation community. Apply now!

Curve Lake First Nation has an exciting opportunity for a full-time, permanent Director of Finance and Administration
, based in Curve Lake, Ontario.

Ideal backgrounds include experience at engineering services firms, Big Four consulting organizations, technology consultancies, or hyperscaler partner/consulting/alliance organizations.

Achieve sales and revenue targets with minimal oversight and direction.

Partner with the right stakeholders at your clients, cloud technology partners, and within PwC to evolve and shape complex sales opportunities. 
Successfully build solutions consisting of multiple distinct capabilities within our organization to bring a comprehensive, differentiated solution to our clients.

Develop solutions with various technology partners which you can jointly take to our clients.

Partner with PwC account teams to develop and maintain an annual sales plan and account strategies for key accounts. 
Effectively use internal tools (CRM) to manage your pipeline of opportunities. 
Successfully navigate a complex internal organization consisting of dozens of distinct capabilities and practices. 
Thrive in an unstructured and evolving team environment.

Your skills, knowledge, and experiences are what set you apart. Here's what we look for:

Have carried and met a personal sales quota for 5+ years

Candidates from professional services firms, technology consultancies, or hyperscaler services organizations are strongly preferred. High energy and focus to perform under short time constraints and meet tight deadlines 
This role does not require professional engineering licensure and is not classified as a formal engineering position under provincial regulatory definitions. This newly created role reflects our commitment to growth and delivering distinctive value for our clients and stakeholders.

Expérience en planification budgétaire, gestion des fournisseurs, priorisation de portefeuille ou prise de décisions d’investissement technologique.

Compétences et expériences privilégiées

Expérience avec les plateformes cloud, les stratégies API, les microservices, l’architecture événementielle (event-driven), le DevSecOps ou l’ingénierie de plateformes.

Position Purpose

The ITFM (IT Financial Management) practice helps IT leaders around the world answer a hard question with evidence: how does our technology spend compared to our peers, and where should we improve? As Research Director, you own the delivery of Infotech's flagship IT Spend and Staffing Benchmarking service - the engagements that put that evidence in front of CIOs and CFOs.

You will provide experience-based benchmarking insight and guidance that helps IT leaders drive measurable results, maintaining an active pulse on the needs of Members located globally and staying current on industry developments so you can deliver exceptional service across calls and benchmark engagements - in collaboration with analysts, Research Directors, and colleagues across the Research Division.

This is a senior, client-facing advisory role. While it is not a formal people-management position, you set the standard the wider ITFM analyst team works to, and your judgment shapes how the benchmarking service itself evolves.

Our promise to you

You will work for a rapidly growing company that understands the importance of supporting employees through flexibility, inclusiveness, learning and development, internal career mobility, measurement of the Employee Experience and actioning on employee feedback, and building strong relationships.

What You Will Do, Includes, But Not Limited To

Lead ITFM Benchmarking engagements

Lead and deliver ITFM’s flagship offering - IT Spend and Staffing Benchmarking engagements with analyst support.
Act as a trusted guide for C-suite clients in IT Financial Management, sharing insight on how to manage costs better and lessons from their industry on improving IT’s cost-to-value through benchmarking.
Improve the benchmarking service through your expertise — new ways of representing data and new opportunities to enhance the insights delivered.
Keep a pulse on industry trends and best practices in your areas of expertise, contributing ideas that shape the benchmarking service.

Cross Departmental Collaboration & Support

Support Call Advisory, Workshops, and Global Services teams by advising peers on IT Spend and Staff Benchmark research and analysis as needed.
Provide subject-matter expertise and feedback to other Research Division teams and to partnering divisions — Sales, Public Relations & Marketing, and others — as needed.
Design and build high-quality keynote and other presentations and deliver them successfully as needed.

Practice & Analyst Development

Contribute to and help with own benchmarking methodology, mapping standards, and delivery toolsets, working with Research Directors and the Practice Lead.
Support automation and data infrastructure initiatives that improve engagement consistency and scalability.
Mentor Research Analysts, reviewing their benchmark outputs and client-ready materials and helping them progress toward independent engagement leadership.
Make active use of AI productivity tooling (e.g., Claude, Copilot) in analysis, research, and writing workflows, and help bring effective practices to the wider team.

Required

Undergraduate degree required (business or technology preferred).

Experience in project-driven environments.
Presentation and facilitation experience demonstrated through prior client-facing engagements.

History of gaining and maintaining trusted-advisor status with management; strong working relationships with the C-suite.
Experience leading teams, given the advisory nature of the services offered (this is not a formal people-management role).
Professional certifications in Finance and Accounting, Project Management, Business Analysis, or other related disciplines.
Active use of AI productivity tooling (e.g., Claude, Copilot) in analytical, research, or writing workflows.

Assets

MA, MBA, or MSc.

Language Skills:

Client Interaction & Facilitation - Leads calls and benchmark engagements with C-suite Members; facilitates discussion and builds trusted-advisor standing.

jobs.description:
About The Team

OpenAI’s User Operations team shepherds our customers’ adoption of AI and ensures that our customers' product experience is nothing short of exceptional. We are building the very first post-AGI support team. We resolve complex issues, provide technical guidance, and support customers in maximizing value and adoption from deploying our products. We work closely with Sales, Technical Success, Product, Engineering and others, to deliver the best possible experience to our customers at scale. OpenAI's customers represent a range of diverse backgrounds and maturity, from early-stage startups to established global enterprises.

About The Role

We’re looking for dedicated, experienced, and deeply curious individuals to help solve some of the most complex challenges faced by our customers while building the future of post-AGI support alongside us. In this role, you’ll work directly with customers through support tickets and live calls, troubleshooting high-impact issues and resolving novel, often ambiguous technical problems in one of the fastest-moving environments in technology. As AI adoption rapidly accelerates, the work you do will directly support mission-critical systems being built on OpenAI’s platform, serving as a critical line of defense for customers operating at massive scale.

Beyond resolving technical issues, you’ll help define what world-class support looks like in an AGI-driven future. You’ll partner closely with Engineering, Product, and Operations to improve systems, reduce bugs, and elevate the customer experience, while leveraging automation, agents, and our own AI technology to transform how support operates at scale.

This Toronto-based role is currently remote and is expected to transition to an in-office arrangement.

In This Role, You Will

Work directly with customers to troubleshoot and resolve their most complex technical issues, including API failures, integration challenges, authentication errors, and production incidents. Providing end-to-end ownership through debugging logs, analyzing system behavior, reproducing issues, and delivering expert guidance.
Become a trusted expert on OpenAI’s products and platform, serving as a go-to resource for complex technical issues.
Serve as a critical escalation point and line of defense for complex technical issues, partnering closely with customers and Engineering teams to troubleshoot, resolve, and proactively prevent recurring problems while leveraging scripting and emerging AI capabilities to improve internal tooling and automate operational workflows.
Take learnings from resolving customer issues and creating our approach to scaling these solutions, partnering with Product and Go-To-Market teams.
Drive operational excellence by identifying opportunities for automation and AI-powered workflows, implementing scalable improvements that increase team efficiency, reducing manual effort, and elevating the overall support experience.
Provide occasional holiday and weekend support on call coverage, as needed, to support business and customer needs.

You Might Thrive In This Role If You

Have 5+ years of experience in User Operations, Engineering, Support Engineering or similar technical roles, ideally within high-growth tech startups or other fast-paced environments.
Are comfortable using emerging technologies (ie. Codex, ChatGPT, OpenAI API, etc.) to script or engineer code (e.g., Python) for automating repetitive tasks and integrating tools.
Have expert-level SaaS troubleshooting skills with the ability to rapidly understand new technologies and complex concepts.
Polished enterprise communication and are calm with high-stakes customers during live incident calls.

jobs.title: Director, Developer Platform & Experience
jobs.description:
Who We Are

Motive empowers the people who run physical operations with tools to make their work safer, more productive, and more profitable. For the first time ever, safety, operations and finance teams can manage their drivers, vehicles, equipment, and fleet related spend in a single system. Combined with industry leading AI, the Motive platform gives you complete visibility and control, and significantly reduces manual workloads by automating and simplifying tasks.

Motive serves nearly 100,000 customers – from Fortune 500 enterprises to small businesses – across a wide range of industries, including transportation and logistics, construction, energy, field service, manufacturing, agriculture, food and beverage, retail, and the public sector.

Visit gomotive.com to learn more.

About The Role

Motive is moving to an AI-driven development lifecycle. Agents that plan, generate, test, review, and help operate our systems — with engineers directing the work rather than typing all of it — are where software engineering at Motive is going. That direction is set. What we need now is a leader to build it.

We are hiring a Director of Developer Platform & Experience to own that execution and the platform underneath it. This role owns Motive's internal developer ecosystem end to end: developer experience, developer infrastructure, build and CI/CD systems, and the testing frameworks that let hundreds of engineers move quickly without breaking things. It also owns AI-DLC in practice — the tooling, cloud agent infrastructure, evaluation practice, and governance that determine whether agentic development actually makes us faster or just makes us noisier.

Our engineering organization spans North America, Europe, and Asia, across a Rails monolith, Go services, mobile, and embedded systems. How fast and how confidently that organization ships is one of our most important business levers.

This is a builder's leadership role, not a strategy role. You will inherit real systems and real teams, and be measured on whether engineers at Motive ship faster, with higher confidence, and with less friction than they did the quarter before.

The mandates

AI-driven development — make agentic development a governed, measured, everyday part of how Motive builds software.
Cloud-based agentic development infrastructure — build the substrate that lets agents run in the cloud, in parallel, safely.
Developer experience — make the inner loop fast and the right path the easy path.
Developer infrastructure — make build, CI/CD, and release systems fast, reliable, and cost-aware at scale.

The defining challenge: agentic development in the cloud

Most AI coding adoption stops at the laptop — one engineer, one agent, one local checkout. That ceiling is low, and moving past it is the signature technical challenge of this role.

You will build the infrastructure that runs agentic development in the cloud: ephemeral, reproducible, isolated environments where many agents work concurrently on real Motive codebases, run real tests against real dependencies, and open real pull requests — without an engineer babysitting a terminal, and without compromising security or blowing up spend.

This is a hard distributed-systems and platform problem, not a tooling procurement exercise. Done right, engineers stop being throughput-bound by their own machines and start operating as reviewers and directors of parallel work. We want a leader who finds that problem exciting and has the platform depth to solve it.

What you'll own

AI-driven development lifecycle (AI-DLC)

Translate Motive's AI-driven development direction into an executable multi-year plan — how agents plan, generate, test, review, and operate under human direction, what "human in the loop" means at each stage, and where engineers spend their time as a result.
Evaluate, select, and roll out AI developer tools (coding agents, code review, test generation, incident investigation, documentation) and build the internal scaffolding — context, MCP servers, evals, guardrails — that makes them effective on Motive's actual codebases rather than on a demo repo.
Stand up a rigorous LLM and agent evaluation practice: benchmarks, offline and online evals, quality and cost regression tracking, and a defensible model and vendor selection process that survives a fast-moving landscape.
Own the governance layer with Security, Legal, and Platform: acceptable use, code provenance and licensing, secrets and data handling, and audit trails for AI-generated changes.
Define and report the adoption and impact metrics that tell us whether this is actually working — not just seat counts and enthusiasm.
Bring the organization along. Drive enablement, internal advocacy, and the cultural shift from "write code, then review" to continuous review of agent-generated work.

Cloud-based agentic development infrastructure

Build and own the platform that runs agentic development in the cloud: on-demand, reproducible, isolated workspaces provisioned per task, with the right source, dependencies, secrets, and services already in place.
Design for concurrency and safety — sandboxed execution, least-privilege credentials, network egress controls, and blast-radius limits so many agents can run against real codebases without becoming a security or reliability incident.
Make agent runs fast and cheap: warm environment pools, caching and snapshotting, incremental builds, and test selection so a cloud agent loop is measured in minutes, not tens of minutes.
Own the orchestration and control plane — queueing, scheduling, autoscaling on Kubernetes, session lifecycle, artifact and log retention, and observability into what agents did and why.
Own unit economics. Instrument per-task and per-agent cost, set budgets and quotas, and keep the platform financially sustainable as usage scales across the org.
Build the human interface layer: how engineers dispatch work to cloud agents, monitor fleets of concurrent runs, review and merge results, and intervene when a run goes sideways.
Design for multi-region (US and EU) from the start, with configuration-driven rather than hardcoded regional behavior, and honor data residency and code-egress constraints.

Developer Experience

Own the inner loop end to end: local and cloud development environments, code search and navigation, IDE and agent tooling, dependency management, and onboarding time-to-first-PR.
Treat developers as your customers. Run regular DevEx research — surveys, interviews, instrumented telemetry — and publish a prioritized backlog the whole engineering org can see.
Define and drive the internal developer platform: golden paths, service scaffolding, and self-service capabilities that make the right way the easy way.

Developer infrastructure and engineering velocity

Own build systems, CI/CD, artifact and release pipelines, and the platform's outer loop across a Rails monolith, Go services, mobile, and embedded/firmware codebases.
Drive step-function improvements in DORA and velocity metrics: PR lead time, build and CI duration, CI reliability and flake rate, change failure rate, and time to restore.
Make cost, scale, and reliability of the developer platform a first-class concern — including multi-region (US and EU) behavior and configuration flexibility rather than hardcoded assumptions.

Testing and quality engineering

Own the testing strategy and frameworks: unit, integration, contract, end-to-end, hardware-in-the-loop, and performance. Drive test reliability, isolation, and speed so engineers trust the signal.
Build the infrastructure that makes high-quality testing cheap: fixtures, factories, test data management, environment provisioning, parallelization, and flake detection and quarantine.
Partner with quality and release engineering to shift quality left without slowing teams down.

Leadership

Lead a multi-team organization as a manager of managers, hiring and developing engineering managers and senior/staff-plus ICs.
Run an org distributed across North American and Asian time zones with genuine care for handoffs, overlap hours, on-call fairness, and inclusion — not just calendar math.
Operate as a peer to product and infrastructure leaders, influence a large engineering org without direct authority, and communicate strategy and results credibly to executives.

What we're looking for

Required

12+ years in software engineering with 6+ years leading engineering teams, including 2+ years as a manager of managers (Director, Senior Manager of Managers, or equivalent scope).
A real developer background — you have shipped and operated production systems, and engineers respect your technical judgment.
Deep DevOps and infrastructure depth: CI/CD, build systems, containers and Kubernetes, infrastructure as code (Terraform), cloud platforms (AWS preferred), and observability.
Demonstrated ownership of developer productivity, developer platform, or developer infrastructure at meaningful scale (hundreds of engineers or a large multi-language codebase), with measurable velocity outcomes you can describe.
Hands-on experience with modern AI developer tooling and a clear, opinionated point of view on where agentic development genuinely helps and where it does not.
Experience building or operating cloud-based development or execution environments — remote dev environments, ephemeral CI/build workers, container sandboxing, or multi-tenant compute platforms — including the security and cost controls that make them viable at scale.
Practical understanding of LLM evaluation — how to benchmark models and agents for coding tasks, how to measure quality and cost, and how to avoid being sold a demo.
Strong empathy for developers: you instrument the pain, listen to it, and prioritize accordingly rather than shipping platforms nobody adopts.
Experience leading distributed teams across multiple time zones.

Preferred

Experience with a large monolith undergoing modernization, and with polyglot environments (Ruby on Rails, Go, mobile, embedded).
Background in test infrastructure at scale — flake reduction, test selection, parallelization, hermetic environments.
Experience running platform work as a product: roadmaps, adoption funnels, internal customers, feature-flagged rollouts.
Familiarity with multi-region deployment and data residency constraints (US/EU).
Open source contribution, developer community involvement, or public writing on developer productivity or AI-assisted engineering.

Pay Transparency

Your compensation may be based on several factors, including education, work experience, and certifications. For certain roles, total compensation may include restricted stock units. Motive offers benefits including health, pharmacy, optical and dental care benefits, paid time off, sick time off, short term and long term disability coverage, life insurance as well as 401k contribution (all benefits are subject to eligibility requirements). Job Description:

About The Role

The Corporate AVP, Underwriting Risk & Governance is accountable for maintaining the organization's underwriting philosophy, risk appetite, technical standards, and governance framework across all life and health insurance businesses. The role serves as a corporate risk subject matter expert on mortality, morbidity, product, underwriting, and fraud risks, providing underwriting risk management guidance to business units globally, with particular emphasis on emerging risks, high-net-worth markets, and the impact of underwriting and product design decisions on long-term business performance.

The incumbent will lead the evaluation and approval of underwriting and product-related risk initiatives, assess the mortality and morbidity implications of underwriting requirement changes, product innovations, and distribution strategies, and ensure alignment with corporate risk management objectives, with primary focus on our Asia business units and Private Wealth business. The role provides technical leadership to underwriters and input to actuarial, product development, and risk management teams on underwriting-specific risk while championing sound underwriting practices, risk governance, and sustainable growth.

Operating in a highly collaborative, consultative, and project-oriented environment, the Corporate AVP, Underwriting Risk & Governance will lead complex initiatives across the Asia business units and jurisdictions, influence business unit underwriting leadership and risk management decision-making, and represent the organization on underwriting and insurance industry matters under the direction of the Corporate Chief Underwriter.

Key Responsibilities

Enterprise Underwriting Governance

Support and champion corporate underwriting philosophy, risk appetite, and underwriting governance standards.
Provide enterprise oversight of underwriting practices across life, health, critical illness, disability, and medical reimbursement products.
Evaluate proposed changes to underwriting requirements, underwriting evidence, accelerated underwriting programs, automation initiatives, and digital underwriting solutions.
Assess and communicate the mortality and morbidity implications associated with underwriting and product design changes.

Mortality and Morbidity Risk Management

Evaluate mortality and morbidity risks associated with existing and proposed products, underwriting methodologies, and distribution strategies.
Assess the impact of product features, underwriting evidence requirements, and benefit structures on expected mortality and morbidity outcomes.
Partner with actuarial, product, and risk management teams to monitor emerging experience trends and recommend mitigation strategies.
Provide technical leadership on mortality and morbidity risk management across multiple markets.

Product and Anti-Selection Risk Assessment

Assess product design features for anti-selection, fraud, claims, and sustainability risks.
Identify underwriting controls, medical requirements, and risk management measures necessary to mitigate adverse selection and fraud exposure.
Provide risk guidance during new product development and product enhancement activities.
Evaluate the potential impact of product design changes on underwriting outcomes and claims experience.

Fraud Risk Oversight

Identify emerging fraud risks and vulnerabilities within underwriting and product frameworks.
Recommend underwriting, medical, and operational controls designed to mitigate fraud exposure.
Partner with claims, investigations, and risk management teams to identify trends and strengthen preventive measures.

High

Worth and Complex Risk Expertise

Provide technical leadership on high-net-worth and Private Wealth underwriting practices, particularly within Asian markets.
Evaluate large face amount and complex financial underwriting cases.
Monitor market developments and emerging risk trends impacting high-net-worth and Private Wealth business.
Support business units in developing prudent underwriting strategies for complex and high-exposure risks.

Retention and Reinsurance Management

Provide leadership and guidance regarding retention management practices.
Evaluate retention limits, concentration risk, and reinsurance effectiveness.
Partner with reinsurance stakeholders as permitted to ensure alignment between underwriting strategies and risk transfer objectives.

Strategic Leadership

Lead complex cross-functional underwriting initiatives involving multiple business units, jurisdictions, and product lines.
Influence senior leaders and business partners on underwriting, mortality, morbidity, and product risk matters.
Provide strategic recommendations balancing growth opportunities with responsible risk management.
Serve as a trusted advisor to the Corporate Chief Underwriter on emerging underwriting and insurance risks.

Technical Thought Leadership

Research emerging medical, underwriting, product, and industry developments.
Participate in the development and maintenance of underwriting manuals, medical guidelines, and risk assessment standards.
Translate emerging medical evidence and industry research into practical underwriting guidance.
Represent the organization externally through industry associations, conferences, forums, and professional organizations.

What You'll Need To Succeed

Minimum 15 years of progressive life and health underwriting experience.
Minimum 5 years holding an individual underwriting approval authority of at least $30 million (preferred).
Significant experience assessing complex mortality and morbidity risks.
Experience underwriting high-net-worth and large face amount business, including exposure to Asian insurance markets.
Demonstrated experience evaluating underwriting implications of life, health, disability, critical illness, hospital indemnity, and medical reimbursement products.
Proven experience leading complex underwriting, governance, or risk initiatives across multiple business units or jurisdictions.
Experience working with reinsurance and retention management frameworks.
Experience developing underwriting philosophy, guidelines, manuals, and risk governance standards.
Proven ability to influence business risk management and underwriting leaders.
Strong strategic thinking and risk assessment capabilities.
Exceptional communication, presentation, and stakeholder management skills.
Ability to work independently with minimal direction while managing multiple concurrent priorities.
Strong collaboration skills with the ability to drive alignment across diverse stakeholders.
Comfortable operating in a dynamic environment focused on governance, consultation, project leadership, innovation, and enterprise risk oversight rather than production underwriting activities.

Preferred Designations

FALU
FLMI
Additional designations in risk management, supplemental health, or related disciplines.

Being a member of the Sun Life family, a group of people united by our Purpose: to help Clients and Employees achieve lifetime financial security and live healthier lives.
In 2024, Sun Life ranked among the top 100 most sustainable global corporations by Corporate Knights for the 15th consecutive year, leading Canadian insurers.
We are proud to be on the 2024 Best Workplaces in Canada list by Great Place to Work.
We’re also listed as one of the Best Workplaces for Women and Best Workplaces with Most Trusted Executive Teams.
Our unique Sabbatical Program gives you the opportunity to take up to 6 weeks off, every five years.
Care Days available for self-care or care of others (i.e., family or others you may support) and Sick Days to support your well-being.

The Base Pay range is for the primary location for which the job is posted. It may vary depending on the work location of the successful candidate or other factors. In addition to Base Pay, eligible Sun Life employees participate in various incentive plans, payment under which is discretionary and subject to individual and company performance. Certain sales focused roles have sales incentive plans based on individual or group sales results.

Diversity and inclusion have always been at the core of our values at Sun Life. A diverse workforce with wide perspectives and creative ideas benefits our Clients, the communities where we operate and all of us as colleagues. We welcome applications from qualified individuals from all backgrounds.

Persons with disabilities who need accommodation in the application process, or those needing job postings in an alternative format, may e-mail a request to thebrightside@sunlife.com.

jobs.title: Director of Product, AI Growth
jobs.description:
1Password is growing. We’ve surpassed $500M in ARR and we’re continuing to accelerate, earning a spot on the Forbes Cloud 100 for four years in a row and teaming up with iconic partners like Oracle Red Bull Racing. 

 About 1Password 
 At 1Password, we’re building the foundation for a safe, productive digital future. Our mission is to unleash employee productivity without compromising security by ensuring every identity is authentic, every application sign-in is secure, and every device is trusted. We innovated the market-leading enterprise password manager and pioneered Unified Access Management, a new cybersecurity category built for the way people and AI agents work today. As one of the most loved brands in cybersecurity, we take a human-centric approach in everything from product strategy to user experience. Over 180,000 businesses, from Fortune 100 leaders to the world’s most innovative AI companies, trust 1Password to help their teams securely adopt the SaaS and AI tools they need to do their best work. 

 If you're excited about the opportunity to contribute to the digital safety of millions, to work alongside a team of curious, driven individuals, and to solve hard problems in a fast-paced, dynamic environment, then we want to hear from you. Come join us and help shape a safer, simpler digital future. 

 This is a Director-level individual contributor role, designed for an experienced leader who drives strategic impact through deep expertise, cross-functional influence, and ownership of key initiatives rather than direct people management.

 Reporting to the Senior Director of Product, the Director of Product, AI Growth grows 1Password's new business in artificial intelligence. In this role, you own driving growth for our AI opportunities by identifying which customers we target, which outcomes we win on, and proving it with design customers. You scale growth through our go-to-market organization and through partnerships with the agent ecosystem and channel partners.

 How we’re using AI today 
 Our Engineering, Product, and Design teams are thoughtfully integrating AI across the full software and product development lifecycle to move faster without sacrificing quality or security. In practice, that looks like engineers using AI-assisted coding tools to accelerate reviews and catch bugs earlier, product managers synthesizing user research at scale, and designers rapidly prototyping and iterating with AI-generated mockups. We approach AI the same way we approach security: with clear principles, human accountability at every consequential decision point, and rigorous evaluation before anything ships to customers.

 This is a remote opportunity within Canada and the US.

 What we're looking for: 
 Minimum of 8 years of product management experience, including experience carrying a revenue or adoption target, with a preference for experience in security products, agentic products, or developer tools.

 Experience owning the strategy for a new product area or market entry, and taking it from hypothesis to customers running in production.

 Experience working directly with enterprise customers on a technical deployment, as the person accountable for the outcome, and turning what those deployments proved into a repeatable motion a sales team can run.

 Experience building technology partnerships and integrations, including judging where a product should sit in a larger technology ecosystem and working with business development on commercial terms.

 Technical depth to hold a credible conversation with developers and security architects about how AI agents are built, deployed, and given access to systems.

 Demonstrated ability to build alignment across go-to-market and engineering teams toward a shared goal, without direct authority over either.

 Demonstrated ability to make decisions and move work forward with incomplete information in a fast-changing market.

 Takes ownership end to end, including the work that falls between teams.

 Works AI-first: uses agents in daily work, and applies their own judgement to decisions, product taste, and customer and internal relationships.

 Preferred: familiarity with agentic access products, meaning the products that give AI agents credentials and access to the systems they work in.

 What you can expect: 

 Growth strategy
 Own the growth thesis for 1Password's AI opportunities, covering the customer segments we target, the outcomes we deliver that we win on, and the workflows we get embedded into. Revise it as evidence arrives from customers, partners, and the market.

 Form and test hypotheses using customer feedback, product usage data, partner input, and market research gathered with the go-to-market, product, user experience, and product marketing teams.

 Lead a weekly business review that brings the voice of the customer, field feedback, and product usage telemetry into one view, so the team can refine targets, forecast the roadmap's impact on growth, and prioritize the blockers that hold adoption back.

 Identify what stops customers from adopting, and drive each blocker to a resolution with the product team that owns it.

 Design customer program
 Run the design customer program for new artificial intelligence opportunities, from selecting customers through to delivered outcomes.

 Act as the general contractor for each design customer: the single person accountable for getting that customer deployed on 1Password for their agentic access, and for delivering the security and convenience outcomes they came for. Coordinate every team the deployment touches, and build what it requires together with a forward deployed engineering team.

 Bring in solutions engineering, customer success, and product managers to help each customer reach their goal, and run feature betas with the product managers who own those features.

 Turn what the program proves into the repeatable signal the company needs to scale, meaning the customer evidence, the deployment pattern, and the measured outcomes that the go-to-market and channel teams build sales plays on.

 Improve the program each cycle so it reaches more design customers, raises delivery success rates and customer satisfaction, and shortens the time it takes the company to commercialize a new product.

 Partnerships
 Decide where 1Password should play in the customer's artificial intelligence stack to deliver the most customer value in securing agent access. Agent access can be controlled at several points in that stack, so weigh those points and choose the ones that solve the most of the customer's problem, rather than the ones we fit into most easily. Base the call on how customers run AI today and on how the industry is evolving.

 Identify and pursue the partnerships that let us play at those points and that complete an end-to-end customer outcome, meaning the outcome a customer cannot reach with 1Password alone.

 Work with partners to deliver integrations, and find the patterns that let us repeat an integration across similar partners instead of building each one from scratch.

 Work with the business development team to structure commercial relationships that grow both companies' business and deliver value to shared customers.

 Scale through the field and the developer community
 Work with product enablement to build demos and enablement content that the field and our channel partners can use without your involvement.

 Work with developer relations to grow adoption organically among developers, through reference architectures, sample code, and open source contributions.

 Travel
 Travel to design customer sites, partner meetings, and industry events approximately 10 to 20% of a given year.

 USA-based roles only: The annual base salary for this role is between $238,000 USD and $357,000 USD, plus immediate participation in 1Password's benefits program (health, dental, 401k and many others), utilization of our generous paid time off, an equity grant and, where applicable, participation in our incentive programs.

 Canada-based roles only: The annual base salary for this role is between $208,000 CAD and $312,000 CAD, plus immediate participation in 1Password’s generous benefits program (health, dental, RRSP and many others), utilization of our generous paid time off, an equity grant and, where applicable, participation in our incentive programs.

At 1Password, we approach each individual's compensation with a promise of fair market value and internal equity commensurate with experience and specific skill set.

 This posting is for an existing vacancy. 

 Our culture 
At 1Password, we prioritize collaboration, clear and transparent communication, receptiveness to feedback, and alignment with our core values: keep it simple, lead with honesty, and put people first. 

You’ll be part of a team that challenges the status quo, and is excited to experiment and iterate in search of the best solution. That said, 1Password is not for everyone. Our work is demanding, we strive for excellence, and the pace is fast. We need people who are keen to take on challenging problems, who seek feedback to grow, and who are driven to make an impact. If you're looking for a place where you can settle into a comfortable routine, this might not be the right fit for you. We’re looking for individuals who are proven experts in their fields, as well as those who are highly adaptable, can thrive in ambiguity and through change, are curious, and above all deliver results. 

 How we work with AI 
We are committed to leveraging cutting-edge technology—including AI—to achieve our mission. We also understand that thinking critically about AI in its current forms will help us create better solutions for our customers and ourselves with its future forms, which will help us continue to close the gap between security and privacy and achieve our mission. We want team members at all levels to take the approach of actively learning AI best practices, identifying opportunities to apply AI in meaningful ways, and driving innovative solutions in their daily work. Embracing the future of AI isn't just encouraged—it's an essential part of how we will be successful at 1Password.

 This approach extends to our hiring process—candidates are welcome to use AI tools responsibly and thoughtfully during the application process. To us, this means we do ask that you join live interviews without using AI tools so we can get to know how you communicate, solve problems, and collaborate with others.

 Our approach to remote work 
We believe in the power of remote work, but recognize that in-person connection is important to help us achieve our mission. While we are a remote-first company, travel for in-person engagement is a part of almost all roles, and we require our employees to be ready and willing to take part. Frequency will depend on role and responsibilities, and may include, but is not limited to: annual department-wide offsites, team meetings, and customer/industry events.

 What we offer 
We believe in working hard, and rewarding that hard work through our benefits. While not an exhaustive list, here is a glance at what we currently offer: 

 Health and wellbeing 
👶 Maternity and parental leave top-up programs
🩺 Competitive health benefits
🏝 Generous PTO policy 

 Growth and future 
📈 RSU program for most employees
💸 Retirement matching program
🔑 Free 1Password account

 Community 
🤝 Paid volunteer days 
🏆 Peer-to-peer recognition through Bonusly
🌎 Remote-first work environment
 *Some roles in our GTM team are currently being hired for in-person hybrid work in Toronto and Austin. These roles will specify on the posting. 

 You belong here. 

 1Password is proud to be an equal opportunity employer. We are committed to fostering an inclusive, diverse and equitable workplace that is built on trust, support and respect. We welcome all individuals and do not discriminate on the basis of gender identity and expression, race, ethnicity, disability, sexual orientation, colour, religion, creed, gender, national origin, age, marital status, pregnancy, sex, citizenship, education, languages spoken or veteran status. Be yourself, find your people and share the things you love. 

 Accommodation is available upon request at any point during our recruitment process. If you require an accommodation, please speak to your talent acquisition partner or email us at nextbit@agilebits.com and we’ll work to meet your needs. 

 Remote work is a part of our DNA. Given that our company was founded remotely in 2005, we can safely say we're experts at building remote culture. That said, remote work at 1Password does mean working from your home country. If you've got questions or concerns about this, your talent partner would be happy to address them with you.

Experience establishing architecture governance processes and reference models within regulated industries.

jobs.title: Transfer Pricing - Financial Transactions, Director
jobs.description:
A career within our Transfer Pricing & Customs practice will provide you with the opportunity to help multinational clients navigate complex cross-border tax, trade and financing matters. Our team advises clients on transfer pricing, customs valuation, trade compliance and international tax planning, helping them achieve compliant, commercially sound outcomes aligned with evolving global regulatory expectations. In this role, you will focus on financial transactions transfer pricing, including interest rate analyses, debt capacity, cash pooling, guarantees, hedging, providing services related to documentation, planning and dispute resolution matters. You will primarily support complex intercompany financing projects and collaborate closely with tax, treasury, valuation and legal stakeholders. Driven by curiosity, you are a reliable, contributing member of a team. In our fast-paced environment, you are expected to adapt to working with a variety of clients and team members, each presenting varying challenges and scopes. Every experience is an opportunity to learn and grow. You are expected to take ownership and consistently deliver quality work that drives value for our clients and success as a team. As you navigate through the Firm, you build a brand for yourself, opening doors to more opportunities.

The opportunity

As a Transfer Pricing Director focused on Financial Transactions, you’ll work as part of a team of problem solvers, helping clients address complex intercompany financing issues while delivering high-quality client service and practical, supportable recommendations. Responsibilities include but are not limited to:

Lead and manage financial transactions transfer pricing projects, including intercompany loan pricing, debt capacity analyses, guarantee fee analyses, cash pooling arrangements and related documentation
Oversee multiple client engagements, ensuring quality and timely delivery
Develop robust economic analyses that consider credit risk, capital markets data, borrower and lender perspectives, and the commercial terms of related-party financing arrangements
Prepare and review technical memoranda, transfer pricing reports and client deliverables that clearly explain methodologies, assumptions, conclusions and supporting evidence
Advise clients on transfer pricing planning, controversy, and audit defence matters involving intercompany financing transactions
Build and grow client relationships by understanding clients’ businesses, treasury policies, financing structures and broader tax objectives
Use financial data, market evidence and technology-enabled tools to develop efficient, defensible and insightful analyses
Explore and embrace emerging technologies, including artificial intelligence, and guide the team in incorporating these tools to enhance the quality and efficiency of client service delivery
Collaborate with PwC tax, valuation and international network teams to deliver integrated advice on complex cross-border financing issues
Guide, coach and develop team members by providing clear direction, technical guidance and timely feedback on financial transactions transfer pricing work
Contribute to business development by identifying client needs, supporting proposals and helping market financial transactions transfer pricing services to existing and prospective clients
Uphold the firm’s code of ethics and business conduct

What You’ll Bring

Demonstrated experience in transfer pricing at the Director level, with significant experience advising on financial transactions and intercompany financing arrangements:
Strong knowledge of financial transactions transfer pricing concepts, including arm’s length interest rate setting, credit ratings, credit risk, debt capacity, guarantees, cash pooling and capital structure considerations
The CFA or CPA designation is a strong asset
MBA, MA or advanced degree in Economics, Tax, Finance or Business Administration, or an equivalent combination of education and professional experience
Strong research, writing and quantitative analytical skills, with comfort working with detailed financial analysis, capital markets data and technical transfer pricing guidance
Ability to explain complex financial and economic concepts clearly to clients, tax authorities and internal stakeholders
Ability to think creatively, solve complex problems and develop practical, commercially grounded recommendations
Interest in identifying tax and business consulting opportunities and contributing to the growth of financial transactions transfer pricing services
High motivation, initiative and interest in developing yourself and others, with the ability to manage, coach and retain a team of tax professionals

This position ensures continuity and upholds our standards of excellence following the departure of a valued team member.

The salary range for this position is $152,000 - $202,000. The posted salary range represents the expected hiring range for PwC locations in major city centers. Given our national recruiting approach, ranges may vary for positions in other locations. At PwC Canada, base salary is determined by your skills, experience, qualifications and work location. In addition to base salary, eligible employees may have opportunities to participate in variable incentive pay programs which are designed to reward individual and firm-wide achievements.  We are committed to offering competitive compensation and adhering to all relevant pay transparency legislation. During the hiring process, our Talent Acquisition team will provide details about our comprehensive total rewards package. 

Why you’ll love PwC

We’re inspiring and empowering our people to change the world. Powered by the latest technology, you’ll be a part of diverse teams helping public and private clients build trust and deliver sustained outcomes. This meaningful work, and our continuous development environment, will take your career to the next level. We reward your impact, and support your wellbeing, through a competitive compensation package, inclusive benefits and flexibility programs that will help you thrive in work and life. Learn more about our Application Process and Total Rewards Package at: https://jobs-ca.pwc.com/ca/en/life-at-pwc

We're looking for a Senior Vice President, Strategy
to lead and evolve our strategy practice across the Americas. You Will Thrive In This Role If You Are

A curious problem solver who challenges the status quo

Experienced in Agile methodologies and consulting (a plus)

Role Responsibilities

Executive Client Advisory

Build trusted relationships that open, expand, and strengthen client partnerships.

Strategic Pursuits & Business Development

We’ll help you succeed in a globally connected powerhouse of diverse teams and take your career wherever you want it to go.

The Assistant Director partners closely with Consumer Industry leadership, including the Industry Leader, sector leaders, service line leaders, and Global Client Service Partners (GCSPs), to enable an integrated, client‑centric growth agenda aligned to Consumer market priorities.

The Assistant Director, Strategy & Operations (Consumer) reports to the Director of Operations, Clients & Industries, with day‑to‑day alignment to the Consumer Industry Leader. Performance is evaluated based on contribution to Consumer revenue growth, sales and pipeline effectiveness, and overall operational excellence.

This job posting relates to an existing vacancy within our organization.

Key Responsibilities

Enabling Consumer Growth

Facilitate annual strategic planning for the Consumer Industry, working with stakeholders across service lines, finance, alliances, accounts, business development, and markets to define and execute Consumer‑specific priorities.
Project manage strategic growth initiatives within the Consumer Industry plan, leading cross‑functional teams (including BCM and Markets stakeholders) to deliver programs and campaigns that drive measurable market impact.
Support Consumer account planning and execution by cascading account management best practices to GCSPs across priority and replenishment accounts, encouraging cross‑service‑line teaming and value creation.
Support execution of the Client Experience (CX) program for Consumer clients, in partnership with CX and Business Development teams, ensuring high‑quality client interactions, insights, and feedback loops.
Champion Consumer account and pipeline reviews, ensuring a regular cadence, strong leadership engagement, and clear, actionable outcomes.

Data Literacy & Decision Support

Analyze and interpret Consumer performance data (revenue, sales, pipeline, forecasting) to support Consumer leadership forums and decision‑making; identify trends, risks, and opportunities and recommend corrective actions.
Track Consumer BD and marketing investments and perform variance analysis to support margin improvement and investment optimization.
Modernize Consumer reporting outputs by adopting innovative tools and practices, ensuring consistent definition, interpretation, and use of Consumer performance KPIs.

Collaboration & Process Optimization
