jobs.description:
Directeur(trice) Principal(e) de la Technologie et de l'Innovation

À propos de Crowe BGK

Depuis 75 ans, Crowe BGK S.E.N.C.R.L. est un chef de file de confiance en matière de services de comptabilité et de conseil au Canada. Notre équipe compte plus de 250 professionnels qui servent nos clients à partir de nos bureaux de Montréal et d’Ottawa. Nous offrons des services d’audit, de fiscalité, de conseil et de consultation, aidant les particuliers et les sociétés privées à relever des défis complexes. Nous sommes fiers d’avoir été nommés parmi les 100 meilleurs employeurs de PME au Canada et parmi les meilleurs employeurs de Montréal, car nous croyons qu’il est essentiel de créer un milieu de travail où les gens se sentent soutenus, valorisés et inspirés à progresser.

Nous sommes à la recherche d’un(e) Directeur(trice) Principal(e) de la Technologie et de l'Innovation

expérimenté(e) et pratique pour aider Crowe BGK à maintenir un environnement technologique fiable et à faire progresser l’utilisation des logiciels à l’échelle du cabinet. La personne retenue combinera une compréhension des processus d’affaires, une discipline opérationnelle et une expertise technologique afin d’améliorer le service à la clientèle, l’efficacité, l’évolutivité et l’expérience employé.

Vous Serez Responsable De

Stratégie et gouvernance des logiciels d’entreprise

Élaborer et maintenir la feuille de route pluriannuelle des applications du cabinet, l’inventaire des logiciels, le modèle de propriété et la gouvernance pour la sélection, les accès, les changements, les intégrations, les renouvellements et le retrait.
Identifier les lacunes en matière de capacités, les dédoublements, les outils sous-utilisés ou non pris en charge ainsi que les occasions émergentes; conseiller le ou la COFO, les associé(e)s et la direction sur les priorités, les investissements, les compromis, la normalisation et les coûts.

Amélioration des processus d’affaires et innovation

Analyser et repenser les processus dans les services à la clientèle et les fonctions corporatives, en mobilisant les parties prenantes afin de résoudre les irritants, les lacunes de contrôle, le travail à refaire, les problèmes de données et les besoins non satisfaits avant l’automatisation.
Utiliser les données et les commentaires pour prioriser les améliorations à forte valeur ajoutée et évaluer les flux de travail, l’automatisation, l’analytique, l’intelligence artificielle et les technologies émergentes en tenant compte de la confidentialité, de la qualité, des contrôles et de la supervision humaine appropriés.

Évaluation des logiciels et analyses de rentabilité

Traduire les besoins d’affaires en exigences mesurables sur les plans fonctionnel, technique, des données, de la sécurité, de l’intégration, des contrôles, du service et des utilisateurs; diriger les démonstrations, les projets pilotes, les vérifications de références, les grilles d’évaluation, la diligence raisonnable des fournisseurs et la comparaison objective des risques et des solutions de rechange.
Préparer et présenter des analyses de rentabilité pour les décisions d’aller de l’avant ou non, couvrant le coût total de possession, le rendement du capital investi, les échéanciers, les ressources, l’incidence du changement, la formation, l’atténuation des risques, le soutien et les coûts de sortie; soutenir les négociations commerciales et contractuelles.

Gouvernance et responsabilité de la mise en œuvre

Agir à titre de responsable imputable du volet affaires et technologie, en partenariat avec le ou la gestionnaire de projet attitré(e), afin de définir la portée, les résultats, le budget, les ressources, la gouvernance, les jalons, les droits décisionnels, les risques, les communications et les mesures de succès.
Coordonner les parties prenantes et veiller à la conception des processus, à la configuration, aux intégrations, à la conversion des données, aux essais, aux contrôles, à la formation, à la mise en production, au soutien, à la préparation, à la stabilisation, à l’adoption et à la réalisation des bénéfices; faire remonter les lacunes importantes et maintenir la visibilité auprès de la direction.

Gestion du portefeuille, des fournisseurs, des données et des risques

Gérer les budgets logiciels, les licences, l’utilisation, les renouvellements, les fournisseurs, les contrats, les niveaux de service, les indicateurs du portefeuille, la rationalisation et le retrait des solutions.
Collaborer avec les ressources en TI, cybersécurité, protection de la vie privée, affaires juridiques et gestion des risques afin d’encadrer les intégrations, les données, les contrôles d’accès, la continuité des activités, les risques liés aux tiers, l’intelligence artificielle et l’automatisation.

Leadership du changement et mobilisation des parties prenantes

Établir des relations de confiance avec les associé(e)s, les dirigeant(e)s, le personnel, les fournisseurs et les prestataires de services; diriger les employé(e)s attitré(e)s et les équipes interfonctionnelles en assurant une responsabilisation claire et une forte orientation vers le service.
Diriger les communications, la formation, l’adoption, la documentation, le soutien et la propriété des applications; développer des ambassadeurs internes, contribuer au plan d’affaires du cabinet et tenir le ou la COFO ainsi que les parties prenantes informés.

Autorité et responsabilité

Responsable du portefeuille de logiciels, de la feuille de route des applications, des normes de gouvernance et de la direction des équipes de mise en œuvre des TI et des processus dans le cadre de la stratégie et des budgets approuvés; peut exiger les examens appropriés en matière d’affaires, de sécurité, de protection de la vie privée, d’intégration, de contrôle et de mise en œuvre.
Recommande la sélection, le séquencement, le renouvellement, l’expansion, la consolidation ou le retrait des logiciels; peut suspendre ou faire remonter les préoccupations non résolues et est responsable de la qualité des recommandations, de la gouvernance de la mise en œuvre, de l’adoption, de la stabilisation et des bénéfices approuvés.

Mesures de succès

Gérer un inventaire à jour des logiciels, une propriété claire, une gouvernance rigoureuse, une feuille de route approuvée, des analyses de rentabilité crédibles et des dépenses contrôlées.
Réaliser les mises en œuvre avec une gouvernance, une préparation, des contrôles, une adoption et un soutien durable efficaces, ainsi qu’avec la réalisation des bénéfices approuvés.
Obtenir des améliorations mesurables en matière d’efficacité, de capacité, de qualité, de fiabilité des données, d’expérience employé et client, de performance des fournisseurs, de gestion des risques et de confiance des parties prenantes.

Les Qualifications Qui Comptent

Baccalauréat en systèmes d’information, administration des affaires, comptabilité, finance, informatique, génie ou dans un domaine connexe; une combinaison équivalente de formation et d’expérience sera considérée.
Sept années ou plus d’expérience progressive en logiciels, systèmes d’affaires, amélioration des processus, transformation technologique, gestion de produits ou gestion de programmes, dont au moins trois années dans un rôle de leadership ou de responsabilité à l’échelle de l’entreprise.
Une expérience dans un cabinet comptable ou un autre environnement de services professionnels est privilégiée, avec une compréhension des décisions dirigées par les associé(e)s, du service à la clientèle soumis à des échéanciers, de la confidentialité et du changement entre les groupes de pratique.
Succès démontré dans la direction d’évaluations de logiciels, d’analyses de rentabilité, de sélection de fournisseurs et de mise en œuvre de solutions SaaS à l’échelle du cabinet ou de l’entreprise.
Expérience pratique de la cartographie et de la refonte des processus, des exigences, des essais, de la formation, de la gestion du changement et de la réalisation des bénéfices.

Vous Pouvez Compter Sur Nous Pour

Une rémunération compétitive
Un modèle de travail hybride flexible
Des assurances collectives complètes dès le premier jour d’emploi pour soutenir votre bien-être global
Des vacances généreuses et 8 journées personnelles pour responsabilités familiales
Des fermetures du cabinet pendant les Fêtes pour décrocher pleinement
Des vendredis d’été avec fermeture hâtive durant la saison estivale
Stationnement gratuit sur place ou remboursement du transport en commun
Une allocation annuelle mieux-être pour soutenir la santé physique et mentale
Une allocation pour l’aménagement du bureau à domicile afin d’assurer un environnement confortable et productif
Une culture de bureau dynamique et accueillante, où les chiens sont les bienvenus et où l’énergie est au rendez-vous. Entre les 5 à 7 animés, les cours de spinning hebdomadaires, les ateliers de peinture en équipe, les soirées quiz et karaoké, il y a toujours une activité rassembleuse. Sans oublier notre Camp Crowe, une expérience estivale unique remplie d’activités amusantes qui favorisent la camaraderie et créent des souvenirs mémorables

Si vous cherchez un endroit où vos idées comptent et où votre carrière peut s'épanouir, postulez dès aujourd'hui!

Cultivez votre curiosité. Inspirez votre esprit. Façonnez votre carrière.

Nous maintenons un environnement de travail inclusif et offrant des chances égales afin que chaque professionnel de Crowe BGK puisse réaliser son potentiel d'évolution. Nous considérons tous les candidats qualifiés pour un emploi sans distinction de race, de couleur, de religion, de sexe, d'orientation sexuelle, d'identité de genre, d'origine nationale, d'âge, d'état matrimonial, de handicap, de statut d'ancien combattant protégé ou de tout autre facteur protégé par la loi.

Nous remercions tous les candidats pour leur intérêt et nous ne contacterons que ceux que nous souhaitons poursuivre.

Director of Software Technology and Innovation

About Crowe BGK

For 75 years, Crowe BGK LLP has been a trusted leader in accounting and advisory services in Canada. We are a team of 250+ professionals serving clients from our Montreal and Ottawa offices. We provide audit, tax, advisory, and consulting services, helping individuals and private companies navigate complex challenges. We’re proud to be named one of Canada’s Top 100 SME Employers and one of Montreal’s Top Employers, because we believe in creating a workplace where people feel supported, valued, and inspired to grow.

We’re looking for an experienced, hands-on Director of Software Technology and Innovation

to help Crowe BGK maintain a reliable technology environment and advance the use of software across the firm. The successful candidate will combine business process insight, operational discipline, and technology expertise to improve client service, efficiency, scalability, and the employee experience.

You Will Be Accountable For

Enterprise Software Strategy and Governance

Develop and maintain the firm's multi-year application roadmap, software inventory, ownership model, and governance for selection, access, changes, integrations, renewals, and retirement.
Identify capability gaps, duplication, underused or unsupported tools, and emerging opportunities; advise the COFO, partners, and leadership on priorities, investments, trade-offs, standardization, and cost.

Business Process Improvement and Innovation

Analyze and redesign processes across client service and corporate functions, engaging stakeholders to address pain points, control gaps, rework, data issues, and unmet needs before automation.
Use data and feedback to prioritize high-value improvements and evaluate workflow, automation, analytics, artificial intelligence, and emerging technologies with appropriate confidentiality, quality, controls, and human oversight.

Software Evaluation and Business Cases

Translate business needs into measurable functional, technical, data, security, integration, control, service, and use

Job Details

About Salesforce

Salesforce is the #1 AI CRM, where humans with agents drive customer success together. Here, ambition meets action. Tech meets trust. And innovation isn’t a buzzword — it’s a way of life. The world of work as we know it is changing and we're looking for Trailblazers who are passionate about bettering business and the world through AI, driving innovation, and keeping Salesforce's core values at the heart of it all.

Ready to level-up your career at the company leading workforce transformation in the agentic era? You’re in the right place! Agentforce is the future of AI, and you are the future of Salesforce.

The Experience

As the Senior Director within the Salesforce Controllership group, you will be the strategic owner of our Finance system architecture, data flow, and enhancement roadmap. It is a critical leadership position requiring you to bridge the gap between complex accounting requirements and technical execution. You will oversee initiatives, drive the evolution of our Workday Cloud ERP ecosystem, and ensure AI is at the forefront of our financial automation strategy. With Agentforce woven into every layer of our platform, our team builds intelligent systems that automate repetitive subledger flows, elevate strategic accounting tasks, and power better financial decision-making at scale.

What You'll Actually Be Doing

Strategic Record to Report (R2R) Leadership: Direct and oversee comprehensive R2R initiatives involving complex data streams across both revenue and non-revenue business functions.
Systems: Act as the business sponsor for the finance technology stack, deploying ERP enhancements, automation, and reporting infrastructure to reduce manual touchpoints.
Processes: Redesign end-to-end R2R cycles (close, consolidation, statutory reporting) to drive operational efficiency and shorten time-to-insight.
People: Serve as the primary change agent, guiding cross-functional teams through transition periods, breaking down silos between technical and accounting teams, and transforming workforce capabilities to support a modern digital finance organization.

ERP System Ownership: Serve as the primary business owner for the accounting ERP system. Define the strategic vision for system architecture, data integrity, and operational scale.
IT Partnership & Issue Resolution: Partner directly with IT to manage, prioritize, and resolve critical ERP production issues, ensuring minimal disruption to accounting operations.
AI & Automation Roadmap: Champion and lead initiatives to continuously automate and enhance the ERP system, actively identifying and integrating AI-driven solutions to modernize accounting workflows.
Cross-Functional Influence: Act as a central strategic partner. Drive alignment, influence decision-making, and secure buy-in from senior stakeholders across Accounting, Finance, Engineering, and Operations.
AI & Automation Enablement: Identify and deploy with finance transformations high-impact AI/agent use cases to scale automated, data-driven operations across Controllership.
Lead Global Controllership Alignment: Serve as a central integration point to ensure that as we scale, our initiatives are aligned across our Global Process Owners (GPOs), cross-functional partners, and technology teams.
Drive Holistic Stakeholders Engagement: Facilitate alignment across diverse groups (Tax, Treasury, Legal, M&A) to ensure that Controllership initiatives consider the full financial picture and regulatory landscape.
Strategic Decision Support: Lead key strategic projects within the Global Accounting organization, specifically identifying decision bottlenecks and presenting clear facts to the appropriate stakeholders to facilitate resolution.
Technology & Business Liaison: Serve as a key bridge between the Accounting function and the Digital Enterprise Transformation (DET) team. You will help articulate clear business facts, define requirements, and support critical design decisions to ensure our systems support our accounting needs.
Executive Communication & Storytelling: Transform complex project updates and accounting data into clear, compelling narratives. You will act as the content creator for executive presentation

You're Our Person If...

12+ years of progressive experience in accounting, financial systems, or finance transformation, with a strong background in R2R processes.
Technical Acumen - Deep expertise in enterprise-level ERP systems and accounting data architecture.
Strategic Execution - Proven ability to act as a strategic driver rather than a task manager, with a track record of translating complex financial needs into scalable system solutions.
Stakeholder Influence - Exceptional executive communication skills with the ability to influence cross-functional technical and non-technical stakeholders without direct reporting authority.
Forward-Thinking - Demonstrated passion for exploring and implementing emerging technologies, specifically AI and machine learning, within the finance and accounting domain.
Demonstrated track record of successfully designing and implementing process improvements that reduced manual effort and improved accuracy
BA/BS degree is required in Accounting, Finance, Business Administration, Information Systems, or related subject area or equivalent relevant experience required. Experience will be evaluated based on the Core Competencies for the role (e.g. extracurricular leadership roles, military experience, volunteer roles, work experience, etc.
Expertise in US GAAP, IFRS and local statutory requirements; Robust experience with SOX audit framework
You bring exceptional problem-solving skills using structured frameworks to dissect complex operational failures and present technical roadmaps to finance leadership.

You have a combination of prior experience in management or technology consulting focused on transformation and have hands-on Finance Operations experience.
System experience - Workday experience preferred
You have first-hand experience driving AI transformation initiatives, specifically implementing agentic automation and intelligent workflows within Finance.

jobs.title: Associate Director, Global Customer Experience & Compensation Strategy
jobs.description:
About The Role

Within Global Customer Experience (GCX), our mission is to advance the HelloFresh customer relationship from reactive resolution to proactive, trust-building service. The compensation function sits at the heart of that mission: it is the mechanism through which the business acknowledges failures, restores customer confidence, and, when done well, turns a bad experience into a reason to stay.

The Associate Director, Customer Compensation & Policy is responsible for the global strategy, architecture, and governance of how HelloFresh compensates customers across all markets and brands. This is not a policy maintenance role. It is a strategic function that sits at the intersection of customer economics, operational data, behavioral experimentation, and cross-functional influence.

You will own one of the most financially material and customer-sensitive levers in the business. You will shape a multi-year roadmap and hold peers in Operations, Technology, Finance, and Market Leadership accountable for the quality of inputs that determine how well and how efficiently we recover customer trust.

The ideal candidate brings a rare combination: analytical rigor sharp enough to architect a global compensation engine from first principles, and the executive presence to drive adoption across a complex, multi-market organization without formal authority over most of the people they need to move.

What You'll Own

Global Compensation Strategy & Engine Architecture

Own the end-to-end strategic vision for how HelloFresh categorizes customer errors and determines compensation across all markets, brands, and contact channels.
Lead the design and continuous evolution of the compensation engine: along with Tech, you’ll define the the rules, thresholds, segmentation logic, and automation frameworks that govern recovery decisions at scale.
Define the principles that govern trade-offs between customer generosity and cost discipline and translate those principles into operational rules that hold across market complexity and brand variation.
Partner with Technology to ensure the compensation engine is scalable, auditable, and capable of supporting dynamic, AI-assisted decisioning as the product evolves.

Experimentation & Behavioral Economics

Set the global roadmap for compensation experimentation: A/B testing across offer types, value levels, channel timing, and segmentation variables.
Apply behavioral economics frameworks to compensation design understanding how recovery offers shape long-term retention, repurchase behavior, and brand perception, not just immediate satisfaction.
Define the measurement framework for experimentation: what constitutes a successful test, what confidence warrants global rollout, and how results are synthesized into durable policy change.
Partner with Analytics & Insights to ensure test design, sample integrity, and rollout analysis meet a rigorous standard of evidence.

Financial Stewardship & Cost Governance

Own the global compensation P&L line: tracking spend by market, error category, customer segment, and channel — and holding yourself accountable to defined cost-per-incident and avoidable-contact targets.
Identify and close financial leakage: cases where compensation is being issued without policy justification, at incorrect values, or at the wrong frequency.
Build the reporting infrastructure that makes compensation economics visible to GCX leadership, market GMs, and Finance — with the granularity and context needed to drive decisions.
Define the right balance between cost optimization and customer lifetime value investment: not just 'spend less' but 'spend where it earns back.

Fraud Policy & Global Governance

Own the global fraud and abuse prevention framework: the policies, detection logic, thresholds, and escalation paths that protect the business without creating friction for genuine customers.
Lead the governance rhythm for policy: quarterly reviews, market exception management, escalation adjudication, and framework versioning across a multi-brand, multi-market environment.
Act as the final authority on complex, cross-market policy gaps — resolving ambiguity with speed, consistency, and strategic clarity rather than routing decisions upward by default.
Maintain global standards while creating principled space for market-level adaptation where local context genuinely requires it.

Cross-Functional Leadership & Stakeholder Accountability

Represent the compensation function in senior forums translating customer economics into requirements that peers in Operations, Technology, Finance, and Market GMs must respond to.
Hold cross-functional partners accountable for the upstream data quality, operational accuracy, and system reliability that the compensation engine depends on.
Drive adoption of policy changes across markets and brands, building communication and change management plans that make new frameworks land — not just launch.
Influence at VP and Director level across multiple functions; escalate only strategic blockers, not routine alignment.

What You'll Bring

Education

MBA or equivalent postgraduate qualification required.
Undergraduate degree in Economics, Business, Engineering, or a quantitative discipline.

Experience

8–12 years of progressive experience in customer strategy, pricing, operations, or a directly adjacent domain with meaningful exposure to global, multi-market environments.
Demonstrated track record of owning a financially significant operational lever and managing it with both analytical precision and strategic judgment.
Prior experience leading and developing teams; comfort operating as a senior individual contributor and a people leader simultaneously.
Background in subscription commerce, logistics, or consumer-facing operations strongly preferred. Familiarity with the economics of customer recovery in high-volume, low-margin environments is a distinct advantage.

Technical & Analytical

Advanced proficiency in SQL and data analysis; able to build and pressure-test the analytical models that underpin policy decisions without delegating the logic to others.
Fluency with experimentation methodology: test design, statistical significance, holdout analysis, and the translation of results into policy not just reporting.
Experience working with or alongside engineering teams to define product and system requirements for rules-based or AI-assisted decisioning tools.
Comfort with financial modeling: building the business case for compensation investment, forecasting spend impact, and tracking actuals against plan.

Leadership & Influence

Senior executive presence: able to walk into a GM, COO, or CFO conversation with a clear point of view, defend it under pressure, and leave with alignment.
A credible voice with peers and upward stakeholders not because of title, but because of the quality of analysis and clarity of communication.
Structured and decisive under ambiguity: able to make a defensible call with incomplete information and adjust as evidence develops.
Genuinely collaborative across markets and functions able to hold people to standards without damaging the relationships needed to sustain them.

What we offer

Box Discount-Amazing discounts on 1 box per week! 75% discount on weekly HelloFresh and Chefs Plate meal kits AND 50% off weekly Factor meal box.
Health & Wellness-Health & Dental benefits from day 1, a Health Spending Account, unlimited access to the Headspace app to meet your self-care needs, and 25% discount on GoodLife fitness memberships!
RRSP Matching-Competitive RRSP matching program offered
Vacation & PTO-Time off is also an important part of self-care! We offer generous vacation and PTO to help you create a good work-life balance.
Family Benefits-A parental leave top-up program for expectant parents.
Growth & Development-We support your career progression, provide development opportunities, and invest in your continued learning through our organization wide L&D fund.
Work Hard & Have Fun-From team socials to engaging company days, you’ll have plenty of opportunity to experience the fun!
Diversity & Inclusion Initiatives- With impactful ERG’s like FreshPride, Women Empowered and LIMES, we are committed to our diversity, equity & inclusion efforts.

Flexible Hybrid Approach

At HelloFresh, we know that flexible work arrangements are essential in enabling you to do your best work, while balancing your personal and life needs. Offering remote work flexibility, along with the opportunity to interact and collaborate in the office are all a part of creating a great employee experience.

To meet these needs, we are pleased to provide Flexible Hybrid work. Flexible Hybrid is a people-first approach that is based on choice, trust, personalization, and empowers teams to choose when and how often they work from the office and work from home, in addition to team days and company days. This means a minimum of 3 days in office per week.

HelloFresh Canada uses AI-integrated technology to help us process and evaluate applications more efficiently. This includes tools that screen and assess candidate qualifications based on the requirements for this role. While these tools assist our workflow, all final selection decisions are made by our hiring team.

At UBC, we believe that attracting and sustaining a diverse workforce is key to the successful pursuit of excellence in research, innovation, and learning for all faculty, staff and students. Our commitment to employment equity helps achieve inclusion and fairness, brings rich diversity to UBC as a workplace, and creates the necessary conditions for a rewarding career.

Job Description Summary

The Director, Space Planning and Facilities Management is responsible for the overall strategic leadership of the planning, development, management and utilization of Faculty of Medicine Academic Space.

The Director, Space Planning & Facilities Management leads staff and external consultants, ensures appropriate space allocation and management policies and procedures are developed and implemented, space and facility plans are successfully executed to meet the changing needs of the Faculty, key partner’s relationships are built and maintained, and a culture of integrity, collegiality, and agility is fostered.

As most of the Faculty’s 1.8M square feet of Academic Space is built, owned, operated and/or maintained by other agencies and institutions under legislation, utilization agreements, or institutional regulations, the Director initiates, directs, and negotiates on behalf of the Faculty to ensure the Faculty’s space and facilities requirements are met.

Organizational Status

Reports directly to the Managing Director, Operations, Faculty of Medicine.

Leading a cross-functional team of professionals, the Director, Space Planning & Facilities Management provides strategic direction and planning for all aspects of Faculty of Medicine Academic Space to align Faculty goals, objectives, and strategies with those of the University and institutional partners.

With the high volume and complexity of the position requirements, it is important that the successful candidate have a team-oriented and flexible disposition and demonstrated leadership, problem-solving, and collaborative planning skills.

The Director’s primary work site is UBC Vancouver campus. The Director is required to travel to and work at various clinical campuses and academic sites across BC.

Work Performed

Strategic & Tactical Leadership

Represents the Faculty of Medicine’s s interest while interacting with Ministries, Health Authorities and University Leaders regarding academic facilities, capital project requirements, and other related academic space issues. Ensures Health Authority projects conform to Section 45 of the Hospital Act and Academic Space Protocol requirements.
Makes recommendations to Senior Leadership Team on strategic and policy matters related to the allocation, management and utilization of Academic Space, construction and renovation projects, and facility operations.
Resolves Academic Space disputes through negotiations and/or arbitration, developing innovative solutions and approaches to reconcile issues, ensuring that key partners’ relationships are built and maintained.
Forms, leads and participates in University and Health Authority committees and meetings, ensuring that appropriate consultative processes have been followed when developing policies, space and facility plans and reviews or when planning for new capital projects.
Provides strategic guidance and leadership to the Space Planning & Facilities Management Team, ensuring that resources and support are available to optimize performance and productivity within the unit.
Initiates and develops strategic and operational plans for the Space Planning & Facilities Management Team, creating tactics and action plans so that team goals can be achieved.
Provides leadership and direction for change management initiatives and risk management processes, with Health Authorities, University stakeholders, Faculty of Medicine key groups, consultants, contractors and other partners.
Oversees the general administration, project management, renovation and equipment budgets for Space Planning and Facilities Management unit , as required.
Develops projects, procedures, policies and other initiatives intended to maximize the allocation, management and utilization of Academic Space, reduce costs, or improve efficiency of space and facility operations.

Capital Projects Management

Leads short-term & long-term construction project planning for the Faculty of Medicine education programs, overseeing the compilation of requirements and specifications, evaluating and prioritizing options, coordinating funding requests, identifying and securing resources, obtaining financial and contractual approvals, establishing project goals, timelines and budgets.
Oversees capital projects at University and Health Authority facilities across BC, ensuring that functional program and technical requirements, as well as space and other related guidelines and policies as agreed are followed by University and/or Health Authority planners, contractors, architects and other parties, at times within a Public Private Partnership environment.
Ensures that the requirements and best interests of the Faculty of Medicine are realized in each project, integrating and coordinating with Academic Leaders of Clinical, Community, Research and Education, Department Heads and School Directors, AV/IT professionals and other consultants.
Forms, leads, and participates in project committees or working groups, ensuring that consultative processes have been followed and fostering relationships with key groups to enhance collaborations and partnerships.
Engages in the selection and activities of planners, architects, consultants, and contractors retained for planning, designing, construction, operations and maintenance of Faculty of Medicine facilities, consistent with appropriate University, Health Authority and Ministry policies.
Oversees the management of Ministry of Infrastructure minor capital l funding for Academic Space upgrades and renovations at Health Authorities sites.
Ensures all engineering life-cycle and maintenance standards for faculty assets are adhered to by University or Health Authority staff and external contractors, as appropriate.
Guides senior Academic Leaders in the design process for new and renovated teaching and learning facilities and the development of Academic Space allocation, management and booking policies.

Space Planning & Facility Management

Initiates and approves the creation and development of functional programs for Faculty of Medicine teaching and learning facilities across BC, and provides technical expertise and recommendations to the Managing Director, Operations, Faculty of Medicine. .
Leads short-term and long-term space and facility reviews of Departments, Research Centres/Institutes, Schools, Education programs and administrative units, , including moves and new acquisitions, negotiating and coordinating with Ministry, Health Authority, University, and key partners to secure spatial resources and approvals.
Provides direction and assistance to Department Heads, School Directors and Associate Deans in planning and allocating administrative and research space, ensuring compliance with Faculty space allocation & management policies and compatibility with the long-term objectives of the Faculty.
Participates in University and Health Authority space planning and facility management committees, such as the UBC Property & Planning Advisory Committee, UBC Learning Spaces, and other initiatives, including negotiations for leasing, acting in the best interests of the Faculty.
Ensures that all Faculty Academic Space is allocated and utilized equitably and efficiently, in accordance with Faculty, University and Health Authority guidelines, standards and policies, and as required in the Academic Space Protocols with Health Authorities

Academic Learning Spaces

Oversees the management of over 500+ Faculty of Medicine teaching and learning spaces including video-conference facilities, seminar rooms, lecture theatres, on-call rooms, lounges and other teaching facilities across the Province, ensuring that Faculty requirements are met, while promoting collaborative agreements with Health Authority and other University groups to attain optimal utilization of these spaces and resources.
Oversees the development of tools, systems and processes to ensure efficient and effective management of Academic Space, including the Faculty of Medicine Academic Space Inventory (through Archibus).
Leads the development of space policies, guidelines and processes for the Faculty of Medicine, incorporating national and international space standards for administrative, research and teaching facilities, and within the Health Authority and University contexts, to ensure equitable, efficient and collaborative allocation and utilization of Faculty resources.
Participates on the Faculty of Medicine Health & Safety Committee to ensures that health, safety & security concerns in Academic Space are addressed appropriately, and any deficiencies are actioned.

Consequence of Error/Judgement

The work Space Planning & Facilities Management unit is used in decision making, reporting, planning and provision of information to the University, Health Authorities, and Ministries. High level of decision -making is required. The position is required to exercise independent judgement in all areas of Space Planning & Facilities Management operation along with maturity, collegiality and initiative while developing relationships and partnerships.

Inappropriate actions or indiscretions in judgment can negatively impact the Faculty of Medicine reputation with internal and external partners and , have a detrimental effect on Faculty operations.

Supervision Received

The Director reports to the Managing Director, Operations, Faculty of Medicine, and works independently within the general policy guidelines to achieve overall objectives..

Supervision Given

Directly supervises the Senior Planner, Manager-Major Capital Projects, and three Facility Managers: Academic Learning Spaces, LSC Operations, and Administration & Research Space on the Space Planning & Facilities Management team.

Makes bi-weekly checks of work progress to ensure milestones are achieved. Position provides guidance to reporting staff on more strategic issues. Determines objectives, priorities, status and measures accomplishments against operational plan goals, objectives and performance standards.

The incumbent:

Establishes and maintains close and effective working relationships with the Ministries of Health Infrastructure, and Post-Secondary Education, Health Authority and University partners to ensure Academic Space functional requirements of the Faculty of Medicine are met. Works with all parties at policy, program, functional, implementation and management levels;
Advises Senior Faculty leadership, Departments, Schools, Research Institutes, Centres, and other key players (both faculty and staff) in the Faculty of Medicine;
Works closely with the Senior Education and Research Leaders, AV/IT professionals, and user groups in projects and other initiatives; and

Job Description:

The Director of AI Engineering, Corporate IT leads the engineering of artificial intelligence for internal enterprise delivery, from strategy and architecture through production delivery. This role builds secure, scalable and responsible AI capabilities that modernize enterprise systems, automate IT operations and improve employee productivity.

What will you do?

AI Strategy & Roadmap

Lead intake, value assessment and prioritization of AI use cases across functions such as Actuarial, Risk, Compliance, Human Resources, Finance, Legal, Procurement etc.
Manage AI licensing, vendor contracts and cloud spend within the IT budget.
Rationalize AI tools, reduce duplication and address unapproved or shadow AI use.
Assess emerging capabilities, including copilots, agents and SaaS AI features, for enterprise fit.

Enterprise AI Patterns, Architecture & Integration

Define AI patterns and align them with Enterprise Architecture standards.
Guide integration of AI with collaboration platforms and enterprise data services.
Govern build-versus-buy decisions across packaged AI, SaaS capabilities and custom solutions.
Align AI solutions with identity and access management, single sign-on, API gateways and enterprise data platforms.

AI Platform, AIOps & Automation

Partner with Risk, Legal, Compliance and Privacy to establish and operate AI controls.

People, Talent & Adoption

Design roles, career paths and team structures that build sustainable AI capability within Corporate IT.
Mentor IT employees in AI engineering and secure, responsible AI practices.
Drive employee AI adoption and literacy in partnership with corporate function owners.
Manage strategic partners and managed service providers and hold them accountable for outcomes.

IT Service Delivery & Operations

Own service-level expectations, support models, runbooks and operational readiness for AI services.

Overview

We are seeking a Director, Digital Commerce to lead PepsiCo Canada’s next phase of digital growth. This role will shape and deliver an integrated digital commerce strategy across customers, channels and brands. The Director will lead priority initiatives, embed digital commerce in omnichannel planning, build cross-functional partnerships and drive sustainable growth through strategic investment, capability building and talent development.

What you can expect from us:

Competitive compensation and comprehensive benefits designed to fit your unique needs
A dynamic and inclusive culture that promotes you to bring your whole self to work
Inspiring positive change for people and the planet with sustainability goals
A supportive team that will encourage your professional growth and development

Responsibilities

Own PepsiCo Canada’s digital commerce strategy and roadmap, defining growth priorities, investments, milestones and performance measures.
Lead strategies for priority digital customers and platforms, including omnichannel retailers, Amazon and delivery partners.
Build senior customer partnerships and joint business plans across sales, assortment, content, retail media, availability, service and data sharing.
Embed digital commerce into commercial planning and ways of working across the organization.
Improve online assortment, availability, visibility, content quality and conversion by setting standards and addressing execution gaps.
Guide marketing and retail media investments, using performance and incremental growth to prioritize the strongest opportunities.
Advance data, analytics and technology capabilities by connecting dashboards and retailer data to improve decision-making.
Partner with supply chain and customer teams to improve fulfillment, in-stock performance and online assortment across digital channels.
Identify and scale new growth opportunities, including digital-first products, emerging platforms, new business models and pilot programs.
Lead and develop the digital commerce team, clarify accountabilities and build specialist capabilities.
Influence senior leaders, clarify trade-offs and secure the resources and decisions needed to deliver the strategy.
Translate customer, shopper and financial data into clear performance insights, risks and recommendations for senior leaders.

Qualifications

A post-secondary degree; advanced business education is an asset.
10+ years of progressive leadership experience in customer development, digital commerce, sales or marketing.
Proven success leading complex customer or channel strategies and cross-functional growth.
Strong knowledge of omnichannel retail, online grocery, digital marketplaces, retail media, digital shelf practices and shopper behaviour.
Experience with Amazon Vendor Central, retail media platforms, retailer data and performance marketing is an asset.
Strong commercial and financial acumen to balance growth, share, investment and profitability.

jobs.description:
Are you looking for a leadership role where you can shape the future of project delivery, corporate planning, and organizational performance? Can you see yourself leading enterprise-wide planning, portfolio governance, and project controls to support strategic decision-making and long-term success? If you answered yes, this may be the job for you. Apply today!
Our Chalk River location is looking for a Deputy Vice President, Project Controls & Corporate Planning
(PCCP) to provide strategic leadership for enterprise project controls, corporate planning, portfolio governance, and performance management.

What you will be doing!

Enterprise Planning & Strategy
Leading integrated annual, multi-year, and long-range enterprise planning.
Supporting the development of the organization's 10-Year Strategy and Plan of Work.
Translating enterprise strategy into executable plans, resource requirements, and performance measures.
Aligning corporate priorities with available funding, resource capacity, and delivery commitments.
Advising executive leadership through strategic analysis and recommendations.

Annual Program of Work & Budget (APWB)
Leading the development, integration, critical review, and consolidation of the APWB.
Ensuring alignment across strategic commitments, budgets, schedules, milestones, and resource forecasts.
Advising executive leadership on funding allocations and investment priorities.
Assessing the strategic and delivery implications of emerging opportunities, scope changes, and funding adjustments.
Supporting strategic negotiations and engagement with key external stakeholders on planning and funding requirements.

Project Controls Leadership
Providing enterprise leadership for:
Cost management
Schedule management
Risk management
Change control
Performance measurement
Portfolio reporting

Setting enterprise standards and governance expectations for project controls, supported by consistent procedures and tools.
Driving continuous improvement in enterprise project controls processes and capabilities.
Ensuring accurate, timely, and reliable performance information informs executive decision-making.

Portfolio Governance & Prioritization
Leading enterprise portfolio prioritization and optimization.
Advising executive governance bodies on resource allocation and prioritization.
Facilitating enterprise-wide evaluation of competing demands across Capital, Operations, Infrastructure, and Strategic Initiatives.
Developing strategic recommendations on:
Capital investments
Infrastructure renewal
Capability retention
Resource allocation
Scope prioritization
Strategic alternatives

Ensuring portfolio decisions balance affordability, risk, regulatory requirements, organizational objectives, and long-term sustainability.

Capital Planning & Investment Management
Supporting the development of long-term capital investment strategies aligned with enterprise objectives.
Overseeing integrated enterprise capital planning.
Evaluating the strategic merits of business cases, investment proposals, and major project initiatives.
Ensuring capital investments align with enterprise priorities and available funding.
Supporting the resolution of affordability challenges, funding gaps, and competing investment needs.

Corporate Performance & Executive Reporting
Leading the development of executive dashboards, performance reports, and strategic planning updates to inform enterprise decisions.
Monitoring enterprise performance against approved commitments and strategic objectives.
Identifying emerging risks, issues, and opportunities affecting enterprise delivery.
Presenting performance insights and strategic recommendations to senior leadership and governance committees.

Resource Planning & Organizational Analysis
Overseeing enterprise resource forecasting and the integration of workforce and corporate planning.
Ensuring enterprise plans reflect realistic workforce capacity assessments.
Advising executive leadership on organizational resource requirements.
Evaluating the implications of workforce constraints for planned delivery and strategic objectives.

Other duties as assigned by your manager.

What We Are Looking For

Education
An undergraduate degree in Business, Accounting, Finance, or Economics (or international equivalent).
Preferably MBA and/or C.P.A (or international equivalent).

Experience
15+ years of progressively responsible experience in:
Project Controls
Corporate Planning
Portfolio Management
Capital Program Management
Strategic Planning
Executive Governance
Significant leadership experience managing multidisciplinary teams.

Experience supporting executive leadership and governance bodies.
Experience developing and managing large capital programs and enterprise portfolios.
Experience in planning, at the strategic, project and operational level, budgeting, execution and reporting of PCCP activities.

Knowledge, Skills & Abilities
Strong client and stakeholder focus, with the ability to balance service expectations with enterprise priorities.
Excellent executive communication skills, including the ability to present complex information, strategic advice, and recommendations clearly and persuasively.
Credibility, sound judgment, and the ability to build trust and influence decisions at senior levels.
Demonstrated ability to mobilize multidisciplinary teams within PCCP and across a matrixed organization, establish accountability, and deliver results.
Ability to operate effectively under broad direction and advise executive leadership on strategic priorities and organizational direction.
Proven ability to lead transformational change in a complex organization with multiple stakeholders.
Strong critical thinking and analytical skills, with the ability to distill complex issues into clear, actionable recommendations.
Demonstrated organizational leadership and management capabilities.
Ability to build high-performing teams and communicate a compelling vision aligned with enterprise strategy.
Strong interpersonal and presentation skills, with the ability to build consensus among diverse stakeholders.
Ability to identify trends, establish benchmarks, and translate analysis into strategic insights and business recommendations.
Strong negotiation and contract management skills.
Ability to establish priorities and assess competing demands in support of enterprise objectives.
Extensive planning, budgeting, financial management, and performance reporting capabilities.
Strong project and risk management capabilities.
Experience in corporate services, preferably within large, cross-functional organizations.
Strong relationship-building skills, with the ability to engage staff, management, executives, customers, and external partners.
Ability to manage competing priorities and maintain focus on strategic commitments in a demanding environment.

Why CNL?

jobs.description:
About The Role

Grade Level (for internal use):

14

The Role

Credit Ratings is a core part of the Global Ratings Services team, bringing together a diverse group of over 1,400 analysts across key financial centers worldwide. The Financial Services practice delivers forward-looking credit insights on banks, insurers, and other financial institutions, assessing capital strength, funding and liquidity, asset quality, governance, and operating environments to inform rating opinions that markets depend on. The practice supports stakeholders in understanding how evolving risks — from regulation and macroeconomic shifts to digital assets and decentralized finance — can affect financial stability and credit performance and plays a significant role in S&P Global Ratings' private markets strategy.

Impact

As Sector Lead in the Financial Services practice, you will lead the development of independent credit opinions that markets rely on, combining rigorous analytical leadership with innovative, AI-enabled approaches that strengthen the depth, speed, and consistency of insight. You will also shape the next generation of credit talent — coaching, empowering, and developing others while modeling the curiosity, integrity, and collaborative spirit that define leadership at S&P Global Ratings.

Responsibilities

Leadership & Talent Development

Coach and mentor analysts and senior analysts, building capability in sector expertise, credit judgment, market engagement, and AI-enabled analytical practices.
Collaborate across sectors, regions, and asset classes to share best practices, enhance global analytical consistency, and address complex cross-market developments.

Core Analytical & Delivery

Lead market-relevant, forward-looking sector analysis to ensure high-quality analytical coverage and differentiated insight across the Financial Services sector.
Translate sector and issuer developments into clear, decision-ready analytical and thematic perspectives, leveraging data, advanced analytics, and AI-enabled tools to enhance the depth, speed, and consistency of insight delivered to internal and external audiences.

Stakeholder & Market Engagement

Serve as a visible, market-facing leader with key stakeholders — including management teams, investors, regulators, and other market participants — representing S&P Global Ratings' analytical perspective through high-quality dialogue while upholding independence, objectivity, and analytical integrity.
Partner with Methodology teams and represent the Financial Services sector in relevant forums to support consistent criteria interpretation and application globally, while contributing market insights and analytical learnings to strengthen methodologies and practices.

Risk Management and Operating

Contribute to the oversight of innovation in sector analysis with the goal of improving efficiency, consistency, and decision-making, while maintaining strong analytical discipline and governance.

Compensation And Benefits Information (US Candidates)

S&P Global states that the anticipated base salary range for this position is $240,000 USD to $289,000 USD. Final base salary for this role will be based on the individual’s geographic location, as well as experience level, skill set, training, licenses, and certifications. In addition to base compensation, this role is eligible for an annual incentive plan. For more information on the benefits we provide to our employees, please click here.  

Compensation and Benefits Information:
 (Canadian candidates)

S&P Global states that the anticipated range of compensation for this position is 260,000 CAD to 295,000 CAD. Final compensation for this role will be based on the individual’s performance, geographic location, as well as experience level, skill set, training, licenses, and certifications. In accordance with Ontario's new regulations effective January 1, 2026, this job posting provides information on expected compensation. S&P Global will not be utilizing artificial intelligence in our hiring process. Additionally, we are committed to transparency and will inform all interviewed candidates of hiring decisions within 45 days of their interview. This posting is for an existing vacancy, and we encourage you to reach out for further information regarding our hiring practices or any questions you may have. Thank you for considering a career with us!

What We're Looking For

Required Skills and Experience

Practice Nuances

Serve as the analytical leader for the North America Non-Bank Financial Institutions (NBFI) team, building a culture focused on customer service excellence, strong analytical decision-making, talent development, collaboration with business partners, and leadership in broader business transformation across the practice.
Lead the production of differentiated credit insights pertinent to the NBFI sector, as well as broader credit insights and research that bring together analytics from across the Financial Services practice, Global Analytics, Research, and Methodologies teams.
Drive analytical decision-making focused on broader risk assessment, considering market dynamics and innovation in financing structures without being constrained by existing analytical constructs.
Champion a culture of service excellence for issuers, investors, intermediaries, and influential market participants — delivering clear, thoughtful analytics with speed and agility — while identifying opportunities to redesign workflows, embed automation and AI, and scale repeatable analysis, maintaining strong analytical discipline, controls, and governance.
Lead Private Markets initiatives and actively participate in key analytical forums.

Leadership & Talent Development

Ability to partner effectively with Methodology and Research & Development teams to support consistent criteria interpretation and application, while contributing sector insights to strengthen analytical frameworks.
Ability to coach and develop analytical talent at multiple levels, building sector expertise, credit judgment, and modern analytical capability across the team.

Core Analytical & Delivery

Recognized analytical leader with the ability to develop differentiated, decision-useful sector commentaries and thematic insights, translating complex developments into concise, evidence-based narratives.

Stakeholder & Market Engagement

Proven ability to represent S&P Global Ratings' analytical perspective with senior external stakeholders, building trust through clarity, rigor, and consistent engagement.

Risk Management and Operating

Ability to connect issuer and sector developments to forward-looking risk themes, identifying emerging trends that inform monitoring activities, research, and rating committee discussions.
Ability to oversee and contribute to innovation in sector analysis, balancing efficiency and consistency goals with strong analytical discipline and governance.

Preferred Or Helpful Experience

Education: Bachelor's degree or equivalent required. A master's degree or professional certification (such as CFA) is highly valued. We welcome candidates from traditional finance disciplines as well as diverse academic backgrounds that support innovative and critical thinking.

Additional Information

An S&P Global employee at this level would typically have 10 or more years of relevant experience in credit analysis or financial services.
We require all candidates who reach the final stage of our interview process to attend at least one in-person interview, which is ordinarily at your nearest S&P Global Ratings office. This must be completed before we can proceed to an offer.
Employees are required to work from the office a minimum of two days per week.

Right to Work Requirements:
This role is limited to persons with an indefinite right to work in the United States.

About S&P Global Ratings

At S&P Global Ratings, our analyst-driven credit ratings, research, and sustainable finance opinions provide critical insights that are essential to translating complexity into clarity so market participants can uncover opportunities and make decisions with conviction. By bringing transparency to the market through high-quality independent opinions on creditworthiness, we enable growth across a wide variety of organizations, including businesses, governments, and institutions.

S&P Global Ratings is a division of S&P Global (NYSE: SPGI). S&P Global is the world’s foremost provider of credit ratings, benchmarks, analytics and workflow solutions in the global capital, commodity and automotive markets. With every one of our offerings, we help many of the world’s leading organizations navigate the economic landscape so they can plan for tomorrow, today.

For more information, visit www.spglobal.com/ratings

What’s In It For
You?

Our Mission

Advancing Essential Intelligence.

Our People

We're more than 35,000 strong worldwide—so we're able to understand nuances while having a broad perspective. Our team is driven by curiosity and a shared belief that Essential Intelligence can help build a more prosperous future for us all.From finding new ways to measure sustainability to analyzing energy transition across the supply chain to building workflow solutions that make it easy to tap into insight and apply it. We are changing the way people see things and empowering them to make an impact on the world we live in. We’re committed to a more equitable future and to helping our customers find new, sustainable ways of doing business. Join us and help create the critical insights that truly make a difference.

Our Values

Integrity, Discovery, Partnership

Throughout our history, the world's leading organizations have relied on us for the Essential Intelligence they need to make confident decisions about the road ahead. We start with a foundation of integrity in all we do, bring a spirit of discovery to our work, and collaborate in close partnership with each other and our customers to achieve shared goals.

Benefits

We take care of you, so you can take care of business. We care about our people. That’s why we provide everything you—and your career—need to thrive at S&P Global.

Our Benefits Include

Health & Wellness: Health care coverage designed for the mind and body.
Flexible Downtime: Generous time off helps keep you energized for your time on.
Continuous Learning: Access a wealth of resources to grow your career and learn valuable new skills.
Invest in Your Future: Secure your financial future through competitive pay, retirement planning, a continuing education program with a company-matched student loan contribution, and financial wellness programs.
Family Friendly Perks: It’s not just about you. S&P Global has perks for your partners and little ones, too, with some best-in class benefits for families.
Beyond the Basics: From retail discounts to referral incentive awards—small perks can make a big difference.

For more information on benefits by country visit: https://spgbenefits.com/benefit-summaries

Global Hiring And Opportunity At S&P Global

At S&P Global, we are committed to fostering a connected and engaged workplace where all individuals have access to opportunities based on their skills, experience, and contributions. Our hiring practices emphasize fairness, transparency, and merit, ensuring that we attract and retain top talent. By valuing different perspectives and promoting a culture of respect and collaboration, we drive innovation and power global markets.

jobs.description:
Job Description

Mackenzie Investments

IGM Financial Inc. is a leading wealth and asset management company in Canada, managing approximately $ 310 billion in assets as of December 31, 2025 . It offers financial planning and investment services to over two million Canadians through IG Wealth Management and Mackenzie Investments.

Mackenzie Investments, founded in 1967, is a key part of IGM's business model, serving as a comprehensive asset-management partner for Canadian financial advisors and their clients.

At Mackenzie Investments You Can Build Your Career with Confidence
.
We are proud to be recognized as one of Canada’s Top 100 Employers for the fourth consecutive year and one of Canada’s Best Diversity Employers. Our vision and strategy aim to innovate the industry and support Canadians in achieving their financial goals.

Join our team to engage in continuous learning and skill development in a supportive environment. Experience the best of both worlds with our hybrid work environment, where you spend three days a week in the office, connecting, collaborating, and enjoying quality time with your amazing colleagues ! Our Values: Be better ; we strive for improvement in everything we do . Be accountable ; we foster clarity and are empowered to act responsibly . Be a team ; we are united to drive collective impact to achieve our goals .

The Role:
This is an opportunity to shape how HR works and how people experience HR at IGM. As AVP, HR Services Delivery and Technology, you will help turn our future-state service model into a practical, multi-year roadmap and lead the evolution of the technology and services that support it.

You will bring together HR service delivery, HR operations and HR technology so that people can find answers, complete transactions and access support with less friction. You will work closely with the HR Leadership Team, HR Centres of Expertise, Technology, Risk, Legal, Compliance and business leaders to simplify work, clarify ownership and use technology where it creates real value.

Your work will directly influence employee and leader experience, service quality, operational efficiency and HR’s capacity to focus on higher-value work. It is a role for a leader who is comfortable connecting strategy to execution and building the capabilities, governance and teams needed to make change stick.

Key Responsibilities

Partner with HR Leadership and the Centres of Expertise to implement the future service model, moving appropriate work into scalable self-service, automated and centralized delivery while maintaining clear tiering, ownership and escalation paths.
Translate HR priorities into an integrated roadmap across SAP SuccessFactors, ServiceNow and other HR platforms. Reduce fragmentation, duplicate entry and unnecessary hand-offs so HR feels like one connected experience.
Lead the implementation and ongoing evolution of ServiceNow as HR’s digital front door. Simplify processes, strengthen knowledge management and expand automation and AI-enabled services while preserving appropriate controls and human judgment for complex or sensitive matters.
Provide business leadership and oversight for the HR technology portfolio, holding internal teams and delivery partners accountable for execution, platform health, adoption and value realization.
Set meaningful service standards and measures for case resolution, service levels, experience, quality and risk. Use operational data and feedback to identify root causes, reduce recurring demand and continuously improve services.
Build effective partnerships across HR, Technology, Risk, Legal, Compliance and the business. Operationalize agreed governance and decision rights, and lead the change required to adopt new ways of working.
Lead a multidisciplinary HR Services & Technology organization and develop the leaders, digital, service and analytical capabilities needed to operate as an integrated, employee-focused function.

Required Qualifications

Undergraduate degree in Human Resources, Business Administration or a related field.
12+ years of progressive leadership experience in HR operations, service delivery, HR technology or a related field within a large, complex organization, including enterprise transformation and team leadership.
Demonstrated experience in service ownership, operating model design, technology roadmap ownership, data-led service leadership, and risk and governance leadership.
Strong change leadership and executive influence, with the ability to work across functions and establish clear accountability and decision rights.
Experience using experience-led design thinking to improve service delivery and the people experience.
CHRP, CHRL or equivalent HR designation, completed or in progress..

Preferred Qualifications

Experience in financial services or another regulated environment.
Experience leading an HR technology portfolio and/or a shared-services or service-delivery transformation.
Experience with ServiceNow HRSD or a comparable enterprise service-management platform.
Experience in digital product management and AI or automation implementation.
Lean, Six Sigma or service-management certification such as ITIL.

As this position is posted in Montréal, Toronto and Winnipeg, we specify that bilingualism (French, English, both oral and written) is required for Quebec only for the frequent interactions with English. 

Benefits

COMPETITIVE COMPENSATION & RECOGNITION: competitive base salary, performance-weighted bonus, education/career support, option to join Employee Share Purchase Plan with employer matching component.
EMPLOYEE BENEFITS & INSURANCE: competitive health and dental coverage, flexible plan for you and your family and short-term & long-term disability plans.
RETIREMENT SAVINGS PROGRAMS: voluntary Defined Contribution Pension Plan
WORK LIFE BALANCE: paid volunteer days, competitive time off, including 10 wellness days off, WorkPerks discount program, hybrid & flex work arrangements.
INCLUSIVE CULTURE AND DIVERSITY: living our core values: Be a Team, Be Accountable, Be Better, engaging with community through Business Resource Groups (BRG communities are volunteer employee-led groups formed around a common interest, identity, or background).

IGM is a diverse workplace committed to doing business inclusively - this starts with having a representative workforce! We encourage applications from all qualified candidates that represent the diversity present across Canada – including racialized persons, women, Indigenous persons, persons with disabilities, 2SLGBTQIA+ community, gender diverse and neurodiverse individuals, as well as all who may contribute to the further diversification of ideas.

Mackenzie Investments is an accessible employer committed to providing barrier -free recruitment experience. If you require accommodation or this information in an alternate format at any stage of the recruitment process, please reach out to the Talent Acquisition team who will work with you to meet your needs .

How to Apply: Interested candidates are invited to submit their resume and a cover letter detailing their qualifications and experience to https://www.ig.ca/en/careers

We thank all applicants for their interest in IG Wealth Management; however, only those candidates selected for an interview will be contacted.

Artificial Intelligence in Recruitment: As part of our Talent Acquisition process, we may use artificial intelligence and automated tools to support activities such as candidate sourcing, application review, and interview scheduling. These tools support the recruitment process; all hiring decisions are made by people.

jobs.description:
Our Story & Purpose

We’re Vancity, a member-owned credit union built on the principles of inclusion and social justice. Since 1946, our commitment to these values has helped us challenge the status quo and break down barriers. We’ve made bold commitments to become net-zero by 2040 across all mortgages and loans, and we’re actively pursuing strategies in Indigenous banking and financial resilience for our members.  
As the largest private-sector Living Wage Employer in Canada, we’re proud to be consistently recognized as one of the country’s Top Employers. If you’re ready to join our team of 2,300 diverse individuals, access competitive rewards and benefits, and be part of a greater movement, apply today!   

Your Role in Supporting Our Members

As the Director, Strategic Insights
, you will lead the Strategic Insights team within the Analytics Centre of Excellence and oversee how the organization engages with analytics to support informed, evidence-based decision-making. You will partner with leaders across the organization to scope analytics work, execute the analytics strategy, and advance Vancity’s data utilization and advanced analytics capabilities.  
You will play a critical role in translating complex insights into meaningful recommendations, strengthening analytical practices, and helping teams use data effectively to achieve organizational priorities.  
This is a full-time, permanent
role based out of Vancity Head Office
and will report directly to the Vice President, Analytics Centre of Excellence
.  While this position provides a hybrid
work arrangement, you will be expected to be on-site for events and business demands.

How You’ll Make an Impact

Providing strategic leadership and direction for the Strategic Insights function and its evolving priorities  

Leading the execution of the Analytics Centre of Excellence strategy in partnership with teams across the organization  

Developing frameworks, practices, and approaches that support organizational objectives across multiple divisions  

Guiding the effective use of analytics by educating stakeholders and briefing subject-matter experts on analytical findings and recommendations  

Influencing business decisions and organizational strategies through relevant analytics methodologies and evidence-based insights  

Advising senior leaders and making recommendations that help shape strategic priorities and decision-making  

Identifying opportunities to improve current practices and strengthen how insights are applied across the organization  

Building trusted relationships with business leaders and supporting the strategic vision of the Analytics Centre of Excellence  

Leading ongoing enterprise communications that promote an analytical mindset and share progress  

Building an engaged, capable, and efficient Strategic Insights team while managing evolving talent and skill requirements   

What You’ll Bring to the Team

Significant experience leading strategic insights, business intelligence, analytics, data strategy, or a related function  

Demonstrated experience translating complex data and analysis into clear recommendations for senior leaders and business stakeholders  

Strong people-leadership experience, including building team capability, setting priorities, and supporting employee development  

Experience developing and implementing analytics frameworks, methodologies, and organizational best practices  

Proven ability to influence enterprise-level decisions and work effectively across multiple business areas  

Strong relationship-management, consultation, and executive communication skills  

Sound judgment and the ability to balance strategic priorities, organizational risk, and member needs  

A degree in business, analytics, economics, data science, finance, or a related discipline, or an equivalent combination of education and experience  

Extra Skills That Set You Apart

Experience working in financial services, a credit union, or another highly regulated environment  

Experience leading an analytics centre of excellence or enterprise-wide analytics function  

Knowledge of advanced analytics, data utilization, predictive modelling, or machine-learning practices  

Experience supporting organizational change and strengthening data literacy across diverse stakeholder groups  

You’ll Thrive Here If You Are

A strategic thinker
who connects analytics, business priorities, and member needs to support better decisions.  

An influential communicator
who makes complex information clear, relevant, and actionable for different audiences.  

A collaborative leader
who builds trusted relationships and brings people together around shared goals.  

A people-focused manager
who develops talent, encourages innovation, and creates a safe and respectful team environment.  

We value lived experience, so if you are interested in this role, we encourage you to apply even if you feel your skills don’t perfectly align with those listed. 

What You’ll Earn

This role offers a salary range of $148,000 to $191,500 per annum
. The base pay offered may vary depending on factors such as relevant qualifications, skills, previous experience, and internal equity. As part of our total rewards package, employees may also be eligible for our annual incentive program, subject to program eligibility requirements.   

Why You’ll Love Working Here

A career at Vancity is more than just a job. You’re joining a tradition of change-makers who are creating lasting change for our communities. Beyond base pay, we offer a comprehensive total rewards package to ensure our employees are empowered to thrive:  
Living Wage Employer:
We’re the largest private-sector Living Wage Employer in Canada and consistently ranked among Canada’s Top Employers  

Customizable Benefits:
Permanent employees receive flexible benefit packages that can be tailored annually to meet evolving needs  

Generous Vacation:
New employees start with three to four weeks of vacation per year, with additional days earned over time  

Extra Stat Holidays:
In addition to BC’s statutory holidays, we offer two extra days, plus care days for personal or family illness  

Immediate Health Coverage:
Health and dental benefits begin on your hire date, with three levels of coverage to choose from  

Defined Benefit Pension:
Our retirement plan provides a guaranteed income for life, recognizing that retirement looks different for everyone  

Vancity Talent Programs:

Vancity supports an inclusive hiring process for candidates who self-identify as Indigenous, Black, or Trans. With special permission from the BC Human Rights Commissioner, this initiative provides access to career development opportunities, prioritized job screening, and feedback. Any information you choose to share will be stored securely and used only for recruitment and career development connected to this initiative, in line with the BC Personal Information Protection Act (PIPA). For details, please see our dedicated Talent Programs job posting
