SearchLabs has been exclusively retained to Partner with rybka Group Inc. on a multitude of different roles and opportunities across the Country. rybka Group Inc. is a leading Canadian consulting engineering firm that specializes in mechanical, electrical, and commissioning engineering services for the built environment. Headquartered in Markham, Ontario, the firm was formed in 2025 through the strategic merger of two legacy engineering firms: rybka Group Inc., established in 1913, and Ellard-Willson Engineering Limited, founded in 1954. This merger unites over a century of combined expertise, a shared commitment to human-centric design, and a passion for sustainable, innovative engineering solutions.

Who is rybka Group Inc.:

rybka Group Inc. stands at the forefront of building services engineering, offering comprehensive solutions across a broad spectrum of sectors, including:
Commercial and residential developments
Healthcare and long-term care facilities
Educational and institutional buildings
Hospitality and cultural venues
Retail and Food Services
Critical Systems

rybka Group Inc. believes in the power of Perpetual Building Engineering, an approach that integrates sustainable thinking at every stage of a building’s lifecycle. By blending engineering precision with architectural vision and environmental stewardship, their work contributes to healthier, more resilient communities. A family 1st ethos, rybka Group is not only looking to be the firm of choice across all building sectors across all disciplines (Mechanical, Electrical, Structural, and Commissioning), but is looking to build the most positive/productive work environment second to none.

Heritage and Innovation:

rybka Group brought to the merger a distinguished history of pioneering projects in Toronto, including Maple Leaf Gardens and the Toronto Stock Exchange.
Ellard-Willson Engineering contributed a strong track record in institutional and public infrastructure, with work reaching as far back as the original CN Tower.
This deep-rooted legacy informs their forward-thinking practice, ensuring clients benefit from both proven experience and progressive design.

Director of Finance (Professional Services / Engineering Consulting)

Role Overview

rybka is seeking an experienced Director of Finance to provide financial leadership and oversight across the organization.
As a mechanical and electrical engineering consulting firm, our financial performance is closely connected to project delivery, utilization, billing, work-in-progress (WIP), accounts receivable, project profitability, and effective cash flow management. The Director of Finance will work closely with the CEO, Managing Principal, Principals, Project Managers, and administrative team to strengthen financial controls, improve visibility into business performance, and support informed decision-making.
This is a hands-on leadership role suited to an individual who can operate strategically while remaining actively involved in the day-to-day financial management of the business

Key Responsibilities

Financial Leadership & Planning

Lead the company's overall finance and accounting function and provide financial guidance to senior leadership.
Develop and maintain annual budgets, forecasts, cash flow projections, and financial plans.
Provide the CEO, Managing Principal, and Principals with clear and timely financial reporting and analysis.
Identify financial risks, trends, and opportunities and recommend appropriate actions.
Support strategic planning, financing initiatives, banking relationships, and other corporate financial matters.
Develop financial models and scenario analyses to support business and operational decisions.

Project Financial Management

Provide financial oversight of the firm's engineering projects, including project budgets, WIP, revenue recognition, billing, utilization, and profitability.
Work closely with Principals and Project Managers to review project financial performance and identify projects that are over budget, under-billed, delayed, or otherwise financially at risk.
Establish consistent project financial planning, forecasting, and reporting practices across the firm.
Monitor project performance against fee proposals, contracts, budgets, and approved scope.
Support leadership in understanding project margins, resource allocation, write-offs, and financial performance by project, client, and business area.

Cash Flow, Billing & Accounts Receivable

Maintain short- and medium-term cash flow forecasts and provide leadership with clear visibility into the company's liquidity requirements.
Oversee the billing cycle and ensure invoices are issued accurately and on a timely basis.
Lead accounts receivable monitoring and collection strategies in collaboration with Principals and Project Managers.
Monitor aging reports, outstanding receivables, and collection risks.
Oversee accounts payable and payment planning while balancing operational requirements and cash flow priorities.
Maintain effective relationships with the company's banks, lenders, and other financial partners.

Accounting & Financial Reporting

Oversee month-end and year-end close processes and ensure accurate and timely financial reporting.
Review balance sheet reconciliations, income statements, cash flow reporting, and supporting schedules.
Maintain appropriate accounting policies, procedures, internal controls, and approval processes.
Coordinate with external accountants, auditors, tax advisors, payroll providers, and other professional advisors.
Ensure compliance with applicable accounting, tax, statutory, and corporate reporting requirements.
Oversee corporate filings, remittances, and other financial compliance obligations.

Systems, Processes & Controls

Provide financial leadership for Deltek Vision and related accounting and project-management systems.
Improve the quality and consistency of financial data, project setup, billing information, WIP reporting, and project forecasting.
Develop and document finance policies, procedures, approval authorities, and internal controls.
Identify opportunities to automate and streamline financial and administrative processes.
Establish reliable management dashboards and KPIs for leadership.

Ensure payroll changes, deductions, remittances, and financial reporting are properly controlled.
Work collaboratively with HR on compensation budgeting, benefits costs, vacation liabilities, staffing forecasts, and other people-related financial matters.

Promote a culture of financial discipline, accountability, and timely decision-making across the organization.

Lead risk management and insurance review processes.

About Sonance Financial

Sonance Financial launched in October 2026, bringing together founder-led advisory firms in Lethbridge, Ottawa, Edmonton and Phoenix. We are building one operating model and one modern technology platform, and we need an experienced technology leader to make it work across every office.

About the role

As our first in-house technology leader, the IT Director (Digital Operations) is a hands-on role. You will be the bridge between our people and our managed IT services partner: you'll turn business needs into clear requirements, solve problems directly, and hold vendors to a high standard. You will also lead our first practical steps with AI and own our IT and AI policies. This is a chance to build technology at a growing wealth firm from the ground up, with a clear path to Head of Technology as we grow.

Reporting to the CEO on an interim basis. You will work closely with the Director of Integrations, the Director of Support Services and the Chief Compliance Officer. The role has no direct reports at launch.

What you'll do

IT operations and managed services:
Own the relationship with our managed IT services partner, including escalations, invoices and monthly service reviews. Troubleshoot hands-on across devices, networks, Teams calling and meeting rooms.
Identity, SSO and client portal:
Roll out Microsoft Entra ID single sign-on with MFA for all users. Support the launch of our client portal and resolve login issues. Run joiner, mover and leaver processes and quarterly access reviews.
Partner firm onboarding:
Build a repeatable playbook so every new office is fully working on day one. This covers device setup, Microsoft 365 email and file migration, platform access, and retiring legacy systems.
Platform vendors:
Oversee our wealth-management platforms (CRM, portfolio accounting, financial planning, ERP and related tools), keep vendor oversight records, and evaluate new tools.
AI enablement:
Work with an outside consultant to pilot practical AI workflows and scale the ones that work. Make sure each one is signed off by Compliance, and keep an inventory of AI tools.
Security, continuity and policy:
Run our information security program with our IT partner, including the annual risk assessment, vulnerability testing, incident response and staff training. Test our business continuity and disaster recovery plans every year, maintain the IT and AI policy framework, and provide evidence for audits and due diligence.
Strategy and budget:
Keep a rolling technology roadmap, manage the technology budget, and report progress to leadership.

What success looks like in your first year

The client portal is live with single sign-on.
A clear support model is in place with our IT partner, with SLA reporting every month.
Our IT and AI policy framework is approved and covered in staff training.
We have a full inventory of systems, vendors and licences, plus a 2–3 year technology roadmap.
Two or three AI pilots have been delivered, with measured results.

What you bring

5+ years in IT or technology management, including oversight of managed service providers and vendors.
Hands-on Microsoft 365 administration (Exchange Online, SharePoint, Entra ID, Intune) and experience implementing SSO.
A track record of delivering migrations from start to finish.
Working knowledge of security frameworks (NIST or CIS), incident response and business continuity planning.
Knowledge of Canadian privacy and record-keeping requirements for financial services, such as PIPEDA and securities regulator expectations.
A genuinely AI-forward mindset, balanced with good judgment about risk.
A calm, clear communicator who can support people across several offices and time zones.

Nice to have

Experience in wealth management or other regulated financial services.
Familiarity with wealth platforms such as CRM, portfolio accounting, custodian integrations and client portals.
A degree in Computer Science or Management Information Systems, or equivalent experience.

Full-time, permanent. This posting is for an existing vacancy.
Hybrid, based in Ontario (Greater Toronto Area preferred), with up to about 20% travel to our offices.
Base salary range: $130,000 – $180,000 CAD per year, depending on experience.

As Associate Vice President, Financial Crime Risk Management (FCRM) Data Management, Canada, you will lead the team responsible for strengthening the data foundations that support TD’s financial crime risk management capabilities. Reporting to the Vice President, FCRM Monitoring Coverage and Capabilities, you will help shape the FCRM data strategy and lead data governance, data delivery and the continued evolution of the Canadian data management operating model. Partner with technology teams to translate content models into platform requirements

Lead content audits, inventories, rationalization and gap analyses
Define content migration approaches and mapping

Translate SEO/AEO requirements into content models, metadata and structured content approaches

Content Operations & Governance

Design governance models that sustain modular and reusable content at scale, including regulated content review
Identify opportunities to improve consistency, efficiency and scale across content operations

Facilitate workshops and present recommendations to senior client stakeholders
Communicate the role and value of content systems clearly to cross-functional teams and clients

10–15+ years in content strategy, content design or digital experience strategy, including senior leadership of content strategy workstreams

Experience defining content requirements for personalization, dynamic content or next best action
Working knowledge of SEO, AEO and GEO, and how content structure supports search and AI-driven discovery
Experience designing content operations, governance and lifecycle models
Experience scoping and estimating content strategy work within agency or consulting environments
Experience leading or mentoring content strategy teams

Partners with the Head of Content Strategy, North America on practice standards, methods and growth
Defines content strategy scope, sequencing and staffing with project leadership

Builds content strategy capability across disciplines

Chief Information Security Officer

Canadian Blood Services is an essential part of the country’s network of healthcare systems. Together, with donors, recipients, employees, partners and volunteers, Canadian Blood Services is Canada’s Lifeline
, providing lifesaving products and services in transfusion and transplantation for Canadian patients, and safeguarding Canada's systems of life essentials in blood, plasma, stem cells, and organs and tissues.

Canadian Blood Services continues to strengthen its enterprise security and advance organizational resilience in support of its mission. It is within this exciting context that the organization is seeking a Chief Information Security Officer.

Reporting to the Vice-President, Digital Solutions & Technology, the CISO provides executive leadership for cybersecurity strategy, governance, risk management, security operations and transformation. As the organization’s senior-most cybersecurity leader, you will advise senior leadership and the Board, lead a skilled team of cybersecurity professionals, and translate complex security risks into clear priorities and practical action.

As a supply chain organization with a national footprint, Canadian Blood Services employs significant and mission-critical Operational Technology (OT) and Internet of Things (IoT) environments to support its biologics manufacturing processes. As CISO you are accountable for enhancing the existing OT/IoT security strategy, governance framework, standards, and risk-management program aligned with recognized practices such as NIST Cybersecurity Framework and IEC 62443.

You must work collegially and collaboratively across operational, engineering, facilities, biomedical, IT, privacy, and business teams to build a culture in which robust security behaviours are embedded in daily work while cybersecurity requirements are balanced with safety, reliability, regulatory obligations, and the continuity of essential operations and availability of mission-critical services. You will shape and deliver a risk-based cybersecurity maturity roadmap, establish accountable ownership of security initiatives and demonstrate measurable progress in remediation through strong enterprise governance and reporting.

As the ideal candidate, you bring at least 10 years of progressive cybersecurity and information security experience, including proven leadership as a CISO or equivalent cybersecurity executive. You bring demonstrable understanding of Canadian privacy and cybersecurity requirements and can apply recognized frameworks such as NIST CSF, ISO 27001, CIS Controls, etc. Combining strategic judgment with hands-on execution skill, you have built sustainable capabilities and supported structured knowledge transfer in areas such as artificial intelligence, identity and access management; privileged access controls; network segmentation; cloud and Microsoft 365 security; incident response; and vendor risk management. You are an influential communicator and trusted advisor who easily builds credibility with executives, Boards, technical teams and business leaders. You bring integrity, collaboration, sound risk-based decision-making and the ability to lead change under pressure.

Demonstrable experience leading security improvement and remediation in other complex, highly regulated environments will equip you to navigate Canadian Blood Services’ unique operational demands. A bachelor’s degree in a relevant discipline and CISSP, CISM or a comparable certification are preferred; an equivalent combination of education, training and experience may also be considered.

This is a term contract position with the potential for permanency. Experience in interim, fractional, advisory or turnaround CISO engagements is an asset.

Remuneration is expected to be in the range of $152,500–$197,340 salary plus an annual performance incentive of up to 12%. The final salary will be commensurate with expertise and professional background. During the contract term additional recruitment incentives may be offered in lieu of pension, benefits and vacation.

To apply, please visit: boyden.thriveapp.ly/job/3459. For more information, please contact Virginia Warren at vwarren@boyden.com.

It aims to reflect the diversity of Canadians and exemplify a culture of inclusion where all employees have equitable opportunities to succeed and contribute. jobs.title: Head of Domain, Technology Development
jobs.description:
Who We Are

Geotab ® is a global leader in IoT and connected transportation and certified “Great Place to Work™.” We are a company of diverse and talented individuals who work together to help businesses grow and succeed, and increase the safety and sustainability of our communities.
Geotab is advancing security, connecting commercial vehicles to the internet and providing web-based analytics to help customers better manage their fleets. Geotab’s open platform and Geotab Marketplace ®, offering hundreds of third-party solution options, allows both small and large businesses to automate operations by integrating vehicle data with their other data assets. Processing billions of data points a day, Geotab leverages data analytics and machine learning to improve productivity, optimize fleets through the reduction of fuel consumption, enhance driver safety and achieve strong compliance to regulatory changes.
Our team is growing and we’re looking for people who follow their passion, think differently and want to make an impact. Ours is a fast paced, ever changing environment. Geotabbers accept that challenge and are willing to take on new tasks and activities - ones that may not always be described in the initial job description. Join us for a fulfilling career with opportunities to innovate, great benefits, and our fun and inclusive work culture. Reach your full potential with Geotab. To see what it’s like to be a Geotabber, check out our blog and follow us @InsideGeotab on Instagram.

Who You Are

Geotab is looking for entrepreneurial product and business leaders to head our domains – focused teams that each own a customer outcome and the business results that come with it. As a Head of Domain, you'll own the strategy, roadmap and results for your area, lead a multi-disciplinary team of product managers, designers and engineers, and turn customer problems into products that customers adopt and pay for.

What You'll Do

This is a role for someone who has
built and sold something
: a leader who measures success by business results, not by what shipped, and who uses AI to change how work gets done. You'll report to Geotab's Technology Development Board and operate with real autonomy as the business owner of your domain.
We welcome applicants nationwide! If you’re based near one of our office hubs, this role follows our hybrid model, blending the comfort of working from home with regular on-site days to connect and collaborate.
This is an evergreen posting. We're building a pipeline of exceptional leaders for current and future domain leadership opportunities across Technology Development.

How You'll Make An Impact

Own the outcome. Set the vision, strategy and roadmap for your domain and be accountable for its primary business results – adoption, revenue, retention and customer impact.
Run it like a business. Make clear build, buy and partner decisions, prioritize by customer and revenue impact, and say no when the return isn't there.
Stay close to customers. Ground your team in customers' real experience to find the problems worth solving, and work with sales, support and partners to bring solutions to market.
Lead the AI shift. Redesign how your domain works around AI to move faster, and help others across the organization do the same.
Build a high-performing team. Hire the right talent without settling, place people where their strengths matter most, set a clear and high bar, and develop the next generation of leaders.
Work across Geotab. Partner closely with platform, segment and other domain leaders, contribute beyond your own goals, and help shape strategy with the Technology Development Board.
Manage your investment. Own your domain's people and budget plan, make investment cases, and report on results and risks to the board.

What You'll Bring To This Role

10+ years of experience in product management, product engineering, or related customer-facing product roles.
5+ years of senior product and people leadership with cross-functional scope and direct accountability for customer-facing business outcomes.
Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or a related technical field (or equivalent combination of education and work experience).
Strong product leadership capability with demonstrated ability to define and execute customer-facing product strategy tied to measurable business outcomes, with P&L literacy and revenue attribution.
Cross-functional leadership experience managing teams across product management, product design, and product engineering disciplines, with proven capability in identifying and coaching high-potential leaders.
Excellent stakeholder management, change readiness, and communication skills to effectively collaborate with platform teams, segment leads, and executive leadership in evolving organizational structures.
Familiarity with modern product discovery, validation practices, and engineering practices (CI/CD, cloud-native delivery, agile), alongside the ability to redesign domain workflows around AI to compress effort.

Please note: Geotab does not accept agency resumes and is not responsible for any fees related to unsolicited resumes. Please do not forward resumes to Geotab employees.

This posting is not for an existing vacancy.

Why Job Seekers Choose Geotab

Flex working arrangements
Baby bonus & parental leave top up program
Online learning and networking opportunities
Electric vehicle purchase incentive program
Competitive medical and dental benefits
Retirement savings program

*The above are offered to full-time permanent employees only

How We Work

At Geotab, we thrive on a flexible hybrid work model that combines the dynamic energy and connection of in-person collaboration with the independence and flexibility of virtual work. We believe that coming together in person is fundamental to cultivating trust, nurturing a vibrant culture of belonging, and fostering meaningful innovation across our diverse teams. Office visit schedules are tailored thoughtfully based on role requirements. Specific expectations regarding workplace location and on-site attendance for this position will be shared during the hiring process.
We believe that ensuring diversity is fundamental to our future growth and progress and is an integral part of our business. We believe that success happens where new ideas can flourish – in an environment that is rich in diversity and a place where people from various backgrounds can work together. Geotab encourages applications from all qualified individuals. We are committed to accommodating people with disabilities during the recruitment and assessment processes and when people are hired. We will ensure the accessibility needs of employees with disabilities are taken into account as part of performance management, career development, training and redeployment processes. If you require accommodation at any stage of the application process or want more information about our diversity and inclusion as well as accommodation policies and practices, please contact us at careers@geotab.com. By submitting a job application to Geotab Inc. or its affiliates and subsidiaries (collectively, “Geotab”), you acknowledge Geotab’s collection, use and disclosure of your personal data in accordance with our Privacy Policy. Click here to read our Privacy Notice.
The annual base salary for this position is the expected annual salary for this role, and may be subject to change. Geotab offers various perks and benefits and other compensation components that an individual may be eligible for. The actual base salary for this position depends on a variety of factors such as but not limited to skills, qualifications, education and overall experience, including the location the applicant lives while performing the job. This also includes equity with other team members and alignment with local market data. 12-18 years of progressive retail planning experience in premium apparel/lifestyle specialty retail, including 3+ years in direct leadership.
Deep expertise in single-pool omnichannel models across retail, e-commerce, and wholesale.
Mastery of MFP, OTB governance, WSSI cadences, and algorithmic markdown optimization.
Proven experience leading, mentoring, and upskilling planning and allocation teams.

jobs.description:
Job Description

You will be working on a flexible hybrid schedule as part of Fidelity’s dynamic working arrangement.

The work location for this role is 483 Bay Street in Toronto until approximately late 2026, when the work location will change to the new Mississauga office at 3 Robert Speck Parkway.

Current work authorization for Canada is required for all openings.

At Fidelity, we’ve been helping Canadian investors build better financial futures for over 35 years. We offer individuals and institutions a range of trusted investment portfolios and services - and we’re constantly seeking to find new and better ways to help our clients. As a privately owned company, we boldly embrace innovation in all areas as we continue to grow our business into the future.

Working with us means you’ll be part of a diverse and dedicated group of people who make a real difference for our clients and communities every day. You’ll have a wide range of opportunities to grow and develop your career in an inclusive environment where you’ll feel valued and supported to be your best - both personally and professionally.

How You’ll Make An Impact

The Director, Product Strategy and Commercialization will lead the commercial strategy for Fidelity’s digital investing platform, ensuring the Investly product roadmap, go-to-market priorities, incentives, lifecycle programs and client value proposition are directly tied to measurable business outcomes. Working within their team and cross-functionally, they will be accountable for translating the Investly vision into a prioritized growth agenda that supports funded investor growth, AUM growth, revenue generation, margin improvement, client lifetime value and long-term P&L performance.

They will own the commercial planning discipline for Investly, including business case development, roadmap prioritization, experimentation, commercialization planning, incentive optimization, feedback collection, partner alignment and performance management against agreed business targets.

Within the team, the Director, Product Strategy and Commercialization will establish, maintain and iterate the operating cadence, goals and metric framework required to run Investly with stronger commercial discipline. They will ensure team members and cross-functional partners understand how their work contributes to growth, revenue, cost efficiency, client outcomes, enterprise value and P&L performance.

Own the commercial strategy, business planning and P&L accountability framework for Investly, including the strategic plan, business cases and performance targets that guide product and growth decisions.
Own the commercialization programme for priority growth initiatives, coordinating cross-functional execution and ensuring initiatives deliver against agreed business outcomes.
Translate customer, market and performance insights into product, commercialization and lifecycle priorities that improve user experience and drive profitable growth.
Champion a data-informed, user-centric and commercially disciplined approach to product strategy, commercialization and P&L performance.
Build and lead a high-performing team that aligns with Fidelity’s values and that collaborates well in cross-functional environments Collaborate with Digital Client Experience, Product Managers, Investly, Incentive Managers and cross-functionally with Business Development, Social Media, Data Analytics, Finance, Risk, Compliance and Marketing to deliver customer-centric, compliant and financially sound outcomes.
Identifying products and services, building rigorous business cases, setting high-level business requirements for Software Product, defining GTM briefs for Marketing, and making clear trade-off recommendations based on expected commercial value, resource requirements, risk and P&L impact.

What We’re Looking For

Degree in Business, Software or a related field/equivalent experience
7+ years in digital products, product strategy, commercialization, growth, business planning or related strategy roles, including experience managing commercial outcomes
3+ years of experience managing and growing a high-performing team
Experience in digital platforms within the wealth industry
Experience in strategy, business planning and P&L-oriented decision-making
Experience building business cases, performance scorecards and commercialization plans tied to measurable financial and growth outcomes

The Skills Set You Bring

Strong understanding of industry dynamics, strategy, business planning, product commercialization and digital platform economics
Advance communication and team-building skills
Skills in leadership through influence
The ability to gain expert-level knowledge in a wide variety of areas
Proven people leadership experience with a focus on developing and leveraging the capabilities of a high-performing team.
Use of AI and data tools for strategy creation, business case development, performance analysis, experimentation and product outcomes
Understanding of securities, digital assets and mobile application development
Product and growth portfolio prioritization
Experimentation and data-driven decision making
Strong financial and commercial acumen, including P&L management, business case development, unit economics, investment prioritization, growth forecasting, CAC/LTV analysis and resource allocation against growth objectives

jobs.title: Director, International Business Transformation & Strategy Execution (flexible location)
jobs.description:
At ABB, we help industries run leaner and cleaner—and every person here makes that happen. You’ll be empowered to lead, supported to grow, and proud of the impact we create together. Join us and help run what runs the world.

The work model for the role is:
Hybrid

Your Role And Responsibilities

This Director role is a strategic transformation position within ABB's NEMA International division, reporting to the EVP International Sales. The role is pivotal in building a scalable international business platform by strengthening alignment across Regions, Business Lines and functions, removing structural barriers to growth and driving implementation of the Stabilize-Optimize-Scale roadmap. The successful candidate will drive business transformation across regions while building scalable operating foundations, combining expertise in strategy execution, operating-model redesign, business process management, change leadership, and executive influence within a complex global matrix.

The work model for the role is: hybrid ;

The role is contributing to the Motion NEMA Motors division globally.

International travel of approximately 30-40% will be required for the role.

You will be mainly accountable for:

Own and drive the NEMA International transformation roadmap aligned with the Stabilize-Optimize-Scale journey, translating strategy into prioritized initiatives with clear outcomes, milestones and success measures while maintaining visibility of progress and risks to leadership.
Act as senior integrator between NEMA International and Global Business Lines, establishing governance mechanisms and cross-functional commitments that align product, portfolio, and investment priorities with international market requirements while escalating critical dependencies that constrain growth.
Lead resolution of systemic barriers at the interfaces between International Sales, Global Operations, IT, Finance, HR and other supporting functions, converting fragmented issues into prioritized root-cause initiatives with clear accountability and measurable outcomes.
Serve as custodian of the NEMA International target operating model, ensuring organizational accountabilities, governance, processes, technology and capabilities evolve coherently to enable profitable international growth, from stabilization through optimization and scale, while designing the organization for future growth and acquisitions.
Lead an executive-level International Transformation Office that manages the transformation portfolio, governance cadence, dependency view and risk escalation, mobilizing cross-functional workstreams and intervening to resolve ownership gaps, resource constraints or delayed decisions.
Lead adoption of the new international organization and ways of working through change leadership, stakeholder engagement and capability building, while establishing a continuous improvement framework that connects frontline issues to structural business improvements and embeds continuous improvement into leadership accountability.

Qualifications for the role:

Minimum 10 years of progressive experience in business transformation, strategy execution, operating-model design, commercial excellence, enterprise program leadership or management consulting.
Bachelor's or Master's degree in Business Administration, Engineering, Strategy, Operations, Information Systems or a related discipline.
Experience in an internal strategy, transformation, business excellence or consulting role.
Demonstrated experience leading complex, cross-functional transformation across multiple geographies or business units.
Proven ability to align senior stakeholders and functions behind a shared agenda without relying on direct authority.
Experience translating strategy into executable roadmaps, governance, operating mechanisms and measurable outcomes.
Strong business acumen and ability to connect transformation to customer value, growth, margin, cash, productivity and organizational capability.
Excellent executive communication, facilitation and synthesis skills.
Ability to constructively challenge established practices and navigate ambiguity with pace and judgement.
Familiarity with international commercial models, CRM/ERP environments and end-to-end customer processes.
Experience in an industrial, manufacturing, electromechanical or B2B technology environment is an advantage. Recognized transformation, change management, Lean, Six Sigma or program-management certification is a plus.
Fluent English language skills.

More about us:

ABB’s NEMA Motors Division is a marketer, designer and manufacturer that offers Baldor-Reliance® industrial electric motors, primarily in North America. The Division focuses on quality, reliability and efficiency to provide a comprehensive offering of NEMA motors in the market across most industrial segments and applications.

We value people from different backgrounds. Apply today for your next career step within ABB and visit www.abb.com to learn about the impact of our solutions across the globe. #MyABBStory

We look forward to receiving your application (documents submitted in English are appreciated). If you want to discover more about ABB, take another look at our website
www.abb.com
.

_________________

Directeur(-trice) transformation des activités internationales et exécution de la stratégie (lieu de travail flexible)

Nos convictions

Chez ABB, nous nous engageons à relever les défis mondiaux. Nos valeurs fondamentales — la bienveillance, le courage, la curiosité et la collaboration —combinées à notre engagement envers la diversité, l’inclusion et l’égalité des chances, sont au cœur de notre volonté de donner à chacun et chacune les moyens de créer des solutions durables.

Écrivez le prochain chapitre de votre histoire chez ABB.

Votre rôle et vos responsabilités

Ce poste de direction est axé sur la transformation stratégique au sein de la division NEMA International d’ABB et relève du vice-président exécutif, ventes internationales. Il joue un rôle essentiel dans la mise en place d’une plateforme d’affaires internationales évolutive en renforçant l’alignement entre les régions, les secteurs d’activité et les fonctions, en éliminant les obstacles structurels à la croissance et en pilotant la mise en œuvre de la feuille de route Stabiliser-Optimiser-Déployer à grande échelle. La personne retenue pilotera la transformation des activités dans les différentes régions tout en établissant des fondations opérationnelles évolutives, en mettant à profit son expertise en exécution de la stratégie, en refonte des modèles opérationnels, en gestion des processus d’affaires, en leadership du changement et en influence auprès de la haute direction dans une structure matricielle mondiale complexe.

Le mode de travail pour ce poste est : hybride;

Ce poste contribue aux activités de la division Moteurs NEMA du secteur Motion à l’échelle mondiale.

Ce poste exige des déplacements internationaux représentant environ 30 à 40 % du temps de travail.

Vos principales responsabilités seront les suivantes :

Prendre en charge et piloter la feuille de route de transformation de NEMA International, en cohérence avec le parcours Stabiliser-Optimiser-Déployer à grande échelle, en traduisant la stratégie en initiatives prioritaires assorties de résultats, de jalons et de critères de réussite clairs, tout en assurant à la direction une visibilité sur les progrès et les risques.
Agir comme principal point d’intégration entre NEMA International et les secteurs d’activité mondiaux, en établissant des mécanismes de gouvernance et des engagements interfonctionnels qui alignent les priorités en matière de produits, de portefeuille et d’investissements sur les exigences des marchés internationaux, tout en portant à l’attention de la direction les interdépendances critiques qui freinent la croissance.
Piloter la résolution des obstacles systémiques aux interfaces entre les ventes internationales, les opérations mondiales, les TI, les finances, les RH et les autres fonctions de soutien, en regroupant les problèmes isolés en initiatives prioritaires visant leurs causes fondamentales, assorties de responsabilités claires et de résultats mesurables.
Veiller au maintien du modèle opérationnel cible de NEMA International, en s’assurant que les responsabilités organisationnelles, la gouvernance, les processus, les technologies et les capacités évoluent de façon cohérente pour soutenir une croissance internationale rentable, de la stabilisation à l’optimisation, puis au déploiement à grande échelle, tout en concevant l’organisation en fonction de sa croissance et de ses acquisitions futures.
Diriger un bureau de transformation internationale au niveau de la haute direction, responsable du portefeuille de transformation, du rythme de gouvernance, du suivi des interdépendances et du signalement des risques, en mobilisant les chantiers interfonctionnels et en intervenant pour résoudre les lacunes dans l’attribution des responsabilités, les contraintes de ressources ou les retards décisionnels.
Piloter l’adoption de la nouvelle organisation internationale et des nouvelles façons de travailler grâce au leadership du changement, à la mobilisation des parties prenantes et au développement des capacités, tout en établissant un cadre d’amélioration continue qui relie les problèmes de première ligne aux améliorations structurelles des activités et intègre l’amélioration continue aux responsabilités de la direction.

Qualifications Requises Pour Le Poste

Au moins 10 ans d’expérience avec des responsabilités croissantes en transformation des activités, en exécution de la stratégie, en conception de modèles opérationnels, en excellence commerciale, en direction de programmes d’entreprise ou en conseil en gestion.
Baccalauréat ou maîtrise en administration des affaires, en génie, en stratégie, en gestion des opérations, en systèmes d’information ou dans une discipline connexe.
Expérience dans un rôle interne en stratégie, en transformation, en excellence opérationnelle ou en consultation.
Expérience démontrée dans la direction de transformations complexes et interfonctionnelles touchant plusieurs régions géographiques ou unités d’affaires.
Capacité éprouvée à rallier les parties prenantes de la haute direction et les fonctions autour de priorités communes, sans s’appuyer sur une autorité hiérarchique directe.
Expérience dans la traduction de la stratégie en feuilles de route réalisables, en structures de gouvernance, en mécanismes opérationnels et en résultats mesurables.
Solide sens des affaires et capacité à relier la transformation à la valeur pour la clientèle, à la croissance, aux marges, aux flux de trésorerie, à la productivité et aux capacités organisationnelles.
Excellentes aptitudes en communication auprès de la haute direction, en animation et en synthèse.
Capacité à remettre en question les pratiques établies de façon constructive et à évoluer dans l’ambiguïté avec rapidité et discernement.
Connaissance des modèles commerciaux internationaux, des environnements de gestion de la relation client (CRM) et de planification des ressources de l’entreprise (ERP), ainsi que des processus clients de bout en bout.
Une expérience dans un environnement industriel, manufacturier, électromécanique ou de technologies interentreprises (B2B) constitue un atout. Une certification reconnue en transformation, en gestion du changement, en Lean, en Six Sigma ou en gestion de programmes constitue un atout.
Maîtrise de l’anglais.

Pour en savoir plus sur nous

La division Moteurs NEMA d’ABB commercialise, conçoit et fabrique des moteurs électriques industriels Baldor-Reliance®, principalement en Amérique du Nord. La division mise sur la qualité, la fiabilité et l’efficacité afin d’offrir une gamme complète de moteurs NEMA sur le marché, couvrant la plupart des segments et des applications industriels.

Nous valorisons les personnes de tous horizons. Postulez dès aujourd’hui po

jobs.title: Director of Information Technology
jobs.description:
Director of Information Technology (SOC 2 ownership a Must)

Company Aarista Technology LLC
Location Burnaby,BC (On-Site)
Employment type Full-time
Direct reports 5

Direct ownership and successful completion of a SOC 2 Type II audit is required. Candidates must have hands-on experience managing audit preparation, evidence collection, control testing, auditor coordination, and remediation.

The Director of IT runs day-to-day IT operations at Aarista, a healthcare software company. You will own our security and compliance programs (SOC 2, HIPAA/HITECH, ONC/Cures Act, EPCS, Surescripts and public health reporting), lead the IT team, own service desk quality, keep our processes documented, and manage IT assets, procurement and budget. You will also translate the VP of IT's strategy into an executable roadmap and drive it to completion.

Key responsibilities:

Security and compliance

Own Aarista's security program and the operational side of every compliance framework we hold or are pursuing:
o SOC 2 Type I and Type II
o HIPAA Privacy, Security and Breach Notification Rules, and HITECH
o ONC Health IT certification and 21st Century Cures Act requirements, including the FHIR Patient Access API and information blocking rules
Coordinate audits and certifications: evidence collection, control testing, auditor requests and remediation tracking.
Maintain IT and security policies, including access control, change management, incident response, backup and disaster recovery.
Run periodic access reviews, risk assessments, vendor risk reviews and security awareness training.
Partner with Engineering, Clinical and Operations teams to keep PHI handling and regulated product features compliant.

Team leadership and service desk

Lead, coach and evaluate the IT team; set priorities, assign work and run regular one-on-ones and team reviews.
Own the ticketing process end to end: intake, triage, prioritization, escalation and closure.
Define and enforce service levels (response and resolution times) and report performance monthly.
Run root-cause reviews on recurring or high-impact incidents and drive permanent fixes.
Plan staffing, on-call coverage and hiring needs as the company grows.

Process and documentation

Make sure every IT process is documented, current and stored in SharePoint, our system of record.
Maintain runbooks, SOPs, onboarding and offboarding checklists, and access-provisioning procedures.
Establish a review cadence so documentation stays accurate after system or process changes.
Support the company-wide documentation initiative with IT standards and templates.

Assets, procurement and budget

Maintain an accurate inventory of hardware, software and licenses across the full lifecycle.
Manage ordering, vendor relationships, renewals and contract negotiations.
Build, track and report against the annual IT budget; flag variances early.
Find cost savings through license right-sizing and vendor consolidation.

IT strategy execution

Translate the VP of IT's strategy into a prioritized roadmap with owners, milestones and budgets.
Track progress and report status, risks and decisions to the VP of IT.
Evaluate new tools and platforms and make recommendations.
Act as the IT point of contact for cross-functional projects.

Required qualifications:

8+ years in IT operations, including 3+ years managing an IT team.
Hands-on experience running a service desk with defined SLAs and a ticketing platform.
Direct experience running SOC 2 audits and HIPAA/HITECH compliance programs; exposure to ONC certification, EPCS or other healthcare regulatory audits.
Proven ownership of an IT budget, vendor contracts and asset lifecycle management.
Strong working knowledge of Microsoft 365, Entra ID (Azure AD), endpoint management and SharePoint.
A track record of writing clear, maintained process documentation.
Excellent communication skills with both technical and non-technical stakeholders.
Bachelor's degree in IT, Computer Science or a related field, or equivalent experience.

Preferred qualifications:

Experience in healthcare IT or at a SaaS/EHR vendor handling PHI.

Join a purpose driven winning team, committed to results, in an inclusive and high-performing culture.

The Team

Global Wealth Banking and Markets Engineering (GWBMT) is the fast-moving, award-winning technology engine that powers Scotiabank's Wealth and Capital Markets businesses.

The Platform Engineering organization provides the foundational technology platforms and cloud services that enable application teams to innovate rapidly, securely, and at scale. Our portfolio includes enterprise Kubernetes platforms spanning on-premises and Google Cloud environments, Cloud Enablement Services, Kafka as a Service, Airflow as a Service, Fine-Grained Access Management capabilities, and future developer platform offerings that accelerate application modernization and cloud adoption.

We are seeking a Director Platform Product Owner to lead the product strategy, roadmap, adoption, and delivery of a portfolio of enterprise platform products that serve hundreds of engineers and mission-critical applications across the bank.

This role sits at the intersection of technology, product management, engineering, and business strategy. The successful candidate will be responsible for defining and evolving platform products that enable cloud adoption, application modernization, developer productivity, security, and operational excellence.

As a senior product leader, you will partner closely with Platform Engineering, Architecture, Security, Infrastructure, and application development teams to ensure our platforms deliver measurable business value, exceptional user experiences, and scalable solutions that meet the needs of a rapidly evolving enterprise landscape.

You will act as the voice of the engineering customer while balancing engineering priorities, platform sustainability, risk management, and strategic technology objectives.

Is this role right for you? In this role you will:

Define and execute the strategic vision, roadmap, and lifecycle management of a portfolio of platform engineering products and services.
Develop product strategies that accelerate cloud adoption, platform standardization, application modernization, and engineering productivity.
Identify emerging customer needs and market trends to drive innovation and platform evolution.

Own the end-to-end platform user experience across onboarding, self-service workflows, documentation, observability, support engagement, and lifecycle management.

Experience working with cloud platforms, enterprise infrastructure, and application modernization initiatives.

They will also provide subject matter expertise and point of view on how to advance our technology capabilities such as AI, machine learning, large language models, and cloud-based tools.

Manage the design, development and implementation of data strategies, data standards, data procedures, data governance and data security to support Global Human Resources and ensure alignment with the Bank’s Data Governance Framework.
Establish data quality rules, standards and thresholds and ensure appropriate data quality monitoring practices are in place; lead the identification and root-cause analysis of data quality issues and support remediation efforts in a timely manner based on priority.
Develop teams and create a high performing culture that nurtures talent and helps bring to life our values of collaboration, growth, and respect.
Manage direct reports and the broader department to achieve organizational goals in accordance with company policies and practices.

Build a high-performance environment and implements a people strategy that attracts, retains, develops and motivates their team by fostering an inclusive work environment and using a coaching mindset and behaviors; communicating vison/values/business strategy; and, managing succession and development planning for the team.
Create an environment in which the team pursues effective and efficient operations of the respective areas in accordance with Scotiabank’s Values and Code of Conduct, while ensuring the adequacy, adherence to and effectiveness of day-to-day business controls to meet obligations.

 Develop a proactive strategic intelligence function to monitor emerging trends, risks, and opportunities across animal agriculture, corporate practices, public policy, technology, and relevant markets.

 Translate complex research, external developments, and quantitative and qualitative data into clear, actionable recommendations that support organizational strategy and systemic change.

 Establish an organization-wide impact measurement framework, including meaningful performance indicators, evaluation methodologies, and learning mechanisms to assess effectiveness across programs and geographies.

 Lead technology-enabled transformation by identifying opportunities to improve productivity and organizational effectiveness through AI, automation, integrated data systems, and emerging technologies.

 Oversee the development, integration, and adoption of technology solutions that streamline workflows, strengthen decision-making, and improve operational performance.

 Define and implement a practical technology roadmap, prioritizing investments according to organizational needs, expected value, scalability, and implementation feasibility.

jobs.title: Associate Vice President, Corporate Finance
jobs.description:
Overview

At KPMG in Canada, our people bring their unique perspectives to Canada’s most important challenges. Here, you can build momentum that reaches beyond our business, develop skills for the future, and take ownership of your career with support at every stage. Join a firm where your career can make a difference.

KPMG Corporate Finance Inc. is the Ontario Securities Commission (OSC)-regulated entity through which KPMG LLP provides investment banking services in Canada. KPMG Corporate Finance services are principally comprised of merger, acquisition and divestiture services and financing services, including raising debt and equity capital. We offer independent financial advisory and investment banking services to both private and public companies.

With over 100 professionals across Canada and a global network of 3,000+ bankers in 160 offices, we combine local execution expertise with global reach. KPMG Corporate Finance is consistently ranked the #1 mid-market investment bank in Canada.

Our growing diversified investment banking team is seeking an Associate Vice President (Manager) to join our team in Calgary, Edmonton or Winnipeg to play a key role across all aspects of transaction delivery.

What You Will Do

Assume responsibility for the day-to-day execution and delivery of service on a range of corporate finance projects.
Draft pitch books, teasers, confidential information memorandums (CIM) and other transaction process documentation.
Manage, mentor and train junior corporate finance professionals (Analysts & Associates).
Prepare and review various forms of financial analysis, including complex financial models.
Conduct market and industry research, detailed financial analysis and business valuations.
Assist in the identification of potential acquisition targets, purchasers and/or investors.
Undertake engagement and practice management responsibilities, including billings and adherence to professional practice requirements.
Lead proactive business development and deal initiation activities.

This role provides significant learning opportunities and increasing responsibility over time. At times, business needs arise, and employees are required and agree to work beyond their normal workday or work week to fulfill the accountabilities required for their job. Likewise, employees need time to devote to personal matters, and our approach to flexibility provides for this.

What You Bring To The Role

An undergraduate degree in finance, commerce, business, accounting, economics or other related field.
4-6 years of relevant post-graduate experience, in Corporate Finance, or a related field e.g. transaction advisory, investment banking, private equity, or corporate development.
Proven track record of M&A transaction initiation/execution in a fast-paced professional setting – as exhibited by your deal credential list which should accompany your cover letter.
CPA, CBV or CFA designations are all considered assets.
Strong technical finance proficiency, including knowledge of financial statements and general accounting principles.
Demonstrated experience or ability in training and developing junior staff members.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills (English).

What We Offer

Support for candidates enrolled in professionally accredited designation programs (CPA, CBV, CFA, etc.) including paid enrollment costs, paid study / exam days, ongoing coaching and third-party courses / materials for exam preparation.
Meaningful roles on a variety of Corporate Finance assignments for some of Canada’s premier companies, with support and coaching from senior Corporate Finance executives that promote professional growth and development.
Assignment of a Performance Manager on day one to help guide and grow your career as a Corporate Finance professional.
Deal Advisory team events throughout the year to help build a strong team culture.
Modern office space in our recently renovated downtown offices in Calgary, Edmonton and Winnipeg.

Providing you with the support you need to be at your best

Our Values, The KPMG Way

Integrity
, we do what is right | Excellence
, we never stop learning and improving | Courage
, we think and act boldly | Together
, we respect each other and draw strength from our differences | For Better
, we do what matters

KPMG in Canada is a proud equal opportunities employer and we are committed to creating a respectful, inclusive and barrier-free workplace that allows all of our people to reach their full potential. A diverse workforce is key to our success and we believe in bringing your whole self to work. We welcome all qualified candidates to apply and hope you will choose KPMG in Canada as your employer of choice.

Adjustments and accommodations throughout the recruitment process

At KPMG, we are committed to fostering an inclusive recruitment process where all candidates can be themselves and excel. We aim to provide a positive experience and are prepared to offer adjustments or accommodations to help you perform at your best. Adjustments (informal requests), such as extra preparation time or the option for micro breaks during interviews, and accommodations (formal requests), such as accessible communication supports or technology aids, are tailored to individual needs and role requirements. You will have an opportunity to request an adjustment or accommodation at any point throughout the recruitment process. If you require support, please contact KPMG’s Employee Relations Service team by calling 1-888-466-4778.

AI Usage

We embrace the use of artificial intelligence (AI) to enhance the candidate experience and streamline our recruitment processes. AI tools may help with organizing applications or surfacing relevant qualifications. However, no hiring decisions are made using AI. Every hiring decision is made by our hiring managers and recruitment professionals, who are equipped with training that empowers them to use these tools responsibly. AI technologies used in our recruitment process undergo detailed risk assessments, including security and privacy requirements, that align with KPMG’s Trusted AI framework.

We believe technology should empower human judgment, not replace it. It’s one of the many ways we’re delivering on our vision of being a technology-first, people-driven firm.

jobs.title: Chief Information Officer
jobs.description:
Putting people first, every day

BDO is a firm built on a foundation of positive relationships with our people and our clients. Each day, our professionals provide exceptional service, helping clients with advice and insight they can trust. In turn, we offer an award-winning environment that fosters a people-first culture with a high priority on your personal and professional growth.

Your Opportunity

The Chief Information Officer (CIO)
is responsible for establishing and executing the firm's enterprise technology strategy, ensuring technology capabilities enable business growth, operational excellence, security, and an exceptional people experience.

Reporting to the Chief Digital & Technology Officer, the CIO partners closely with Managing Partners, business leaders, and C-suite colleagues to align technology investments and services with strategic priorities. The CIO leads enterprise technology operations, architecture, infrastructure, end-user technology services, cybersecurity enablement, vendor partnerships, and workforce planning while fostering a modern, secure, and high-performing digital workplace.

The CIO is accountable for delivering reliable, scalable, secure, and cost-effective technology services that enable our people to do their best work and support the firm's continued growth and transformation. This role requires technical depth to guide architecture, platforms, security, data, integration, and service delivery decisions, combined with the business fluency to align stakeholders around practical outcomes.

Key Accountabilities & Responsibilities:

Enterprise Technology Strategy & Business Partnership

Develop and execute a multi-year enterprise technology strategy, roadmaps, investment priorities, and operating plans aligned with firm priorities and business objectives.
Serve as a trusted advisor to the Executive Leadership Team, Managing Partners, and business leaders, translating business priorities into practical technology initiatives with measurable outcomes and clear value realization.
Anticipate emerging technology trends and assess opportunities to leverage AI, automation, cloud, and modern workplace capabilities to improve productivity, employee experience, and business performance.
Communicate technology strategy, risks, investments, and outcomes in clear business terms and represent technology leadership in executive forums, governance committees, and strategic planning discussions.

Technology Architecture, Platforms & Modernization

Provide senior technical leadership across enterprise architecture, infrastructure, applications, integration, identity, data, cloud, and solution architecture, establishing standards and decision frameworks that support secure, scalable, resilient, and maintainable solutions.
Lead technical trade-off and investment discussions across modernization, build-versus-buy decisions, platform consolidation, integration patterns, technical debt, resiliency, lifecycle management, and total cost of ownership.
Guide the evolution of cloud and hybrid platforms, enterprise integration, data platforms, automation, and AI-enabled capabilities in partnership with data, AI, security, and business leaders.
Drive modernization of infrastructure, networks, identity and access management, endpoint and collaboration platforms, monitoring, and operational tooling, supported by disciplined delivery practices such as DevSecOps, automation, observability, and continuous improvement.
Translate complex technical issues into clear business choices, risks, investment implications, and recommended actions for senior stakeholders.

Technology Operations, Digital Workplace & Resilience

Provide strategic oversight of enterprise technology operations, infrastructure, end-user services, service management, and the modern workplace, ensuring reliable, scalable, resilient, and productive technology experiences.
Establish service standards, operating metrics, and performance expectations, using employee feedback and service insights to continuously improve the technology experience.
Lead business continuity, disaster recovery, operational resiliency, and technology adoption efforts while balancing user experience, accessibility, security, scalability, and cost effectiveness.

Security, Risk, Governance & Investment

Partner closely with Information Security leadership to maintain a strong enterprise security posture while enabling business agility, ensuring technology operates within established security, privacy, risk, compliance, and regulatory requirements.
Establish and maintain effective technology governance, architecture standards, policies, controls, and risk-management practices that are measurable, auditable, and aligned with enterprise risk appetite.
Develop and manage the enterprise technology budget and strategic vendor portfolio, overseeing sourcing, contract negotiations, performance, and investment decisions to maximize business value, service quality, and cost effectiveness.

People & Organizational Leadership

Build, lead, and develop a high-performing technology organization focused on service excellence, accountability, collaboration, and continuous improvement.
Attract, develop, retain, and succession-plan technology talent capable of supporting current and future business needs, partnering with Human Resources on workforce planning, career development, and organizational effectiveness.
Foster an inclusive, learning-oriented culture where people are empowered to grow, collaborate, challenge thinking, and deliver meaningful outcomes.

How Do We Define Success for Your Role?

You bring BDO's strategy to life by leading with genuine care, focusing on what matters most, embracing progress over preservation, and fostering a culture where people can do more together.
You establish technology as a trusted business partner and strategic enabler, translating firm priorities into measurable technology outcomes.
You deliver a secure, resilient, reliable, and modern technology environment that supports exceptional employee and client experiences while enabling innovation and business agility.
You build a high-performing, accountable technology organization with the talent and capabilities required to support the firm's continued growth and transformation.
You maximize value from technology investments through disciplined planning and execution, strong governance, strategic partnerships, and continuous improvement.

Your Experience & Education

You are a forward-thinking, people-focused technology executive with significant experience leading enterprise technology functions within large, complex organizations.
You have a proven track record developing and executing enterprise technology strategies and leading significant modernization, transformation, operating model evolution, and organizational change.
You bring practical technical fluency across enterprise architecture, cloud and hybrid infrastructure, applications, cybersecurity, data platforms, integration, automation, identity and access management, service management, and modern workplace technologies.
You understand how AI, automation, cloud, cybersecurity, and emerging digital capabilities can be applied responsibly to improve productivity, resilience, service quality, and employee experience.
You are an exceptional communicator and business partner who can influence C-suite executives and senior leaders, translate complex technology decisions into clear business implications, and align investments to organizational priorities and measurable outcomes.
You have significant experience managing enterprise technology investments, budgets, strategic vendors, service performance, risk, governance, and operational resilience.
You bring strong leadership, talent development, and coaching capabilities, with a demonstrated ability to build inclusive, high-performing technology teams.
You are familiar with recognized technology, architecture, security, and service-management frameworks such as ITIL 4, COBIT, TOGAF, NIST CSF, ISO 27001, CIS Controls, Zero Trust, Agile, DevSecOps, SRE, FinOps, and cloud well-architected practices.
You hold a university degree in Information Technology, Computer Science, Engineering, Business, or a related discipline. An advanced degree or relevant executive technology certification is considered an asset.
Experience within professional services, consulting, or a similarly complex, relationship-driven organization is considered a strong asset.

Why BDO?

Our people-first approach to talent has earned us a spot among Canada’s Top 100 Employers for 2026. This recognition is a milestone we’re thrilled to add to our collection of awards for both experienced and student talent experiences.

At BDO, our people experience is guided by three core pillars— Do work with genuine care, Do what matters with purpose, and Do what’s next
- shaping how we support our people, serve our clients, and grow together.

Our firm is committed to providing an environment where you can be successful in the following ways:

We enable you to engage with how we change and evolve, being a key contributor to the success and growth of BDO in Canada.
We help you become a better professional within our services, industries, and markets with extensive opportunities for learning and development.
We support your achievement of personal goals outside of the office and making an impact on your community.
We foster a collaborative, inclusive environment where your ideas are valued, and you can do your best work with genuine care and purpose
We encourage innovation and forward thinking, empowering you to embrace what’s next and help shape the future of our firm

Giving back adds up:
Where company meets community. BDO is actively involved in our communities by supporting local charity initiatives. We support staff with local and national events where you will be given the opportunity to contribute to your community.

Total rewards that matter:
We pay for performance with competitive total cash compensation that recognizes and rewards your contribution. We provide comprehensive benefits from day one, and a flexible personal time off policy. We’re committed to supporting your overall wellbeing and provide reimbursement for wellness initiatives that fit your lifestyle.

Everyone counts:
We are committed to creating a workplace where employees can participate fully, contribute meaningfully and succeed without barriers. We are dedicated to fostering a workplace defined by respect, fairness, and a true sense of belonging for everyone. We recognize and celebrate the unique experiences, identities, and perspectives that each of us bring – and that these experiences strengthen how we work together. Our commitment extends to ensuring that our application process is both inclusive and accessible. If you require accommodation to complete the application process, please contact us.

Flexibility:
All BDO personnel are expected to spend some of their time working in the office, at the client site, and virtually unless accommodations or alternative work arrangements are in place.

Our model is a blended approach designed to support the flexible needs of our people, the firm and our clients. It’s about creating work experiences that meet everyone’s needs and providing flexibility to adjust when, where and how we work to meet the expectations of our role.

Code of Conduct:
Our Code of Conduct sets clear standards for how we conduct business. It reflects our shared values and commitments and includes guiding principles to help us make ethical decisions and maintain trust with each other, our clients, and the public.

BDO may use artificial intelligence enabled tools to support certain aspects of the recruitment process. While these tools assist our teams, our use of AI does not replace human decision making, and all employment-related outcomes are made by BDO personnel.

We’re building a relationship-oriented bank for the modern world. We need talented, passionate professionals who are dedicated to doing what’s right for our clients.

At CIBC, we embrace your strengths and your ambitions, so you are empowered at work. Our team members have what they need to make a meaningful impact and are truly valued for who they are and what they contribute.

To learn more about CIBC, please visit CIBC.com

What You'll Be Doing

As a key member of the Distribution Strategy team for Personal Banking and Imperial Service, you’ll help shape the strategy and priorities for CIBC’s banking centre and advisor channels. Reporting to the Senior Director, Distribution Strategy & Enablement, you’ll lead high-priority strategic and financial management work that supports growth, productivity, and stronger client and advisor experiences. Under the new CIBC Way operating model, the Distribution Strategy team supports the Banking Centre Distribution & Mass Affluent domain and is part of the Portfolio Value & Financial Management Centre of Excellence. In this role, you’ll connect channel strategy with portfolio-level insights and investment decisions, identify opportunities, and develop data-driven recommendations that help senior leaders prioritize investments and maximize value. You’ll partner with Crew Leads, Product Owners, Squads, Finance, and other Centres of Excellence to advance strategic priorities. You’ll also lead complex research and analysis, create materials for senior executive forums, and help strengthen the Centre of Excellence’s capabilities, operating practices, and talent.

At CIBC we enable the work environment most optimal for you to thrive in your role. You'll have the flexibility to manage your work activities within a hybrid work arrangement where you'll spend 1-3 days per week on-site, while other days will be remote.

Strategy development and decision support - Lead the development and evolution of strategies for CIBC’s banking centre and advisor channels. Connect client, market, operational, and financial insights to identify growth and productivity opportunities, establish strategic priorities, and inform multi-year roadmaps.
Financial management and benefit sizing - Lead rigorous financial and quantitative assessments of priority initiatives. Apply consistent methodologies, assumptions, tools, and benchmarks to evaluate expected benefits, test the reasonableness of estimates, and strengthen the quality and credibility of investment decisions.

jobs.description:
GitLab is the intelligent orchestration platform for DevSecOps. GitLab enables organizations to increase developer productivity, improve operational efficiency, reduce security and compliance risk, and accelerate digital transformation. More than 50 million registered users and more than 50% of the Fortune 100* trust GitLab to ship better, more secure software faster.

The same principles built into our products are reflected in how our team works: we embrace AI as a core productivity multiplier, with all team members expected to incorporate AI into their daily workflows to drive efficiency, innovation, and impact. GitLab is where careers accelerate, innovation flourishes, and every voice is valued. Our high-performance culture is driven by our values and continuous knowledge exchange, enabling our team members to reach their full potential while collaborating with industry leaders to solve complex problems. Co-create the future with us as we build technology that transforms how the world develops software.

Fortune 500® is a registered trademark of Fortune Media IP Limited, used under license. Claim based on GitLab data. Fortune 100 refers to the top 20% ranked companies in the 2025 Fortune 500 list, published in June 2025. Fortune and Fortune Media IP Limited are not affiliated with, and do not endorse products or services of GitLab.

An Overview Of This Role

As Director, Data Science, you'll lead GitLab's Product, Sales, and Finance Data Science teams and report to the VP of Data & Insights. You have two mandates:

Make Data Science a driver of growth. Connect the team's work to GitLab's biggest priorities: supporting product innovation, making sure what we launch is improved and scaled with data, improving product adoption through our GTM motions, and growing the consumption business. Make sure the work changes decisions at the executive level.
Set the bar for great data science. Define what makes a great Data Scientist at GitLab, from business partnership to technical rigor, and develop managers who build teams where everyone shows up to that standard.

You lead through your managers with an overall team size of 12 including data scientists and analysts, ensuring direction with the team across the data organization, and staying close enough to the work to pressure-test the analyses and models that matter most.

What You’ll Do

Build trusted relationships with executives across Product, Finance, and GTM, and act as their thought partner, shaping the questions the business should be asking, not just answering them
Own investment and prioritization across teams: decide where Data Science spends its time, and make trade-offs visible to senior leaders
Lead high-impact, cross-functional programs, such as driving new product adoption and growing our consumption business, from strategy through measurable business impact
Coach and mentor managers and senior ICs to grow as leaders, building succession and a bench of future leaders
Hold a high talent bar, and make sure every teammate grows into a trusted thought partner in their area
Set org-wide standards for metric definition, causal inference, and predictive modeling, and the role of AI in each
Build a high-trust culture of urgency, accountability, and open communication, and act on engagement and feedback across teams
Partner with Analytics Engineering, Data Engineering, and other data teams across the company to solve data opportunities together, aligned on a shared data and AI roadmap

What You’ll Bring

12+ years in data science, product analytics, or a related field, including 6+ years leading teams and 3+ years managing managers in B2B SaaS or tech
Track record of building and scaling a data science or analytics organization that executives treat as a strategic partner
Strong business acumen across product and go-to-market, with experience connecting data work to revenue and growth outcomes
Executive presence: communicates complex findings and trade-offs clearly to the C-suite, and coaches managers to do the same
Deep expertise in statistics, experimentation, and causal inference, with enough technical depth in SQL, Python, and ML to guide and pressure-test the team's work
Clear point of view on how AI is reshaping data science and analytics, and experience leading teams through that shift
Able to use GitLab, thrive in an all-remote, asynchronous company, model and coach GitLab's remote working competencies, and work in line with GitLab's values

Nice to Have

Experience with developer tools, DevSecOps, or product-led growth products
Experience with usage-based or consumption pricing models
Experience merging or restructuring data science and analytics teams
Thought leadership in data science or analytics, internally and externally
Advanced degree in a quantitative field

About The Team

Data Science at GitLab brings Data Science and Analytics together into one function. Our Data Scientists are business partners first, pairing strong business judgment with analytical rigor and statistical expertise. We help leaders decide where to invest, measure what worked, and understand how customers get value from GitLab.

The opportunity is growing fast. AI is driving growth in GitLab's consumption business, creating new ways for data to drive growth. As routine reporting becomes self-serve, the team focuses on the hard problems: experimentation, causal inference, production models, and recommendations leaders act on.
