jobs.description:
Infrastructure Ontario (IO), an Ontario crown corporation, provides a wide range of services to support the Ontario government’s initiative to modernize and maximize the value of public infrastructure and realty. IO has been recognized domestically and internationally for the way it does business and the success it has had with its major projects, real estate services, infrastructure lending, commercial projects, and development mandate. IO delivers some of the most complex, ambitious commercial and land development solutions for the Province and continues to evolve and expand its capabilities to maximize its public impact and deliver on its vision of creating a connected, modern and competitive Ontario.

Position Purpose

The Director, Capital Delivery (Healthcare planning and Initiatives) is responsible for leading a portfolio of complex healthcare infrastructure projects through pre-planning, planning, and project development, leading to procurement, transaction and implementation phases.

Working closely with healthcare organizations, government partners, consultants, advisors, and industry stakeholders, the Director is accountable for overseeing project development activities in early planning, managing due diligence and initial delivery model selections, navigating governance and approvals, and ensuring projects are effectively positioned for successful delivery. The role also provides leadership to project teams and serves as a key advisor on healthcare infrastructure investments and capital planning initiatives.

What You Will Do

Lead a portfolio of healthcare infrastructure projects through early planning and project development mainly, with opportunities to proceed further to procurement, and transaction phases.
Provide strategic oversight for business case development, capital planning activities, governance reviews, procurement processes, and transaction execution.
Manage and support multidisciplinary teams responsible for project planning, financial analysis, commercial strategy, procurement management, stakeholder engagement, and project development activities.
Collaborate with healthcare organizations, government ministries, consultants, legal advisors, financial advisors, and technical advisors to advance projects through key approval and procurement milestones.
Lead the development, evaluation, and implementation of business cases, based on a good understanding of procurement documents, project agreements, transaction strategies, and commercial frameworks.
Provide strategic advice on project governance, procurement approaches, commercial structures, risk allocation, and transaction strategies working closely with the commercial management team.
Identify and manage project risks, develop mitigation strategies, and facilitate resolution of complex commercial, financial, operational, and stakeholder-related issues.
Lead negotiations related to procurement processes, commercial agreements, consultant engagements, and transaction activities.
Prepare executive briefing materials, recommendations, reports, and presentations for senior leadership and governance bodies.
Establish and maintain effective relationships with healthcare partners, government representatives, consultants, advisors, and industry participants.
Support continuous improvement initiatives and contribute to the development of best practices related to healthcare capital planning, procurement, and transaction management.
Mentor and provide guidance to project staff and external partners fostering professional development and supporting successful project outcomes.

You bring significant experience leading complex healthcare, infrastructure, advisory, procurement, project development, or capital planning initiatives within the public or broader infrastructure sector. Procurement strategy development, transaction management, and commercial structuring of complex infrastructure projects.

jobs.title: Director, Product Analytics
jobs.description:
The Director, Product Analytics will lead the Product Analytics function within Group Benefits, with primary accountability for using data and analytics to deepen understanding of our products, customers and members and to support better product and business decisions.

The incumbent will shape the strategy and evolution of Product Analytics, partnering closely with Product, Distribution and other business leaders to provide trusted, relevant and actionable insights across the product lifecycle. The role will help identify emerging trends, understand product performance and customer needs, evaluate opportunities and support decisions that strengthen our Group Benefits products and the value they provide to Canadians.

Through better use of data and insights, the Director will help connect product decisions to customer and member outcomes, supporting the broader ambition of improving the health and well-being of Canadians.

In addition to Product Analytics, the Director will contribute to and lead broader analytics initiatives across Group Benefits where the team's capabilities, data and expertise can create value. This may include customer and member analytics, portfolio insights, operational analytics, strategic business priorities and emerging analytical needs.

Working closely with Product, Distribution, Operations, Data and Technology partners, the Director will lead the development and evolution of analytical capabilities, including advanced analytics, dashboards and reporting, self-service analytics, data products and strategic insights. The role will balance immediate business needs with scalable analytical solutions, strong data governance, appropriate data protection and a clear focus on business and customer value.

The Director will also lead and develop a high-performing analytics team, establishing clear priorities, strengthening analytical capabilities and building a culture focused on curiosity, partnership and measurable business outcomes.

Position Responsibilities

Lead the Product Analytics function and team. Establish priorities and a clear analytics roadmap aligned with Group Benefits' product and business strategies. Coach and develop employees while fostering a collaborative, accountable and high-performing team.
Partner closely with Product leaders and teams. Understand strategic priorities, opportunities and business questions and translate them into meaningful analytics, insights and recommendations.
Advance the Product Analytics strategy. Evolve the organization beyond traditional reporting toward proactive, insight-driven analytics that influence product strategy, development and ongoing management.
Deepen understanding of product performance and customer needs. Use data to identify trends, opportunities, emerging issues and areas where products or customer experiences can be improved.
Support decisions across the product lifecycle. Bring analytical perspectives to product development, enhancements, portfolio management, customer adoption and ongoing product performance.
Use analytics to improve outcomes for customers and members. Identify insights that enable better product and business decisions and contribute to improving the health and well-being of Canadians.
Develop and evolve Product Analytics capabilities. Advance dashboards, recurring reporting, exploratory analytics, self-service capabilities, data products and more sophisticated analytical approaches.
Enable data and analytics for AI adoption. Partner with Data and Technology teams to improve the quality, structure, accessibility and governance of data so it is appropriately prepared for use in AI and advanced analytics, helping unlock new Product Analytics and broader Group Benefits use cases.
Support broader Group Benefits analytics priorities. Apply the team's analytical expertise to strategic business questions beyond Product Analytics where appropriate, including customer, member, sponsor, portfolio and operational analytics.
Identify emerging analytical opportunities. Partner with business leaders to frame complex or ambiguous questions, assess available data, develop analytical approaches and translate findings into actionable recommendations.
Strengthen data storytelling. Translate complex information into clear, relevant and actionable insights for Product partners, senior leaders and other business stakeholders.
Drive consistency, efficiency and automation. Reduce manual effort and create reusable analytical capabilities that can be leveraged across products and other areas of Group Benefits.
Advance the analytics data ecosystem. Partner with Data and Technology teams to establish the data, platforms and capabilities required for reliable, timely and increasingly sophisticated product and business analytics.
Champion data quality, governance and protection. Ensure analytical products and insights are based on trusted data and adhere to enterprise governance, privacy and data protection standards.
Establish measures of success. Define and monitor business impact, stakeholder value, adoption, analytical effectiveness and continued advancement of capabilities.
Drive innovation and continuous improvement. Assess emerging technologies, including AI and advanced analytics, and identify practical opportunities to strengthen Product Analytics, improve analytical efficiency and create value across Group Benefits.
Represent Product Analytics in cross-functional initiatives. Ensure analytical needs and opportunities are appropriately considered in Group Benefits product, data, technology and business decisions.

Required Qualifications

University degree in business, finance, analytics, technology, mathematics, engineering or another quantitative field. An advanced degree is considered an asset.
Significant leadership experience within analytics, business intelligence, product analytics or a related data function, with demonstrated experience leading teams through change and transformation.
Strong experience using data and analytics to support product, customer or business decision-making, with an ability to translate complex information into meaningful insights and recommendations.
Demonstrated ability to apply analytics to a range of business problems, moving comfortably between recurring reporting, exploratory analysis, strategic insights and scalable analytical solutions.
Strong understanding of the Group Benefits business and product landscape, including the needs of customers, members, Distribution partners and internal business stakeholders.
Demonstrated experience developing and executing an analytics strategy and roadmap that balances immediate stakeholder needs with longer-term opportunities and scalable capabilities.
Experience partnering with Product and business teams to assess opportunities, understand performance and use data to influence strategic and tactical decisions.
Strong ability to use data visualization and storytelling to communicate insights and recommendations to technical and non-technical audiences.
Experience with modern analytics, business intelligence and data technologies, including dashboards, automated reporting and self-service analytical capabilities.
Understanding of the data foundations required to support AI and advanced analytics, including data quality, structure, governance, accessibility and responsible use.
Ability to identify analytical opportunities, structure ambiguous business questions and translate data into recommendations and measurable business outcomes.
Strong understanding of data management principles, including data quality, governance, privacy and protection.
Demonstrated ability to challenge business requests appropriately and prioritize analytical work based on customer value, business value, strategic alignment and organizational capacity.
Strong executive communication and stakeholder management skills, with demonstrated ability to establish credibility with senior leaders and cross-functional partners.
Ability to operate effectively across a complex, matrixed organization and bring together Product, business, Data and Technology partners around shared objectives.
Curious, pragmatic and outcome-oriented, with a passion for using data and analytics to improve products, customer experiences and the health and well-being of Canadians.

Preferred Qualifications

Bilingualism (English and French) is an asset. If the successful candidate is in Québec, proficiency in both languages will be required to support clients from various provinces outside of Quebec.

When You Join Our Team

We’ll empower you to learn and grow the career you want.
We’ll recognize and support you in a flexible environment where well-being and inclusion are more than just words.
As part of our global team, we’ll support you in shaping the future you want to see.

jobs.title: VP Senior Applied AI Full-Stack Engineer
jobs.description:
We are seeking a senior technical leader specializing in building high-performance, interactive data visualization platforms and enterprise reporting engines. This is an expert-level role focused on creating advanced, web-based analytical applications that combine rich, interactive frontends with highly optimized, data-intensive backends and distributed query engines. A mandatory and critical secondary focus of this role is the design and creation of custom Model Context Protocol (MCP) tools. You will build the bridge between LLMs/AI agents and our enterprise data layers, including Starburst, enabling AI to autonomously and securely query, analyze, and report on massive datasets.

Core Responsibilities

You will own the end-to-end design and delivery of sophisticated FinTech tools used directly by investment bankers, front-office traders, and financial analysts. This requires translating complex financial workflows into intuitive, high-fidelity web interfaces. Your primary focus will be on architecting and building highly interactive, web-based analytical dashboards using Angular and React, allowing users to slice, dice, and explore massive datasets in real-time.

A key function is leveraging Starburst (Trino) to query massive, distributed datasets with sub-second latency. You will design and implement robust backend microservices (Java/Spring Boot) optimized for low-latency data retrieval, heavy aggregation, and streaming large datasets to the frontend. Furthermore, you will be responsible for designing and optimizing scalable ETL processes to manage huge volumes of financial data.

A mandatory responsibility is to design, build, and maintain custom Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers and tools. This enables AI agents and LLMs to securely interface with internal databases, APIs, and reporting engines. You will also architect enterprise-grade document generation engines using the Aspose suite to programmatically create high-fidelity financial reports from complex templates.

As a hands-on player/coach, you will deliver complex data visualizations and reporting engines while mentoring junior engineers. This includes critically reviewing and taking ownership of all AI-generated code (Java, Angular, React, SQL) to ensure structural integrity, security compliance, and production readiness, while applying a deep functional understanding of Corporate and Investment Banking (CIB) to all projects.

Key Qualifications

Required Skills & Experience:

Systems Fundamentals: Strong foundation in systems analysis, design patterns, data analysis, and the full software development lifecycle (SDLC), including unit testing and CI/CD practices.
Backend Development: Extensive hands-on experience with Java and Spring Boot for building scalable, low-latency microservices and reactive data streaming APIs.
Frontend & Visualization: Strong, hands-on experience with Angular 19+, React, TypeScript, HTML5, and Web Sockets for building interactive, data-intensive dashboards.
Data Federation & Querying: Hands-on experience with Starburst (Trino) for querying massive, distributed datasets across federated enterprise data sources.
Databases & Data Modeling: Deep experience with relational databases (Oracle, SQL Server) and NoSQL (MongoDB), including physical/logical database design, data modeling, and performance tuning.
ETL & Data Processing: Proven experience designing high-throughput ETL pipelines and optimizing data flows for real-time reporting.
Enterprise Reporting: Experience building document generation engines using the Aspose suite (Aspose.Words, Aspose.Cells, Aspose.PDF).
MCP Tool Creation: Demonstrated ability to design and build custom Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers to securely connect LLMs and AI agents to enterprise data.
AI-Assisted Engineering: Hands-on proficiency with AI coding tools (e.g., Claude Code, Cursor, GitHub Copilot) and the ability to write structured prompts and engineer high-quality context (schemas, API specs) for AI agents.
Collaboration Tools: Strong experience with GitHub for source control and Jira for project management.

Preferred Skills & Experience:

8+ years of relevant experience
Experience designing and implementing agentic AI workflows and integrating AI agents directly into CI/CD pipelines.
A strong understanding of event-driven systems and real-time message streaming platforms like Apache Kafka or RabbitMQ.

Domain

Functional understanding of Banking — able to articulate why their work matters, not just how it is built.

What Sets This Role Apart

This is not a conventional engineering role. You are expected to operate as a force multiplier — directing AI agents across multiple workstreams, validating output for production safety, and coaching others to do the same. The measure of success is not lines of code written, but outcomes delivered, quality maintained, and the team's collective capability raised.

Sunpan is looking for a hands-on technology leader for our technology and digital transformation strategy. The Director will define how we structure, grow and continuously improve our IT function, guide the implementation of business systems, and lead our innovation, AI and automation strategy in line with the organization's priorities.

Technology is central to how Sunpan grows, and this role sets its direction. At Johnson & Johnson, we believe health is everything. Our strength in healthcare innovation empowers us to build a world where complex diseases are prevented, treated, and cured, where treatments are smarter and less invasive, and solutions are personal. Through our expertise in Innovative Medicine and MedTech, we are uniquely positioned to innovate across the full spectrum of healthcare solutions today to deliver the breakthroughs of tomorrow, and profoundly impact health for humanity. Learn more at jnj.com

As guided by Our Credo, Johnson & Johnson is responsible to our employees who work with us throughout the world. We provide an inclusive work environment where each person is considered as an individual. At Johnson & Johnson, we respect the diversity and dignity of our employees and recognize their merit.

Job Function

Finance

Treasury

Professional

New Brunswick (Any City), Palm Beach Gardens, Florida, United States of America, Raynham, Massachusetts, United States of America, Warsaw, Indiana, United States of America, West Chester, Pennsylvania, United States of America

Job Description

DePuy Synthes is currently recruiting for a Senior Director, Acquisitions & Divestitures (A&D) Finance to ideally be located in Raynham, MA.

The Corporate A&D Finance team is seeking a seasoned, strategic, and influential Senior Director to serve as the enterprise finance thought partner on portfolio shaping and capital deployment decisions across our sectors (Pharmaceuticals and Medical Technologies). This leader will set the financial point of view behind DePuy Synthes’s acquisitions, partnerships, and divestitures, determining how each transaction fits the enterprise strategy, creates sustainable long-term value, and aligns with capital allocation priorities. The Senior Director will partner with corporate and sector executives, Business Development, the A&D Community of Practice, and external advisors to establish valuation frameworks, challenge key assumptions, and deliver clear, decision-ready recommendations to the most senior leaders of the company (GOC, EC/MC, and Board of Directors).

Johnson & Johnson announced plans to separate our Orthopedics business to establish a standalone orthopedics company, operating as DePuy Synthes. The process of the planned separation is anticipated to be completed within 18 to 24 months, subject to legal requirements, including consultation with works councils and other employee representative bodies, as may be required, regulatory approvals and other customary conditions and approvals. Should you accept this position, it is anticipated that, following conclusion of the transaction, you would be an employee of DePuy Synthes and your employment would be governed by DePuy Synthes employment processes, programs, policies, and benefit plans. In that case, details of any planned changes would be provided to you by DePuy Synthes at an appropriate time and subject to any necessary consultation processes.

Responsibilities

Serve as a strategic finance advisor to enterprise and sector leaders on portfolio strategy, helping shape the pipeline of acquisitions, partnerships, and divestitures so that it reflects long-term growth objectives, capital allocation priorities, and the evolving competitive landscape. Provide an independent, objective perspective that balances opportunity with risk.
Lead and oversee objective financial and business analyses of new acquisitions, partnering relationships (i.e. options, licenses, equity investments, etc.), and divestitures, ensuring objectivity, transparency, and completeness in strategic assessments, valuations, and due diligence (highlighting both opportunities and risks) as well as transaction closing activities (purchase price allocation, deal financings, etc.). Distill complex analyses into clear insights and recommendations for senior management, the GOC, EC/MC, and the Board of Directors.
Provide senior financial leadership across the full deal lifecycle, guiding deal structuring, contract and purchase price negotiations, valuation, due diligence, EC/MC and BOD presentations, Investor Relations support and framing, EPS analyses, and capital structure impacts. Direct the work of deal teams, external advisors, and investment bankers to ensure transactions deliver the intended value.
Oversee the review of key legal documents and required regulatory filings in support of specific transactions, partnering with Legal, Tax, and Controllership to structure transactions that protect value and manage risk.
Own the vision for, and continuously evolve, the enterprise A&D valuation and decision-making framework. Design, develop, enhance, and implement processes that lead to more accurate valuation assessments, drive value creation, and mitigate risk. This includes driving compliance with EC/MC approved Acquisition and Divestiture processes/standards and ensuring that standardized information is reviewed and output templates are used during investment decision-making meetings (consistency cross-sector, cross deal type).
Drive improved acquisition and divestiture outcomes by leading post-transaction reviews that measure results against the original deal thesis, and by translating lessons learned into process improvements and guidance for management and business development partners.
Lead special enterprise projects of a financial nature as required, including, but not limited to capital allocation analytics, share repurchase programs, cost of capital, dividend proposals, J&J and affiliate valuations, capital structure, credit ratings, etc.
Build and sustain influential relationships with key members of the J&J Finance, Business Development, and A&D Community of Practice teams to foster a culture of objectivity, transparency, and constructive dialogue on financial and valuation matters. Act as a trusted advisor to senior executives and be recognized as a J&J Finance leader and thought partner in the M&A and portfolio management discipline. Demonstrate an open and flexible mindset that inspires creative and innovative solutions while maintaining a value creation discipline. This position works closely with other key M&A oriented groups including the following: Sector BD, A&D Operations, Controllership/GTAAS, Tax, Investor Relations, Legal, HR, third party advisors and investment bankers.

Qualifications

Bachelor’s Degree is required, preferably in Finance, Accounting, or other business-related discipline. If undergraduate degree is not in Finance or Accounting, then an MBA in Finance is highly recommended.
CMA, CPA, CFA and/or an MBA is preferred (or its equivalents).
A minimum of 12 years of finance, accounting or related business experience is required.
BU Finance experience (in Commercial/Supply Chain/R&D finance) at the Senior Manager or Director level is preferred.
Experience with Financial Analysis, Financial Valuation Modeling, and Investment decision-making is preferred.
Ability to understand and interrogate all financial statements and their key linkages is required.
Excellent analytical, communication and business partnership skills as well as the ability to lead and collaborate in a highly matrix environment across multiple sectors, regions, and functions.
Demonstrate the ability to challenge the status quo and provide recommendations to enhance value creation opportunities required.
Strong system skills (i.e. Excel, PowerPoint & Word) are required for this role, along with the ability to work well independently, manage complexity, and handle multiple projects simultaneously.
This position requires a highly motivated individual with strong analytical and research skills, intellectual curiosity and proven leadership capabilities.
The candidate will be principally based out of New Brunswick, NJ and limited domestic and international travel may be required. (10%).

About Us

At the Department of Opportunities and Social Development (OSD), we are a large and diverse department providing a broad portfolio of programs and services including Child and Family Wellbeing (CFW), Income Assistance (IA), Supportive Housing and Homelessness, and the Disability Support Program (DSP).

Through our services, we advocate and help vulnerable Nova Scotians be independent, self-reliant, and secure. We work collaboratively across the province with a strong, dedicated network of supports and staff to achieve desired and shared outcomes for all.

About Our Opportunity

Financial leadership in OSD has a direct connection to the programs, services and external providers that support Nova Scotians. As Director of Finance, you will lead a complex, province-wide financial operation and help ensure that leaders have the accurate information, practical advice and effective controls needed to make responsible decisions.

This is an opportunity to combine professional accounting expertise with broader leadership. You will guide financial operations, strengthen planning and risk management, support sound decision-making, and lead a sizeable team through competing priorities and organizational change. Your success will depend not only on technical knowledge, but also on your judgement, communication, relationship-building, and ability to help others deliver results.

Primary Accountabilities

In this role, you have the opportunity to lead a substantial finance function, advise senior decision-makers and improve the systems and practices that support programs and services across Nova Scotia. A few of your key responsibilities are to:

Provide strategic and operational financial advice to the Executive Director and senior leaders, translating complex financial and non-financial information into clear options, risks and recommendations.
Lead the delivery and continuous improvement of financial operations that support departmental programs, regional teams and external service providers.
Provide leadership for budgeting, forecasting, financial analysis and the management of cost pressures, helping leaders make informed choices about resources and program delivery.
Strengthen financial accountability through effective internal controls, risk management, transparent reporting and compliance with applicable accounting standards and government financial policies.
Lead, support and develop a geographically distributed finance team. Set clear direction, build management capability, encourage collaboration and create the conditions for people to take ownership of their work.
Provide clear direction and leadership to managers and staff by establishing priorities, clarifying accountabilities, delegating effectively and supporting consistent delivery across the finance function.
Build the capability and resilience of the finance team through workforce planning, coaching, performance management and succession development.
Exercise sound professional judgment and critical thinking in interpreting and applying provincial government financial policies and applicable accounting standards within complex and diverse contexts, considering both financial and non-financial information.
Build productive relationships across OSD and with central agencies, internal audit, legal partners, service providers and other stakeholders. Address difficult issues with diplomacy while maintaining professional standards and public accountability.
Lead practical improvements to financial processes, systems and service delivery. Sequence change thoughtfully so that essential operations remain stable and responsive.
Represent the department on relevant cross-government initiatives, committees and working groups, and communicate financial issues clearly to both financial and non-financial audiences.

Qualifications And Experience

You are a designated Chartered Professional Accountant (CPA) with progressively responsible experience leading financial operations and people in a complex organization. Your experience demonstrates that you can:

lead managers and professional staff in a complex work environment, including setting expectations, delegating responsibility, developing capability and addressing performance concerns.
assess workforce and organizational needs, strengthen team capacity and guide employees through operational or organizational change while maintaining service delivery.
prepare and deliver briefings or presentations for executive-level audiences, including providing credible financial advice and explaining complex issues
support budgeting, forecasting, financial analysis and the management of significant or competing financial pressures;
establish or strengthen internal controls, accountability and risk-management practices;
build effective relationships and resolve difficult issues with sound judgement, discretion and diplomacy; and
organize work, adapt to changing priorities and deliver accurate advice within tight timeframes.

You bring a practical understanding of professional accounting standards and the ability to apply financial policy in a complex operating environment. You also understand that strong financial management requires attention to program and service outcomes, not only financial results.

audit, assurance or control-review work;
public-sector, human-services, not-for-profit or other complex service-delivery finance;
financial relationships with funded organizations, service providers, grants or contribution agreements;
Public Sector Accounting Standards and government financial policy

jobs.description:
The Director, Financial Planning & Analysis (FP&A) leads enterprise budgeting, forecasting, management reporting, and decision support. This role partners with senior leadership and business units to align financial and operational realities, provide proactive insights, and drive performance. The Director manages a high-performing FP&A team and ensures disciplined governance, clear executive reporting, and continuous improvement, leveraging strong analytics and modeling.

 What we offer (and why you’ll love it here!): 

 Epic Work-Life Balance: Flexible remote work options because we value your time and well-being.  

 Growth Opportunities: Committed to fostering a culture of growth, where every team member is encouraged to pursue new skills, expand their knowledge, and advance their careers.

 Vibrant Culture: Over 1,500 team members across Canada and year over year we manage to maintain an overall above industry engagement score by using a monthly pulse survey.

 Attractive Compensation: Competitive salary, incentive program, and comprehensive benefits package.    

 What & Where: Full-Time, Permanent & Moncton, NB or Oakville, ON

 Why BioScript Solutions? 

 At BioScript, we're not just a company—we're a fast-growing company always putting patients first. Recognized as one of Canada’s Best Managed Companies, we believe in pushing boundaries, setting trends, and creating meaningful experiences that captivate and inspire. Our vibrant team is made up of innovative minds who are passionate about driving success and making an impact. Ready to be a part of this exhilarating journey?

 Your Mission: 

   Budgeting & Forecasting 

 Lead the annual budgeting process and short and long-term financial forecasting to support business strategy and advise senior leaders on financial implications of strategic choices.

 Coordinate cross-functional inputs to ensure realistic plans, aligned assumptions, and accountability for outcomes.

   Management Reporting & Insights 

 Establish and monitor financial and operational KPIs, ensuring robust analytics to assess progress, profitability, and efficiency.

 Chair senior management meetings, coordinating the preparation, consolidation, and presentation of reporting packages, including financial results, KPIs, and related commentary.

 Oversee the provision of monthly results and interpretations to business units to support achievement of departmental goals.

 Develop, implement, monitor, and continually improve management reporting to keep pace with structural changes and growth.

 Leverage analytics and modeling to interpret results and articulate clear, actionable recommendations.

 Review performance versus plan/forecast, identify significant variances, and drive corrective actions.

 Business Partnering 

 Collaborate with senior management to ensure operational and financial realities are aligned.

 Challenge business units through proactive insights and the identification of opportunities to improve growth, margin, productivity, and cash performance.

 Support key business decisions and initiatives with data-driven analysis and clear financial implications.

 Scenario & Investment Analysis 

 Direct scenario and sensitivity analyses for strategic decisions, investments, and resource allocation.

 Evaluate trade-offs and risk/return dynamics; synthesize recommendations for executive decision-making.

 Governance & Controls 

 Partner with Accounting to align on accounting policies, close calendars, and reconciliation of actuals to plans/forecasts.

 Maintain disciplined methodologies for budgeting, forecasting, KPI definitions, and variance analysis.

 Board & Executive Reporting 

 Prepare executive and board-level materials with clear insights, risks, opportunities, and recommendations.

 Craft concise narratives and visuals that translate complex financials into strategic implications for decision-makers.

 Coordinate timelines and inputs to ensure accurate, timely delivery of all board/executive reporting packages.

 Leadership Responsibilities: 

 Provides clear direction, sets measurable goals, and holds team members accountable for performance and results.

 Coaches, develops, and supports team members through regular feedback, performance reviews, and career development planning.

 Fosters a high-performing, inclusive team culture that aligns with company values and business objectives.

 What You Bring to the Table: 

 Education: 

 Bachelor’s degree in accounting, Finance or related field.

 CPA designation required.

 Experience: 

 Minimum of 10 years’ financial and team management experience.

 Skills: 

 Strong business acumen with clear understanding of industry trends, able to think strategically.

 Advanced financial modeling, forecasting, and budgeting capabilities.

 Strong analytical mindset and communication skills; adept at presenting complex financial concepts to non-financial stakeholders.

 Impeccable attention to detail.

 Extensive experience leading budgeting and forecasting for mid-to-large sized organizations.

 Strong background in management reporting, budgeting and analytics.

 Experience partnering with and influencing senior executives and divisional leaders.

 Excellent verbal and written communication skills.

 Works effectively in teams.

 Strong organizational skills with the ability to handle multiple deadlines and competing priorities.

 Results-oriented and process-driven.

 Proficiency with Microsoft Office applications.

 English proficiency is required for this position to effectively communicate with internal and external stakeholders.

 Compensation: At BioScript, your base pay is one part of your total compensation package and is determined within a range. Our pay ranges are based on the local cost of labor benchmarks for each specific role, level, and geographic location.

 We're proud to be an equal opportunity employer.  As a people-centric organization, we’re committed to fostering a welcoming culture free of discrimination, and to providing a healthy and safe work environment where all team members can thrive as individuals. Through our commitment to diversity, inclusion, belonging, and equity, we strive to provide an accessible workplace, where individuals feel valued, respected, and supported every day.

 We are committed to creating an inclusive and accessible work environment across Canada. In accordance with applicable provincial legislation, including Quebec’s Charter of the French Language, this job posting is provided in both French and English when required. For positions based in Quebec, French language proficiency is required to perform day-to-day duties.

 We encourage and accept all applications, however, only candidates selected for interviews will be contacted. Accommodations can be made available on request for candidates taking part in all aspects of the selection process. For inquiries, please email the talent acquisition team at recruitment@bioscript.ca. 

 Ready to make your mark? If you’re passionate about transforming ideas into extraordinary results and excited to join a forward-thinking team, we want to hear from you!

 ______________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________

 À titre de directeur(-trice) de la planification financière et de l’analyse, vous serez responsable des activités d’établissement de budgets, de prévision financière, de production de rapports en matière de gestion, et de soutien à la prise de décisions à l’échelle de l’entreprise. Vous travaillerez en étroite collaboration avec la haute direction et les unités fonctionnelles afin de faire concorder les réalités financières et opérationnelles, de fournir des analyses proactives et de stimuler le rendement. Vous dirigerez une équipe de la planification financière et de l’analyse hautement performante, et vous assurerez une gouvernance rigoureuse, produirez des rapports clairs à l’intention de la direction et veillerez à une amélioration continue, et ce, grâce à une forte expertise en analyse et en modélisation financières.

 Ce que nous offrons (et ce qui fera que vous aimerez travailler avec nous!) 

 Excellent équilibre travail-vie personnelle: nous offrons des modalités de travail à distance flexibles, car votre temps et votre bien-être sont importants pour nous.

 Possibilités de croissance: nous nous engageons à favoriser une culture axée sur la croissance qui permet à tous les membres de l’équipe d’acquérir de nouvelles compétences, d’approfondir leurs connaissances, et de progresser dans leur carrière.

 Culture dynamique: nous comptons plus de 1 500 membres de l’équipe dans tout le Canada, et année après année, nous parvenons à maintenir des résultats globaux supérieurs à la moyenne de l’industrie en matière d’engagement, mesurés à l’aide d’un sondage éclair mensuel.

 Rémunération attrayante: nous offrons des salaires concurrentiels, un programme d’incitation au rendement et des avantages sociaux complets.

 Détails et lieu de l’emploi: temps plein, permanent, Moncton (N.-B.) ou Oakville (Ont.)

 Pourquoi choisir BioScript Solutions? 

 BioScript n’est pas qu’une simple entreprise; elle est une entreprise en forte croissance qui accorde toujours la priorité aux patients. BioScript est reconnue comme l’une des sociétés les mieux gérées au Canada et nous croyons en l’importance de repousser les limites, d’établir des tendances et de créer des expériences significatives, captivantes et inspirantes. Notre équipe dynamique est composée de personnes innovatrices qui ont une passion pour le succès et qui souhaitent faire bouger les choses. Pourquoi ne pas vous joindre à nous dans notre aventure exaltante?

 Votre mission 

 Établissement des budgets et prévisions financières 

 Diriger le processus annuel d’établissement du budget et de prévisions financières à court et à long terme afin de soutenir la stratégie d’entreprise et de conseiller les cadres supérieurs sur les incidences financières découlant des choix stratégiques.

 Coordonner les contributions des différentes unités de façon à ce que les plans soient réalistes, les hypothèses, cohérentes et les résultats, pris en charge.

 Rapports de gestion et analyses 

 Mettre en place et surveiller les indicateurs de rendement clés financiers et opérationnels, et en produire des analyses fiables permettant d’évaluer les progrès, la rentabilité et l’efficacité.

 Présider les réunions de la haute direction, et effectuer la préparation, la synthèse et la présentation des rapports, notamment sur les résultats financiers, les indicateurs de rendement clés et les commentaires connexes.

 Superviser la communication des résultats mensuels et de leur analyse aux unités fonctionnelles afin de contribuer à la réalisation des objectifs fonctionnels.

 Produire, mettre en œuvre, suivre et améliorer en permanence les rapports de gestion de sorte à s’adapter aux changements structurels et à la croissance.

 Exploiter les outils d’analyse et de modélisation pour interpréter les résultats et pour formuler des recommandations claires et réalisables.

 Analyser le rendement par rapport au plan ou aux prévisions, indiquer les écarts importants et mettre en œuvre des mesures correctives.

 Établissement de partenariat d’affaires 

 Collaborer avec la haute direction afin de garantir la cohérence entre les réalités opérationnelles et financières.

 Motiver les unités fonctionnelles à l’aide de rétroaction proactive et d’occasions d’amélioration de la croissance, des marges, de la productivité et du rendement financier.

 Appuyer les principales décisions et initiatives stratégiques de l’entreprise à l’aide d’analyses fondées sur des données et d’incidences financières.

 Analyse des investissements et scénarios 

 Réaliser des analyses de scénarios et de sensibilité pour orienter les décisions stratégiques, les investissements et l’affectation des ressources.

 Évaluer les options et le risque par rapport au rendement; formuler des recommandations pour contribuer à la prise de décision.

 Gouvernance et contrôle 

 Collaborer avec l’équipe de comptabilité pour assurer l’alignement sur les politiques en matière de comptabilité, les calendriers de clôture et le rapprochement des chiffres réels par rapport aux plans/prévisions.

 Appliquer des méthodologies rigoureuses en matière d’établissement de budgets, de prévisions, de définition des indicateurs de rendement clés et d’analyse des écarts.

 Rapports à l’intention du conseil d’administration et de la direction 

 Préparer des documents destinés à la direction et au conseil d’administration; y présenter des analyses claires, les risques, les occasions et des recommandations.

 Élaborer des textes et des supports visuels concis permettant de traduire des données financières complexes en incidences stratégiques visant à orienter la prise de décision.

 Coordonner les calendriers et les contributions afin de garantir la remise exacte et opportune de tous les rapports destinés au conseil d’administration et à la direction.

 Responsabilités de leadership 

 Offrir une orientation claire, établir des objectifs mesurables et tenir les membres de l’équipe responsables de leur rendement et de leurs résultats.

 Encadrer, former, et soutenir les membres de l’équipe par l’entremise de rétroaction régulière, d’évaluations du rendement, et de planification du perfectionnement professionnel.

 Favoriser une culture d’équipe inclusive axée sur le rendement qui correspond aux valeurs et aux objectifs de l’entreprise.

 L’expérience que vous apportez 

 Formation 

 Avoir un baccalauréat en comptabilité, en finance ou dans un domaine connexe.

 Être titulaire du titre professionnel en comptabilité (CPA) est requis.

 Expérience 

 Au moins 10 ans d’expérience dans la gestion financière et d’équipe.

 Aptitudes 

 Avoir un excellent sens des affaires et une excellente compréhension des tendances du secteur; faire preuve d’un esprit stratégique.

 Avoir des connaissances approfondies sur la modélisation financière, les prévisions et l’établissement de budgets.

 Faire preuve d’un esprit d’analyse affûté et d’excellentes compétences en communication; être en mesure de présenter des concepts financiers complexes à des parties prenantes non spécialisées en finance.

 Avoir un souci minutieux du détail.

 Posséder une vaste expérience dans la gestion de budgets et des prévisions pour des organisations de moyenne à grande envergure.

 Avoir une solide expérience dans la production de rapports de gestion, dans l’établissement de budgets et dans l’analyse.

 Avoir collaboré avec des cadres supérieurs et des gestionnaires de services, et avoir exercé une certaine influence sur eux.

 Avoir d’excellentes compétences en communication, écrite et orale.

 Être capable de travailler efficacement en équipe.

 Posséder d’excellentes compétences organisationnelles et être capable de gérer de nombreuses échéances ainsi que des priorités concurrentes.

 Être axé(e) sur les résultats et les processus.

 Avoir une excellente maîtrise des applications de Microsoft Office.

 Avoir une bonne maîtrise de l’anglais est nécessaire dans le cadre de ce poste afin de communiquer efficacement avec les parties prenantes internes et externes.

 Rémunération: Chez BioScript, votre salaire de base ne constitue qu’une partie de votre rémunération totale et est déterminé en fonction d’une échelle. Nos échelles salariales sont calculées selon les valeurs de référence locales en matière de coût de la main-d’œuvre propre à chaque poste, chaque niveau de poste et chaque emplacement géographique.

 C’est une fierté d’être un employeur favorable à l’égalité professionnelle. En tant qu’entreprise centrée sur les personnes, BioScript croit foncièrement à l’importance de favoriser une culture accueillante exempte de discrimination, et de fournir un lieu de travail sain et sûr où l’ensemble des membres de l’équipe peuvent exprimer leur individualité. Grâce à notre engagement à la diversité, l’inclusion, l’appartenance et l’équité, nous sommes déterminés à fournir un milieu de travail où chaque personne se sent appréciée, respectée et soutenue chaque jour.

 Nous nous engageons à créer un environnement inclusif et respectueux dans l’ensemble du Canada. Conformément aux lois provinciales applicables, y compris la Charte de la langue française du Québec, l’affichage du présent poste est publié en français et en anglais, le cas échéant. Pour les postes au Québec, la maîtrise du français est nécessaire afin d’effectuer les tâches quotidiennes.

 Nous encourageons et acceptons toutes les candidatures; toutefois, nous communiquerons seulement avec les personnes dont la candidature a été retenue pour une entrevue. Des mesures d’adaptation sont offertes sur demande aux candidates et candidats qui participent à tous les aspects du processus de sélection. Si vous avez des demandes, veuillez envoyer un courriel à l’équipe d’attraction de talents à recruitment@bioscript.ca.

 Laissez votre marque! Si transformer vos idées en résultats extraordinaires vous passionne, et si vous joindre à une équipe tournée vers l’avenir vous réjouit, nous aimerions recevoir votre candidature!

jobs.description:
**Job Description**
-------------------

**About Agilent**

  

Agilent is a global leader in laboratory and clinical technologies, we are passionate about bringing great science to life. We help scientists, researchers, and clinicians address some of the world’s most important challenges across life science research, pharmaceuticals, diagnostics, food, environmental testing, and related markets.  



  

Leveraging more than 50 years of expertise, we develop advanced instruments, software, consumables, and services that enable customers to generate reliable scientific results and improve scientific, economic, and operational outcomes. Our global organization combines deep technical expertise with a commitment to quality, innovation, and customer impact. We work collaboratively with our customers on their journey to make a real difference in human lives. Our culture is founded on trust, respect, and uncompromising integrity, and we pride ourselves on being a dynamic and inclusive workplace that empowers employees and fosters innovation.

 **The Role**

  

Agilent is seeking a highly experienced product strategy leader to help define how laboratories will evolve over the next five to ten years and translate that vision into actionable strategies for our businesses and product organizations.


This senior individual contributor works across the enterprise at the intersection of customer insight, science, technology, and business strategy. As a recognized internal expert, you will lead high\-impact, long\-range initiatives, advise senior leadership, and independently solve complex challenges spanning multiple functions with limited support. You will connect external signals and customer needs with business\-group priorities, product roadmaps, and execution.

 **Key Responsibilities**

  

* Assess how AI, automation, robotics, connected instruments, digital workflows, data platforms, and autonomous experimentation could change laboratory work. Identify practical applications in scientific productivity, instrument operation, workflow optimization, decision support, and service; distinguish durable shifts from short\-term technology cycles.
* Evaluate new products, solutions, partnerships, and business models. Develop strategic and financial cases that assess customer value, differentiation, and feasibility; recommend when to build, partner, invest, acquire, or apply existing capabilities differently.
* Develop and continually refine Agilent’s view of Autonomous Labs. Synthesize scientific, technological, economic, and operational trends, including changing workforce models and productivity pressures, into scenarios and implications for our portfolio, business models, and investments.
* Engage scientists, laboratory leaders, executives, key opinion leaders, and strategic customers to understand current operations and emerging needs. Identify workflow bottlenecks, fragmented data, automation gaps, usability challenges, and inefficiencies that span individual instruments or product categories.

jobs.title: Chief Financial Officer
jobs.description:
Ontario Plants Propagation (OP) is a leading North American plant propagation company focused on producing high-quality young vegetable and soft fruit plants for commercial greenhouse growers. As a critical supplier to the controlled environment agriculture sector, OP combines horticultural expertise, advanced growing capabilities, and a commitment to innovation to support a more resilient, productive, and sustainable food system.

Following the development of its state-of-the-art Glencoe greenhouse facility and significant capital investment, OP is entering an exciting next phase of growth and transformation. The organization is focused on optimizing operations, enhancing profitability, expanding capabilities, and strengthening its position in a market benefiting from growing demand for greenhouse-grown food production.

The Mandate

Reporting directly to the CEO and working closely with ownership, the Chief Financial Officer (CFO) will play a central role in helping build a high-performing, scalable, and profitable organization. This is not a traditional finance leadership position focused solely on stewardship and reporting. It is an opportunity to become a true business partner and strategic leader, influencing critical decisions that will shape the future of the company.

The successful candidate will join at a pivotal point in OP's evolution. With substantial investments already made in infrastructure and growth, the organization is seeking a finance leader who can help unlock value by improving profitability, strengthening cash generation, enhancing decision-making capabilities, and building the financial and operational foundations needed to support long-term success.

For an executive who enjoys rolling up their sleeves, building capabilities, and creating lasting impact, this role offers a rare opportunity to influence strategy, strengthen culture, enhance performance, and leave a visible mark on a growing business.

Leadership and Stewardship

The company is seeking a CFO who leads with maturity and earns trust through action. This is not a role for someone who relies on title or tenure to get things done. More than just a technical financial leader, the successful candidate will be a thoughtful and credible executive who fosters trust, accountability, and collaboration across the organization and partners effectively with external stakeholders.
Operationally curious and highly intelligent, with a low-ego leadership style
Comfortable navigating ambiguity and complexity
A builder of high-performing teams and organizational culture
Results-oriented and accountable
An enabler of exceptional data-driven decision making
Collaborative, trusted, and relationship-focused
Energized by operational challenges and continuous improvement
An effective and transparent communicator

Ideal Background

The successful candidate will be a strategic and operational finance executive who enjoys complexity and thrives in a growth-oriented environment. They will bring both financial expertise and a passion for helping businesses improve performance and create value.
CPA designation required.
Proven track record of success as a CFO or senior finance executive within a complex operating environment with a minimum of 15 years, including optimizing and scaling organizations
Accomplished as a strategic business partner, advisor to the CEO and the senior leadership team
Hands-on and strategic capabilities in financial planning, forecasting, cash flow management, and business intelligence, driving operational improvements through financial insights and performance management.
Experience operating in asset-intensive, capital-intensive, or leveraged environments.
Track record of building high-performing teams and influencing leaders across an organization.
Experience in manufacturing, food production, agriculture, horticulture, or other operationally intensive industries is strongly preferred.
Experience working with sophisticated lenders, private equity sponsors, family offices, or institutional investors is also an asset.

Location

The CFO will maintain a meaningful on-site presence and build strong relationships across both operating locations. Regular travel between St. Thomas and Glencoe is expected as part of developing a deep understanding of the business and supporting operational excellence.

Why This Role

This is an opportunity to join an organization at a defining moment in its journey. Significant investments have been made, the platform for growth is in place, and the leadership team is focused on realizing the full potential of the business. For a finance executive who wants to influence strategy, strengthen operations, develop teams, and help create long-term enterprise value, this role offers both challenge and impact.

If you are energized by building, improving, and leading from the front, we welcome the opportunity to connect.

jobs.title: Senior Director, Product Management – Developer & AI
jobs.description:
1Password is growing. We’ve surpassed $500M in ARR and we’re continuing to accelerate, earning a spot on the Forbes Cloud 100 for four years in a row and teaming up with iconic partners like Oracle Red Bull Racing. 

 About 1Password 
 At 1Password, we’re building the foundation for a safe, productive digital future. Our mission is to unleash employee productivity without compromising security by ensuring every identity is authentic, every application sign-in is secure, and every device is trusted. We innovated the market-leading enterprise password manager and pioneered Unified Access Management, a new cybersecurity category built for the way people and AI agents work today. As one of the most loved brands in cybersecurity, we take a human-centric approach in everything from product strategy to user experience. Over 180,000 businesses, from Fortune 100 leaders to the world’s most innovative AI companies, trust 1Password to help their teams securely adopt the SaaS and AI tools they need to do their best work. 

 If you're excited about the opportunity to contribute to the digital safety of millions, to work alongside a team of curious, driven individuals, and to solve hard problems in a fast-paced, dynamic environment, then we want to hear from you. Come join us and help shape a safer, simpler digital future. 

 The Senior Director of Product Management for Developer & AI will lead product strategy and execution across one of 1Password’s most future-defining portfolios. This role spans our Developer Experience (DevX) products, Security for AI, and AI for Security initiatives, as well as the product surface area that supports standards adoption and developer engagement.

 Reporting to the VP of Developer & AI Engineering, this leader will be responsible for defining the product vision, roadmap, and outcomes for how developers and AI-powered systems securely interact with 1Password—from local development and secrets management, to programmatic agent access, to secure runtime environments.

 This role requires deep partnership with engineering, design, marketing, partnerships, and GTM teams, and leadership of a senior group of product managers operating across highly technical, platform-oriented problem spaces.

 How we’re using AI today 
 Our Engineering, Product, and Design teams are thoughtfully integrating AI across the full software and product development lifecycle to move faster without sacrificing quality or security. In practice, that looks like engineers using AI-assisted coding tools to accelerate reviews and catch bugs earlier, product managers synthesizing user research at scale, and designers rapidly prototyping and iterating with AI-generated mockups. We approach AI the same way we approach security: with clear principles, human accountability at every consequential decision point, and rigorous evaluation before anything ships to customers.

 This is a remote opportunity within Canada and the US.

 What we're looking for: 
 10+ years in product management, including 5+ years leading senior PMs or product portfolios.

 Experience owning platform, developer-facing, or infrastructure products strongly preferred.

 Track record of shipping impactful developer tools, platforms, or security products used by large or fast-growing audiences.

 Strong familiarity with the modern AI landscape, including LLMs, orchestration frameworks, and agentic workflows.

 Ability to reason about AI capabilities and limitations through a product and customer lens.

 Solid understanding of modern security concepts such as identity, secrets management, access control, and secure system design.

 Comfort operating in highly technical problem spaces alongside senior engineers.

 Ability to connect long-term product vision with near-term priorities and measurable outcomes.

 Experience balancing discovery, delivery, and platform investment.

 Demonstrated success partnering deeply with engineering, design, marketing, and external stakeholders.

 Strong communication skills with the ability to influence without authority.

 What you can expect: 
 Set and evolve the product vision, strategy, and roadmap for 1Password’s Developer Experience, AI security, and AI-powered security initiatives.

 Ensure clear articulation of customer problems, value propositions, and success metrics across the portfolio.

 Lead product definition for secure, agentic workflows including identity, delegation, secrets delivery, and access control for both developers and AI agents.

 Translate emerging AI capabilities and risks into durable, differentiated product primitives.

 Work in lockstep with the VP of Developer & AI Engineering to align product strategy with technical vision, architecture, and delivery.

 Enable strong product-engineering collaboration that balances innovation, speed, and long-term platform integrity.

 Partner with Marketing, Partnerships, Security, and GTM teams to ensure successful launches, platform integrations, and ecosystem adoption.

 Represent product strategy internally and externally, ensuring consistency across messaging, documentation, and developer engagement.

 Provide product leadership and input into standards participation and developer advocacy efforts, ensuring standards work is grounded in real customer needs and product direction.

 Help position 1Password as a trusted product leader in the AI and security ecosystem.

 Recruit, mentor, and lead senior product managers working across complex, technical domains.

 Establish product operating rhythms, decision-making frameworks, and outcome-oriented metrics.

 USA-based roles only: The annual base salary for this role is between $267,000 USD and $401,000 USD, plus immediate participation in 1Password's benefits program (health, dental, 401k and many others), utilization of our generous paid time off, an equity grant and, where applicable, participation in our incentive programs.

 Canada-based roles only: The annual base salary for this role is between $248,000 CAD and $372,000 CAD, plus immediate participation in 1Password’s generous benefits program (health, dental, RRSP and many others), utilization of our generous paid time off, an equity grant and, where applicable, participation in our incentive programs.

At 1Password, we approach each individual's compensation with a promise of fair market value and internal equity commensurate with experience and specific skill set.

 This posting is for an existing vacancy. 

 Our culture 
At 1Password, we prioritize collaboration, clear and transparent communication, receptiveness to feedback, and alignment with our core values: keep it simple, lead with honesty, and put people first. 

You’ll be part of a team that challenges the status quo, and is excited to experiment and iterate in search of the best solution. That said, 1Password is not for everyone. Our work is demanding, we strive for excellence, and the pace is fast. We need people who are keen to take on challenging problems, who seek feedback to grow, and who are driven to make an impact. If you're looking for a place where you can settle into a comfortable routine, this might not be the right fit for you. We’re looking for individuals who are proven experts in their fields, as well as those who are highly adaptable, can thrive in ambiguity and through change, are curious, and above all deliver results. 

 How we work with AI 
We are committed to leveraging cutting-edge technology—including AI—to achieve our mission. We also understand that thinking critically about AI in its current forms will help us create better solutions for our customers and ourselves with its future forms, which will help us continue to close the gap between security and privacy and achieve our mission. We want team members at all levels to take the approach of actively learning AI best practices, identifying opportunities to apply AI in meaningful ways, and driving innovative solutions in their daily work. Embracing the future of AI isn't just encouraged—it's an essential part of how we will be successful at 1Password.

 This approach extends to our hiring process—candidates are welcome to use AI tools responsibly and thoughtfully during the application process. To us, this means we do ask that you join live interviews without using AI tools so we can get to know how you communicate, solve problems, and collaborate with others.

 Our approach to remote work 
We believe in the power of remote work, but recognize that in-person connection is important to help us achieve our mission. While we are a remote-first company, travel for in-person engagement is a part of almost all roles, and we require our employees to be ready and willing to take part. Frequency will depend on role and responsibilities, and may include, but is not limited to: annual department-wide offsites, team meetings, and customer/industry events.

 What we offer 
We believe in working hard, and rewarding that hard work through our benefits. While not an exhaustive list, here is a glance at what we currently offer: 

 Health and wellbeing 
👶 Maternity and parental leave top-up programs
🩺 Competitive health benefits
🏝 Generous PTO policy 

 Growth and future 
📈 RSU program for most employees
💸 Retirement matching program
🔑 Free 1Password account

 Community 
🤝 Paid volunteer days 
🏆 Peer-to-peer recognition through Bonusly
🌎 Remote-first work environment
 *Some roles in our GTM team are currently being hired for in-person hybrid work in Toronto and Austin. These roles will specify on the posting. 

 You belong here. 

 1Password is proud to be an equal opportunity employer. We are committed to fostering an inclusive, diverse and equitable workplace that is built on trust, support and respect. We welcome all individuals and do not discriminate on the basis of gender identity and expression, race, ethnicity, disability, sexual orientation, colour, religion, creed, gender, national origin, age, marital status, pregnancy, sex, citizenship, education, languages spoken or veteran status. Be yourself, find your people and share the things you love. 

 Accommodation is available upon request at any point during our recruitment process. If you require an accommodation, please speak to your talent acquisition partner or email us at nextbit@agilebits.com and we’ll work to meet your needs. 

 Remote work is a part of our DNA. Given that our company was founded remotely in 2005, we can safely say we're experts at building remote culture. That said, remote work at 1Password does mean working from your home country. If you've got questions or concerns about this, your talent partner would be happy to address them with you. 

 Successful applicants will be required to complete a background check that may consist of prior employment verification, reference checks, education confirmation, criminal background, publicly available social media, credit history, or other information, as permitted by local law. 

 1Password uses artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) technologies, including natural language processing and predictive analytics, to assist in the initial screening of employment applications and improve our recruitment process. See here for the latest third party bias audit information. If you prefer not to have your application assessed using AI/ML features, you may opt out by completing this form. For additional information see our Candidate Privacy Notice.

Lead technical direction and delivery across client engagements, overseeing architecture, quality, scope, timelines, budgets, and resolution of complex platform and delivery issues.

Lead technical discovery, requirements definition, solution scoping, client presentations, and strategic recommendations while partnering with director-level and executive client stakeholders.

Required:

8+ years of progressive experience in marketing technology, software development, or digital platform delivery, including 3+ years leading technical teams, with responsibility for delivery, architecture, or people management.
Hands-on experience with enterprise CMS platforms including Contentful and AEM, with demonstrated delivery of production digital experiences and platform integrations.
Experience leading and mentoring technical teams across onshore and offshore delivery models, including workload distribution, capacity planning, performance management, and career development.
Experience designing and implementing enterprise digital measurement solutions using tag management, event-based tracking, data layers, consent-compliant analytics, and platforms such as Google Analytics 4 or Adobe Analytics.
Experience with enterprise DAM, personalization, and experimentation platforms, including metadata governance, workflow configuration, audience targeting, A/B or multivariate testing, and integrations with CMS, CDP, CRM, or marketing technology platforms.
Experience delivering client-facing technology programs in an agency or consulting environment using Agile/Scrum or comparable SDLC methodologies, including requirements, scope, technical recommendations, and executive-level communication.

Desired:

Comfort and enthusiasm for using AI as a regular part of how work gets done.
Experience supporting technology programs within pharmaceutical, biotech, healthcare, or life sciences agency environments.
Experience integrating AI-powered capabilities such as semantic search, content recommendations, generative personalization, or AI-enabled content workflows into production digital experience platforms.
Experience with AI-assisted development tools such as GitHub Copilot, Claude Code, or equivalent, with examples of improved engineering workflows or delivery efficiency.
Experience advising clients on platform-native AI capabilities across Contentful, AEM, Optimizely, or related MarTech platforms.
Experience contributing to business development through SOW development, technical proposal reviews, capability presentations, or client growth initiatives.

jobs.title: Digital Marketing Director (Remote, Hamilton)
jobs.description:
Blacksmith Agency

Marketing
Full time
Remote (USA, Canada or South Africa)

About The Role

Blacksmith Agency runs PPC and SEO for clients across multifamily, B2B and technical verticals. As Digital Marketing Director you lead that department. The PPC strategist and the SEO strategist report to you and they are the specialists in their channels. Right now nobody owns this function, which is the whole reason this seat is open.

This is a management seat, not a senior individual contributor one.
You will not be building campaigns, and on technical SEO your strategist will know more than you do. That is the arrangement, not a gap. You carry channel strategy and where budget goes as accounts scale. The strategists carry the execution of it, and you carry whether the department delivers.

What You Own

The PPC strategist and the SEO strategist: their quality bar, their development, their reviews, and the call when someone is not going to get there.
The standard the work is held to. What a good audit looks like, what gets checked before work leaves the agency, how an account is reported. You write it and you hold two specialists to it.
Client results across the whole function, including whether our reporting is honest. Nobody here is auditing attribution and GA4 accuracy today.
The escalation when an account is at risk. You diagnose it, you direct the strategist who fixes it, and you are on the call with the client.
Channel strategy and where budget goes as accounts scale.
What we tell sales we can credibly deliver, before it gets sold.
The hiring plan for the department, and first-round interviews for your own team, within about a quarter.

What You Need

Strategists or specialists who have reported to you, where their reviews, their development and the decision when someone was not working out were yours. Managing accounts is not this.
7+ years across paid media and SEO. Owning one channel while sitting beside the other does not count here.
Enough depth in Google Ads, GA4, Search Console, Meta and Microsoft Ads to tell good work from work that merely looks good. That is a lower bar than doing it and a higher bar than reading a report.
One account you turned around that you can talk through: the metric, the figure before, the figure after, and why the change worked. Whose hands were on the keyboard matters far less than whether the diagnosis was yours.
Comfortable being the client-facing owner when an account is underperforming. That call comes to you, not to the strategist.
Agency experience carrying many accounts at once.

Please do not apply if

Nobody has ever reported to you, or you have never owned someone's review or had to performance-manage anyone.
You have only ever run one channel.
All of your experience is in-house on a single brand.
What you actually want is to keep building campaigns yourself. That is not a lesser ambition, it is a different job, and this is not it.

None of these are preferences we bend on. They are how we screen, so applying anyway costs you an hour and gets you a no.

Process

Three conversations, then a decision. A thirty minute screen with our recruiter, a first round with the founder this seat reports to, and a final. No take-home project and no panel interview.

How To Apply

Four fields at the link, then a short 6 minute Predictive Index assessment. Use the same email throughout. No cover letter.

jobs.description:
Job Description

On behalf of our public-sector client, Affinity is seeking a Chief Courts Information Officer to be accountable for the strategic leadership, governance, and delivery of information management (IM), information technology (IT), and digital services for the Courts. The CCIO ensures that court information systems, digital services, and technology investments support judicial independence, court administration, access to justice, operational efficiency, privacy, and security.

Responsibilities

Develop and implement information management strategies and polices to ensure the secure and efficient handling of Court information.
Project management, change management and strategic planning processes for the effective delivery and management of both short and long-term information technology goals set by the judiciary.
Represent the interests of the judiciary recognizing judicial independence in their day-today operations of and/or projects involving implementing and/or updating software, databases and digital tools used by the judiciary or involving judicial data and court information.
Must operate with full confidence of the Chief Justices and the Chief Judge, be discreet as required and understand the highly confidential and sensitive nature of the work that they perform.
The Chief Court Information Officer (“CCIO”) must have the ability to work cooperatively and harmoniously with all members of the judiciary and both senior and front-line court administration staff, as we as internal and external stakeholders.
Lead the modernization of court information systems, including case management, e-filing, digital evidence, and courtroom technology.

Qualifications

Education and/or training involving computer science, information technology, cyber security or related field.
Significant work experience, preferably 5 years or more, in information technology and information governance, with a focus on cybersecurity and records retention.
Strong understanding of legal and regulatory requirements related to information management, cybersecurity, and records retention.
Excellent communication and interpersonal skills, with the ability to work effectively with stakeholders at all levels of the organization.
Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with the ability to develop and implement effective information management strategies for an increasingly digital legal work environment.
Extensive experience conducting IT and information security research and providing advice and opinions, preferably at a senior executive level.
Demonstrated ability to prepare written opinions, memoranda and reports.
The incumbent must have a superior understanding of the principles of judicial independence and possess strong political acumen and experience in the application of discretion and diplomacy to ensure positive outcomes and confidence in the administration of justice.
Well-developed planning and organizational skills in order to accomplish the position’s responsibilities and meet target dates and set priorities.
Experience using MS Office, including Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Visio and Outlook and online legal research databases which may be used by the judiciary. Familiarity with JUDICLOUD (federally appointed judges email network) and/or PowerBI is considered an asset.
Stakeholder engagement - Build effective relationships with the judiciary, court administrators, justice partners, central government IT organizations, and external stakeholders.
Represent the Courts on inter jurisdictional, justice sector, and government technology forums, as required.
Communicate complex technical concepts clearly to non-technical audiences.
On-site attendance is a mandatory requirement for this role.
Must be able to provide a satisfactory criminal record check and security clearance.
The Resource will be required to execute a Non-Disclosure Agreement (NDA) and maintain strict confidentiality with respect to all information obtained or accessed in the course of performing the Services.
Relevant certifications such as the Certified Information Systems Security Professional (CISSP)
A law degree from an accredited university or college recognized in Manitoba.

Affinity Earn

Know someone who’s great for this, or any of our open roles? Earn up to $4,000/year for each successful referral through Affinity Earn. You can also earn up to $50,000 for helping us find new clients. Learn about our referral program at https://affinity-group.ca/earn/ or browse our jobs & follow us at https://www.linkedin.com/company/affinity-staffing/jobs/

Electronic Arts creates next-level entertainment experiences that inspire players and fans around the world. Here, everyone is part of the story. Part of a community that connects across the globe. A place where creativity thrives, new perspectives are invited, and ideas matter. A team where everyone makes play happen.
