Who We Are

Gildan is a leading manufacturer of everyday basic apparel, with a strong portfolio of brands, including Gildan®, Hanes®, Comfort Colors®, American Apparel®, ALLPRO™, GOLDTOE®, Peds®, Bali®, Playtex®, Maidenform®, Bonds®, as well as Champion® which is under an exclusive licensing agreement for the printwear channel in the U.S. and Canada.

Gildan owns and operates vertically integrated, large-scale manufacturing facilities which are primarily located in Central America, the Caribbean, North America, and Asia. Gildan operates with a strong commitment to industry-leading labour, environmental and governance practices throughout its supply chain in accordance with its comprehensive ESG program embedded in Gildan's long-term business strategy. Together with our global team of dedicated employees, Gildan is united in its vision of Making Apparel Better®. Discover the full scale of Gildan and prepare to be surprised at gildancorp.com .

The opportunity

Reporting to the Principal Accounting Officer, the Director Consolidation & Financial Operations is a strategic leader responsible for the monthly close and consolidation process, as well as the corporate finance & accounting processes for operations, supply chain and cost of sales reporting. The Director Consolidation & Financial Operations is responsible for providing Corporate guidance to the divisional finance teams, coordinating/supporting the external audit process, leading new financial reporting system implementations and upgrades, and managing key vendor relationships.

Lead the monthly financial close and consolidation process.
Oversee, direct, develop and organize the work of the corporate financial operations team
Direct the corporate finance & accounting processes for operations, supply chain and costs of sales
Review and analyse internal monthly results, and consolidation level adjustments.
Review the monthly cost of sales reconciliations and inventory costing deferral.

Support the various business unit finance teams for the month-end close, accounting procedures, and reporting requirements.
Support the tax department including preparation of annual documents for tax returns and transfer price studies, prepare monthly debt covenants, computation of monthly transfer price, and ensure compliance with the tax structure.
Lead finance related projects to improve processes, leverage financial systems and support financial operations projects. Coordinate and implement the integration of the financial systems and accounting procedures and controls during acquisitions, and operational and tax reorganizations.
Support the treasury department in movement of funds.
Coordinate and support the external audit process.

Corporate oversight of standard cost process, inventory revaluation process and cost estimates.

Review of Executive level reporting packages

The Requirements

University degree in Finance, Accounting, or a related field.

Experience in a manufacturing and publicly reported company with a multi-unit geographically dispersed structure. Background in financial information systems.

jobs.title: Senior Director, Brand & Cultural Strategy
jobs.description:
Proof Strategies is an independent, Canadian‑owned strategic communications agency that charts its own path. Built on a simple philosophy – that you can do great work with great people and be a great place to work – Proof has grown into an award‑winning agency where curiosity, integrity, and collaboration are deeply valued. Today, we are proud to be one of Canada’s leading communications agencies, partnering with some of the world’s most respected brands and trusted organizations.



Guided by this foundation and a belief in the power of strong human relationships, we are on a mission to help our clients capture attention, earn trust, and move people to action. To support us on this journey, we’re hiring a Senior Director, Brand Strategy, who’s excited to build with us and help shape the agency’s next chapter.


### **The opportunity**



Proof is seeking a Senior Director, Brand Strategy to lead strategic thinking across the agency, elevate the quality and effectiveness of our client work, and help define the next generation of communications planning.



This role combines audience insight, cultural strategy, trend identification, communications planning, and creative inspiration. You will uncover emerging signals, identify shifts in audience behaviour and culture, and translate those insights into powerful communications strategies, earned\-first ideas, brand platforms, campaigns, and stakeholder engagement programs that connect to clear client objectives and create meaningful impact.



You will work closely with client teams, creatives, integrated planners, and research partners to ensure our work is rooted in insight and connected to what matters most to people. You will help teams turn strategic thinking into clear direction, stronger ideas and excellent client initiatives from opportunity and brief through development, execution and evaluation.



Beyond client work, you will help build and grow the agency’s strategic planning capability by evolving our methodologies, integrating AI and new technologies into our process, mentoring talent, and supporting business development efforts and identifying opportunities to strengthen client relationships and agency growth.



Our strategists are active partners to our clients, not behind\-the\-scenes strategists. This role requires someone who can lead and present strategic thinking with confidence, build trusted client relationships, and stay close to the work from insight through execution. You’ll be expected to bring strategic perspective into client conversations, shape the work alongside creative and account teams, and help ensure strategy translates into ideas and outcomes that deliver for our clients.


### **Key responsibilities**


#### **Audience, Cultural \& Market Intelligence**


* Lead primary and secondary research to uncover audience insights, behaviours, motivations, barriers, and opportunities.
* Identify emerging cultural shifts, market signals, risks, and opportunities before competitors.
* Monitor social, economic, technological, media, and consumer trends to inform client strategies and agency thinking.
* Apply AI\-enabled research, intelligence, listening, and forecasting tools to accelerate insight generation and strategic planning.
* Transform complex research findings into compelling narratives and actionable recommendations that inform decisions, shape strategy and identify opportunities for client impact.

#### **Strategic Planning**


* Write insightful and inspiring creative briefs that spark breakthrough ideas.
* Develop strategies that connect business objectives, brand, audience insight, culture, and communications.
* Define clear measures of success and guide teams on performance evaluation and learning.
* Partner with creative, digital, content, and communications teams to develop earned\-first ideas capable of competing with both communications and advertising agencies.
* Lead strategic thinking throughout the development of major client initiatives, ensuring insight, strategy, creative ideas and execution remain connected to the client’s objectives.
* Raise the strategic quality and effectiveness of client work by challenging and strengthening ideas, recommendations and approaches.
* Ensure creative territories and execution remain aligned with audience insight, strategic objectives, and brand positioning.
* Bring cultural relevance and audience understanding into every stage of campaign development.
* Define what success looks like at the outset of an initiative and use insights, data and results to evaluate impact and strengthen future work.
* Translate strategic thinking into clear direction that enables client and agency teams to make strong decisions and move work forward.

#### **Agency Strategy Leadership**


* Define and evolve Proof’s strategic planning offering and point of view.
* Build tools, frameworks, processes, and best practices that strengthen strategic thinking across the agency.
* Champion the adoption of audience\-first and insight\-led planning methodologies.
* Establish Proof as a recognized leader in communications strategy, audience intelligence, and cultural insight.
* Contribute thought leadership, speaking opportunities, articles, and agency marketing initiatives.

#### **Growth \& Business Development**


* Provide strategic leadership in new business opportunities and agency growth.
* Lead strategic discovery, audits, workshops, and planning sessions with prospective clients.
* Contribute to pitch strategy, insight development, positioning, and presentation storytelling.
* Identify and develop new strategic products, services, and opportunities that create value for clients and support agency growth.

#### **Team Development \& Collaboration**


* Mentor teams across the agency, including client leads, and emerging talent.
* Foster a culture of curiosity, learning, experimentation, and innovation.
* Collaborate across practices and disciplines to elevate strategic thinking

jobs.title: Senior Director Finance
jobs.description:
Senior Director, Finance – The Mustard Seed

This executive search is conducted by Nelson/Kraft & Associates on behalf of The Mustard Seed

EXECUTIVE SUMMARY

The Mustard Seed is searching for a seasoned and collaborative financial leader with initiative and drive to join their team as Senior Director, Finance.
The Senior Director, Finance is the CFO’s principal operational finance leader and trusted second-in-command. The role provides enterprise leadership across accounting, financial reporting, grants, budgeting and forecasting, treasury, audit, internal controls, finance systems, and process improvement. The successful candidate combines deep Controller-level technical expertise with strong people leadership, sound judgment, and the ability to translate financial complexity into practical decisions that support The Mustard Seed’s mission and long-term sustainability.
If you are an experienced CPA and team leader who comes from a mid to large sized organization with similarly complex moving parts, we would love to hear from you!

WHO WE ARE

The Mustard Seed is a Christian humanitarian organization whose vision is to build community, grow hope, and support change. Intentionally following Jesus Christ and partnering with the community, The Mustard Seed combats the root causes of poverty in Alberta, British Columbia, and Saskatchewan and works to create positive, lasting change in the lives of those we serve. The Mustard Seed provides basic services (food, clothing, housing, and support services), education, and employment to those living in poverty in the locations we serve.

OUR HISTORY

Pat Nixon founded The Mustard Seed in 1984 with a single street ministry location in central Calgary. Today, the organization operates in multiple cities – Calgary, Edmonton, Red Deer, Medicine Hat, and Grande Prairie in Alberta, Kamloops in British Columbia, and Saskatoon in Saskatchewan. All locations offer a different range of programs and services to serve our most vulnerable community members.

Programs & Services Include:

Basic Needs – emergency shelter, meals, clothing and hygiene items
Health and Wellness
Housing
Employment
Spiritual Care
Community Engagement
Community Impact Centres

IDEAL CANDIDATE PROFILE

The ideal candidate is a senior CPA finance leader with deep Controller-level technical expertise and a successful record of leading finance functions in a complex, larger organization. They have personally led significant year-end audits, overseen accounting and financial reporting, managed grant-funded operations, strengthened internal controls, improved budgeting and forecasting, and led finance systems and process transformation. They are equally comfortable resolving a technical accounting issue, guiding a manager, challenging a budget assumption, working with auditors and funders, and advising the CFO and Executive Team. The successful candidate will provide dependable operational leadership while helping modernize Finance and strengthen The Mustard Seed’s financial sustainability, stewardship, and organizational capacity.

QUALIFICATIONS

Education & Professional Designations, Required

Chartered Professional Accountant (CPA) designation in good standing.
Bachelor’s degree in accounting, finance, commerce, business administration, or a related discipline.
Ongoing professional development in accounting standards, financial reporting, governance, internal controls, audit, risk management, and finance leadership.

Preferred Assets

CRMA, CFE, CIA, or another relevant risk, controls, audit, fraud, or governance designation.
Advanced training or certification in ERP systems, data analytics, business intelligence, financial systems implementation, finance transformation, or project management.

Experience Requirements

Approximately 12 to 15+ years of progressive finance and accounting experience, including significant senior leadership responsibility.
A minimum of 5 to 7 years of leading managers and professional finance teams in a large or larger mid-sized, complex organization.
Significant experience serving in a Controller, Corporate Controller, or equivalent senior controllership role, with accountability for the integrity of financial reporting, accounting operations, internal controls, and close processes.
Extensive experience leading the annual external audit from planning through completion, including audit schedules, working papers, issue resolution, management responses, and relationships with external auditors and governance committees.
Demonstrated leadership across financial reporting, general accounting, grants accounting, budgeting and forecasting, treasury, internal controls, risk management, and audit coordination.
Substantial experience with grant-funded operations, including grant budgeting, restricted funding, contribution agreements, eligible expenditures, cost allocations, claims, financial reporting, compliance, funder audits, and closeout.
Experience leading finance systems and process improvement, including ERP optimization or implementation, systems integration, reporting automation, data quality, business intelligence, and finance workflow redesign.
Experience building, restructuring, developing, or stabilizing a finance function while maintaining reliable day-to-day delivery.
Experience advising executives and presenting clear, decision-focused financial information to senior leadership and governance bodies.

Strongly Preferred

Experience in a large charity, not-for-profit, healthcare, public sector, social services, affordable housing, or similarly complex mission-driven environment.
Experience managing a large portfolio of municipal, provincial, federal, or other government funding agreements.
Deep practical experience with fund accounting, restricted contributions, contribution revenue recognition, capital projects, and government-funded initiatives.
Experience with Salesforce-based ERP environments such as Certinia/FinancialForce, budgeting and forecasting tools, Tableau or similar BI platforms, and broader data governance initiatives.

jobs.title: Director Financial Risk
jobs.description:
The Financial Risk Oversight team has overall responsibility within Group Risk Management to provide independent oversight of risk taking and risk mitigation activities related to market and liquidity risk. The team also provides subject matter expertise with respect to market and liquidity risk and how it affects the organization. This role focuses on, but is not limited to, market and liquidity risk oversight for Manulife Bank. The individual will work collaboratively with the Bank Risk function and the General Account to ensure key market and liquidity risks are properly addressed.

Position Responsibilities

Identify and monitor market and liquidity risk independent of Operating Segments and Treasury.
Review and provide constructive input on risk policies including but not limited to Liquidity Management Policy, Interest Rate Risk Management Policy, Foreign Exchange Risk Management Policy.
Review the Liquidity Contingency Plan and make recommendations to improve its transparency and efficiency.
Ensure key market and liquidity risks are identified based on regulatory guidance, measured appropriately and incorporated in the overall risk management framework.
Review and validate the risk limits, parameters and assumptions used in various metrics for assessing liquidity risk and interest rate risk.
Monitor exposures against approved risk limits.
Have an expert knowledge of OSFI’s regulations such as the Liquidity Adequacy Requirements (LAR) Guideline, Interest Rate Risk Management Guideline, and ensure appropriate and effective implementation of these key guidelines.
Review and assess methodologies and assumptions for measuring key market and liquidity risk metrics.
Review and recommend stress testing scenarios / assumptions used for stress testing exercises (e.g., bank deposits run-offs).
Review and provide constructive feedback on the Bank’s funding plan.
Provide regular input and effective challenge over the first line of business’ risk management practices including but not limited to risk metrics, limits and methodologies.
Support and provide subject matter expertise to the Bank CRO and General Account Business CRO in areas of market and liquidity risk.
Review and provide input on all regulatory issues relating to market and liquidity risk.
Assess risk positions and risk exposures and steps being taken to address them.
Assess and opine on the adequacy of risk versus return in current portfolio and any proposed strategies.

Required Qualifications

Advanced degree in Finance or another quantitative discipline.
FRM and/or CFA designation an asset.
Ability to communicate effectively (oral and written), build strong working relationships and influence outcomes within and across segments.
Self-starter and ability to work with little guidance.
Minimum 5 years’ experience in the financial services industry, preferably in Treasury, Retail Banking and Insurance
Outstanding analytical and conceptual skills.
Excellent management and interpersonal skills.

Problems/Challenges

Increasing complexity associated with liquidity risk policies and the supporting measurement, monitoring and reporting infrastructure.
Balancing the requirements and expectations of multiple internal and external partners.

Personal Attributes And Cultural Fit

Inspires and motivates others.
Role model of ethics and integrity who builds a culture of respect.
Highly effective change agent who embraces change and leads change management.
Provides courageous advice.
Results-driven; highly focused on accountability.
Ability to handle multiple stakeholders
Demonstrates a commitment to delivering excellent service balanced with appropriate risk management and strategic perspective.
Highly collaborative working style.

When You Join Our Team

We’ll empower you to learn and grow the career you want.
We’ll recognize and support you in a flexible environment where well-being and inclusion are more than just words.
As part of our global team, we’ll support you in shaping the future you want to see.

The role being advertised is an existing vacancy.

The Bank is accelerating its transformation by placing artificial intelligence at the core of its business and technology strategies. AI is a key enabler for innovation, operational efficiency, and hyper-personalized customer experiences. To support this ambition, we are creating a strategic role dedicated to shaping the Bank’s AI architecture vision.

You thrive in uncertainty and fast‑moving environments, consistently demonstrating initiative, sound judgment, and accountability. Your role

Define and evolve the Bank’s enterprise AI architecture strategy, roadmap, and reference architectures in alignment with business priorities, enterprise architecture, and risk appetite.
Establish pragmatic AI principles, guardrails, and reusable patterns that accelerate delivery while ensuring consistency, reuse, and control across the organization

Partner with AI delivery, governance, business, data, and technology stakeholders to drive a coherent enterprise AI approach, clarify decision rights, and translate opportunities into scalable golden paths.

Reporting to the Chief Architect, you ensure that AI solutions can scale safely, remain aligned with enterprise standards, and operate within the Bank’s risk appetite.

Prerequisites

Minimum of 15 years of experience in enterprise and/or solution architecture, including significant hands-on experience in AI-related domains.
Deep expertise in AI technologies, including machine learning, generative AI, agent-based systems, and the enterprise platforms required to operationalize them.

They are intellectually curious, commercially minded, and action-oriented. They know how to move seamlessly between strategy and execution, challenge and support, analysis and action. Most importantly, they have a demonstrated ability to help organizations deliver on their most important priorities and achieve meaningful outcomes.

 Job Description: 
 Reporting to the Vice President, Finance & CFO, Canadian Personal & Small Business Banking (CPSB), the Associate Vice President leads Finance support for Real Estate Secured Lending (RESL), Specialized Sales Force (SSF), Operations and the Chief Operating Officer (COO) organization. The role is the senior Finance partner to the SVP, RESL; SVP, Specialized Sales Force; and SVP & COO, CPSB, connecting strategy with financial outcomes across significant revenue, balance sheet, expense and investment portfolios.

 The role provides forward-looking advice and independent challenge on growth, profitability, productivity, transformation and resource allocation. It brings an enterprise perspective to decisions, identifies opportunities for value creation and maintains strong financial management, controls and performance discipline.

 As a member of TD's leadership team, the AVP sets high ethical and performance standards, develops talent and collaborates across the Bank to deliver sustainable results. The role requires strategic insight, business acumen, sound judgment and integrity.

 POSITION-SPECIFIC ACCOUNTABILITIES:
 Lead portfolio planning, forecasting, reporting and performance management. Develop driver-based forecasts and scenarios, explain variances, and translate risks and opportunities into executive insight and recommended actions.
 Advise and independently challenge RESL pricing and offers. Assess volume, retention, margin and risk-adjusted return trade-offs, considering funding costs, customer behaviour and competition.
 Lead SSF financial planning and analysis, including MMS and broker channel financials and compensation models. Evaluate acquisition costs, incentives, conversion, retention and lifetime profitability; advise on compensation changes and channel mix across branch, specialist, broker and digital distribution.
 Assess portfolio economics across volumes, market share, margins, credit, funding, expenses and returns. Analyze profitability by product, segment and origination cohort, isolating mix, pricing, renewals and runoff. Partner with Treasury, Risk, Product and Distribution on rate scenarios, funding and capital implications.
 Advise on investment prioritization and allocation of capital, expense and capacity. Challenge business cases, returns, costs and milestones; track benefits and cross-CPSB dependencies and trade-offs. Recommend reprioritization when economics or delivery assumptions change.
 Analyze operational cost drivers, unit costs, cost-to-serve and capacity. Link volumes, service levels, staffing and demand to expense plans; challenge assumptions and identify productivity and operating-leverage opportunities while protecting controls and customer outcomes.
 Partner with COO leaders to connect strategic priorities, transformation and operating performance to financial outcomes. Assess cross-business initiatives and execution risks, balancing near-term commitments with longer-term value.
 Provide oversight and independent challenge of reporting, controls, allocations and accounting. Reinforce direct and shared cost ownership, reliable management information and consistent financial treatment; resolve issues with Finance and enterprise partners.
 Finance Talent, Capability & Leadership 
 Build a high-performing Finance team with the capabilities to deliver stronger business partnership, insight and independent challenge. Shape talent priorities, attract and develop talent, and strengthen succession and leadership depth, with a focus on commercial acumen, strategic judgment and executive influence.
 Advance the portfolio's Finance operating model in alignment with enterprise and CPSB strategy. Shape and implement changes within the team, and strengthen team capacity for higher-value advisory work.
 Champion data, digital and AI-enabled Finance, influencing priorities with enterprise partners and accelerating adoption of tools, analytics and automation that improve decision-making, information quality, productivity and colleague capacity. Provide leadership and accountability for a sound financial control environment within the portfolio. Ensure changes to processes, tools and responsibilities maintain clear ownership and effective governance; partner with enterprise control owners to address risks and sustain confidence in financial information.
 Lead through the TD Way, creating an inclusive, high-performing culture grounded in clear expectations, accountability, constructive challenge, continuous improvement and colleague development. Set clear objectives, provide ongoing coaching and feedback, recognize strong performance and address performance gaps Operate as an enterprise Finance leader, building partnerships across CPSB and enterprise Finance, Treasury, Risk, Accounting, Tax, Data & Analytics and Technology; contribute to the broader CPSB Finance agenda beyond the immediate portfolio.

 QUALIFICATIONS & EXPERIENCE: 
 The successful candidate will bring:
 Significant senior-level financial management, business advisory and leadership experience, with strong banking economics and commercial acumen.
 Strong understanding of secured lending profitability, pricing and channel economics, together with operational cost management and investment evaluation; ability to connect product, distribution and operating decisions to financial performance.
 Experience evaluating growth, investment, transformation, productivity and resource-allocation decisions, with sound judgment in balancing financial outcomes, customer needs and risk.
 Strong analytical and communication skills; ability to synthesize complex issues into concise executive recommendations and influence decisions through constructive challenge.
 Proven experience developing talent and succession depth and implementing Finance improvements across team operating models, processes, tools and controls; ability to partner with enterprise teams and deliver sustained adoption and measurable benefits.
 Ability to manage competing priorities effectively and maintain resilience in a fast-paced environment.

 EDUCATIO N

jobs.description:
Putting people first, every day

BDO is a firm built on a foundation of positive relationships with our people and our clients. Each day, our professionals provide exceptional service, helping clients with advice and insight they can trust. In turn, we offer an award-winning environment that fosters a people-first culture with a high priority on your personal and professional growth.

Your Opportunity

Reporting to the Chief Human Resources Officer and serving as a member of the HR Leadership Team, the Director, Talent Management & Workforce Insights
leads an integrated portfolio spanning Talent Management, Total Rewards, HR Operations and People Analytics. The Director sets priorities across the portfolio, leads experienced specialist teams and helps these capabilities evolve to better support the firm’s business and people priorities.

Working closely with HR Business Partners, Talent Acquisition and leaders across the firm, the Director will shape the talent systems, workforce insights, rewards and HR services that help BDO retain its people, create meaningful opportunities for talent, and support the firm’s evolving workforce needs. The Director leads through experienced leaders and is not expected to be the technical expert in every area of the portfolio.

Key Accountabilities

Portfolio Leadership

Lead the Organizational Development, Total Rewards, HR Operations and People Analytics portfolio, setting clear priorities, accountabilities and measures of success.
Turn the firm’s people priorities into focused plans and practical outcomes.
Use workforce data, external information and business context to identify risks and opportunities and provide clear recommendations.
Connect the work across the portfolio so leaders and employees receive clear and consistent support.
Review what is working, stop or simplify lower-value work and improve the portfolio based on evidence and business needs.
Foster strong collaboration across HR so firmwide approaches are practical, consistent and responsive to business needs.

Talent Management

Strengthen the firm’s approach to Talent Management, with an initial focus on reviewing how performance, talent and succession decisions are supported across the firm.
Work with HR Business Partners and business leaders to improve the quality and consistency of talent discussions and decisions.
Use talent data and feedback to identify firmwide themes, risks and areas requiring attention.
Clarify roles, accountabilities and ways of working across HR as these practices evolve.

Workforce Insights

Lead the firm’s workforce insights agenda by identifying the workforce questions, trends and risks that matter most to the business.
Work through the People Analytics team to strengthen the quality, relevance and use of workforce reporting and analysis.
Move the function beyond producing standard reports toward providing insights and recommendations that support business, talent and workforce decisions.
Set priorities for the People Analytics team based on the decisions and workforce questions the firm needs to address.
Work with Finance, HR Business Partners, Talent Acquisition and other stakeholders to bring together business context, workforce data and external talent-market information.
Help define how the firm’s workforce insights capability should evolve, including opportunities to make better use of analytics, technology and AI.

Total Rewards & Wellbeing

Ensure reward programs remain competitive, sustainable and aligned with business priorities, market trends and workforce needs.
Oversee the evolution of reward and recognition practices that support attraction, retention and performance.
Advance the firm’s approach to employee wellbeing, ensuring it remains responsive to evolving workforce needs and expectations and supports sustainable performance and a positive employee experience.

HR Operations & Enablement

Provide strategic oversight of HR Operations, working through the leaders responsible for day-to-day service delivery, reporting and operational performance.
Set clear priorities for improving HR processes, systems and services, with a focus on simplicity, consistency and the needs of employees, leaders and HR teams.
Sponsor practical opportunities to use technology, automation and AI to reduce manual work and improve service delivery.
Ensure the People Analytics team provides accurate, timely and useful workforce reporting and analysis.
Connect operational, reporting and technology priorities to the broader needs of HR and the business.

Stakeholder Relationships

Build trusted relationships across the firm and serve as a strategic advisor on talent, workforce and organizational matters.
Lead and develop leaders across Organizational Development, Total Rewards, HR Operations and People Analytics, setting clear priorities and building shared accountability across the portfolio.

What You Will Help Us Achieve

Success in this role means:

A more focused approach to Talent Management, including stronger performance and succession practices over time.
Competitive and sustainable reward programs that support attraction, retention, wellbeing and performance.
Workforce reporting and insights that help leaders understand workforce trends, risks and opportunities and make better decisions.
Clear roles and accountabilities across the portfolio as its capabilities evolve.
Practical use of technology, automation and AI to simplify work and improve HR delivery.

What You Bring

Significant progressive HR experience, including leadership responsibility for an enterprise talent, rewards, HR operations, workforce insights or related portfolio.
Meaningful depth in at least one of Talent Management, Total Rewards, HR Operations or People Analytics, together with the range and learning agility to lead experienced specialists across the broader portfolio.
Experience improving enterprise HR practices or functions and showing clear results.
A track record of using workforce data and insight to influence business decisions and improve outcomes.
Evidence of questioning established approaches, simplifying work and improving outcomes for the business and employees.
Practical understanding of workforce trends, technology and AI, and the judgement to apply them where they can improve decisions or ways of working.
Demonstrated ability to lead through others, set clear priorities and build shared accountability across specialist teams.
Exceptional relationship-building, communication and influencing skills, including the ability to work effectively with senior leaders.
Strong judgement and business acumen, with the ability to balance employee experience, business priorities, risk and operational realities.
Experience within professional services or another complex, relationship-driven organization would be considered a strong asset.
University degree in Human Resources, Business or a related discipline. A relevant professional designation and/or advanced degree would be considered an asset.

Why BDO?

Our people-first approach to talent has earned us a spot among Canada’s Top 100 Employers for 2026. This recognition is a milestone we’re thrilled to add to our collection of awards for both experienced and student talent experiences.

At BDO, our people experience is guided by three core pillars— Do work with genuine care, Do what matters with purpose, and Do what’s next
- shaping how we support our people, serve our clients, and grow together.

Our firm is committed to providing an environment where you can be successful in the following ways:

We enable you to engage with how we change and evolve, being a key contributor to the success and growth of BDO in Canada.
We help you become a better professional within our services, industries, and markets with extensive opportunities for learning and development.
We support your achievement of personal goals outside of the office and making an impact on your community.
We foster a collaborative, inclusive environment where your ideas are valued, and you can do your best work with genuine care and purpose
We encourage innovation and forward thinking, empowering you to embrace what’s next and help shape the future of our firm

Giving back adds up:
Where company meets community. BDO is actively involved in our communities by supporting local charity initiatives. We support staff with local and national events where you will be given the opportunity to contribute to your community.

Total rewards that matter:
We pay for performance with competitive total cash compensation that recognizes and rewards your contribution. We provide comprehensive benefits from day one, and a flexible personal time off policy. We’re committed to supporting your overall wellbeing and provide reimbursement for wellness initiatives that fit your lifestyle.

Everyone counts:
We are committed to creating a workplace where employees can participate fully, contribute meaningfully and succeed without barriers. We are dedicated to fostering a workplace defined by respect, fairness, and a true sense of belonging for everyone. We recognize and celebrate the unique experiences, identities, and perspectives that each of us bring – and that these experiences strengthen how we work together. Our commitment extends to ensuring that our application process is both inclusive and accessible. If you require accommodation to complete the application process, please contact us.

Flexibility:

Our model is a blended approach designed to support the flexible needs of our people, the firm and our clients. It’s about creating work experiences that meet everyone’s needs and providing flexibility to adjust when, where and how we work to meet the expectations of our role.

Code of Conduct:
Our Code of Conduct sets clear standards for how we conduct business. It reflects our shared values and commitments and includes guiding principles to help us make ethical decisions and maintain trust with each other, our clients, and the public.

jobs.title: Directeur(trice) de l’analytique marketing / Director of Marketing Analytics
jobs.description:
Brief Description

Qui est Manmade?

Nous sommes un détaillant en ligne de produits essentiels de première qualité basé à Montréal, connu particulièrement jusqu'à présent pour nos boxer pour hommes. Nous avons connu une croissance rapide depuis notre lancement en 2021, et la marque est véritablement à un tournant pour devenir un nom familier au Canada, et elle se développe déjà en parallèle sur le marché américain.

Qui recherchons-nous?

Nous recherchons un(e) Chef(fe) de l’analytique marketing
pour bâtir et diriger la fonction d’analytique marketing de Manmade.

Vous serez responsable de la façon dont nous mesurons et interprétons la performance marketing, en regroupant les données de nos différents canaux pour offrir une vision claire et fiable des facteurs qui contribuent aux résultats de l’entreprise. Une priorité sera de créer une source de référence unique et centralisée
pour la performance marketing et de mettre en place les tableaux de bord, les indicateurs clés de performance et les cadres de mesure qui guideront les décisions de nos équipes.

Il s’agit d’un poste de niveau senior avec une forte implication opérationnelle
. Vous devrez explorer les données, créer des tableaux de bord, analyser la performance et résoudre vous-même les problèmes, tout en établissant les bases d’une équipe et d’une fonction capables d’évoluer avec Manmade.

Si vous aimez transformer des données complexes en décisions d’affaires claires et souhaitez bâtir une fonction à partir de zéro, nous aimerions vous rencontrer.

Ce poste est-il fait pour vous ?

Nous nous développons rapidement, les choses changent vite et une présence en interne est nécessaire.

Ce que nous offrons?
Nous pensons qu'un travail de qualité commence par un environnement de qualité. En tant que membre de notre équipe, vous bénéficierez de déjeuners quotidiens gratuits, de collations et de boissons pour vous permettre de rester en forme et concentré. Nous offrons une assurance de groupe payée à 100 %, des salaires compétitifs qui sont révisés régulièrement avec des augmentations annuelles garanties, et une structure de primes de partage des bénéfices pour que tout le monde participe à notre succès.

Nous sommes dans une phase de croissance, ce qui signifie de réelles opportunités pour vous d'apprendre, de vous développer et de faire passer votre carrière au niveau supérieur. Avant tout, vous ferez partie d'une culture amusante, innovante et respectueuse où vos idées sont valorisées et où votre impact est réel.

Responsabilités

Bâtir et prendre en charge la fonction d’analytique et de mesure marketing de Manmade, tant pour l’acquisition que pour la fidélisation de la clientèle.
Créer une source de référence unique pour la performance marketing en regroupant les données de Meta, Google, TikTok, du marketing par courriel, du marketing d’influence, de Shopify et de l’analytique Web.
Concevoir et maintenir des tableaux de bord, des cadres d’indicateurs clés de performance et des rapports offrant aux équipes Marketing et à la direction une vision claire de la performance.
Analyser les indicateurs clés, notamment le coût d’acquisition client (CAC), la valeur vie client (LTV), le rendement des dépenses publicitaires (ROAS), le ratio d’efficacité marketing (MER), la rétention, la conversion, les cohortes de clients et la performance des canaux.
Collaborer avec les équipes Marketing et Finance pour relier les investissements et la performance marketing aux revenus, à la rentabilité par client et à une croissance rentable.
Évaluer la performance des canaux, des campagnes, des audiences et des créations publicitaires, puis traduire les résultats en recommandations claires et concrètes.
Développer l’approche de Manmade en matière d’attribution, d’incrémentalité, d’expérimentation et de mesure marketing, notamment au moyen de tests A/B, de tests géographiques et de groupes témoins.
Consolider et valider les données provenant des différentes plateformes afin de garantir l’exactitude et la fiabilité des rapports.
Mener des analyses approfondies pour répondre à des questions d’affaires complexes et repérer des occasions d’amélioration en matière d’acquisition, de fidélisation et de valeur vie client.
Mettre en place des processus, des outils et une infrastructure analytiques capables de soutenir la croissance, et définir la feuille de route de la fonction.
Maintenir une forte implication opérationnelle tout en bâtissant et en dirigeant, à terme, une équipe d’analytique marketing performante.

Éxigences

De 7 à 10 ans d’expérience progressive en analytique marketing, en analytique de croissance, en intelligence d’affaires, en analyse de données ou dans un domaine connexe.
Solide expérience en commerce électronique, en vente directe aux consommateurs (DTC), dans le secteur des produits de consommation ou au sein d’une autre entreprise numérique à forte croissance.
Expérience démontrée dans la création ou le développement d’une fonction d’analytique marketing, notamment les tableaux de bord, les cadres d’indicateurs clés de performance, les rapports et les processus de mesure.
Maîtrise avancée de SQL et d’Excel, ainsi qu’une solide expérience avec des outils d’intelligence d’affaires comme Looker, Tableau, Power BI ou des outils similaires.
Expérience avec Shopify, GA4, Meta, Google, TikTok et d’autres plateformes de marketing numérique.
Compréhension approfondie du CAC, de la LTV, du ROAS, du MER, de la rétention, de la conversion, de l’analyse de cohortes, de l’attribution et de la rentabilité par client.
Expérience en expérimentation marketing et en mesure de l’incrémentalité, notamment les tests A/B, les tests géographiques et les groupes témoins.
Solide sens des affaires et capacité à relier la performance marketing aux résultats commerciaux et financiers de l’entreprise.
Capacité à définir la stratégie analytique tout en explorant personnellement les données et en développant des solutions.
Excellentes aptitudes en communication et capacité à traduire des données complexes en constats clairs pour les équipes Marketing, Finance et la direction.
Une expérience dans la constitution d’équipes, le mentorat ou la gestion de professionnels en analytique est fortement souhaitée.
Baccalauréat dans un domaine pertinent ou expérience professionnelle équivalente.

Who is Manmade?

We’re a Montreal-based online retailer of premium quality essentials, known particularly so far for our men’s boxer briefs. We have been rapidly growing since launching in 2021, and the brand is truly at a turning point to becoming a household name in Canada, and already growing rapidly in parallel in the US market.

Who is Manmade looking for?

We’re looking for a Head of Marketing Analytics
to build and lead Manmade’s marketing analytics function.

You’ll own how we measure and understand marketing performance, bringing together data across our channels to create a clear, trusted view of what’s driving the business. A key priority will be building a unified source of truth
for marketing performance and establishing the dashboards, KPIs, and measurement frameworks our teams use to make decisions.

This is a senior but deeply hands-on role
. You’ll be expected to dig into the data, build dashboards, analyze performance, and solve problems yourself while creating the foundation for a team and function that can scale with Manmade.

If you love turning complex data into clear business decisions and want the opportunity to build something from the ground up, we’d love to hear from you.

Is this for you?

We are growing so rapidly so things are changing so quickly and an in-house presence is required

What are we offering?
Aside from a competitive compensation package, the opportunity in itself is what you make of it. With the company growing 250%+ year over year for the past 3 years, and with expected growth to continue at a high pace for the next 2-3 years, there will be many different ways to grow within the company as it enters new markets, channels, and so on.

We offer extended health and dental benefits, 100% fully paid by the employer. We offer catered lunches every day and all the snacks, drinks, coffee, and fruit you could want.

Responsibilities

Own and build Manmade’s marketing analytics and measurement function across customer acquisition and retention.
Create a unified source of truth for marketing performance across Meta, Google, TikTok, Email, Influencer, Shopify, and web analytics.
Build and maintain dashboards, KPI frameworks, and reporting that give Marketing and leadership a clear view of performance.
Analyze key metrics including CAC, LTV, ROAS, MER, retention, conversion, customer cohorts, and channel performance.
Partner with Marketing and Finance to connect marketing investment and performance to revenue, customer economics, and profitable growth.
Evaluate channel, campaign, audience, and creative performance and turn findings into clear, actionable recommendations.
Develop Manmade’s approach to attribution, incrementality, experimentation, and marketing measurement, including A/B tests, geo studies, and holdouts.
Consolidate and validate data across platforms, ensuring reporting is accurate, reliable, and trusted.
Conduct deep-dive analyses to answer complex business questions and identify opportunities across acquisition, retention, and customer lifetime value.
Build scalable analytics processes, tools, and infrastructure, and establish the roadmap for the function as Manmade grows.
Remain deeply hands-on while eventually building and leading a high-performing marketing analytics team.

Qualifications

7–10 years of progressive experience in marketing analytics, growth analytics, business intelligence, data analytics, or a related field.
Strong experience in e-commerce, DTC, consumer, or another high-growth digital business.
Proven experience building or scaling a marketing analytics function, including dashboards, KPI frameworks, reporting, and measurement processes.
Advanced proficiency in SQL and Excel, with strong experience in BI tools such as Looker, Tableau, Power BI, or similar.
Experience with Shopify, GA4, Meta, Google, TikTok, and other digital marketing platforms.
Deep understanding of CAC, LTV, ROAS, MER, retention, conversion, cohort analysis, attribution, and customer economics.
Experience with marketing experimentation and incrementality, including A/B testing, geo testing, and holdouts.
Strong commercial acumen with the ability to connect marketing performance to broader business and financial outcomes.
Ability to operate at both levels: setting analytics strategy while personally digging into the data and building solutions.
Strong communication skills with the ability to translate complex data into clear insights for Marketing, Finance, and leadership.
Experience building, mentoring, or leading analytics talent is strongly preferred.
Bachelor’s degree in a relevant field or equivalent professional experience.

Based on the US East Coast or in Montreal, you report to the VP Marketing in Paris. This is a player-coach role: you lead a team of three (an ABM / Campaign Manager, a field marketer in Europe and a field marketer in the US you will hire) and work hand in hand with Growth, Brand & Content and the BDR & SDR team.

WHAT YOU WILL OWN
• End-to-end enterprise marketing strategy: own the plan, budget and results in every market, to grow enterprise pipeline, framework agreements signed and their activation.

US East Coast or Montreal. Regular travel to Europe and across the US. Competitive base salary, variable, equity and benefits.

RSM is seeking a growth-oriented Management Consulting Director to join our Technology Performance practice. This leader will play a critical role in driving the continued growth of the practice by expanding strategic client relationships, developing new market opportunities, and leading complex technology transformation engagements.

This Director will combine strong business development capabilities with deep expertise in Technology Strategy, ERP Strategy, IT Architecture, and complex transformation program leadership. The role requires a leader who can originate opportunities, shape solutions, build trusted executive relationships, oversee complex engagements, and develop high-performing consulting teams.

The ideal candidate is a proven consulting leader who can connect business strategy with technology, helping organizations make critical technology investment decisions, modernize their enterprise environments, and successfully execute large-scale transformation initiatives. This individual will also help shape the continued evolution of the Technology Performance practice by developing talent, strengthening capabilities, and bringing differentiated solutions to market.

Responsibilities

Practice Growth & Market Leadership

Drive growth of the Technology Performance practice through business development, account expansion, relationship building, and new client acquisition.
Build and manage a strong pipeline of technology consulting and transformation opportunities.
Develop trusted relationships with senior executives, including CIOs, CTOs, CFOs, COOs, and other business and technology leaders.
Lead strategic pursuits from opportunity identification and solution development through proposal creation, executive presentations, and contract award.
Identify opportunities to expand existing client relationships by connecting business priorities with RSM’s broader technology and consulting capabilities.
Develop and execute go-to-market strategies around key Technology Performance offerings and emerging client needs.
Contribute to the practice’s market presence through thought leadership, industry events, executive presentations, and development of differentiated offerings.

Client & Engagement Leadership

Serve as a senior trusted advisor to executives navigating complex technology strategies, investments, and transformation programs.
Lead engagements spanning Technology Strategy, ERP Strategy and Selection, IT Architecture, enterprise application modernization, digital transformation, and technology operating model design.
Advise clients on aligning technology investments and roadmaps with business strategy, growth objectives, operational needs, and financial priorities.
Lead and oversee complex, multi-workstream transformation programs involving business stakeholders, technology teams, vendors, and third-party partners.

Advise clients on ERP strategy, modernization, selection, implementation planning, and optimization, including the broader business and operating model implications of ERP transformation.
Assess existing IT and enterprise architecture and develop future-state architectures that support scalability, integration, modernization, and business objectives.
Provide leadership across complex technology environments involving ERP, cloud, data and analytics, AI, automation, enterprise applications, infrastructure, and integration architecture.

Evaluate technology environments and recommend practical, business-focused solutions that balance modernization goals, investment requirements, organizational readiness, and risk.
Stay current on emerging technologies, market trends, ERP platforms, AI capabilities, and evolving technology operating models and translate those developments into practical client solutions and new market opportunities.

People & Practice Leadership

Lead, mentor, and develop consulting professionals across multiple levels, creating a culture of high performance, accountability, collaboration, and continuous development.
Build scalable consulting capabilities by developing talent, methodologies, intellectual capital, and repeatable solutions.
Coach and develop team members while identifying and preparing future leaders within the practice.

Demonstrated experience selling, shaping, and delivering complex technology consulting engagements.
Proven track record of business development, account growth, executive relationship management, and consulting sales.
Deep experience in one or more core areas including Technology Strategy, ERP Strategy, IT Architecture, or large-scale technology transformation.

Experience leading and developing multidisciplinary consulting teams.
Strong executive presence with the ability to advise and influence C-suite and senior business and technology leaders.
Exceptional communication, presentation, facilitation, and relationship-building skills.
Strong commercial and financial acumen, including experience managing engagement economics, delivery quality, risk, and client expectations.

jobs.description:
Director, Accounting & Finance

Toronto, ON (Hybrid – Tuesdays and Thursdays in Toronto office)

$125,000–$150,000 base salary, plus benefits and RRSP matching

Our client is an established organization with a small Canadian team and long-tenured employees. They are looking for a Director, Accounting & Finance to take ownership of full-cycle accounting and financial reporting. Reporting to the Executive Director, you will supervise one direct report and work closely with finance colleagues across the broader organization.

This is a hands-on role for a CPA who enjoys preparing the numbers and explaining them to leadership. You will manage the monthly close, oversee payroll and help the team transition to Workday Financial and its integration with ADP. The organization is targeting a January 2027 start. They offer very good work/life balance, 12 sick days and an office closure between Christmas and New Year’s. Some weeks you will only be expected to go into the office one day per week, but mostly it will be two days. This is a very hands-on Director role, so you should be prepared to handle bank reconciliations, journal entries, HST filing and more.

Responsibilities

Manage the monthly and year-end close, including journal entries, general ledger reconciliations and the preparation of financial statements. Prepare monthly management reports and explain variances against budget.
Oversee accounts payable and accounts receivable, manage day-to-day banking and complete bank reconciliations.
Record investment transactions, reconcile holdings to investment statements and prepare monthly investment reports. Review distribution approvals and complete the related accounting and reconciliations.
Oversee Ontario payroll through ADP. Review and approve each pay run, verify salary changes and ensure payroll information flows accurately between Workday and ADP.
Coordinate the annual audit, prepare working papers and financial schedules, and respond to questions from external auditors.
Prepare monthly GST/HST returns and coordinate withholding tax reporting, annual information returns and other regulatory filings with external advisers.
Review accounting policies, approval procedures and the segregation of duties. Help improve processes as the team transitions to new systems.
Supervise and develop one direct report whose current focus is accounts receivable. Help identify opportunities for that role to take on more financial analysis over time.

Requirements

Canadian CPA designation and a bachelor’s degree in accounting, finance or a related field.
At least eight years of progressive accounting experience, including hands-on responsibility for full-cycle accounting, bank reconciliations and monthly financial reporting.
Preference will be given to individuals with Workday and ADP experience.
Strong understanding of audit preparation, internal controls and payroll oversight.
Advanced EXCEL skills and the ability to investigate discrepancies, explain findings and manage competing deadlines.
Strong written and verbal communication skills, sound judgment when handling confidential information and the ability to guide a direct report while managing your own accounting work.

jobs.description:
Description

Director Strategy and Delivery Real World Late Phase

Syneos Health® is a leading fully-integrated life sciences services organization built to accelerate customer success. We partner with innovators at every point across the drug development and commercialization continuum, helping them navigate complexity, anticipate change and accelerate progress.

Our Clinical Solutions team members act with a drug development mindset, applying their years of experience and deep expertise to truly understand customer needs and represent those in the solutions we shape.

Whether you join us in a Functional Service Provider partnership or a Full-Service environment, you’ll collaborate with passionate problem solvers, innovating as a team to help our customers achieve their goals. We are agile and driven to deliver – for one another, our customers, and, most importantly, for those in need.

Discover what your 25,000 future colleagues already know:

Why Syneos Health

We are passionate about developing our people, through career development and progression; supportive and engaged line management; technical and therapeutic area training; peer recognition and total rewards program.
We are committed to building an inclusive culture – where you can authentically be yourself. Central to this is our purpose – Driven to Deliver – which captures the passion of our colleagues to show up each day and shape solutions that have the ability to dramatically impact someone’s life.
We are continuously building the company we all want to work for and our customers want to work with. Why? Because we know that when we bring together smart colleagues from across the world, we can shape the future of healthcare, driving impact for customers and defining the pace of patient progress.

Job Responsibilities

Job Summary

The Director, Strategy & Delivery, Real World Late Phase (RWLP), independently leads customer engagements from pre-award strategy through study delivery. The role combines ownership of study strategy, proposal development and bid defenses with operational and financial oversight of assigned studies, programs and portfolios. The Director partners with Business Development and Medical Strategy to secure new business, support account growth and ensure that proposal commitments translate into achievable delivery plans.

The Director develops practical delivery solutions for non-interventional and interventional late-phase research, including prospective and retrospective observational studies, registries, postmarketing safety and effectiveness studies, pragmatic studies and long-term follow-up. Working with Business Development, Medical, Epidemiology, Biostatistics and other functional leaders, the Director translates evidence needs into feasible study plans, budgets and delivery commitments. The role is accountable for customer satisfaction, study and portfolio performance, and the development of assigned teams.

Strategy and customer engagement

Lead strategy for assigned RWLP opportunities, aligning customer evidence needs with study design, data availability, country requirements, operational feasibility and budget.
Lead proposal development and writing and bid defense preparation, including delivery models, country and site strategy, staffing, assumptions, timelines, budgets and risk mitigation. Coach team members to present their expertise and proposed solutions clearly.
Partner with Business Development and account leaders to develop customer relationships, identify follow-on opportunities and demonstrate RWLP capabilities through credible delivery commitments.
Ensure an effective transition from proposal to delivery, with clear ownership of commitments, assumptions, scope, resources and customer expectations.

RWLP study design and delivery

Apply working knowledge of interventional and non-interventional study designs, including cohort, case-control and cross-sectional studies; prospective and retrospective registries; chart reviews; pragmatic trials; postmarketing studies; and extension or long-term follow-up programs.
Partner with Epidemiology, Biostatistics and Medical to assess whether proposed populations, endpoints, follow-up schedules and data sources can answer the study objectives. Translate scientific recommendations into operational plans without substituting for specialist scientific accountability.
Assess delivery options using primary data collection, secondary data sources or a combination of both, including electronic health records, claims and existing registries. Identify data access, completeness, linkage, consent and site-workflow requirements with the relevant specialists.
Oversee feasibility, country and site selection, startup, recruitment, retention, monitoring, data collection and closeout. Adapt delivery to routine care and site capabilities while meeting protocol and applicable quality requirements.
Ensure monitoring and oversight are proportionate to study design, data risks and applicable requirements. Coordinate safety reporting, vendor oversight and event adjudication where required by the protocol.
Oversee assigned studies and portfolios against scope, timeline, quality and financial commitments. Review performance trends, resolve escalations and lead recovery plans with clear owners and deadlines.

Operational leadership and people management

Lead portfolio reviews and governance discussions; identify recurring delivery issues, capacity constraints and opportunities to improve execution across studies.
Partner with functional and resource leaders to forecast demand, allocate staff and balance workload, skills, continuity and cost across the assigned portfolio.
Provide line management for designated employees where assigned, including recruitment, onboarding, objective setting, coaching, performance reviews, development planning and succession planning.
Assess employee readiness for assigned responsibilities, identify training needs and oversee project handovers and role transitions. Address performance concerns with HR and the appropriate functional leaders.
Develop project leaders and cross-functional teams, clarify accountability and promote consistent delivery practices. Maintain defined decision rights with the ODL and functional leadership under the approved operating model.

Financial performance, quality and compliance

Own financial oversight for assigned studies and programs, including budget review, forecasting, resource utilization, profitability, scope management and timely change orders. Resolve variances with project teams and Finance.
Apply Good Pharmacoepidemiology Practices (GPP), Good Clinical Practice (GCP) and applicable local requirements according to study classification and activities. Work with Regulatory and Quality to confirm the appropriate framework.
Ensure compliance with company procedures, contractual commitments and applicable customer requirements. Coordinate ethics review, informed consent or approved waivers, privacy and data governance requirements with the responsible functions.
Maintain oversight of quality risks, deviations and corrective and preventive actions; support audit and inspection readiness and timely resolution of findings.
Use delivery metrics, customer feedback and lessons learned to improve RWLP processes, proposal assumptions, budget models and execution.

Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in life sciences, nursing, public health, epidemiology or a related discipline, or equivalent education and related experience. An advanced relevant degree is preferred.
Extensive relevant research experience within a CRO, pharmaceutical, biotechnology or comparable research organization, including demonstrated leadership of RWLP programs. Direct experience delivering both non-interventional and interventional late-phase studies is required.
Demonstrated understanding of observational and interventional study designs, routine-care research, primary and secondary data collection, and their operational implications.
Working knowledge of GPP, GCP and applicable global and local requirements for late-phase and non-interventional research, with the ability to apply the appropriate framework with specialist support.
Proven experience leading proposals, bid defenses and senior customer discussions, and translating evidence objectives into feasible, appropriately costed delivery plans.
Demonstrated portfolio or multi-study oversight, operational problem-solving, financial forecasting, resource planning and scope management.
Experience developing staff and leading cross-functional teams. Direct people-management experience is required where the role includes line-management accountability.
Ability to work effectively with Medical, Epidemiology, Biostatistics, Regulatory, Safety, Data Management and technology partners; sufficient therapeutic-area knowledge to lead credible customer discussions and identify when specialist input is needed.
Strong communication, presentation, negotiation and decision-making skills; ability to manage competing priorities and resolve issues with senior stakeholders.
Proficiency in core business and project-management tools; fluency in English; willingness to travel approximately 25%, consistent with business needs.

Critical Skills

RWLP strategy and delivery; study-design literacy; customer engagement; bid defense leadership; portfolio oversight; people development; resource planning; financial management; risk-based quality oversight; cross-functional decision-making.

US Experience Requirements

At least eight years of relevant research experience, including at least seven years managing studies, with demonstrated experience leading RWLP programs across interventional and non-interventional research.

jobs.title: Director, Patient Access & Channel Strategy
jobs.description:
Aperçu

Build the connections that bring innovation to patients.

Scientific progress creates possibilities. Helping patients access treatment takes people who can connect the dots—between support programs, reimbursement, pharmacies and the partners who deliver medicines.

At Incyte Canada, we are looking for an Associate Director / Director, Patient Access & Channel Strategy to strengthen those connections across oncology, hematology, immunology and dermatology. As our portfolio evolves and we prepare for upcoming launches, you will shape how patients access our therapies, building the programs, partnerships and capabilities to support them.

Patient Support Programs will be at the heart of your mandate. You will lead their strategy and delivery, strengthen our distribution partnerships and develop our pharmacy and channel approach. Working closely with colleagues across Market Access, Medical, Finance and Legal, you will turn complex challenges into practical solutions, combining strategic vision with the willingness to get into the detail and make things work.

We are looking for a builder, a thoughtful negotiator and a relationship leader. Someone who brings structure to ambiguity, earns trust across a complex healthcare ecosystem and takes ownership from strategy through execution.

An opportunity to shape a critical capability for Incyte Canada, and help patients access the innovation we work to deliver.

The Associate Director/Director, Patient Access & Channel Strategy is responsible for the strategic leadership, development, and execution of best-in-class Patient Support Programs (PSPs), trade relations, supply chain, and pharmacy/channel strategy supporting Incyte Canada's oncology/hematology and immunology/dermatology portfolio.

This role oversees a complex ecosystem of PSPs, vendors, wholesalers, distribution partners, pharmacies, and Group Purchasing Organizations (GPOs), ensuring seamless patient access to innovative therapies. The incumbent serves as the primary point of contact for Supply Chain within Canada, acts as the Quality Assurance (QA) Ambassador for the affiliate, and represents the organization externally with the Health Products Stewardship Association (HPSA).

In addition, the incumbent holds accountability for budget oversight and financial governance across PSP, trade, and channel-related activities. Working cross-functionally with Government Affairs, HEOR/Reimbursement Strategy, Private Insurance, Medical, Legal, Finance, and other key stakeholders, the incumbent drives operational excellence, compliance, and continuous improvement while delivering patient-centric solutions at scale.

Reporting to the Senior Director, Market Access & Government Affairs, this position will be filled at the Associate Director or Director level depending on the successful candidate's experience and demonstrated readiness for the full scope of commercial, pharmacy, and GPO responsibilities described below.

Essential Functions Of The Job (Key Responsibilities)

Patient Support Program Leadership (Primary Focus)
Own PSP strategy, performance, and day-to-day program integrity across the oncology/hematology and immunology/dermatology portfolios
Scale and adapt PSPs ahead of anticipated public reimbursement wins and upcoming launches
Set and monitor KPIs for program effectiveness, patient outcomes, and vendor performance; lead vendor selection, onboarding, and governance
Act as Incyte Canada’s internal Quality Assurance (QA) Ambassador for PSP operations — overseeing SOP adherence, supporting inspection readiness, and championing continuous improvement across vendor-delivered programs

Channel Strategy & Innovation

Build a multi-year channel and PSP strategy roadmap aligned to portfolio evolution
Continue to assess and refine the foundational infrastructure (governance, SOPs, vendor framework, KPIs)
Develop and maintain the business case for additional headcount and/or ongoing vendor support as scope is validated; lead hiring/onboarding as resources are approved

Cross-Functional Integration

Partner with Government Affairs, HEOR/Reimbursement Strategy, and the Private Insurance lead to ensure channel, trade, and pharmacy strategy reflects and reinforces active pCPA negotiations, CDA-AMC/INESSS outcomes, and payer strategy
Partner with Medical for Real World Evidence (RWE) generation
Provide a channel/trade lens into pricing and contracting strategy for both in-line and pipeline assets

Financial & Vendor Governance

Own PSP, trade, and channel-related budgets; manage forecasts, variance, and ROI reporting in partnership with Finance
Ensure cost-effective, compliant vendor management across PSP, trade, and GPO/pharmacy relationships, including short-term external vendor/agency engagements where internal capacity is still being built
Trade Relations & Supply Chain (Outsourced Vendor Management)
Own wholesaler and distribution partner relationships and commercial agreements
Negotiate and renew trade terms, ensuring uninterrupted product flow for publicly reimbursed, privately reimbursed, and pCPA-negotiated brands
Serve as the primary point of contact for Supply Chain in Canada; oversee 3PL operations, forecasting, and distribution planning
Where internal capacity is constrained, engage and manage external vendors/agencies to maintain trade and supply chain continuity
Serve as Incyte Canada’s liaison to the Health Products Stewardship Association (HPSA), ensuring compliance with environmental stewardship and product-return obligations tied to the wholesaler and distribution network
Pharmacy Strategy & Group Purchasing Organizations (As Strategic Build-Out)
Develop and execute Incyte Canada's pharmacy channel strategy across retail, specialty, and hospital pharmacy
Build and manage relationships with relevant GPOs and hospital shared-services organizations, prioritized around hospital-administered/infused oncology products and pipeline
Lead GPO and hospital contract negotiations in partnership with Legal and Finance, ensuring alignment with PMPRB pricing rules, the Competition Act, and Incyte's compliance framework
Assess buy-and-bill vs. PSP-mediated distribution models for infused and hospital-administered assets as they approach launch
Coordinate with the Private Insurance lead where pharmacy/specialty network strategy intersects with private payer plan design

Qualifications (Education, Experience & Competencies)

Education & Experience

Bachelor's degree in Life Sciences, Business, or related field; advanced degree an asset
Significant pharmaceutical/biotech experience leading Patient Support Programs at scale
Experience in trade relations, wholesaler management, and Canadian pharmaceutical distribution/supply chain
Experience with pharmacy channel strategy and/or GPO negotiation strongly preferred, ideally including hospital-administered or infused specialty products and buy-and-bill models
Working knowledge of Canadian public (CDA-AMC, INESSS, pCPA, PMPRB) and private reimbursement frameworks
Experience managing external vendors/agencies as an extension of a lean internal team; prior people-leadership experience, or demonstrated readiness to build and lead a team, considered an asset

Core Competencies

Program management rigor, particularly for PSP operations at scale
Commercial negotiation skill, with wholesalers, GPO/hospital counterparts, and vendors
Ability to operate with significant ambiguity, sequence competing priorities, and build structure from a limited existing foundation
Vendor and cross-functional stakeholder management, including managing agency/vendor resources as short-term capacity
Compliance and risk-awareness in a regulated, PMPRB-governed pricing environment
Collaborative mindset — able to identify and act on synergies with adjacent Market Access functions (e.g., Private Insurance)

Additional Requirements

Bilingualism (French and English) considered an asset.

Disclaimer

The above statements describe the general nature and level of work performed and are not intended to be an exhaustive list of all responsibilities, duties, or skills required. Management reserves the right to modify the role as needed.

Résumé du poste (fonction principale)

Le/la directeur(trice) associé(e)/directeur(trice), Accès aux patients et stratégie des canaux, est responsable de la direction stratégique, du développement et de la mise en œuvre de programmes de soutien aux patients (PSP), de relations commerciales, de chaîne d’approvisionnement et de stratégies pharmaceutiques et de canaux de distribution de premier ordre, soutenant le portefeuille d’oncologie/hématologie et d’immunologie/dermatologie d’Incyte Canada.

Ce poste supervise un écosystème complexe comprenant des PSP, des fournisseurs, des grossistes, des partenaires de distribution, des pharmacies et des organismes d’achats groupés (GPO), afin d’assurer un accès fluide des patients aux thérapies innovantes. Le titulaire agit à titre de principal point de contact pour la chaîne d’approvisionnement au Canada, assume le rôle d’ambassadeur de l’assurance qualité (AQ) pour la filiale et représente l’organisation à l’externe auprès de la Health Products Stewardship Association (HPSA).

De plus, le titulaire est responsable de la supervision budgétaire et de la gouvernance financière des activités liées aux PSP, aux relations commerciales et aux canaux de distribution. En collaboration étroite avec les équipes des Affaires gouvernementales, de l’HEOR/Stratégie de remboursement, de l’Assurance privée, des Affaires médicales, des Affaires juridiques, des Finances et d’autres parties prenantes clés, il favorise l’excellence opérationnelle, la conformité réglementaire et l’amélioration continue tout en offrant des solutions axées sur les patients à grande échelle.

Relevant du/de la directeur(trice) principal(e), Accès au marché et Affaires gouvernementales, ce poste sera pourvu au niveau directeur(trice) associé(e) ou directeur(trice), selon l’expérience du/de la candidat(e) retenu(e) et sa capacité démontrée à assumer l’ensemble des responsabilités commerciales, pharmaceutiques et liées aux GPO décrites ci-dessous.

Fonctions essentielles du poste (principales responsabilités)

Leadership des programmes de soutien aux patients (principal domaine d’activité)
Assurer la responsabilité de la stratégie PSP, de la performance et de l’intégrité opérationnelle quotidienne des programmes dans les portefeuilles d’oncologie/hématologie et d’immunologie/dermatologie.
Développer et adapter les PSP en prévision des gains attendus en matière de remboursement public et des lancements à venir.
Définir et suivre les indicateurs clés de performance (KPI) liés à l’efficacité des programmes, aux résultats pour les patients et à la performance des fournisseurs; diriger la sélection, l’intégration et la gouvernance des fournisseurs.
Agir à titre d’ambassadeur interne de l’assurance qualité (AQ) d’Incyte Canada pour les opérations PSP, notamment en supervisant le respect des procédures opérationnelles normalisées (SOP), en soutenant la préparation aux inspections et en favorisant l’amélioration continue des programmes gérés par des fournisseurs.

Stratégie de canaux et innovation

Élaborer une feuille de route pluriannuelle pour les stratégies de canaux et de PSP, alignée sur l’évolution du portefeuille.
Évaluer et optimiser continuellement l’infrastructure de base (gouvernance, SOP, cadre de gestion des fournisseurs, KPI).
Élaborer et maintenir l’analyse de rentabilisation pour l’ajout de ressources internes et/ou le soutien continu de fournisseurs externes à mesure que les besoins sont validés; diriger le recrutement et l’intégration lorsque les ressources sont approuvées.

Intégration interfonctionnelle

Collaborer avec les équipes des Affaires gouvernementales, de l’HEOR/Stratégie de remboursement et de l’Assurance privée afin de garantir que les stratégies de canaux, commerciales et pharmaceutiques reflètent et soutiennent
