About Us

At Baycrest Hospital, older adults receive specialized post-acute inpatient care informed by deep expertise in aging and brain health, delivered with compassion and clinical excellence.

The Finance Department provides financial planning, accounting, financial reporting, budgeting support, regulatory reporting, treasury, and financial management services in support of Baycrest Hospital operations. The department ensures the integrity of financial information, compliance with applicable accounting and reporting requirements, effective stewardship of financial resources, and timely decision support for leaders across the organization.

Job Summary

Reporting to the Vice President, Finance and CFO, the Director, Financial Accounting and Systems Integration works as a partner with the Director, Finance and provides leadership for Baycrest Hospital's financial accounting, reporting, compliance, and financial systems functions.

The Director is responsible for ensuring the integrity, accuracy, and timeliness of financial information through the effective management of accounting operations, financial reporting, accounts payable, accounts receivable, capital accounting, internal controls, regulatory reporting, audit coordination, and compliance activities.

The Director serves as the Finance lead for major technology, systems, and business transformation initiatives impacting financial operations, reporting, controls, data management, and decision support capabilities. Working collaboratively with Information Technology, Human Resources, Payroll, Decision Support, operational leaders, project teams, and external partners, the Director ensures Finance requirements are appropriately incorporated into the planning, design, implementation, integration, testing, and optimization of enterprise systems and related business processes.

The Director works collaboratively with Payroll and Human Resources to support the integrity, governance, integration, reconciliation, reporting, and analysis of workforce-related financial and operational data.

The Director is responsible for the management of assigned staff and works collaboratively with Finance leadership and organizational stakeholders to support operational excellence, continuous improvement, regulatory compliance, and informed decision-making across Baycrest Hospital.

Key Responsibilities

Financial Accounting, Reporting and Compliance

Provides strategic and operational leadership for Baycrest Hospital's financial accounting, reporting, and financial operations functions.
Oversees the integrity, accuracy, completeness, and timeliness of financial information and reporting.
Directs and oversees monthly, quarterly, and annual financial close processes, including account reconciliations, accruals, journal entries, and financial statement preparation.
Oversees the management and reconciliation of the General Ledger and related accounting records.
Ensures financial transactions are recorded and reported in accordance with Generally Accepted Accounting Principles (GAAP), Public Sector Accounting Standards (PSAS), organizational policies, and applicable legislation.
Leads the preparation and review of internal financial statements and supports financial planning processes.
Oversees Accounts Payable, Accounts Receivable, banking, cash management, and assigned financial operations.
Oversees capital accounting, capital project reporting, asset management, deferred contributions, and related funding requirements.
Provides expert advice and guidance to leaders across the organization regarding accounting standards, financial reporting, internal controls, financial policies, and financial risk management.
Supports organizational planning, resource allocation, and operational decision-making through the provision of financial expertise and analysis.

MIS Submissions

Monitors data quality, reporting integrity, and compliance with reporting standards and recommends corrective actions as required.

Internal Controls, Audit and Risk Management

Develops, implements, and maintains financial controls, policies, procedures, and monitoring processes to safeguard organizational assets and ensure financial accountability.
Leads annual external audit activities and serves as the primary liaison with auditors for assigned hospital operations and reporting areas.
Coordinates audit requests and ensures timely completion of audit schedules, supporting documentation, analyses, recommendations, and action plans.
Identifies financial, operational, reporting, compliance, and system-related risks and develops mitigation strategies where appropriate.
Supports organizational risk management initiatives through strong financial oversight, governance, and accountability practices.
Recommends and implements improvements to strengthen financial controls, reporting accuracy, operational effectiveness, and regulatory compliance.

Systems Integration and Business Transformation

Serves as the Finance lead for enterprise systems initiatives, major technology projects, and business transformation efforts impacting financial processes, reporting, controls, and data management.

Ensures financial, accounting, reporting, compliance, control, and data governance requirements are incorporated into enterprise systems and related business processes.

Oversees financial data conversion, integration, validation, and reconciliation activities associated with system implementations and upgrades.
Identifies opportunities to improve business processes through automation, standardization, workflow redesign, and enhanced system functionality.
Supports the development and enhancement of financial reporting, analytics, and decision-support capabilities.
Promotes effective governance, stewardship, integrity, and security of financial and operational data across systems.
Collaborates with Payroll, Human Resources, and operational stakeholders regarding workforce-related financial data integrations, reconciliations, analytics, and reporting requirements.

Leadership and People Management

Provides leadership, coaching, direction, and support to assigned staff.
Fosters a collaborative, accountable, customer-focused, and high-performing work environment.

Oversees workload distribution, performance management, and staff development activities.

Planning and Continuous Improvement

Develops and implements short- and long-term operational plans for assigned areas of responsibility.
Supports organizational strategic priorities through financial leadership, innovation, collaboration, and continuous improvement initiatives.
Identifies opportunities to improve financial processes, compliance activities, reporting capabilities, systems functionality, internal controls, and operational effectiveness.

Organizational and Stakeholder Relations

Quality, Safety and Compliance

jobs.title: Vice President, Finance
jobs.description:
Our client is a long-established, privately held organization operating a multi-site, customer-focused business across retail, wholesale, distribution, logistics and related services. The company has grown significantly and built a strong reputation through operational excellence, long-term relationships and a commitment to continuous improvement. Its culture is highly collaborative, performance-oriented and grounded in servant leadership, with leaders expected to be accountable, approachable and engaged while fostering an environment focused on teamwork, accountability and results.

Reporting to the President and Chief Executive Officer, the Vice President, Finance leads the organization’s Finance and People & Culture functions and serves as a key member of the senior leadership team. This is a highly operational leadership role for a finance executive who takes an active interest in how the business runs and enjoys working directly with leaders and teams across the organization. Leading accounting, financial reporting, budgeting, forecasting, data analysis, credit, cash flow, working capital and financial controls, the Vice President will provide timely and meaningful insight into performance. The role’s financial responsibilities also extend to a related property business that owns most of the organization’s operating locations, together with a small portfolio of other commercial properties.

Working closely with ownership and business leaders, the Vice President will strengthen visibility into sales, margins, expenses, inventory and profitability; enhance planning, reporting and decision support; and help drive greater consistency across financial processes, systems and controls. By engaging directly with the business and developing a firsthand understanding of operational challenges, the Vice President will help translate financial and operational insight into practical improvements in performance.

A key priority will be supporting the continued adoption and optimization of a recently implemented enterprise system, improving the quality and accessibility of financial and operational data, and helping business leaders leverage analytics to make better decisions. The successful candidate will also bring an active interest in artificial intelligence and a commitment to ongoing learning, working with leaders across the organization to identify practical applications that improve productivity, decision-making and business performance.

In addition to leading Finance, the Vice President will provide executive oversight to the People & Culture function. Working closely with the Senior Director, People & Culture, this leader will help ensure the organization’s talent, leadership and organizational capabilities support its strategic and operational priorities. The Vice President will strengthen a capable, service-oriented team across both functions while building the processes and discipline necessary to support future growth.

The ideal candidate is a finance leader with demonstrated success leading accounting and finance functions in a complex, customer-focused business. Experience in retail, wholesale distribution or another operationally complex, inventory-intensive environment would be highly relevant. Collaborative, humble, credible and highly hands-on, this servant leader will be equally comfortable rolling up their sleeves to work through complex issues as they are coaching and developing others. They will bring strong business judgment, intellectual curiosity and a practical problem-solving approach, with the ability to identify root causes, navigate ambiguity and translate analysis into action. Experience with ERP system optimization and enhanced reporting through data analytics will be highly valued.

Based in Metro Vancouver, this is an exceptional opportunity to make a meaningful impact within a respected privately held organization. Working closely with ownership, senior leadership and teams across the business, the successful candidate will build on a solid foundation and help position the company for continued success.

To explore this opportunity further, please submit your resume by clicking ‘apply’.

We thank all applicants for their interest in this position. Please note that we will only be in contact with those individuals moving forward with our client.

jobs.title: Director, Security Architecture
jobs.description:
You are as unique as your background, experience and point of view. Here, you’ll be encouraged, empowered and challenged to be your best self. You'll work with dynamic colleagues \- experts in their fields \- who are eager to share their knowledge with you. Your leaders will inspire and help you reach your potential and soar to new heights. Every day, you'll have new and exciting opportunities to make life brighter for our Clients \- who are at the heart of everything we do.  



  

At Sun Life, we're driven by our Purpose: helping our Clients achieve lifetime financial security and live healthier lives. Our values shape how we work: caring, authentic, bold, inspiring, and impactful.  



  

When you join Sun Life, you'll work with passionate colleagues and empowering leaders who support your growth and celebrate your contributions, so you can make a meaningful difference in our Clients' lives.  



  

Discover how you can make a difference in the lives of individuals, families and communities around the world.  



  

**Job Description:**

**Role Summary**

  

You will represent the Security Architecture team across our enterprise architecture and technology community, shaping how security is designed into everything we build including the AI systems now reaching production.  



  

This is a senior, influence\-led role. You will prioritise the strategic concepts and capability sets that matter most, align security to the architecture process and the NIST framework, and advance technology modernisation and defense\-in\-depth across multiple clouds and on Prem.  



  

You will set direction for a substantial security technology stack including: cloud security posture and workload protection, endpoint detection and response, SIEM, secrets and privileged access management, data protection, application security and perimeter defense and make strategic decisions on the future of the technology stack  



  

**What will you do?**

  

* Partner with global domain architects to review enterprise architecture patterns and guardrails, ensuring security is designed in rather than retrofitted.
* Evaluate and recommend emerging technologies, providing technical and thought leadership through proofs of concept and business cases that demonstrate value.
* Represent security technology and capability strategy at senior executive forums and enterprise technology review boards.
* Provide architecture and design expertise on enterprise projects and security initiatives, including cross\-domain functions, and certify domains in line with architecture governance.
* Lead the strategic evolution of security capabilities with a zero\-trust\-first approach, working alongside delivery teams.
* Define the security architecture for AI adoption covering AI and agentic systems, the data that feeds them, and the platforms that host them. This includes model and agent governance, AI security posture management, data\-classification controls for training and inference, guardrails against prompt injection and model misuse, and secure\-by\-design patterns for AI\-enabled products.
* Set a modernised approach to security tooling, services and capability sets, focused on technical feasibility across emerging technologies, controls and functions.
Drive multi\-cloud consistency, ensuring controls, telemetry and posture management extend uniformly across all cloud providers rather than clustering around the best\-covered one.  
* 

  

**What will you need to succeed?**

  

**Experience**
--------------

* Minimum 7–10 years in information security architecture, engineering and design.
* Proven ability to navigate complex organisations across the security, network, infrastructure and global architecture stack.
* Proven experience migrating and upgrading core security technologies as part of an evolving security and infrastructure stack, including API security, web filtering, cloud security, email security and endpoint security.
Experience managing third\-party security service providers in delivering security services.  
* 

  

**Technical depth**
-------------------

* Strong knowledge of core security domains: endpoint, cloud, infrastructure, perimeter and data protection.
* Multi\-cloud security architecture across at least two major providers, with an appreciation of how native controls and third\-party platforms differ in coverage.
* Working knowledge of the modern security toolset CNAPP/CSPM, EDR/XDR, SIEM, secrets management, privileged access management, SSE/CASB, WAF and perimeter protection, database activity monitoring, and SAST/SCA/DAST in the pipeline.
* AI security: familiarity with AI and LLM threat models (such as the OWASP Top 10 for LLM Applications), AI governance frameworks (such as the NIST AI Risk Management Framework), AI security posture management, model and agent identity, and the data\-security implications of AI adoption.
Pragmatic understanding of security problems as a mix of technology and process, with the ability to pursue solutions at multiple levels throughout the organisation.  
* 

  

**Leadership and communication**
--------------------------------

* Expert presentation and communication skills, written and verbal.
* People leadership experience preferred, including the ability to engage, mentor, coach and develop.
* Extensive knowledge of information security principles, best practices and industry standards.
Self\-starter, strategic thinker, negotiator and consensus builder.  
* 

**Education**

* University degree/college diploma in related discipline(s) or equivalent co\-op work experience,
Professional designation in IT security (such as CISM, CISSP, CISA) preferred  
* 

  

**What's in it for you?**

JOB TITLE:
Director, Finance and Business Intelligence
STATUS:
Permanent, Full Time
LOCATION:
Home Office Based
Candidates are required to reside in the province of Ontario or National Capital Region, maintain a private and safe workspace, and have a high-quality internet connection.
HOURS OF WORK:
35 hours/week (regular office hours)
GRADE:
Grade 11
The hiring range for this position ranges from $166,261.26 to $182,887.39, with the opportunity to grow within the broader salary range as you advance in your role.

About Us

Workplace Safety & Prevention Services (WSPS) is a not-for-profit organization committed to protecting Ontario’s workers and businesses. It serves more than 174,000 member firms and 4.2 million workers across the agricultural, manufacturing and service sectors. A proud partner in the province’s occupational health and safety system and a trusted safety advisor since 1917, WSPS has a rich history of making workplaces safer.

Our focus on healthy workplaces extends to our own strong safety culture. We’re committed to helping employees thrive in a remote-first world, and we’re honoured to be recognized as a Great Place to Work for two consecutive years for 2024 and 2025.

Why Work with WSPS

As a member of our team, you'll benefit from a compensation package aimed at keeping you happy, healthy, motivated and safe. Highlights include:
Make a meaningful impact by supporting our mission to protect Ontario’s workers and businesses
35-hour work week
Flexible working arrangements within the province of Ontario
Comprehensive life and health benefits (100% company paid Health & Dental)
Defined Benefit Pension Plan
Generous vacation and leave entitlements (including paid time off over Christmas and New Year's, paid parental leave benefits)
Internet allowance
And more!

Role

Reporting to the CFO and Vice President, Corporate Services, this position is responsible for the strategic planning, leadership and oversight of the Finance, Accounting and Business Intelligence functions. The Director, Finance and Business Intelligence will work as a member of the Senior Leadership Team (SLT) to support the achievement of the WSPS strategic plan. As future focused leader, this role plays an integral part in formulating best practices and process improvements while leveraging technology and tools for financial planning, accounting services, financial and business reporting.

Responsibilities

Note: Percentages refer to approximate % of time spent on each area, over the course of a given year.
1. TEAM LEADERSHIP, DEVELOPMENT AND ADMINISTRATION (20%)

Provide leadership to Finance, Accounting and Business Intelligence managers. Guide and coach team members to effectively perform and achieve objectives.
Ensure the development of a highly skilled, knowledgeable, and motivated workforce in the team.
Ensure team structures, positions and skills are appropriate for delivery of the team’s and organization’s mandate.
Provide the necessary training, resources, and support to ensure that team members are continually developing and enhancing their capabilities.
Evaluate and lead the team through succession planning to ensure continuity in roles.
Review and analyze engagement results with a focus on solutions to increase employee engagement in satisfaction in the department. Assure strong employee engagement/satisfaction results in the department.
Collaborate with the team to ensure clear understanding and alignment related to changes within the organization.
Reinforces the WSPS vision and employees’ connection to that vision.
Lead multi-disciplinary project teams as needed.
Upholds and promotes ethical standards, integrity, and a strong sense of corporate responsibility as per WSPS policies and procedures.

2. RELATIONSHIP BUILDING (20%)

Develop strong customer and stakeholder relationships with all divisions/business units in the organization to support financial management, business intelligence processes, and continuous improvement efforts at WSPS.
Act as a liaison between WSPS and the Ministry of Labour, Immigration, Training and Skills Development (MLITSD), representing WSPS’ interests while developing collaborative and effective relationships.

3. LEADERSHIP OF ACCOUNTING SERVICE DELIVERY (20%)

Lead the team responsible for the design, implementation, monitoring and evaluation of internal controls to safeguard the assets of WSPS and to mitigate business risks.
Review existing/new/proposed accounting policies to assess adherence to GAAP and well as consider operational impacts.
Oversee the preparation of monthly, quarterly and annual internal and Board of Director financial statements, as well as preparation of annual external financial statements, ensuring the format and disclosure within statements are effective for decision-making, while adhering to GAAP requirements.
Identify areas for improvement in current systems required to comply with TPA reporting requirements and partner with appropriate functional areas to implement improvements.
Participate in TPA audit relating to both financial information provided to the Ministry and reporting of performance indicators.
Ensure effectiveness and efficiency of internal monitoring processes that assess accounting transactions for validity, completeness, accuracy and adherence to all government directives and WSPS policies to minimize risk of loss.
Ensure procurement policies and procedures comply with government directives.
Ensure consistent training and advice on procurement activities are communicated across the organization, including monitoring of emerging requirements as mandated by government for implementation and compliance.
Act as liaison with government agencies on procurement reporting requirements.
Participate in the design and management of an investment strategy to achieve strategic and financial goals of WSPS, including meeting cash flow requirements, while adhering to parameters set by government directives and internal policies.

4. LEADERSHIP OF BUDGETING, FINANCIAL REPORTING AND AUDIT PROCESS (20%)

Ensure the implementation of an accurate, efficient, and timely annual budget process and provide leadership to the organization in the preparation of an annual budget that adheres to ministry requirements.
Serve as liaison between WSPS and the Ministry for financial planning and Transfer Payment Agreement (TPA) reporting related matters.
Provide guidance to the executive and senior leadership teams during the budgeting process to achieve a balanced budget.
Ensure the implementation of an accurate, efficient, and timely forecasting process, including reporting to senior management in support of effective decision-making.
Oversee the preparation of forecast and spending reports, ensuring they are effective in communicating the organization’s financial position, highlighting any areas of risk, and recommending mitigation strategies.
Provide advice and develop recommendations on financial management practices across the organization.
Oversee monthly and quarterly variance analysis and develop recommendations for achieving a balanced budget at year-end.
Oversee analysis and develop recommendations on sales, contribution margins and pricing strategies.
Lead development of Ministry reporting packages, including annual business plan and quarterly reports, ensuring they meet all requirements.
Work closely with the external actuary in the annual employee future benefits valuation process to ensure accurate data is reflected in the valuation results and the reports are available for year-end audit and budgeting purposes.
Oversee the team leading the audit preparation process to ensure audit process and procedures performed are effective and efficient and to identify areas where documents/procedures can be updated to facilitate a more efficient audit process.
At year end audit, ensure appropriate documentation/supporting documents are available for auditor’s review and act as liaison between auditor and other WSPS departments where ownership of supporting information/documents does not lie within Corporate Services.

jobs.description:
About UJA Federation Of Greater Toronto

At UJA Federation of Greater Toronto, our vision is to lead the most vibrant Jewish community in North America — a community characterized by its diversity, unity, compassion, generosity and commitment to Jewish values. Together with our philanthropic, volunteer and professional leadership, we're changing lives.

As one of North America's leading Jewish non-profits, UJA Federation of Greater Toronto works to preserve and strengthen the quality of Jewish life in Greater Toronto, Canada, Israel and around the world. UJA advances this mission through fundraising, planning, and research focused on our strategic pillars: fighting poverty and improving well-being, growing Jewish education and identity, countering antisemitism and hate, and strengthening connections with Israel and Jewish communities worldwide.

About The Opportunity

At a pivotal time for UJA Federation of Greater Toronto, the Chief Financial Officer serves as a strategic partner to the President & CEO, Chief Operating Officer, Board, and senior leadership team. Building on a stable financial foundation and a capable finance team, the CFO is responsible for advancing finance into a forward-looking enterprise function focused on planning, resource allocation, decision support, organizational performance, and long-term financial sustainability. Initially, the CFO will work closely with the existing team to understand how work is currently performed, strengthen accountability and capability, and create the foundation for a more scalable and strategic finance function. The role exists to ensure that financial insight, forecasting, scenario analysis, performance measurement, and resource allocation effectively support organizational priorities and decision-making. The CFO will develop trusted relationships across professional leadership, Board and committee members, lay leaders, donors, partner agencies, and other key stakeholders, while leading improvements in analytics, systems, data, and processes that strengthen organizational effectiveness and scalability. Success in this role will depend on sound judgment, strong relationships, and the ability to build alignment across a complex stakeholder environment.

Responsibilities include, but are not limited to:

Lead the Finance function across UJA entities and operating activities, with accountability for financial stewardship, planning, reporting, controls and team performance.
Own and lead the annual budget process and strengthen multi-year planning, forecasting and scenario analysis, aligning financial plans with strategic priorities.
Lead resource allocation, reserve strategy and long-term sustainability planning, helping leadership assess competing priorities and strengthen UJA's financial resilience.
Oversee investments and organizational assets, working with relevant Board committees and advisors to ensure sound governance, risk management and long-term stewardship.
Lead financial reporting and discussions with the Board and relevant committees, providing clear context, insight and recommendations to support decision-making.
Oversee the annual audit, internal controls, governance and compliance with internal requirements and external obligations, including CRA requirements.
Ensure financial or other risks are appropriately identified, understood and addressed.
Lead, mentor and develop the finance team, establishing clear accountabilities, succession depth and a culture of ownership and continuous improvement.
Champion systems, data and process improvements and strengthen financial acumen across the organization.

Qualifications:

CPA designation.
Senior financial leadership experience, ideally as a CFO or equivalent, within a complex organization with multiple stakeholders and competing priorities.
Demonstrated success as a strategic partner to a CEO, senior leadership team and Board, with the judgment to influence effectively without relying solely on formal authority.
Proven ability to succeed in a consensus-driven environment and build alignment across stakeholders with differing perspectives and priorities.
Board experience is highly valued, particularly with philanthropic or community organizations that combine fundraising with meaningful operating activities.
Track record of developing high-performance finance teams, developing leaders and leading thoughtful organizational change without creating unnecessary disruption.
Strong governance, investment oversight, risk and analytical capabilities, with the ability to translate financial information into clear implications and choices for non-financial stakeholders.
Strategic in orientation while sufficiently hands-on to understand the function, people and processes during a period of transition and evolution.
Passion for UJA’s mission and an appreciation for the complexity of serving a broad and highly engaged community.
This is a full-time position. This posting complies with applicable Ontario employment legislation regarding compensation disclosure requirements.

UJA supports a flexible work schedule and all of our employees engage in hybrid work. Engagement and connection are key to supporting the best employee experience and we want to ensure that this puts balance and well-being at the forefront of our approach to ways of working. In addition to a rich time off policy, UJA's offices are closed on all Jewish holy days (yom tov) and we support early office closures to observe the Jewish Sabbath (Shabbat).

Qualified applicants are invited to submit a cover letter and resume. Only those applicants invited for interview will be contacted. Please be advised that all offers of employment are contingent upon the successful completion of professional references and background checks including Social Media Account(s) and a Police Records Check/Vulnerable Sector Screening.

Commitment to Inclusion and Accessibility:

UJA Federation supports a diverse candidate and employment experience. We are proud of our dynamic professional team, which reflects the diversity of the Jewish community and general community alike in Greater Toronto. We are an equal opportunity employer and welcome applicants from all communities. We encourage you to follow us to get regular updates on open roles. We are committed to creating an inclusive and accessible workplace and believe this is essential to ensure that every member of our team can thrive.

We adhere to barrier-free and accessible employment practices in compliance with the Accessibility for Ontarians with Disabilities Act (AODA). Should you require Code-protected accommodation through any stage of the recruitment process, please notify us and we will work with you to meet your needs.

jobs.title: Interim Director, Financial Planning & Analysis
jobs.description:
IMMEDIATE INTERIM OPPORTUNITY

Interim Director, Financial Planning & Analysis (FP&A)

Duration: 3 Months

Reports: Chief Financial Officer

Location: Downtown Toronto (Hybrid)

Our client a North American professional services organization with multiple locations is seeking an experienced financial planning & analysis professional to lead a small team through a critical budgeting process. This individual will play a key role in guiding the organization through a complex budgeting and forecasting cycle while bringing greater structure, discipline, and insight to the overall financial planning process.

This is a highly hands-on assignment requiring an individual who is comfortable working directly in the details, partnering closely with operational and finance stakeholders, and supporting a team through a demanding planning period. The successful candidate will be equally comfortable rolling up their sleeves in Excel while providing strategic recommendations on process improvement, automation, and future-state planning capabilities.

Key Mandate

The Interim Director will be responsible for stabilizing, coordinating, and enhancing the organization's budgeting and forecasting processes while identifying opportunities to simplify workflows, improve data quality, and introduce practical technology solutions.

Key Responsibilities

Lead and manage the organization's annual budgeting and forecasting process.
Provide day-to-day leadership, coaching, and support to a team of four FP&A professionals.
Work directly with budget owners and operational leaders to develop, validate, and challenge assumptions.
Consolidate and analyze budget submissions, identifying risks, opportunities, and variances.
Develop financial models and scenario analyses to support decision-making.
Ensure budget timelines, milestones, and deliverables are achieved.
Perform detailed hands-on analysis and modelling within a largely Excel-based environment.
Improve the consistency, accuracy, and transparency of financial reporting and forecasting.
Identify process bottlenecks and inefficiencies within the current budgeting framework.
Recommend practical opportunities for automation, simplification, and technology enablement.
Partner with senior leadership to provide meaningful insights into financial performance and future outlook.
Support the development of a roadmap for a more scalable and sustainable FP&A function.

Desired Experience

10+ years of progressive finance, FP&A, and business planning experience.
Previous experience serving as an Interim Director, FP&A Director, Finance Director, or equivalent senior finance leadership role.
Demonstrated success leading large-scale budgeting and forecasting cycles in complex organizations.
Strong people leadership experience with the ability to motivate and develop teams during periods of change.
Advanced Excel modelling skills and experience working in less structured finance environments.
Proven ability to create structure and discipline in processes that have evolved organically over time.
Experience implementing reporting, planning, or performance management improvements.
Exposure to budgeting and forecasting technologies, FP&A platforms, Power BI, automation tools, or similar solutions is considered an asset.
Strong communication and stakeholder management capabilities.

Ideal Candidate Profile

The ideal candidate is not a pure strategist nor a pure analyst. They are a pragmatic finance leader who can quickly earn credibility, work collaboratively with the existing team, and balance immediate execution with longer-term process improvements.

They bring experience navigating ambiguity, are comfortable operating in Excel-based planning environments, and have a track record of introducing practical innovations that improve efficiency, accuracy, and decision-making without overcomplicating processes.

Expected Outcomes After 90 Days

Successful completion of the budgeting and forecasting cycle.
Improved forecasting accuracy and reporting consistency.
Enhanced structure, accountability, and governance within the planning process.
Increased confidence among stakeholders in financial plans and assumptions.
Identification of practical automation and technology opportunities.
Clear recommendations for future-state FP&A processes and tools to support scalability and improved decision-making.

jobs.title: Director of Information Technology
jobs.description:
POSITION DESCRIPTION

Athletica Sport Systems Inc. is a global leader in the design, manufacturing, and installation of dasher board and arena systems, and the Preferred Rink Equipment Supplier of the NHL® and AHL®. Guided by our philosophy of “Safety through Innovation,” we have completed more than 3,000 projects worldwide from our headquarters in Waterloo, Ontario and operations in Minneapolis, London, and Vancouver.

Athletica is seeking a Director of Information Technology to join our leadership team in Waterloo. Reporting to the Chief Financial Officer, this role owns technology, systems, and data across Athletica and its operating entities, supporting daily operations, organic growth, and acquisitions. The successful candidate will build and lead a growing IT team, stay hands-on while it matures, and lead the clean-up and cloud migration of our Epicor ERP, the technology side of a move to a new facility within 18 months of hire, and completion of our Microsoft Dynamics CRM implementation.

Key Responsibilities

Strategy and budget: Translate business strategy into a sequenced technology roadmap with the CFO and leadership team, and manage the IT operating and capital budget, licensing, and vendor contracts.
Team: Staff, structure, and develop the IT team to meet business needs, using skills assessments to set hiring and training priorities and to engage outside partners. Stay hands-on while the team matures.
Epicor improvement: Own Epicor Kinetic end to end. Lead the clean-up and improvement of the existing implementation, including workflows, customizations, reports, and data quality, and standardize setups across entities.
Epicor platform: Keep Epicor current and supported, and lead the planned move from on-premises to Epicor in the cloud.
Epicor expertise: Build and train the IT team toward deep Epicor expertise and act as the conduit to outside specialists, including Six S Partners, reviewing designs, testing deliverables, and approving releases.
Manufacturing modernization: Keep operations on efficient, effective tools. Work with Operations, Engineering, and Projects to implement Epicor capabilities and technology such as barcode scanning, shop floor data collection, and mobile tools, and support Finance, which owns costing, with reliable system data.
Security & controls: Maintain role-based security in Epicor and other core systems, enforce segregation of duties and change management, and support financial controls and audits. Build a practical cybersecurity program covering multifactor authentication, endpoint protection, backup and recovery testing, and incident response.
Microsoft 365 & infrastructure: Own the Microsoft 365 environment and set direction for infrastructure and security, including which workloads stay on-premises and which move to the cloud.
Facility transition: Plan and lead the technology side of the move to the new facility, including network, telephony, shop floor connectivity, and cutover planning that limits disruption to production, installs, and shipping. Lead the expected Microsoft tenant reorganization, and sequence it with the Epicor upgrade and cloud migration.
CRM: Own Microsoft Dynamics CRM. Complete the partial implementation with sales, service, and finance leaders, fix data quality, simplify workflows, and integrate with Epicor and Microsoft 365.
Projects & platforms: Determine what project management capability Epicor and Dynamics already provide before recommending new platforms, and replace ad hoc spreadsheets and email processes with system workflows the business adopts.
Data, reporting & AI: Establish data ownership and standards, and set the reporting approach, including Power BI dashboards for bookings, backlog, margin, labor, capacity, and installs. Lead AI tool use, with Claude as the primary tool and Microsoft Copilot in limited use, within the company AI usage policy, and deploy a few high-value analytics and AI use cases.
M&A integration: Own the systems workstream for acquisitions, from diligence through integration, using a repeatable playbook for data migration, access setup, and process standardization.
Executive partnership: Translate how work happens across the business into system configurations, lead rollouts with training and post-go-live support, and represent technology with the board, banks, investors, and senior leadership.
Other duties as required

POSITION REQUIREMENTS

Education & Certifications:
·      Bachelor's degree in Information Systems, Computer Science, Engineering, or a related field, or equivalent experience.
·      Certifications such as PMP, ITIL, CISSP, Microsoft, or Epicor are an asset.

Knowledge, Experience, and/or Technical Skills:
·      10+ years of progressive IT experience, including 5+ years leading an IT team in a manufacturing environment (required).
·      Hands-on experience with Epicor or another full-featured manufacturing ERP, including upgrades and role-based security design (required). Entry-level accounting packages do not qualify.
·      Experience with Epicor Kinetic, including on-premises to cloud migration, is a strong asset.
·      Working knowledge of manufacturing and financial processes, from bills of materials and routings to inventory, work in process, and the general ledger (required).
·      Microsoft 365 administration experience, including a tenant reorganization or migration (required).
·      Working knowledge of Microsoft Dynamics CRM, Power BI, and SQL.
·      Knowledge of IT general controls and cybersecurity practices, with experience supporting financial audits.
·      Experience delivering major technology projects, such as an ERP upgrade or facility move, with limited disruption to operations.
·      Proven ability to lead and develop a junior team, hire for skill gaps, manage vendors, and explain technical matters to business leaders.
·      Experience with multi-entity environments, acquisition integration, and applying AI tools is an asset.

Work Environment, Hours & Travel:
·      This role is based on-site at our Waterloo, Ontario facility, with occasional remote work at the discretion of the Chief Financial Officer.
·      Occasional travel is required to support other business units (Minneapolis, MN; London, ON; Vancouver, BC).
·      Standard full-time office hours, Monday to Friday, with flexibility for after-hours work during upgrades, cutovers, the facility move, and urgent incidents.
·      Some time on the production floor should be expected.

Compensation & Benefits:
·      Annual salary range: $120,000 to $150,000 CAD, commensurate with experience and qualifications.
·      Full-time, permanent position with eligibility to participate in Athletica's benefits program.
·      Opportunity to lead technology modernization at a global market leader.

jobs.title: Director Data Platform Governance
jobs.description:
Director Data Platform Governance
Toronto, Canada (Hybrid)
Full Time

Position Overview
The Director of Data Platform Governance is responsible for establishing, operating, and continuously improving the Digital Technology governance capabilities that ensure Enterprise Data Platform and related governance tooling ecosystem are controlled, integrated, secure, scalable, traceable, and fit for enterprise use. This includes platform governance standards, certified EDP table usage, metadata, catalog, lineage, data quality monitoring, lifecycle controls, automation, bots, agents, and other tools and services that support governed data creation, certification, publication, and consumption.
The role provides DT leadership for the technical enablement, enterprise integration, architecture and security alignment, platform controls, and operational reliability of this tooling ecosystem. SimpleMDG is a key Data Governance capability sitting on top of SAP, and the Director ensures it is integrated and governed consistently with EDP, SAP, downstream platforms, and other governance-enabling tools across the enterprise technology landscape. The Director also works closely with Technology Architects to ensure proper data flow, lineage, traceability, and integration patterns across the Enterprise Data Platform.
The Director works in close alignment with Business Transformation Data Governance through a shared agenda, agreed priorities, and clear ownership boundaries. Business Transformation Data Governance and business data owners remain accountable for business definitions, semantic layer, approval workflow design, mandatory business rules, reference data certification, stewardship logic, and business adoption, while DT ensures those decisions can be embedded consistently across platforms, workflows, tools, certified data assets, data products, and consumption layers.

Key Responsibilities

1. Enterprise Data Platform Governance and Certified Data Consumption
Establish, operate, and continuously improve DT governance standards for the Enterprise Data Platform, ensuring that data products are created and consumed using certified EDP tables where available.
Define platform-level controls, metadata, lineage, traceability, catalog, and data product governance expectations for EDP assets and consumption layers.
Partner with Business Data Governance and DT delivery teams to embed certified data consumption, lineage, controls, and governance checkpoints into delivery standards and ways of working.
Work with Technology Architects to ensure proper data flow, integration patterns, certified consumption paths, lineage, and traceability across the Enterprise Data Platform.
2. Governance Tooling Ecosystem Enablement
Provide DT leadership for the implementation, integration, controls, security, scalability, and operational reliability of the governance tooling ecosystem, including SimpleMDG, metadata and catalog solutions, lineage tools, data quality monitoring, automation, bots, agents, and related platform services.
Ensure governance tools are connected appropriately across SAP, EDP, downstream platforms, workflows, and consumption layers so that business-approved governance decisions can be executed consistently.
Maintain clear ownership boundaries by enabling business-led configuration decisions while ensuring the technical design, integration, access, auditability, and sustainability of the tools.
3. Master Data Platform Enablement and Enterprise Integration
Support business-led master data governance model by ensuring master data capabilities are technically enabled, integrated, secure, scalable, and aligned with enterprise architecture and data platform standards.
Ensure governed and certified master data can be integrated, exposed, monitored, and consumed appropriately across SAP, SimpleMDG, EDP, downstream enterprise applications, and certified data products.
Maintain lineage, traceability, metadata, issue visibility, platform controls, and certified consumption paths for master data from source systems through EDP and downstream usage.
4. Data Quality Monitoring, Controls, and Issue Visibility
Enable data quality monitoring, profiling, dashboards, scorecards, preventative controls, and issue visibility across EDP and related governance tooling.
Ensure business-defined rules, thresholds, and quality expectations can be technically implemented, measured, and monitored across platforms and consumption layers.
Partner with BT Data Governance, business stewards, Data Product Owners, and DT teams to support root-cause analysis, remediation tracking, and continuous improvement of data quality controls.
5. Metadata, Catalog, Lineage, and Data Intelligence
Establish and operate technical metadata, catalog, lineage, discovery, classification, and transparency capabilities for EDP and related data assets.
Ensure BT-owned business definitions, glossary content, critical data elements, and certification decisions are made visible and usable through platform tools, catalogs, workflows, and data products.
Work with Technology Architects and EDP teams to maintain end-to-end lineage and traceability from source systems through certified EDP tables, data products, and consumption layers.
6. Data Lifecycle, Archiving Governance, Retention, and Platform Compliance Controls
Operate technical lifecycle, data archiving governance, retention, archival, disposition, and compliance controls for EDP and related data platforms in alignment with enterprise policy, legal, regulatory, audit, and information governance requirements.
Ensure enterprise data remains manageable, controlled, compliant, traceable, and cost-efficient throughout its lifecycle, including active use, retention, archiving, and disposition across platform and consumption layers.

Required Qualifications
• Bachelor's degree in Information Systems, Computer Science, Business, Supply Chain, or related discipline.
• 12+ years of progressive experience in Data Management, Data Platforms, Master Data Management, or Enterprise Information Management
• 5+ years leading data platform or MDM organizations.
• Strong expertise in SAP Master Data structures and business processes.
• Hands-on experience implementing and operating SAP MDG and/or SimpleMDG.
• Experience leading enterprise data quality initiatives.
• Experience enabling governance operating models and stewardship programs through platform capabilities
• Strong understanding of ERP transformation programs.
• Experience managing enterprise-scale cross-functional initiatives.

Preferred Qualifications
The ideal candidate demonstrates strong expertise in:

• Enterprise Data Platform governance, including certified data assets, governed consumption layers, platform standards, controls, and auditability.
• Data product and certified consumption governance, including ownership visibility, certification practices, guardrails, and governance checkpoints across data products and analytics use cases.
• Metadata, catalog, lineage, and data intelligence capabilities, including traceability, classification, discovery, and transparency across source systems, EDP, data products, and consumption layers.
• Data quality monitoring and control frameworks, including profiling, dashboards, scorecards, preventative controls, issue visibility, and remediation tracking.
• SAP, SimpleMDG/SAP MDG, and master data platform enablement, including integration across SAP, EDP, enterprise applications, analytics platforms, and downstream consumption layers.
• Enterprise integration and lifecycle governance, including source-to-consumption data flows, integration patterns, retention, archiving, compliance, and platform controls.
• Governance-enabling tooling and enterprise transformation, including workflow automation, bots, agents, metadata/catalog tools, lineage tools, data quality platforms, ERP transformation, and enterprise-scale data platform change.
• Critical enterprise data domains and operating models, including supply chain, customer, commercial, and other core data domains, with clear distinction between business-owned governance decisions and DT-owned platform enablement.

The successful candidate will demonstrate:

• Pragmatic execution, solves complex business and data problems and turns governance concepts into measurable results.
• Business process orientation, understands how trusted data supports operational execution, performance, analytics, and decision-making.
• Enterprise mindset, connects platform governance, certified data consumption, and data quality to business outcomes and transformation priorities.
• Influential leadership, builds alignment across Business Transformation, Digital Technology, Data Product Owners, architects, and senior stakeholders.
• Change and adoption focus, drives practical adoption of governance standards, platform controls, tooling, and ways of working.
• Continuous improvement discipline, improves data quality, platform reliability, governance effectiveness, and operational efficiency.

You are as unique as your background, experience and point of view. Here, you’ll be encouraged, empowered and challenged to be your best self. You'll work with dynamic colleagues - experts in their fields - who are eager to share their knowledge with you. Your leaders will inspire and help you reach your potential and soar to new heights. When you join Sun Life, you'll work with passionate colleagues and empowering leaders who support your growth and celebrate your contributions, so you can make a meaningful difference in our Clients' lives.

Job Description:

Role Summary

You will represent the Security Architecture team across our enterprise architecture and technology community, shaping how security is designed into everything we build including the AI systems now reaching production.

This is a senior, influence-led role. You will prioritise the strategic concepts and capability sets that matter most, align security to the architecture process and the NIST framework, and advance technology modernisation and defense-in-depth across multiple clouds and on Prem.

You will set direction for a substantial security technology stack including: cloud security posture and workload protection, endpoint detection and response, SIEM, secrets and privileged access management, data protection, application security and perimeter defense and make strategic decisions on the future of the technology stack

What will you do?

Partner with global domain architects to review enterprise architecture patterns and guardrails, ensuring security is designed in rather than retrofitted.
Evaluate and recommend emerging technologies, providing technical and thought leadership through proofs of concept and business cases that demonstrate value.
Represent security technology and capability strategy at senior executive forums and enterprise technology review boards.
Provide architecture and design expertise on enterprise projects and security initiatives, including cross-domain functions, and certify domains in line with architecture governance.
Lead the strategic evolution of security capabilities with a zero-trust-first approach, working alongside delivery teams.
Define the security architecture for AI adoption covering AI and agentic systems, the data that feeds them, and the platforms that host them. This includes model and agent governance, AI security posture management, data-classification controls for training and inference, guardrails against prompt injection and model misuse, and secure-by-design patterns for AI-enabled products.
Set a modernised approach to security tooling, services and capability sets, focused on technical feasibility across emerging technologies, controls and functions.
Drive multi-cloud consistency, ensuring controls, telemetry and posture management extend uniformly across all cloud providers rather than clustering around the best-covered one.

What will you need to succeed?

Experience

Minimum 7–10 years in information security architecture, engineering and design.
Proven ability to navigate complex organisations across the security, network, infrastructure and global architecture stack.
Proven experience migrating and upgrading core security technologies as part of an evolving security and infrastructure stack, including API security, web filtering, cloud security, email security and endpoint security.
Experience managing third-party security service providers in delivering security services.

Technical depth

Strong knowledge of core security domains: endpoint, cloud, infrastructure, perimeter and data protection.
Multi-cloud security architecture across at least two major providers, with an appreciation of how native controls and third-party platforms differ in coverage.
Working knowledge of the modern security toolset CNAPP/CSPM, EDR/XDR, SIEM, secrets management, privileged access management, SSE/CASB, WAF and perimeter protection, database activity monitoring, and SAST/SCA/DAST in the pipeline.
AI security: familiarity with AI and LLM threat models (such as the OWASP Top 10 for LLM Applications), AI governance frameworks (such as the NIST AI Risk Management Framework), AI security posture management, model and agent identity, and the data-security implications of AI adoption.
Pragmatic understanding of security problems as a mix of technology and process, with the ability to pursue solutions at multiple levels throughout the organisation.

Leadership and communication

Expert presentation and communication skills, written and verbal.
People leadership experience preferred, including the ability to engage, mentor, coach and develop.
Extensive knowledge of information security principles, best practices and industry standards.
Self-starter, strategic thinker, negotiator and consensus builder.

Education

University degree/college diploma in related discipline(s) or equivalent co-op work experience,
Professional designation in IT security (such as CISM, CISSP, CISA) preferred

What's in it for you?

A competitive salary and bonus program, based on market scale
A flexible group insurance program starting on your first day of work to meet your needs and those of your family.
Time off that allows you to focus on the moments that matter most. 20 vacation days per year.

An Overview Of This Role

As Director, Analytics Engineering, you'll lead a team of 8 and report to the VP of Data & Insights. You set direction across the data organization, stay close enough to the work to guide technical decisions credibly, and partner with Data Engineering, Data Science, IT, and business leaders.

You Will Have Three Mandates

Build trusted, AI-ready self-service. Deliver a semantic model that answers business questions correctly, with the telemetry, evals, and model flexibility to prove it and keep costs in check.

Build evals and ground-truth datasets that measure answer quality, and use them to drive improvements and catch regressions
Instrument telemetry to see who uses the semantic model and AI tools, what they ask, and where they get stuck
Build a model-selection harness so GitLab can route work across LLMs and stay flexible on cost and quality
Own data modeling and curated datasets for self-service, with the ownership, data contracts, testing, and documentation that make them AI-ready
Define the AI data access strategy: when to use BI, Claude, MCP servers, or Slack agents, with the governance and security to keep access trusted and reliable
Own the enterprise BI and self-service tools strategy (e.g., Tableau, Omni), including evaluation, adoption, and cost
Build self-service capabilities, such as Claude skills, documentation, and guided workflows, that help people find and use data on their own
Build and own company-wide data applications, from Claude-built single-page apps to apps inside BI tools, that combine Snowflake data, API calls, AI-powered deep dives, and write-back to Postgres or Snowflake
Set engineering standards for data apps (security, authentication, testing, deployment, and monitoring) so they're reliable at company scale
Set a long-range roadmap tied to company strategy, and a lightweight operating model that balances urgent stakeholder needs with investment in reusable data products and tech-debt reduction
Hire, coach, and retain a high-performing team of 8: build career paths, develop leaders, distribute ownership, and recognize great work
Act as customer zero for GitLab and GitLab Duo in data workflows, sharing feedback with Product and Engineering

What You'll Bring

12+ years in analytics engineering, data engineering, or BI, including 5+ years leading teams and 2+ years managing managers or senior leads
Deep expertise in data modeling and semantic layers (e.g., dbt Semantic Layer, Snowflake semantic views, LookML, Cube), and expert dbt, including testing and CI/CD across a multi-team project
Hands-on experience building LLM-powered data access (text-to-SQL, agents, MCP servers), including evals and telemetry for answer quality, and advanced use of AI coding agents such as Claude Code
Expert SQL and strong Snowflake experience; working knowledge of Python
Strong data governance experience: data quality, lineage, certified datasets, and access controls (RBAC, row access and masking policies)
Track record of leading cross-functional data initiatives from strategy through adoption and measurable business impact, including enterprise BI and self-service at scale
Systems thinker who sees how models, pipelines, and architecture decisions connect, and designs for second-order effects
Exceptional communicator who writes clear technical specs, sets a clear vision, makes trade-offs visible, and influences executives and peers across the company
Pragmatic in ambiguity: makes sound decisions on emerging technology and ships the right next version rather than waiting for the ideal end state
Able to use GitLab, thrive in an all-remote, asynchronous company, model GitLab's remote working competencies, and work in line with GitLab's values

Nice to Have

Experience with LLM routing or gateway tools and managing model costs
Experience with Tableau, Omni, or a BI platform migration
Experience with web app development (e.g., React, TypeScript) and Postgres
Experience owning finance or revenue-critical data (e.g., ARR, consumption) where accuracy and auditability are non-negotiable

About The Team

Analytics Engineering makes GitLab's data trusted, easy to find, and ready for anyone to use, whether they ask a dashboard, Claude, or a Slack agent. We own the curated data models, the semantic layer, the self-service tools, and the data applications that let teams answer their own questions.

AI is changing how people get to data. Questions that once went through an analyst now go straight to AI tools, so the answers are only as good as the data models and business definitions behind them. Our job is to make those answers correct, consistent, and measurable.

jobs.description:
At Equitable, we believe work should be a place where you feel supported, inspired, and empowered to grow. In our caring and collaborative environment, your curiosity is encouraged, your passion is recognized, and your contributions truly matter. Together, we create meaningful impact, for our clients, our communities, and each other.

The Opportunity:
  At Equitable, we believe great things happen when we work together. We’re a Canadian mutual company driven by purpose - putting people first and helping Canadians protect today and prepare for tomorrow. If you’re passionate about making a difference and growing your career in an inclusive and collaborative environment, we’d love to hear from you.

Our culture is built on care, passion and curiosity. We put people above all else, strive to be our best and welcome new ideas to deliver positive outcomes.

As Director, Enterprise Third-Party Management, you will lead the development and oversight of Equitable’s enterprise-wide third-party management framework, ensuring third-party relationships deliver value, support strategic objectives, and operate within the Company's risk appetite and regulatory requirements. In this highly visible leadership role, you will oversee third-party governance, procurement, vendor management, and cost optimization initiatives while ensuring compliance with OSFI Guideline B-10 and other applicable regulations. Working closely with senior leaders across the organization, you will provide expert guidance on third-party strategy, risk management, commercial relationships, and operational resilience. You will also lead a high-performing team and help strengthen Equitable’s ability to manage third-party risk while driving business performance and operational efficiency.

Join one of the region’s top employers and be part of something that truly makes a difference.

Work Arrangements:
This is a hybrid role. You will work in our office in Waterloo, ON a minimum of two (2) assigned, consecutive days every other week, plus a fifth (5th) assigned day per month. You are welcome to work from the office more than the minimum requirement and there may be some roles that are required to work in our office more than the minimum requirement.

What you’ll do:

Develop, implement, and continuously enhance Equitable’s Third-Party Risk Management program, ensuring compliance with OSFI Guideline B-10 and other applicable regulatory requirements
Establish and maintain enterprise-wide standards for third-party due diligence, onboarding, risk assessment, oversight, performance monitoring, and termination processes
Provide oversight and effective challenge for significant third-party relationships across the organization, including MGAs, reinsurers, and vendors
Monitor emerging third-party risks, industry trends, and regulatory developments, recommending program enhancements to strengthen governance and risk management practices
Deliver regular reporting and insights to senior management and governance committees on third-party risks, program effectiveness, and key performance indicators
Lead procurement and vendor management activities, including strategic sourcing, supplier selection, contract negotiation, vendor governance, and supplier performance management
Drive enterprise vendor cost management initiatives focused on spend visibility, contract optimization, value realization, service quality, and operational efficiency
Lead and develop a high-performing team while partnering with Risk, Legal, Compliance, Finance, Information Security, Privacy, and business leaders to support strategic initiatives, outsourcing arrangements, and business transformation programs

What you’ll bring:

University degree in Business, Finance, Risk Management, Supply Chain Management, Commerce, Law, or a related field
10+ years of progressive leadership experience in third-party risk management, procurement, vendor management, operational risk, or a related discipline
Experience working within financial services, insurance, or another highly regulated industry
Strong knowledge of third-party risk management principles, governance frameworks, and regulatory expectations, including OSFI Guideline B-10
Demonstrated success leading procurement, strategic sourcing, supplier governance, contract management, and vendor performance programs
Proven ability to negotiate complex commercial agreements and deliver measurable cost optimization and value realization initiatives
Exceptional leadership, stakeholder management, communication, analytical, and problem-solving skills, with the ability to influence and collaborate across multiple business functions
Professional designation such as CPA, CFA, PMP, SCMP, or an equivalent credential is considered an asset, along with experience identifying, monitoring, and managing operational risks through effective controls, assessments, and testing

What’s in it for you:

Career Growth: Regular learning sessions and development opportunities 
Total Rewards: Incentive pay, annual salary reviews, employer-paid benefits and pension matching 
Time Away: Competitive vacation plus one paid volunteer day each year

jobs.description:
Who We Are Is What We Do.

Deel is the all-in-one payroll and HR platform for global teams. Our vision is to unlock global opportunity for every person, team, and business. Built for the way the world works today, Deel combines HRIS, payroll, compliance, benefits, performance, and equipment management into one seamless platform. With AI-powered tools and a fully owned payroll infrastructure, Deel supports every worker type in 150+ countries—helping businesses scale smarter, faster, and more compliantly.

Among the largest globally distributed companies in the world, our team of 7,000 spans more than 100 countries, speaks 74 languages, and brings a connected and dynamic culture that drives continuous learning and innovation for our customers.

Why should you be part of our success story?

As the fastest-growing Software as a Service (SaaS) company in history, Deel is transforming how global talent connects with world-class companies – breaking down borders that have traditionally limited both hiring and career opportunities. We're not just building software; we're creating the infrastructure for the future of work, enabling a more diverse and inclusive global economy. In 2024 alone, we paid $11.2 billion to workers in nearly 100 currencies and provided healthcare and benefits to workers in 109 countries—ensuring people get paid and protected, no matter where they are.

Our momentum is reflected in our achievements and customer satisfaction: CNBC Disruptor 50, Forbes Cloud 100, Deloitte Fast 500, and repeated recognition on Y Combinator's top companies list – all while maintaining a 4.83 average rating from 15,000 reviews across G2, Trustpilot, Captera, Apple and Google.

Your experience at Deel will be a career accelerator. At the forefront of the global work revolution, you'll tackle complex challenges that impact millions of people's working lives. With our momentum—backed by a $17.3 billion valuation and $1 B in Annual Recurring Revenue (ARR) in just over five years—you'll drive meaningful impact while building expertise that makes you a sought-after leader in the transformation of global work.

About The Studio

Deel is one of the fastest-growing companies in the world, and we're building the brand and creative studio to match. We make global campaigns, partnerships, film, design, and social at real scale, for businesses and for workers in almost every country there is.

We're looking for someone exceptional to raise the bar on what we make. This is a hands-on role. You'd set the standard by making the work.

The role

Deel is a truly global, people-first brand, and it's taking off. We're looking for a creative director who works at the front edge of AI-native production across video and design. Most AI creative work is technically impressive and creatively empty. Some of it is good work that used AI somewhere in the pipeline. We think there's a real discipline in between, and we want you to build it here. You'd define how we make this work, and you'd prove it by making it. This is a hands-on role.

What You'll Make

AI-native creative. Work where generative tools are central to how it's made, at a standard the category hasn't reached.
The stack. Our AI creative tooling and the workflows around it, including the principles for where we don't use it.
Video and motion. Brand films, campaign work, and product storytelling that blend traditional and AI-led production.
A repeatable method. Something the rest of the team can use, so the capability outlives any one project.

What You Bring

At least ten years across video, motion, or design, with direction as well as production.
Recent work made or directed with generative AI that stands up as creative work first.
Deep knowledge of the current tooling, and clear judgment about where it breaks.
Proven ability to build a workflow other people can actually use.
A point of view on likeness, disclosure, and provenance. We take these seriously.

What Would Set You Apart

A reel with range across live-action, motion, and generative work.
Experience establishing an AI practice inside a creative team.
A public point of view on AI in creative work.

Who You'll Work With

You'll sit inside the creative studio and work alongside our Creative Director, the video and motion teams, and the brand designers who'll build on what you establish.

How We Work

We're a studio, not a request queue. People here make things rather than manage from a distance. We use AI seriously, and we're deliberate about where we don't.
