jobs.description:
About The Foundation

At the St. Joseph’s Health Centre Foundation we are committed to continuing to transform St. Joe’s as a leading community hospital that delivers the best care experiences to Toronto’s west end. We are guided by our mission to inspire philanthropy from our community and raise the funds needed to support that transformation.

St. Joe’s has provided care for millions of people in Toronto’s west end for more than a century. Today it is one Canada’s busiest community teaching hospitals, looking after a vibrant community of over half a million.

The Foundation has grown in recent years to be a leading community hospital foundation with a strong and engaged board of directors. We are looking for a new team member to help with gift management and donor engagement that helps to deliver the best care possible for our community.

About The Position

The Director, Finance, Data & Analytics provides strategic and operational leadership across financial management, business intelligence, fundraising analytics and organizational performance for the Foundation.

As the Foundation enters an ambitious next phase of campaign growth, this role will be responsible for ensuring that the organization has the financial discipline, data infrastructure and insights required to support informed decision-making and maximize fundraising performance.

Working closely with the President & CEO, VP, Operations, Senior Leadership Team and fundraising leaders, the Director will connect financial and fundraising data to provide a clear, timely and actionable view of organizational and campaign performance.

The Director will be the Foundation’s lead resource for financial reporting, fundraising analytics, campaign intelligence, data quality and performance reporting, ensuring that leaders have the information they need to identify opportunities, manage risk, allocate resources and achieve campaign objectives.

The successful candidate will combine strong financial expertise with an analytical and business-oriented mindset, an understanding of fundraising and donor data, and the ability to translate complex information into clear insights and recommendations.

Key Areas of Responsibility

Financial Leadership & Management
Lead the Foundation’s financial planning, budgeting, forecasting and reporting processes.
Prepare timely, accurate decision-useful financial reports for the President & CEO, Senior Leadership Team, Finance Committee and Board.
Monitor financial performance against budget and provide analysis of material variances, trends, risks and opportunities.
Lead the annual budgeting and collaborate on the business planning process with the VP, Operations and Senior Leadership Team.
Oversee cash flow, investments, receivables, payables and other core financial management activities.
Lead the annual audit and maintain strong financial controls, policies and procedures.
Ensure appropriate financial oversight of designated funds, restricted gifts, commitments and disbursements.
Work closely with external accounting and investment partners as required.
Ensure compliance with applicable accounting standards, regulatory requirements and Foundation policies.
Campaign & Fundraising Analytics
Own the development and ongoing management of the Foundation’s campaign reporting and fundraising analytics framework.
Partner with fundraising leadership to establish clear definitions, methodologies and performance measures for campaign pipeline, proposals, asks, commitments and revenue.
Develop and maintain campaign dashboards that provide management and Board-level visibility into campaign progress and future potential.
Provide analysis that identifies emerging gaps, opportunities and trends and supports proactive campaign management.
Develop forecasting models to support campaign revenue projections and scenario planning.
Work with fundraising leaders to assess portfolio capacity, prospect movement and pipeline sufficiency.
Translate fundraising data into concise insights and recommendations for the Senior Leadership Team, Campaign Leadership, Finance Committee and Board.
Data Strategy, Quality & Business Intelligence
Serve as the Foundation’s internal lead for data strategy, data governance and business intelligence.
Establish standards for data quality, consistency, definitions and reporting across financial and fundraising systems and oversee implantation with Database Manager.
Partner with fundraising and operations teams to improve the use of Raiser's Edge NXT and other systems as strategic management tools.
Identify opportunities to automate reporting and improve data accessibility.
Develop and maintain dashboards and reporting tools using appropriate business intelligence platforms.
Connect financial, fundraising, donor and operational data to provide a more complete picture of organizational performance.
Establish appropriate data governance, privacy, security and access practices in partnership with organizational leadership.
Identify technology and systems improvements that will increase efficiency, insight and fundraising productivity.
Prospect & Donor Intelligence
Support the fundraising team with data-driven prospect identification, qualification and prioritization.
Develop reporting to help assess prospect capacity, relationship activity, portfolio composition and movement through the fundraising cycle.
Partner with fundraising leadership to identify gaps in prospect pipelines and opportunities for portfolio development.
Support analysis of donor behaviour, giving patterns, retention, upgrades and other trends that inform fundraising strategy.
Organizational Performance & Decision Support
Working with VP, Operations develop a consistent framework of organizational KPIs aligned with the Foundation’s strategic and business plans.
Provide analysis to support resource allocation, staffing decisions, event and program performance, fundraising investments and operational planning.
Identify trends and insights across revenue, expenses, fundraising activity and organizational performance.
Prepare clear, concise analysis and visualizations for leadership and Board audiences.
Act as a strategic thought partner to leaders, moving beyond reporting results to helping the organization understand what the data means and what action it should inform.
Leadership, Collaboration & Continuous Improvement
Lead continuous improvement of financial and fundraising reporting processes.
Provide leadership and coaching to the administration team, including the Database Manager.
Identify opportunities to streamline workflows, automate repetitive activities and improve organizational efficiency.
Contribute to a culture of accountability, curiosity, continuous learning and evidence-informed decision-making.
Provide leadership and coaching to staff, contractors or external resources supporting finance, data and analytics.

Qualifications & Experience

CPA designation.
7+ years of progressive experience in finance, financial management, analytics, business intelligence or a related field.
Experience working in a nonprofit, healthcare, fundraising or similarly complex environment is an asset.
Demonstrated experience developing budgets, forecasts, financial models and management reporting.
Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with the ability to translate data into clear business insights.
Experience with CRM and fundraising databases; experience with Raiser's Edge NXT is an asset.
Experience developing dashboards and reporting using tools such as Power BI or equivalent is an asset.
Experience working with large or complex datasets and improving data quality and reporting processes.
Strong understanding of data governance, privacy and information management.
Excellent communication skills and the ability to present financial and analytical information clearly.
Demonstrated ability to work collaboratively.
Strong organizational skills and the ability to manage competing priorities in a fast-paced environment.
Strategic, curious and improvement-oriented.

Chief Financial Officer

Regional Municipality of Wood Buffalo | Fort McMurray, Alberta

Aplin is proud to partner with the Regional Municipality of Wood Buffalo (RMWB)
in the search for an accomplished and strategic Chief Financial Officer (CFO)
to join its senior leadership team.

Reporting directly to the Chief Administrative Officer (CAO), the CFO will provide executive leadership across Financial Services, Procurement, and Assessment and Taxation. This is an opportunity for a forward-thinking financial executive to influence the Municipality's long-term financial strategy, strengthen governance, and contribute to a business-focused, accountable, and data-driven organization.

The successful candidate will be a confident and decisive executive who brings deep financial expertise, strong business acumen, and exceptional communication skills. They will demonstrate sound judgment, a collaborative leadership style, and the ability to navigate the complexity of a large public-sector organization while building credibility with Council, senior leadership, employees, and key stakeholders.

The Opportunity

As a key member of the senior leadership team, the CFO will:

Lead the Municipality's financial strategy, long-term planning, budgeting, financial reporting, and governance.
Provide strategic financial advice and recommendations to the CAO, Council, and senior leadership.
Oversee Financial Services, Procurement, and Assessment and Taxation, ensuring effective and accountable service delivery.
Champion operational excellence, financial sustainability, continuous improvement, and informed decision-making.
Build and lead high-performing teams while fostering collaboration, transparency, and accountability.
Present complex financial information clearly and confidently to Council and other stakeholders.

The Ideal Candidate

We are seeking an accomplished financial leader who brings:

A minimum of 15 years of progressive financial or corporate services leadership experience, including five years at a senior management level.

St. Francis Xavier University (StFX) is one of Canada's leading primarily undergraduate universities, recognized for excellence in teaching, research, community engagement, and student success. Located in Antigonish, Nova Scotia, StFX offers an immersive learning environment through its Faculties of Arts, Science, and Education; the Gerald Schwartz School of Business; the Rankin School of Nursing; and the Coady Institute. Home to approximately 5,000 students, 250 faculty members, and 460 staff, the University is supported by an engaged global alumni network of more than 50,000. StFX is known for fostering intellectual growth, leadership, service, and lifelong connections while advancing its commitment to community development and social justice.

StFX is seeking a forward-thinking, inclusive, and collegial leader to serve as its next Vice President (VP), Finance. This is a significant leadership opportunity at an important time for StFX and the Canadian post-secondary sector. Building on a proud tradition, a strong sense of community, and a deeply held commitment to student success, the University is looking to advance its priorities with creativity and focus on emerging opportunities to enhance resilience, invest strategically, and expand the University’s capacity to achieve its goals. The VP will help shape thoughtful, forward-looking choices that strengthen StFX’s long-term position.

Reporting to the President and Vice-Chancellor and serving as a key member of StFX’s executive leadership team, the VP, Finance will provide strategic financial leadership, oversight, and stewardship in support of the University’s academic mission, distinctive student experience, and long-term sustainability. In close partnership with the Academic Vice President and Provost, senior leaders, the Board of Governors and the broader University community, the Vice President will bring an enterprise-wide perspective to financial planning, budgeting, resource allocation, risk, and institutional priorities.

The Vice President leads Financial Services, including Accounts Payable, Financial Reporting, Procurement Services, Student Accounts and Risk Management, and will position the portfolio as a trusted, responsive partner to the University. Combining strong financial acumen with integrity, sound judgment and a collaborative approach, they will advance modernization, evidence-based decisions, and service excellence, while empowering a high-performing team.

The successful candidate will bring senior financial leadership experience in complex organizations, with a track record of improving financial performance, and a post-secondary education in finance, business or a relevant discipline. The VP combines strong financial acumen across strategy, capital planning, cash flow, treasury, debt and risk with sound knowledge of accounting, fund accounting, financial reporting, controls and governance. They will have demonstrated success leading change, improving operations, advising executives and boards, communicating complex matters clearly, and building trust across diverse stakeholder groups. jobs.title: Associate Director S&OP Excellence and Planning Analytics
jobs.description:
Earlier this year, Unilever announced an agreement to combine its Foods business with McCormick & Company, creating a scaled global flavour powerhouse. The proposed combination would bring together iconic Foods brands, including Hellmann’s and Knorr, with McCormick’s portfolio to create a global leader across spices, seasonings, condiments and complementary food categories, supported by strong retail and foodservice platforms. McCormick brings more than 135 years of heritage, a presence in 150+ countries and territories, and a portfolio of trusted brands. The transaction remains subject to regulatory approvals and other customary closing conditions, with completion estimated for mid-2027.

Job Purpose

This role exists to strengthen how the North America Foods business plans, decides, and delivers across demand, supply, inventory, service, cost, and business waste. As Associate Director, S&OP Excellence and Planning Analytics, you will lead the planning excellence and analytics agenda that connects business ambition with practical, reliable operating plans. You will help build a more resilient, data-driven, and collaborative supply chain that enables trusted Foods brands to serve customers and consumers with confidence. This is inclusive of planning technology, analytics, and process.

You will be part of a team that believes planning is more than a process. It is a critical way of bringing people together, making better decisions, and creating the conditions for sustainable growth.

Key Responsibilities

In this role, you will lead the development and continuous improvement of integrated planning and sales and operations planning practices across North America Foods (Retail and Foods Solutions; US and Canada). You will partner closely with Demand Planning, Supply Planning, Material Planning, Manufacturing, Finance, Customer Development, Marketing, and senior Supply Chain leaders to ensure the business has clear plans, strong governance, reporting/tools, and actionable insights to support growth, service, efficiency, and transformation.

Lead a team of WL1s/2s to drive the sales and operations planning excellence agenda. Ensure robust process and technology are in place to ensure demand, supply, inventory, service, cost, and financial assumptions are connected through clear business rhythms and decision-making forums.
Partner with integrated planning teams to identify risks, opportunities, and gaps within planning technology/process and drive improvement plans. Identify / build business cases or drive cross functional process improvement.
Strengthen integrated planning capability by improving processes, tools, routines, governance, and ways of working across the North America Foods planning community.
Lead planning performance management, including the maintenance and creation and use of clear measures, scorecards, dashboards, reports, and insights that help teams make faster and better decisions. This can include modifying existing dashboards due to new business insights
Drive continuous improvement, simplification, and standardization across planning processes to improve reliability, reduce complexity, and support scalable ways of working.
Act as the primary point of contact for Planning TSAs.
Support the transition to the future Foods organization by helping design, build, and embed planning capabilities that enable business continuity from day one and maturity over time.
Build trusted relationships across functions and levels, creating a collaborative planning culture where teams are aligned, accountable, and focused on shared outcomes.

What The First Year Looks Like

During the first year, you will play a visible role in building planning excellence for the future North America Foods organization. You will learn the current planning landscape, connect with key partners across the business, and help establish the routines, measures, and decision-making forums needed to support business continuity and performance.

In your first few months, you will focus on understanding the end-to-end planning processes, key business priorities, current pain points, and transition requirements. You will build relationships with the planning community, data/tech teams, and cross-functional partners, assess existing tools and processes, and identify where stronger governance or simplification is needed.

As the year progresses, you will lead improvements to planning routines, performance reporting, and sales and operations planning governance. You will help teams align on clear roles, timelines, inputs, decisions, and escalation paths, while supporting capability-building across the planning organization.

By the end of the first year, you will have helped create a stronger integrated planning foundation for North America Foods, with clearer decision-making, improved planning visibility, stronger cross-functional alignment, and practical tools that support service, inventory, cost, waste reduction, and growth.

Required Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in Supply Chain, Operations, Business, Engineering, Finance, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience.
Significant experience 10y+ in integrated planning, demand planning, supply planning, business planning, supply chain transformation, or related end-to-end supply chain roles.
Strong understanding of sales and operations planning, forecasting, inventory management, capacity planning, supply planning, service management, and business waste reduction.
Experience leading cross-functional planning decisions and balancing service, inventory, cost, responsiveness, and growth priorities.
Strong analytical, problem-solving, communication, and stakeholder management skills, with the ability to turn complex information into clear business recommendations.
Experience influencing senior stakeholders and leading change in a complex, fast-moving environment.
Demonstrated ability to build capability, improve processes, and create practical ways of working that teams can adopt and sustain.
Strong understanding of planning tools and technology including back end master data.

Preferred Qualifications

Experience in consumer goods, food and beverage, manufacturing, retail, or another complex supply chain environment.
Experience leading sales and operations planning improvements, integrated planning transformation, or planning excellence programs across multiple teams or markets.
Experience with advanced planning systems, enterprise resource planning systems, business intelligence tools, or planning analytics platforms.
Experience supporting organization transition, business separation, integration, or large-scale transformation activities.
Advanced degree or professional certification in supply chain, operations, planning, project management, or continuous improvement.

jobs.description:
Finding the right finance leader for a stadium is about more than producing accurate financial statements. It's about finding someone who can thrive in a fast-paced, event-driven business where concert nights can run late, operational decisions happen in real time, and leadership teams rely on financial insight to drive strategy. This role is ideal for a senior finance leader who loves getting into the details, building strong teams, and turning complex financial information into a clear business story.

Reporting to the Chief Financial Officer, the Director, Finance of BC Place is an experienced business and people leader responsible for providing financial oversight, direction, and leadership across the organization. Working closely with the Finance team, senior leadership, and operational stakeholders, this role ensures best-in-class financial reporting, analysis, controls, and compliance while helping drive strategic business decisions.

This is a highly visible leadership role within a dynamic venue and events environment. No two days are the same at BC Place. One day you may be leading the annual budgeting process, negotiating financial terms within a major contract, or presenting forecast updates to executives. The next, you may be overseeing event settlements following a sold-out concert that wrapped long after most offices have turned off the lights.

The successful candidate is a strong accounting professional first and foremost. They bring deep technical expertise, exceptional analytical capabilities, and the ability to translate financial results into meaningful business insights. They are equally comfortable reviewing complex reconciliations, coaching a finance team, supporting negotiations, and presenting strategic recommendations to executives.

What You Will Do

Lead all day-to-day financial operations for the BC Place, including oversight and integration of shared services accounting functions.
Ensure the accuracy, integrity, and completeness of financial records across all departments.
Oversee general ledger management, account reconciliations, and month-end and year-end close processes.
Deliver accurate, timely, and meaningful financial statements and management reporting.
Lead the annual budgeting, forecasting, capital planning, and long-range financial planning processes.
Provide detailed financial analysis, operational reporting, and business insights that support strategic decision-making.
Analyze operating trends, financial performance, and key business drivers to identify efficiencies, risks, and opportunities for improvement.
Oversee event settlement preparation, review, analysis, and presentation while ensuring accuracy and strong client relationships.
Manage recurring billings, accounts receivable performance, credit management, and revenue reconciliation activities.
Lead capital asset management activities, including additions, disposals, write-downs, and maintenance of the capital asset register.
Ensure payroll processes are completed accurately and on time through effective procedures, support, and training.
Manage the annual external audit process and maintain strong relationships with auditors and external stakeholders.
Maintain and continuously improve financial policies, procedures, workflows, and internal controls.

Provide financial guidance on contracts, leases, supplier agreements, sponsorship agreements, and other commercial arrangements.
Support leadership with contract reviews, negotiations, and financial risk assessments.
Advise senior leaders on financial impacts, emerging issues, and opportunities affecting business plans and budgets.
Build, mentor, and develop a high-performing finance team while fostering a culture of accountability, collaboration, and excellence.

What You Will Bring

CPA designation is required.
University degree in Accounting, Finance, Commerce, or a related discipline. A combination of education and experience may also be considered.
7+ years of progressive finance and accounting leadership experience, ideally including Controller-level responsibilities.
Proven success leading and developing finance teams within complex, multi-stakeholder organizations.
Deep technical accounting expertise with strong knowledge of financial reporting, internal controls, and accounting standards.

Demonstrated excellence in financial planning, budgeting, forecasting, and analytical reporting.
Advanced financial modeling and business analysis capabilities with a natural curiosity for understanding the "why" behind the numbers.
Experience leading month-end and year-end close processes in fast-paced operational environments.
Strong audit management experience and ability to ensure compliance while driving process improvements.
Experience managing capital assets, contract reviews, lease accounting, and financial implications of commercial agreements.

Exceptional attention to detail and commitment to accuracy.
Strong communication and presentation skills with the ability to influence and build credibility with executives, operational leaders, clients, and external partners.
A collaborative leadership style paired with strong business judgment and decision-making skills.
Ability to balance strategic thinking with hands-on execution.
Comfortable working in an events-driven environment where business needs occasionally extend beyond traditional office hours.
Passion for building efficient processes, creating strong controls, and helping an organization make informed decisions through data and financial insight.

This is a unique opportunity for a finance leader who enjoys rolling up their sleeves, leading through complexity, and partnering with a business that operates at the intersection of live events, operations, and community impact. jobs.title: Chief Financial Officer
jobs.description:
About Jim Peplinski Capital

At most companies, finance supports the business. At Jim Peplinski Capital (JPC), finance is our business.

For over 35 years, Jim Peplinski Capital has financed and managed the vehicles and equipment Canadian businesses run on. We combine capital, fleet expertise and technology to help our clients get the most from the assets that keep them moving. Now we're building the next generation of fleet management, with ambitious growth plans and the balance sheet to pursue them.

We're looking for a steady, strategic, and commercially minded CFO to partner with the President and Executive Team on the decisions and execution that shape our future.

About The Role

Reporting directly to the President, you'll lead JPC's Finance, Credit and Risk function and serve as a trusted partner to the Executive Team. Two leaders report to you, a Finance Manager and a Credit Manager, along with their teams.

This is not a back-office finance role. As a lender and fleet manager, how we fund, price and manage risk is how we compete, and you'll own it. That covers capital and liquidity, funding and banking relationships, pricing and return on capital, portfolio risk and credit discipline, financial reporting and planning, and accounting, controls and compliance.

You'll shape how JPC funds its growth, manages risk, allocates capital, and you'll build the people and systems we need to scale. It's hands-on leadership: you set the direction, and you’ll roll up your sleeves when the work calls for it.

What You’ll Do

Team Leadership. Build, mentor and develop high-performing Finance and Credit teams with a culture of sound judgment, ownership, accountability and practical problem solving.
Capital, Funding and Liquidity. Ensure JPC has the capital, liquidity and funding structure to support growth. You'll manage banking relationships, funding facilities, interest rate exposure, covenant compliance and lender reporting, and build capacity ahead of where the business is going.
Residuals and Portfolio Risk. You'll own concentration limits, provisioning and credit performance across the portfolio. Collaborating with our VP, Asset Management, you'll set and monitor residual assumptions.
Credit and Adjudication. Keep credit discipline strong while finding practical ways to say yes to good business. You'll be the second set of eyes for the Credit Manager on the decisions that need it.
Financial Reporting and Planning. Deliver accurate, timely reporting to the President, Board and lenders. You'll lead budgeting, forecasting and planning, and provide the Executive Team the insights to make better decisions faster.
Accounting, Compliance and Controls. Own accounting, lease accounting, tax, audit, treasury and financial controls, plus our regulatory program, including FINTRAC and AML.
Client engagement. Work directly with clients on the decisions that matter most, from structuring deals to managing delinquencies and payment workouts, balancing a strong relationship with protecting the portfolio.
Commercial Judgment. Bring financial rigor to decisions on new products, services and partner programs. You'll lead negotiation of key commercial agreements and embed financial and risk thinking across JPC.
Systems & Technology: Own the finance and credit systems that support our growth, driving automation and building a scalable foundation for reporting, adjudication and accounting.

What We’re Looking For

You have 12+ years of progressive finance experience, including senior leadership. Experience in fleet management, automotive and/or equipment finance or specialty lending is a strong asset. Bank or boutique, we care about the depth of your experience, not the logo. A CPA is preferred but not required for candidates with deep experience as a CFO or senior finance leader in a lending business.

Credit Management

TD is committed to providing fair and equitable compensation opportunities to all colleagues. Growth opportunities and skill development are defining features of the colleague experience at TD. The base pay actually offered may vary based upon the candidate's skills and experience, job-related knowledge, geographic location, and other specific business and organizational needs.

As a candidate, you are encouraged to ask compensation related questions and have an open dialogue with your recruiter who can provide you more specific details for this role.

Job Description:

Additional Job Description

Department Overview

TD Commercial National Accounts services the unique needs of public and private Canadian businesses, customizing a broad range of products. The Financial Institutions Group within National Account is an industry leading team focused on providing best-in-class products and services to firms in the financial services sector. As part of the FI team the Director, Credit Execution guides and leads a team of Associates and Associate Directors whose job is to assist with structuring credit proposals and analyzing the risks associated with lending facilities for new and existing business clients that borrow in excess of $ 25 million. The Director, Credit Execution is part of the senior management group for a business banking unit and reports directly to the AVP, Credit Management, Commercial National Accounts.

Job Description

In the role of Director, Credit Execution ("DCE"), you are principally responsible for managing the credit and operational risk for an industry-specific commercial / junior corporate loan portfolio. You are a subject matter expert and have the ability to analyze and understand complex credit proposals, including multi-lender situations. You can anticipate and assess the risks associated with entering into a lending relationship under a wide range of economic scenarios and ensure solicitor-prepared loan agreements are relevant, supportive and competitive for the bank and our clients on an ongoing basis. You will assess, analyze and perform due diligence in support of all applications, approving credits within delegated limits and making recommendations on all others. You will interface with TD's risk management group on a regular basis to ensure that your understanding of the Bank's risk models and pricing platforms allows you to effectively interpret and apply policy. Recognizing that your credibility and influence with them is based on the credit proposals that are well-crafted and presented by your team, you make the development of your Associates' and Associate Directors' risk evaluation skills your primary priority. Thus, you will establish yourself as a trusted business leader who is sought after for guidance regarding matters relating to the credit facilities that are supporting the clients’ business strategy. You support your Unit’s efforts to meet their business development targets by recommending credit packaging alternatives and actively discuss credit solutions with internal TD partners, external professional advisors, and other lenders as appropriate. You feel comfortable in a team based business environment where you are expected to balance risk management objectives with our ongoing business building targets.

Job Requirements

Education/Accreditations:

Undergraduate/Graduate degree in business or relevant professional designation.

Other Qualifications/Skills/Experience:

Successful DCEs have the proven ability to understand the economic and industry specific circumstances that will impact the long term viability of their clients, leveraging them to structure solid credit solutions. Through their coaching expertise and experience as a mentor, they effectively impart their experience on a team of Associates and Associate Directors, developing these individuals to be better equipped to structure credit proposals and evaluate business risks. In addition to your undergraduate/graduate degree in business or relevant professional designation, you will ideally have proven your suitability for this role with at least 5 years experience in a combination, and / or Manager Commercial Credit roles in a banking environment. You have well developed analytical, relationship management, credit structuring, coaching, and negotiation skills, and have a personal goal to expand them further in this role. Your passion for enhancing the customer experience guarantees that we provide credit solutions that serve the best interests of both the bank and our client.

Number of Years Experience

5+

Who We Are:

TD is one of the world's leading global financial institutions and is the fifth largest bank in North America by branches/stores. Every day, we strive to make every interaction, product, and experience remarkably human and refreshingly simple for over 27 million households and businesses in Canada, the United States and around the world. More than 95,000 TD colleagues bring their skills, talent, and creativity to foster deeper relationships, ensure disciplined execution, and build a simpler, faster banking experience. TD is deeply committed to being a leader in client experience, that is why we believe that all colleagues, no matter where they work, are client facing. Together, we are reimagining what banking can be for our clients, colleagues and communities.

Our Total Rewards Package

Our Total Rewards package reflects the investments we make in our colleagues to help them and their families achieve their financial, physical, and mental well-being goals. Total Rewards at TD includes a base salary, variable compensation, and several other key plans such as health and well-being benefits, savings and retirement programs, paid time off, banking benefits and discounts, career development, and reward and recognition programs. Learn more

Additional Information:

We’re delighted that you’re considering building a career with TD. Through regular development conversations, training programs, and a competitive benefits plan, we’re committed to providing the support our colleagues need to thrive both at work and at home.

Please be advised that this job opportunity is subject to provincial regulation for employment purposes. It is imperative to acknowledge that each province or territory within the jurisdiction of Canada may have its own set of regulations, requirements.

Colleague Development

If you’re interested in a specific career path or are looking to build certain skills, we want to help you succeed. You’ll have regular career, development, and performance conversations with your manager, as well as access to an online learning platform and a variety of mentoring programs to help you unlock future opportunities.

If you’re passionate about helping clients and building deep, lasting relationships, TD offers diverse career paths where you can grow your expertise and make a meaningful impact.

We're committed to your success and foster a respectful workplace where diverse perspectives are valued, everyone has fair opportunities to grow, and you can unlock your full potential to achieve your career goals. Here at TD, we hire and develop the best.

Training & Onboarding

We will provide training and onboarding sessions to ensure that you’ve got everything you need to succeed in your new role.

Interview Process

We’ll reach out to candidates of interest to schedule an interview. We do our best to communicate outcomes to all applicants by email or phone call.

Accommodation

Your accessibility is important to us. Please let us know if you’d like accommodations (including accessible meeting rooms, captioning for virtual interviews, etc.) to help us remove barriers so that you can participate throughout the interview process.

We look forward to hearing from you!

Sans Objet

About Toronto Community Housing Corporation
  
  

Toronto Community Housing Corporation (“TCHC”) is the largest social housing provider in Canada and the second largest in North America. We are wholly owned by the City of Toronto and operate in a non\-profit manner. TCHC provides homes to over 41,000 low and moderate\-income households in 88 of Toronto's neighbourhoods, with 93,000 tenants from many different backgrounds with a diversity in age, education, language, mental and physical ability, religion, ethnicity and race. We are an essential part of the City of Toronto's fabric and social system.
  
  

Our over 2,000 employees work to achieve our vision of quality homes in vibrant communities where people are proud to live and work.
  
  

**Vacancy Type:** Full\-time Permanent
  
**Salary Range:** $165,001\.67 \- $198,002\.01

Hybrid Eligible Yes

What we offer
  
In addition to competitive compensation and a rewarding career where you can truly make a difference, we offer a comprehensive package that meets the various needs of our diverse employees, including:
  
* Ability to participate in inclusive employee\-led networks to educate, inspire, amplify voices, build relationships and provide development opportunities;
* Minimum four (4\) weeks of paid annual vacation days, increasing with years of service;
* Four (4\) paid personal days;
* Defined benefit pension plan with OMERS, includes 100\-per\-cent employer matching;
* Health and dental benefits, including a health spending account available upon your start date;
* Employee and family assistance program;
* Maternity and parental leave top up (93% of base salary);
* Training and development programs including tuition reimbursement of $1500 per calendar year;
* Fitness membership discount.


**Work location:** This job offers the opportunity to work from home as part of a hybrid work arrangement. This arrangement will allow you to work some days at a TCHC work location (Metro Hall – 55 John Street and/or 729 Petrolia Road) and the rest of the time from home. The amount of time required to work at a TCHC work location is flexible, while considering operational and service delivery requirements.
  
  

Make a difference
  
As the Director, Corporate Compliance and Enterprise Risk, you have a unique opportunity to build and operate TCHC’s corporate compliance function while shaping the future of enterprise risk management. Reporting directly to the President \& CEO, you will develop practical frameworks, tools, and reporting that enable leaders to identify, assess and manage significant risks and compliance obligations.
  
As a trusted advisor to leaders across TCHC and to the Board of Directors, you will bring clarity to complex and emerging risks and inform enterprise\-wide decisions. Your advice will strengthen transparency and accountability while ensuring leaders remain responsible for their processes, risks, controls, and corrective actions.
  
Through coaching, facilitation and fit\-for\-purpose solutions, you will build risk and compliance capability across TCHC, helping TCHC make informed decisions and ultimately deliver better outcomes for tenants and communities.
  
  

What you’ll do
  
Corporate Compliance
  
* Design, establish and operate a corporate compliance model that enables divisions to identify and manage legislative, regulatory, shareholder, funding, policy and other obligations.
* Develop practical compliance tools, guidance, learning resources and reporting that business units can apply within day\-to\-day operations.
* Partner with compliance owners to clarify obligations, assess exposure, address capability gaps and develop proportionate improvement plans.
* Monitor changing requirements, coordinate enterprise\-level compliance insights, and support escalation of significant compliance matters.


Enterprise Risk Management (ERM)
  
* Shape and operate TCHC’s existing enterprise risk management model, including common risk language, assessment practices, risk appetite and tolerance, the enterprise risk profile and reporting cycle.
* Facilitate enterprise and cross\-divisional risk identification, assessment, prioritization and response planning with executives, risk owners and subject\-matter leaders.
* Support risk owners in developing proportionate responses, indicators and monitoring approaches, while ownership of risks, business processes and actions remains with management.
* Integrate internal controls as one component of ERM by advising leaders on controls that support the treatment of priority risks and by helping them evaluate whether those controls remain fit for purpose.


Risk Advisory and Capacity Building
  
* Provide concise, risk\-based advice on the enterprise risk profile, significant compliance obligations and emerging risks.
* Prepare and present integrated compliance and ERM reporting that supports executive and Board discussion, direction, and oversight while distinguishing management\-owned corrective actions.
* Support appropriate escalation of significant risk or compliance matters and track management commitments for executive and Board visibility.
* Coach executives, leaders, risk owners and staff in risk\-informed decision\-making and compliance management.
* Build sustainable capability through workshops, training, templates, communities of practice and decision supports.
* Lead, coach and develop team, setting priorities and quality expectations.


What you’ll need
  
* An undergraduate degree in Risk Management, Business Administration, Public Administration, Law, Compliance, Finance or related discipline.
* A recognized professional designation

jobs.description:
Division:  IGM Technology

Location:  Toronto/Winnipeg

IGM Financial Inc. is a leading wealth and asset management company in Canada, managing approximately $310 billion in assets as of December 31, 2025. It offers financial planning and investment services to over two million Canadians through IG Wealth Management and Mackenzie Investments.

Founded in 1926, IG Wealth Management is a key part of IGM's business model, providing comprehensive wealth management services to Canadian financial advisors and their clients.

With a vision to inspire financial confidence, IG Wealth Management is recognized as one of Manitoba’s Top Employers, Canada’s Top 100 Employers, and Best Diversity Employers, aiming to innovate the industry and support Canadians in achieving their financial goals.

Join our team to engage in continuous learning and skill development in a supportive environment. Experience the best of both worlds with our hybrid work environment, where you spend three days a week in the office, connecting, collaborating, and enjoying quality time with your amazing colleagues! Our Values: Be better; we strive for improvement in everything we do. Be accountable; we foster clarity and are empowered to act responsibly. Be a team; we are united to drive collective impact to achieve our goals.

Overall Job Purpose

The Director, Citizen Development & Employee Technology Experience Pod Owner is responsible for leading and advancing two connected enterprise capabilities: enabling employees to safely improve how work gets done through Microsoft Copilot, Power Automate and approved low-code/no-code capabilities; and reducing technology friction through stronger employee experiences, communications, onboarding, short-form learning, TechTalks and adoption programs.

This role shapes and delivers the pod strategy, roadmap, operating model, governance, prioritization and measurable outcomes. The Director balances speed, innovation and employee empowerment with security, privacy, risk, operational resilience and supportability, ensuring employee-led technology adoption remains practical, governed and sustainable.

Key Accountabilities

Lead the pod vision, strategy, roadmap and priorities for Citizen Development and Employee Technology Experience, ensuring alignment to enterprise objectives, portfolio priorities and measurable business outcomes.
Operate and launch and then continuously improve the Citizen Development operating model, including scope, intake, prioritization, decision rights, solution classification, lifecycle oversight, support model, escalation paths and value measurement.
Enable governed adoption of Microsoft Copilot, Power Automate and approved low-code/no-code capabilities, with clear boundaries between employee-led solutions and work requiring business-led or technology-led delivery.
Maintain practical guardrails for safe innovation, including solution registration, ownership, risk tiering, control gates, security review, privacy considerations and operational supportability.
Identify employee technology friction across corporate and advisor communities and sponsor practical improvements that improve productivity, adoption, service experience and confidence in technology.
Lead employee technology communications, TechTalks, digital learning content, short video learning, tech tips, onboarding support and awareness campaigns that make technology easier to understand and adopt.
Manage and refine the pod backlog, making informed trade-offs across value, risk, cost, capacity, quality, employee experience, technical sustainability and operational impact.
Coordinate agile planning, backlog refinement, sprint execution, reviews and retrospectives to maintain delivery discipline, transparency and momentum.
Provide day-to-day leadership, coaching and feedback to pod team members; partner with Product and Delivery Chapters on standards, capability development, staffing and best practices.
Build strong partnerships across business teams, Technology, Security, Risk, Privacy, Architecture, Service Management, enterprise platform teams and corporate support functions.
Communicate roadmaps, progress, risks, decisions, dependencies and performance clearly to stakeholders and senior leaders.
Track measures for adoption, employee experience, productivity, business value, cost, operational health, risk and supportability, and use insights to improve priorities and outcomes.

Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in Business, Technology, Digital Transformation or a related field required; equivalent experience considered an asset
5–8 years of progressive experience in enterprise technology, digital workplace, product, automation, artificial intelligence, employee experience, service management or technology delivery
Experience supporting strategies, operating models, roadmaps, governance frameworks and measurable outcomes for enterprise technology capabilities
Knowledge of Microsoft 365, Microsoft Copilot, Power Platform, Power Automate and related enterprise technology environments
Strong understanding of governance, security, privacy, technology risk, operational resilience and support models in a regulated environment
Ability to translate emerging technology into practical employee and business value
Strong communication, influencing, stakeholder-management and decision-framing skills
Proven ability to lead multidisciplinary work, manage priorities and coordinate delivery across organizational boundaries
Collaborative, pragmatic, change-oriented and outcome-focused leadership style
Passion for improving employee technology experience, reducing friction and enabling safe, governed innovation

What Success Looks Like

Success means employees can confidently adopt technology and safely improve how work gets done; technology friction is visible and addressed; Citizen Development operates within clear boundaries and guardrails; and leaders have reliable visibility into adoption, employee experience, business value, cost, operational health and risk.

The expected annual base salary range for this role is $149,500 - $192,500 which is determined based on skills, knowledge and experience and geographic location. In addition to base salary, this role is eligible for annual short-term incentive, health and well-being benefits, retirement and savings plan, paid time off and career development.

Benefits

COMPETITIVE COMPENSATION & RECOGNITION: competitive base salary, performance-weighted bonus, education/career support, option to join Employee Share Purchase Plan with employer matching component.
EMPLOYEE BENEFITS & INSURANCE: competitive health and dental coverage, flexible plan for you and your family and short-term & long-term disability plans.
RETIREMENT SAVINGS PROGRAMS: voluntary Defined Contribution Pension Plan
WORK LIFE BALANCE: paid volunteer days, competitive time off, including 10 wellness days off, WorkPerks discount program, hybrid & flex work arrangements.
INCLUSIVE CULTURE AND DIVERSITY: living our core values: Be a Team, Be Accountable, Be Better, engaging with community through Business Resource Groups (BRG communities are volunteer employee-led groups formed around a common interest, identity, or background).

IGM is a diverse workplace committed to doing business inclusively - this starts with having a representative workforce! We encourage applications from all qualified candidates that represent the diversity present across Canada – including racialized persons, women, Indigenous persons, persons with disabilities, 2SLGBTQIA+ community, gender diverse and neurodiverse individuals, as well as all who may contribute to the further diversification of ideas.

IG is an accessible employer committed to providing a barrier- free recruitment experience. If you require an accommodation or this information in an alternate format at any stage of the recruitment process, please reach out to the Talent Acquisition team who will work with you to meet your needs.

How to Apply: Interested candidates are invited to submit their resume and a cover letter detailing their qualifications and experience to https://www.ig.ca/en/careers

We thank all applicants for their interest in IG Wealth Management; however, only those candidates selected for an interview will be contacted.

Please apply before November 12 2026.

Through coaching, facilitation and fit-for-purpose solutions, you will build risk and compliance capability across TCHC, helping TCHC make informed decisions and ultimately deliver better outcomes for tenants and communities.

What You’ll Do

Corporate Compliance

Design, establish and operate a corporate compliance model that enables divisions to identify and manage legislative, regulatory, shareholder, funding, policy and other obligations.
Develop practical compliance tools, guidance, learning resources and reporting that business units can apply within day-to-day operations.
Partner with compliance owners to clarify obligations, assess exposure, address capability gaps and develop proportionate improvement plans.
Monitor changing requirements, coordinate enterprise-level compliance insights, and support escalation of significant compliance matters.

Enterprise Risk Management (ERM)

Shape and operate TCHC’s existing enterprise risk management model, including common risk language, assessment practices, risk appetite and tolerance, the enterprise risk profile and reporting cycle.
Facilitate enterprise and cross-divisional risk identification, assessment, prioritization and response planning with executives, risk owners and subject-matter leaders.
Support risk owners in developing proportionate responses, indicators and monitoring approaches, while ownership of risks, business processes and actions remains with management.
Integrate internal controls as one component of ERM by advising leaders on controls that support the treatment of priority risks and by helping them evaluate whether those controls remain fit for purpose.

Risk Advisory and Capacity Building

Provide concise, risk-based advice on the enterprise risk profile, significant compliance obligations and emerging risks.
Prepare and present integrated compliance and ERM reporting that supports executive and Board discussion, direction, and oversight while distinguishing management-owned corrective actions.
Support appropriate escalation of significant risk or compliance matters and track management commitments for executive and Board visibility.
Coach executives, leaders, risk owners and staff in risk-informed decision-making and compliance management.
Build sustainable capability through workshops, training, templates, communities of practice and decision supports.
Lead, coach and develop team, setting priorities and quality expectations.

What You’ll Need

An undergraduate degree in Risk Management, Business Administration, Public Administration, Law, Compliance, Finance or related discipline.
A recognized professional designation in enterprise risk management or compliance designation, such as CRM, CRMA, RIMS-CRMP, an IRM qualification, or CCEP (Certified Compliance & Ethics Professional) from the Society of Corporate Compliance and Ethics (SCCE), or an equivalent credential.
Minimum of 10 years of progressive senior experience establishing and operating complex enterprise risk management and corporate compliance functions, including experience designing practical frameworks, advising executives and Boards, leading professional teams, and building organizational capability in an organization of similar size and complexity.
Demonstrated success implementing or maturing compliance programs and ERM in a large public-sector, housing, non-profit or similarly regulated, complex and multi-stakeholder organization.
Expert knowledge of corporate compliance and ERM frameworks and practices, including COSO ERM, ISO 31000, ISO 37301.
Proven ability to translate risk and compliance principles into practical operating models, decision tools, reporting and coaching for business leaders.
Strong understanding of public-sector accountability, Board governance, shareholder and funding obligations, and risk-based reporting applicable to a large social housing provider.
Excellent strategic judgment, facilitation, relationship-building, coaching, change leadership and communication skills
Effective verbal and written communication skills, including the ability to present complex risk and compliance matters as clear options and advice.

What’s Next

Once you apply, we’ll review your resume and contact you if we believe your skills and experience will make you successful in the role. If you are selected to move forward, the process will include one or more interviews and/or assessments and reference checks.

jobs.description:
Job Description:

Chef de la Planification Budgétaire et de la Gouvernance / Head of Business Planning & Governance

***English job description follows***

Description de l'emploi :

Vous avez une expérience en gestion de programme/projet, vous souhaitez travailler dans l’environnement du service à la clientèle au sein d’une équipe dynamique et vous souhaitez évoluer et développer de nouvelles compétences? Ce poste est pour vous !

Le programme d'avions commerciaux A220 recherche un Chef de la Planification Budgétaire et de la Gouvernance pour rejoindre notre équipe Efficacité de la Flotte en service basée à Mirabel (Québec, Canada), où vous travaillerez conjointement avec toute l’organisation de Service à la Clientèle pour supporter les opérateurs A220.

Vous ferez partie de l’équipe Efficacité de la Flotte qui est chargée d’assurer une exploitation sûre et économique de la flotte A220 en service. L'organisation de l'équipe est établie de manière à promouvoir la collaboration transversale de manière autonome, en se soutenant mutuellement et en apprenant collectivement.

Relevant du Chef Efficacité de la flotte en service A220, vous contribuerez à la mission fondamentale de l'équipe qui consiste à garantir une exploitation efficace, sûre et économique de la flotte Airbus A220 en service, tout en améliorant en permanence la satisfaction des clients.

Vous travaillerez sur la gestion de la gouvernance des services clients A220 et soutiendrez précisément la performance de la résolution des principaux problèmes en service de la flotte A220.

Votre environnement de travail:

Le siège du programme d'avions commerciaux A220 est situé à Mirabel, dans la région métropolitaine de Montréal, à deux pas de la ville dynamique de Montréal. Réputée pour son environnement paisible et sûr, la région offre une grande qualité de vie aux jeunes professionnels ou aux professionnels expérimentés, ainsi qu'aux familles, en équilibrant parfaitement les opportunités de carrière et les activités de plein air, ce qui en fait un endroit vraiment spécial où il fait bon vivre.

Parce que nous prenons soin de vous :

Avantages financiers: Salaire attractif, bonus annuel, régime d’assurances collectives, régime de retraite et régime d’achat d’actions.
Équilibre vie privée / professionnelle: Une politique de travail hybride, une cafétéria sur site, une politique de congés très concurrentielle.
Bien-être / santé: Programme d’Aide aux Employé.e.s (PAE), programme de rabais et service médical sur site.
Développement individuel: des opportunités d’évolution et des possibilités de formations nombreuses (catalogue de plus de 10.000 e-formations disponibles en libre accès pour développer votre employabilité, certifications, programmes de développement accéléré, mobilité nationale et internationale).

Chez Airbus, nous vous aidons à travailler, à vous connecter et à collaborer plus facilement et de manière plus flexible. Partout où cela est possible, nous favorisons la flexibilité dans nos modes de travail afin de stimuler l'esprit d'innovation.

Vos défis:

Piloter la performance opérationnelle et économique de l’équipe Efficacité de la Flotte en service et la gouvernance globale de l'organisation Services à la Clientèle A220 en menant les activités transverses suivantes :
Diriger les instances majeures de gouvernance :
Gouvernance MISP / SISP (Major / Significant In-Service Problems) : Assurer le pilotage de la performance de résolution des problèmes majeurs en service, le suivi du calendrier, la gestion des risques et des coûts, la coordination transversale avec l’Ingénierie et les Opérations en service, et la visibilité mensuelle aux clients avec escalade si nécessaire jusqu'au comité exécutif
Comité d'Arbitrage et de Décision du Portefeuille “Amélioration de la satisfaction client” : Structurer et animer la gouvernance d'arbitrage budgétaire et de sélection des projets (validation des business cases, ROI flotte, critères de sévérité, arbitrages et capacité d'exécution).

Coordonner la définition des indicateurs de performance (KPI) pour l'ensemble de l'organisation Services à la Clientèle A220 et garantir leur parfait alignement avec les Top Objectifs Compagnie (TCO/TFO) A220.
Consolider, analyser et rapporter les performances mensuelles de l'entité, et intégrer ces données dans les plateformes de suivi Airbus pour assurer une visibilité transverse complète entre les différents programmes.
Coordonner la sécurité et la navigabilité de la flotte en service en monitorant les campagnes d'actions de modification et d'amélioration en cours d'exécution.
Optimiser les processus internes de gouvernance, garantir l'adhérence aux standards de l'entreprise et déployer la démarche d'Excellence Opérationnelle.
Préparer l'avenir en pilotant la stratégie de transformation, d'évolution du portefeuille de projets transverses et de régionalisation de l'équipe en soutien direct de la proximité client.

Superviser la planification financière globale (AOP - Annual Operating Plan), la gestion du compte de résultat (ABS P&L) et la gestion des risques et opportunités pour l'ensemble des Services à la Clientèle A220.
Gérer les business cases, le suivi des dépenses et les provisions budgétaires des campagnes majeures de modification d'avions (Aircraft Retrofit), représentant un budget de plusieurs dizaines de millions de dollars
Assumer le rôle de responsable du portefeuille (Portfolio Leader) de projets d'amélioration de la satisfaction client, avec la responsabilité complète de l'enveloppe budgétaire annuelle et des arbitrages stratégiques.
Développer la maturité en gestion de projet au sein de l’équipe Efficacité de la Flotte en service, incluant le déploiement de méthodologies, d'outils structurants et de compétences en leadership.

Votre profil:

Diplôme en ingénierie ou gestion de projet;
Minimum de quinze (15) ans d'expérience dans l'ingénierie, l'exploitation d'aéronefs ou la gestion de programmes, avec un minimum de cinq (5) ans dans un rôle de gestion;
Démontre de solides compétences en gestion de projet/programme, y compris en approche agile;
Solide sens financier spécifique à Airbus Canada et expérience souhaitable dans la gestion d'importants projets multidisciplinaires et de budgets à forte valeur;
Excellentes compétences interpersonnelles, de présentation et de communication pour interagir à tous les niveaux de la direction, y compris la capacité à faire des présentations aux cadres supérieurs (Executives) et aux clients;
Est à l'aise dans des écosystèmes complexes et a une compréhension des organisations axées sur la gestion de programmes;
Est orienté(e) processus et a de l'expérience dans l'intégration de nouvelles méthodes de travail;
Promeut le travail d'équipe et agit avec leadership;
Est axé sur le client et fait preuve d'intégrité en tout temps, sans compromis;
Fait preuve d'innovation, d'engagement et de persévérance;
Une expérience en Airbus et/ou A220 et/ou en services à la clientèle est un atout certain.

En raison du secteur d’activité (aéronautique), de multiples contacts avec des entités Airbus situées dans le monde entier, et d’interactions avec les fournisseurs et clients également situés dans le monde entier, la connaissance de l’anglais est demandée dans ce poste.

Ce travail nécessite une prise de conscience liée à tous les risques potentiels de conformité et à un engagement à agir avec intégrité, ces valeurs sont le fondement du succès, de la réputation et de la croissance durable de l'entreprise.

Donnez une nouvelle dimension à votre carrière en soumettant votre candidature en ligne maintenant !

The A220 commercial aircraft Programme is looking for a Head of Business Planning & Governance to join our Fleet Efficiency in-service team based in Mirabel (Québec, Canada), where you will work jointly with our Customer Services organization to support the A220 operators.

Known for its peaceful and safe environment, the region offers a high quality of life for younger or experienced professionals and families, perfectly balancing career opportunities and outdoor activities that makes it a truly special place to call home.

Coordinate the definition of Key Performance Indicators (KPIs) for the entire A220 Customer Services organization and ensure their alignment with A220 Top Company Objectives (TCO/TFO).
Consolidate, analyze, and report monthly entity performance, and integrate these data into Airbus tracking platforms to ensure complete cross-programme visibility.
Coordinate safety and airworthiness of the in-service fleet by monitoring ongoing modification and improvement action campaigns.
Optimize internal governance processes, ensure adherence to company standards, and deploy Operational Excellence practices.
Prepare for the future by leading the transformation strategy, evolution of the transverse project portfolio, and team regionalization in direct support of customer proximity.

Oversee overall financial planning (AOP - Annual Operating Plan), P&L management (ABS P&L), and risk & opportunity management for all A220 Customer Services.
Manage business cases, expenditure tracking, and budget provisions for major aircraft retrofit campaigns, representing a multi-ten million dollar budget.

jobs.description:
About the role

Cinareo is hiring a Vice President, Technology: a hands-on technical leader who will own our platform, lead our engineering team and drive our AI roadmap through a period of rapid growth. This role is designed to grow into Chief Technology Officer as Cinareo scales.

This is a hands-on leadership role. You will lead, mentor and coordinate the engineers who build our platform, set the technical direction that carries the company through its next stage, and own the results: what we ship, how well it works and how quickly we deliver.

What you will do

First 90 days

Take full ownership of the platform, cloud infrastructure, release process and engineering roadmap from our current engineering lead.
Learn our customers, integrations and data model well enough to make architecture decisions with confidence.
Assess our delivery, quality, security and reliability practices, and set out a plan to strengthen them.

Technical leadership

Architecture and technical direction.
Be the final technical decision-maker on platform architecture, data design and infrastructure. Review designs and critical changes, set engineering standards, and step into the code yourself when a problem calls for it.
Delivery and quality.
Own the release process, test strategy and defect management so we ship predictably and safely.
Reliability and IT operations.
Own uptime, monitoring, incident response and disaster recovery, along with internal IT, identity and access, and device management.
Security and compliance.
Own our compliance program. We hold SOC 1 Type 1 and are completing our SOC 2 Type 2 examination. Maintain control evidence and handle enterprise security reviews accurately and quickly.
Customer and commercial support.
Act as the senior technical counterpart in enterprise sales, partner conversations, onboarding, integration scoping and escalations.

People and team

Lead our distributed engineering team.
Manage, mentor and coordinate a team of full-time and contract engineers across time zones, including off-shore, with clear priorities, deliverables and accountability.
Build the team as we grow.
Decide when to hire, contract or partner; recruit strong engineers; and develop our first technical leads.
Set the culture.
Build an engineering culture grounded in intellectual honesty, ownership and close collaboration with product and design.

AI and growth

AI roadmap.
Lead delivery of our AI roadmap, from AI Assist through Intelligence and Predictive Optimization. This includes the data foundations, LLM and machine-learning capabilities, and the responsible-AI governance enterprise buyers expect.
AI-native engineering.
Make AI part of how we build, using AI-assisted development, testing and operations so a small team can move like a much larger one.
Platform for scale.
Evolve the architecture so reliability, performance and infrastructure cost keep pace as customers and data volumes grow.
Integrations and partnerships.
Own our integration strategy and APIs across CCaaS and WFM and business systems our customers run and support our technology partnerships.
Planning and governance.
Turn the product roadmap into capacity and budget, recommend build, buy or partner decisions, and report technology strategy and risk to the executive team and Board.

How you will work

At first, much of the work is close to the ground: taking ownership of the platform, tightening delivery, quality, reliability and security, and guiding the team through shipping our first AI capabilities. As the team grows and operations run through process and people, the balance shifts toward strategy, the AI roadmap and scaling the organization, and toward the CTO role.

We need someone who moves easily between strategy and execution: working through a production incident with the team in the morning and presenting the technology roadmap to the Executive and the Board in the afternoon, making sound calls with incomplete information, and adjusting quickly as the business scales.

What success looks like

In 6 months:
you own the platform end-to-end, releases are predictable, our AI Assist has shipped, and our SOC 2 Type 2 report is complete.
In 12 months:
the team has clear technical leadership in place, the next phases of our AI roadmap are in delivery, and the platform is ready for the customer growth and technical due diligence that comes with our next stage.

What you bring

10+ years in software engineering, including senior technical leadership at a B2B SaaS company.
A former developer with a strong engineering foundation: you know how to write code, can review it with authority, and earn the respect of the engineers you lead.
A track record of owning delivery outcomes, being accountable for what a team ships, how reliably it runs and whether it lands on time.
Experience shipping AI capabilities, such as LLM-based features, machine learning or both, into a production SaaS product.
Experience designing or evolving cloud SaaS architecture (multi-tenant ideally), including cost and performance management.
Experience leading and mentoring distributed teams, including contractors or partner teams both on-shore and off-shore, and hiring and developing engineers.
Credibility with enterprise customers and partners on architecture, security and integration.
Clear written communication that executives and Board members can act on.
Real enthusiasm for AI and how it is changing both software products and the way software gets built.

Nice to have

Contact center technology: WFM and CCaaS (Genesys, Aspect, Verint, NICE, Five9, Amazon Connect or similar)
Leading a security compliance program (SOC 2, ISO 27001 or equivalent) at the level of controls and evidence.
Calculation-heavy domains such as forecasting, simulation or optimization.
Responsible-AI governance.

Details

Chief Operating Officer
Career path:
Designed to grow into Chief Technology Officer
Location:
Remote. Ontario preferred, but must be based in Canada

Commensurate with experience

Send your CV to hr@cinareo.com
with a short note covering:
a SaaS platform or engineering team you scaled, and how you led the team that built it; and
your experience with AI and where you see it making the biggest difference in the dev-ops and our production platform.
