jobs.title: Anthropic Fellows Program, The Anthropic Institute (Economics & Policy)
jobs.description:
About Anthropic

Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.

Anthropic Fellows Program Overview

The Anthropic Fellows Program is designed to foster AI research and engineering talent. We provide funding and mentorship to promising technical talent - regardless of previous experience.

Fellows will primarily use external infrastructure (e.g. open-source models, public APIs) to work on project aligned with our research priorities, with the goal of producing a public output
(e.g. a paper submission). In one of our earlier cohorts, over 80% of fellows produced papers. We run multiple cohorts of Fellows each year and review applications on a rolling basis.

Submit your application to the Economics & Policy workstream at the bottom of this page. We are accepting applications on a rolling basis for the next cohort expected to start in January 2027. In some circumstances, we can accommodate fellows starting outside the usual cohort timelines — please note in your application if the January 2027 start date doesn't work for you.

What To Expect

4 months of full-time research
Direct mentorship from Anthropic researchers
Weekly stipend of 3,850 USD / 2,310 GBP / 4,300 CAD + benefits (these vary by country)
Substantial funding for compute and other research expenses

Interview process

The interview process will include an initial application, assessments, and interviews. We may ask for references later in the process as well.

We encourage you to apply even if you do not believe you meet every single qualification.
Not all strong candidates will meet every single qualification as listed. Research shows that people who identify as being from underrepresented groups are more prone to experiencing imposter syndrome and doubting the strength of their candidacy, so we urge you not to exclude yourself prematurely and to submit an application if you're interested in this work. We think AI systems like the ones we're building have enormous social and ethical implications. We think this makes representation even more important, and we strive to include a range of diverse perspectives on our team.

Compensation

The expected base stipend for this role is 3,850 USD / 2,310 GBP / 4,300 CAD per week, with an expectation of 40 hours per week for 4 months (with possible extension).

The Anthropic Institute Fellows (Economics & Policy)

Mentors, research areas, & past projects

Fellows will undergo a project selection & mentor matching process. Potential research areas and mentors include:

Economics
Maxim Massenkoff
Peter McCrory

Policy, Security, and Society
Jack Clark
Marina Favaro
Jim Baker

Projects In This Workstream May Include

Designing and conducting empirical research on AI's economic effects, drawing on external data sources
Developing new methodological approaches for studying AI's impact on labor markets, the future of work, and society
Analysing the offense–defense balance for AI-enabled cyber and bio capabilities as models scale
Measuring the extent to which model performance increases with custom harnesses
Identifying market driven mechanisms that could improve societal resilience to anticipated threats from AI systems
Identifying which metrics relating to AI R&D could serve as early warning signals for recursive self-improvement

For Past Project Examples, See

How AI Impacts Skill Formation: Judy Shen and Alex Tamkin
Stress-Testing Model Specs Reveals Character Differences among Language Models: Jifan Zhang, Henry Sleight, Andi Peng, John Schulman, and Esin Durmus

Unique candidate criteria

You might be a particularly great fit for this workstream if you:

Have an interest in economics or policy research; prior experience in this area is a plus but not required
Are adaptable and collaborative, able to take direction and contribute to team priorities rather than needing to pursue a predetermined research agenda
Are skilled at writing up and communicating your results, even when they're null or unexpected
Are passionate about translating research insights into actionable recommendations for improving AI systems and informing policy

You May Be a Good Fit If You

Are motivated by making sure AI is safe and beneficial for society as a whole
Are excited to transition into AI research and would be interested in a full-time role at Anthropic
Strong track record of empirical research
Thrive in fast-paced, collaborative environments
Can implement ideas quickly and communicate clearly

Candidates Must Be

Fluent in Python programming
Available to work full-time on the Fellows program

Logistics - Fellows Program

Submit your application to the Anthropic Institute Fellows at the bottom of this page.

Logistics Requirements:
To participate in the Fellows program, you must have work authorization in the US, UK, or Canada and be located in that country during the program.

Workspace Locations:
We have designated shared workspaces in SF. We are also open to remote fellows in the UK, US, or Canada
.

Visa Sponsorship:
We are not
currently able to sponsor visas for fellows. To participate in the Fellows program, you need to have or independently obtain full-time work authorization in the UK, the US, or Canada.

Program Duration:
The program runs for 4 months, full-time. If you can't commit to the full duration, please still apply and note your constraints in the application. We review these requests on a case-by-case basis.

The below are Anthropic's policies for full time roles. These do NOT apply to the Fellows Program.

Logistics

Minimum education:
Bachelor’s degree or an equivalent combination of education, training, and/or experience

Required field of study:
A field relevant to the role as demonstrated through coursework, training, or professional experience

Minimum years of experience:
Years of experience required will correlate with the internal job level requirements for the position

Location-based hybrid policy:
Currently, we expect all staff to be in one of our offices at least 25% of the time. However, some roles may require more time in our offices.

Visa sponsorship:
We do sponsor visas! However, we aren't able to successfully sponsor visas for every role and every candidate. But if we make you an offer, we will make every reasonable effort to get you a visa, and we retain an immigration lawyer to help with this.

We encourage you to apply even if you do not believe you meet every single qualification.
Not all strong candidates will meet every single qualification as listed. Research shows that people who identify as being from underrepresented groups are more prone to experiencing imposter syndrome and doubting the strength of their candidacy, so we urge you not to exclude yourself prematurely and to submit an application if you're interested in this work. We think AI systems like the ones we're building have enormous social and ethical implications. We think this makes representation even more important, and we strive to include a range of diverse perspectives on our team.

Your safety matters to us.
To protect yourself from potential scams, remember that Anthropic recruiters only contact you from @anthropic.com email addresses. In some cases, we may partner with vetted recruiting agencies who will identify themselves as working on behalf of Anthropic. Be cautious of emails from other domains. Legitimate Anthropic recruiters will never ask for money, fees, or banking information before your first day. If you're ever unsure about a communication, don't click any links—visit anthropic.com/careers directly for confirmed position openings.

How We're Different

We believe that the highest-impact AI research will be big science. At Anthropic we work as a single cohesive team on just a few large-scale research efforts. And we value impact — advancing our long-term goals of steerable, trustworthy AI — rather than work on smaller and more specific puzzles. We view AI research as an empirical science, which has as much in common with physics and biology as with traditional efforts in computer science. We're an extremely collaborative group, and we host frequent research discussions to ensure that we are pursuing the highest-impact work at any given time. As such, we greatly value communication skills.

The easiest way to understand our research directions is to read our recent research. This research continues many of the directions our team worked on prior to Anthropic, including: GPT-3, Circuit-Based Interpretability, Multimodal Neurons, Scaling Laws, AI & Compute, Concrete Problems in AI Safety, and Learning from Human Preferences.

Come work with us!

Anthropic is a public benefit corporation headquartered in San Francisco. We offer competitive compensation and benefits, optional equity donation matching, generous vacation and parental leave, flexible working hours, and a lovely office space in which to collaborate with colleagues. jobs.title: Anthropic Fellows Program, ML Systems & Reinforcement Learning
jobs.description:
About Anthropic

Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.

Anthropic Fellows Program Overview

The Anthropic Fellows Program is designed to foster AI research and engineering talent. We provide funding and mentorship to promising technical talent - regardless of previous experience.

Fellows will primarily use external infrastructure (e.g. open-source models, public APIs) to work on an empirical project aligned with our research priorities, with the goal of producing a public output
(e.g. a paper submission). In one of our earlier cohorts, over 80% of fellows produced papers. We run multiple cohorts of Fellows each year and review applications on a rolling basis.

Apply at the bottom of this page. We are accepting applications on a rolling basis for the next cohort expected to start in January 2027. In some circumstances, we can accommodate fellows starting outside the usual cohort timelines — please note in your application if the January 2027 start date doesn't work for you.

What To Expect

4 months of full-time research
Direct mentorship from Anthropic researchers
Access to a shared workspace
Connection to the broader AI safety and security research community
Weekly stipend of 3,850 USD / 2,310 GBP / 4,300 CAD + benefits (these vary by country)
Funding for compute (~$15k/month) and other research expenses

Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Applications are now open for our January cohort - apply here by October 30.

The Anthropic Fellows Program is designed to foster AI research and engineering talent. We provide funding and mentorship to promising technical talent - regardless of previous experience.

Can implement ideas quickly and communicate clearly

Available to work full-time on the Fellows program

Mentors, research areas, & past projects

Sam Bowman
Sara Price
Alex Tamkin
Nina Panickssery
Trenton Bricken
Logan Graham
Jascha Sohl-Dickstein
Joe Benton
Collin Burns
Fabien Roger
Samuel Marks
Kyle Fish
Ethan Perez

Our mentors will lead projects in select AI safety research areas, such as:

Scalable Oversight: Developing techniques to keep highly capable models helpful and honest, even as they surpass human-level intelligence in various domains.
Adversarial Robustness and AI Control: Creating methods to ensure advanced AI systems remain safe and harmless in unfamiliar or adversarial scenarios.
Model Organisms: Creating model organisms of misalignment to improve our empirical understanding of how alignment failures might arise.
Model Internals / Mechanistic Interpretability: Advancing our understanding of the internal workings of large language models to enable more targeted interventions and safety measures.
AI Welfare: Improving our understanding of potential AI welfare and developing related evaluations and mitigations.

jobs.title: Finance Director
jobs.description:
**Company Overview:** Big Al's is a leading company in the aquatic and pet industry, dedicated to providing high\-quality products and services to pet enthusiasts worldwide. We are committed to innovation, excellence, and the well\-being of pets. We are seeking a dynamic and experienced Financial Director to join our executive team and drive our financial strategy and growth.

**Position Summary:**

**The Finance Director** will be responsible for overseeing all financial aspects of the company, driving financial planning, and ensuring the company’s financial health. The Finance Director will collaborate closely with the executive team to develop and implement financial strategies that support the company’s goals and objectives. This role requires a strategic thinker with strong financial acumen, excellent leadership skills, and a deep understanding of the financial, aquatic and pet industry.

**Key Responsibilities:**

**1\. Financial Strategy and Planning:**

* Develop and implement financial strategies, goals, and objectives to support the company’s overall business strategy.
* Lead the annual budgeting process and ensure alignment with company goals.
* Monitor financial performance, analyze variances, and recommend corrective actions.

**2\. Financial Reporting and Analysis:**

* Oversee the preparation of accurate and timely financial reports, including income statements, balance sheets, cash flow statements, and forecasts.
* Conduct financial analysis to identify trends, opportunities, and risks, and provide insights to the executive team.
* Ensure compliance with accounting standards, regulations, and internal policies.

**3\. Cash Flow and Capital Management:**

* Manage the company’s cash flow to ensure liquidity and optimize working capital.
* Develop and implement strategies for capital structure, including debt and equity financing.
* Oversee investment activities and manage relationships with financial institutions.

**4\. Risk Management and Compliance:**

* Identify and manage financial risks, including market, credit, and operational risks.
* Ensure compliance with all financial and regulatory requirements, including tax filings and audits.
* Develop and implement internal controls to safeguard company assets and ensure financial integrity.

**5\. Operational Efficiency:**

* Drive cost optimization initiatives and identify opportunities for operational efficiency.
* Collaborate with other departments to streamline processes and improve financial performance.
* Oversee the financial aspects of supply chain management, inventory control, and procurement.

**6\. Team Leadership and Development:**

* Lead and mentor the finance team, fostering a culture of excellence, collaboration, and continuous improvement.
* Provide training and development opportunities to enhance the skills and capabilities of the finance team.
* Work closely with the executive team to align financial goals with overall business objectives.

**7\. Strategic Partnerships and Growth:**

* Identify and evaluate potential mergers, acquisitions, and strategic partnerships.
* Conduct due diligence and financial analysis for potential business opportunities.
* Support the development and execution of growth strategies, including new product launches and market expansion.

**Qualifications:**

* Bachelor’s degree in finance, Accounting, Business Administration, or a related field; CPA is preferred.
* Proven experience as a Finance Director or in a senior financial leadership role, preferably within the financial, aquatic, pet industry or a related sector.
* Strong knowledge of financial management, accounting principles, and regulatory requirements.
* Excellent analytical, strategic planning, and problem\-solving skills.
* Proficiency in financial modeling, forecasting, and analysis.
* Experience with ERP systems and financial software.
* Strong leadership and team management skills, with the ability to inspire and develop a high\-performing finance team.
* Excellent communication and interpersonal skills, with the ability to effectively collaborate with cross\-functional teams and external stakeholders.
* High level of integrity, ethics, and professionalism.

**Benefits:**

* Competitive salary and performance\-based bonuses.
* Comprehensive health, dental, and vision insurance.
* Retirement savings plan with company match.
* Professional development opportunities.
* Friendly and dynamic work environment.
* Employee discounts on company products.
* Paid time off
* Casual dress

**Application Process:** Interested candidates are invited to submit their resume and a cover letter outlining their qualifications and experience related to this position to hr@bigals.ca. Please include "Finance Director Application" in the subject line.

jobs.title: Vice President, Technology Operations
jobs.description:
BCI is working with an external recruitment firm. Please do not submit your application directly to BCI. Applications submitted through this site will not be reviewed.

To explore this opportunity, please contact Boyden . Only qualified candidates who match the requirements will be contacted.

Closing Date: Open Until Filled

Located in either Vancouver or Victoria (with a preference for Victoria), this opportunity will appeal to a leader who is energized by possibility rather than crisis. The mandate calls for someone with the attitude, curiosity and influence to challenge established thinking, bring people through change, and create a modern operating environment that keeps pace with an ambitious, AI-first business. The role offers an exciting opportunity to influence the future of BCI’s technology function and contribute to the continued success of one of Canada’s most dynamic investment organizations.

With $313.7 billion of gross assets under management, British Columbia Investment Management Corporation (BCI) is one of the largest institutional investors in Canada. Since its inception in 1999, BCI has grown significantly and is now regarded as one of the most influential financial institutions globally, investing across a broad range of asset classes and strategies in both public and private markets. Today, BCI employs more than 800 people across offices in Victoria, Vancouver, New York and London, and continues to be recognized as one of Canada’s Top 100 Employers, Canada’s Top Family-Friendly Employers, Canada’s Top Employers for Young People and BC’s Top Employers.

In recent years, BCI has made substantial investments in modernizing its technology operations and has established a leading-edge platform, recently winning Info-Tech Innovator of the Year (2025) and CIO of the Year (2026). With a stable and well-managed foundation now in place, the Technology function is focused on sustaining that momentum through continued innovation and the thoughtful adoption of new technologies. The next phase will build on BCI’s existing strengths by accelerating cloud-native capabilities, AI-enabled services, automation and modern engineering practices, ensuring the technology environment continues to evolve ahead of business needs and enables the organization to move with greater speed, intelligence and confidence.

Key to this ambition is the role of Vice President, Technology Operations. Reporting to the SVP, Technology & Innovation and CTO, and leading a team of ~32, the Vice President will oversee cloud and infrastructure services and systems, digital workplace services and systems, Service Desk and service management, as well as disaster recovery. This is a role not simply focused on day-to-day operations but on the continued evolution and shaping of BCI’s future state technology platform. The VP will be on the pulse of the external operational environment, actively assessing current performance and future trends, identifying opportunities for continuous improvement, and providing senior technical advisory services to the CTO for strategic consideration and action.

The ideal candidate will be a technology leader who has led large teams in a technology-forward, entrepreneurial environment such as fintech, technology-enabled services or complex organizations where modern infrastructure and exceptional user experience are viewed as business enablers. They will be a transformational and technically credible leader who combines strategic vision with enough technical depth to challenge assumptions and bring new ideas to the table. Rather than being constrained by traditional infrastructure models, they will be curious about what is possible, question the status quo, be comfortable leading change in an already stable environment, and focused on speed, innovation and the end-user experience.

BCI offers a competitive total rewards package which includes a performance-based incentive plan, comprehensive health & dental benefits, a defined benefit pension plan and paid time off.

The annualized base salary range for this role based in Victoria is CAD $190,000-$240,000.

The base salary offered to the successful candidate will consider a wide array of factors including but not limited to the individual’s skill set, level of experience applicable to the role they are being offered and consideration to internal equity.

We pay our people competitively in the markets in which we compete for talent and with consideration to internal equity and job structure. We aim for actual pay to be around the median of the market for target or expected levels of performance, and around the upper quartile of the market for excellent performance.

Actual salaries may vary and may be above or below the range based on various factors, including, but not limited to, experience and expertise.

To explore this opportunity, please contact Boyden .

We thank all applicants for their interest in this position. Please note that we will only be in contact with those individuals moving forward with our client.

Location: Toronto, Winnipeg

Referral Level: Level 1

Mackenzie Investments

IGM Financial Inc. is a leading wealth and asset management company in Canada, managing approximately $ 310 billion in assets as of December 31, 2025 . It offers financial planning and investment services to over two million Canadians through IG Wealth Management and Mackenzie Investments.

Mackenzie Investments, founded in 1967, is a key part of IGM's business model, serving as a comprehensive asset-management partner for Canadian financial advisors and their clients.

At Mackenzie Investments You Can Build Your Career with Confidence
.
We are proud to be recognized as one of Canada’s Top 100 Employers for the fourth consecutive year and one of Canada’s Best Diversity Employers. Our vision and strategy aim to innovate the industry and support Canadians in achieving their financial goals.

Join our team to engage in continuous learning and skill development in a supportive environment. Experience the best of both worlds with our hybrid work environment, where you spend three days a week in the office, connecting, collaborating, and enjoying quality time with your amazing colleagues ! Our Values: Be better ; we strive for improvement in everything we do . Be accountable ; we foster clarity and are empowered to act responsibly . Be a team ; we are united to drive collective impact to achieve our goals .

Overall Job Purpose

The Director, Citizen Development & Employee Technology Experience Pod Owner is responsible for leading and advancing two connected enterprise capabilities: enabling employees to safely improve how work gets done through Microsoft Copilot, Power Automate and approved low-code/no-code capabilities; and reducing technology friction through stronger employee experiences, communications, onboarding, short-form learning, TechTalks and adoption programs.

This role shapes and delivers the pod strategy, roadmap, operating model, governance, prioritization and measurable outcomes. The Director balances speed, innovation and employee empowerment with security, privacy, risk, operational resilience and supportability, ensuring employee-led technology adoption remains practical, governed and sustainable.

Key Accountabilities

Lead the pod vision, strategy, roadmap and priorities for Citizen Development and Employee Technology Experience, ensuring alignment to enterprise objectives, portfolio priorities and measurable business outcomes.
Operate and launch and then continuously improve the Citizen Development operating model, including scope, intake, prioritization, decision rights, solution classification, lifecycle oversight, support model, escalation paths and value measurement.
Enable governed adoption of Microsoft Copilot, Power Automate and approved low-code/no-code capabilities, with clear boundaries between employee-led solutions and work requiring business-led or technology-led delivery.
Maintain practical guardrails for safe innovation, including solution registration, ownership, risk tiering, control gates, security review, privacy considerations and operational supportability.
Identify employee technology friction across corporate and advisor communities and sponsor practical improvements that improve productivity, adoption, service experience and confidence in technology.
Lead employee technology communications, TechTalks, digital learning content, short video learning, tech tips, onboarding support and awareness campaigns that make technology easier to understand and adopt.
Manage and refine the pod backlog, making informed trade-offs across value, risk, cost, capacity, quality, employee experience, technical sustainability and operational impact.
Coordinate agile planning, backlog refinement, sprint execution, reviews and retrospectives to maintain delivery discipline, transparency and momentum.
Provide day-to-day leadership, coaching and feedback to pod team members; partner with Product and Delivery Chapters on standards, capability development, staffing and best practices.
Build strong partnerships across business teams, Technology, Security, Risk, Privacy, Architecture, Service Management, enterprise platform teams and corporate support functions.
Communicate roadmaps, progress, risks, decisions, dependencies and performance clearly to stakeholders and senior leaders.
Track measures for adoption, employee experience, productivity, business value, cost, operational health, risk and supportability, and use insights to improve priorities and outcomes.

Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in Business, Technology, Digital Transformation or a related field required; equivalent experience considered an asset
5–8 years of progressive experience in enterprise technology, digital workplace, product, automation, artificial intelligence, employee experience, service management or technology delivery
Experience supporting strategies, operating models, roadmaps, governance frameworks and measurable outcomes for enterprise technology capabilities
Knowledge of Microsoft 365, Microsoft Copilot, Power Platform, Power Automate and related enterprise technology environments
Strong understanding of governance, security, privacy, technology risk, operational resilience and support models in a regulated environment
Ability to translate emerging technology into practical employee and business value
Strong communication, influencing, stakeholder-management and decision-framing skills
Proven ability to lead multidisciplinary work, manage priorities and coordinate delivery across organizational boundaries
Collaborative, pragmatic, change-oriented and outcome-focused leadership style
Passion for improving employee technology experience, reducing friction and enabling safe, governed innovation

What Success Looks Like

Success means employees can confidently adopt technology and safely improve how work gets done; technology friction is visible and addressed; Citizen Development operates within clear boundaries and guardrails; and leaders have reliable visibility into adoption, employee experience, business value, cost, operational health and risk.

The expected annual base salary range for this role is $149,500 - $192,500 which is determined based on skills, knowledge and experience and geographic location. In addition to base salary, this role is eligible for annual short-term incentive, health and well-being benefits, retirement and savings plan, paid time off and career development.

Benefits

Benefits
:

COMPETITIVE COMPENSATION & RECOGNITION: competitive base salary, performance- weighted bonus, education/career support, option to join Employee Share Purchase Plan with employer matching component .
EMPLOYEE BENEFITS & INSURANCE: competitive health and dental coverage, flexible plan for you and your family and short-term & long-term disability plans.

jobs.title: Director, Internal Audit (Information Technology)
jobs.description:
Join a Challenger

At EQ, we're remaking banking so every Canadian gets ahead, every day. Serving nearly 4 million Canadians from coast to coast, we offer a wide variety of financial services from banking and lending, to trust and credit union solutions.

We've been at this since 1970, challenging the conventions of traditional banking with smarter, faster, and more connected financial experiences.

What's kept us moving?
The people behind it all: challengers who ask better questions, push back on old assumptions, and look for a better way forward.

If you're driven to help reshape how banking works for Canadians and the businesses that power our economy, this could be your next big opportunity.

We can’t wait to get to know you!

Purpose of the Job

The Director, Internal Audit IT will be responsible for leading the risk assessment, control identification, documentation, testing, findings and recommendation process for various Information Technology audits across the Bank, with a focus on Cyber Security and Artificial Intelligence. The incumbent will also be responsible for developing and implementing audit coverage for new technology systems/applications in line with the Bank’s strategic initiatives. This may involve auditing of certain Bank projects. Notably, the role is expected to be provide expert-level knowledge of current financial services information technology control expectations with respect to the Bank’s IT Operations and Cyber Security practices for a mainly Digital Banking cloud-based environment.

The Core Parts Of Your Role Would Be To

Independently develops and implements audit coverage of IT Technology processes and develops effective coverage of new technology implemented by the Bank - 60 %

Taking into account the Bank’s IT policies, established technology control frameworks (ITIL and NIST), and applicable regulatory expectations, the incumbent will create audit programs for the Bank’s technology processes which include:
Technology applications which support the bank’s business lines including: retail and commercial lending, credit cards, Trust and Digital Banking deposit products.
Technology infrastructure
Cyber Security
Cloud Technology
Artificial Intelligence

Responsible for executing the end-to-end audit engagement process: commences with the development of an audit plan, followed by identification of risks, assessment/testing of the adequacy of associated internal controls, and development of conclusions based on audit testing.
Draft audit reports at the conclusion of each audit for submission to the Chief Auditor
Maintain ongoing awareness of applicable regulatory requirements, and the Bank’s strategic initiatives and industry developments in order to ensure audit work is relevant and value-added. This may include monitoring or auditing large-scale technology projects.
Follow-up and report on adequacy of management actions to resolve audit findings and report progress to the Chief Auditor on an ongoing basis.

Risk Assessment -25%

Maintain up-to-date knowledge of regulatory expectations, the Bank’s strategic initiatives, significant technology process changes, and industry developments related to the Bank’s technology practices. Incorporate into audit coverage as required.
Provide consulting advice on Bank policies/projects related to Technology controls.
Develop a Risk and Control assessment for each individual audit engagement to guide the development of each audit program.
The position will be required to take into consideration the size and complexity of the Bank when conducting risk assessments and in developing audit observations as a result of audit testing.
Maintains an awareness of key strategic technology projects initiated by management and identifies potential change management risks which may be associated with management initiatives.
Effectively communicates risks to all levels, including Senior Management across the Bank, both verbally and orally, in a concise manner tailored to the audience level.

Relationship Management/Communication - 15%

Maintain positive working relationships with Senior Management of Information Technology units and IT control functions to ensure effective communication flow throughout the audit engagement process; maintain ongoing awareness of Senior Management’s concerns and any emerging risks.
Able to influence senior management with respect to acceptance of key findings and/recommendations.
Keep the Chief Auditor informed of the status of key risks or findings identified during the audit.
Commit to ongoing professional development by completing 40 training hours per year.
Share knowledge of areas of expertise with other members of the Internal Audit team in order to provide cross-training.

Let’s Talk About You!

Post-secondary degree with a specialised IT designation is required (e.g. CISA, CISSP)
10+ years’ proven experience in a financial institution information technology audit role (senior manager or above).
Knowledge of Data Analytics, and Artificial Intelligence practices and controls is an asset.
Expert knowledge of ITIL and NIST control frameworks.
Proven experience of independently auditing IT infrastructure, cyber and application environments.
Expert knowledge of applicable regulatory requirements; including OSFI Cybersecurity expectations.
Strong level of previous experience auditing technology projects/strategic initiatives.
Proven excellent written and verbal communication skills, ability to communicate with both a technical and non-technical audience. Ability to break down complex subject matter into concise points for purposes of communicating audit findings.
Ability to influence and impact Senior Management with respect to accepting/implementing recommendations related to identified control issues.
Excellent effective organizational, time management and project management abilities; including the ability to manage multiple priorities (and potentially other staff resources) within deadlines.
Ability to work independently and perform under pressure and within tight time constraints.
Consistently continues to develop/maintain broad knowledge and awareness of the financial industry, risk management practices and regulatory and/or policy changes.

What we offer [For full-time permanent roles]

💰 Competitive discretionary bonus

✨ Market leading RRSP match program

🩺 Medical, dental, vision, life, and disability benefits

📝 Employee Share Purchase Plan

👶🏽 Maternity/Parental top-up while you care for your little one

🏝 Generous vacation policy and personal days

🖥 Virtual events to connect with your fellow colleagues

🎓 Professional development and comprehensive Career Development program

💛 A fulfilling opportunity to join one of the top FinTechs and help create a new kind of banking experience

The incumbent will be working hybrid and in office time will be spent working from EQ Bank’s additional office space located at 2200-25 Ontario Street, Toronto, ON
.

SaskTel is entering a defining period of change. As the organization accelerates its transformation into a modern tech forward communications leader, we are seeking a Chief Information Officer (CIO) who can bring clarity, courage and conviction to a division that sits at the centre of SaskTel’s future. This is a role for a leader who thrives in complexity, sees opportunity in legacy, and understands how to evolve a technology function into a true strategic engine for the business.

The Opportunity

Reporting to the President & CEO, the CIO is accountable for SaskTel’s enterprise technology strategy, digital modernization, cybersecurity posture, data governance, and the delivery of reliable, secure, and efficient technology services. The CIO also serves as SaskTel’s Chief Security Officer and holds enterprise accountability for data governance.
This leader will oversee a large, diverse team responsible for enterprise applications, infrastructure, cloud services, cybersecurity, architecture, and service delivery. This role requires a leader who can modernize a complex, legacy heavy environment and ensure they have a high-performing team who is willing and welcoming of the new technology horizon SaskTel is entering into.

The Mandate

For SaskTel, the role goes beyond providing telecommunications services. Technology connects Saskatchewan, strengthen communities, enables businesses and support the province’s economic growth. As technology continues to reshape how we live and work, it is increasingly central to Saskatchewan’s future.
This is not a caretaker role. It is a once in a career mandate to modernize, simplify, and elevate a technology environment that underpins every connection SaskTel delivers.

The Ideal Candidate

As the ideal candidate, you are a seasoned technology executive with a proven record of leading large, complex organizations through meaningful modernization. You bring deep expertise in enterprise systems, cloud transformation, cybersecurity, and data governance, paired with the leadership presence and elevate information services as a true strategic partner.
You have assembled 15+ years of progressive technology leadership experience, including significant time at the senior executive level, and a history of modernizing legacy environments, improving delivery performance, and driving cultural change. You understand how to strengthen execution, introduce modern development practices, and lead teams through ambiguity with clarity and confidence.
Academically grounded with a bachelor’s degree in a relevant field, such as business, technology, or a related discipline and you are comfortable operating in regulated or public sector environments. Experience with large scale enterprise transformations, including OSS/BSS, CRM, ERP, or cloud native modernization, is highly valued.
Above all, you are courageous, collaborative, and forward looking. You bring the courage to challenge entrenched norms, the backbone to make risk based decisions, and the leadership maturity to reset a long standing operating model. You build trust quickly, communicate with executive presence, and bring the mindset and energy required to help SaskTel evolve.
If you are energized by meaningful transformation, if you thrive in environments where change is both necessary and possible, and if you want your work to matter beyond the balance sheet, this role offers a rare platform to make a lasting impact.

jobs.description:
Who We Are 🇨🇦

Tetra Digital Group is Canada’s leading institutional digital asset infrastructure provider.

As Canada’s first and only regulated digital asset custodian, we’ve built the institutional foundation the market demands. We’re backed by Urbana Corporation, National Bank, ATB Financial, Wealthsimple, Purpose Unlimited, Shakepay, Shopify, and Coinbase Ventures — some of the most consequential names in Canadian finance and fintech.

We operate two interconnected businesses: Tetra Trust, our regulated custody arm and CADD Digital, Canada’s first Canadian dollar-backed stablecoin issued by a regulated financial institution. It’s live on Base, Ethereum, and Tempo, with Solana next. CoinDesk and BNN Bloomberg covered it as the arrival of Canada’s first regulated digital dollar. 🚀

Here’s the problem we’re solving: Canada clears roughly $424 billion every business day, and much of the retail payment infrastructure underneath it was designed in the 1980s. Batch windows. Cut-off times. Weekends off. We’re building rails that settle continuously, programmatically, and under regulatory oversight.

We’re a team of ~30 people. We punch well above our size, and so does the opportunity ahead.

The Role 📊

You make sure the numbers behind Tetra hold up to anyone who checks them.

This is the senior finance seat at Tetra, and it’s genuinely hands-on. You’ll own accounting, FP&A, treasury, tax, audit, and regulatory reporting across all three businesses, and you’ll be the CEO and board’s partner on capital strategy, partnerships, M&A, and the next raise. You’ll work with a licensed trust company and a Canadian stablecoin company.  

You’ll be building the finance function for a business model that’s being defined in real time.

You’ll report to our [CEO], work directly with senior leaders of the firm, the board and its audit committee, and partner closely with our compliance, legal, engineering, and partnerships leads.

What You’ll Own 🎯

Capital, deals, and the next raise.
Own capital strategy across equity, debt, and strategic investment. Lead fundraising alongside the CEO, structure partnerships, M&A, and financing deals from first model to close, and manage the cap table and investor reporting for a shareholder base that includes some of Canada’s biggest banks and fintechs. The data room is ready before anyone asks for it. 💰
Board and executive partnership.
Be the key financial advisor to the CEO, executive team, and board on planning, controls, budgeting and audit committee materials.
Accounting and reporting under IFRS.
That includes consolidated reporting across Tetra’s entities, crypto-asset accounting and fair value measurement, accounting for CADD in circulation and the reserves behind it, revenue recognition for custody and issuance fees, and intercompany agreements and transfer pricing.
Reserve economics.
Reserve income is a core part of how CADD makes money, and it moves with every rate decision. With operations, compliance, and risk, you’ll shape the reserve investment policy: what we hold, where, at what duration, and with what liquidity buffer for weekend and holiday redemptions. You’ll model reserve income across rate scenarios and make sure the business still works when rates fall. 💵
Treasury and liquidity.
Account for corporate cash, runway, and liquidity across CAD, USD, and the digital assets among financial partners, counterparties, clients, issuers and holders. 
Regulatory capital and filings.
Trust company capital and liquidity requirements, regulatory financial reporting and FINTRAC, and readiness for evolving regulations. You will own audit readiness and support SOC 1 and SOC 2 Type II work and reserve attestations.
Controls.
🔐 Design internal controls built for a regulated crypto business and a Canadian trust company, including, but not limited to, segregation of duties, maker-checker on payments and wallet movements. 
Tax, done right the first time.
Corporate income tax, GST/HST on digital asset and payment services, SR&ED, transfer pricing, and the new crypto-asset information reporting arriving under the Crypto-Asset Reporting Framework (CARF).
Planning and Analysis.
📈 Budget, rolling forecast, and scenario models for each business line. Pricing, partner economics, and unit economics to propel our growth.
Finance systems, automated.
🤖 An ERP we won’t outgrow, a crypto sub-ledger, automated reconciliations, and AI-enabled reporting, and analytics.  
The team that comes next.
You’ll start with a small team and do plenty of the work yourself. As Tetra grows, you’ll hire, mentor, and lead a growing team.

What We’re Looking For 🔍

10+ years of progressive finance leadership, ideally a blend of experience in both regulated industries and high-growth startups, fintech, and institutional financial services.
Accountability for a finance function whose numbers were audited and regulated.
A bachelor’s degree in business administration, finance, or accounting, and a CPA or equivalent professional designation. 
Advanced IFRS, regulatory financial reporting, internal controls, and audit readiness. 
Capital and deal experience. Equity and debt raises, M&A structuring and due diligence, negotiations, and cap table management across complex corporate entities.
Multi-currency treasury, liquidity management and forecasting, and counterparty, operational, and regulatory risk assessment experience.
Digital asset fluency. Digital-asset accounting and fair value, integrating crypto and fiat rails, and how a stablecoin’s reserves, supply, and redemptions show up in the financial statements.
Canadian payments fluency. Interac, Lynx, EFT, and the Real-Time Rail, plus emerging standards like ISO 20022 and the Travel Rule.
Design thinking to build and improve billing systems, crypto sub-ledgers, and processes. 
Strategic thinking. You align finance strategy with where the business is going, and you can see how the finance function needs to scale before it breaks.
Strong communication skills. You can present to a board, client, regulator, and investor in the same week.
Comfort with ambiguity. You’ve led in fast-moving environments where the standards were still being written, and you built frameworks anyway.

Digital asset experience matters here, but it doesn’t have to come from a crypto company. If you’ve led finance at a bank, a payments processor, or a regulated fintech, and you understand how custody and stablecoins work, we welcome your application.

Extra points for: 🏆

You’ve led finance through a SOC 2 Type II, a reserve attestation, or a provincial or federal regulatory examination
You’ve worked on stablecoin, e-money, prepaid, or safeguarded-funds issuance, where every unit outstanding has to be backed by something real
You’ve run finance inside a trust company, bank, or other prudentially regulated institution, including regulatory capital reporting
You’ve completed capital raising efforts with strategic investors, banks and VCs
Experience with APIs, smart contracts, and blockchain analytics tools
You’ve built a finance function from scratch, including the first real ERP and sub-ledger implementation, not just run one someone else built
You’ve handled crypto tax and information reporting, including CARF readiness

What You Get 💼

💰 [$210,000–$265,000] base salary, commensurate with experience
🦷 Comprehensive health, dental, and paramedical coverage
🌱 $1,000 annual learning budget for finance, accounting, and digital asset certifications, courses, and conferences [plus professional designation dues]
🏢 3 days a week in office, with periodic travel 
🏝 Generous vacation allowances 
🇨🇦 A front-row seat to Canada’s digital dollar with a small, high-calibre team where your work is visible, your contributions are felt, and your growth is real

A Note on Fit 🧭

Tetra moves fast and the expectations are high. If you’ve spent your career waiting for a fully defined job description before getting started, this isn’t the right fit. If you are a leader who sees an opportunity and executes, who thrives in ambiguity, and takes ownership of outcomes, this role was built for you.
If that sounds energizing rather, we’d love to hear from you. 🤝
﻿

Submit your resume along with thoughtful answers to the application questions. Tell us who you are, what drives you, and why this role at this moment makes sense for you.
Tetra is committed to building a diverse and inclusive team. We encourage candidates from all backgrounds to apply and will provide accommodation throughout the hiring process upon request.

Pay at Intact is about much more than just salary.

About The Role

At Intact, we believe innovation and customer experience are at the heart of everything we do. With a commitment to excellence, we push the boundaries of digital marketing to deliver smart, customer-focused solutions. We’re looking for a visionary leader to spearhead our marketing technology, digital platforms and marketing analytics strategy while enhancing our capabilities in an ever-evolving environment.

Role Overview

As the Director, Marketing Technology, Analytics and Digital Platforms,
you will lead the development and implementation of Intact’s MarTech, Digital Platforms and Marketing Analytics strategy. Chief Technology Officer
Or a VP Engineering who wants to take the next big step

Our client is a growing software company of 20+ people serving the skilled trades and union sector through a portfolio of specialized technology products.

Their business includes three major products:

1. Member Management SaaS Platform

A SaaS product designed for skilled trades unions to manage members, dues, dispatch, communications, reporting, and administrative workflows.

2. Trade School SaaS Platform

A SaaS product focused on apprenticeship and trade school administration, including student records, class scheduling, curriculum tracking, attendance, evaluations, and compliance-related reporting.

3. XR Training and Simulation Platform

An advanced XR development platform that uses virtual reality, mixed reality, motion capture, volumetric video, and agentic AI to create highly detailed, customized training scenarios for the skilled trades. This platform supports immersive, scenario-based learning that can simulate complex work environments, safety procedures, field conditions, and hands-on technical instruction.

Our client’s customers rely on them for dependable systems that support critical operational workflows, member services, education, and training. As they continue to scale, they are looking for a senior technology leader who can bring strategic direction, operational discipline, technical depth, and practical AI leadership to their engineering organization.

Role Summary

We are seeking a CTO / VP Engineering to lead our technology organization through its next stage of growth.

This is a hybrid executive and operational leadership role. The ideal candidate can contribute to company strategy at the leadership table while also driving execution across engineering, architecture, platform reliability, security, AI governance, and product delivery.

This person will be responsible for ensuring that our technology organization is scalable, accountable, secure, and aligned with business priorities. They will help shape the technical vision for our SaaS platforms and XR/AI products while improving delivery predictability, team structure, engineering practices, and long-term product quality.

The successful candidate will be comfortable working in a mid-sized company where leadership requires both strategic thinking and hands-on operational involvement. They should be able to move fluidly between product strategy, engineering management, customer impact, architecture decisions, AI governance, and team coaching.

Key Responsibilities

Own and evolve the overall technology strategy across the company’s SaaS and XR/AI product portfolio.
Lead the engineering organization, including software development, architecture, infrastructure, DevOps, QA, technical support escalation, and AI-related engineering practices.
Partner with the CEO, product leadership, customer success, sales, and operations to align technology decisions with business goals.
Establish clear engineering priorities, delivery processes, accountability structures, and performance expectations.
Improve predictability of product delivery through better planning, estimation, roadmap execution, release management, and communication.
Balance new product development, customer-specific needs, technical debt, security, scalability, and platform reliability.
Provide technical leadership for multi-tenant SaaS architecture, integrations, data management, reporting, automation, and platform modernization.
Guide the continued development of agentic AI features and immersive XR training capabilities.
Oversee engineering budgets, tooling decisions, vendor relationships, infrastructure costs, and AI-related cost controls.
Build, mentor, and manage a high-performing engineering team.
Define and track engineering performance metrics.
Ensure the company maintains appropriate standards for security, privacy, uptime, auditability, and customer trust.
Represent the technology function in executive planning, customer conversations, strategic partnerships, and board or investor discussions as needed.

AI Leadership and Governance

AI is already an important part of both our internal development practices and our customer-facing product strategy. This role will be responsible for ensuring that AI is used effectively, securely, and responsibly.

Define the company’s practical AI strategy across internal operations and external product features.
Establish governance for AI-assisted software development, testing, documentation, support, and engineering workflows.
Ensure internal AI tools are used in ways that improve productivity without compromising intellectual property, customer data, security, or code quality.
Lead the architecture and governance of agentic AI features in the company’s SaaS and XR products.
Create standards for AI model selection, prompt management, evaluation, logging, observability, cost management, and human oversight.
Ensure AI-enabled features are designed for reliability, transparency, auditability, and customer trust.
Partner with product leadership to identify high-value AI use cases that solve real customer problems rather than pursuing AI for novelty.
Implement guardrails for privacy, data access, hallucination risk, permissions, workflow automation, and customer-specific data boundaries.
Evaluate vendors, models, frameworks, and AI infrastructure options pragmatically.
Establish internal policies for the safe use of generative AI, agentic workflows, code generation, and customer data.
Help the organization distinguish between experimental AI capabilities and production-grade AI features.

The ideal candidate understands that AI adoption requires more than enthusiasm. It requires governance, testing, security, user experience design, operational monitoring, and clear business value.

People Management

The CTO / VP Engineering will be responsible for developing a strong, accountable, and collaborative engineering culture.
Lead, coach, and mentor software developers, technical leads, QA resources, DevOps/infrastructure personnel, and other technology team members.
Clarify roles, responsibilities, decision rights, and expectations within the engineering organization.
Build career development paths and performance management practices for technical staff.
Hire, onboard, and retain strong engineering talent.
Create a culture of ownership, accountability, continuous improvement, and practical problem-solving.
Support technical leads and managers in improving estimation, delivery planning, code quality, and team communication.
Identify skills gaps and make recommendations for hiring, training, outsourcing, or team restructuring.
Foster collaboration between engineering, product, customer success, implementation, and support teams.
Encourage high standards without creating unnecessary bureaucracy.
Address underperformance directly and constructively.
Promote a low-ego, high-trust environment where people can challenge ideas, improve systems, and deliver meaningful outcomes.

Technical Leadership

This role requires enough technical depth to make sound architectural decisions, challenge assumptions, evaluate trade-offs, and guide the team through complex product and platform decisions.
Own the technical architecture and long-term scalability of the company’s product platforms.
Provide leadership across SaaS architecture, cloud infrastructure, APIs, integrations, data models, security, reporting, performance, and system reliability.
Guide architectural decisions for multi-tenant SaaS environments, customer-specific configurations, and integration-heavy workflows.
Lead modernization efforts where appropriate, while avoiding unnecessary rewrites or over-engineering.
Establish standards for code quality, automated testing, CI/CD, observability, documentation, and production readiness.
Ensure systems are maintainable, secure, performant, and cost-effective.
Manage technical debt through clear prioritization and business-aligned trade-off decisions.
Provide technical guidance for the XR development platform, including immersive content workflows, AI-enabled training scenarios, data capture, and platform extensibility.
Evaluate build-versus-buy decisions and vendor/platform choices.
Ensure engineering practices support both innovation and operational stability.

The ideal candidate does not need to be the strongest individual contributor in every technology area, but must be technically credible, architecturally sound, and able to lead senior technical staff effectively.

Product and Customer Partnership

The CTO / VP Engineering will work closely with product, customer success, implementation, and sales teams to ensure that technology supports customer value and business growth.
Partner with product leadership to translate business priorities and customer needs into achievable technical plans.
Help prioritize roadmap items based on customer value, revenue impact, technical complexity, risk, and strategic importance.
Support customer conversations where senior technical credibility is required.
Help evaluate large customer requests, custom development opportunities, integrations, and implementation risks.
Balance the needs of individual customers with the long-term health of the core product.
Ensure technical teams understand the operational realities of unions, trade schools, apprenticeship programs, and skilled trades training environments.
Improve communication between engineering and customer-facing teams.
Help define product capabilities that are scalable, configurable, and repeatable rather than overly customized.
Support go-to-market efforts for AI-enabled and XR-based training capabilities.
Ensure that customer commitments are realistic, well-understood, and aligned with engineering capacity.

Security, Risk, and Compliance

Ensure appropriate controls are in place for access management, authentication, authorization, data privacy, backups, disaster recovery, and incident response.

Implement governance for the use of customer data in AI systems, analytics, testing, support, and development workflows.
Ensure customer data boundaries are respected across multi-tenant SaaS environments.

Develop policies for data retention, audit logging, administrative access, and production support access.

Communicate clearly with customers and internal stakeholders about security, risk, and technical controls.
Balance appropriate governance with the needs of a growing, pragmatic software company.

Prior experience as a CTO, VP Engineering, Head of Engineering, Director of Engineering, or similar senior technology leader.

jobs.description:
Chief Strategy & Enrolment Officer

Glenlyon Norfolk School | Victoria, British Columbia

An exceptional opportunity to shape the future of one of Canada's leading independent schools.

Glenlyon Norfolk School (GNS) is seeking an accomplished, forward-thinking and entrepreneurial leader to join our Senior Leadership Team as our Chief Strategy and Enrolment Officer (CSEO).

This is more than an admissions leadership position. It is an opportunity for an exceptional strategist, relationship builder and organizational leader to help shape the future of GNS, strengthen our position in an evolving educational landscape and advance our long-term strategic priorities.

We are looking for someone who brings fresh perspectives, entrepreneurial thinking, demonstrated leadership and a genuine passion for education. Someone who sees opportunities where others see challenges, understands the importance of exceptional relationships and knows how to translate ambitious ideas into measurable results.

About Glenlyon Norfolk School

Established in 1913, GNS is a co-educational, not-for-profit International Baccalaureate (IB) World Continuum School serving students from Junior Kindergarten through Grade 12 on two beautiful campuses in Victoria, British Columbia.

We provide an exceptional educational experience for students, emphasizing robust academics, healthy social and emotional development, and inquiry-based, student-centred learning within a supportive community. Grounded in our five core values—Truth, Courage, Caring, Individuality and Community—we are committed to empowering students to do their best through truth and courage in learning and in life.

Guided by our Momentum strategic directions, GNS is entering an exciting chapter of innovation and growth. With distinctive day and boarding programs, personalized learning pathways and ambitious campus renewal plans, we are building on a strong foundation to shape the school's future.

The Opportunity

Reporting directly to the Head of School. the CSEO will provide executive leadership in advancing a comprehensive, data-informed enrolment strategy that strengthens demand, expands our reach and supports the long-term sustainability of GNS.

Working collaboratively across the school, you will:

Lead strategic growth: Develop and execute a multi-year enrolment strategy, identify emerging opportunities and strengthen GNS's competitive position across domestic, international and boarding markets.

Elevate the family experience: Champion a personalized, relationship-centred approach to admissions, engagement and retention that fosters meaningful and lasting connections with families.

Drive informed decision-making: Leverage market intelligence, financial insights and performance data to guide strategic priorities, enrolment planning and organizational growth.

Strengthen institutional partnerships: Collaborate with academic and operational leaders, Marketing and Communications, and Advancement to align enrolment priorities with the school's broader strategic direction.

Inspire high performance: Lead and develop a talented Admissions team, fostering innovation, collaboration, accountability and a commitment to exceptional service.

As a trusted strategic partner to the Head of School and an active member of the Senior Leadership Team, you will help influence decisions that extend beyond enrolment and contribute to the overall success of GNS. Working closely with Advancement and Marketing and Communications, you will strengthen strategic alignment across these functions, recognizing the important connections between enrolment, reputation, philanthropy and community engagement.

As GNS continues to evolve, this role offers the potential to contribute to a broader, more integrated approach to institutional strategy and advancement. We are seeking a leader who is energized by this opportunity and brings the vision, adaptability and ambition to grow alongside the school and help shape its future.

What We're Looking For
We are seeking an accomplished and engaging executive who combines strategic vision and commercial acumen with exceptional interpersonal skills, sound judgment and a genuine passion for education.

The ideal candidate will bring:

Significant progressive senior leadership experience in enrolment management, strategic growth, business development, marketing, constituent engagement or a related field, with demonstrated success delivering measurable results.

Proven ability to develop and execute strategies, identify growth opportunities and translate complex financial and market information into informed decisions.

Exceptional relationship-building, communication and influencing skills, complemented by personal warmth, authenticity and emotional intelligence.

A collaborative and empowering leadership style, with a track record of developing high-performing teams, leading change and building strong organizational partnerships.

A degree in a relevant discipline or an equivalent combination of education and senior leadership experience.

Experience in independent schools, post-secondary education or other mission-driven organizations is valued. A background in teaching, advancement, marketing and communications, familiarity with the IB, and/or international recruitment or boarding programs would also be considered an asset, but is not essential.

We welcome candidates who bring fresh perspectives, transferable expertise and the ability to balance ambitious strategic thinking with thoughtful, results-oriented execution.

To learn more about the full scope of this executive opportunity, please review the Chief Strategy and Enrolment Officer Job Description.

Why Join GNS?
This is an opportunity to make a meaningful and lasting contribution to a highly regarded independent school at an exciting stage in its development. You will work alongside a collaborative and committed leadership team, influence strategic decisions and help shape the future of a vibrant school community.

GNS offers a competitive total compensation package, including comprehensive health benefits, a health spending account, virtual health care, a generous RRSP program, tuition discounts, wellness programs and access to our fitness centre.

Located on beautiful Vancouver Island, Victoria offers an exceptional quality of life in one of Canada's most desirable coastal communities.

How to Apply
We invite qualified candidates to submit a letter of interest and detailed résumé by November 20, 2026. However, this position will remain open until filled.

Salary range: $140,000 - $165,000

Anticipated start date: Flexible, no later than summer 2027.

For more information about GNS, visit www.mygns.ca.

Glenlyon Norfolk School is committed to fostering a diverse, equitable, inclusive and welcoming community. We encourage applications from qualified individuals of all backgrounds and experiences. Accommodations are available throughout the recruitment process.

Personal information collected through the recruitment process will be treated confidentially and used only for recruitment purposes.

This is an exciting opportunity for an experienced Finance executive to help lead a significant organizational transformation within a large, complex public sector institution. As Executive Director, Integrated Finance Services, you'll play a pivotal role in launching a new service delivery model, bringing together Finance teams, strengthening partnerships and creating a more consistent, responsive approach to financial services.
This role calls for more than technical Finance expertise. You'll be a visible, empathetic leader who can navigate change, build trust with senior stakeholders and create a strong sense of team identity. You'll balance strategic oversight with hands-on execution, ensuring the new operating model delivers meaningful results for the people and departments it supports.

What's In It for You

• An opportunity to operationalize a significant Finance transformation with institution-wide impact.
• A collaborative environment where relationship-building, thoughtful leadership and continuous improvement are valued.
• The chance to develop high-performing leaders, influence executive decisions and build a service-oriented team culture.
• An exceptional and competitive total rewards package, including comprehensive health and wellness benefits, free day care for families, education reimbursement for immediate family members, and a generous pension plan designed to support your long-term financial well-being.
• Relocation reimbursement support may be provided on a case-by-case basis

• You'll lead the implementation and continuous improvement of an integrated Finance operating model, translating strategic priorities into effective service delivery across multiple portfolios.
• You'll oversee Finance Directors and their teams, establishing clear accountability, service standards, governance frameworks, performance measures and escalation protocols.
• You'll monitor service quality, responsiveness, operational capacity and client outcomes, identifying systemic challenges and driving timely corrective action.

• You'll coach, mentor and develop senior Finance leaders, fostering accountability, succession planning, collaboration and a strong, service-focused team culture.

jobs.description:
Industrial Minerals and Fertilizer Production
Location: Saskatoon, Saskatchewan (in-office)
Reports To: Vice President
Position Type: Full-Time, Executive Leadership
Position Overview

The Chief Financial Officer (CFO) is responsible for the financial management, strategy, and performance of the Company, an industrial minerals and fertilizer producer with mining, mineral processing, manufacturing, and distribution operations.

As a key member of the executive leadership team, the CFO will oversee financial reporting, accounting, treasury, taxation, budgeting, forecasting, financing, and risk management. The CFO will also provide financial leadership for major capital projects, operational improvements, and strategic growth initiatives.

The successful candidate will combine strong financial and commercial judgment with an understanding of capital-intensive industrial operations, manufacturing economics, and commodity markets.

Key Responsibilities

1. Financial Strategy and Leadership

Develop and execute the Company's financial strategy in support of its operational and long-term business objectives.
Advise executive management and the Board of Directors on financial performance, capital allocation, business risks, and strategic opportunities.
Provide financial leadership in major business decisions, investments, acquisitions, and strategic initiatives.
Support corporate governance, Board reporting, and shareholder communications.

2. Financial Reporting and Controls

Oversee corporate accounting, consolidated financial reporting, taxation, and financial systems, coordinating with the accounting teams at both plant locations.
Ensure timely and accurate financial statements in accordance with applicable accounting standards.
Maintain effective financial policies, internal controls, and reporting procedures.
Manage external audits and relationships with auditors, tax advisors, and other professional service providers.
Ensure compliance with applicable financial, tax, and regulatory requirements.

3. Treasury and Corporate Financing

Manage liquidity, cash flow, working capital, and capital structure.
Maintain relationships with banks, lenders, shareholders, and other capital providers.
Negotiate and administer credit facilities, debt financing, and other funding arrangements.
Monitor financial covenants and lender reporting requirements.
Oversee financial risk exposures, including foreign exchange, interest rates, and commodity-related risks.

4. Financial Planning and Performance Management

Lead annual operating and capital budgets, financial forecasts, and long-term financial planning.
Monitor financial performance against budgets and operating plans.
Analyze profitability, production costs, operating margins, and working capital performance.
Establish financial and operational performance indicators to support management decisions.
Work with operations and commercial management to identify opportunities for improved profitability and cost efficiency.

5. Oversight of Plant Finance and Accounting

Provide financial leadership and oversight to professional accounting staff at the Company's two plant locations.
Ensure plant accounting teams maintain responsibility for day-to-day accounting, financial reporting, cost accounting, and financial controls.
Establish consistent financial policies, reporting standards, and procedures across both facilities.
Coordinate with plant accounting personnel on budgets, forecasts, financial performance, and operational cost analysis.
Support plant accounting teams in maintaining effective financial management, accountability, and alignment with corporate financial objectives.

6. Capital Projects and Project Financing

Provide financial oversight of major capital projects, including plant expansions and new production facilities.
Evaluate project economics, financial returns, and investment risks.
Monitor capital budgets, project costs, forecasts, and cash flow requirements.
Support project financing, lender due diligence, and government funding applications.
Ensure appropriate financial controls and reporting throughout project development and construction.

7. Commercial and Operational Support

Provide financial analysis to support product pricing, customer profitability, and commercial decisions.
Evaluate the financial implications of procurement, transportation, distribution, and supply chain arrangements.
Support negotiations involving major customers, suppliers, and service providers.
Monitor customer credit exposure and commercial financial risks.

8. Leadership and Organizational Development

Lead the corporate finance function and provide financial leadership and support to professional accounting personnel at both plant locations.
Establish clear responsibilities, performance expectations, and accountability.
Improve financial systems, reporting capabilities, and business processes.
Promote collaboration between finance, operations, commercial, and executive management.

Qualifications and Experience

Required Qualifications

Professional accounting designation (CPA or equivalent).
Bachelor's degree in accounting, finance, business administration, or a related discipline.
Minimum 15 years of progressive financial management experience, including senior leadership responsibilities.
Experience as a CFO, Vice President Finance, Finance Director, or equivalent senior financial executive.
Experience in manufacturing, mining, mineral processing, chemicals, fertilizers, or another capital-intensive industrial sector.
Strong knowledge of financial reporting, taxation, treasury, internal controls, and corporate financing.
Demonstrated experience with budgeting, forecasting, financial modelling, and capital management.
Experience providing financial oversight of major capital projects.
Proven leadership and team development capabilities.

Preferred Qualifications

Experience in the fertilizer, industrial minerals, potash, or specialty chemicals industries.
Familiarity with Canadian and U.S. markets and cross-border business operations.
Experience with project financing, government funding programs, and industrial construction projects.
Experience with mergers, acquisitions, and corporate restructuring.
Knowledge of mining royalties, environmental liabilities, and asset retirement obligations.
Experience with ERP systems and manufacturing cost accounting.

Key Competencies

Strategic and Commercial Judgment: Ability to evaluate financial and business opportunities and support sound management decisions.

Operational Understanding: Appreciation of manufacturing economics, production costs, capital investment, and supply chain management.

Financial Management: Strong capabilities in cash flow management, financial controls, financing, and financial planning.

Leadership: Ability to develop effective teams and work collaboratively across the organization.

Communication: Ability to present financial information clearly to management, the Board, shareholders, and lenders.

Execution and Accountability: Practical, results-oriented approach with strong organizational and problem-solving skills.

Key Performance Expectations

The CFO will be expected to:

Maintain adequate liquidity and a sustainable capital structure.
Deliver accurate, timely, and meaningful financial reporting.
Support achievement of profitability, cash flow, and working capital objectives.
Maintain effective financial controls and regulatory compliance.
Provide financial oversight of major capital investments and financing initiatives.
Develop an effective finance organization that supports operations and future growth.

Position Profile

The ideal candidate is a commercially minded, hands-on financial executive with experience in capital-intensive industrial operations.

The CFO will be expected to balance financial stewardship with strategic business support, working closely with executive management, plant accounting personnel, and commercial teams to improve financial performance, manage risk, and support profitable growth.
