jobs.description:
Meet Benevity

Benevity is the way the world does good, providing companies (and their employees) with technology to take social action on the issues they care about. Through giving, volunteering, grantmaking, employee resource groups and micro-actions, we help most of the Fortune 100 brands build better cultures and use their power for good. We’re also one of the first B Corporations in Canada, meaning we’re as committed to purpose as we are to profits. We have people working all over the world, including Canada, Spain, Switzerland, the United Kingdom, the United States and more!

Benevity is looking for a Director, Financial Planning & Analysis to lead revenue planning, reporting and operations in one connected team. Reporting to our SVP, Finance, you will own how we set revenue targets, track commits and actuals, forecast, and pay for performance, and you will lead the Revenue Operations team that powers our go-to-market engine.

This is a new, expanded role that brings FP&A and RevOps together. You will turn revenue data into decisions: building commission plans that motivate the right behaviour, forecasting with Sales, Client Success and Finance, and giving executives a single, trusted view of the revenue business. You will lead a team that includes a Revenue Operations group and an FP&A analyst who owns accounting and reporting for revenue.

If you love the intersection of finance and go-to-market, want to move a team from reporting to planning, and are motivated by a mission-driven company, this role is for you.

What You’ll Do

Revenue planning and forecasting

Own the revenue plan: set bookings, ARR and revenue targets and translate them into quotas and territory or segment capacity in partnership with Sales, Client Success and Marketing
Lead company-wide revenue forecast cycle in partnership with GTM Operations.
Prepare scenario analysis and sensitivity modeling to support GTM planning and Sales leadership conversations.
Partner with Finance and GTM leadership during the annual planning cycle, aligning revenue targets, headcount assumptions and GTM investment with financial models and board-level plans.
Build and maintain financial models that link GTM drivers (pipeline, conversion, retention, expansion) to financial outcomes.

Revenue reporting and insight

Develop executive-level dashboards and deliver trusted weekly, monthly and quarterly reporting on top line performance
Translate complex data into clear, actionable insights that shape GTM strategy and drive performance improvements.
Standardize KPIs and definitions across Sales, Marketing and Customer Success, creating a single source of truth for the organization.
Oversee revenue reporting and reconciliation work with Accounting to keep reported revenue accurate, timely and auditable

Sales Compensation

Design, model and refresh sales commission and incentive plans aligned to company strategy and budget
Oversee commission calculation, administration, auditing and dispute resolution, including tooling and controls
Forecast commission expense and report on plan effectiveness, attainment and payout trends

Leadership

Lead, coach and develop a team that includes Revenue Operations and an FP&A analyst, building planning capability alongside strong reporting
Act as a trusted advisor to the executive team, translating financial and operational data into recommendations
Drive continuous improvement in processes, systems and controls as we scale and implement new financial planning tools

What You’ll Bring

8+ years of progressive experience in FP&A, revenue operations, sales finance or a related field, including 3+ years leading people; SaaS or fintech experience strongly preferred
Hands-on experience designing sales commission and incentive plans, and administering them in a tool such as CaptivateIQ or Xactly
Deep experience with revenue reporting and forecasting: targets, pipeline and commit management, actuals, and variance analysis
Advanced financial modeling skills, plus experience with planning software (e.g., Pigment, Adaptive Insights, Anaplan) and an ERP such as NetSuite
Strong command of Salesforce and BI tools (e.g., Tableau), and an understanding of SaaS and fintech metrics
Proven ability to build and scale processes, systems and controls across a go-to-market organization
Curiosity about AI tools (e.g., Claude, ChatGPT) and a track record of using them to improve analysis and automate reporting
Excellent communication skills, with the ability to present to executives and influence Sales, Client Success and Finance leaders
A coaching mindset: you build teams, develop talent and bring people together across functions
Bachelor's degree in Finance, Accounting, Business or a related field; MBA, CPA or CFA is an asset

Discover your purpose at work

We’re not employees, we’re Benevity-ites. From all locations, backgrounds and walks of life, who deserve more …

Innovative work. Growth opportunities. Caring co-workers. And a chance to do work that fills us with a sense of purpose.

If the idea of working on tech that helps people do good in the world lights you up ... If you want a career where you’re valued for who you are and challenged to see who you can become …

It’s time to join Benevity. We’re so excited to meet you.

Where We Work

At Benevity, we embrace a flexible hybrid approach to where we work that empowers our people in a way that supports great work, strong relationships, and personal well-being. For those located near one of our offices, while there’s no set requirement for in-office time, we do value the moments when coming together in person helps us build connection and collaboration. Whether it’s for onboarding, project work, or a chance to align and bond as a team, we trust our people to make thoughtful decisions about when showing up in person matters most.

Join a Company Where DEIB Isn’t a Buzzword

Diversity, equity, inclusion and belonging are part of Benevity’s DNA. You’ll see the impact of our massive investment in DEIB daily — from our well-supported employee resources groups to the exceptional diversity on our leadership and tech teams.

We know that diverse backgrounds, experiences, skills and passions are what move our business and our people forward, so we're committed to creating a culture of belonging with equal opportunities for everyone to shine.

That starts with a fair and accessible hiring process. If you want to feel seen, heard and celebrated, you belong at Benevity.

Candidates with disabilities who may require accommodations throughout the hiring or assessment process are encouraged to reach out to accommodations@benevity.com.

jobs.title: Sales Leader, Enterprise - Americas
jobs.description:
Sales at Ashby is a unique opportunity to sell a product customers genuinely love during an AI-fueled market expansion. Over 5,000 companies rely on Ashby including Shopify, Snowflake, OpenAI, Bolt, and Notion, and our business is durably growing faster than 100% year-over-year. We’re well funded, and on a path to profitability. That's exceptionally rare for a company at our scale, and puts us in the top 10% of benchmarks.

We have, in just a few years, replaced incumbents Greenhouse and Lever more than 500 times each, clear evidence of strong product-market fit and a meaningful opportunity to help modern teams move beyond legacy recruiting software. Ashby replaces 3-5 tools in a consolidation & efficiency play that’s equally loved by recruiters and CFOs. We’re known as a clear AI-leader in the recruiting space.

And the market opportunity is growing. We are rapidly extending from a best-in-class recruiting product toward a multi-product platform, expanding upmarket, into new industries, and internationally. For sales reps, that means a large market full of legacy tools, and a product portfolio that creates room for both new business and expansion. This is a chance to participate in how a category-defining company wins in its next phase of growth.

We are equally intentional about how we build the business. We have established a remote-first, high-performing sales organization that rewards learning and accountability. We use data to set achievable quotas, and reward sustained impact with competitive compensation and meaningful upside. We prioritize coaching and career development, with AEs advancing to Enterprise & Leadership roles in just a few years — 38% of the team who have been here more than a year have been promoted or taken on a new role!

You will work with people who care about craft, customer outcomes, and winning together—without sacrificing the trust, autonomy, and balance required to do your best work over the long term. Don’t just take my word for it, see what the team has to say about working here.

About This Role

TA tools in the Enterprise represent a huge market opportunity, a $1B+ TAM, and the incumbents are legacy players. We are displacing a collection of tools (ATS, Sourcing & CRM, Scheduling, Analytics, Offers & Approvals) with a consolidated talent suite. This is a proven playbook that Workday used to win the HCM market as customers realize value in a multitude of ways, and we are on track to do the same.

Responsibilities

We are seeking an experienced Enterprise Sales Leader in North America to lead the segment and scale our Enterprise AE team - West (Mountain, Pacific, Central). There are three primary responsibilities that this sales leader will take on:

Own the revenue outcomes for the segment, with clear accountability for delivering results. Partner with the senior AEs in a team selling motion to maximize our win rates on the company's largest opportunities. Manage deal risks and help navigate the complexities of large-scale competitive replacement deals.
Build a high caliber team in lock step with market demand. In general we believe that smaller, high caliber teams can achieve remarkable results. Your Enterprise team will be an adept group of solution selling experts.
Establish a reputation for excellence by fostering alignment across Product, Marketing, Solutions Engineering & Professional Services creating a flywheel for future enterprise customer acquisition.

In this role, you’ll report to our Head of AMER Sales (Leigh Brown) and have significant impact in defining our go-to-market strategy and sales methodology. If we are even moderately successful relative to our ambition, we'll have an incredible growth story to tell in just a few years!

You Could Be a Great Fit If

💼 You’ve led and scaled a team of SaaS Enterprise Account Executives delivering $5M/yr+ at a company that has scaled beyond $100M ARR
💰 You have helped win $1M+ SaaS deals with publicly traded companies, and can help your team see around corners on complex deals
🥇 You have a proven track record of hiring and onboarding Ent AEs who can create their own pipeline and close both more tactical ($100k) and strategic ($500k+) deals
📊 You have a strong mental model for enterprise sales execution. At the same time, you're a lifelong learner and are open to new ideas and experimentation.
🤝 You build trusted relationships with customers and confidently facilitate peer-to-peer conversations between senior leaders to deepen partnerships and elevate strategic engagements.
🤓 You become a product and industry expert. You connect the dots quickly. Customers and your team trust you to provide practical advice and relevant stories.
⚙️ You have successfully sold a complex multi-product platform and have won competitive rip-and-replace sales motions.

Bonus

You have sold to Talent and/or People leaders and are familiar with their pains and priorities

You Shouldn't Apply If

You're a dashboard-and-forecast manager who doesn't like to get into the deals and daily operations
You're not keen on learning our substantial product. "That's for SEs" isn't how we approach things here.

Our Philosophy

Here Are a Few Key Points That Should Give You An Idea Of What It Is Like To Work With Us

We have clear expectations about what it means to be a leader at Ashby
We're highly collaborative and we believe in a team-based sales motion to maximize our win rates on high impact deals
We believe in developing subject matter expertise (not just on our product but also the TA space broadly) which allows us to provide a differentiated buyer experience
We continue to make material investments in engineering and product because we know at the end of the day, having the best product makes winning new customers easier

We value a strong sense of ownership, principled thinking over decades of experience, and thoughtful & clear communication both internally and with customers.

Interview Process

Our interview process is designed so you can showcase your achievements and points of learning and apply those to a practical exercise. We'll provide you with sample customer calls and pipeline data so you can develop a well informed perspective on our product and the Enterprise segment. You’ll have opportunities to ask questions of our team throughout.

The interview process for this role is four rounds in the following order:

Intro Call (30 min) - You'll meet with Recruiting to discuss your fit for the role and address questions about our market and solution.
Experience Deep Dive (1 hr) - You'll walk Leigh through your career journey in some detail to highlight your experience, achievements, and points of learning to understand how you've developed into the leader you are today.
Panel Presentation (1 hr) - We'll provide you with pipeline data and seek your perspective on the segment. You'll discuss your approach to hiring, coaching and sales execution.

Job Description

What is the opportunity?

Join RBC's US CIO Technology Strategy and Architecture team as Director, Enterprise Integration Services for the OneRBC: CNB Integration program—a transformational, multi-year initiative that will reshape how RBC operates post-acquisition. In this strategic role, you'll architect and drive the technology integration of City National Bank into RBC's operating model, designing solutions that enable seamless cross-entity operations while establishing repeatable playbooks for future M&A activities.

This is a career-defining opportunity where you'll partner with RBC and CNB enterprise leadership to synthesize complex requirements into cohesive technology strategies spanning identity & access management, cloud infrastructure, network architecture, security posture alignment, and modern workplace modernization. You'll own the validation and de-risking of integration decisions through proof-of-concept initiatives, ensuring solutions deliver tangible business outcomes while maintaining enterprise standards and regulatory compliance.

Beyond CNB, you'll build RBC's M&A integration capability—establishing integration playbooks, standards, and governance models that position RBC to confidently and efficiently integrate future acquisitions. If you're a strategic thinker with deep Microsoft and infrastructure expertise, comfort with constructive challenge, and passion for building organization-scale solutions, this role offers the scope and impact to make a lasting difference at an enterprise scale.

What will you do?

Strategic Integration Design & Delivery

Develop end-to-end integration plans and solutions: Define and evolve technology integration for CNB across identity, cloud, network, security, and workplace domains.
Synthesize requirements into phased roadmaps: Translate competing business/technical needs into actionable plans, balancing trade-offs (e.g., security vs. usability).
Drive alignment with RBC standards: Partner with enterprise teams to ensure CNB solutions adhere to RBC frameworks while fostering innovation.

Stakeholder Leadership & Alignment

Operational Readiness & Governance

Familiarity with RBC’s technology landscape, architecture frameworks, and governance models.
Prior involvement in technology integration during mergers/acquisitions.

jobs.description:
At FSRA, our vision is to ensure financial safety, fairness, and choice for Ontarians. As a financial services regulator, we’re passionate about protecting consumers. Our principles-based approach means we can quickly and effectively respond to the changing needs of consumers and the industry. 

 Our team combines industry expertise with commitment to public service. We attract individuals who are interested in meaningful work and who measure success through outcomes, not inputs. 

 At FSRA, we invest in the personal and professional growth of our team.  We offer a competitive compensation package that includes an employer-matched  defined benefit pension plan, and a comprehensive and competitive benefits plan. We prioritize learning and development, wellbeing, diversity, equity, inclusion and belonging, and community giving. 

 Join FSRA and help us shape the future of regulation for generations to come! 

 Job Description:

 PURPOSE OF POSITION 
 To provide strategic leadership, business ownership, and program direction for FSRA’s Property & Casualty Auto Transformation Program, a multi-year initiative to modernize auto insurance regulation through the implementation of a new supervisory technology platform and future-state operating model.

 The position leads the design, implementation, change management, benefits realization, and operational transition required to enable FSRA’s future Auto Insurance Supervisory Model, including insurer accreditation, risk-based supervision, advanced analytics, streamlined regulatory processes, and enhanced market oversight. Working collaboratively with internal business areas, technology partners, system integrators, insurers, and other stakeholders, the position supports FSRA’s broader modernization agenda by advancing innovative, data-driven, automated, and sustainable supervisory approaches that strengthen regulatory effectiveness and improve consumer outcomes in Ontario.

 KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

jobs.title: AVP, GTO Strategy & Transformation
jobs.description:
As AVP, GTO Strategy & Transformation, you will lead GTO's strategy, transformation agenda, and multi-year roadmap, while also overseeing the GTO global AI platform roadmap. Your focus will be on shaping where GTO is going and ensuring its transformation delivers measurable business value. You will lead multi-year strategy development, operating model transformation, AI enablement, value realization, workforce modernization, and enterprise-scale transformation initiatives. Working closely with Technology, Operations, Finance, People Partners, and business leaders, you will identify opportunities to redesign how work gets done, convert productivity gains into measurable business outcomes, and help build an AI-enabled growth engine that supports growth while maintaining expense discipline. This is an AI-native team — the team uses AI tools, agentic workflows, and LLM-connected platforms as its primary way of working, not as an occasional add-on. 

 Position Responsibilities: 
 GTO Strategy & Strategic Planning: Lead development of multi-year GTO strategy, transformation roadmaps, investment priorities, and strategic planning processes. Translate enterprise objectives into executable plans across Technology and Operations, ensuring strategic intent is reflected in investment and delivery decisions before resources are committed.
 AI-Native Operating Model Transformation: Design and evolve future-state operating models that combine AI, automation, workforce transformation, and technology productivity to sustainably improve capacity, customer outcomes, and efficiency across Technology and Operations — including delivery models, product operating models, workforce structures, and technology ways of working.
 Technology Productivity Realization: Partner with CIOs, COOs, and segment leaders to identify, quantify, and realize value from technology productivity improvements — including product operating models, engineering productivity, and delivery modernization — ensuring productivity gains translate into measurable operational and business outcomes rather than remaining theoretical.
 Operational Transformation & Value Realization: Lead enterprise operational transformation initiatives across customer service, operations, digital channels, workforce productivity, and support functions. Current focus areas may include contact centre transformation, containment optimization, service modernization, and AI-enabled efficiency programs — with the underlying methodology (diagnostic rigor, cross-source data reconciliation, quantified business cases) designed to generalize to future transformation priorities as GTO's agenda evolves.
 Workforce Transformation & Future Skills: Define workforce transition strategies, future-skill requirements, role redesign opportunities, and redeployment approaches required to support AI-enabled operating models. Partner with People Partners, L&D, and segment leaders to drive execution — setting direction, tracking progress, and identifying opportunities to accelerate adoption in partnership with segment leaders.
 Enterprise Value Realization: Own benefit targets and KPI commitments across the GTO transformation portfolio. Establish and govern enterprise value realization methodologies, validate assumptions, reconcile benefit calculations across data sources, create defensible performance baselines, and ensure reported outcomes remain transparent and defensible to senior leadership and ELT — explicitly separating transformation-driven impact from organic or external trends.
 Product & Portfolio Leadership Strengthened: Own and evolve the GTO AI product roadmap, defining priorities and sequencing releases across initiatives and reusable capabilities. Ensure product investments align with GTO strategic priorities and target-state operating model objectives, rather than being pursued independently of the broader transformation agenda.
 Executive & Board-Level Narrative Ownership: Own the preparation of ELT and Board/Technology Committee-ready materials — portfolio checkpoints, anticipated-Q&A briefs, and strategic narratives — translating complex, multi-segment operational and financial data into clear, decision-ready formats. Anticipate scrutiny across every segment and function represented, not just the primary owner's area, and ensure diplomatic, precise, and defensible framing throughout.
 GTO Global AI Platform Roadmap Ownership: Own and oversee the GTO global AI platform roadmap — set the AI direction and transformation agenda for GTO across 14 countries, translate enterprise AI vision into operational priorities, and ensure the platform roadmap is directly sequenced against GTO's broader multi-year strategy and transformation agenda rather than developed in isolation. Apply strategic rigour to problem framing and solution design, ensuring the right problems are prioritized before delivery resources are committed, and assess strategic AI hypotheses through structured pilots prior to scaling investment.
 Outcome Measurement: Establish clear success measures — adoption, operational impact, cycle-time improvements, reliability — and report progress to senior leadership.
 Delivery Execution: Lead end-to-end delivery planning and execution for approved transformation and AI initiatives, ensuring predictable release rhythms and timely removal of blockers.
 Competitive Intelligence: Maintain ongoing awareness of AI and transformation developments across financial services and the broader enterprise landscape. Translate external signals — competitor moves, emerging capabilities, regulatory shifts — into strategic implications for the GTO agenda.
 Production Readiness: Drive readiness reviews with Technology, Enterprise AI, and Risk partners to confirm controls, documentation, and deployment plans are in place prior to release.
 Cross-functional Escalation: Act as escalation point for delivery throughput issues, coordinating cross-functional resolution and trade-off decisions.
 Platform Reuse & Scaling: Lead the shift from project-by-project delivery to a reusable capability model — shared components, templates, evaluation patterns, and connectors.
 Governance Alignment: Ensure solutions align with Responsible AI and model risk expectations, including appropriate documentation and monitoring plans.
 Opportunity Identification & Prioritization: Identify, quantify, and prioritize AI and operational-transformation opportunities across GTO using structured analysis and operational input — including digital-capability heatmapping, deflection/containment sizing, and repeat-contact root-cause analysis. Build data-driven business cases with Finance and Operations leaders, using the same rigor applied to product investment decisions.
 Transformation Investment Prioritization: Evaluate strategic initiatives, validate business cases, recommend investment priorities, and support trade-off decisions across the GTO portfolio.
 Executive Decision Support & Strategic Communications: Serve as a primary architect of executive decision support across GTO — ELT materials, Board and Technology Committee narratives, investor-facing content, anticipated-Q&A preparation, and strategic storyline development. Treat this as a defining capability of the function, not a byproduct of other work: the quality of this synthesis directly shapes how senior leadership and the Board understand GTO's transformation progress.
 AI-First Operating Model: Lead by example in how the team works. Personally use LLM-connected agents, enterprise agentic AI platforms, and AI-augmented workflows to reimagine how portfolio reporting, strategy synthesis, operational diagnostics, and executive communications are produced — including live querying of enterprise data platforms to validate findings in real time. Set the standard for the team and demonstrate that AI-first ways of working are operational — not aspirational.
 People Leadership: Build and lead a high-performing team focused on operational discipline, delivery excellence, and continuous improvement.

 Required Qualifications: 
 Experience leading enterprise strategy, operating model redesign, or large-scale transformation efforts across Technology, Operations, or shared services environments.
 10+ years of experience in strategy, transformation leadership, product leadership, technology delivery, platform programs, and/or AI-enabled transformation, preferably in regulated industries.
 Proven track record delivering complex products, transformation programs, or platforms into production with measurable outcomes, including release planning and dependency management.
 Experience operating at enterprise scale across multiple geographies or business units, including setting targets and holding accountability for benefit realization.
 Demonstrated experience in operational analytics — diagnosing performance issues from raw operational data, reconciling discrepancies across data sources, and translating findings into funded business cases.
 Strong ability to lead cross-functionally in matrixed environments and communicate clearly with senior stakeholders.
 Strong experience in quantitative modeling, scenario analysis, and business case development.
 Working knowledge of modern AI solution patterns (e.g., LLM-enabled assistants, intelligent document processing, agent-based workflows) and production readiness considerations.
 Hands-on orientation with AI productivity tools and agentic workflows; personally comfortable using LLM-connected enterprise tools — including direct querying of enterprise data platforms — to accelerate strategy, reporting, and synthesis work.
 Experience working with executive leadership teams, Boards, Technology Committees, or governance forums to support strategic decision-making.

 Preferred Qualifications 
 Experience evolving operating models from project-based to product/platform delivery.
 Familiarity with MLOps/LLMOps concepts, evaluation approaches, monitoring, and model governance practices.
 Experience influencing people strategy, workforce transformation, or AI reskilling programs in a tech/operations context.
 Demonstrated ability to validate strategic hypotheses through pilots and translate early wins into enterprise momentum.
 Experience with contact centre or operations analytics — IVR/self-service containment, FCR/repeat-contact analysis, workforce management metrics — in a multi-country or multi-segment environment.
 Advanced degree or equivalent experience in engineering, computer science, data science, or business.

 When you join our team: 
 We’ll empower you to learn and grow the career you want. 
 We’ll recognize and support you in a flexible environment where well-being and inclusion are more than just words. 
 As part of our global team, we’ll support you in shaping the future you want to see.

jobs.description:
WorkplaceNL
administers Newfoundland and Labrador’s mandatory, no-fault workplace injury compensation system, funded by employer assessments and investment returns. We promote safe workplaces and provide benefits and services to injured workers, helping improve quality of life across the province.

Overview

Reporting to the Chief Executive Officer, the Vice President, Enterprise Services brings an organization-wide perspective to strategy, performance, technology, people and enterprise risk.
This position provides executive leadership and strategic direction for Enterprise Services and is integral to WorkplaceNL’s modernization agenda, working in partnership with those leading transformation initiatives to ensure improvements are effectively integrated into ongoing operations. This is a long term temporary position, anticipated to span several years while WorkplaceNL advances its transformation and modernization program.

As a member of the Executive Team, you will help set WorkplaceNL’s direction and align people, resources and investments behind shared priorities. Your mandate extends beyond leading your portfolio: you will work across organizational boundaries, navigate competing needs and build support for changes that strengthen services and organizational performance.

You will also lead the continued development of WorkplaceNL’s Enterprise Risk Management Framework and report to the Board’s Governance Committee.

Responsibilities include but are not limited to:

Strategy and planning:
Working with the Executive Team and senior leaders to translate long-term priorities into evidence-based, multi-year plans with clear accountabilities and measurable outcomes.

Technology and information management:
Guiding technology investments, budgets and service delivery to support organizational priorities. Overseeing information management, cybersecurity and business resilience, and advising senior leaders and the Board on technology opportunities and risks.

Performance and improvement:
Leading corporate performance measurement, reporting and continuous improvement. Overseeing Internal Review, program evaluation and quality assurance, and guiding compliance with the Transparency and Accountability Act, annual performance reporting and CEO performance contracts.

Policy and government relations:
Guiding the policy framework and annual policy plan, overseeing statutory reviews and legislative priorities, and maintaining productive relationships with government and other stakeholders.

People and culture:
Setting the context for HR strategies that support employee health and safety, engagement, recruitment, retention and succession. Working with leaders to strengthen organizational capability and foster an ethical, inclusive and accountable workplace.

Enterprise risk:
Strengthening risk management across the organization, ensuring risks inform planning, investment and operational decisions, with clear reporting to the Executive Team and Board.

Who you are

You lead with an enterprise perspective, making decisions based on what serves the organization as a whole. You build trust across functions and understand the people dynamics that shape organizational performance. You can surface competing interests, work through disagreement and bring people together around a clear direction. Where delivery relies on shared resources, you help leaders make sound trade-offs, establish priorities and agree on how work will move forward.
You are comfortable leading change and transformation through influence, ingenuity as well as authority. You communicate the reasons for change clearly, build commitment and maintain accountability for results. You develop strong leaders, address concerns directly and create the conditions for teams to work effectively together.

You bring sound judgement and executive presence to discussions with the CEO, Board, government, and other stakeholders. You can explain complex issues clearly, offer candid advice and connect operational decisions to strategy, risk, financial stewardship and client service.

What you bring:

A university degree in business, public administration, humanities, science or relevant disciplines. A master’s degree in a relevant discipline would be considered an asset.
Minimum of ten years of progressive management experience in a public or private organization leading multiple lines of business and providing services to diverse client groups.
Demonstrated ability to navigate a public sector environment, balancing government priorities, board oversight, public accountability and organizational objectives.
Strong leadership abilities with exceptional interpersonal and communication skills and a proven track record of building effective stakeholder relationships.
Experience conceptualizing and executing strategies that advance cross-organizational priorities, including in the areas of information technology, data and analytics.
Experience applying best practices in enterprise risk management.
Experience with project planning, management and governance, especially as it relates to information technology.
Ability to think strategically, analytically, and use good judgement in providing oversight and solutions to corporate opportunities, challenges and risks.

jobs.title: Director, PCO Strategy Lead
jobs.description:
Director, Strategy Lead, Patient Centered Outcomes (PCO)

Reports to Practice Area Lead, Patient Centered Outcomes

Job Summary

Our Director, Strategy Lead, Patient Centered Outcomes (PCO) is responsible for supervision of the pyschometrics service area unit within PCO to oversee and advise on the development and execution of clinical outcome assessment (COA) studies. Specifically, these studies will focus on supporting our clients’ COA strategy in clinical trials and non-interventional/observational studies. The PCO team supports studies of instrument development, psychometric evaluation (classical and modern methods), and analysis of COA-based study endpoints (e.g., longitudinal modelling, survival analysis, trial exploration, missing data & intercurrent event adjustment).

The majority of the work in this team is regulatory-focused. Therefore, the role involves generating evidence for submission to federal regulators at the US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) and European Medicines Agency (EMA) and occasional interaction with other international regulators. Experience with regulatory agencies is essential for this role.

Essential Duties

Primary duties and responsibilities include, but are not limited to:

Collaborating with business development, marketing, and other service areas to build greater awareness of OPEN Health Group’s (OHG) PCO team capabilities
Leading the development of proposals and proactively engaging in seeking new opportunities
Managing and mentoring of mid-level and junior team members
Overseeing the design and execution of COA studies that align with international scientific standards and regulatory authority recommendations
Overseeing and advising on the development of study documents (such as study proposals, protocols, statistical or psychometric analysis plans, technical reports, and study presentations) and supervising psychometric and/or quantitative analyses to meet the study objectives
Leading or advising on the COA-focused strategy for client interactions/submissions with regulatory agencies (FDA, EMA)
Representing OHG as a COA thought leader and subject matter expert through extramural scientific activities such as: presenting research findings to clients and other external stakeholders, development of presentations at scientific congresses, developing and delivering COA-related educational content (via webinars, scientific congress short courses, etc.), serving as a peer-reviewer, and collaboration with established scientific organizations (ISPOR, ISOQOL, C-PATH) through sub-committee or task force participation. It is anticipated that these extramural scientific activities to will represent approximately 15% of the time spent in this role.

Required Experience, Skills, And Qualifications

Masters degree or PhD in Biostatistics or Psychometrics, or a relevant science (e.g., Health economics, Health Services Research, Public Health, Epidemiology, Pharmacoeconomics, or Psychology)
8+ years of experience in a consulting, pharmaceutical, or industry setting
Strong experience in COA/patient-reported outcomes research: COA instrument development/psychometric validation, quantitative analysis of COA-based clinical study endpoints, measurement strategy advising, and regulatory dossier development and submissions
Proven track record of interacting with regulatory agencies (FDA, EMA, PMDA) and/or health authorities
History of effective leadership of a global team, including strong skills in mentorship of early career professionals
Strong familiarity with current analytic methods used in COA development and validation, including an understanding of appropriate methodology applications and ability to review and interpret results
Extensive working knowledge of relevant regulatory guidance on COAs
Strong communicator (both written and verbal) with attention to detail and accuracy
Strong organizational and project management skills, including the ability to juggle a number of different projects and work to deadlines
Strong experience in business development and ability to generate organic growth opportunities
Well-developed problem-solving skills and a genuine interest in delivering high-quality deliverables
Highly proficient in MS365 including Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Teams and Outlook

About OPEN Health

At OPEN Health, we connect visionary minds, pioneering science, and advanced technology to drive real impact. By uniting people, science, and technology, we activate new opportunities for biopharma innovation. Our expertise across medical affairs and market access unlocks faster, smarter routes to market. We are committed to improving patient outcomes worldwide. To learn more, visit www.openhealthgroup.com.

OPEN Health. The right combination to unlock possibilities.

What We Offer

The Director, Global Technology & Operations Strategy & Transformation will help shape and execute strategic priorities across Global Technology & Operations (GTO), with a significant focus on leading the AI program and translating strategy into measurable business outcomes.

 The Director will lead the AI program across GTO, bringing together strategy, business case development, funding, program governance, technical delivery, adoption, and value realization. This includes managing AI program funding, ensuring funding is directed to the appropriate initiatives and teams, and maintaining visibility into how initiatives are progressing against delivery commitments, defined success criteria, and approved budgets.

 Working closely with the VP of GTO and senior stakeholders across Business, Technology, Enterprise AI, Finance, and Risk, the Director will provide an integrated view of the AI program, drive accountability across teams, identify areas requiring leadership attention, and enable informed decisions on priorities, funding, execution, and outcomes.

 The Director will also help shape how GTO delivers its AI agenda, establishing approaches to prioritize and sequence initiatives, accelerate execution, and scale reusable AI capabilities across segments and countries. This includes helping establish a practical path from opportunity identification through development, production, and adoption, while focusing resources on initiatives that can deliver the greatest strategic and business impact.

 Position Responsibilities
 GTO Strategy & Transformation: Partner with the VP of GTO and senior leaders to translate strategic priorities into executable strategies, roadmaps, initiatives, and measurable outcomes. Connect priorities across teams, identify opportunities and risks, and provide insights and recommendations to support executive decision-making.
 AI Program Leadership & Governance: Lead the end-to-end AI and Automation program across GTO, establishing a single integrated view of initiatives, priorities, dependencies, funding, and outcomes. Establish program governance and operating rhythms and work across Product Owners, Segment Leads, Technology, and business and functional partners to drive execution, alignment, and accountability.
 AI Strategy, Prioritization & Delivery Approach: Help define how GTO identifies, assesses, prioritizes, sequences, and delivers AI initiatives. Develop practical prioritization and delivery approaches that consider strategic alignment, business value, delivery readiness, scalability, complexity, funding requirements, dependencies, and risk. Continuously assess the portfolio to ensure resources remain focused on the highest-value opportunities and identify where initiatives should be accelerated, repositioned, or deprioritized.
 Business Case & AI Program Funding: Lead the planning, mobilization, and partner engagement required to develop business cases for AI execution and future funding, including cost-benefit analysis, expected outcomes, success criteria, delivery requirements, and risk considerations. Manage AI program funding and recommend allocation or reallocation across initiatives and teams based on strategic priorities, expected value, delivery readiness, and performance.
 Delivery Excellence, Performance & Value Realization: Oversee AI initiatives across technical delivery, business outcomes, adoption, success criteria, budget utilization, risks, and dependencies. Assess whether initiatives are delivering against their original commitments, drive accountability for results, and identify where intervention, reprioritization, or funding adjustments are required. Ensure realized outcomes can be traced back to approved business cases and defined success measures.
 Executive Reporting & Stakeholder Management: Provide the VP of GTO and senior leadership with a consolidated view of the AI program, including roadmap progress, funding utilization, delivery performance, value realization, risks, dependencies, and decisions required. Maintain effective engagement across sponsors, segments, Technology, Enterprise AI, Finance, Risk, and other partners, translating complex information into clear executive insights and recommendations.
 AI-Driven Transformation & Reusable Capabilities: Identify opportunities to fundamentally redesign processes and ways of working through AI and Automation, moving beyond incremental improvements. Drive the development, reuse, and adoption of scalable AI capabilities, standards, playbooks, and common approaches that accelerate delivery and reduce duplication across GTO.

 Required Qualifications
 8+ years of experience across strategy and transformation, technology, AI, program management, product management, or related disciplines, with demonstrated experience leading complex, cross-functional programs.

 Strong strategic and analytical capabilities, with demonstrated experience translating strategy into prioritized programs, roadmaps, business cases, funding recommendations, and measurable outcomes.
 Strong financial acumen, including experience developing and evaluating business cases, cost-benefit analysis, managing budgets and funding, establishing success measures, and assessing value realization.
 Strong understanding of AI platforms and modern AI solution patterns, with sufficient technical fluency to understand delivery plans, challenge assumptions, assess dependencies and risks, and engage credibly with Technology and AI leaders.

 Exceptional executive communication and stakeholder management skills, with the ability to synthesize complex strategic, financial, business, and technical information into clear insights, recommendations, and decisions for senior leadership.
 Demonstrated ability to influence and challenge senior stakeholders, drive accountability without direct authority, create structure in ambiguous environments, and manage competing strategic priorities.
 Demonstrated use of AI productivity tools and agentic workflows to accelerate analysis, synthesis, reporting, decision-making, and content development.

 Preferred Qualifications
 Experience leading or managing an enterprise-scale AI, Automation, technology, innovation, or transformation program, including prioritization, funding, delivery, and value realization.

jobs.title: Director, Internal Controls & Finance Transformation
jobs.description:
Neo Performance Materials Helps Build Technologies of Tomorrow

Neo is fast-forwarding the green energy transition by manufacturing the critical building blocks of modern, sustainable technologies. Our advanced industrial materials - including magnetic powders and magnets, specialty chemicals, metals, and alloys - enhance efficiency and performance in everyday products and next-generation innovations.

Neo operates three business segments: Magnequench, Chemicals & Oxides, and Rare Metals. With a global footprint, we have eight manufacturing facilities across China, the United States, Germany, Canada, Estonia, Thailand, and the United Kingdom, along with a dedicated research and development centre in Singapore.

Be part of a global organization driving innovation and sustainability. At Neo, you will have the opportunity to contribute to meaningful work while growing your career in a collaborative and dynamic environment.

Join us in shaping a cleaner, more sustainable future.

Role Overview:

Neo is seeking a Director to strengthen how we manage internal controls, policies and continuous improvement across its global business. This role combines ownership of the finance policy and controls environment with delivery of practical, cross-functional improvement initiatives. The Director will work with Corporate and regional Finance, IT, operations, senior management and external advisors, and will lead the Manager, Finance Systems & Data Governance and work closely with external service providers.

What you will do:

Lead the continued development and elevating Neo’s internal control environment, including control ownership, documentation, evidence standards, issue assessment and remediation tracking.
Own governance and ongoing maintenance of the finance policy suite—including the accounting policy manual, standard operating procedures (SOPs) and delegation of authority / approval matrix—coordinating technical accounting content with Corporate Accounting.
Establish an appropriate cadence for policy reviews, approvals, communication, training and implementation in relation to ICFR.
Establish and manage a pipeline of Finance improvement initiatives: identify and prioritize opportunities, define scope and deliverables, assign owners, and project-manage work through implementation.
Partner with Neo’s regional Finance, IT and operations functional leaders to strengthen processes and controls, including system-dependent controls, spreadsheets, reporting and approval workflows.
Manage external advisors by agreeing scope, evaluating recommendations and deliverables, monitoring timelines and ensuring follow-through.

We are looking for a hybrid social strategist who balances creative vision with deep analytical rigor to guide our social and creator-led initiatives. In this role, you will act as the strategic engine for client accounts—building sharp social playbooks, scoping complex programs, consulting and collaborating with internal teams and translating performance data into clear creative direction and effective strategy.

We are looking for someone who understands social because they have actively helped shape brands’ social presences, understand how to identify culturally relevant opportunities, know how to source strategic creator partners, cultivate communities, and evolve a brand’s social approach in real time based on data and insights.

Look beyond topline metrics to understand why content is or is not working, and train teams to do the same.
Build a culture of test-and-learn across client work, using performance signals to sharpen creative output in real time.
Extract actionable insights from performance data to directly inform future creative iterations and strategic pivots.

Bring a strong social and performance-led POV to creative conversations
Consult with and advise the dedicated influencer team on campaign strategy, target creator personas, and content themes to ensure strategic alignment (hands-off on logistics and campaign management).
Partner with creative teams to advise on creative social strategy on active programs.

Evaluate emerging platforms, viral trends, and AI-assisted creative workflows to continuously elevate agency output.

The role combines strategic leadership, technical oversight, people leadership, delivery execution, operational accountability, and vendor/financial management to drive technology excellence and measurable business value. The AVP partners closely with Product, Client Experience, Architecture, Cybersecurity, Operations, Engineering, and Business leaders to ensure digital assets are resilient, scalable, secure, reusable, and aligned to enterprise priorities.

This role operates in a complex, high-visibility environment where digital platform reliability, modernization, and cross-business enablement are critical to Client outcomes. The leader must be able to bring clarity to a broad mandate, make decisions in ambiguity, and build a high-performing technology organization that balances speed, stability, security, and long-term platform health.

What will you do?

Technology Strategy, Platform Enablement & Engineering
Shape, communicate, and align the digital technology strategy across business units, ensuring it supports near-term delivery commitments and longer-term modernization objectives.
Partner with Business Leads, Product, Client Experience, Architecture, Cybersecurity, Operations, and Enterprise Technology to define platform roadmaps, OKRs, sequencing, and investment priorities.
Provide thought leadership on the evolution of shared digital platforms, including identity, web, mobile, integration, data enablement, and reusable digital capabilities.
Promote technology stack standards, modern engineering practices, automation, and architectural discipline, balancing build vs. buy vs. partner decisions in a complex technology ecosystem.
Ensure design and engineering decisions account for reusability, scalability, security, maintainability, accessibility, and technical debt reduction.
Create the conditions for exceptional digital experiences by enabling business and product teams with reliable, scalable, secure, and reusable platforms.
Platform Delivery & Execution
Accountable for end-to-end delivery of digital platform capabilities, including oversight of internal delivery teams, vendors, system integrators, and total cost of ownership.
Drive delivery excellence by improving velocity, quality, reliability, predictability, and agile maturity across multiple squads.
Track delivery metrics, identify bottlenecks, and implement targeted productivity and delivery maturity improvements.
Serve as the primary escalation point for platform, delivery, vendor, and dependency-related issues, enabling rapid resolution in a complex environment.
Ensure delivery is integrated across product, architecture, engineering, operations, cybersecurity, and business priorities.
Embed test-and-learn, automation, and continuous improvement practices to improve speed, quality, and sustainability.
People Leadership & Capability Development
Lead, mentor, and develop technology leaders and teams, fostering a collaborative, inclusive, accountable, and execution-focused culture.
Design and optimize team structures to support clear ownership, delivery outcomes, modernization priorities, and clear accountabilities.
Partner with Chapter, Engineering, Product, and Business leaders on workforce planning, role clarity, succession planning, and capability development.
Build internal capability in digital engineering, enablement, agile delivery, vendor management, and operational excellence.
Coach leaders to manage performance effectively, clarify ownership, and build resilient teams through change and transformation.
Financial & Vendor Management
Lead budget management, including annual planning, cost tracking, capitalization, forecasting, and investment prioritization.
Manage strategic vendor and system integrator relationships, holding partners accountable for delivery quality, outcomes, knowledge transfer, and value realization.
Drive cost transparency and technology spend optimization across applications, infrastructure, security, vendor, and platform investments.
Identify opportunities to reduce long-term dependency on external partners while strengthening internal platform ownership and capability.
Operational Excellence, Risk & Security
Ensure stability, security, technology currency, resiliency, and end-of-life decommissioning for applications within scope.
Establish governance processes that balance speed of delivery with risk management, audit, regulatory, cybersecurity, and control requirements.
Partner with Application Operations to ensure effective incident management, change management, disaster recovery, and business continuity planning.
Proactively manage operational risk, application health, technical debt, and service reliability across shared digital capabilities.
Cross-Functional Collaboration & Stakeholder Engagement
Act as a strategic technology partner to leaders across Product, Client Experience, Business, Operations, Architecture, Cybersecurity, and Enterprise Technology.
Communicate digital strategy, delivery status, risks, trade-offs, and dependencies with clarity and transparency.
Represent the Digital technology function in executive forums, bringing enterprise perspective, external insight, and pragmatic recommendations.
Strengthen alignment between technology investments, business priorities, Client experience outcomes, and enterprise digital strategy.

Accountabilities

Align digital strategy with business objectives, Client outcomes, enterprise standards, and shared technology priorities.
Define and monitor roadmaps, OKRs, modernization priorities, and delivery sequencing.
Oversee execution across delivery teams, vendors, system integrators, and enterprise partners.
Establish governance, track delivery metrics, and drive productivity, quality, and reliability improvements.
Manage budgets, vendor relationships, and cost optimization opportunities.
Build and sustain a high-performing, engaged, inclusive, and platform-oriented technology organization.
Ensure digital platforms are secure, scalable, resilient, reusable, and positioned to support future growth.

What you need to succeed?

Qualifications & Experience

Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or related field; advanced degree or MBA is an asset.
10+ years of experience in senior technology leadership roles with demonstrated success delivering complex, mission-critical digital platforms.
Experience leading modernization and enablement of digital platforms such as identity, web, mobile, integration, or client/advisor experience platforms.
Proven ability to lead technology teams through transformation, platform ownership, and operating model evolution.
Strong financial acumen with experience managing sizable technology budgets, vendor portfolios, and total cost of ownership.
Strong stakeholder management, executive communication, and organizational leadership skills.
Experience in regulated financial services is valuable; depth in digital enablement, engineering excellence, and vendor-heavy delivery environments is prioritized.
As this position is posted in several locations, we specify that bilingualism (French, English, both oral and written) is required for Quebec only for the frequent interactions with English and French-speaking colleagues or internal partners across Canada or worldwide

Mindset & Behaviours

Decisive leader comfortable operating in ambiguity, complexity, and transformation.
Strong technical credibility with the ability to challenge architecture, delivery practices, platform decisions, and CI/CD approaches.
Builder mindset with equal focus on fixing, scaling, enabling, and simplifying.
Pragmatic, outcomes-driven decision-maker who balances speed, stability, risk, and long-term application health.
Collaborative leader who builds trust, drives momentum, and creates clarity across complex stakeholder groups.
Critical thinker who challenges the status quo constructively and drives continuous improvement.
Strong coaching orientation with a commitment to developing leaders, teams, and internal capability.

What’s in it for you?

A competitive salary and bonus program, based on market scale
A flexible group insurance program starting on your first day of work to meet your needs and those of your family.
Time off that allows you to focus on the moments that matter most. 20 vacation days per year.
Our Share Ownership Program gives you the opportunity to invest in Sun Life while benefiting from employer matching contributions.
We are proud to be included in Great Place to Work's 2026 list of Canada's Best Workplaces.
A warm, supportive, and inclusive culture.

In addition to Base Pay, eligible Sun Life employees participate in various incentive plans, payment under which is discretionary and subject to individual and company performance. Certain sales focused roles have sales incentive plans based on individual or group sales results.

Diversity and inclusion have always been at the core of our values at Sun Life. A diverse workforce with wide perspectives and creative ideas benefits our Clients, the communities where we operate and all of us as colleagues. We welcome applications from qualified individuals from all backgrounds.

Persons with disabilities who need accommodation in the application process, or those needing job postings in an alternative format, may e-mail a request to thebrightside@sunlife.com.

We are proud to be a hybrid organization that offers our employees the choice and flexibility to work from both the office and virtually based on the needs of the business, our Clients and you.

jobs.description:
Imagine yourself…

Doing meaningful work that makes an everyday impact on the world around you.
Growing your expertise and expanding your skillset with every project.
Owning your ambition and fueling your career growth.

At Trojan Technologies, you have the power to make it possible.

Trojan Technologies, a Veralto company, plays a vital role in making the various stages of the water treatment process more effective and efficient. Our products and services have applications across municipal wastewater, drinking water, environmental contaminant treatment, and residential water treatment, along with ultra-purification of water used in food and beverage manufacturing, pharmaceutical processing and semiconductor applications.

When you join the Trojan Technologies team and the broader Veralto network, you become part of a unique culture where purpose meets possibility: where the work we do makes an everyday impact on the world’s vital water resources, and where you’ll have the power to deepen your skillset, own your ambition, and fuel your career growth.

Take a moment to watch our video: The Power to Make Things Possible (https://vimeo.com/burnsmarketing/review/823050239/c5d19b300c)

We are seeking a Director, Planning, Procurement & Inventory to lead the enterprise function that turns customer demand into a credible, executable supply plan, secures material availability, and optimizes inventory across regions and fulfilment models.

This is an opportunity to bring Demand Planning, Supply and Production Planning, Tactical Procurement, and Inventory into one connected operating model. You will lead through significant organizational and ERP-enabled change while improving customer service and working capital together.

This position is located in London, Ontario, and will be onsite.

What You Will Do

Lead enterprise planning and SIOP. Own demand planning, forecasting, executive SIOP, the approved enterprise supply plan, planning risk, and cross-functional escalation across regions and businesses.
Strengthen supply and production planning. Lead master production scheduling, MRP, material-availability management, shortage recovery, and planning logic across Make-to-Stock, Engineer-to-Order, Configure-to-Order, and aftermarket flows.
Direct tactical procurement and inventory governance. Lead tactical buying, supplier-delivery performance, purchasing master data, inventory strategy, service-level policy, E&O governance, record accuracy, and inventory improvement.
Own Procurement Planning & inventory business processes through ERP transformation. Lead relevant Order-to-Cash and Procure-to-Pay workstreams from design and testing through cutover, adoption, stabilization, process governance, and master-data health.
Build one capable enterprise organization. Establish a common KPI architecture, management cadence, decision rights, standard work, talent development, succession coverage, and an everyday continuous-improvement operating system.

The essential requirements of the job include:

A bachelor’s degree in Supply Chain, Engineering, Operations, Business, or a related field.
Progressive leadership of enterprise planning, tactical procurement, and inventory in a complex manufacturing environment.
Demonstrated leadership across a combination of Make-to-Stock, Engineer-to-Order, Configure-to-Order, and aftermarket or service-parts planning.
Direct ownership of Demand Planning and an executive S&OP or SIOP process that drove cross-functional decisions.
End-to-end leadership of a major ERP business-process transformation covering design, testing, cutover, adoption, and stabilization.

It would be nice if you also possess:

Experience leading substantial tactical buying and multi-site or multi-region inventory, with evidence of improved service, supplier delivery, inventory productivity, and record accuracy.
Experience with Infor LN or a comparable enterprise ERP, APICS CPIM or CSCP certification, Lean or Six Sigma certification, or deployment of VES, DBS, Lean, or a comparable operating system.

Location and travel

The role is based in London, Ontario and supports sites and teams across multiple regions. Approximately 25% travel is expected, including periodic international travel. Travel may increase during major ERP deployment and operational-transformation activities.

Why this role matters

You will shape how demand, supply, procurement, inventory, commercial requirements, manufacturing execution, customer service, logistics, finance, and technology connect around one enterprise plan. Success means creating durable processes and capable teams that sustain performance without individual heroics or permanent expediting.

We offer:

Flexible working hours
Paid vacations
Professional onboarding and training options
Powerful team looking forward to working with you
Career coaching and development opportunities
Health benefits
RSP

jobs.title: Associate Director / Director, Financial Advisory
jobs.description:
The Financial Advisory Team at Teneo

Teneo’s global Financial Advisory business advises corporates, creditors and other financial stakeholders in situations of financial stress and distress. No two situations are the same. Our advice and approach is tailored to each situation and each client. At Teneo, we believe such occurrences present new opportunities for our clients. Opportunities to restore value, raise new capital, pivot in a new direction and ultimately, identify certainty amidst chaos. Teneo partners with clients to find viable opportunities that will protect and enhance value and help them to build strategies that will most benefit their business and/or investment goals.

Integrating the disciplines of financial advisory, management consulting, investor relations, strategic communications, government affairs, risk analysis and talent advisory, Teneo’s global Financial Advisory team guides companies and their stakeholders through periods of uncertainty and stress. We help address the challenges a business faces, whether that is targeted performance improvement to Financial Advisory, or delivering a route to recover value, our focus is delivering certainty from uncertainty.

Teneo is expanding its already established global Financial Advisory footprint, now in Canada. The Canadian Financial Advisory team will join forces with the already established Strategy and Communications platform which has offices in Toronto, Montreal and Calgary. We are hiring at several levels.

The Role – Associate Director, Toronto

This is an excellent opportunity to work alongside our established team who will support you to utilise and enhance your advisory skills and experience. You will work alongside some of the most experienced practitioners in the field advising the boards, management teams, lenders and shareholders of companies which are underperforming and/or facing any financial stress.

As an Associate Director / Director in the team, you will have the opportunity to work and lead on a diverse range of engagements across all sectors, with plenty of responsibility for leading workstreams, managing junior staff and supporting Directors and Managing Directors in client-facing delivery.

Key Responsibilities

Client Service

Preparation of engagement letter(s) and ensuring adherence to all compliance requirements.
Manage parts or all of the engagement, providing support to the Managing Director/ Director (or often directly to Senior Managing Director) in managing external stakeholders.
Managing insolvency engagements under the Bankruptcy and Insolvency Act, the Companies’ Creditors Arrangement Act and other statutes.
Support management teams in preparing and challenging business plans, short term cash flow forecasts and Financial Advisory plans.
Providing comprehensive financial restructuring and cash management services to identify working capital and other cash flow improvements.
Reviewing and stress-testing integrated business plans, budgeting and forecasting models using a fact-based, data driven approach, including KPI definition, data visualization, reporting automation and touchless forecasting.
Establishment or enhancement of company finance functions and processes.
Develop, analyse and present Financial Advisory options using input from other teams, e.g. insolvency or tax analysis, sector and financial modelling. Liaise with the Company’s legal advisors to understand key aspects of legal documentation and also drive any documentation processes (term sheets, waivers, loan documentation etc.)
Apply an understanding of engagement economics.
Apply an understanding of financial and risk management.

Knowledge Acquisition

Build client relationship skills, sector knowledge and continue to develop leadership skills.
Continue to build technical expertise, broader business advisory and people management skills.
Understand the market, topical issues and our Financial Advisory propositions.

People and Leadership

Support practice and talent development.
Provide on-job coaching and development to staff.
Develop junior staff outside of jobs through appraising and mentoring.
Support wider Financial Advisory training initiatives.
Manage diverse teams within an inclusive team culture where people are recognised for their contribution.

Business Development

Start to own elements of business development including actively supporting business development activities, building and expending your own contact network and supporting Director/ Managing Director/Senior Managing Director-led marketing and sales activities.
Participate in existing business development programmes and key client accounts.
Identify opportunities to expand engagments as well as opportunities to provide wider Teneo services to existing clients.
Take responsibility for leading marketing initiatives aimed at specific channels to market, or events.

Key Skills & Experience

Qualified accountant (CPA or equivalent), both time and exam qualified.
Financial Advisory experience gained either as an advisor within a professional services company, consultancy or investment bank; as an analyst in a debt or special situations funds. An understanding of debt markets, banking, loan agreements and other relevant financial and legal documentation.
Understanding of financial statements and related data to assess historical financial performance and future outlook for client companies and prospects.
Good understanding of the Financial Advisory marketplace, its trends, and key players (principals and advisors).
Very strong analytical skills, including: business analytics, business planning, short term cash flows, financing options. A basic understanding of insolvency legislation and practice is not a prerequisite but helpful.
Excellent interpersonal skills.
Strong project management skills, with ability to lead mid-large teams and develop people.

What We Offer

As a Teneo employee, you'll enjoy unique benefits including flexible time off policy; medical, dental, and vision coverage; long-term disability, and life insurance; RRSP plan with corporate matching; team events; snacks; and other perks.

Our Commitment to Diversity and Inclusion

Teneo is an equal opportunity employer and promotes a diverse and inclusive workplace. Teneo considers all applicants without regard to race, color, religion, creed, national origin, age, sex, marital status, ancestry, disability, veteran status, gender identity, genetic information, or sexual orientation or any other status protected by applicable law.

Total Compensation Package

Expected compensation for Associate Director is CAD110,000 - CAD160,000 plus annualized bonus. Expected compensation for Director level is CAD150,000 - CAD200,000 plus annualized bonus.

RRSP match, healthcare coverage and a broad range of additional benefits and perks.

About Teneo

Teneo is the global CEO advisory firm. We partner with our clients globally to do great things for a better future.

Drawing upon our global team and expansive network of senior advisors, we provide advisory services across our five business segments on a stand-alone or fully integrated basis to help our clients solve complex business challenges. Our clients include a significant number of the Fortune 100 and FTSE 100, as well as other corporations, financial institutions, and organizations.

Our full range of advisory services includes strategic communications, investor relations, financial transactions and restructuring, management consulting, physical and cyber risk, organizational design, board and executive search, geopolitics and government affairs, corporate governance, ESG and DE&I.

The firm has more than 1,800 employees located in 40+ offices around the world.

jobs.title: Head of Machine Learning
jobs.description:
Company Description
Uyir Lab is an AI research lab focused on making AI agents accurate in underrepresented languages, as they are truly spoken in everyday life. The lab addresses gaps in dialects, code-mixing, and cultural context for languages that are widely spoken but barely present on the web, starting with Tamil and expanding to Sinhala, Punjabi, Swahili, Hausa, Amharic, Fula, Oromo, Javanese, Bhojpuri, and more. Uyir Lab’s approach combines consented voice data from native speakers, deep linguistic mapping, and proprietary models like Nila for Tamil, delivered via a “Language Brain” layer that plugs into existing AI agents. As AI takes on critical work in sectors such as banking, health, and customer service, Uyir Lab’s mission is to reduce costly misunderstandings and give every language a life in AI, working closely with agent builders, native speakers, and community partners.
Role Description
The Head of Machine Learning is a full-time remote role leading the design, development, and deployment of language-focused ML systems across Uyir Lab’s growing portfolio of models and languages. This position oversees end-to-end machine learning pipelines: defining research directions, shaping model architectures, guiding experimentation, and driving productionization of models for real-world AI agents. The role includes managing and mentoring a multidisciplinary ML team, collaborating with data engineers and linguists to build high-quality datasets, and ensuring robust evaluation for dialect-aware, culturally grounded performance. The Head of Machine Learning partners with product and engineering teams to integrate Uyir Lab’s “Language Brain” into external applications, sets technical standards for scalability and reliability, and contributes to strategic decisions about new languages, platforms, and partnerships.
Qualifications

Strong foundations in Computer Science, including algorithms, data structures, distributed computing, and software engineering best practices.
Expertise in Machine Learning and Data Science, covering model development, training at scale, evaluation, optimization, and experimentation workflows.
Specialized experience in Natural Language Processing (NLP), particularly for low-resource or multilingual settings, including sequence models, transformers, and representation learning.
Hands-on skills in Pattern Recognition, statistical modeling, and signal processing methods relevant to speech, text, and multimodal data.
Proficiency with modern ML ecosystems (e.g., Python, PyTorch or TensorFlow, Hugging Face, ML Ops tools) and cloud-based training infrastructure.
Demonstrated experience leading ML or research teams, setting technical direction, and delivering production-ready models in collaboration with product and engineering.
Background in building or improving language technologies (ASR, MT, chatbots, dialogue systems, or language understanding) is highly beneficial.

jobs.title: Head of Data Analytics - Veeva Ostro
jobs.description:
Veeva Systems is a mission-driven organization and pioneer in industry cloud, helping life sciences companies bring therapies to patients faster. As one of the fastest-growing SaaS companies in history, we surpassed $3B in revenue in our last fiscal year with extensive growth potential ahead.

At the heart of Veeva are our values: Do the Right Thing, Customer Success, Employee Success, and Speed. We're not just any public company – we made history in 2021 by becoming a public benefit corporation (PBC), legally bound to balancing the interests of customers, employees, society, and investors.

As a Work Anywhere company, we support your flexibility to work from home or in the office, so you can thrive in your ideal environment.

Join us in transforming the life sciences industry, committed to making a positive impact on its customers, employees, and communities.

The Role

Veeva Ostro operates as a startup within Veeva, and sits at the intersection of life sciences, marketing, and artificial intelligence. We empower pharmaceutical brands, healthcare providers (HCPs), and patients by orchestrating AI-enabled omnichannel engagement across the entire patient and prescriber lifecycle.

As the Head of Data Analytics
, you will lead the design, development, and continuous improvement of the data systems and associated measurement analyses that sit at the intersection of our products, customers, and commercial strategy. Our products generate significant data as users ask questions and take action, and you will work with the product team to surface and execute on insights that govern how our product evolves. This data is also used by our customers in their planning efforts, and you will work closely with our client service and implementation teams to enable and deliver on customized analyses that reflect the nuances of each client’s strategy. To deliver on the above, you will proactively architect, build, and scale the next generation of our data platform to make it modern, scalable, and AI-ready.

As the leader of the Data Analytics team, you will contribute to the team in a “player / coach” capacity, providing both executive leadership and hands-on expertise and contributions.

What You'll Do

Modern Data Architecture & Engineering: Work alongside platform and data engineers to upgrade our existing data architecture to be high fidelity, AI-ready, and easily accessible for both internal and external users
Customer Data Integrations: Guide the execution of data integrations into select customer systems in partnership with our solutions engineering team
Product Analyses: Uplevel our standard suite of analytics and measurement insights in partnership with our product team
Custom Analyses: Execute on client-specific, custom analytical requests in partnership with our client services team
Leadership & Team Mentorship: Direct and grow a team of data analysts and data engineers

Requirements

Deep, hands-on expertise in SQL / Python and strong capabilities in data modeling, advanced quantitative analysis, and working with large data sets
Strong command of modern data architecture particularly in enabling AI readiness. You will not be the sole engineer building every component yourself, but you need enough technical depth to actively participate in the design and build
10+ years of progressive experience in data science/analytics and/or data engineering roles including in a managerial capacity leading teams
Recent work experience should relate to the pharmaceutical / life sciences industry
Undergrad or masters in a technical discipline (computer science, statistics, engineering, math, physics, etc.)

Interviewing with Veeva

We value your time and believe in a transparent hiring process. Here is the process you can expect.

Follow the application process and submit your resume.
If moving to the interview stage, our process is as follows:
A conversation with the hiring manager
A personality assessment (unless you have already completed it with Veeva previously)
A practical case exercise
A final conversation with our group's Senior Leader

Once all interviews are complete, the manager will be in touch with a final decision.

Perks & Benefits

Medical, dental, vision, and basic life insurance
PTO and company-paid holidays
Retirement programs
1% charitable giving program
