jobs.title: Vice President Finance, Americas
jobs.description:
The Vice President, Finance, Americas is responsible for providing strategic financial leadership and oversight across the Americas region. This role partners with executive and business leaders to drive financial performance, support growth initiatives, ensure compliance with financial and regulatory requirements, and deliver accurate financial planning, reporting, and analysis. The VP Finance leads regional finance functions, including accounting, budgeting, forecasting, tax, treasury, internal controls, and financial operations, while fostering a high-performing team and supporting the achievement of organizational objectives.

Reports to the Chief Financial Officer.

Responsibilities

1. Financial Reporting & Accounting

Oversee accounting operations for the Americas region, including general ledger, month-end/quarter-end closing, and consolidation.
Own inventory accounting for the Memphis distribution center — valuation methodology, standard costing, cycle counts, and obsolescence/reserve policy.
Ensure COGS accuracy and margin analysis tied to distribution operations.
Ensure accuracy of financial statements prepared in accordance with local GAAP in each jurisdiction (US, Canada, and LatAm countries).
Prepare and submit financial reports in compliance with IFRS and Group accounting standards, ensuring quality and compliance.
Coordinate with external auditors for annual audits, implement improvement plans, and maintain effective communication with internal and external audit teams.
Work closely with the HQ finance team to ensure consistency in reporting formats, policies, and processes.

2. Compliance

Maintain and enhance internal control and accounting procedures to align with Group policies and US/Canadian/LatAm regulations.
Ensure customs and bonded warehouse compliance — duty deferral, in-bond transfers, and CBP requirements — for the Memphis distribution center, partnering with trade compliance and logistics teams.
Ensure compliance with local direct and indirect tax regulations, including corporate income tax, VAT/GST, and multi-state US sales/use tax nexus; complete filings accurately and on time.
Regularly review the reasonableness of intercompany transfer pricing across US, Canada, and LatAm entities, and assess associated risks.

3. Treasury & Financial Planning

Manage cash flow, working capital, and banking relationships across the Americas to ensure liquidity and efficient funding.
Support financing activities and treasury optimization.
Provide budgeting, forecasting, and financial analysis to support operational decision-making across HQ, sales & marketing offices, and the distribution center.

4. System & Process Enhancement

Drive ERP system integration and automation to improve reporting efficiency, data accuracy, and close timelines.
Identify process improvement opportunities across order-to-cash and purchase-to-pay to enhance timeliness and reliability of financial information.

Qualifications and Experience

Bachelor's degree or above in Accounting, Finance, or related field; CPA/ACA/ACCA qualification preferred.
Minimum 15 years of accounting or finance experience, including at least 6 years in a managerial or Controller role.
Solid knowledge of IFRS, US/Canadian tax regulations, compliance, and internal controls.
Experience with distribution or logistics operations, including inventory accounting and customs/bonded warehouse environments, strongly preferred.
Hands-on SAP experience, particularly ERP implementation or migration, is a strong plus.
Previous experience in multinational or listed companies is a strong plus.
Proven leadership experience building and managing multi-country/multi-entity finance teams.
Strong written and verbal English communication skills for global stakeholder management. Chinese is a plus for Group-level communication.

Competencies (Skills & Behaviors)

Strong AI awareness with hands-on experience implementing AI tools or automation workflows within a finance environment.
Experience supporting regional or global finance functions.
Strong analytical and problem-solving skills.
Familiar with transfer pricing and cross-border tax principles.
Comfortable operating at senior leadership/executive committee level, with strong stakeholder management and influencing skills.
Familiar with inventory and sales/purchase management.

Leadership & Strategic Influence

Partner with Americas business, sales, and marketing leadership to provide financial insights, operational performance analysis, and cost control recommendations.
Build, lead, and develop a high-performing finance team across Montreal HQ, sales & marketing offices, and the Memphis distribution center; drive talent development and succession planning.
Act as a strategic finance partner to the Americas leadership team, contributing to regional business strategy, investment decisions, and capital allocation.
Report to the Group CFO on financial performance, risks, and strategic priorities, representing Americas Finance in Group-level executive discussions.

jobs.title: Director of Financial Planning and Analysis
jobs.description:
About the Company

Our client is a leading capital markets organization. They are looking for a Director, Corporate FP&A who will be responsible for leading the Corporate FP&A team responsible for enterprise planning, while also playing a key role in supporting Finance Business Partnering (FBP) teams.
In this leadership role, you empower financially sound planning and decision-making throughout the organization. You do this by spreading financial acumen, telling compelling, data-driven stories to spur action, bridging the knowledge gap between Finance and Operations, and assisting in the creation of FP&A decision-support tools. You will simplify FP&A analysis into easily digestible business logic and take a more technology-guided and teaching-focused approach to business partnering, enabling decision-makers to make sound financial decisions more independently

Requirements

CPA designation or similar (MBA/CFA)
10-15+ years of progressive finance experience with main focus in FP&A
Exposure to IFRS at a public listed entity
Strong business partnering with board reporting experience
Experience in a multi-entity environment with complex organization structures

Salary Range

$160,000 - $180,000/year

Why Work Here

High visibility with CEO, CFO and Board
Enterprise-wide impact as acquisitions has outpaced finance processes
This hire would ideally hit VPs succession map
Exposure to investor relations and strategic finance

About the Opportunity

Enterprise Planning

Ownership of forecasting and annual business planning across the group, including:
Coordination of timelines and assumption alignment across business units
Multi-stage reviews with senior leadership
Creation of final presentations for the Board of Directors
Ownership of Adaptive Planning (Workday Planning tool)
Lead the corporate target-setting process to optimize investment allocation while establishing achievable and stretch performance targets that drive desired behaviours and outcomes
Ownership of the long-term strategic forecast model used in the annual strategic planning process and longer-term modelling
Conduct business analysis on key enterprise performance drivers (e.g., headcount, profitability)

Corporate Performance Reporting

Accountable for corporate performance reporting to senior management and the Board of Directors, with a focus on forward-looking, actionable insights
Responsible for content creation, key messaging, and performance insights
Lead presentations of results to the Operating Committee
Accountable for operating segment reporting in external financial statements and MD&A
Partner closely with Investor Relations to synthesize monthly performance data into:
Quarterly earnings scripts
Q&A preparation materials
Analyst consensus models
Investor presentation metrics
Prepare supplementary schedules and analyze/proof quarterly and annual MD&A, press releases, Investor Relations presentations, and communications with shareholders and analysts
Partner closely with other Finance leaders and teams to improve data capture and GL reporting structures and optimize straight-through processing
Ownership of incentive plan performance measurement and associated liabilities across TMX; contribute to the design of incentive plans in partnership with HR

Enterprise Portfolio Governance

Oversee and recommend processes for annual and in-year discretionary investment allocations that balance governance, transparency, and business outcomes in alignment with TMX's growth strategy
Facilitate transparency for material new initiatives outside approved budgets to support CEO, CFO, and SMT approval decisions
Partner with the PMO and Integration Management Office on overall project governance and tracking
Co-owner of company-wide policies, including the TMX Expenditure and Budget Authorization Policy

Cost Allocation (Shared Services) Model

Ownership of the enterprise-wide cost allocation framework across legal entities and operating segments
Lead the design and structure of the model, including:
Tools
Principles
Governance
Regulatory compliance
Tax compliance
Provide detailed transparency to senior management and Business Unit FBPs regarding key drivers and outcomes, with a focus on understanding value delivery and influencing shared services costs
Provide variance analysis (budget vs. actual, prior period comparisons, etc.) in a manner that is easily understood by senior management
Support FBPs in stakeholder discussions to improve confidence in model integrity
Partner closely with team members to enhance data capture and GL reporting structures and improve straight-through processing
Conduct business analysis on key enterprise cost drivers
Enhance the rigour and control framework surrounding model updates and design
Build flexibility and adaptability into the model to accommodate a rapidly evolving corporate structure, including M&A activity
Collaborate with external auditors during quarterly reviews and annual audits
Improve efficiency of model updates and monthly/quarterly journal entries through automation where possible
Develop a roadmap for the next generation of the model and framework

Other

Ownership of quarterly and annual goodwill impairment testing and valuation processes, including:
Alignment with strategic plans
Input into external disclosure requirements
Partner with Corporate Strategy and Strategic Finance teams to advance enterprise analysis and insight generation
Champion and participate in knowledge-sharing forums for FBPs and FP&A professionals to exchange best practices on educating business leaders through FP&A decision-support processes
Assist in defining success criteria for FP&A tools and establishing measurable business and technical metrics to monitor utilization and quality

jobs.title: Director, Digital Safety
jobs.description:
Are you looking for a role where you can define the future of digital safety in a complex, mission\-critical environment? Can you see yourself leading enterprise\-wide cybersecurity programs while establishing the standards, controls, and governance frameworks that protect critical digital systems and information assets? If you answered yes, this may be the job for you. **Apply today,** as our Chalk River location is looking for a **Director, Digital Safety** to lead the development and implementation of CNL's Digital Safety Framework.

**What you will be doing!**

* Digital Safety Framework \& Standards Authority
	+ Defining, maintaining, and evolving the enterprise Digital Safety Framework, incorporating nuclear safety principles such as defence\-in\-depth, graded approach, and continuous improvement.
	+ Establishing and governing mandatory, non\-negotiable digital safety control requirements applicable to:
		- Information systems
		- Operational technologies
		- Nuclear\-related digital assets
		- Identity and access managemen
		- Data protection and asset lifecycle management
	+ Translating external standards (CSA N290\.7, ISO 27001, NIST, IAEA) into a cohesive, internally consistent Digital Safety Framework.
	+ Defining the baseline conditions required for safe digital operations, ensuring clarity in expectations across all business and operational areas.
* Program Implementation
	+ Embedding Digital Safety requirements into all business processes, projects, and operational activities to obtain compliance with defined safety standards.
	+ Developing and delivering enterprise\-wide programs to build digital safety awareness, competency, and behavioural accountability.
	+ Driving the integration of human factors and behavioural science into digital safety practices, reinforcing safe decision\-making and risk\-awareness across the workforce.
	+ Promoting and enforcing understanding so that all employees and contractors understand their role in maintaining digital safety and operate within defined safety expectations.
* Control Oversight and Operational Assurance
	+ Exercising authority to mandate that all digital systems and activities comply with established Digital Safety requirements.
	+ Conducting assessments, audits, and monitoring to validate adherence to safety standards and identifying gaps or vulnerabilities.
	+ Leading incident response readiness and coordinating response activities, ensuring compliance with defined safety and regulatory requirements.
	+ Maintaining enterprise visibility of digital assets and establish appropriate classification, protection, and lifecycle management.
* Governance, Compliance, and External Alignment
	+ Overseeing and confirming alignment with regulatory requirements and maintain readiness for audits and inspections.
	+ Building and maintaining relationships with regulatory bodies, industry organizations, and external experts.
	+ Monitoring emerging threats, technologies, and regulatory changes, incorporating them into the Digital Safety Framework as appropriate.
* Leadership and Organizational Capability
	+ Leading and developing a high\-performing team of digital safety professionals, fostering a culture of accountability, excellence, and continuous improvement.
	+ Developing workforce capability plans to build and sustain the skills required to execute Digital Safety objectives.
	+ Managing budgets, resources, and priorities to deliver on strategic Digital Safety objectives.

Other duties as assigned by your manager.  
* 

**What we are looking for:**

* **Education**
	+ Bachelor's or Master's degree in cyber Security, Information Systems, Business Administration or related field, or equivalent work experience.
	+ Relevant certifications (e.g., CISSP, CISM, ITIL) are highly desirable.
* **Experience**
	+ 10\+ years of experience in cyber security, with specific expertise in nuclear or critical infrastructure protection preferred.
	+ 10\+ years in progressive leadership roles.
	+ Demonstrated experience establishing and governing enterprise security or control frameworks.
	+ Experience implementing and interpreting industry and regulatory standards (e.g., CSA N290\.7, ISO 27001, NIST).
	+ Proven ability to lead large\-scale organizational transformation and embed control disciplines in complex environments.
	+ Experience in operational technology (OT), industrial control systems (ICS), or SCADA environments strongly preferred.
	+ Experience in managing budgets, strategic planning, and resource allocation.

	+ Ability to define and communicate a clear Digital Safety vision and framework aligned to nuclear safety principles.
	+ Strong understanding of defence\-in\-depth, risk\-based control models, and safety\-critical system governance.
	+ Exceptional decision\-making and judgement in high\-risk and complex environments.
	+ Ability to establish authority and enforce standards in environments with competing priorities.
	+ Strong influencing and negotiation skills, particularly in cross\-functional and non\-hierarchical contexts.
	+ Deep understanding of current and emerging cyber threats and mitigation strategies.
	+ Ability to translate technical controls into clear, actionable safety requirements.
	+ Strong leadership and people development capabilities.
	+ Ability to drive behavioural and cultural change across a diverse workforce.
	+ Excellent communication skills, including the ability to engage both technical and executive audiences.
	+ Strong knowledge of:  
	
	o CSA N290\.7 (Nuclear Cyber Security)  
	
	o ISO 27001  
	
	o NIST Cybersecurity Framework  
	
	o IAEA guidance and nuclear regulatory expectations
	+ Familiarity with OT/ICS environments and digital instrumentation \& control systems.
	+ Understanding of how nuclear safety principles apply to digital systems.

jobs.title: Sr. Director, Strategy & Foresight
jobs.description:
The Greater is looking for a Sr.
Director, Strategy & Foresight
to join our team.

This is a senior strategy role for someone who understands how organizations use brand, sponsorships and other strategic partnerships to drive their business. You’ll work across a range of client projects, helping organizations make better decisions, identify opportunities, solve complex problems and bring new thinking to the table.

Sponsorship and partnerships are an important part of our work, but this role will also contribute across broader business and brand strategy projects.

We’re looking for someone who can do the work, not just manage it. You should be equally comfortable conducting a landscape scan, writing an executive brief, facilitating a workshop, analyzing data or sitting across from a senior client and delivering a clear recommendation.

Most importantly, we’re looking for someone who is proactive. Someone who sees something interesting and brings it forward. Who has a point of view. Who doesn’t wait for a perfectly defined brief, but can mobilize quickly to turn an observation or opportunity into a recommendation.

What you'll do:

Your work will include:

Leading and contributing to strategy development across business, brand, sponsorship and partnership challenges.
Conducting landscape scans, research and competitive analysis to identify trends, opportunities and implications for clients.
Turning data, research and cultural signals into clear insights, recommendations and strategic stories.
Developing executive communications, strategic presentations, briefs and recommendations for senior audiences.
Designing and facilitating working sessions, ideation sessions and senior-client discussions.
Bringing proactive ideas and perspectives to clients, not just responding to briefs.
Working across client and agency teams, navigating different disciplines, organizations and perspectives while keeping the work moving.
Helping clients consider how changing consumer behaviour, technology, culture and business models could affect their organizations and strategies.
Applying strategic foresight, trends analysis and scenario thinking to identify what may be coming and what it could mean for clients.

What we're looking for:

You have meaningful experience in strategy, brand, sponsorship, partnerships or a closely related field, and you’re comfortable operating at a senior level.

You can move between big-picture thinking and hands-on delivery. You know how to take in a lot of information, find what matters and make it simple. You’re confident enough to have a point of view and collaborative enough to work within a larger team.

Specifically, we're looking for someone who:

Has strong strategy experience, with meaningful experience in sponsorship, partnerships or brand strategy.
Has experience or strong working knowledge of financial services and banking. Experience in payments, fintech, neobanks and/or loyalty programs is also valuable.
Is tapped into sport, entertainment and culture and genuinely curious about what's changing.
Has experience working with senior clients and is polished and credible in executive settings.
Can navigate complex, multi-agency and inter-agency teams.
Is a strong writer and communicator who can make complicated ideas clear.
Is comfortable with numbers, data and analysis — and knows how to turn them into a story and recommendation.
Is proactive and self-directed. You bring forward insights, recommendations and ideas rather than waiting to be asked.
Understands traditional sponsorship models but isn't beholden to them. We're looking for someone interested in new approaches, new business models and new ways sponsorship can create value.
Can facilitate a workshop and help groups make decisions.
Has experience with strategic foresight, trends analysis, scenario planning or related methodologies. This is an asset, not a requirement.
Experience or strong working knowledge across arts and entertainment and/or Latin America would also be an asset. If you have relevant experience in these areas, we'd like to hear about it.

How we work:

This role reports to the Partner & Head of Strategy at The Greater and works closely with colleagues across the firm, as well as with clients and agency partners.

This is not a remote role. You should expect to work in person three to four days per week across The Greater, client and other locations in the GTA. Some travel will also be part of the role. Occasional evening and weekend availability will be needed for client events and other work-related commitments.

Compensation:

The expected salary range for this role is $140,000–$155,000, depending on experience.

Interview process:

Our interview process will involve multiple conversations and is designed to give us a sense of both your experience and how you think.

Candidates should be prepared for:.

Scenario-based and case-style questions based on the types of strategic challenges you would encounter in the role.
A potential conversation with members of a client team and/or interagency partners.

Please note:
In effort to ensure a fair hiring process, we will not be taking any meetings with prospective candidates ahead of time to discuss the role. If you're selected, you'll have lots of time to learn more about the role through the interview process.

How to apply:

Send the following to info@thegreater.ca with the subject line “Sr. Director, Strategy & Foresight”

Link to you LinkedIn profile.
A short note — 500 words or less — explaining what makes you a strong fit for this role.
One prediction for the future of sponsorship or partnerships. Tell us what you think is coming and why it matters.
Note: applying through LinkedIn is insufficient and you most follow these instructions to be considered for the role.

About The Greater:

The Greater is a strategy consulting firm and social enterprise with a deep specialization in sport and entertainment. We help organizations win the right way — finding clarity in complexity across business, brand and partnership strategy.

We are strategists first, combining senior-level counsel and hands-on delivery with deep sector expertise and a connected network across the Canadian sport and entertainment industry.

Founded on the belief that business can be great and do good, The Greater reinvests 50% of its net profit back into community organizations — an industry-leading commitment that has driven more than $400,000 in community investment to date.

jobs.description:
About Big Viking Games

Founded in 2011, Big Viking Games is an independent Toronto-based consumer entertainment company behind YoWorld and Fish World, two long-running social games played by tens of millions of people over the years. Our business is built on loyal communities, recurring player engagement and a team with deep roots in web and live-service technology.

Today, we are modernizing how the company operates to keep pace with a fast-moving technology landscape. We are rethinking how our teams plan, execute and grow the business, and building an organization designed for the next decade of consumer digital products.

About The Role

As VP, Operations & Transformation, you will lead the modernization of Big Viking Games and run the operations that power the business. You will report to the CEO, serve on the leadership team and work alongside our product, engineering and creative leaders to set direction and deliver results across functions. Your remit covers studio production, product operations, people operations, accounting and IT, and the systems that connect them.

Success in this seat calls for an AI-native operator who builds with AI firsthand and leads the shift to a modernized operating model across the business. You bring a systems view of the organization, a strong command of operating leverage and capital efficiency, and the judgment to balance near-term performance with long-term value creation, while leading change through clear communication and strong stakeholder alignment.

We value in-person collaboration, and this role works from our Toronto Harbourfront office 3 to 4 days a week.

What You'll Do

This is a hands-on executive role at the center of the business, connecting strategy, operations and people across every function:

Lead the transformation agenda. Define the roadmap for modernizing the company's operating model, and drive it from design through adoption across every function
Run operations across the business. Lead studio and product operations, people operations, accounting and IT, with clear ownership and measurable outcomes
Own the operating plan. Partner with the CEO on the P&L, set the annual operating plan and cost structure, and track performance against it
Modernize processes and systems. Bring in modern tools and practices, including AI, where they create the most value, and measure the impact they deliver
Build the team and culture. Shape the structure, roles and culture for the company's next chapter, and develop the leaders who will carry it forward

Requirements

15+ years of experience, including 3+ years leading a P&L or operating budget
Experience in consumer software or digital services businesses, ideally with transactional or subscription revenue
You use and build with AI daily, have led its adoption across teams, and set a high bar for how effectively your organization puts it to work

A track record of leading company-wide transformation or operating model redesign, from strategy through execution

Access to leading AI tools

jobs.title: Chief Financial Officer
jobs.description:
Chief Financial Officer

Hamilton, Ontario

The Role

Lancaster Group is a growing multi-trade construction company is seeking an experienced Chief Financial Officer (CFO) to provide strong financial leadership, strengthen financial controls and reporting, and support the continued growth of the organization.
Reporting directly to the President and ownership group, the CFO will be a key member of the senior leadership team, acting as a trusted financial partner to the President and the business.
This role requires more than strong technical financial expertise. We are seeking a confident, hands-on leader who can manage and develop a finance team, work effectively with ownership, managers and operational teams, and translate complex financial information into clear, practical business direction.

The ideal candidate will have strong experience in a multi-trade, unionized construction environment and understand the financial complexities associated with project-based work, multiple trades, collective agreements, labour costing, job costing, and project profitability.
The organization is currently transitioning from Sage 300 Construction and Real Estate (Timberline) to Maestro ERP. The CFO will play an important role in supporting the financial side of this transition and ensuring strong financial processes, controls, reporting and data integrity within the new system. The CFO will also follow through with a new structured bonus plan initiative and set budgets within the organization.

Key Responsibilities

Financial Leadership and Strategy

Lead the company's overall financial strategy, planning and reporting
Act as a trusted financial advisor to ownership and senior leadership
Provide timely, accurate financial information and analysis to support business decisions
Clearly communicate financial performance, risks, trends and opportunities
Lead annual budgeting, forecasting and long-term financial planning
Provide financial guidance to support strategic decisions and continued growth
Develop and monitor financial KPIs, dashboards and management reporting
Identify financial concerns proactively and bring forward practical recommendations and solutions

Financial Reporting and Controls

Oversee monthly, quarterly and annual financial reporting
Ensure the accuracy and integrity of financial statements and management reporting
Establish and maintain strong financial controls, policies and procedures
Oversee cash flow, working capital, banking and treasury functions
Strengthen cost controls and financial accountability across the organization
Manage relationships with external accountants, financial institutions, insurers and other financial partners
Ensure compliance with applicable accounting, tax and regulatory requirements

Construction and Project Financial Management

Oversee project financial reporting, job costing, WIP and profitability analysis
Monitor project margins, costs, commitments and overall financial performance
Oversee progress billing and other construction-related financial processes
Work collaboratively with project managers and operational leaders to strengthen forecasting, cost control and financial accountability
Ensure accurate and timely job costing and financial reporting across projects
Analyze project performance and identify financial risks, cost overruns and margin opportunities
Improve visibility into project performance and overall company profitability

Multi Trade and Union Financial Management

Understand the financial complexities of operating across multiple construction trades
Understand labour costing, labour burden, union-related costs and their impact on project profitability
Support accurate costing and financial administration in an environment involving multiple collective agreements and labour structures
Work effectively with finance, project management and operations to ensure labour costs are appropriately captured, allocated and reported
Understand how varying trade and labour requirements affect estimating, forecasting, job costing and project financial performance

ERP and Process Improvement

Provide financial leadership during the transition from Sage 300 to Maestro ERP
Ensure appropriate financial controls, processes and reporting are established within the ERP
Support data integrity and accurate financial reporting throughout the transition
Identify opportunities to streamline financial workflows and improve reporting
Work collaboratively with internal teams to support successful ERP adoption
Establish scalable financial processes and systems that support continued company growth

Leadership and Team Development

Provide strong, visible leadership to the finance and accounting team
Lead, mentor, coach and develop team members
Establish clear expectations and hold the finance team accountable for results
Build a strong, capable and accountable finance function
Communicate expectations, priorities and financial information clearly and effectively
Build strong working relationships with ownership, senior leadership, project managers, operations and employees across the organization
Address issues directly and constructively and drive matters through to resolution
Foster a collaborative, professional and results-focused environment
Lead by example and promote accountability, accuracy and continuous improvement

The Ideal Candidate

As the ideal candidate, you are an experienced and visionary leader with strategic thinking and strong interpersonal skills, and the ability to communicate effectively at all levels of an organization. This includes the ability to explain complex financial information clearly to both financial and non-financial stakeholders and a proven ability to lead, develop and hold teams accountable. Preferably, you bring significant senior financial leadership experience at the CFO, VP Finance or senior Controller level in a multi-trade construction environment, having worked within a unionized construction environment and through multiple collective agreements.

Qualifications and Required Experience:

We recognize that no one candidate is likely to meet all qualifications in equal measure. Those listed below are desirable and will be used to compare candidates.
CPA designation is required
Minimum 5 years of progressive financial leadership experience within construction or a closely related project-based industry
Minimum 4 years of progressive financial leadership experience within multi-trade construction environments
Minimum 3 years of unionized construction environment experience
Minimum 3 years of experience in job costing, WIP, project margins, and construction accounting
Construction operational skills and COR recertification are assets
Strong knowledge of construction accounting, job costing, WIP, labour costing, project margins, progress billing, cash flow and forecasting
Demonstrated ability to understand project financial performance and work effectively with project and operational teams
Demonstrated experience with budgeting, forecasting, financial analysis and internal controls
Experience with ERP implementation, conversion or significant system improvement
Experience with Sage 300 Construction and Real Estate (Timberline) and/or Maestro ERP is an asset
Confident and comfortable challenging assumptions, raising concerns and providing practical financial recommendations
Comfortable working in a growing, hands-on and fast-paced construction environment

You are someone with:

The ability to build and lead a high-performing team and engage with internal and external stakeholders to achieve goals and outcomes
The ability to effectively explain decisions and bring clarity to complex issues to a variety of audiences, including boards
A high capacity to balance multiple priorities while being responsive, including maintaining ROCE and all government grants and incentives
A growth-oriented mindset, both organic and acquisition
Excellent verbal and written communication skills
Strong analytical, problem-solving and decision-making skills

Salary and Benefits

431516

Connection is everything. It drives us to innovate, explore, and stay close to what matters to us most. At Bell, we’re building a more connected future through world-class networks, AI-powered solutions, and digital experiences that elevate how people live, work, and play every day.

We believe in empowering people. That’s why we equip our teams with cutting-edge technology, AI tools, and a collaborative environment that supports creativity and growth. Want to be part of a diverse team where your work makes a real impact? If you’re inspired by innovation that advances how people connect and transforms what’s possible, you belong on #TeamBell.

On the Bell Business Markets team, you’ll be a vital part of making innovation happen for enterprise-scale customers. You’ll deliver advanced solutions in areas such as IoT, Mobility/5G, Cloud, Cyber Security, Voice, Collaboration & Contact Centre and Internet & Private Networks.

At Bell, your skills and expertise will help set us apart as we continue to be the leading provider of digital connections and next generation services to businesses and governments.

Summary

Bell’s AI Fabric initiative is pioneering a secure, sovereign AI compute network across Canada. This transformative portfolio includes seven large-scale, high-density data centres, anchored by a 500 MW British Columbia supercluster and a future 1.2GW flagship site in Regina, Saskatchewan.

As Program Director, you will be accountable for the end-to-end delivery of the national data centre build program—orchestrating scope, schedule, budget, and cross-functional execution across multiple concurrent sites. You'll be the integrating force connecting construction, engineering, commissioning, procurement, and program controls into one predictable, well-governed program, ensuring Bell delivers these mission-critical facilities on time, on budget, and to standard as the initiative scales aggressively nationally.

Key Responsibilities

Own end-to-end delivery accountability for the national data centre build program, integrating scope, schedule, budget, and quality across multiple concurrent sites.
Orchestrate cross-functional execution across construction, engineering, commissioning, procurement, and program controls, ensuring alignment to program objectives.
Establish and govern the program delivery framework—stage gates, milestones, governance cadence, and decision rights—across the portfolio.
Own the integrated master schedule and program-level budget, driving predictability, transparency, and schedule discipline across all builds.
Lead program-level risk management, change governance, and interdependency management, escalating and resolving systemic issues before they impact delivery.
Provide executive-level program reporting to AI Fabric and Capital Programs leadership, translating complex delivery status into clear, decision-ready insight.
Manage program financials, forecasting, and capital planning in partnership with finance and program controls.
Drive resource planning and prioritization across sites, balancing competing demands as the program scales
Build and mature Bell's program delivery capability at a formative stage, embedding repeatable processes, playbooks, and lessons learned across the fleet.
Serve as a senior point of escalation and executive interface for site directors, functional leads, and external delivery partners.

Critical Qualifications

15+ years leading large-scale capital program delivery, with direct experience on hyperscale or mission-critical data centres (multi-site / multi-billion-dollar portfolios preferred)
Proven track record owning end-to-end program delivery across multiple concurrent construction projects, not just single-project management.
Deep command of program management disciplines—integrated master scheduling, budget/cost control, risk management, and change governance.
Strong understanding of the full data centre delivery lifecycle—construction, engineering, MEP, and commissioning through to operational handover.
Demonstrated ability to integrate and align diverse cross-functional teams and external delivery partners.

Exceptional executive presence, able to influence and challenge senior engineering, construction, finance, and executive leaders.
Experience building and maturing a program delivery organization from a formative stage.

* Weigh how to deploy limited capital across community solar, commercial and industrial solar, standalone storage and hybrid solar\-plus\-storage.
* Identify capital constraints, concentration risks, funding gaps and dependencies that could affect construction schedules or commercial operation dates.

The Director, IT leads day-to-day delivery of technology services and operational security. Reporting to the VP Finance, IT and Risk, this role is YWCA's senior technology leader, setting technology direction and translating it into execution by running reliable IT operations and strengthening cybersecurity controls that protect YWCA’s clients, staff, and organisational reputation.

Reports to:
Vice President, Finance, IT and Risk
Direct reports:
Senior IT Systems Manager, plus additional technical staff as required
Governance:
provides operational metrics and risk updates to the VP Finance, IT and Risk; participates in cross-functional governance forums as required

Delegated authority and decision rights

Runs day-to-day operations across sites, including escalation pathways, on-call structure, service workflows, and operational communications to staff.
Approves routine operational changes, configuration standards enforcement, and remediation plans (patching, vulnerability remediation coordination, endpoint baselines) consistent with standards approved by the VP Finance, IT and Risk.
Recommends technology standards, policies, and the annual IT operating and capital budget for approval by the VP Finance, IT and Risk.
Defines and enforces operational processes (incident/problem/change), service catalogue structure, and operational metrics.
Manages renewals, service performance, and vendor issue escalation; can approve vendor work orders and operational purchases within budget and delegated signing limits.
Owns operational control implementation and upkeep (monitoring, endpoint protection, email protections, conditional access operations) and ensures evidence is maintained for audits and cyber insurance.
Leads performance management, scheduling, coverage planning, and hiring for operational roles (with VP Finance, IT and Risk approval for net-new roles or material restructuring).

What you’ll be doing:

1) IT operations and service management

Run day-to-day IT operations, ensuring stable services, responsive support, and clear escalation pathways for front-line teams.
Implement service management practices, including ticketing workflows, incident and problem management, and change coordination.
Define and track operational performance metrics (for example, ticket volumes, time to resolution, recurring issues) and drive continuous improvement.

2) Infrastructure, platforms, and endpoint management

Oversee network, connectivity, collaboration, and core cloud services to ensure availability, security, and supportability.
Ensure consistent execution of endpoint management, patching, configuration standards, and identity and access operations (including Joiner-Mover-Leaver (JML) processes and access reviews).
Support the operational health of data pipelines and BI tools, ensuring data sources are reliable and accessible for enterprise reporting.
Provide operational support for network-connected physical security systems (e.g., CCTV, access control).
Oversee configuration, support, and integration of core business applications (e.g., client management, finance, and HR systems), working with system owners across the organisation.
Maintain backup, disaster recovery, and business continuity capabilities for critical systems, including regular restore testing.

3) Vendor, procurement, and asset management

Own the device and asset lifecycle program: standards, procurement coordination, tagging, inventory accuracy, deployment, transfers, replacements, secure wiping, and disposal.

Operationalise security controls and maintain security tooling configurations and monitoring across endpoints, networks, and cloud services.
Coordinate vulnerability management, including scanning, risk-based prioritisation, and remediation tracking.
Maintain operational readiness for incidents, including runbooks, escalation, evidence preservation support, and post-incident corrective actions.
Apply privacy and safety safeguards to systems that hold sensitive client information, and support privacy impact assessments and breach response.
Maintain IT policies and staff guidance (e.g., acceptable use) and deliver security awareness training, including phishing simulations.

5) Project delivery and change enablement

Lead delivery of operational technology projects (upgrades, migrations, tooling improvements), managing scope, timelines, and stakeholder communication.
Work with program leaders to translate needs into feasible solutions and sustainable support models.
Ensure changes are adopted successfully through training, communications, and transition to steady-state operations.
Develop and maintain the multi-year technology roadmap in partnership with the VP Finance, IT and Risk, and translate it into actionable project plans, ensuring operational readiness for all new deployments.

6) People leadership

Lead, coach, and develop the IT operations team, including performance management, training plans, and coverage planning.
Establish clear on-call, escalation, and handoff practices that protect staff wellbeing and maintain service reliability.

Required experience and capabilities

8+ years of progressive IT experience, including leadership of infrastructure and end-user computing in a multi-site environment.
Demonstrated experience operating and improving IT service delivery, including ticketing, incident management, and operational metrics.
Practical cybersecurity experience, including patching discipline, endpoint security, identity and access practices, and incident response support.
Strong vendor and contract operations capability, including renewals, service performance management, and procurement coordination.
Ability to communicate clearly with non-technical stakeholders and drive adoption of consistent practices.
People leadership experience, including coaching, performance management, and coverage planning for reliable operations.
Experience developing multi-year technology roadmaps and managing IT budgets.
Post-secondary degree or diploma in information technology, computer science, or a related field, or an equivalent combination of education and experience.

Preferred experience

Experience in non-profit, housing, or human services environments with heightened privacy and safety considerations.
ITIL or comparable service management training, and project delivery experience (formal or practical).

Position Overview

The Sr. Director Product & Platform Trust is accountable for shaping how Autodesk product teams build safe and secure products at scale. The Senior Director, Product & Platform Trust will partner closely with product and engineering leaders across Autodesk's product & platform divisions to understand their development environments, security needs, and emerging challenges, and systemic barriers to timely remediation. You will lead an organization spanning application security, trust engineering, and product management including product-team enablement. Together, these teams will develop the tools, platforms, practices, guidance, and expertise that embed security throughout the product development lifecycle and make secure development easier and more consistent for Autodesk teams.

Reporting to the Chief Trust Officer, you will influence product and engineering strategy across a highly distributed, matrixed organization. Success in this role means building trusted partnerships with product organizations, defining the right security capabilities, driving adoption, and enabling teams to increasingly build security and trust into the software development lifecycle.

This is a highly collaborative, cross-functional leadership role requiring strong product and engineering judgment, deep product security expertise, and the ability to drive change through influence across a global organization.

jobs.description:
Job Description

What is the opportunity?

This leader sets one standard way to build, secure and run AI across RBC Technology & Operations. They own the reference architecture for retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), AI agents, model access and AI-native software delivery (AI-DLC). The role turns the 2030 T&O ambitions, including AI-native delivery and 30% of GenAI volume on open-weight models, into patterns teams actually use.

Success means fewer bespoke stacks, faster delivery with maintainable code, and AI that Internal Audit, Model Risk and OSFI can trust.

What will you do
?

AI architecture standards as code. Define the enterprise AI reference architecture and approved patterns. Encode them as harness skills, agent constitutions and automated fitness checks, so standards apply at generation time rather than at review.
Common RAG substrate. Converge the many RAG solutions onto one shared platform: ingestion, chunking, embeddings, hybrid retrieval, reranking and evaluation. Retrieval must respect source entitlements by default. Set a retirement plan for duplicate stacks.
Agent sandboxing and security architecture. Design the sandbox standard for every agentic workload: ephemeral environments, egress allow-lists, short-lived task-scoped credentials and no standing production access. Own agent identity, tool access through a governed MCP gateway and registry, and defenses against prompt injection and poisoned tools.
AI-DLC harness and quality gates. Own the harness architecture from spec to release. Make quality gates deterministic and mandatory: tests and coverage, static analysis, complexity and duplication limits, dependency and license checks, security scanning and architecture fitness checks. Enforce separation of duties (the agent that writes a change cannot approve it), PR size limits and traceability from spec to deployment.
Skills and evaluation lifecycle. Treat skills like code: owned, versioned, regression-tested with evals and retired when stale. Re-run evals before any model upgrade reaches teams.
Model gateway and inference architecture. Route work across frontier and open-weight models by cost, risk and jurisdiction. Build in token metering, caching and data-classification rules so cost and residency are enforced by the platform.
Risk-tiered control model. Partner with Internal Audit, Model Risk and Cyber to define human-oversight tiers, from human-on-the-loop for low-risk work to human-in-the-loop for payments and core banking. Align with OSFI Guidelines E-23 and B-13.
Design authority and innovation. Chair AI architecture review, keep decision records and manage exceptions. Graduate proven lab work into the platform and evaluate emerging technology, such as agent protocols and new open-weight models.

What do you need to succeed?

15+ years in architecture or engineering, including 5+ years leading architects or engineers at enterprise scale.
Hands-on depth in LLM systems: RAG, agent frameworks, MCP, evaluation and inference serving on cloud and on-premises GPUs.
Security architecture for AI, including the OWASP Top 10 for LLM applications, sandboxing and identity for non-human actors.
Strong DevSecOps and SDLC background; you have shipped quality gates engineers accepted rather than routed around.
Experience in a regulated industry, ideally financial services under OSFI.
Credibility with engineers: you still prototype and read code. Able to explain trade-offs plainly to executives and audit.

What’s in it for you?

We thrive on the challenge to be our best, progressive thinking to keep growing, and working together to deliver trusted advice to help our clients thrive and communities prosper. We care about each other, reaching our potential, making a difference to our communities, and achieving success that is mutual.

About The Role

Reporting directly to the Chief Operations Officer, the Director, Enterprise Risk Management
will play a pivotal role in building and leading a modern, scalable first-line risk management function to support goeasy’s next stage of growth. This leader will shape the strategy, establish risk management frameworks, and partner with senior executives to identify and manage key non-credit risks, strengthen operational resilience, and enable smarter, risk-informed decisions. Leveraging data, technology, AI, and automation, this role will modernize how risk is identified, monitored, and managed, helping the business anticipate challenges, drive operational excellence, and scale with confidence.

Who You Are

You are a strategic and progressive risk leader who brings a strong combination of business acumen, analytical thinking, and hands-on execution. You have experience building or evolving risk management frameworks and know how to translate complex risk principles into practical, scalable solutions that drive meaningful business outcomes.

You view risk management as an enabler of growth, not a barrier. You are comfortable challenging conventional thinking, influencing senior stakeholders, and balancing risk mitigation with commercial priorities. You thrive in dynamic environments, embrace technology and innovation, and are passionate about building high-performing teams and fostering a culture of accountability and proactive risk management.

What You'll Do

Build and lead the function: Establish and mature a first-line enterprise risk management function, defining its strategy, operating model, governance, and priorities to support organizational growth.
Strengthen risk frameworks: Develop and implement scalable risk management practices, including risk and control assessments, risk registers, control inventories, issue management, remediation tracking, and executive reporting.
Drive enterprise-wide accountability: Partner with business leaders to establish clear risk ownership, strengthen internal controls, and embed risk management into day-to-day operations and strategic decision-making.
Provide strategic risk advisory: Serve as a trusted advisor to senior leadership, providing insights, constructive challenge, and practical recommendations that balance business objectives, customer outcomes, and regulatory expectations.
Modernize through technology: Leverage data analytics, AI, automation, dashboards, and emerging technologies to identify risk trends, monitor key risk indicators, improve controls, and enable proactive decision-making.
Enhance governance and reporting: Establish effective governance routines, escalation processes, and reporting mechanisms that provide leadership with clear visibility into emerging risks, control effectiveness, and remediation priorities.
Build a high-performing team: Lead, coach, and develop risk professionals while fostering a culture of ownership, collaboration, transparency, and continuous improvement.

What You Bring

7–10 years of progressive experience in enterprise risk management, operational risk, governance, internal controls, compliance, audit, consulting, or related disciplines.
Demonstrated experience designing, implementing, or transforming risk management frameworks, governance structures, control environments, or enterprise-wide risk programs.
Strong knowledge of established risk management principles and frameworks, including COSO, the Three Lines Model, risk appetite, risk assessments, control design, monitoring, and remediation.
Proven experience leading teams or functions across risk management, governance, internal controls, compliance, or operational risk.
Strong analytical capabilities, with experience leveraging data, KPIs/KRIs, dashboards, automation, AI, or governance, risk, and compliance (GRC) platforms to generate actionable insights.
Exceptional communication, stakeholder management, and influencing skills, with the ability to engage senior executives, challenge constructively, and translate complex risk matters into clear business recommendations.
Experience within financial services, consumer lending, banking, fintech, insurance, payments, consulting, or another regulated industry is strongly preferred.
Relevant post-secondary education or professional designations in risk management, business, finance, audit, compliance, or related fields are considered an asset.

 Job Summary   
 The Executive Assistant (“EA”) plays an important role in supporting the Chief Technology, Data & AI Officer (CTDAIO) and the day-to-day operations of the Information Technology Division. Reporting directly to the CTDAIO, the EA provides proactive administrative and operational support and works closely with the IT leadership team.  

 This role goes beyond day-to-day executive support. The EA will help the CTDAIO stay organized and focused across priorities related to technology, data, AI, cybersecurity, talent, and transformation. The successful candidate will anticipate what is needed, take ownership, use good judgment, and follow through on decisions and commitments. 

 What you will do:   

 Note: This role is required to work in the office full-time. 

 Executive & Divisional Support  
 Provide administrative support to the CTDAIO, including calendar management, meeting coordination, travel arrangements, correspondence, and preparation for executive, Board, committee, and divisional commitments.

 Work with the IT leadership team and partners across the organization to clarify owners, actions, and timelines and follow up on commitments.

 Leadership Meetings & Follow-Through

 Expense and Administrative Support  
 Process invoices, expense claims, purchase documentation, and payments accurately and on time.

 Events, Engagement & Coordination  
 Coordinate IT leadership meetings, divisional calls, town halls, offsites, training sessions, and events, managing logistics and follow-up from start to finish.  
 Coordinate leadership updates, key messages, presentations, and opportunities to share team progress and innovation across the division.  
 Support activities that encourage ownership, accountability, collaboration, open communication, and continuous improvement.  
 Partner with other Executive Assistants and teams across the organization on shared initiatives, events, and executive priorities. 

 Relationship Management & Collaboration  
 Build strong working relationships with the CTDAIO, IT leaders, Executive Assistants, and stakeholders across the organization.

 Use good judgment when handling sensitive issues and know when to act independently, seek input, or escalate.  
 Communicate directly and constructively and help resolve coordination gaps before they cause delays. 

 Ways of Working & Continuous Improvement

 Bring a strong sense of ownership, urgency, and follow-through to a fast-paced and changing environment.  
 Look for practical ways to simplify administrative processes and make work easier across the division.

 What you bring:   
 University or college education, or equivalent experience.  
 At least five years of executive administrative experience, including direct support to a C-suite or similarly senior executive in a complex organization.  
 Proven ability to manage complex calendars, competing priorities, executive meetings, confidential matters, and time-sensitive work with limited direction.  
 Experience supporting executive, Board, committee, or senior leadership meetings, including coordinating agendas and materials, taking minutes, capturing decisions, and tracking actions.  
 Experience with vendor administration, invoices, expense claims, purchase documentation, and related tracking.  
 Advanced skills in Microsoft 365, including Outlook, Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Teams, and SharePoint. Experience using AI and automation tools is an asset.  
 Strong organizational and prioritization skills, with the ability to manage several priorities while maintaining accuracy and follow-through.  
 Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to prepare clear, accurate, and polished executive materials.  
 A proactive and practical approach, with the confidence to take ownership, work independently, ask questions, and respectfully challenge when needed.  
 Strong interpersonal skills and the ability to build effective relationships at all levels of the organization.  
 Sound judgment and discretion when handling sensitive and confidential information.  
 Adaptability, resilience, curiosity, and a commitment to continuous improvement.  
 Alignment with HOOPP’s values and a commitment to fostering an accountable, collaborative, respectful, and positive workplace.

jobs.title: Associate Creative Director - Creative Technology
jobs.description:
Agency: 
Critical Mass 
 Job Function: 
Creative 
 Job Subfunction: 
Creative Direction

 Job Description: 
 You bring ideas to life before they’re ready to be a deck. 

 You work in a creative pod concepting campaigns and promotions. The traditional dimensions of that work are real: strong craft, clear thinking, ideas that hold up under scrutiny. But what you bring that no one else in the pod does is the question “what else could this be?” You spin up a landing page to show how a campaign breathes in the wild. You build a demo of how a product experience might work inside a banner ad. You find a way to stretch an existing Adobe tool into something unexpected. Creative technology isn’t a layer you add to an idea after it’s formed: it’s how you think from the start.

 As art directors design and copywriters write, one of your mediums is code. You carry a full creative load — concepting, developing, presenting across Adobe’s campaign and product work — and you bring the same rigor your creative partners bring. What’s different is that when the team is figuring out how to express a concept, you’re the one who can make a version of it exist. Scrappily, quickly, real enough for someone to react to.

 You will:
 What You Produce - Campaign concepts and executions expressed as working prototypes, interactive demos, not just decks. A proof-of-concept that tests whether the technology will support the idea, and a functional prototype that shows what it looks and feels like. Traditional campaign work — concepting, presenting, iterating — at the level expected of any ACD on this team.

 The Standard   - The clearest measure of this role: the ideas you bring couldn’t have been expressed any other way. The technology dimension should be integrated from the start — shaping what ideas you bring forward, how you express them, and what you push the team to consider. If you’re asking, “can we prototype this?” after the concept is approved, you’ve arrived too late. The question belongs in the briefing itself. 

 You Have: 
 A portfolio that demonstrates both strong creative thinking and things you’ve built — not one or the other.

At PlantBest, we're changing the way the world grows.

For over 20 years, we have transformed discarded coconut husks into innovative, high-performance growing solutions that deliver superior results while reducing environmental impact. Guided by our purpose, Better for your garden. Better for our planet.
, we are challenging conventional growing practices and creating a more sustainable way to grow.

PlantBest is seeking an E-Commerce & Digital Marketing Director

This is a highly visible, strategic and hands-on role responsible for driving our e-commerce, marketplace and digital marketing growth across North America. The successful candidate will own both strategy and day-to-day execution, developing and implementing initiatives that increase brand awareness, traffic, conversion, customer loyalty and profitable revenue growth.

The ideal candidate is equally comfortable developing strategy, analyzing business performance and rolling up their sleeves to execute. They bring deep expertise in Amazon, Shopify, digital advertising, content marketing and customer acquisition, with a proven track record of delivering measurable results in consumer products, retail or e-commerce environments.

E-Commerce Leadership

Improve conversion rates, average order value and customer lifetime value.
Monitor competitive activity, marketplace trends and emerging technologies.

Amazon & Marketplace Management

Lead PlantBest's Amazon strategy across North America.
Manage listing optimization, SEO, content, advertising and marketplace performance.
Identify and launch new marketplace opportunities.
Manage agency and partner relationships where required.
Develop plans to internalize key marketplace capabilities.

Digital Marketing

Develop and execute annual digital marketing plans aligned to business objectives.
Manage paid media activities including Google, Amazon, Meta and other digital channels.
Build customer acquisition and retention programs that generate profitable growth.
Oversee email marketing, marketing automation and CRM initiatives.
Manage marketing budgets and maximize ROI.

Content & Brand Development

Lead content strategy across all digital channels.
Oversee creation of website content, photography, video, blogs, newsletters and product content.
Develop and manage the social media strategy and content calendar.
Build influencer and creator partnerships that strengthen the PlantBest brand.
Ensure consistent execution of brand standards across all customer touchpoints.

Website & Customer Experience

Own the PlantBest website experience.
Improve site usability, navigation and customer journeys.
Optimize product pages and content to improve conversion.
Develop customer engagement and loyalty initiatives.
Lead ratings and reviews programs.

Analytics & Performance

Establish dashboards, KPIs and performance reporting.
Monitor revenue, traffic, conversion, acquisition costs, ROAS and profitability.
Translate data into actionable recommendations.
Present regular business reviews and strategic recommendations to senior leadership.

Cross Functional Leadership

Partner with Sales, Operations, Supply Chain and Finance to support business goals.
Support demand forecasting and inventory planning.
Coordinate digital product launches and promotions.
Build scalable processes and documentation to support future growth.

What You Bring

Experience

7-10+ years of progressive experience in e-commerce, digital marketing or omnichannel retail.
Demonstrated success growing DTC and marketplace businesses.
Experience managing Amazon Seller Central and other major online marketplaces.
Proven track record in customer acquisition, conversion optimization and digital marketing.

Strong knowledge of Amazon, Shopify, Google Analytics and digital commerce platforms.
Experience with Google Ads, Meta Ads and marketing automation platforms.

ABOUT US

At Planitar, we build technology that helps people see and understand the world’s spaces more clearly.

We are the creators of iGUIDE, a powerful property technology solution that combines immersive 3D tours, accurate floor plans and reliable spatial data into a single, easy-to-use system. Our cameras and software platform are used by professionals in real estate, insurance, construction and property management to simplify their work and deliver better results.

Planitar recently joined REA Group, one of the world’s leading digital property companies. REA operates Australia’s largest residential and commercial property platforms, including realestate.com.au and has a growing global footprint across Asia and North America. Together, we are shaping the future of property technology, combining Planitar’s deep spatial data expertise with REA’s global scale and innovation engine.

OUR VISION

A connected future where reliable spatial data enables informed decisions across the property lifecycle.

OUR VALUES

Integrity:
We do the right thing even when it’s hard.
Teamwork:
We are one team, on a big mission.
Innovation:
We value creative solutions for emerging opportunities.
Accountability:
We honour our commitments.

ABOUT THE ROLE

Planitar is looking for a VP, Finance to lead our finance function through a period of continued growth. This is a hands-on leadership role for someone who has operated inside a company with $100M+ in revenue, but who thrives in the scaling-company environment ($50M–$100M).

The ideal candidate is someone comfortable building process and infrastructure rather than simply administering what's already in place. You'll lead a team of 5-8, including a Sr. Manager, Finance and 4-5 Financial Analysts/Billing Specialists, and will be a key partner to the CEO and executive team on financial strategy, M&A, and IFRS based accounting.

RESPONSIBILITIES

Own the finance function end-to-end: financial planning & analysis, accounting operations, billing, treasury, and financial reporting.
Lead and develop a team of 5-8, including direct management of a Sr. Manager, Finance and oversight of 4-5 Financial Analysts/Billing Specialists.
Drive M&A activity, including deal evaluation, due diligence, structuring support, and post-acquisition financial integration across international entities.
Design and implement scalable financial processes and controls appropriate for a company moving towards its next growth stage — replacing manual processes with repeatable, integrated systems.
Lead or support ERP/financial systems implementations (NetSuite experience strongly preferred), improving automation, reporting accuracy, and close efficiency.
Partner with the CEO and executive team on financial strategy, budgeting, forecasting, and both parent and board-level reporting.
Oversee cash flow management, banking relationships, and treasury operations across multiple currencies/jurisdictions as applicable.
Ensure compliance with tax, statutory, and regulatory requirements across all operating geographies.
Build out and mature FP&A capabilities to support data-driven decision-making across the business.
Act as a key advisor to the CEO on capital structure, financing strategy, and long-term financial planning.

QUALIFICATIONS

10+ years of progressive finance leadership experience, including prior experience at the VP level.
Direct experience with global M&A; deal evaluation, due diligence, integration, and managing finance across multiple international entities/jurisdictions.
A track record of designing and implementing financial processes and controls, ideally having taken a finance function through a period of scaling.
Experience operating inside a company with $100M+ in revenue, combined with genuine comfort operating in a leaner, faster-moving organization in the $50M range — this is not a "run what already exists" role.
Proven people leadership experience managing teams of 5+ across finance/accounting functions.
NetSuite implementation or optimization experience strongly preferred; broader ERP design & implementation experience considered.
CPA (or equivalent) designation preferred.
Strong communication skills and comfort operating as a direct financial advisor to the CEO/executive team.
Experience in a technology, SaaS, or hardware-adjacent business is an asset given Planitar's product line.

WHAT SUCCESS LOOKS LIKE IN THE FIRST YEAR

Financial processes and controls are meaningfully more scalable and automated than when you started.
The finance team is well-managed, with clear roles, development plans, and reporting cadence.
Any active or upcoming M&A activity is well-supported from a financial diligence and integration standpoint.
Leadership has clearer, faster, and more reliable financial visibility into the business.
Key financial, tax and operational risks are clearly identified, and regularly reported to leadership.
The broader organization understands why a timely, accurate close matters, how their own inputs affect it, and how reliable financial information helps drive key business decisions.
IFRS transition complete with a clean audit opinion and an approved accounting policy manual which is applied across all entities.

PERKS AND BENEFITS

100% employer-paid flexible benefits plan

Comprehensive Health & Dental coverage
Health Spending Account (HSA) or Lifestyle Spending Account (LSA) options
DPSP match
Hybrid Work Environment
Professional Development Incentive
Opportunities to grow as we scale
The backing of a global industry leader through REA Group

ACCESSIBILITY, INCLUSION & AI DISCLOSURE

Planitar is committed to a diverse, equitable, inclusive workplace and welcomes applications from all backgrounds. This is a back fill position. We provide accommodation under AODA at any hiring stage upon request.

In line with Ontario law, we use AI only to summarize interview notes, never to screen, assess, or decide on candidates — all decisions are made by our team. Please note this is a new position.

jobs.description:
**Company Description** **The Klick Group**—comprising Klick Health (including Klick Katalyst and btwelve), Klick Media Group, Klick Applied Sciences (including Klick Labs), Klick Consulting, and Klick Ventures—is an ecosystem dedicated to realizing the full potential of our people and clients in life sciences. Founded in 1997, we have offices in New York, Philadelphia, Saratoga Springs, Toronto, London, São Paulo, and Singapore. Consistently named a Best Managed Company, Most Admired Corporate Culture, and Great Place to Work, Klick is committed to fostering a high\-performance, people\-first culture with creativity, collaboration, innovation, and impact across everything we do.

**About our Technology Craft**

  

The Technology Craft powers Klick’s platforms, products, and delivery capabilities across healthcare and life sciences. Teams design, build, and operate scalable, secure, and compliant solutions across web, CRM, data, and marketing technologies. By partnering closely with Strategy, Creative, and Client Services, the Technology Craft enables integrated omnichannel experiences that deliver real business impact.

 **Job Description**  

The Vice President, Technology (Technology Enablement) is accountable for the successful delivery of Klick’s core omnichannel technology solutions across a portfolio of healthcare and life sciences clients. Reporting to the SVP of Technology, this role provides portfolio\-level delivery leadership, ensures consistent execution across teams, and builds client confidence in complex, regulated environments. The VP leads through senior Technology Enablement Leads, balancing delivery excellence, operational rigor, and scalable practices as client needs and platforms evolve.

**What You’ll Do**

* Lead delivery execution across a multi\-client technology portfolio spanning web platforms, CRM systems, Veeva, and integrated marketing technologies.
* Own end\-to\-end accountability for technology delivery outcomes across Klick\-hosted and client\-managed environments, ensuring adherence to SDLC, quality, and regulatory requirements.
* Partner with Client Services, Omnichannel Enablement, Strategy, Creative, PMO, and Technology leaders to align delivery plans with business and omnichannel objectives.
* Act as the escalation point for delivery risk, making informed trade\-offs across scope, resourcing, timing, and quality to maintain predictability and client confidence.
* Evolve Klick’s technology delivery operating model by improving governance, forecasting, KPIs, and delivery standards to support scalable, repeatable execution.

  

**Qualifications** **Required:**

* 12\+ years of experience delivering complex enterprise technology solutions, with accountability for large\-scale, multi\-stream delivery programs.
* Demonstrated leadership overseeing omnichannel technology delivery across platforms such as Salesforce, Veeva, Adobe Experience Manager, or comparable enterprise ecosystems.
* Proven experience leading through senior delivery leaders and cross\-functional teams, with clear ownership of outcomes across multiple concurrent initiatives.
* Hands\-on experience with delivery governance frameworks, including SDLC, portfolio planning, risk management, and delivery performance metrics.
* Strong executive communication skills, including translating technical risk and delivery trade\-offs for senior business, IT, and client stakeholders.

**Desired:**

* Comfort and enthusiasm for using AI as a regular part of how work gets done.
* Experience delivering technology solutions within US pharmaceutical or healthcare environments, including exposure to regulatory and MLR considerations.
* Agency or consulting background supporting enterprise clients across multiple accounts and delivery models.
* Experience contributing to growth and solution shaping efforts by assessing feasibility, delivery risk, and execution readiness.
* Demonstrated success building and scaling delivery leadership teams while fostering continuous improvement and operational maturity.

  

**Additional Information**  

This posting is to backfill a role at Klick.

*Klick is consciously creating a culture where everyone can thrive and grow in their careers. We believe that our best work comes from our diverse backgrounds, perspectives, and skills. We strongly encourage members of historically underrepresented communities to apply, including Black people, Indigenous peoples, and other people of color, people with disabilities, people from gender and sexually diverse communities and people with intersectional identities.
