 About the role: 
 BMO Canada Wealth Digital is accelerating the adoption of Artificial Intelligence (AI) across its customer-facing digital platforms to enhance client experiences, improve operational efficiency, and enable innovative wealth management solutions. We are seeking an experienced AI Delivery Director to lead the planning, execution, and delivery of strategic AI initiatives that support the evolution of our Wealth Management digital capabilities.

 This is a senior delivery leadership role requiring the coordination of cross-functional teams across Engineering, Architecture, Security, Risk Management, Compliance, and Business organizations. The successful candidate will be responsible for driving the delivery of secure, compliant, and resilient Multi-Agent AI solutions that leverage enterprise AI capabilities, including the AI Gateway, Policy Engine, Identity Fabric, AI Registry, Guardrails Runtime, Model Context Protocol (MCP) services, and AI Observability platforms.

 The AI Delivery Director will provide end-to-end leadership across the delivery lifecycle, from intake, discovery, and prioritization through implementation, deployment, adoption, and business value realization by adopting and utilizing AI tools in SDLC. Working closely with engineering leaders, product owners, architects, and executive stakeholders, the role will ensure AI-enabled solutions are delivered on schedule, aligned with enterprise standards, and integrated effectively within the broader technology ecosystem.

 Key Responsibilities 

 1.      End-to-End Technology Delivery 

 Lead delivery across multiple cross-functional product and platform teams, establishing one integrated plan, clear critical path, transparent dependencies, and accountable owners.
 Convert the product roadmap into executable technology increments, release plans, capacity models, milestones, and outcome-based commitments.
 Drive delivery discipline across scope, schedule, cost, quality, resources, risk, and benefits, using forecasts rather than artificial certainty.
 Identify constraints early, remove impediments, resolve cross-team trade-offs, and escalate decisions with clear options and recommendations.
 Ensure each release has explicit entry, exit, acceptance, operational readiness, and rollback criteria.

 2. AI Engineering and AI SDLC Leadership 

 Apply deep knowledge of generative AI and agentic systems, including LLM orchestration, tool use, retrieval-augmented generation, prompt and context engineering, evaluations, guardrails, memory, and human oversight.
 Embed full-lifecycle AI SDLC practices across requirements, design, build, test, evaluation, deployment, monitoring, and model or prompt change management.
 Ensure AI quality is measured using fit-for-purpose evaluations covering safety, groundedness, relevance, accuracy, latency, reliability, and client experience.
 Champion specification-driven development, automation, reusable engineering patterns, and AI-assisted software delivery where approved.
 Ensure deterministic software testing and probabilistic AI evaluation are integrated into CI/CD and release decisions.

 3.      Azure, Architecture and Platform Integration 

 Provide senior technical leadership for solutions deployed on Microsoft Azure and integrated with BMO InvestorLine and Wealth Management platforms.
 Partner with solution, enterprise, security, data, and platform architects to maintain an approved, scalable target architecture and prevent local optimization or avoidable technical debt.
 Ensure APIs, event flows, data services, identity, access, observability, resilience, and non-functional requirements are designed and delivered end to end.
 Drive environment readiness, infrastructure as code, automated deployment, telemetry, performance engineering, capacity planning, disaster recovery, and production support readiness.
 Promote reuse of enterprise AI capabilities, shared services, patterns, and controls while preserving clear service boundaries and ownership.

 4.      Advanced Agile and Value-Stream Delivery 

 Establish and continuously improve an advanced Agile operating model organized around persistent, cross-functional teams and measurable client or business outcomes.
 Lead portfolio and product-level planning, backlog readiness, dependency management, release forecasting, and flow optimization across multiple teams.
 Use evidence-based metrics such as lead time, cycle time, throughput, work in progress, predictability, escaped defects, reliability, evaluation performance, and value realization.
 Reduce handoffs, unnecessary governance, meeting load, and blocked work; create fast decision paths and clear single-point accountability.
 Coach delivery leaders, Scrum Masters, engineering leads, and teams in modern product delivery, DevSecOps, continuous delivery, and learning-driven retrospectives.

 5.      Quality, Risk and Responsible AI 

 Build quality, privacy, security, regulatory compliance, model risk, accessibility, and responsible AI requirements into delivery from inception, not as release-end checkpoints.
 Partner with Legal, Risk, Compliance, Cybersecurity, Privacy, Model Risk, Data Governance, and Technology Risk to establish proportionate controls and auditable evidence.
 Ensure full-spectrum observability across application, infrastructure, data, model, prompt, agent, safety, and client-experience performance.
 Lead incident response, root-cause analysis, corrective action, and learning reviews for technology or AI quality events.
 Maintain transparent risk, issue, dependency, and decision records and ensure material risks are escalated promptly.

 6.      Stakeholder, Financial and Partner Leadership 

 Serve as the senior technology delivery voice for Em with InvestorLine, Wealth, Technology & Operations, Applied AI, governance partners, and executive forums.
 Provide concise, fact-based reporting on outcomes, delivery confidence, risks, financials, quality, and decisions required.
 Own technology delivery financial stewardship, resource planning, vendor performance, commercial dependencies, and delivery commitments.
 Lead co-build and vendor engagements with clear accountability, knowledge transfer, architecture compliance, security obligations, and measurable outcomes.
 Create an inclusive, high-accountability environment that develops leaders, strengthens technical depth, and keeps teams focused on client outcomes.

 Key Success Measures 

 Predictable delivery of roadmap outcomes and releases, with transparent forecast accuracy and controlled scope change.
 Measurable improvement in delivery flow, engineering productivity, automation, quality, and time to value.
 AI evaluation thresholds and non-functional requirements met before release and sustained in production.
 Stable, secure, resilient production performance with effective observability, incident management, and continuous improvement.
 Clear ownership, faster decisions, fewer cross-team handoffs, and effective dependency resolution.
 Measurable client adoption, experience, business value, and risk outcomes delivered in partnership with the Product Owner.
 Effective financial, capacity, vendor, and technical-debt management.

 Required Skills and Competencies 

 Expert-level technology delivery leadership in large, complex, regulated environments, with accountability for multiple teams and production outcomes.
 Deep practical knowledge of AI/ML and generative AI delivery, including agentic architectures, LLM application patterns, evaluations, guardrails, observability, and responsible AI controls.
 Strong knowledge of wealth management and digital investing platforms, including client journeys, advice or guidance experiences, market and portfolio data, trading-related integrations, and regulatory considerations.
 Advanced proficiency with Microsoft Azure cloud architecture and delivery, cloud-native engineering, APIs, integration, identity and access, data services, telemetry, resilience, and DevSecOps.
 Mastery of advanced Agile, product operating models, value-stream management, Lean flow, Scrum or Kanban, portfolio planning, CI/CD, test automation, and evidence-based delivery metrics.
 Ability to challenge constructively, make decisions under ambiguity, translate technical complexity into business implications, and influence senior executives.
 Commercial and financial acumen, including technology investment, capacity, vendor, contract, and delivery-performance management.
 Exceptional leadership, communication, facilitation, negotiation, and talent-development skills.

 Qualifications and Experience 

 15+ years of progressive experience in technology delivery, engineering, architecture, platform, or product technology leadership, including senior leadership accountability.
 Demonstrated success delivering enterprise-scale digital products or platforms from strategy through production and ongoing operation.
 Demonstrated delivery of AI/ML or generative AI solutions in production, ideally involving multi-agent systems or other complex AI-enabled client experiences.
 Significant experience with Microsoft Azure and modern software engineering practices in a regulated enterprise.
 Experience in wealth management, brokerage, digital investing, banking, or similarly regulated financial services is strongly preferred.
 Proven experience leading cross-functional internal and partner teams through complex dependencies and high-stakes releases.
 University degree in Computer Science, Engineering, Information Systems, Business, or a related discipline; relevant advanced degree or certifications are considered assets.
 Experience in Wealth Management or Capital Markets AI space (highly desirable) or Financial Institutions or Technology firms.
 Domain knowledge of investment, securities, trading from a technology perspective, having worked in such ecosystems.

 Leadership Expectations 

 Act as an owner: accountable for outcomes, not activity or coordination alone.
 Put clients, safety, quality, and sustainable value ahead of pace without evidence.
 Create clarity: make responsibilities, decisions, risks, dependencies, and delivery confidence visible.
 Lead with technical credibility while empowering engineering and product leaders closest to the work.

jobs.title: Senior Director, Data Architecture
jobs.description:
Job Description 

 What is the opportunity? 

 The Senior Director, Data Architecture simplifies and unifies RBC's data architecture across the full lifecycle: manufacturing, distribution, discovery, consumption and governance. They own the target data architecture, the RBC Lumina reference architecture and the standards that make data machine-readable for people, applications and AI agents.
 Success means fewer data stores and point-to-point feeds, one trusted source for each critical data element, and data products agents can find and use within their entitlements.

 What will you do? 
 Manufacturing (data sources). Name the authoritative source for every critical data element. Own the canonical data model and business glossary alignment. Set the standard for producer data contracts covering schema, semantics, quality rules and SLAs, so quality is fixed at the source.
 Distribution (RBC Lumina). Own the Lumina reference architecture and the standard ingestion patterns: batch, streaming, CDC, events and APIs. Move data once, reliably and traceably. Run the roadmap to retire point-to-point interfaces.
 Discovery and machine readability. Define what counts as a data product and the minimum metadata each must carry: meaning, owner, lineage, quality and entitlements. Build the semantic layer and ontology that lets agents interpret data, not just locate it. Set the agent-access pattern for data products, such as MCP.
 Consumption. Define the consumption archetypes (BI, operational APIs, analytics and ML, RAG, agents) with one supported pattern for each. Feed curated, entitlement-aware data products into the common RAG substrate.
 Governance by design. Act as design authority through architecture review, decision records and exceptions. Partner with the CDO, who owns policy and accountability, while this role owns how standards are built in. Support BCBS 239 lineage and jurisdiction-aware data placement for sovereignty.
 Simplification and transformation. Inventory data platforms, stores and tools across RBC's stacks and give each a disposition: tolerate, invest, migrate or eliminate. Tie the roadmap to in-flight programs such as Finance Modernization and AML Transformation, and to third-party rationalization.

 What do you need to succeed? 
 15+ years in data architecture or data engineering, including 5+ years leading architects at enterprise scale.
 Depth across lakehouse and warehouse platforms, streaming and CDC, data products and mesh, catalogs and metadata, semantic layers and knowledge graphs.
 A track record of measurable simplification: platforms retired, feeds removed and costs taken out.
 Working knowledge of BCBS 239, privacy regulation and OSFI expectations for data risk.
 Clear view on making data AI-ready, including retrieval, entitlement propagation and agent access.
 Able to align the CDO, platform engineering and business data owners without direct authority over them.

 What’s in it for you? 
 We thrive on the challenge to be our best, progressive thinking to keep growing, and working together to deliver trusted advice to help our clients thrive and communities prosper. We care about each other, reaching our potential, making a difference to our communities, and achieving success that is mutual.

 A comprehensive Total Rewards Program including bonuses and flexible benefits, competitive compensation, commissions, and stock where applicable
 Leaders who support your development through coaching and managing opportunities
 Ability to make a difference and lasting impact
 Work in a dynamic, collaborative, progressive, and high-performing team
 A world-class training program in financial services

jobs.description:
About The Role

GFL is seeking a visionary, high-energy leader with a passion for financial modeling, advanced analytics, and commercial business insights. Are you a strategic leader who thrives at the intersection of complex data, technology, and executive strategy? As the Director of Business Analytics, you will drive our enterprise-wide intelligence roadmap and foster a high-impact, data-driven culture across our fast-paced, high-growth organization.

This is a newly created position driven by our consistent expansion, appetite for data-driven decision-making, and relentless push for continuous improvement. You will join our leadership team at an exceptionally exciting time as we’ve embarked on our pricing program transformation, placing you at the forefront of this value creating engagement. Working with a "no can't do" attitude, you will translate complex technical data into compelling commercial narratives that shape global corporate strategy and optimize bottom-line performance.

Key Responsibilities

Reporting directly to the VP, Operations Strategy, you will lead a dynamic team to drive performance and deliver value-added decision support across the business. Key responsibilities include:

Pricing Excellence: Assess enterprise pricing performance, build advanced pricing models from scratch, identify margin opportunities, and challenge assumptions. Influence Area Vice Presidents and Business Unit leaders to translate analytical insights into actionable strategies that optimize commercial outcomes.
Advanced Analytics & AI: Champion statistical modeling, machine learning, and predictive analytics to transition the business from descriptive reporting to prescriptive intelligence. Accelerate speed-to-insight by integrating modern analytics tools, AWS-native workflows, predictive machine learning, and responsible GenAI/copilots.
Strategic Roadmap Development: Define and execute the long-term vision for the Business Analytics department. Scale enterprise data platforms and ensure full alignment between analytics initiatives and global corporate objectives.
Operational Excellence: Oversee the full data lifecycle—from ingestion and pipeline collaboration to the delivery of interactive executive dashboards, automated workflows, and high-impact predictive tools.
Data Governance & Integrity: Establish rigorous standards for data quality, security, and governance. Define control frameworks and KPIs to ensure business intelligence is accurate, reliable, and meeting compliance benchmarks.
Stakeholder Influence: Partner closely with Operations, Sales, Marketing, and Finance leadership. Translate ambiguous operational and market questions into clear recommendations, guiding executive partners through trade-offs with decision-ready narratives.
Team Leadership: Hire, coach, and retain a high-performing team of analysts and data professionals. Foster a culture of continuous improvement, analytical rigor, and collaborative business partnering.

Qualifications

10+ years of progressive experience in analytics, data science, or related quantitative fields, including experimentation frameworks, statistical modeling, and time-series analysis.
5+ years in pricing, revenue management, or applied data science within B2B or service-oriented industries, with a proven track record of building dynamic pricing and financial models from scratch.
5+ years of people management experience, including structuring team processes for service delivery in fast-paced environments, presenting to C-suite audiences, and driving cross-functional alignment.
Expert-level modeling skills and hands-on proficiency with major BI tools (Power BI, QuickSight, Tableau) and database querying (SQL).
Direct experience with AWS cloud data environments (e.g., S3, Glue, Athena, Forecast, or SageMaker) and leveraging GenAI/copilots to accelerate insight generation.
Executive Communication & Influence: Exceptional ability to distill complex data insights into concise, persuasive presentations for senior leaders.
Commercial & Financial Acumen: Deep understanding of operational finance, FP&A, and business operations, with the ability to link data metrics directly to bottom-line profitability.
Bachelor’s degree in Engineering, Finance, Economics, Statistics, or Computer Science required; Master’s degree in a quantitative field highly preferred.

KidSport Canada is a multi-sport children’s charity that provides financial assistance for registration fees to sport programs for kids aged 18 and under. We are a community based program with KidSport chapters in 176 communities across Canada. Our staff and over 3000 volunteers believe that all kids should have the opportunity to enjoy the lifelong benefits of sport participation.

The Opportunity

The Director of Finance and Administration will work closely with the CEO as part of the small staff team that operates KidSport Canada. This is a multi-faceted leadership position which is vital to the success of the KidSport program in communities across the country.  

This full-time position requires a strong leader to ensure that formal financial procedures are followed to safeguard KidSport Canada's financial assets, and provides accurate, timely financial reporting and administration to support organizational decision-making, compliance, and Board oversight.
﻿
The Director of Finance and Administration will be responsible for the following areas of the KidSport Canada program:
Budgeting, Financial Reporting and Transaction Processing
Tax Receipting
Donor Platform Management
Financial Risk Management
National IT Vendor Management
Statistical and Sponsor Reporting
Finance and Audit Committee Support
Administration and Compliance
National Leadership Team Participation

The candidate should have a passion for sport and believe in the life-long social development benefits that kids get from participating. This is a Senior Management position requiring a professional accounting designation (CPA) or equivalent finance / accounting credential. Ideally, they will possess 5+ years of progressive experience in financial management within a non-profit or charitable organization and be fluent in both official languages.

gingalls@kidsport.ca

Notre personnel et nos plus de 3 000 bénévoles estiment que tous les enfants devraient avoir la possibilité de profiter des bienfaits que procure la pratique du sport, et ce, tout au long de leur vie.

La possibilité

Le directeur ou la directrice des finances et de l’administration travaillera en étroite collaboration avec le chef de la direction au sein de la petite équipe qui assure l’exploitation de SportJeunesse Canada. Il s’agit d’un poste de direction aux multiples facettes, essentiel au succès du programme SportJeunesse dans les communautés partout au pays.

Ce poste à temps plein exige une personne dotée de solides compétences en leadership, qui sera chargée de veiller au respect des procédures financières établies afin de protéger les actifs financiers de SportJeunesse Canada. Le ou la titulaire du poste devra assurer la production de rapports financiers précis et ponctuels, ainsi qu’une gestion administrative pour soutenir la prise de décision et la conformité au sein de l’organisme, de même que la supervision par le conseil d’administration.  
Le directeur ou la directrice des finances et de l’administration sera responsable des aspects suivants du programme SportJeunesse Canada :
Budgétisation, rapports financiers et traitement des transactions
Reçus aux fins de l’impôt
Gestion de la plateforme des donateurs
Gestion des risques financiers
Gestion des fournisseurs informatiques nationaux
Rapports statistiques et de commandite
Soutien au comité des finances et de vérification
Administration et conformité
Participation de l'équipe de direction nationale

Le candidat ou la candidate

Le candidat ou la candidate doit avoir une passion pour le sport et être convaincu(e) des bienfaits sur le plan du développement social que la participation sportive procure aux enfants tout au long de leur vie. jobs.description:
Evinova is a health-tech business within the AstraZeneca Group, created to accelerate better health outcomes by driving digital transformation across the life sciences sector. We bring together science-based expertise, evidence-led rigor, and deep human insight to design digital solutions that help healthcare work better for everyone. Operating at the intersection of healthcare, technology, data, and analytics, we are changing how clinical research is conducted, how care is delivered, and how patients experience it, with solutions built to scale and to deliver better outcomes for patients worldwide.

We are driven by a shared purpose: to transform health through data and digital innovation. Our teams collaborate across disciplines to solve complex problems, continuously learning and evolving in a fast-paced, high-impact environment.

We are seeking a Director, Clinical Development Change & Transformation Lead to drive the change management and adoption work that turns Evinova's solutions into new ways of working across clinical development. Working within the transformation strategy and roadmap set by Evinova's Clinical Development Digital Innovation & Transformation leadership, you will lead the day-to-day delivery: redesigning processes with functional owners, preparing and equipping the workforce for change, and building the working relationships with Therapeutic Areas and Clinical Operations that turn deployment into real adoption and captured benefit.

You will be a visible, trusted presence on the ground in Mississauga — understanding the stakeholder landscape, running rollout and readiness activities, keeping communication and governance cadences moving, and channelling frontline insight and new ideas back to our product teams. As our solutions mature, you will help turn what works into repeatable playbooks and deliverables that support external customers on their own change journeys.

This is a hands-on leadership role for an experienced change practitioner who combines clinical development fluency with practical transformation delivery — organized, independent amid ambiguity, credible with senior customers, and energized by turning bold technology into real-world change.

Responsibilities

Change & Adoption Delivery: Lead the delivery of change management and adoption plans for Evinova's AI-enabled solutions across clinical development, translating the transformation strategy and roadmap into actionable workstream plans, turning points, and deliverables.

Stakeholder Engagement & Relationships:
Build and maintain working relationships across Therapeutic Areas, Clinical Operations, and enabling functions (e.g., Biometrics, Regulatory, Medical Writing, Quality). Maintain the stakeholder landscape map, act as a day-to-day point of contact for adoption, and prepare and support senior-level engagement where needed.

Process Redesign:
Lead process redesign workshops with functional and process owners: document current-state workflows, co-design AI-enabled future-state ways of working, and drive the actions needed to transition, including inputs to the controlled procedure and training updates that a regulated environment requires.

Workforce Readiness & Capability Building:
Deliver role and skills impact assessments, develop and run training and upskilling programs, and help embed responsible, compliant use of AI into daily work.

Rollout Execution:
Manage rollout execution in partnership with Product, Delivery, and customer teams — wave plans, readiness assessments, training logistics, hypercare, and post-launch support — and track issues and risks through to closure.

Communications & Governance:
Develop and run communication plans and engagement cadences across functions and sites, prepare executive updates and governance materials, and facilitate working groups and change forums.

Adoption Measurement & Benefits Tracking:
Track adoption and value measures — utilization, cycle-time and effort reduction, time-to-value, and user satisfaction — build the associated reporting and dashboards, and contribute to benefits validation with Finance against the argument.

Feedback Channels & Product Input: Run structured feedback channels — user advisory groups, voice-of-customer sessions, and adoption analytics — synthesize insight into prioritized recommendations and new ideas for Product, and support pilots and user validation of improvements before scaling.

Playbooks & External Customer Support: Contribute to and maintain transformation playbooks, toolkits, and deliverables, and support Commercial and Delivery teams in deploying them with external sponsors and CROs on their change journeys.

Change Champion Network: Build and coach the change champion and practitioner network across the portfolio, and lead the matrixed or small-team resources assigned to change workstreams [confirm team scope with Talent Acquisition].

Qualifications

Required (Must-Have)

Significant experience delivering change management, transformation, or technology adoption programs within pharmaceutical R&D, biotech, or health technology.
Strong understanding of clinical development and Clinical Operations processes, roles, and pain points — from protocol design through study conduct and close-out.
Hands-on experience implementing AI or digital solutions into ways of working, including impact assessments, process redesign, and training and capability building.
Strong stakeholder management: credibility with Director- and Senior Director-level stakeholders and the ability to influence across a matrixed, global organization.
Practical process redesign and facilitation skills (e.g., Lean, design thinking, or service design methodologies), with the ability to run workshops and produce clear current-state and future-state deliverables.
Excellent communication skills, with the ability to craft change narratives, training content, and executive-ready updates.
Experience running feedback mechanisms and translating user insight into actionable recommendations.
Comfort defining and tracking adoption metrics and benefits, including building reporting and dashboards.
Organized, independent delivery: able to manage multiple workstreams amid ambiguity and competing priorities and drive issues to resolution.
Bachelor's degree required; advanced degree a plus.

Additional Qualifications

Experience within a SaaS, product-led, or digital health organization.
Formal change management certification (e.g., Prosci/ADKAR, ACMP CCMP).
Familiarity with GxP-regulated environments and clinical trial technologies (study design platforms, eCOA, RBQM, and monitoring solutions).
Experience supporting generative or agentic AI deployments in an enterprise setting.
Experience building and leading change champion networks or communities of practice.
Experience in customer-facing roles across sponsor, CRO, or vendor environments.

At CIBC, we embrace your strengths and your ambitions, so you are empowered at work. Our team members have what they need to make a meaningful impact and are truly valued for who they are and what they contribute.

To learn more about CIBC, please visit CIBC.com

What You’ll Be Doing

As a Director, Capital Markets Finance, you will provide high quality reporting & advisory support to the Global Markets management team on financial and business performance, planning and forecasting. This includes reporting & analysis of the financial resources (e.g. revenue, expense, leverage, assets, liabilities, & FTE), planning and forecasting, performing/providing insights to Actual to Plan and DFE to GL variance analysis, and assessing the financial performance and developing financial plan for initiatives. This role will support Global Equities desks in Global Markets. It is an individual contributor role.

At CIBC we enable the work environment most optimal for you to thrive in your role. You’ll have the flexibility to manage your work activities within a hybrid work arrangement where you’ll spend 1-3 days per week on-site, while other days will be remote.

How You’ll Succeed

Reporting & analysis – Review daily, weekly, monthly and quarterly financial results and provide high quality, insightful and timely analysis of financial performance for Global Markets businesses. Identify opportunities for cost savings and support the effective management of Balance Sheet, Funding/Liquidity and Capital Resources (RWA, Leverage and Regulatory Capital). Ensure that reporting and analysis keep pace with the changing business and environment.
Planning and forecasting – Coordinate and support the development of the financial strategic and business plans for Global Markets. Work closely with business heads, Risk and Capital Management, to ensure reasonableness of market assumptions and impact of expected regulatory changes to ensure successful execution. Understand and review allocations to the business and be able to work closely with the counterparts in other areas of the bank to challenge allocations and ensure they are reasonable.
Business initiatives - Work closely with the business leader to provide sound financial advice on strategic and tactical initiatives and projects. Provide leadership, accountability and facilitate the implementation of business optimization/process reengineering, and strategic initiatives impacted supported businesses.
Collaboration - Establish and build healthy working relations and partnerships with the business leaders in Global Markets, as well as peers in Risk Management, Operations, Technology, Treasury and other areas of Finance.

Who You Are

You can demonstrate a minimum of 5 years experience in a Finance role, have a professional accounting designation and/or a post graduate business degree; good financial accounting knowledge and the ability to comprehend complex accounting issues and summarize them for the business; strong problem solving, analytical, judgment and change implementation capabilities.
You act like an owner. You thrive when you're empowered to take the lead, go above and beyond, and deliver results.
You're passionate about people. You find meaning in relationships, and surround yourself with a diverse network of partners. You build trust through respect and authenticity
You're driven by collective success. You know that collaboration can transform a good idea into a great one. You understand the power of an inclusive team that enjoys working together to bring a shared vision to life.
You give meaning to data. You enjoy investigating complex problems, and making sense of information. You're confident in your ability to communicate detailed information in an impactful way.
You live your values. You bring high standards, genuine care to your relationships, and want to grow with an employer that shares your values and brings out your best.

What CIBC Offers

At CIBC, your goals are a priority. We start with your strengths and ambitions as an employee and strive to create opportunities to tap into your potential. We aspire to give you a career, rather than just a paycheck.

We work to recognize you in meaningful, personalized ways including a competitive salary, incentive pay, banking benefits, a benefits program*, defined benefit pension plan*, an employee share purchase plan, a vacation offering, wellbeing support, and MomentMakers, our social, points-based recognition program.

jobs.title: Vice President of Technology and Data
jobs.description:
About the Role

The Vice President, Technology & Data will build the technology and data foundation Equiton needs to operate with greater confidence, efficiency and insight. The VP will assess Equiton’s current systems and capabilities, set a clear direction for improvement, and lead the work to create a more integrated, reliable and well-governed environment.

This is a player-coach role with broad impact across Equiton’s businesses. The VP will modernize core systems, centralize ownership of business applications, build an enterprise data warehouse and reporting capability, and advance practical uses of AI and automation, working with leaders across the organization to prioritize initiatives and deliver measurable results.

***Please note this is an in-office position based in Burlington, ON.

What You’ll Do

Strategy and Priorities

Assess Equiton’s technology environment, including systems, infrastructure, data, vendors, team capabilities and risks, and translate business priorities into a phased technology roadmap.
Define Equiton’s technology architecture and standards, building on our existing Microsoft environment and introducing new platforms where there is a clear business case.
Own the technology budget and build business cases for major investments, setting clear outcomes and tracking delivery, adoption, costs and benefits.

Systems and Delivery

Lead the modernization and integration of Equiton’s enterprise systems, including the transition to HubSpot CRM and the selection and implementation of accounting, property management and construction management platforms.
Guide projects from requirements through testing and launch, improving reliability, performance and adoption.
Take central ownership of all business applications and SaaS: maintain the inventory, approve new purchases, decide what to build, buy, improve or retire, and manage vendors, contracts, licensing, renewals, access and spend, with defined stakeholders and administrators for each application.

Data and AI

Lead the design and development of an enterprise data warehouse that brings Equiton’s core systems together in a reliable source of truth, with clear data ownership and quality standards.
Build reporting and analytics, including Power BI dashboards and self-service reporting, that give leaders timely insight into fund, portfolio, investor and operational performance.
Develop an enterprise approach to AI and automation, leading practical initiatives that improve productivity and decision-making, with appropriate safeguards for data protection, security and human oversight.

Governance and Team Leadership

Serve as Equiton’s senior information security leader, accountable for the cybersecurity program, including security policies, identity and access management, endpoint and vulnerability management, third-party risk, security awareness training and cyber-risk reporting to the CEO and leadership team.
Establish governance for technology, applications, data and vendors that supports applicable Canadian and U.S. requirements, and oversee incident response, disaster recovery and business continuity.
Lead and develop Equiton’s technology team, including internal development, data and reporting, and desktop support.
Partner with leaders across Equiton to understand business needs, drive adoption and deliver practical results.

What You’ll Bring

12+ years of progressive technology experience, including 5+ years in a senior leadership role setting strategy and leading the modernization of an existing environment, including enterprise system implementations (accounting, property management or construction management platforms especially relevant).
Bachelor's Degree in Computer Science, Information Technology, Engineering, Data Management, Business Information Systems, or a related field.
Deep experience with the Microsoft ecosystem (Microsoft 365, Azure, Entra ID, Power Platform) is required; experience leading a CRM migration (HubSpot preferred) or with AWS is an asset.
Strong, hands-on data background, including data architecture, warehousing, integrations, governance and BI, and a track record of delivering practical AI and automation initiatives.
Experience leading development, data and analytics teams or external partners, and managing a business application portfolio, vendors and technology spend.
Strong knowledge of cybersecurity and IT risk frameworks (such as NIST or CIS), with experience leading security, privacy and business continuity programs.
Experience in a regulated, complex or multi-business environment; real estate, private equity, asset management, multinational or U.S. market experience is an asset.
Strong communication and relationship-building skills, with the ability to explain technical decisions in business terms.

About Us

Founded in 2015, Equiton is one of Canada’s fastest-growing private equity firms, helping Canadians build wealth through high-quality real estate investments. Our mission is to make private real estate accessible to more Canadians, and our team is the driving force behind our success.

Follow us on LinkedIn
Visit our Website
Explore #LifeAtEquiton

Why Equiton?

Our culture is built on integrity, accountability, and innovation. We empower our team to take initiative, think independently, and grow personally and professionally. To learn more about our core values, click here.

Our Commitment to Diversity, Equity & Inclusion

We’re an equal opportunity employer committed to building a diverse, inclusive, and accessible workplace where everyone feels valued and supported. If you need accommodation during the hiring process, please let us know. We’re happy to help.

Only those selected for an interview will be contacted.

Please note that at present, legal eligibility to work in Canada is a prerequisite for this role.

AI-assisted tools are used to help improve efficiency and consistency; however, all hiring decisions are made by qualified members of our hiring team. We are committed to ensuring a fair, inclusive, and human-centered recruitment process.

jobs.title: Vice President (Head) of Finance
jobs.description:
Our client is a highly respected, mission-driven organization dedicated to improving well-being and quality of life in the communities it serves. The organization is seeking a strategic and forward-thinking Vice President, Finance to join its Executive Leadership Team. Reporting to the CEO, the Vice President will provide enterprise-wide leadership across Finance and corporate services, while serving as a trusted advisor to the CEO, Board of Directors, and senior leadership team.

The organization delivers essential services to a large and diverse client base. Behind every service are countless financial, operational, and strategic decisions that turn resources into meaningful impact. As Vice President, Finance, the successful candidate will ensure the financial strength, insight, and discipline needed to advance the mission and support long-term sustainability.

This is an exceptional opportunity for an accomplished finance executive who combines strategic insight with operational leadership and wants to influence meaningful outcomes in a purpose-driven organization. More than a functional leader, the Vice President will be a key enterprise partner, helping shape strategy, support growth, and position the organization for continued success in a complex operating environment.

The Mandate

The mandate extends well beyond traditional financial stewardship. As a member of the Executive Leadership Team, the VP will help shape organizational strategy, support evidence-based decision-making, and ensure the long-term sustainability of an organization delivering critical services.

In partnership with the CEO, Board, and senior leadership team, the VP will provide strategic financial leadership across planning, budgeting, forecasting, reporting, treasury, audit, risk management, and compliance. They will ensure financial resources are aligned with organizational priorities while maintaining the discipline and accountability the mission requires.

A key priority will be supporting the organization through a period of growth and change. Using financial insights and performance data, the VP will help evaluate opportunities, inform strategic initiatives, and optimize the deployment of resources in a complex funding and operating environment. Success will require balancing long-term vision with disciplined execution and sound financial management.

Beyond finance, the VP will provide executive oversight of key corporate services, including procurement and facilities, ensuring effective stewardship of organizational resources and infrastructure. The role will also lead efforts to strengthen internal capabilities, foster collaboration across departments, and build a high-performing, engaged team.

The successful candidate will have the opportunity to evolve the finance function from a trusted service provider into an even more proactive strategic partner and to enable data-driven decision-making across the organization. Success will be measured not only by financial outcomes, but also by the ability to influence strategy, support growth, and contribute to long-term sustainability and impact.

Leadership and Stewardship

The organization is seeking a VP Finance who leads with maturity and earns trust through action. This is not a role for someone who relies on title or tenure to get things done. The culture here rewards people who show up prepared, communicate clearly, and follow through.
Operates with humility, credibility, and sound judgment
Brings a practical, solutions-oriented mindset
Communicates clearly and influences at all levels
A good partner to the program managers – asking what they need before explaining what the number say
Leads with integrity, accountability, and transparency

Ideal Background

The successful candidate will bring experience in social services, healthcare, the boarder public sector, or the not-for-profit sector. Those who understand the operational, funding, and stakeholder dynamics of publicly funded organizations will be particular well positioned for success.
A CPA designation and progressive senior finance leadership experience.
Experience leading finance within a complex, multi-stakeholder organization.
A strong understanding of financial planning, financial reporting, treasury, governance, risk management, and internal controls.
Experience working with Boards and senior executives in a strategic advisory capacity.
The ability to translate financial information into actionable business insights.
A collaborative leadership style and a reputation for building strong relationships across an organization.

Why This Role

This is a rare opportunity to combine executive-level impact with genuine purpose. As a strategic partner to the CEO and Executive Leadership Team, the Vice President, Finance will help shape decisions that influence the organization’s direction, sustainability, and growth.

The successful candidate will join an organization at an exciting point in its journey, with the opportunity to strengthen financial stewardship, support strategic priorities, and help position the organization for continued success. The organization measures its success not only by financial performance, but by the positive impact it has on the people and communities it serves.

If you are ready to make a meaningful impact and help shape the future of a mission-driven organization, we encourage you to apply in confidence.

The work you'll do is more than just a job.

At the State of Minnesota, employees play a critical role in developing policies, providing essential services, and working to improve the well-being and quality of life for all Minnesotans. The State of Minnesota is committed to equity and inclusion, and invests in employees by providing benefits, support resources, and training and development opportunities.

This posting may be used to fill multiple vacancies.

The Minnesota Department of Revenue manages the state’s revenue system and administers state tax laws. We manage over 30 different taxes and collect more than $33 billion annually that pays for education, local government aid, property tax relief, social service programs, highways, economic development incentives, and other state operations.

The Department of Revenue is looking for a Chief Financial Officer that has a strong focus on relationship management, stakeholder and customer engagement and satisfaction, strategic partnership, process management, and change leadership qualities. We are looking for someone that champions operational excellence through continuous process improvement efforts that improve financial decision making, while increasing the accuracy and efficiency of fiscal operations.

This key leadership role provides strategic financial direction and services for the Department of Revenue and serves to move the agency toward realizing its mission, vision and strategies through strategic plans and aligned work objectives. This leadership position directs the Financial Management Division to ensure sound financial reporting, policies and procedures, and strong internal controls are in place for all financial aspects of the department while maintaining excellent customer service. As the leader of all financial aspects of the department, this position develops a highly functioning team within a hybrid work environment that is mission focused and provides timely, accurate, and efficient services in the following areas: agency biennial, supplemental and annual budgets, revenue accounting, accounts payable, accounts receivable, encumbrances, contract and grant agreements, and financial reporting.

Telework Info

This position is eligible for hybrid telework. Employees living within 50 miles of the office will be required to work in the office at least 50% of the time each month. Employees may reside outside the state of Minnesota if they live in a state bordering Minnesota and are within 50 miles of the primary work location.

Existing employees who were approved to telework from a bordering state and more than 50 miles from their work location before June 1, 2025, may retain this arrangement unless they move farther away.

Minimum Qualifications

Qualified applicants must possess a bachelor’s degree in Business, Accounting, Finance, Mathematics, Public Administration, Economics, or related field AND six (6) years of high-level management leadership experience that includes supervising and managing employees and financial management, analysis, and reporting.(A Doctorate degree may substitute for two years of experience, Master’s degree may substitute for 18 months of experience)

OR

Nine (9) or more years of advanced professional experience that includes leadership, managerial, or supervisory experience in organizational accounting, finance, budget and/or financial reporting.

Applicants who meet the above experience requirement will be further evaluated based on the following:

Development and use of business and financial analytics to support operations decisions.
Effective use of financial accountability and reporting systems.
Application and use of internal controls.
Development of organization, program, or product budgets.
Experience leading organization-wide financial planning efforts and establishing process timelines and deliverables.
Knowledge and application of generally accepted accounting principles.

Preferred Qualifications

Technical Skills:

Advanced degree (Master’s or higher) in Business, Finance, Accounting, Public Administration, Economics, or a related field.
Professional certification such as CPA, CMA, CGFM, or CGMA.
Demonstrated leadership of enterprise-level financial planning and analysis functions, including forecasting, scenario modeling, and development of data-driven insights used for strategic decision-making.
Experience overseeing complex governmental budgeting processes, including development, monitoring, and reporting of multi-fund, multi-biennium budgets.
Experience leading or directing revenue accounting or large-scale financial operations involving high-volume transactional systems.
Demonstrated experience creating or overseeing organization-wide financial policies, internal controls, and procedures supporting fiscal stewardship and statutory compliance.
Applied knowledge of governmental GAAP, GASB standards, and public-sector accounting principles.
Experience leading large-scale financial system implementations, upgrades, or integrations across multiple divisions.

Leadership Experience

Experience leading a multi-disciplinary financial organization of significant size and complexity (e.g., budget, accounting, revenue accounting, reporting, or audit units).
Demonstrated success managing and developing leaders and teams, including performance management, coaching, and succession planning.
Proven experience driving organization-wide process improvements or operational transformation efforts within a large organization (approx. 500+ employees).
Experience representing financial information to executive leadership, legislative bodies, oversight agencies, or public audiences, with the ability to explain complex financial content to both technical and non-technical stakeholders.
Demonstrated ability to build and maintain effective partnerships with internal divisions, external agencies, and community or governmental stakeholders.
Experience fostering an inclusive, respectful, and equity-driven workplace, including working effectively with individuals from diverse backgrounds and ensuring equitable operational and leadership practices

Physical Requirements

Requires occasional moving of articles such as boxes, accounting records, laptop computer, and portable printer.

Additional Requirements

As part of an offer of employment, a fingerprint-based background check will be conducted in accordance with IRS Publication 1075. This will include, but is not limited to, verification of degrees and licensures, state and federal criminal history checks, and a review of tax filing and payment history. All individual income tax filing and payment obligations must be current prior to interviewing for this position.

Must be legally authorized to work in country of employment without sponsorship for employment visa status (e.g., H1B status). The Department of Revenue is unable to provide sponsorship for work visas. Applicants must be eligible to work in the United States at the start of employment. MDOR does not participate in E-Verify

Select “Apply for Job” at the top of this page. If you have questions about applying for jobs, contact the Careers Help Desk at 651-259-3637 or email careers@state.mn.us. For additional information about the application process, go to http://www.mn.gov/careers.

To receive consideration as a Connect 700 Program applicant, apply online, email the Job ID#, the Working Title and your valid Proof of Eligibility Certificate by the closing date to Jessica Pearo at jessica.pearo@state.mn.us.

Evinova is a health\-tech business within the AstraZeneca Group, created to accelerate better health outcomes by driving digital transformation across the life sciences sector. We bring together science\-based expertise, evidence\-led rigor, and deep human insight to design digital solutions that help healthcare work better for everyone. Operating at the intersection of healthcare, technology, data, and analytics, we are changing how clinical research is conducted, how care is delivered, and how patients experience it, with solutions built to scale and to deliver better outcomes for patients worldwide.


We are driven by a shared purpose: to transform health through data and digital innovation. Our teams collaborate across disciplines to solve complex problems, continuously learning and evolving in a fast\-paced, high\-impact environment.

jobs.description:
Job Description

We are looking for a Senior Director to own the AI roadmap and strategy for our go-to-market organization: Sales, Customer Success, Professional Services, and Partnerships. You will partner with our segments and RevOps to decide where AI creates the most value across the customer lifecycle, and work with Engineering to deliver it through a deliberate mix of best-in-class SaaS platforms (such as Salesforce, Gong) and custom-built solutions where off-the-shelf products fall short.

You will work with internal stakeholders to define the problems worth solving, prioritize ruthlessly, and measure adoption and business impact. You will be the accountable leader for how AI shows up in the way we sell, onboard, deliver, retain, and grow with customers and partners.

Key Responsibilities

GTM AI strategy and roadmap

Define and own a multi-year AI vision and a quarterly roadmap spanning Sales, Customer Success, Professional Services, and Partnerships.
Identify, size, and prioritize AI use cases by revenue impact, productivity gain, cost to serve, and feasibility.
Establish clear principles for build vs. buy vs. configure, and make those calls transparently with business cases and total cost of ownership.
Align the GTM AI roadmap with company strategy, revenue targets, and the broader enterprise AI and data strategy.
Rationalize and govern overlapping tools and prevent AI sprawl across the GTM organization.
Run discovery, prototyping, pilots, and scale-up with clear success criteria and stage gates.

AI Across The GTM Functions

Sales: AI for prospecting and account research, lead and opportunity scoring, call and meeting intelligence, deal inspection and forecasting, proposal and RFP generation, pricing and quoting guidance, and rep coaching and ramp.
Customer Success: AI for health scoring and churn prediction, renewal and expansion signals, automated QBR and meeting prep, sentiment and call analysis, onboarding acceleration, and proactive risk alerts.
Professional Services: AI for scoping and estimation, project planning, knowledge retrieval, delivery acceleration, resource allocation, utilization, and margin improvement.
Partnerships: AI for partner identification and tiering, co-sell and pipeline insight, partner enablement, and ecosystem performance analytics.
Design cross-functional workflows that connect these motions, such as handoffs from sales to onboarding to delivery to renewal, so AI improves the whole customer lifecycle rather than isolated steps.

Adoption, change management, and value realization

Own adoption by partnering with Revenue Operations, enablement, and functional leaders on training, playbooks, and incentives so tools become part of daily work.
Define and report a KPI framework covering usage, productivity, pipeline and win rate, forecast accuracy, retention and expansion, services margin, and partner-sourced revenue.
Quantify ROI and report outcomes to executive leadership on a regular cadence.

Governance, data, and responsible AI

Work with Legal, Security, Privacy, and IT to set guardrails for AI use with customer and partner data, including access controls, data residency, model usage policies, and auditability.
Ensure AI outputs are trustworthy and that humans remain appropriately in the loop for high-stakes decisions.
Partner with Data and Analytics on data quality, definitions, and a shared source of truth.

Leadership and operating model

Build and lead a team of product managers and business analysts, and influence a broader matrixed group of Engineering, Data, and GTM Operations partners.
Establish intake, prioritization, and governance processes so GTM leaders (CRO, CCO, Services, Partnerships) jointly steer the roadmap.
Act as the executive-level voice on GTM AI, internally and externally, including with vendors, analysts, and peer companies.

Required Qualifications

12+ years of experience in product management, GTM operations or strategy, sales or revenue technology, or related roles, with 5+ years leading teams.
Demonstrated success owning a technology roadmap that serves revenue-generating teams, ideally across more than one of Sales, Customer Success, Professional Services, and Partnerships.
Deep working knowledge of the GTM technology stack, including Salesforce and conversation intelligence tools like Gong, and how data flows between systems.
Hands-on experience delivering AI/ML or generative AI solutions into production, including a practical understanding of LLMs, agents, retrieval, prompt and workflow design, evaluation, and cost management.
Strong build-vs-buy judgment, vendor management experience, and comfort building business cases.
Proven ability to drive change and adoption among frontline revenue teams and senior business leaders.
Excellent executive communication, with the ability to translate between technical teams and business stakeholders.
Analytical rigor and a bias toward measurable outcomes.

Preferred Qualifications

Prior experience as a sales, customer success, or services practitioner or leader, or in a hybrid GTM + product role.
Experience with Salesforce platform capabilities (Sales Cloud, Service Cloud, Agentforce or equivalent AI features), data cloud or warehouse integrations, and Gong or similar conversation intelligence tools.
Experience in a B2B, enterprise, or professional-services-oriented environment with long sales cycles and complex account structures.
Familiarity with partner ecosystems, co-sell motions, and channel programs.
Experience establishing AI governance and responsible-AI practices.

This posting is for proactive recruitment purposes and may be used to fill current openings or future vacancies within our organization.

Hybrid Work Model: We’ve adopted a flexible hybrid working environment for our office-based roles while delivering a seamless experience that is digitally and physically connected.
Flexibility & Work-Life Balance: Flex My Way is a set of supportive workplace policies designed to help manage personal and professional responsibilities, whether caring for family, giving back to the community, or finding time to refresh and reset. This builds upon our flexible work arrangements, including work from anywhere for up to 8 weeks per year, empowering employees to achieve a better work-life balance.

Our Grow My Way programming and skills-first approach ensures you have the tools and knowledge to grow, lead, and thrive in an AI-enabled future.
Industry Competitive Benefits: We offer comprehensive benefit plans to include flexible vacation, two company-wide Mental Health Days off, access to the Headspace app, retirement savings, tuition reimbursement, employee incentive programs, and resources for mental, physical, and financial wellbeing.
Culture: Globally recognized, award-winning reputation for inclusion and belonging, flexibility, work-life balance, and more. We live by our values: Obsess over our Customers, Compete to Win, Challenge (Y)our Thinking, Act Fast / Learn Fast, and Stronger Together.
Social Impact: Make an impact in your community with our Social Impact Institute. We offer employees two paid volunteer days off annually and opportunities to get involved with pro-bono consulting projects and Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) initiatives.
Making a Real-World Impact: We are one of the few companies globally that helps its customers pursue justice, truth, and transparency. Together, with the professionals and institutions we serve, we help uphold the rule of law, turn the wheels of commerce, catch bad actors, report the facts, and provide trusted, unbiased information to people all over the world.

About Us

Thomson Reuters informs the way forward by bringing together the trusted content and technology that people and organizations need to make the right decisions. Our products combine highly specialized software and insights to empower professionals with the data, intelligence, and solutions needed to make informed decisions, and to help institutions in their pursuit of justice, truth, and transparency. jobs.title: Program Manager, Critical Harm Operations
jobs.description:
About the Team 
 Critical Harm Operations sits within User Safety & Risk Operations and builds enforcement systems for Frontier Risk and Material Harm that are accurate, fast, defensible, and built to scale. We turn policy intent into operational readiness, review standards, quality systems, escalation paths, automation guardrails, and durable cross-functional operating models.
 About the Role 
 We are looking for an exceptional Program Manager to help build durable operating systems and run some of OpenAI’s most complex safety operations. The core need is a high-agency operator who can take an ambiguous problem, create the right structure, align cross-functional partners, and drive the work through execution.
 This role will move across Critical Harm priorities as needs evolve. You may step into operationalizing national security or violent-activities workflows, support wellbeing and Frontier Risk initiatives, or help scale programs such as Trusted Access. Deep domain expertise is helpful but not required; the strongest candidates will learn quickly, exercise excellent judgment, and make complex programs move.
 This Toronto-based role is currently remote and is expected to transition to an in-office arrangement by end of year.
 In this role, you will: 
 Lead strategic operational builds across priority workflows from problem statement to implemented operating model, including scope, owners, milestones, risks, success measures, and execution cadence.

 Translate policy, safety, technical, legal, and operational constraints into workflows, requirements, playbooks, escalation paths, and decision-making structures that teams can execute.

 Coordinate with User Ops leadership, Product Policy, Integrity, Safety Systems, i2, Legal, Product, Engineering, Support, vendors, and other partners to resolve dependencies and keep critical work moving.

 Move in and out of workflows as priorities shift—standing up new programs, stabilizing operations, improving handoffs, and transitioning durable ownership to the right team.

 Use operational data and frontline signals to identify bottlenecks, quality gaps, capacity needs, ownership failures, and the highest-leverage interventions.

 Drive high-priority escalations and cross-functional decisions to closure, ensuring the right context, accountable owners, clear next steps, and durable follow-up.

 Create the mechanisms that make programs run well: roadmaps, decision logs, status updates, risk registers, operating reviews, and crisp executive communication.

 Identify where AI tools, automation, lightweight systems, or simpler workflows can improve speed, consistency, and scale while preserving appropriate human judgment.

 You might thrive in this role if you: 
 Have 8+ years of experience in program management, strategy and operations, product operations, technical program management, trust and safety, support operations, risk operations, implementation, or a related field.

 Experience in cybersecurity, biosecurity, or related risk and safety operations is a plus

 Have a track record of taking complex, ambiguous work from problem framing through launch and scaled operation.

 Are unusually organized, sharp, and execution-focused; you can manage many moving pieces without losing the few decisions that matter most.

 Build trust and drive alignment across teams without direct authority, while keeping ownership, accountability, and escalation paths clear.

 Are technically and analytically fluent enough to reason about data flows, dashboards, tooling gaps, automation, and failure modes—even if you are not writing production code.

 Communicate clearly with technical, operational, policy, and executive audiences, especially when tradeoffs are sensitive or evidence is incomplete.

 Operate calmly and flexibly in a fast-moving environment, learn new domains quickly, and are comfortable handling high-severity or sensitive work.

 Experience with vendor operations, QA programs, launch readiness, workflow automation, or AI-assisted operations.

 Nice to have: 
 Experience in customer support or other high-stakes scaled operations.

 Deep expertise with national security, violence or other severe-harm domains.

 OpenAI is an AI research and deployment company dedicated to ensuring that general-purpose artificial intelligence benefits all of humanity. We push the boundaries of the capabilities of AI systems and seek to safely deploy them to the world through our products. AI is an extremely powerful tool that must be created with safety and human needs at its core, and to achieve our mission, we must encompass and value the many different perspectives, voices, and experiences that form the full spectrum of humanity.

jobs.title: Vice President, Global Core Trade Finance, TD Securities, Global Transaction Banking
jobs.description:
**Work Location:**

Toronto, Ontario, Canada
**Hours:**

37\.5
**Line of Business:**

TD Securities
**Pay Details:**

150 000 $/$150,000 \- 160 000 $/$160,000 CAD
This role is eligible for a discretionary variable compensation award that considers business and individual performance.
TD is committed to providing fair and equitable compensation opportunities to all colleagues. Growth opportunities and skill development are defining features of the colleague experience at TD. Our compensation policies and practices have been designed to allow colleagues to progress through the salary range over time as they progress in their role. The base pay actually offered may vary based upon the candidate's skills and experience, job\-related knowledge, geographic location, and other specific business and organizational needs.


As a candidate, you are encouraged to ask compensation related questions and have an open dialogue with your recruiter who can provide you more specific details for this role.


**Job Description:**

TD Securities ("TDS") provides a wide range of capital market products and services to corporate, government and institutional clients through Global Transaction Banking ("GTB"), Corporate and Investment Banking ("CIB"), and Global Markets ("GM"). The firm works with clients around the world, focusing selectively and strategically on key global financial centers: Toronto, Montreal, Calgary, Vancouver, New York, London, Singapore, and Tokyo. www.td.com


GTB is a key growth business within TDS that provides the opportunity to make an impact with top tier organizations. We offer innovative solutions and treasury advisory services on large and complex liquidity, payments, and trade and working capital finance needs. The business constantly changes with macroeconomic conditions, unprecedented levels of innovation, interest rate environments, and Foreign Exchange ("FX") movements. Accordingly, GTB continues to invest and innovate to support our clients' evolving needs.


GTB is comprised of three business lines: Trade \& Working Capital ("TWC"), Corporate Cash Management ("CCM"), and Financial Institutions ("FI"), which are underpinned by dedicated support functions, including GTB Risk \& Control, Product Management, Client Solutions, Data \& Analytics, and Deposit Portfolio Management. TWC is made up of Global Core Trade Finance ("GCTF") and Structured Trade \& Export Finance ("STEF"), which is comprised of Export \& Agency ("EAF") Finance and Working Capital Solutions ("WCS").


**Global Core Trade Finance (GCTF):**

* Clients principally include Fortune 500 and 100 companies with head offices located in North America and Europe, as well as key financial institutions.
* Develops client centric solutions to remove or reduce payment risk or facilitate working capital by employing traditional trade finance products (Standby Letters of Credit / Guarantees, Import Letters of Credit, Export Letters of Credit, or Documentary Collections) associated with our clients' domestic business needs or foreign sales and purchases.
* Supports strategic foreign banks and their clients' needs in North America \& UK and acts as a trusted partner to mitigate risks in our markets.
* Works closely with internal TD internal partners to provide "One\-TD" solutions to our clients.

**Job Description:**

Reporting directly to the Managing Director, and Head of Global Core Trade Finance , the candidate will be responsible for providing GCTFFinance product coverage, structuring advice, and risk mitigation solutions to a portfolio of Canadian domiciled, multinational corporates and for driving product penetration within assigned market. Proactivity, flexibility, technical product expertise, and origination discipline are required to deliver value from prospecting and pitching through deal structuring and execution. As a key product partner, the VP interacts with a wide variety of internal stakeholders including industry heads and sector leads within CIB and partners across credit management, GM, and GTB. A collegial and team\-oriented view of success is very important to allow the candidate to fit into the team. Having an entrepreneurial mindset is critical to manage through ambiguity and change associated with growing a business.


**Requirements:**

This role is suited to a detail\-oriented individual with a client\-centric focus, and a strong understanding of and demonstrated judgement related to credit structuring, execution, and risk. This candidate must be a subject matter expert in traditional Trade Finance (SBLCs/bank guarantees, export LCs, imports LCs, etc.) This candidate will have the ability to identify GCTF business opportunities and deliver mandates effectively. The successful candidate will be a strong advocate and trusted advisor to their clients, while balancing the requirements of GTB and the firm.  



  

**Job Responsibilities**

* **Deal Origination \& Structuring**
	+ Responsible for end\-to\-end transaction lifecycle, including origination (due diligence and pitching), structuring, and execution of transactions and opportunities within assigned portfolio.
	+ Lead origination efforts within assigned portfolio by identifying new opportunities to add new clients and increase our GCTF share of wallet.
	+ Provides deal structuring expertise and prepares / oversees delivery of creative and timely term sheets and pitches.
	+ Obtains credit concurrence and coordinates pricing approvals.
	+ Arrange and engage in client calls and presentations.
	+ Maintain an active pipeline of prospective new business.
	+ Work closely with regional teams in the US, Toronto, London, Singapore, Montreal, and Vancouver.

* **Client Engagement \& Relationship Management**
	+ Manage and deepen relationships with existing portfolio of clients through disciplined and dedicated coverage, serving as a trusted advisor and lead contact point for all GCTF matters.
	+ Help clients navigate the organization; engage the relevant

At Ontario Health, we are committed to developing a strong organizational culture that connects and inspires all team members across the province. Our vision is that together, we will be a leader in health and wellness for all. Our mission is to connect the health system to drive improved and equitable health outcomes, experiences and value. How we work together is reflected through our five values: integrity, inspiration, tenacity, humility and care. 

What Ontario Health offers:  

Role

At Ontario Health, your growth and well-being aren’t just supported—they’re celebrated every step of the way. Here, you have the opportunity to make a meaningful impact while shaping a fulfilling and sustainable career. Based on your role, you may receive:

Comprehensive health coverage from day one, with fully paid medical, dental, and vision benefits to support you and your family’s health
Flexible health care or wellness spending accounts, plus an inclusive program to support your overall well-being
A premium defined benefit pension plan, ensuring long-term financial security
Competitive vacation entitlement that encourages time to rest and recharge
Three personal days and two float days annually, providing added flexibility to support work-life balance, in addition to vacation days
Ongoing learning and career development opportunities designed to help you grow, advance, and thrive in your profession
A collaborative, values-driven workplace where integrity, care, humility, inspiration, and tenacity shape everything we do
Opportunities to participate in Communities of Inclusion, fostering belonging, equity, and the sharing of diverse perspectives across our team

Want to make a difference in your career?  Consider this opportunity. 

As Director, Planning and Implementation, you will lead health system strategies that respond to regional needs and advance integrated, equitable care. Reporting to the Vice President, System Strategy, Planning, Design and Implementation, you will turn strategic priorities into achievable program plans and oversee their implementation and evaluation.

Lead a cross-functional team and collaborate with regional and provincial partners across health sectors to close system gaps, strengthen coordination and deliver results. You will be accountable for your portfolio’s planning, team performance, and day-to-day program operations.

This regional role supports the health care needs and priorities of the North East Region.

Here Is What You Will Be Doing

Drive regional strategy: Assess health care needs, set priorities and lead integrated planning, implementation and evaluation aligned with provincial and regional strategies and Ontario Health’s Strategic Plan and Annual Business Plan.
Turn evidence into action: Work with regional colleagues to identify data sources and analysis that inform decisions, strengthen planning, and improve performance. Embed health equity principles and priorities throughout planning processes.
Build partnerships across sectors: Establish committees and communities of practice, engage internal and external partners, and connect regional and provincial teams to address system barriers, resource needs and accountability gaps.
Advance integration and innovation: Represent the portfolio on regional committees and other collaborative bodies, champion best practices and integrated care models, and recommend program improvements and funding allocation priorities informed by emerging health system issues.
Lead people and operations: Guide and manage staff, oversee day-to-day program operations, and ensure work follows accepted best practices, government and ministry directives, and regional policies and procedures.
Deliver measurable results: Establish regional goals and implement initiatives to achieve them. Monitor, evaluate, and report on activities against performance objectives set by the CRO.

Education And Experience

Here is what you will need to be successful:

Master’s degree in health or business administration, or equivalent education/experience.
7 years of work experience in the public or private health care sector.
5 years of experience leading or managing teams directly or indirectly, using relationship-building and management skills, with a solid background in managing staff to achieve corporate objectives.
Solid background in integrating large, complex initiatives in a changing environment, with advanced project management skills and the ability to manage multiple concurrent projects.

Knowledge And Skills

Business acumen: Apply business principles and systems thinking in health care, including financial and human resource management, organizational dynamics and governance, strategic planning, risk management and quality improvement.
Stakeholder engagement and relationship management: Develop networks, alliances and multiple external collaborative relationships that support department performance. Collaborate across functions and boundaries, find common ground with an expanding range of stakeholders, identify key issues, and accommodate key players’ needs on joint projects with external parties or units.
Communication and interpersonal skills: Highly developed verbal and written communication skills to provide and obtain complex, technical or sensitive information effectively, clearly, concisely and logically, at an appropriate level and in an appropriate format. Prepare and deliver presentations on technical and/or sensitive information to diverse audiences. Listen well, encourage open communication, and respond appropriately to others’ needs, feelings and capabilities with tact, compassion, sensitivity, and respect.
Judgement and negotiation: Exercise sound judgement on sensitive and contentious issues and negotiate consensus on complex policy strategies.
Strategic planning and risk management: Align department tasks and objectives with corporate goals, establish clear targets and measures to track progress, evaluate outcomes and adjust direction as appropriate.
Change management: Actively embrace change initiatives to improve department performance and use varied methods to help employees respond positively to change.
Health care planning and system design: Expert knowledge of planning models and approaches, with an understanding of the health care system and environment. Scan for ideas, best practices and system-wide trends, and effectively select options, plan, implement and evaluate health care policies and/or programs.
Program development and innovation: Develop new insights and apply innovative solutions to improve the organization. Foster creative thinking and innovation, and design and implement new or cutting-edge programs and processes.
Health sector and community knowledge: Knowledge of Ontario’s health sector and workforce trends; in-depth knowledge of local health issues, priorities and needs in the context of broader health care policy and system development trends; and knowledge of the needs of Indigenous peoples in urban and community settings and Francophone communities.
