Their Data & AI practice is one of the fastest growing parts of the firm, driven by strong demand from clients across sectors who want to modernize their data platforms and put AI to work at scale. They are looking for a Director to lead the growth and delivery of Google Gemini Enterprise solutions, owning client engagements from AI strategy through to enterprise-wide implementation while working closely with Google Cloud to build and take joint offerings to market.

Act as a trusted advisor to senior client stakeholders, including CIOs, CTOs, CDOs, and CFOs, guiding their AI transformation agendas
Lead AI strategy engagements, including maturity assessments, Gemini Enterprise roadmaps, and operating model and governance design
Translate complex business challenges into clear AI-enabled opportunities and value cases

Advise on scalable deployment models and enterprise integration with ERP, CRM, and collaboration platforms
Lead large-scale AI programs from pilot through enterprise rollout, owning quality, timelines, and value realization
Build reusable assets and accelerators, such as use cases, reference architectures, and deployment playbooks, to scale delivery
Build and manage strategic relationships with Google Cloud, aligning client needs with product roadmap evolution
Co-develop joint solutions and go-to-market offerings with partners and contribute to capability development
Support business development and complex pursuits, including solution shaping, proposals, and pricing models
Present Gemini Enterprise solutions to executive audiences, turning technical concepts into clear business narratives
Drive client-facing storytelling on agentic AI, productivity gains, and ROI
Contribute to thought leadership and market positioning in AI transformation

Requirements

10+ years in consulting, technology, or AI/data leadership roles
Proven track record delivering enterprise AI or cloud transformation programs
Expertise in enterprise AI architecture and design
Strong expertise in generative AI and LLMs, enterprise data architecture, and cloud platforms, with experience on GCP considered an asset
Experience engaging and influencing C-suite stakeholders
Ability to shape, position, and close complex deals
Demonstrated success contributing to business development and revenue growth
Experience with the Google Cloud ecosystem and strategic alliances
Exposure to AI agents, agentic workflows, and enterprise AI governance frameworks
Track record building repeatable consulting offerings and intellectual property

Benefits

Compensation listed on the posting is for base salary only. Total salary includes base salary + annual bonuses.
Comprehensive Total Rewards program
Lead a flagship Google Gemini Enterprise practice inside one of the fastest growing teams at the firm
Shape how major Canadian organizations across sectors adopt generative and agentic AI, moving them from pilot projects to enterprise-wide rollouts
Work directly with Google Cloud to influence product roadmaps and build joint offerings that reach clients across the country
Build the playbooks, reference architectures, and IP that will define how the firm delivers AI transformation for years to come

Submit your application, including your resume and cover letter, through our online portal. Our team will carefully review your qualifications and experiences. Your journey with Toast begins here, and we’re excited to see what you bring to the table!

Vetting Call

This 30-45 minute informal conversation is designed for us to get to know you better and assess your skills. Be prepared to discuss your past projects, the challenges you’ve tackled, and the impact you’ve made. This is your chance to shine and show us why you’re a great fit for the roles we offer.

Profile Creation

Once you’ve impressed us in the vetting call, we’ll create an unbiased profile that highlights your experience while minimizing common biases. Instead, we focus on your skills, industry experience, and the impact you’ve made. This way, your profile reflects your true potential and accomplishments.

Client Submission

After crafting your unbiased profile, we submit it to our trusted clients. We work closely with these clients to ensure they understand the value you bring. Throughout their interview process, we remain by your side, providing support and guidance. Our goal is to help you navigate the hiring process smoothly and confidently, ensuring you have the best chance to secure a role that fits your skills and aspirations.

jobs.title: VP Technology and Innovation Partners
jobs.description:
Dayforce is a global human capital management (HCM) company headquartered in Toronto, Ontario, and Minneapolis, Minnesota, with operations across North America, Europe, Middle East, Africa (EMEA), and the Asia Pacific Japan (APJ) region.

Our award-winning Cloud HCM platform offers a unified solution database and continuous calculation engine, driving efficiency, productivity and compliance for the global workforce.

Our brand promise - Makes Work Life Better™ - Reflects our commitment to employees, customers, partners and communities globally.

About The Opportunity

Dayforce is the AI-powered people platform. One platform for HR, Pay, Time, Talent, and Analytics, with AI built into how work gets done. Partners are central to that strategy. The AI capabilities, data, and solutions our partners bring to the platform extend what Dayforce AI can do for customers and accelerate how fast we grow.

That is changing what our technology ecosystem does for the business. Partners are moving from integrations that sit next to the platform to AI-enabled solutions we resell, transact, and build on together. That shift touches revenue, product strategy, and how Dayforce competes.

The VP, Technology and Innovation Partners owns the strategy, performance, and commercial outcomes of Dayforce’s technology partner ecosystem across five areas: ISV partners Dayforce resells, including Go1, Emburse, Docusign, Aquera, etc.; ISV partners with certified connectors on the Dayforce Exchange across Pay and Benefits and HR and Talent; the Microsoft partnership; In Country Payroll partners; and Dayforce Build.

This is a leader-of-leaders role with a number attached. You will be accountable for resell bookings, partner-sourced and partner-influenced pipeline, marketplace revenue, and the quality of the integrations and solutions partners deliver. You will lead an established team of four senior leaders who own the Microsoft alliance, In Country Payroll, Pay and Benefits ISVs, and HR and Talent ISVs. You will operate as a peer to the leaders of our Services Delivery and Community pillars. We are looking for a leader with the commercial, go-to-market, and technology depth to run all of it as one business.

Work is what you do, not where you go. For this role, we are open to remote work and can hire anywhere in the US or Canada.

What You’ll Get To Do

Business Ownership and Growth

Carry the technology partner number. Own resell bookings, partner-sourced and partner-influenced pipeline, and marketplace revenue, with clear accountability to the CRO organization.
Scale software resell. Grow attach of resold partner solutions to core Dayforce deals. Set the margins, pricing, packaging, and commercial terms that make resell a material, predictable revenue line.
Make the Exchange transactable. Share ownership with Product of moving the Dayforce Exchange from referral-only to transactable. Own the partner commercial model, partner onboarding, and partner readiness.
Make partners a growth engine for Dayforce AI. Build the partner strategy that extends the AI-powered people platform. Bring in the AI partners, agents, and solutions that deepen what Dayforce AI delivers for customers and create new revenue.
Own the portfolio. Decide which partners we resell, which we integrate and refer, which we co-build with, and which we retire. Close gaps in the Dayforce offering through build, partner, or buy recommendations with Product and Corporate Development.

Microsoft

Serve as executive sponsor for Microsoft, supporting the alliance lead who owns the day-to-day relationship across partnership, sales, and product teams.
Grow Dayforce’s position as a strategic HCM and payroll partner in the Microsoft ecosystem, across Azure, Dynamics 365, Copilot, and Teams.
Build and run a joint HCM, Pay, and ERP go-to-market with Microsoft and the SI partners that deliver it, including marketplace, co-sell programs, and field-to-field engagement.
Lead AI co-innovation that turns Microsoft technology into differentiated Dayforce AI capability.

Global Payroll and In-Country Partners

Own the strategy and performance of the In Country Payroll network that delivers and extends Dayforce global payroll.
Set standards for coverage, service quality, compliance, integration, and customer experience, and hold partners to them.
Rationalize and expand country coverage based on customer demand and deal pipeline.
Work with Product and Operations to deliver one consistent global payroll experience, whether Dayforce or a partner runs the payroll.

Dayforce Build

Dayforce Build is the platform customers and partners use to build integrations, extensions, and new capabilities on Dayforce. Partners are already building in it. This role turns that early momentum into a scaled partner ecosystem.

Own the partner strategy and growth of Dayforce Build, sharing ownership of the platform roadmap with Product and Engineering.
Move partner builds, including AI-powered extensions and agents, from proof of concept to production, certified, and in market.
Recruit and grow the ISVs, SIs, and developers building on the platform, including through the Dayforce Developer Community.
Connect what partners build to the Exchange, the resell program, and field go-to-market so builds turn into revenue.
Set quality, security, and certification standards for everything partners build on Dayforce.

GTM and Field Execution

Build repeatable joint go-to-market motions with priority partners: co-sell plays, joint campaigns, enablement, and account mapping.
Drive field adoption of resell and partner solutions across segments.
Equip Dayforce sellers with the positioning, pricing, and proof points to attach partner solutions to core deals, so partner attach is a default consideration rather than an exception.
Partner with Marketing on ecosystem launches, events, and partner showcases.

Leading the Team

You will lead four senior leaders, each running a distinct motion. Your first job is to make them operate as one ecosystem.

Microsoft Alliance owns the day-to-day Microsoft relationship, co-sell, and joint GTM.
In Country Payroll owns the global payroll partner network, coverage, and service quality.
Pay and Benefits ISVs owns the partners that extend Dayforce Pay and Benefits through connectors and resell.
HR and Talent ISVs owns the partners that extend Dayforce HR and Talent through connectors and resell.
Coach, develop, and raise the bar across the team. Have a clear point of view on strengths and gaps within your first quarter.
Establish one scorecard and operating rhythm across all five areas, balancing long-term platform strategy against near-term revenue.

Technology and Product Influence

Serve as the technical voice of the partner ecosystem inside Dayforce.
Partner with Product and Engineering on integration architecture, APIs, connector certification, and partner developer experience.
Partner with Product on the Dayforce AI roadmap, so partner AI capabilities complement and extend what Dayforce builds.
Scout emerging technology and AI partners that expand the Dayforce platform and create new revenue.

Executive and Cross-Functional Influence

Operate as a trusted counterpart to executive leadership across Sales, Product, Engineering, Marketing, Legal, and Finance.
Negotiate complex resell, revenue share, and strategic partner agreements, and hold partners accountable through data, not sentiment.
Present performance, risk, and opportunity directly to the executive team with clarity and conviction, including in forums with sponsor visibility.
Executive exposure to the CRO, Product, and Technology organizations, and to Microsoft executive leadership, as a matter of routine, not exception.

Skills And Experience We Value

15+ years in enterprise software, with at least 7 years leading technology partnerships, alliances, or ecosystem businesses, and meaningful time spent carrying a number.
A track record of growing partner revenue, including resell or OEM models, with specifics: bookings delivered, attach rates moved, marketplace revenue grown.
Direct experience scaling a SaaS marketplace, app ecosystem, or developer platform program, ideally including the move to a transactable model.
Deep experience with Microsoft or another hyperscaler: co-sell programs, marketplace, and executive sponsorship.
Strong commercial judgment. You have structured and negotiated complex resell, revenue share, and strategic partner agreements.
Enough technical depth to lead conversations on APIs, integration architecture, cloud platforms, and AI with engineering teams on both sides.
A clear point of view on how AI is reshaping software ecosystems, and experience bringing AI partners and solutions to market.
Experience leading senior leaders who each run a distinct business and making them operate as one team.
Familiarity with HCM, payroll, ERP, or an adjacent enterprise platform category.
Comfort operating in a private equity-backed environment, with the pace, transparency, and accountability that entails.
Highly analytical and metrics-driven, at ease in complex matrixed environments and in front of an executive audience.

What Would Make You Stand Out

Global payroll experience is a strong advantage.
Prior PE-backed experience is a strong advantage.

What’s In It For You

Dayforce is fueled by the diversity of our talented employees. We are an equal opportunity employer and consider and embrace ALL individuals and what makes them unique. We believe our employees should be happy and healthy, with peace of mind and a sense of fulfillment.

We encourage individuals to apply based on their passions.

Dayforce encourages personal and professional growth. We offer excellent time away from work programs, comprehensive wellness initiatives and recognition through competitive pay and benefits.

With a commitment to community impact, including volunteer days and our charity, Dayforce Cares we provide opportunities for you to thrive both in your career and personal life. Our focus is not just on your job but on supporting you to be the best version of yourself.

This job posting is for an existing vacancy

Artificial intelligence may be used in the screening, assessment, or selection of applicants for this position.

jobs.description:
About The Company

The Northwest Territories Power Corporation (NTPC)
is the primary public electricity utility serving the Northwest Territories and plays a critical role in supporting the territory's economic development, community well-being, and energy security. As a crown corporation wholly owned by the Government of the Northwest Territories through NT Hydro, NTPC is responsible for generating, transmitting, and distributing electricity across one of the most geographically vast and operationally challenging jurisdictions in North America. The organization provides power to more than 43,000 residents across 27 communities and manages a diverse portfolio of hydroelectric, diesel, natural gas, solar, wind, and battery storage assets. With more than $650 million in assets and approximately 151 MW of generating capacity, NTPC operates a geographically dispersed and operationally diverse utility system across the Northwest Territories.

For more information, please download the full position profile: NTPC CFO Position Profile.pdf

Position Overview

The ideal candidate is an accomplished executive with a proven track record leading finance, treasury, risk management, regulatory affairs, and capital planning functions within large, complex, and highly regulated organizations. Experience within the utility, energy, infrastructure, natural resources, transportation, or broader public-sector sectors will be highly valued. They will bring deep expertise in long-term financial planning, capital allocation, enterprise risk management, and organizational performance, alongside a demonstrated ability to support critical investment decisions where commercial outcomes, public accountability, and long-term sustainability must be carefully balanced.

The successful candidate will possess the strategic perspective and business judgment required to help guide NTPC through a period of infrastructure renewal, energy transition, and economic development across the Northwest Territories. As a trusted advisor to the CEO, Board of Directors, and the Audit & Risk Committee, they will bring the credibility to navigate complex relationships with government, regulators, Indigenous governments, lenders, and other key stakeholders.

They will be equally comfortable evaluating major capital projects, supporting regulatory and rate-setting processes, identifying new business opportunities, and helping shape the Corporation's long-term strategic direction. As a leader, the preferred candidate will build strong teams, develop future leaders, and create an environment characterized by accountability, safety, collaboration, and continuous improvement.

With exceptional communication skills and executive presence, they will confidently represent NTPC in boardrooms, government forums, regulatory proceedings, and stakeholder engagements. Above all, they will be motivated by the opportunity to contribute to a purpose-driven organization whose success directly supports the energy security, economic prosperity, and long-term sustainability of communities across the Northwest Territories.

Education And Experience Requirements

Education and Professional Background

CPA designation, MBA, or other relevant postgraduate degree.
Minimum of 10 years of progressive financial leadership experience.
Extensive management and supervisory experience, preferably within a utility or similarly complex operating environment.
Demonstrated experience leading financial management functions, including planning, reporting, analysis, and performance oversight.
Experience working effectively with executive leadership teams, regional leaders, and diverse stakeholder groups.

WORK ARRANGEMENT

The role is based at NTPC’s head office in Hay River and requires a visible leadership presence within the organization and community. Travel to Yellowknife, regional plants, offices and communities throughout the Northwest Territories will be required.

The position requires visits to regional and area plant and office locations, which may involve travel in small aircraft and the possibility of extended travel due to weather conditions. Work pressures and demands often require work outside of normal office hours. In this role, you must maintain the confidentiality of all Corporation information that comes to the incumbent’s attention as a result of their employment with the Northwest Territories Power Corporation.

RECRUITMENT PROCESS

We welcome conversations with individuals interested in learning more about this unique leadership opportunity. To explore the role in confidence, please contact a member of our Executive Search team at MNP.

To apply, please submit a résumé and cover letter in confidence through MNP's online application portal or directly to the contacts below. All inquiries and applications will be managed through MNP to ensure a fair, confidential, and consistent recruitment process.

The Northwest Territories Power Corporation is committed to building a representative workforce and values the contributions of Indigenous peoples. Qualified Indigenous candidates are encouraged to self-identify during the application process and may be eligible for consideration under NTPC's Indigenous Employment Policy.

We thank all applicants for their interest; however, only those selected to move forward in the process will be contacted.

⠀

The Director, Defense Portfolio Strategy reports to the Chief Strategy Officer and directly supports the CSO's enterprise mandate to identify and unlock growth above the underlying market rate. Defense is CAE's largest such opportunity, and this role carries the analytical and transactional workload behind it.

The Defense & Security business unit owns its strategy. This role does not duplicate or adjudicate it. Instead, the Director works on the questions that sit above and across the operating plan — where CAE should allocate capital and capability within the Defense domain, which adjacencies merit entry, what the enterprise should build, buy, or partner for, and how the Defense portfolio should evolve to deliver above-market growth.

The Director operates as a full member of the corporate strategy team. The above-market growth mandate is enterprise-wide and held by the CSO; this role brings dedicated defense-domain depth to it, working alongside colleagues whose expertise spans other domains and functions. Portfolio work remains collective — the addition here is capacity and depth against a specific CEO-level priority, not a redrawing of scope.

Key Responsibilities

Portfolio Strategy and Capital Allocation

Quantify the gap between the Defense market's underlying growth rate and CAE's growth ambition, and maintain a live view of which portfolio moves close it — with what confidence, on what timeline, and at what capital cost.
Develop CAE's point of view on where Defense capital and capability should be deployed to generate above-market growth, and where they should not.
Assess portfolio adjacencies, capability gaps, and whitespace across the Defense domain, framing entry, expansion, and exit questions for executive decision.
Build the build / buy / partner logic for capabilities the Defense portfolio requires.
Contribute the Defense lens to enterprise portfolio reviews and capital allocation discussions alongside corporate strategy colleagues covering other domains.
Develop investment cases for new markets, segments, and capability plays, in partnership with the business unit strategy team.

M&A and Partnership Pipeline

In Collaboration With The Strategy Team Colleagues

Build and actively cultivate a pipeline of acquisition and partnership candidates aligned to the Defense portfolio thesis, maintaining live relationships well ahead of any formal process.
Maintain a standing view of the defense industrial landscape — who is consolidating, who is available, where valuations are moving.
Partner with Corporate Development through diligence and execution; support integration planning where strategic rationale must be preserved.
Evaluate teaming, joint venture, and partnership structures as alternatives to acquisition.

Technology Enabler Pipeline

Identify, map, and cultivate relationships with startup, scale-up, and pre-IPO companies whose technologies could accelerate CAE's Defense capabilities or threaten its positions.
Maintain an ongoing landscape view of emerging technologies relevant to simulation, training, and mission readiness.
Create structured pathways from early engagement through pilot, commercial partnership, investment, or acquisition.
Connect CAE to relevant venture, accelerator, and defense-innovation ecosystems, sharing that access across the strategy team.

Market Intelligence and Enterprise Contribution

Bring outside-in intelligence on defense budgets, procurement trends, geopolitical shifts, and competitor moves into both business unit and corporate strategy discussions.
Contribute to enterprise strategy work beyond Defense where domain insight is relevant — this is a shared-team role, not a single-vertical one.
Prepare executive-level analysis and briefing materials for the CEO, Executive Committee, and Board.
Support Government Relations and business unit leadership with strategic context for key customer engagements.

This Role Succeeds Through Partnership Rather Than Authority

With the Defense & Security business unit — the BU owns its strategy and operating plan. The Director brings portfolio and transaction perspective to that work and takes the BU's market reality into enterprise portfolio decisions. Joint work products, jointly presented.
With corporate strategy colleagues — a peer contributing defense depth to a shared team agenda, drawing on colleagues' functional and domain expertise in turn. Enterprise portfolio work remains collective.
With Corporate Development — origination and strategic framing from this role; transaction execution led by Corporate Development.

Demonstrated experience with portfolio strategy, capital allocation, or build/buy/partner decision-making in a complex global organization.
Strong command of defense markets, government procurement, and allied defense spending dynamics.
Direct experience with M&A origination, partnership development, or technology scouting.

Comfortable operating with ambiguity, across multiple time horizons, in a fast-moving environment.
Excellent written and verbal communication, including executive-level presentation and narrative skill.

You’ll also prepare clear recommendations and insights for senior leaders to support decision-making and the delivery of CIBC’s future workplace strategy. 

 At CIBC we enable the work environment most optimal for you to thrive in your role. You’ll have the flexibility to manage your work activities within a hybrid work arrangement where you’ll spend 1-3 days per week on-site, while other days will be remote. Details on your work arrangement will be discussed at the time of your interview. 

 How you’ll succeed 
 Lead workplace strategy execution – Translate CIBC’s Global Workplace Experience Strategy into practical design strategies, standards and enablement approaches for real estate transformation projects across the portfolio. 
 Provide strategic advice – Partner with leaders and project teams to apply workplace experience principles, align initiatives to enterprise priorities, and recommend solutions that improve the workplace experience and support the future of work. 
 Use insights to inform decisions – Conduct market research, evaluate internal and external trends, and use employee feedback and workplace data to identify opportunities, inform recommendations, and strengthen strategic planning. 
 Support change and enablement – Develop materials, approaches, and change tactics that help leaders and team members adapt to evolving workplace environments and new ways of working. 
 Build strong partnerships – Work closely with partners across Enterprise Real Estate, Human Resources, Design, Technology, Corporate Security, Events, Retail, and Facilities Management to support coordinated planning and successful implementation. 
 Present to senior leadership – Prepare clear, compelling findings, business cases, and recommendations for senior leaders and executive forums, highlighting benefits, risks, dependencies, and considerations for decision-making. 

 Who you are 
 You can demonstrate 10 years of experience in workplace strategy, strategic planning and real estate transformation, and change enablement. You have experience in workplace design, employee experience, operating model change, or enterprise transformation in a large, complex organization. 
 You have a degree or diploma in a relevant field. It’s an asset if you have education or experience related to workplace strategy, business strategy, design, organizational change, or real estate. 
 You’re future focused. You look beyond the moment and help shape strategies that will make a difference today and tomorrow. You identify opportunities to evolve the workplace in support of business and workforce priorities. 
 You’re analytical. You give meaning to data and research. You enjoy investigating complicated problems, identifying trends, and turning insights into clear, practical recommendations. You have well-developed communication and presentation skills, both written and verbal. 
 You’re influential. Your influence makes a difference. You build credibility with senior leaders and partners and help bring about change by sharing your expertise and recommendations in a clear and thoughtful way. 
 You’re collaborative. You’re motivated by collective success and work effectively across functions to bring people together, align priorities, and deliver shared outcomes. 
 You’re a caring and accountable leader. You have experience developing strategic team goals, creating clarity around priorities and ways of working, and coaching others to support strong performance and growth. 
 You live your values. You bring high standards, genuine care to your relationships, and want to grow with an employer that shares your values and brings out your best 

 What CIBC Offers 

 At CIBC, your goals are a priority. We start with your strengths and ambitions as an employee and strive to create opportunities to tap into your potential. We aspire to give you a career, rather than just a paycheck.
 We work to recognize you in meaningful, personalized ways including a competitive salary, incentive pay, banking benefits, a benefits program*, defined benefit pension plan*, an employee share purchase plan, a vacation offering, wellbeing support, and MomentMakers, our social, points-based recognition program.

 Our spaces and technological toolkit will make it simple to bring together great minds to create innovative solutions that make a difference for our clients.

 We cultivate a culture where you can express your ambition through initiatives like Purpose Day; a paid day off dedicated for you to use to invest in your growth and development.

 *Subject to plan and program terms and conditions

 What you need to know 
 CIBC is committed to creating an inclusive environment where all team members and clients feel like they belong. We seek applicants with a wide range of abilities and we provide an accessible candidate experience. If you need accommodation, please contact Mailbox.careers-carrieres@cibc.com

 We use artificial intelligence tools during the recruitment process. Our goal for the application process is to get to know more about you, all that you have to offer, and give you the opportunity to learn more about us.

jobs.title: Vice President, Analytics & Health Outcomes
jobs.description:
WHO WE ARE

GreenShield is a proudly Canadian, national non-profit health care and insurance organization, driven by our mission of Better Health for All. We believe health care is a right, not a privilege, and we are committed to improving health outcomes, advancing health equity, and building a future where every Canadian can reach their full health and well-being potential.
Through our unique integrated payer-provider ("payvider") model, we offer insurance, administer benefits, and pay claims as a ‘payer’ while offering health care services such as mental health, pharmacy, telemedicine, and chronic disease management as a ‘provider’. As a non-profit social enterprise without shareholders, we reinvest our excess earnings to directly support underserved communities. Through GreenShield Cares, we positively impacted the health and well-being of over one million Canadians between 2020 and 2025. What’s driving us now is the commitment to measurably impact an additional three million Canadians by 2030 – across mental health, essential medicines, and chronic disease management – through scalable initiatives that deliver meaningful change in pursuit of our mission of Better Health for All.
At GreenShield, our culture is where purpose meets passion and performance. Our teams work as one to deliver meaningful, measurable impact for the people and communities we serve.

THE ROLE IN A NUTSHELL

Reporting to the SVP, Product, Experience & Health Outcomes, the Vice President, Analytics and Health Outcomes is a strategic senior leadership role responsible for turning GreenShield’s data into actionable insights, measurable outcomes, and clear narratives that inform priorities, support decision-making, and demonstrate impact. This leader will work across the organization to connect analytics and insights to enterprise priorities and measurable impact in a way that helps leaders understand what is happening, why it matters, and where to act.

This role will be responsible for:

Lead enterprise analytics and outcomes capabilities, ensuring data is used to inform priorities, guide investment decisions, and measure impact across the enterprise.
Translate complex data into clear insights, narratives, and recommendations that help executives, product teams, clinical leaders, clients, and partners understand where to act and how to create measurable value.
Build scalable measurement practices that help GreenShield assess performance, outcomes, and impact across its portfolio.
Develop clear, evidence-based insights for internal and external stakeholders to demonstrate impact.
Partner cross-functionally to embed analytics and outcome measures into planning, decision-making, client insights, and performance management.
Use data-driven insights to support better experiences, decisions, and outcomes.
Provide thought leadership on data quality, governance, privacy, responsible AI, and scalable analytics practices, working closely with Technology and enterprise data teams to ensure the right data foundations are in place.
Build and lead a high-performing team that combines analytical depth, business judgment, storytelling, and a practical orientation toward measurable outcomes.

WHO WE'RE LOOKING FOR

15+ years of progressive analytics experience in health care, benefits, insurance, consulting, or a related field, including senior leadership accountability for analytics, insight generation, and business impact.
Proven ability to turn data into insight, insight into action, and action into measurable business, customer, and health outcomes.
Exceptional storytelling skills, with the ability to translate complex analysis into simple, credible, executive-ready narratives for internal leaders, clients, partners, and external audiences.
Business-oriented analytics leader who can ask the right questions, define the right measures, challenge assumptions, and connect data to decisions that improve performance and impact.
Experience building outcome frameworks, dashboards, scorecards, insights, analytics products, or executive reporting that drive decision-making.
Advanced analytics expertise, including predictive modelling, segmentation, measurement design, statistical analysis, data visualization, and practical application to business, customer, and health outcome questions.
Strong advanced analytics capability, including familiarity with AI and machine learning applications.
A collaborative, practical, and outcomes-focused leadership style, with the ability to operate at both strategic and execution levels in a fast-moving environment.

WHAT WE OFFER

Base Salary:
Range exempt
Offer positioning:
Determined using relevant experience, skills, internal equity and current market data.
Additional compensation:
Eligible for a discretionary target bonus.
Total rewards:
Health and dental coverage, retirement savings, paid time off and well-being support (up to $10,000 per year for mental health).
Posting disclosures:
This is for an existing vacancy.
Work model:
Hybrid

THE CULTURE

We believe a career should be meaningful. Not just a means to earn a living. Our culture is one where everyone's voice is heard and valued. Because that’s what it takes to create better health for all. We dare to challenge the status quo. And we’re driven by people who have challenged theirs. We believe that your workplace should empower you to be the best version of yourself. That’s why we provide a place where you can be inspired, challenged, and rewarded.

Where your growth means our growth.
Where your voice is heard and valued.
Where your work has purpose. And purpose matters.

We believe our people are critical to our overall success. Inclusivity makes us a stronger, smarter and more informed organization. Being intentionally inclusive of diverse backgrounds, perspectives and experiences will enhance our company culture to positively impact how we support our communities. A career at GreenShield isn’t just about personal achievements, it's about making a difference together.

Here’s to Better Health for All!

A FEW MORE DETAILS

Proficiency in English is required for this position. As part of this role, you will be required to communicate with colleagues or customers who use English as their primary language. By requiring English proficiency for this position, we aim to ensure that our employees can excel in their roles, collaborate, and communicate effectively, and contribute to the success of our organization.
GS supports diversity, equity and inclusion in our teams and communities, and we value the unique contributions made by all. Even if your experience doesn’t align perfectly to every requirement, we invite you to apply. We encourage applications from all candidates and will accommodate needs under human rights legislation throughout all stages of the recruitment and selection process. Please let us know of any accommodation through requestforaccommodation@greenshield.ca. Information received relating to accommodation will be addressed confidentially.
Providing this information gives GS consent to use your personal information to assess your suitability for specific positions, future opportunities or for your personnel file. Your résumé will be held in strict confidence and will be viewed only by the Organization. Information may be stored outside of Canada and could be used for aggregate statistical purposes (which uses no personal identification).
AI Usage - GreenShield leverages AI to help produce Job Descriptions, and ideate on interview questions. We also leverage AI for interview transcription support.

jobs.description:
Work Location:

Toronto, Ontario, Canada

Hours

37.5

Line Of Business

TD Securities

Pay Details

$155,000 - $215,000 CAD

TD is committed to providing fair and equitable compensation opportunities to all colleagues. Growth opportunities and skill development are defining features of the colleague experience at TD. Our compensation policies and practices have been designed to allow colleagues to progress through the salary range over time as they progress in their role. The base pay actually offered may vary based upon the candidate's skills and experience, job-related knowledge, geographic location, and other specific business and organizational needs.

As a candidate, you are encouraged to ask compensation related questions and have an open dialogue with your recruiter who can provide you more specific details for this role.

Job Description

Role mandate

Lead the Applied AI and Innovation capability for TD Securities and build a high-performing team of applied AI specialists. Identify advances in AI that matter to the business and translate them into practical capabilities that can be tested, proven, and deployed in capital markets workflows.

This is a business-led senior technical leadership role requiring deep AI expertise, strong product judgment, and a pragmatic delivery mindset. The role connects emerging models, methods, and research with complex business problems and works across business, quantitative, data, engineering, and control teams to deliver measurable value.

Strategy and technical direction

Set the applied AI strategy, technical direction, and priorities across generative AI, agentic systems, decision intelligence, multimodal models, retrieval, reasoning, and human-agent operating models for TD Securities.
Assess research and industry developments in generative AI, agentic AI, machine learning, retrieval, reasoning, multimodal models, and related technologies, for practical relevance, then translate the most promising capabilities into experiments, product strategies, operating models, and value opportunities.
Determine where advanced AI provides a material advantage over conventional analytics, rules, or automation, avoiding unnecessary complexity.

Applied AI delivery and value creation

Identify and prioritize high-value opportunities; develop business cases, value hypotheses, adoption plans, measurable baselines, and value-realization frameworks.
Lead applied scientists in designing, building, testing, and improving AI solutions for complex, knowledge-intensive and analytical workflows.
Establish standards for experimentation, benchmarking, statistical rigor, error analysis, robustness, documentation, reproducibility, and production readiness.
Develop or adapt models and methods when existing solutions do not meet requirements for performance, latency, privacy, explainability, control, or cost.
Drive rapid prototyping while ensuring successful solutions can be engineered, governed, scaled, monitored, and supported in production.

Technical leadership

Provide senior technical oversight across model selection and adaptation, fine-tuning, retrieval-augmented generation, agent orchestration, knowledge and semantic methods, tool use, planning, memory, context management, hybrid retrieval, reranking, evaluation, and inference optimization.
Design robust agentic and retrieval systems, spanning tool use, planning, memory, context management, hybrid retrieval and reranking, while proactively addressing scaling, data quality, evaluation blind spots and inference cost.
Set rigorous experimentation and evaluation standards, including controlled ablations, multi-seed testing, statistical significance, red teaming and contamination controls to ensure solutions are reliable and production-ready.
Anticipate and mitigate scaling bottlenecks, evaluation blind spots, data quality issues, model risk, security concerns, and inference cost.
Challenge architecture and model choices; lead design reviews and resolve significant trade-offs with Engineering, Data, Architecture, Technology, and control partners.

AI products and capability development

Apply product-management disciplines to AI capabilities, including vision, roadmaps, lifecycle management, prioritization, adoption, and value tracking.
Work directly with quantitative practitioners, traders, bankers, risk specialists, data scientists, and engineers to frame problems and design practical AI solutions.
Establish reusable AI components, evaluation frameworks, implementation patterns, and technical standards that accelerate delivery across teams.
Apply AI to information extraction and synthesis, decision support, workflow automation, quantitative and analytical tasks, client intelligence, risk analysis, and other complex processes.
Partner with engineering and delivery teams to move validated prototypes into reliable production capabilities.

People and capability leadership

Build, lead, and develop a multidisciplinary applied AI team with a high bar for technical quality, scientific rigor, engineering discipline, and measurable impact.
Lead through technical credibility by authoring design documents, running architecture and technical reviews, and setting expectations for code, experiments, and system quality.

Governance, risk, and responsible adoption

Partner with Risk, Compliance, Legal, Information Security, Technology, and enterprise AI governance teams to ensure responsible, controlled, auditable, and explainable adoption.
Define guardrails, escalation paths, adoption controls, measurement routines, and governance artifacts for AI products and agentic workflows, while preserving clear human accountability for material decisions.

Decision authorities

Prioritize the AI product and transformation portfolio with front-office sponsors and enabling partners.
Determine which emerging capabilities warrant experimentation and which prototypes have sufficient evidence to progress toward production.
Recommend investments in models, tooling, platforms, compute, talent, and external partnerships.
Escalate material risk, control, data, compliance, or technology dependencies to the appropriate accountable partners.

The Role Shares Responsibilities And Decision Interfaces With

Front Office leaders for opportunity prioritization, workflow design, commercial impact, adoption, and value realization.
Data Product teams for reusable, business-ready data; semantic context; quality; lineage; provenance; metadata; and AI-ready information structures.
Technology and Architecture for secure implementation, integration, platform alignment, resiliency, production readiness, and sustainable support.
Risk, Compliance, Legal, Information Security, and enterprise AI Governance for control design, policy alignment, approvals, responsible AI, and auditability.
Finance and Business Management for business cases, budgets, benefits tracking, operating leverage, and value realization.
Operations, Change Management, Human Resources, and Learning for workflow change, adoption, training, role impacts, and capability building.
Product and Delivery partners for execution planning, backlog prioritization, stakeholder engagement, success metrics, and delivery discipline.
Approved universities, research institutes, vendors, and open-source communities for collaboration, talent pipelines, and knowledge exchange.
Key measures will balance technical quality, adoption, and realized business impact:
Realized value from AI-enabled products, capabilities, and workflow transformation, including productivity, decision quality, revenue support, risk insight, or control effectiveness.
Delivery of approved roadmap milestones, business cases, benefits plans, and strategic transformation objectives.
Adoption, outcome improvement, reliability, and production performance of deployed AI capabilities.
Number, maturity, and reuse of AI components, evaluation frameworks, implementation patterns, workflows, and skills.
Team growth, talent development, stakeholder confidence, and cross-functional delivery effectiveness.
Portfolio, project, cost-centre, and value-realization targets to be confirmed.
This role is generally not directly client-facing. It creates client and shareholder value by improving how front-office teams serve clients, identify opportunities, make decisions, manage risk, and execute work.
Improves the speed, quality, and consistency of client coverage through AI-enabled insights, workflow tools, and decision support.
Reduces manual effort and accelerates access to relevant business context and information.
Supports revenue generation and relationship management by helping teams prepare more effectively and act on insights faster.
Simplifies fragmented workflows and embeds intelligence into day-to-day processes.
Strengthens control, transparency, and consistency through governed, explainable, reusable AI capabilities.

Education

PhD strongly preferred in Computer Science, Machine Learning, Artificial Intelligence, Statistics, Mathematics, Operations Research, Engineering, Physics, or a related quantitative discipline. A research-intensive master’s degree may be considered with an exceptional record of applied technical leadership.

Experience And Technical Capabilities

Typically 8+ years of progressive experience in applied AI, machine learning, data science, quantitative research, or advanced analytics, including leadership of multidisciplinary technical teams.
Demonstrated success translating research into robust, production-used systems in complex, regulated, or high-consequence environments.
Deep expertise in several areas such as large language models, natural language processing, retrieval and reasoning, agentic systems, multimodal learning, graph methods, time-series modelling, causal inference, optimization, reinforcement learning, or probabilistic modelling.
Expert command of experimental design, statistical inference, benchmarking, ablation studies, error analysis, model evaluation, reproducibility, contamination controls, and scientific peer review.
Strong hands-on fluency in Python and modern AI/ML ecosystems, with the ability to review code, experiments, model behaviour, architecture, and data pipelines.
Strong understanding of production AI architecture, including feature and data pipelines, vector and graph retrieval, model serving, APIs, distributed compute, cloud platforms, MLOps and LLMOps, observability, security, latency, resiliency, and cost optimization.
Technical depth to challenge designs, assess feasibility and risk, resolve architecture trade-offs, and partner credibly with data, engineering, quantitative, and technology teams.
Experience building and developing applied science or research teams, including talent assessment, mentoring, organizational design, and capability building.
Ability to engage credibly with quantitative practitioners, engineers, data scientists, risk specialists, traders, bankers, and senior technology leaders.
Capital markets or financial-services experience strongly preferred; experience with market, client, transaction, research, risk, or unstructured financial data is advantageous.
Executive communication skills to explain technical findings, uncertainty, limitations, and investment choices precisely without oversimplification.

Who We Are

TD Securities offers a wide range of capital markets products and services to corporate, government, and institutional clients who choose us for our innovation, execution, and experience. With more than 6,500 professionals operating out of 40 cities across the globe, we strive to make every interaction, product and experience remarkably human and refreshingly simple. Our services include underwriting and distributing new issues, providing trusted advice and industry-leading insight, extending access to global markets, and delivering integrated transaction banking solutions. We’re looking for a Manager, Growth Marketing (Head of Web Strategy & Services) to join our team in Vancouver and own asana.com as our front door and as a measurable driver of web conversion and sales pipeline. Husky TechnologiesTM is an exciting company with tremendous potential. We have a great team and great expectations. If you are attracted to bold goals, believe in uncompromising honesty, support mutual respect, care about environmental responsibility, have a passion for excellence and a desire to make a positive contribution – then we want you to join the Husky TechnologiesTM team!

The Finance Director serves as a strategic business partner to the Leadership Team in support of Husky’s Global Service Business and Customer Success Management strategy. This role provides leadership for financial planning, forecasting, performance analysis, governance, and decision support to drive profitable growth, improve operational performance, and strengthen financial visibility across service revenue streams, including field service, contracts, parts, and other aftermarket offerings. The Finance Director is expected to influence strategic decisions, lead transformation initiatives, and build a high-performing finance capability that enables the business to scale effectively.

Key Responsibilities

Financial Planning & Forecasting

Lead the annual budget, quarterly forecast, and long-range planning processes for the service business.
Develop robust revenue, margin, cost, and headcount forecasts based on operational and commercial drivers.
Translate business strategies into financial plans with clear assumptions, risks, and opportunities.
Support scenario planning and sensitivity analysis for service growth, pricing, labor utilization, and investment decisions.

Performance Management & Analysis

Deliver timely and accurate monthly financial reporting and variance analysis for service revenue, gross margin, SG&A, and operating income.
Analyze business performance by region, product line, customer segment, channel, and service offering.
Monitor and explain key drivers of performance, including labor utilization, absorption, contract profitability, attach rates, response times, and service productivity.
Provide actionable insights and recommendations to improve growth, profitability, and working capital performance.

Business Partnering

Serve as the senior finance partner to service leadership, operations, commercial teams, and Customer Success leaders, providing insight and challenge on strategic priorities, business performance, and investment decisions.
Lead financial evaluation of pricing strategies, contract renewals, service program design, and capital or operating investments to support sustainable growth and margin expansion.
Provide proactive challenge and decision support to business leaders by identifying risks, opportunities, and trade-offs across growth, productivity, service delivery, and resource allocation.
Lead cross-functional evaluation of new service offerings, business models, and transformation initiatives that improve service coverage, utilization, fulfillment, cost efficiency, and customer value.
Sponsor finance and business transformation initiatives across Finance and Customer Success Management, including enhancements to processes, reporting, operating metrics, and decision frameworks that support growth, profitability, and scalability.

Management Reporting & KPI Development

Develop and enhance dashboards, reporting tools, and KPIs that improve transparency and decision-making.
Standardize definitions and reporting for critical service metrics across the organization.
Improve reporting automation and self-service analytics capabilities where possible.
Present clear financial results and business insights to senior leadership

Process Improvement & Governance

Strengthen forecasting accuracy, reporting discipline, and financial controls within the service business.
Drive continuous improvement in FP&A processes, planning models, and reporting frameworks.
Ensure alignment with corporate finance requirements, accounting policies, and internal controls
Support month-end close and planning processes in partnership with accounting and finance teams.

Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in Finance, Accounting, Economics, or a related field required.
CPA, CMA, CFA, or MBA preferred.
10+ years of progressive experience in FP&A, finance business partnering, commercial finance, or operational finance, including leadership responsibility.
Experience in a service, aftermarket, field service, maintenance, or contract-based business strongly preferred.
Strong financial modeling, forecasting, and business analysis skills.
Advanced proficiency in Excel and experience with ERP and planning/reporting systems.
Executive presence with strong communication, presentation, and stakeholder management skills, and the ability to influence senior leaders across functions and regions.
Proven ability to work cross-functionally in a fast-paced, performance-driven environment

Preferred Experience In a Service Business

Understanding of service revenue models such as time and materials, service contracts, preventive maintenance, subscriptions, and parts/service bundles.
Experience analyzing operational KPIs such as technician utilization, service efficiency, contract margins, backlog, renewal rates, and service attach rates.
Familiarity with pricing strategy, labor productivity, installed base analytics, and customer lifecycle economics

Core Competencies

Strategic leadership
Financial and commercial acumen
Analytical rigor
Executive business partnership
Influence and executive communication
Problem solving
Process improvement
Results orientation and a bias for action

Team Development

Build and lead a high-performing finance team with strong capability in financial analysis, strategic thinking, business partnership, and change leadership.
Lead, coach, and develop team members, including succession planning, capability building, and development of future finance leaders.

Financial Leadership

Provide consistent, timely, accurate, and decision-oriented financial reporting for the service business, with greater automation and self-service access to insights where possible

About the Opportunity

We are seeking a CPA designated professional to join our client's team on a full-time basis. The ideal candidate will possess a strong technical accounting foundation in a project-based construction environment, along with the leadership skills to take on a broader administrative mandate.

The Director of Finance and Operations is responsible for overseeing all aspects of financial management for a well-established, multi-sector construction group of companies, including corporate accounting, regulatory and financial reporting, budget and forecast preparation, and the development of internal control policies and procedures. This position leads financial risk management, safeguards company assets, and provides the timely, accurate financial insight that guides sound business decisions across the organization. Beyond finance, the role also includes oversight of the company's human resources processes and management of the relationship with its external IT provider, making this a key administrative leadership position.

Duties include but are not limited to:
Prepare head office overhead budgets in consultation with management, collecting, analyzing, and consolidating financial data to recommend plans
Achieve financial plan objectives by scheduling expenditures, analyzing variances, and initiating corrective actions
Manage cash flow by forecasting project and corporate cash requirements, monitoring balances, and ensuring liquidity to meet operational and project obligations
Partner with Project Managers, Estimators, and Operations to review project performance and margins, and improve the accuracy of future bids
Prepare and publish timely monthly, quarterly, and annual financial statements, reporting on the company's financial condition to senior leadership and external stakeholders
Oversee full-cycle accounting, including accounts payable, accounts receivable, and payroll for field and office staff
Monitor the company's externally managed investment portfolio, reconciling third-party statements and reporting on holdings and returns
Oversee project cost accounting, including job costing that tracks labour, equipment, and material costs against project budgets
Lead quarterly work-in-progress (WIP) reviews with Operations and Project Managers, and apply percentage-of-completion revenue recognition
Manage progress billings, subcontractor progress draws, holdbacks/retainage, and lien compliance under the Construction Act
Coordinate regulatory reporting and manage government reporting requirements and tax filings, including CRA and WSIB obligations
Establish, monitor, and enforce financial policies, procedures, and internal controls; coordinate external audits
Manage accounting department operations and staff, including hiring, training, coaching, and performance reviews
Oversee the company's HR function and manage the relationship with its external IT provider

CPA designation preferred

AVP, Financial Risk Management
jobs.description:
Do you want your voice heard and your actions to count?

Discover your opportunity with Mitsubishi UFJ Financial Group (MUFG), one of the world’s leading financial groups. Across the globe, we’re 150,000 colleagues, striving to make a difference for every client, organization, and community we serve. We stand for our values, building long-term relationships, serving society, and fostering shared and sustainable growth for a better world.

With a vision to be the world’s most trusted financial group, it’s part of our culture to put people first, listen to new and diverse ideas and collaborate toward greater innovation, speed and agility. This means investing in talent, technologies, and tools that empower you to own your career.

Join MUFG, where being inspired is expected and making a meaningful impact is rewarded.

Overview

The role supports the Financial Risk function within MUFG Canada Risk Management, with a focus on the production, analysis, governance and continuous enhancement of liquidity risk, market risk, credit risk and interest rate risk in the banking book reporting. Reporting to the Financial Risk Vice President, the incumbent is responsible for preparing and maintaining recurring risk reports, supporting ECL and portfolio credit risk analysis, monitoring risk appetite and limit metrics, maintaining EUC and procedure documentation, and assisting with committee materials for IRC, ECC, Liquidity Risk and Market Risk governance forums. The role requires excellent technical capability, including advanced data analysis, Excel/Power Query/VBA automation, source-data reconciliation, AI literacy and the ability to responsibly leverage AI-enabled tools to improve reporting efficiency, data quality, trend analysis, control effectiveness and management insight. The incumbent must demonstrate strong knowledge of the underlying risk metrics, data sources such as OVS extracts, Bloomberg and internal reporting files, and the ability to translate complex technical outputs into clear, audit-ready commentary and management materials.

Key Accountabilities

Risk reporting, analytics and governance support - responsibilities include:

Prepare, analyze and maintain recurring Financial Risk reports across liquidity risk, market risk, credit risk and IRRBB, including Liquidity Early Warning Indicators, Liquidity Limit Dashboard, Liquidity Stress Testing, daily and monthly liquidity monitoring, VaR, stress testing, DV01, sensitivity measures, portfolio concentration, IFRS 9 ECL, Watchlist inputs, Risk Appetite metrics and interest rate risk analytics.
Compile and validate source data from OVS extracts, Bloomberg, internal risk files, Treasury reports, Middle Office data, Finance inputs, facility and commitment data, exposure reports and locally maintained EUC tools to support recurring production and independent review of risk metrics.
Support the preparation of IRC, ECC, Liquidity Risk, Market Risk and other governance materials by compiling metrics, drafting commentary, preparing exhibits, explaining drivers, documenting assumptions and ensuring materials are accurate, complete and delivered within required timelines.
Perform review and challenge of report outputs, investigate material movements or exceptions, document rationale, reconcile data back to source systems, and escalate breaches, data issues or control concerns in accordance with applicable procedures.

Support for stakeholders - responsibilities include:

Coordinate with Treasury, Middle Office, Finance, Operations, Compliance, business lines, regional risk teams and Head Office to obtain data, validate assumptions, clarify methodology, and support timely completion of Financial Risk deliverables.
Provide support, oversight and guidance to first line and independent risk monitoring functions on risk reporting, risk appetite monitoring, limit usage, breach escalation and remediation tracking.
Support audit, regulatory and internal review requests by maintaining clear evidence, audit trails, version logs, approvals and supporting documentation for recurring reporting processes.
Monitor relevant regulatory, Head Office and regional risk requirements and assist in translating them into local policies, procedures, controls, testing approaches and reporting processes.
Support the review and enhancement of local risk policies, procedures, EUC documentation and user manuals, including documentation for EWI, liquidity limits, LST, market risk reporting, RFR-linked submissions and ECL processes.
Assist with annual recalibration and methodology review processes for liquidity risk metrics, EWI thresholds, LST assumptions, local limits and other Financial Risk measures, including coordination with ALRMO, Head Office and first line stakeholders.
Identify opportunities to automate, streamline and strengthen recurring reports, tracking logs, confirmations and control processes while maintaining appropriate governance, documentation and change management.

Technical Skills

Excellent technical skills, including advanced Microsoft Excel capability with complex formulas, Power Query, pivot tables, data validation, reconciliations, financial modelling, VBA/macros and automation techniques used to streamline recurring risk reporting processes.
Strong knowledge of liquidity risk metrics and reporting, including Early Warning Indicators, Liquidity Stress Testing, liquidity limits, limit utilization, funds position, cash-flow analysis, contingency funding plan inputs, liquidity risk appetite measures, threshold recalibration and breach/escalation monitoring.
Strong knowledge of market risk metrics and analytics, including VaR, stress testing, DV01, sensitivity analysis, limit monitoring, market data validation, rate and spread movements, exposure drivers and recurring market risk reporting packages.
Strong knowledge of credit risk and ECL analytics, including IFRS 9 ECL, exposure and commitment utilization, portfolio concentration, industry and obligor analysis, facility data, credit exposure trends and credit risk appetite reporting.
Working knowledge of IRRBB concepts and tools, including interest rate sensitivity, earnings and economic value perspectives, repricing profile analysis, scenario-based impacts, assumptions review and coordination with regional or Head Office stakeholders on IRRBB methodology and tool development.
Ability to source, extract, reconcile and analyze data from multiple internal and external risk systems, Treasury and Middle Office files, Finance inputs, facility and commitment reports, shared-drive repositories, SharePoint sites and locally maintained EUC tools.
Advanced data analytics capability, including the ability to work with large and complex data sets, identify data quality issues, perform variance and trend analysis, reconcile outputs across systems, design repeatable controls, and convert raw data into meaningful risk insights and executive-level commentary.
Practical knowledge of AI-enabled productivity and analytics tools, with the ability to responsibly leverage AI to support data validation, report drafting, process documentation, variance investigation, coding assistance, workflow automation, knowledge management and management reporting, while maintaining appropriate human review, confidentiality and control standards.
Ability to identify and implement opportunities for automation, AI-assisted analysis and process improvement in recurring reports, EUC tools, tracking logs, confirmations, procedure manuals, management materials and control evidence repositories.
Experience preparing high-quality committee, management and audit materials, including metric dashboards, variance explanations, trend summaries, breach or exception commentary, methodology notes, procedure documentation and evidence packages.
Sound understanding of financial risk concepts, governance expectations and control requirements, including liquidity risk, market risk, credit risk, IFRS 9 ECL, IRRBB, risk appetite metrics, stress testing, concentration risk, EUC governance and risk measurement methodologies.

Experience & Abilities

Minimum of 3 years of banking, risk management, treasury, finance, audit, data analytics or related financial services experience; experience in a second line risk management function is preferred.
Demonstrated ability to prepare, analyze and explain recurring risk reports and supporting materials across liquidity risk, market risk, credit risk and IRRBB, including EWI, LST, liquidity limits, VaR, stress testing, DV01, sensitivity measures, ECL, commitment utilization, concentration, risk appetite and governance reporting.
Strong technical aptitude and curiosity, with a proven ability to learn new systems, adopt emerging technologies, use AI-enabled tools responsibly, and translate technical outputs into practical risk management conclusions.
Strong analytical, investigative and problem-solving skills, with the ability to identify data issues, explain key drivers, assess materiality, reconcile outputs to source data, validate AI-assisted outputs and recommend practical control or reporting improvements.
Effective written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to draft concise commentary, document rationale, present results, and coordinate deliverables with stakeholders at different levels.
Ability to manage multiple recurring deadlines, maintain strong attention to detail, preserve accurate audit trails, and ensure technology-enabled improvements remain transparent, controlled and well documented.

Education & Training

University degree in finance, economics, mathematics, accounting, business, risk management, data analytics, computer science, information systems or a related discipline.
Post-graduate education, professional designation or progress toward a designation such as FRM, CFA, CPA, MBA, data analytics certification, AI-related training or equivalent risk/finance certification is considered beneficial.
Additional training in liquidity risk, market risk, credit risk, IFRS 9, regulatory reporting, data analytics, automation, responsible AI use, prompt engineering, model/EUC governance or technology risk controls is considered an asset.
