jobs.title: AVP, Enterprise Digital Capabilities
jobs.description:
We are seeking a strategic, collaborative and product-minded leader to join our team as Assistant Vice President (AVP), Enterprise Digital Capabilities. This role is a key leader in Manulife's multi-year transformation to modernize and converge our digital ecosystem across Canada, the US, Asia and Global Wealth & Asset Management.

At the heart of this role is a simple objective: identify what is common across our digital experiences, build it once as an enterprise capability, and enable markets and segments to reuse and extend it to accelerate their own digital roadmaps.

Manulife has established a strong portfolio of reusable enterprise digital capabilities that support our Digital Storefront transformation and broader unification ambitions. The next opportunity is to expand and scale this portfolio to accelerate the unification strategies and roadmaps of our segments and advance One Manulife experiences across the enterprise. The AVP will lead this evolution – working across segments to identify where common capabilities can create the greatest incremental value, bringing together requirements to ensure capabilities are designed for enterprise reuse, defining adoption and rollout strategies, and establishing a federated model where capabilities can be developed globally or contributed by segments and scaled for broader enterprise benefit.

The AVP will own the strategy and evolution of this portfolio — identifying new opportunities for reuse, prioritizing investment, establishing strong product management disciplines, driving adoption, optimizing existing capabilities and ensuring that each enterprise investment continues to deliver measurable value.

A critical part of the role is leading the Common Capability Collective, bringing together digital and product leaders from across the enterprise to identify common needs, align roadmaps, determine where enterprise investment can eliminate duplication and accelerate delivery, and create a shared view of capability priorities.

This is an enablement role, not ownership of individual market or segment experiences. The AVP will partner closely with Digital Storefront and segment digital leaders to understand their roadmaps and determine how enterprise capabilities can help them deliver faster, with greater quality, consistency and efficiency.

The AVP will operate in a two-in-a-box partnership with a complementary Global Technology leader, jointly shaping the business and technology evolution of enterprise digital capabilities. Together, they will ensure capabilities are scalable, secure, reusable, well-integrated and designed for long-term enterprise value.

 Position Responsibilities 

 Enterprise Capability Strategy & Portfolio 

 Own the strategy, roadmap and ongoing evolution of Manulife's portfolio of reusable enterprise digital capabilities.
 Establish a clear view of the capabilities required to support digital convergence across markets, segments and channels.
 Continuously identify common business and customer needs that can be solved once and reused across the enterprise.
 Assess existing segment capabilities for opportunities to scale them globally rather than rebuilding equivalent solutions.
 Prioritize enterprise investment based on customer value, segment demand, reuse potential, strategic alignment and economic benefit.
 Maintain a multi-year capability roadmap aligned to Digital Storefront, segment roadmaps and Manulife's broader digital strategy.
 Ensure the portfolio remains focused and sustainable by rationalizing overlapping capabilities, technology and licenses where appropriate.

 Common Capability Collective & Federated Leadership 

 Lead the Common Capability Collective, bringing together Digital Storefront and product leaders from across the enterprise to jointly shape capability priorities and investment.
 Create transparency across segment roadmaps to identify shared needs, opportunities for reuse and potential duplication before investment occurs.
 Establish a federated model that enables capabilities to originate within segments where appropriate and subsequently evolve into reusable enterprise capabilities.
 Build alignment around enterprise standards and shared capabilities while preserving segment accountability for their own customer experiences and business outcomes.
 Create clear decision rights, funding principles, ownership models and governance for the creation and evolution of common capabilities.

 Product Management & Capability Evolution 

 Establish strong product management disciplines across the enterprise capability portfolio, including product vision, roadmaps, adoption, performance measurement and lifecycle management.
 Ensure every capability has clear customer and business outcomes, ownership, success measures and an evolution roadmap.
 Use segment feedback, performance data and emerging customer needs to continuously improve capabilities.
 Drive adoption and reuse across markets and segments, ensuring enterprise investments translate into meaningful acceleration of local roadmaps.
 Ensure capabilities are designed for extensibility so segments can meet differentiated market needs without unnecessarily duplicating core functionality.
 Manage capabilities through their full lifecycle, including investment, enhancement, optimization, consolidation and retirement.

 AI Enablement & Optimization 

 Establish an AI-by-default approach to the development and evolution of enterprise digital capabilities.
 Identify opportunities to embed AI directly into capabilities to improve customer experiences, decisioning, personalization and digital effectiveness.
 Apply AI and automation across the capability lifecycle to accelerate development, testing, implementation, operations and ongoing optimization.
 Partner with Technology and enterprise AI teams to identify emerging AI capabilities that can be productized and reused across the organization.
 Continuously evaluate opportunities to reduce manual effort, improve quality and accelerate time to market through AI-enabled capabilities and ways of working.

 Enterprise Integration & Technology Partnership 

 Co-lead the enterprise capability portfolio in close partnership with Global Technology through a two-in-a-box leadership model.
 Define business requirements and product priorities while partnering with Technology on architecture, engineering, security, scalability and technical lifecycle management.
 Ensure enterprise capabilities are designed to integrate effectively across Manulife's digital ecosystem and can be consumed by multiple platforms, markets and channels.
 Promote API-enabled, modular and reusable approaches that reduce point-to-point solutions and technology duplication.
 Ensure platform and technology decisions support long-term reuse, interoperability and enterprise scale.

 Business Value & Benefits Realization 

 Establish a clear value proposition and business case for enterprise digital capabilities and the overall portfolio.
 Quantify and track the value generated through reuse, including delivery acceleration, avoided duplicate investment, license consolidation, operational efficiency, improved customer experience and reduced ongoing support costs.
 Demonstrate how building once and reusing at scale compounds speed, quality and efficiency with every additional implementation.
 Partner with Global Marketing Strategy, FP&A, Technology and segment teams to track expected and realized benefits.
 Use adoption, utilization, performance and financial data to inform ongoing investment and portfolio decisions.

 Adoption & Enterprise Enablement 

 Partner with segment digital leaders to understand upcoming priorities and proactively identify enterprise capabilities that can accelerate their roadmaps.
 Establish clear onboarding, documentation, implementation patterns and support models that make enterprise capabilities easy for teams to adopt.
 Build awareness and understanding of available capabilities across the organization to increase reuse and prevent unnecessary reinvention.
 Create feedback loops with consuming teams so capabilities continue to evolve based on real implementation and customer needs.
 Champion a culture of reuse and enterprise thinking while recognizing the differentiated needs of individual markets and businesses.

 Required Qualifications 

 Bachelor's degree in Business, Digital, Technology, Marketing or a related discipline; MBA or master's degree preferred.
 10+ years of experience in digital product management, digital transformation, enterprise capabilities, platforms or related leadership roles.
 Demonstrated experience building and scaling reusable digital products, platforms or capabilities across a complex, federated organization.
 Strong understanding of modern digital ecosystems, including APIs, cloud platforms, identity, personalization, search, content, data, analytics, experimentation and customer experience technologies.
 Experience establishing product management disciplines and managing a portfolio of digital products or capabilities through their lifecycle.
 Demonstrated ability to identify opportunities for reuse, simplify complex technology landscapes and translate enterprise investment into measurable business value.
 Strong understanding of AI and automation and their application to digital products, customer experiences and delivery.
 Proven ability to influence and align senior stakeholders across business, marketing, product and technology organizations without relying solely on direct authority.
 Experience operating successfully in a global, federated environment with competing priorities and varying levels of digital maturity.
 Strong strategic, commercial and analytical skills, with the ability to connect technology and capability decisions to customer outcomes, delivery acceleration and financial value.
 Exceptional communication and leadership skills with the ability to translate complex digital concepts into clear business outcomes.

 What Success Looks Like 

Success in this role means Manulife increasingly builds once and benefits many times.

Segments are able to deliver their digital roadmaps faster because proven enterprise capabilities are readily available rather than repeatedly designed, procured and built. Capabilities originating in one part of Manulife can be scaled for the benefit of others. Duplicate technology and investment decline. Adoption and reuse increase. AI and automation continuously improve how capabilities are built, operated and consumed.

Over time, Manulife develops a growing portfolio of reusable digital capabilities that compounds the value of each investment — accelerating delivery, improving quality and customer experience, reducing duplication and creating sustainable enterprise-scale benefits.

About The Company BuildGood is a fundraising growth agency. We help nonprofits change the way they find new donors, retain them longer, and grow lifetime value, building a system that creates moments of generosity from first-time giver to legacy leaver.

Our approach is rooted in understanding why people give. Generosity grows when people feel motivated—when giving supports their identity, creates a sense of connection, and makes supporters feel competent and effective in their giving. We design fundraising systems around building donor motivation and leading first-time donors to become committed supporters.

We partner with nonprofits across North America to grow durable revenue, from donor acquisition and direct mail to digital fundraising, retention, and mid-level giving. Our work blends brand and direct response.

Is This Job For You? Do you get fired up about turning client relationships into long-term, high-impact partnerships?

Do you understand what it takes to grow fundraising and be responsible for revenue targets, and know
how to help others turn that understanding into stronger strategies and better results?

Are you energized by leading a team of Strategists and Account Managers, challenging their thinking, building their confidence, and helping them manage client relationships well?

Can you look at a client’s fundraising program, identify the biggest opportunities, and help your team build a clear plan for growth?

Are you comfortable leading important client conversations, addressing concerns directly, and making the case for renewing or expanding a partnership?

And do you want to build a high-performance client strategy function at a fundraising agency that’s genuinely changing how nonprofits grow?

We’re looking for someone who combines deep fundraising knowledge with strong account management and people leadership. You’ll lead the team that owns our client accounts, set the standard for strategy and client experience, and take responsibility for keeping and growing those partnerships.

What We Offer A workplace that values your need for autonomy, competence and connection
An entrepreneurial culture that places a premium on rigor and accountability
A teamwork environment built on both humour and challenging each other to continuously improve in our craft
Meaningful work that directly influences how organizations grow
Attendance at the Build Good Summit, Canada’s premiere fundraising conference
Work from home anywhere in Canada
4 weeks vacation
Summer Fridays (Fridays off in June, July, and August)
Generous professional development budget
Group Retirement Savings Plan (GRSP)
Flexible Spending Account (HSA)
Performance pay based on meeting goals and targets

What You’ll Do

You will own the strategy and execution for how our client team grows and protects BuildGood’s client portfolio. Your focus will be on client success, retention, renewals, expansion, and the profitability of each account—ensuring our work delivers measurable fundraising results, gives clients a clear reason to deepen their partnership with us, and generates a healthy profit for BuildGood.

You will set the direction for BuildGood’s client strategy function and lead the team responsible for putting it into practice. You’ll manage our Fundraising Strategists and Account Managers, set the standard for fundraising strategy and account management, and own all renewals and expansion across the client portfolio.

Every account will have a clear growth plan that connects the client’s fundraising goals with the work, investment, and decisions needed to achieve them. You’ll help your team build those plans, hold them accountable for progress, and ensure clients understand the value of our work and where the partnership can go next.

You’ll lead through your team while participating directly in strategic reviews, important client conversations, renewals, and escalations. You’ll work closely with the Managing Director, who provides commercial leadership and sets pricing, margin, and other business parameters.

Your main responsibilities:
Lead, coach, and develop BuildGood’s Fundraising Strategists and Account Managers through regular 1:1s, account reviews, clear performance expectations, and professional development.
Review and challenge the fundraising strategy across the client portfolio. Review and challenge recommendations to ensure they reflect donor insights, performance data, and the client’s goals.
Own and iterate the Total Fundraising Review & Revenue Roadmap, our flagship diagnostic, forecasting and planning process at the beginning of each new client relationship built on our Brand → Demand → Expand and Fundraising FlywheelTM IP.
Work closely with the Creative Director to ensure the work we deliver is outstanding—grounded in a strong fundraising strategy, built around donor insights, and executed with exceptional craft. Together, review key campaigns and deliverables, challenge work that falls short, and coach the team toward a consistently high standard.
Ensure every account has a documented growth plan covering fundraising priorities, measurable goals, recommended investment, renewal timing, relationship risks, and opportunities to expand the partnership.
Make annual planning and Quarterly Fundraising Reviews the foundation of account management, ensuring each review leads to clear recommendations, decisions, and next steps.
Hold the team accountable for executing account plans, monitoring results, and adjusting strategy when performance or circumstances change.
Own renewal planning and execution across the portfolio. Maintain a clear renewal calendar and forecast, prepare the team, and lead renewal conversations within the commercial parameters agreed with the Managing Director.
Identify and advance opportunities to expand client partnerships where additional BuildGood services or investment would help the client achieve its fundraising goals.
Monitor account health using fundraising performance, client feedback, engagement, and relationship strength. Act early when results, trust, or renewal prospects are at risk.
Serve as the senior escalation point for client challenges. Lead the response, coordinate the right people, communicate clearly with the client, and follow through to resolution.
Ensure client strategies, presentations, and reports are clear, credible, and useful. Help the team explain what happened, what it means, and what should happen next.
Partner with creative, data, digital, production, and project management leaders to ensure work follows the agreed strategy and meets client expectations.
Own the profitability of each client account. Monitor account revenue, delivery costs, scope, and resource use against agreed profit targets. Address scope creep and unprofitable work early, and work with the Managing Director on pricing, staffing, or scope changes needed to protect profit while delivering excellent client results.
Partner with the Managing Director to ensure commitments made during the sales process carry through into onboarding and account planning.
Hire and onboard members of the client strategy team, and build consistent practices that help the team deliver strong work with greater independence.
Establish regular client feedback and use it to improve account management, service quality, and the client experience.
Serve on BuildGood’s Leadership Team, participating in weekly leadership meetings and quarterly in-person sessions.

Skills & Experience Significant experience in nonprofit fundraising strategy, direct-response marketing, and fundraising agency account management, typically gained over 7 or more years.
At least 5 years of experience managing and developing a team, including setting expectations, coaching performance, hiring, and handling difficult conversations.
Deep knowledge of direct-response fundraising across disciplines and channels, with the ability to connect acquisition, retention, monthly, mid-level, and legacy giving into a coherent growth strategy.
Demonstrated success managing client relationships and leading account planning, renewals, and expansion.
Strong analytical judgment: you can interpret fundraising performance, identify the underlying issues, and turn findings into clear recommendations.
The ability to evaluate other people’s strategies and coach them toward stronger thinking and better work.
A consultative approach: you ask good questions, make complex information understandable, and present recommendations with confidence.
Credibility with senior nonprofit leaders and experience navigating concerns, competing priorities, and difficult client situations.
Commercial awareness: you understand how scope, pricing, and resource decisions affect account profitability.
Experience using CRM and project management tools to maintain visibility into account plans, commitments, risks, and renewal opportunities.
Significant agency experience is required.

The Hiring Process

Subject Line: Application – Director of Client Strategy
In the email, briefly share why you want to work with BG, why it’s a good fit, and a link to a song that gets you excited about fundraising

Attach your resume (we’ll read it) and don’t attach a cover letter (we won’t read it)

We can’t guarantee that we will get back to every single applicant. If you have not heard from us two weeks after you apply, please assume that you were not included in the final field of applicants.

Director of Finance — Landmark Full-Service Resort, Atlantic Canada
$100,000 CAD base + bonus program | Relocation required | Retained search

The step you've been waiting for:

You're the Assistant Director of Finance at a full-service hotel. You already run the close. You already build the forecast. You already answer the questions the DOF gets credit for. What you don't have is the title, the seat on the Executive Committee, and the mandate that comes with them.
This is that seat.
Our client — a celebrated, century-old full-service resort in Atlantic Canada, operated by one of the country's largest hotel owner-operators — has retained Global Hospitality to find its next Director of Finance. We are not screening for a lateral move. We are looking for a strong #2 ready to be the #1.
The property
Two hundred–plus keys. Multiple food and beverage outlets. Championship golf. A full conference centre and spa. A four-season resort with real complexity — the kind of P&L that makes a finance leader, not the kind that babysits one.
Ownership is midway through a substantial capital reinvestment: guestrooms, restaurants, public spaces, and a significant new wellness amenity that extends the property's year-round demand. You will not inherit a static budget. You will help underwrite, monitor, and post-audit the spend that reshapes this asset.
The role
Reporting directly to the General Manager and serving on the Executive Committee, you will own:
All accounting functions and internal controls
— accuracy, timeliness, and compliance across the balance sheet
Financial statements, forecasts, and annual budgets
— prepared, defended, and delivered on time
Capital project finance
— ROI modelling, critical-path budget tracking, post-completion audits
Leadership of Accounting, Purchasing, Receiving, and IT
— hiring, coaching, and developing the team
Strategic partnership with department heads
— translating numbers into decisions for leaders who don't speak finance
Audit readiness, brand reporting, permits, licences, contracts, and insurance compliance

Credit and receivables management
, chairing the bi-weekly credit meeting

What we're looking for:

Progressive financial leadership in full-service hotels or resorts
— this is non-negotiable. Multi-outlet F&B, banquet, and rooms exposure matters here.
Current Assistant DOF, Controller, or Assistant Controller at a full-service property, with team leadership experience
Command of hotel accounting: reconciliations, AP, AR, payroll, budgeting, forecasting
Strong systems proficiency and genuine analytical range
Impeccable integrity, sound judgment, and the discretion the role demands
CPA is an asset, not a requirement

Our client's most successful hires in this seat have been strong second-in-commands who committed to two to three years
and used the role as the platform it is.

The life:

This is a rural, coastal posting — and that is the point.
Picture a walkable seaside town: locally owned restaurants, working harbours, a beach with the warmest swimming in the region, whale watching offshore, and a commute measured in minutes rather than lanes of traffic. It is a place where a professional salary buys a materially better standard of living than it does in a major market, and where the resort is the centre of community life rather than one building among thousands.
It is also genuinely remote. We are candid about that with every candidate, and you should be candid with yourself. The people who thrive here want it — the quiet, the seasons, the space, the community. If that describes you or your family, few opportunities in Canadian hospitality offer more.

Housing:
Company-owned townhouse rentals are available to help you land — two-bedroom units at $1,550–$1,750 per month. Convenient, close, and one less thing to solve during relocation.
Compensation
$100,000 CAD base salary plus participation in the bonus program, with a full benefits package.
Apply in confidence
Global Hospitality is retained on this search. All inquiries are handled in strict confidence, and no information is shared with our client without your explicit permission.

Joshua Platz | Global Hospitality Search Consultants

jobs.description:
About Hamlet of Gjoa Haven

The Hamlet of Gjoa Haven (Uqsuqtuuq) is a northern municipality located on King William Island in the Kitikmeot Region of Nunavut and is home to approximately 1,349 residents. Renowned for its strong Inuit heritage, deep connection to the land and sea, and rich history, Gjoa Haven holds a unique place in the story of Arctic exploration. It is best known as the site where Norwegian explorer Roald Amundsen wintered aboard the Gjoa from 1903 to 1906 while completing the first successful navigation of the Northwest Passage. More recently, the waters surrounding King William Island gained international attention with the discoveries of Sir John Franklin's lost expedition ships, HMS Erebus and HMS Terror, found nearby in 2014 and 2016. Today, Gjoa Haven serves as a gateway to Arctic history, culture, and adventure, offering a rare quality of life defined by vast landscapes, abundant wildlife, and a close-knit community. The Hamlet is committed to strong governance, responsible financial management, and the delivery of essential services that support community well-being, infrastructure, public safety, recreation, and sustainable development. Equally important is the Hamlet's commitment to developing local capacity by training, mentoring, and supporting Inuit employees, creating opportunities for career growth, leadership development, and long-term success within the organization and the community.

Why Gjoa Haven?

This is more than a career move — it's a chance to live and work in one of Canada's most storied Arctic communities. Candidates who join the Hamlet gain:
A true northern experience:
the land and sea, the midnight sun, the aurora, and a slower, community-centred pace of life you won't find anywhere else.
Immersion in Inuit culture and history:
work alongside a community proud of its heritage and its role in Arctic exploration history.
Meaningful impact:
your financial leadership directly shapes the services, infrastructure, and future of a community of just under 1,350 residents — the kind of visible, hands-on impact rarely possible in a larger municipality.
Flexibility to match the north's realities:
the Hamlet is open to discussing a hybrid work arrangement for the right candidate, combining dedicated time on-site in Gjoa Haven with the ability to work remotely for part of the role — offering a balance that supports both community presence and personal flexibility.

About the Role

Reporting to the Chief Administrative Officer (CAO), the Director of Finance plays a critical role in ensuring the Hamlet maintains accurate, transparent, and compliant financial reporting. This position works closely with Mayor and Council, senior management, auditors, and external stakeholders to support decision-making and long-term financial sustainability.

Key Responsibilities

Financial Leadership & Strategy
Oversee all financial operations of the Hamlet, including budgeting, financial reporting, accounts payable/receivable, payroll, and cash management, ensuring compliance with applicable accounting standards and Nunavut municipal regulations.
Develop and monitor annual operating and capital budgets in collaboration with the CAO, Mayor and Council, and department heads.
Provide timely, accurate financial reports and analysis to support Council decision-making and long-term financial sustainability.

Governance & Compliance
Ensure compliance with the Nunavut Hamlets Act, municipal bylaws, and all applicable financial reporting requirements.
Coordinate annual audits and liaise with external auditors, ensuring timely completion and resolution of findings.
Develop, implement, and maintain sound financial policies, procedures, and internal controls.

Stakeholder & Vendor Management
Build and maintain effective working relationships with Mayor and Council, senior management, auditors, government funding partners, and vendors.
Manage vendor and external service provider relationships to ensure value, accountability, and service quality.

Team & Community Leadership
Lead, mentor, and develop finance department staff, fostering a culture of accountability, collaboration, and continuous improvement.
Collaborate cross-departmentally to support infrastructure, public safety, recreation, and sustainable development priorities across the Hamlet.

Qualifications

Bachelor's degree in accounting or finance.
A CPA designation is considered an asset.
7–10 years of progressive experience in accounting or financial management.
5 years of experience developing and monitoring budgets and preparing financial reports.
Experience implementing and maintaining financial policies, procedures, and internal controls.

About TandemLaunch

TandemLaunch is a Canadian venture studio. Since 2010 we have created 30+ deep-tech ventures with a combined portfolio value exceeding $700M. We commercialize innovations in consumer electronics, hardware-enabled technologies, machine learning, and embedded systems, working directly with researchers from major university labs. We are one of very few venture studios globally with 15+ years of track record in building successful companies on research-backed deep tech.

About the Role

We are hiring a Director of Product Strategy and Commercialization to be the product-and-market voice inside several of our ventures at once.

These are companies with IP-backed technologies from cutting edge university research, a founding team, and on their first steps to commercial traction. Your job is to support our founders in identifying who would pay, get in front of them, carry the conversation through technical evaluation to a paid pilot or a design win, and feed what you learn back into what the venture builds next.

This is a leadership-track role that hinges on your ability to mentor and influence growing leaders. You will join our venture development team to help our ventures reach the necessary commercial traction to secure their next stage of financing.

What You'll Do

Own customer and partner engagements end-to-end
— from first conversation, through technical evaluation, to a paid pilot or design win. You find the buyer, you get the meeting, you carry it to money in collaboration with the venture’s leads.
Own product positioning and the customer-facing materials that support it
— product sheets, decks, demo strategies — across multiple ventures simultaneously.
Turn what customers tell you into product direction.
You are the person who helps the venture clarify the reasons to adjust their strategy in response to market needs, and collect the evidence that justifies it.
Run customer discovery and find the next market
— new applications and adjacent segments for ventures that are starting to get traction.
Represent ventures externally
at industry events, partner meetings, and customer conversations.
Mentor and directly work alongside our venture leads
as the commercial half of each venture team.

What We're Looking For

Requirements

5+ years of experience
in business development, product management, or strategy within a startup environment.
You have taken a technical product to a paying customer.
A purchase order, a paid pilot, a signed design win, a contract. Tell us what it was, who bought it, and what they paid. Grants, non-dilutive funding, maturation envelopes, accelerator awards and research scholarships are all valuable, but direct customer engagement is critical.
PhD/M.Sc/M.Eng degree or equivalent research-level technical fluency.
You can hold a real conversation with hardware engineers, ML researchers, or physicists — and are able to provide guidance on their technology strategy.
Professional French and English.

You have worked in ambiguity
— as a product lead, founding PM, co-founder, applications or solutions engineer, or the first commercial hire at an early-stage company.

Also true of the people who thrive at TandemLaunch

Genuine curiosity about novel technology.
You are comfortable navigating low-information environments to develop a strategy.
You are honest about what you do not know.

You might be coming from

Technical product management at a hardware or ML company · the first commercial hire at a deep-tech startup · applications or solutions engineering · product marketing for a technical product · technical sales or business development in B2B hardware · a founding team where you owned go-to-market.

What We Offer

A seat at one of very few venture studios globally with 15+ years of track record in deep tech.
Cross-portfolio exposure — ventures spanning AI, sensors, hardware, materials and audio in your first year.
Participation in fund economics through TandemLaunch's employee incentive pool — long-term upside that grows with the portfolio.
Direct mentorship from operators — co-founders, product leads and CEOs across the portfolio.
A supportive team that values curiosity, initiative and collaboration.

jobs.description:
Purpose. Performance. People. 

 Joining CPP Investments means joining one of the world’s most admired and respected institutional investors to drive a single mandate: to deliver strong, sustainable returns for generations of Canadians.   

 With a long-term horizon and global reach, we deploy capital at scale across public and private markets. Our size, stability, and disciplined investment philosophy allow us to pursue complex opportunities and build enduring partnerships worldwide.  

 For our people, this means meaningful work with tangible impact, real opportunity, and collaboration with exceptional colleagues who value partnership and performance. Here, you’ll contribute to outcomes that matter alongside team members committed to excellence and shared success.   

 The Role 

The Director, Security Architecture & Engineering will provide strategic and technical leadership for CPP Investments' security architecture and engineering function. Reporting to the Managing Director, Security Architecture & Engineering, you will lead the development of enterprise security architecture, cloud security strategy, and security engineering capabilities while partnering across the organization to embed security into technology delivery and operations. You will build and mentor a high-performing team, drive innovation, and help strengthen CPP Investments' overall cybersecurity posture 

 The Team 

 Technology & Operations enables CPP Investments to deliver on its global investment mandate through secure, resilient, and innovative technology capabilities. The department partners across the organization to provide scalable platforms, modern infrastructure, and cybersecurity capabilities that protect the organization while supporting business growth.

 The Security Architecture & Engineering team is responsible for establishing enterprise security architecture standards, advancing security engineering capabilities, and embedding security by design across technology platforms. The team works closely with technology and business partners to deliver secure, resilient solutions that effectively manage cyber risk.

 Accountabilities 
 Provide strategic leadership, direction, and mentorship to the Security Architecture & Engineering team while helping shape and execute the organization's long-term cybersecurity strategy.

 Lead the design, implementation, and continuous improvement of enterprise security architecture, ensuring alignment with business objectives, regulatory requirements, and industry best practices.

 Develop and execute the organization's cloud security strategy, strengthening the security, scalability, and resilience of cloud environments.

 Evaluate emerging cybersecurity technologies, trends, and standards, driving the adoption of innovative solutions that align with the organization's risk appetite.

 Lead security architecture reviews and risk assessments, providing expert guidance and actionable recommendations to stakeholders.

 Partner with technology, operations, and business teams to embed security-by-design principles throughout the technology lifecycle and effectively communicate security strategies and risks to diverse audiences.

 Oversee the design and implementation of security platforms, automation capabilities, and engineering solutions that enhance operational effectiveness and strengthen the organization's security posture.

 What You Bring 
 Bachelor's or Master's degree in Computer Science, Information Security, or a related discipline.

 CISSP, CISM, CCSP, or an equivalent industry certification.

 Minimum of 15 years of experience in security architecture, security engineering, or a related cybersecurity discipline.

 Minimum of 4 years of people leadership experience leading security architecture or security engineering teams.

 Demonstrated expertise in enterprise security architecture, cloud security, security engineering, risk assessment, and security technologies within complex organizations; experience in Canadian financial services is considered an asset.

 Strong leadership, communication, and stakeholder management skills with the ability to influence technical and business audiences.

 Excellent analytical, problem-solving, and collaboration skills, with a commitment to continuous learning and staying current with evolving cybersecurity trends.

 You are motivated to contribute to something larger than yourself, approach complex challenges with rigor, and hold yourself to  high standards in a collaborative, performance-driven environment.   

 We provide colleagues with cutting-edge AI tools, dedicated learning time, and practical support to help them deliver with greater impact.

 Inclusion & Accessibility 
 CPP Investments is committed to  equitable access to employment and building a workforce that reflects diverse talent and perspectives. If you require accommodation at any stage of the recruitment process, please let us know and we will work with you to meet your needs.   

 Attention: Protect Yourself from Fraud 
 CPP Investments is committed to a secure and transparent recruitment process. We will never ask candidates for payment or financial information at any stage of hiring. All legitimate opportunities are posted on our careers page, and communications will come from our applicant tracking system, Workday.

 Represent Enterprise Communications on enterprise projects and governance forums, and improve communications processes, tools and standards.

 Education and experience
 Post-secondary degree or diploma in Communications, Journalism, Public Relations, Business, Finance, Economics, or an equivalent combination of education and experience.
 8 to 10 years of progressive communications experience, including demonstrated ownership of a communications strategy or program at an enterprise level.
 Demonstrated investment and financial knowledge is required, gained through direct experience in investment communications, capital markets, asset management, banking, pension plans or another institutional investment environment.
 Experience as a communications advisor to C-suite executives, including speechwriting and external platform development for a CEO or equivalent.

 Experience operating effectively within a complex, highly regulated, or stakeholder-rich environment.
 Experience leading through influence, including directing cross functional teams, agencies and external partners without direct reporting authority.

 Skills and capabilities
 Exceptional written and oral communication, editing and storytelling skills, adapted to diverse audiences and channels, particularly external ones.
 Solid working knowledge of investment and financial concepts, including asset classes, portfolio construction, capital markets, and risk and return, with the ability to read and interpret financial statements and performance reporting.
 Strong business acumen and the ability to understand complex financial and investment concepts 
 Strong critical thinking to assess communications needs and risks relevant to the CEO, the Executive Team, and the Board of Trustees.
 Deep understanding of corporate communications and multichannel storytelling in building and protecting external reputation.
 Excellent judgement, discretion, attention to detail and project management skills, with the ability to hold several senior priorities at once.
 Demonstrated ability to build trust, influence stakeholders at all levels and respectfully challenge perspectives when appropriate.
 Highly motivated self-starter who delivers high-quality work with minimal direction and brings structure to ambiguous problems.
 Demonstrated proficiency with artificial intelligence tools to improve the effectiveness, efficiency, and impact of communications, including content development, insight generation, stakeholder sentiment analysis and channel optimization.

 Assets
 A CFA, CIM, CAIA, MBA or accounting designation, held or in progress.
 Experience communicating on behalf of a pension plan, institutional investor, or other long-horizon asset owner.

jobs.description:
About RECO

As Ontario’s regulator of more than 110,000 real estate agents and brokerages (often referred to as registrants), RECO administers and enforces the law that regulates trading in real estate in Ontario and enhances consumer confidence in the real estate services sector. RECO’s commitment to pursuing trust in every transaction means consumers can navigate the real estate market with confidence.

A modern regulator with approximately 170 employees, RECO is a collegial and dynamic environment where strategic agility, curiosity and empathy are valued.

Hybrid work environment

RECO has a ‘hybrid’ environment, which typically includes a minimum attendance in the office of two days per week, with some teams/positions requiring more frequent in-office attendance.

RECO’s commitment to diversity and inclusion: They aren’t just words to us!

RECO is committed to promoting an equitable, diverse, and inclusive environment that includes awareness, education, and engagement-building opportunities for all employees.

The role

Reporting to the Chief Data, Technology and Innovation Officer (CDTIO), the Director, Enterprise Architecture & Cyber Security is accountable for RECO's enterprise technology strategy and architecture, cyber security strategy and operations, technology resilience, and the secure, reliable operation of core infrastructure services.

The role provides strategic leadership for the design, modernization, security, and optimization of RECO's infrastructure environment, including cloud platforms, networks, identity and access services, end-user technology, collaboration platforms, security technologies, backup and recovery capabilities, and related infrastructure services.

The Director establishes infrastructure architecture principles, standards, roadmaps, and governance and serves as a senior advisor on cyber security, infrastructure risk, resilience, and technology investment decisions. The role partners with application, data, and business leaders to ensure infrastructure and security capabilities support RECO's strategic objectives, regulatory mandate, and consumer protection responsibilities.

Position responsibilities

Enterprise Infrastructure Architecture & Strategy

Develop and maintain RECO's enterprise infrastructure architecture strategy, vision, principles, standards, target-state architecture, and multi-year roadmap.
Define architecture for cloud, network, compute, storage, identity, collaboration, end-user technology, and core infrastructure platforms.
Ensure infrastructure architecture supports scalability, resilience, security, interoperability, service performance, and organizational priorities.
Provide architectural direction for infrastructure modernization, lifecycle management, technical debt reduction, and platform consolidation.
Advise Executive Leadership on infrastructure architecture risks, investment priorities, emerging infrastructure technologies, and modernization opportunities.

Infrastructure Architecture Governance & Standards

Establish and maintain infrastructure architecture governance, standards, patterns, reference architectures, and technology guardrails.
Lead architecture reviews for infrastructure and security solutions and ensure alignment with approved standards and target-state architecture.
Partner with application and data teams to define infrastructure dependencies, hosting requirements, integration constraints, and security requirements without owning application or data architecture.
Evaluate infrastructure and security technologies, including cloud, network, identity, endpoint, monitoring, automation, and resilience capabilities.
Maintain architecture documentation, technology lifecycle standards, and exception-management processes

Technology Resilience & Continuity

Establish and maintain technology resilience requirements for critical infrastructure and security services.
Oversee disaster recovery, cyber recovery, backup, restoration, redundancy, and continuity capabilities and ensure they are regularly tested.
Define recovery objectives and resilience standards in partnership with business continuity and technology stakeholders.
Identify infrastructure single points of failure, key-person dependencies, and service continuity risks and drive remediation plans.
Provide leadership during significant technology disruptions and ensure post-incident lessons learned are translated into architecture and operational improvements

Cyber Security Operations, Risk & Resilience

Accountable for RECO's enterprise cyber security strategy, security operations, cyber risk management, and information security governance.
Oversee security operations, threat monitoring, vulnerability management, incident response, identity and access management, endpoint security, and security architecture.
Direct the ongoing operation and continuous improvement of security technologies, controls, monitoring, and detection capabilities.
Lead cyber incident response, recovery, lessons learned reviews, and remediation planning.
Establish cyber security policies, standards, controls, and risk practices aligned with industry best practices and regulatory requirements.
Oversee third-party cyber security risk assessments and vendor security management programs.
Provide regular cyber security risk reporting and recommendations to Executive Leadership and governance committees.

Infrastructure, Cloud & Technology Operations

Provide strategic oversight of infrastructure, cloud services, networks, collaboration platforms, end-user technology, identity services, and related operational services.
Ensure infrastructure services are reliable, secure, scalable, supportable, and aligned with business requirements and architecture standards.
Establish service management frameworks, service levels, operational performance measures, and technology lifecycle practices.
Monitor infrastructure capacity, availability, performance, and operational risk and implement continuous improvement initiatives.
Ensure operational changes, releases, and platform upgrades are governed and executed with appropriate risk, security, and continuity controls.

Leadership & Organizational Effectiveness

Lead, develop, coach, and mentor infrastructure and cyber security leaders and team members.
Establish workforce plans, succession plans, and capability development strategies for infrastructure architecture, operations, and cyber security.
Foster a high-performance culture focused on collaboration, accountability, service excellence, security, and continuous improvement.
Promote effective cross-functional partnerships across Technology and the broader organization.

Financial Management & Vendor Governance

Develop and manage operating and capital budgets for infrastructure and cyber security services.
Oversee infrastructure and security procurement, vendor relationships, managed service providers, licensing, and strategic technology partnerships.
Ensure infrastructure and cyber security investments deliver measurable value, manage risk, and align with organizational priorities.
Lead contract negotiations, vendor performance management, and service reviews for infrastructure and cyber security providers.

Qualifications and experience

Minimum 10-15 years of progressively senior technology experience, with significant leadership accountability for infrastructure architecture, technology operations, and cyber security.
Minimum 5-7 years leading managers and professional technology teams.
Demonstrated experience establishing enterprise infrastructure architecture, standards, roadmaps, and governance across cloud, network, identity, endpoint, collaboration, and core infrastructure platforms.
Demonstrated experience leading cyber security operations, security architecture, cyber risk management, incident response, and organizational technology resilience.
University degree in Computer Science, Information Technology, Engineering, Information Systems, Cybersecurity, or a related field.
Master's degree and/or relevant professional certifications such as CISSP, CISM, CCSP, TOGAF, or equivalent are considered assets.
Experience leading large-scale infrastructure modernization, cloud transformation, lifecycle management, and resilience initiatives in a DAA (Designated administrative authority) is nice to have
Experience managing managed service providers, technology vendors, budgets, contracts, and service performance in a DAA (Designated administrative authority) is preferred
Experience advising executive leadership and governance bodies on infrastructure architecture, cyber security, technology risk, and resilience in a DAA (Designated administrative authority) is preferred.
Experience working within highly regulated environments is preferred.

Core competencies

Strategic Leadership
Enterprise Infrastructure Architecture
Cyber Security & Technology Risk Management
Architecture Governance & Standards
Executive Influence & Advisory Skills
Business & Financial Acumen
Vendor & Third-Party Risk Management
Stakeholder Relationship Management
People Leadership & Talent Development
Regulatory & Governance Awareness

Pay Range

$170,000 - $190,000 CAD

Why work for RECO?

Working at RECO means contributing to an organization that supports a fair, transparent, and consumer-focused real estate marketplace.

Community Engagement Manager, Data Centres (Canada)
jobs.description:
About Anthropic 

 Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.

 About the role

 Anthropic is building AI systems that will shape the trajectory of one of the most consequential technologies in human history. That work requires physical infrastructure at significant scale, and building that infrastructure the right way means being a real, long-term partner to the communities where we operate.

 We are looking for a Community Engagement Manager in Canada to join our Public Policy team and serve as Anthropic's on-the-ground presence in the communities where our data centres are sited, built, and operated. This is not a communications role or a government affairs role, though you will do elements of both. It is a relationship role: your job is to make Anthropic a trusted, visible, and valued neighbour, from the earliest stages of site selection through construction and long-term operations.

 You will be the connective tissue between Anthropic's Policy and Infrastructure teams and the local officials, community organizations, economic development partners, and residents who have a stake in what we build. You will surface concerns before they escalate, translate our technical and operational plans into clear local benefits, and build the coalitions that allow us to move quickly and responsibly. Because Anthropic's infrastructure footprint is still early in its growth, you will also help write the playbook: the processes you build in your first markets are the ones we will use as we expand.

 You will travel regularly within your region, up to 50% of the time, and occasionally to other Anthropic data centre markets.

 Key responsibilities

 Build and maintain trusted, sustained relationships with municipal governments, both elected and unelected, provincial ministers and agencies, economic development organizations, community groups, civic leaders, educational institutions, and workforce partners in the data centre markets you cover

 Develop and execute a community engagement strategy for each of your markets, spanning site selection, pre-development, construction, and ongoing operations

 Build external coalitions, host education and listening sessions, and design local solutions that deliver real benefits to the communities where we operate

 Represent Anthropic in public forums, town halls, planning hearings, community events, and local media

 Monitor community sentiment and local political dynamics, and advise internal teams on risks, opportunities, and the right pace and posture for engagement

 Partner with the Real Estate and Infrastructure team to bring community input into how projects are planned, communicated, and delivered, not just how they are announced

 Work with the Communications team to develop proactive, locally relevant messaging

 Coordinate charitable giving, community investment, and economic development commitments in your markets, including managing nonprofit partner relationships

 Partner with the Energy and Sustainability team to explain our approach to environmental stewardship and respond to questions about power, water, and land use

 Build a community engagement playbook and repeatable processes that scale as Anthropic's infrastructure footprint grows

 Minimum qualifications

 Experience in community affairs, public affairs, economic development, government relations, municipal or provincial government, or a closely related field

 Direct experience working for or engaging with municipal governments, both elected councils and administration, and provincial government on behalf of large infrastructure, construction, energy, or technology projects, with a working understanding of how local politics and community dynamics actually play out

 A skilled relationship and coalition builder who earns trust with a diverse group of stakeholders, and who maintains relationships through difficult conversations

 The ability to represent a company credibly in public settings — town halls, hearings, press interviews

 Strong written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to turn a complex operational plan into plain language that a local official or reporter can understand and respond to

 The ability to work independently, get up to speed quickly on complex policy issues, and manage multiple concurrent engagements across different markets without losing track of any of them

 Based in Alberta, Canada or willing to relocate there, and prepared to travel regularly across the region

 Preferred qualifications

 7+ years of experience in community engagement specifically on data centre, utility, energy, or large-scale industrial infrastructure projects, or in local government

 Familiarity with land use, zoning, and development permitting processes at the municipal and provincial level

 Experience managing corporate social responsibility programs

 Established relationships with economic development, workforce, or civic organizations in the markets this role covers

 Experience working with real estate, legal, communications, and policy teams at the same time

 A genuine interest in the communities where you work, not just the projects you are managing

 Logistics 

 Minimum education: Bachelor’s degree or an equivalent combination of education, training, and/or experience

 Required field of study:  A field relevant to the role as demonstrated through coursework, training, or professional experience

 Minimum years of experience: Years of experience required will correlate with the internal job level requirements for the position

 Location-based hybrid policy: Currently, we expect all staff to be in one of our offices at least 25% of the time. However, some roles may require more time in our offices.

 Visa sponsorship:  We do sponsor visas! However, we aren't able to successfully sponsor visas for every role and every candidate. But if we make you an offer, we will make every reasonable effort to get you a visa, and we retain an immigration lawyer to help with this.

 We encourage you to apply even if you do not believe you meet every single qualification. Not all strong candidates will meet every single qualification as listed.  Research shows that people who identify as being from underrepresented groups are more prone to experiencing imposter syndrome and doubting the strength of their candidacy, so we urge you not to exclude yourself prematurely and to submit an application if you're interested in this work. We think AI systems like the ones we're building have enormous social and ethical implications. We think this makes representation even more important, and we strive to include a range of diverse perspectives on our team.

 Your safety matters to us. To protect yourself from potential scams, remember that Anthropic recruiters only contact you from @anthropic.com email addresses. In some cases, we may partner with vetted recruiting agencies who will identify themselves as working on behalf of Anthropic. Be cautious of emails from other domains. Legitimate Anthropic recruiters will never ask for money, fees, or banking information before your first day. If you're ever unsure about a communication, don't click any links—visit  anthropic.com/careers  directly for confirmed position openings.

We're an extremely collaborative group, and we host frequent research discussions to ensure that we are pursuing the highest-impact work at any given time. As such, we greatly value communication skills.

 The easiest way to understand our research directions is to read our recent research. This research continues many of the directions our team worked on prior to Anthropic, including: GPT-3, Circuit-Based Interpretability, Multimodal Neurons, Scaling Laws, AI & Compute, Concrete Problems in AI Safety, and Learning from Human Preferences.

jobs.description:
Total Life

Vancouver· Full-time

Most marketers pick one side: creative or analytical. We need someone who refuses to choose.

Total Life is a national behavioral health telehealth company built for adults in their later years. We offer therapy in all 50 states and DC through 200+ licensed clinicians, and we accept Medicare and most major insurance plans, so care is affordable for the people who need it most. We're adding psychiatry, longevity, and weight-loss services state by state. Our audience is one of the most underserved, and most overlooked, in digital marketing. Whoever learns to reach them well will build something few people have.

We're hiring our Head of Digital Marketing to own paid acquisition end to end: strategy, creative, launch, optimization, and reporting. You'll work directly with the leadership and have real authority over budget, tools, and direction.

What You'll Own

Paid and organic acquisition across Meta, Google, and TikTok. You'll plan, build, launch, and scale campaigns, deciding where every dollar goes and defending those calls with data
The full funnel, from first impression to booked appointment. Landing pages, intake flows, retargeting, and email and SMS nurture are all yours to test and rebuild. You know the ad is only half the job
An AI-powered creative engine. You'll use AI tools to generate, version, and test ad creative and copy at volume, and you'll build a system that keeps every asset organized and findable so the library becomes a compounding advantage
Reporting the team actually uses. You'll build clean dashboards and weekly reports that tie spend to cost per booked patient and patient value, not just clicks and impressions
A testing culture. You'll run a steady pipeline of experiments on audiences, hooks, offers, and pages, document what works, and kill what doesn't quickly
Staying ahead of the platforms. Algorithms, ad policies, and tools change monthly. You'll know before your competitors do and adjust before performance slips

Requirements

You're the person we're looking for if

You've personally run and scaled paid campaigns on Meta, Google, and TikTok, and you can show us results with real numbers
You get as excited about a beautiful ad as about a 20% drop in cost per acquisition, and you think the two are connected
You live in the data: attribution, cohorts, funnel conversion rates, and the story behind a spreadsheet
You already use AI tools daily for creative, copy, analysis, or automation, and you're always trying new ones
You tinker. You've built a landing page, rigged a tracking setup, or automated a workflow because you wanted to see whether you could
You know what changed on each platform in the last 90 days without having to look it up
You can work independently with high ownership and low ego. You'd rather show results than talk about them

Bonus points

Experience marketing in healthcare, telehealth, or another regulated category, including HIPAA-safe tracking and health ad policies on Meta and Google
Experience reaching older adults or their adult children
Comfort with landing-page builders, WordPress, HubSpot or similar CRMs, GHL, and analytics tools such as GA4 and Looker Studio

Benefits

Why join us

Your work gets older adults to mental health care they'd otherwise go without, and you'll see the impact in patients booked
You'll have real ownership: your strategy, your stack, your tests
Your playbook will shape the company as we expand into new services and states
Competitive compensation with salary, performance bonus and equity!

jobs.title: CTO (Chief Technology Officer)
jobs.description:
Chief Technology Officer (CTO)

Total Life

Seed Stage
Equity Package
Full-Time
Remote (North America)

About Total Life

Total Life is a national behavioral health telehealth platform built for adults later in life, the fastest-growing and most underserved population in American healthcare. We offer therapy in all 50 states plus Washington, DC, through a network of 200+ licensed clinicians. We have expanded into psychiatry, longevity, weight loss and cognitive care, and we bill Original Medicare Part B directly. We are in-network nationally with Aetna, Cigna, UnitedHealthcare and Humana, and with most Blue Cross Blue Shield and regional plans.

We are growing quickly. Total Life ranks in the top 10 of the Deloitte Technology Fast 50 (Canada)
and #5 in healthcare on the Inc. 5000
. We have also been named to the C100 and are a member of the AARP AgeTech Collaborative. We are now entering our next phase of hypergrowth, and we need a technical leader to build what comes next.

The Role

This is not a CTO role where you manage from a distance. We want a builder-leader who will write production code every week and also set the technical vision for the company. You will work directly with leadership, on the strategic roadmap. You will own the architecture, and you will build AI-first systems that change how older adults find, start and stay in care.

The role is high-profile, high-impact and hands-on. It suits someone who is all in, energized by an intense, fast-moving environment, and excited to build a category-defining company from the ground up.

What You'll Do

Build and ship.
You will write, review and ship code across the stack. Over the past year we built our native systems, which gives us full control over patient engagement, agentic workflows and a multi-specialty care experience. You'll take that platform to its next level.

Lead AI-first product development.
You will design and scale AI systems that run in real clinical and operational workflows. One example is Lily, our AI companion, which calls patients to schedule appointments, send medication reminders, run screenings and coach CBT exercises. You'll also build intelligent intake, automated eligibility and agentic back-office operations.

Co-own the strategic roadmap.
You will partner with leadership turn company strategy into a technical roadmap. That includes build-vs-buy decisions, sequencing, platform bets and the long-term vision of Total Life as the infrastructure other behavioral health practices can run on.

Champion product design and customer experience.
Our patients are older adults, and many are new to telehealth. You'll bring a sharp design eye to every patient, clinician and partner touchpoint, so that the product is simple, warm and accessible.

Engineer for growth and engagement.
You will build the features and tools that drive acquisition, activation, retention and session completion. Examples include referral loops, partner dashboards, re-engagement flows, and in-platform experiences that keep patients connected to their care.

Integrate marketing technology.
You will connect the platform to our growth engine, including attribution, CRM, messaging, conversion funnels and paid acquisition data, so that marketing and product run on one source of truth.

Own healthcare infrastructure.
You will lead our work on payer and eligibility integrations (including CMS HETS 270/271), interoperability, senior-living integrations such as PointClickCare, and revenue cycle data flows.

Secure and scale the platform.
You will keep HIPAA compliance, security, uptime and data integrity strong as our patient volume, states and service lines grow.

Build and lead the team.
You will set the engineering culture, raise the bar for quality and speed, manage in-house and contract developers, and hire the team that will carry us through Series A and beyond.

To Apply

Send your resume along with a few sentences about something you've built that you're proud of, and why this role excites you. Links to GitHub, shipped products or portfolio work are encouraged.

Requirements

What You Bring

You have 8+ years of software engineering experience, including meaningful time as a technical leader (CTO, VP Engineering, founding engineer or head of engineering) at a startup or high-growth company.

You are still an active hands-on coder and enjoy shipping. You have deep experience with modern backend systems, cloud infrastructure and API design. Experience with Go is a strong plus, along with fluency in modern frontend frameworks.

You have shipped AI and LLM-powered products in production, including agentic workflows, voice or conversational AI, and retrieval systems. You understand both their potential and their failure modes.

You have strong product and design
instincts. You care how things look and feel, and you can tell when a feature will drive engagement and when it won't.

You have a track record of building systems from zero to one and then scaling them through rapid growth.

You can translate between business strategy and technical execution, and you can communicate clearly with the CEO, clinicians, partners and investors.

You thrive with ambiguity, urgency and ownership, and you want to be in the arena.

Huge Pluses

Healthcare technology experience is a major plus, especially EHRs, telehealth, HIPAA, HL7/FHIR, payer integrations, eligibility and claims, or revenue cycle systems. So is experience with marketing technology and growth infrastructure, such as attribution, CRM platforms, lifecycle messaging and experimentation frameworks. We also value experience building products for older adults, caregivers or accessibility-first audiences, experience at a startup through a Series A or later raise, and background in behavioral health, Medicare or value-based care.

Benefits

Why Total Life

You'll do meaningful work. Behavioral health for older adults is one of the largest unmet needs in American healthcare, and your work will directly improve access to care for people who have long been overlooked.

You'll join proven momentum. We are nationally recognized as one of the fastest-growing companies in North America, with a national clinician network and broad insurance coverage already in place.

You'll have real ownership. As CTO you'll hold a seat at the leadership table, have a direct line to the CEO, and shape both the technology and the company.

You'll get meaningful equity. We offer a competitive salary and significant equity in a company at an inflection point.

You'll build from the ground floor. This is the chance to architect the platform that defines tech-enabled care for aging adults.

jobs.description:
Our Purpose

Mastercard powers economies and empowers people in 200+ countries and territories worldwide. Together with our customers, we’re helping build a sustainable economy where everyone can prosper. We support a wide range of digital payments choices, making transactions secure, simple, smart and accessible. Our technology and innovation, partnerships and networks combine to deliver a unique set of products and services that help people, businesses and governments realize their greatest potential.

Title And Summary

Director, Data Science

Overview

The Security Solutions Data Science team is responsible for delivering Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Machine Learning (ML) models that support Mastercard’s Identity and risk products across the payment networks. These models are designed to be production-ready and to power high-value capabilities that protect digital transactions and enable trusted decisioning at scale.

Beyond model development, the organization is responsible for building scalable, repeatable, and resilient data science capabilities that cover the end-to-end lifecycle of machine learning solutions, from data acquisition and feature engineering through experimentation, validation, deployment, and monitoring. These systems must not only perform effectively in production, but also be built in a way that is industrialized, maintainable, and aligned with broader business and platform needs.

Services within Mastercard is responsible for acquiring, engaging, and retaining customers by managing fraud and risk, enhancing cybersecurity, and improving the digital payments experience. Within this mission, the Identity Data Science portfolio plays a significant role in developing intelligence-driven solutions that improve how risk is understood and managed across the merchant lifecycle.

We are looking for a highly skilled and strategic Director to lead a Data Science team that focuses on solving merchant risk during onboarding and monitoring. This role is critical in driving the research and development of a merchant registry and profiling capability within the Identity Data Science portfolio. This includes setting the strategy for how merchant intelligence is built and scaled, guiding the development of reusable data science assets and profiling frameworks, and ensuring strong execution across product, engineering, and data science partners. You will help shape both the technical direction and operational model needed to turn this capability into a durable and scalable advantage.

Role
