 Job Description: 
 About the Role 

 The Corporate AVP, Underwriting Risk & Governance is accountable for maintaining the organization's underwriting philosophy, risk appetite, technical standards, and governance framework across all life and health insurance businesses. The role serves as a corporate risk subject matter expert on mortality, morbidity, product, underwriting, and fraud risks, providing underwriting risk management guidance to business units globally, with particular emphasis on emerging risks, high-net-worth markets, and the impact of underwriting and product design decisions on long-term business performance.

 The incumbent will lead the evaluation and approval of underwriting and product-related risk initiatives, assess the mortality and morbidity implications of underwriting requirement changes, product innovations, and distribution strategies, and ensure alignment with corporate risk management objectives, with primary focus on our Asia business units and Private Wealth business. The role provides technical leadership to underwriters and input to actuarial, product development, and risk management teams on underwriting-specific risk while championing sound underwriting practices, risk governance, and sustainable growth.

 Operating in a highly collaborative, consultative, and project-oriented environment, the Corporate AVP, Underwriting Risk & Governance will lead complex initiatives across the Asia business units and jurisdictions, influence business unit underwriting leadership and risk management decision-making, and represent the organization on underwriting and insurance industry matters under the direction of the Corporate Chief Underwriter.

 Key Responsibilities 

 Enterprise Underwriting Governance 
 Support and champion corporate underwriting philosophy, risk appetite, and underwriting governance standards.

 Provide enterprise oversight of underwriting practices across life, health, critical illness, disability, and medical reimbursement products.

 Evaluate proposed changes to underwriting requirements, underwriting evidence, accelerated underwriting programs, automation initiatives, and digital underwriting solutions.

 Assess and communicate the mortality and morbidity implications associated with underwriting and product design changes.

 Mortality and Morbidity Risk Management 
 Evaluate mortality and morbidity risks associated with existing and proposed products, underwriting methodologies, and distribution strategies.

 Assess the impact of product features, underwriting evidence requirements, and benefit structures on expected mortality and morbidity outcomes.

 Partner with actuarial, product, and risk management teams to monitor emerging experience trends and recommend mitigation strategies.

 Provide technical leadership on mortality and morbidity risk management across multiple markets.

 Product and Anti-Selection Risk Assessment 
 Assess product design features for anti-selection, fraud, claims, and sustainability risks.

 Identify underwriting controls, medical requirements, and risk management measures necessary to mitigate adverse selection and fraud exposure.

 Provide risk guidance during new product development and product enhancement activities.

 Evaluate the potential impact of product design changes on underwriting outcomes and claims experience.

 Fraud Risk Oversight 
 Identify emerging fraud risks and vulnerabilities within underwriting and product frameworks.

 Recommend underwriting, medical, and operational controls designed to mitigate fraud exposure.

 Partner with claims, investigations, and risk management teams to identify trends and strengthen preventive measures.

 High - Net - Worth and Complex Risk Expertise 
 Provide technical leadership on high-net-worth and Private Wealth underwriting practices, particularly within Asian markets.

 Evaluate large face amount and complex financial underwriting cases.

 Monitor market developments and emerging risk trends impacting high-net-worth and Private Wealth business.

 Support business units in developing prudent underwriting strategies for complex and high-exposure risks.

 Retention and Reinsurance Management 
 Provide leadership and guidance regarding retention management practices.

 Evaluate retention limits, concentration risk, and reinsurance effectiveness.

 Partner with reinsurance stakeholders as permitted to ensure alignment between underwriting strategies and risk transfer objectives.

 Strategic Leadership 
 Lead complex cross-functional underwriting initiatives involving multiple business units, jurisdictions, and product lines.

 Influence senior leaders and business partners on underwriting, mortality, morbidity, and product risk matters.

 Provide strategic recommendations balancing growth opportunities with responsible risk management.

 Serve as a trusted advisor to the Corporate Chief Underwriter on emerging underwriting and insurance risks.

 Technical Thought Leadership 
 Research emerging medical, underwriting, product, and industry developments.

 Participate in the development and maintenance of underwriting manuals, medical guidelines, and risk assessment standards.

 Translate emerging medical evidence and industry research into practical underwriting guidance.

 Represent the organization externally through industry associations, conferences, forums, and professional organizations.

 What you'll need to succeed 
 Minimum 15 years of progressive life and health underwriting experience.

 Minimum 5 years holding an individual underwriting approval authority of at least $30 million (preferred).

 Significant experience assessing complex mortality and morbidity risks.

 Experience underwriting high-net-worth and large face amount business, including exposure to Asian insurance markets.

 Demonstrated experience evaluating underwriting implications of life, health, disability, critical illness, hospital indemnity, and medical reimbursement products.

 Proven experience leading complex underwriting, governance, or risk initiatives across multiple business units or jurisdictions.

 Experience working with reinsurance and retention management frameworks.

 Experience developing underwriting philosophy, guidelines, manuals, and risk governance standards.

 Proven ability to influence business risk management and underwriting leaders.

 Strong strategic thinking and risk assessment capabilities.

 Exceptional communication, presentation, and stakeholder management skills.

 Ability to work independently with minimal direction while managing multiple concurrent priorities.

 Strong collaboration skills with the ability to drive alignment across diverse stakeholders.

 Comfortable operating in a dynamic environment focused on governance, consultation, project leadership, innovation, and enterprise risk oversight rather than production underwriting activities.

 Preferred Designations 
 FALU

 FLMI

 Additional designations in risk management, supplemental health, or related disciplines.

 What's in it for you 
 Being a member of the Sun Life family, a group of people united by our Purpose: to help Clients and Employees achieve lifetime financial security and live healthier lives.

 In 2024, Sun Life ranked among the top 100 most sustainable global corporations by Corporate Knights for the 15th consecutive year, leading Canadian insurers. 

 We are proud to be on the 2024 Best Workplaces in Canada list by Great Place to Work. 

 We’re also listed as one of the Best Workplaces for Women and Best Workplaces with Most Trusted Executive Teams.

 Our unique Sabbatical Program gives you the opportunity to take up to 6 weeks off, every five years.

 Care Days available for self-care or care of others (i.e., family or others you may support) and Sick Days to support your well-being.

 The Base Pay range is for the primary location for which the job is posted. It may vary depending on the work location of the successful candidate or other factors. In addition to Base Pay, eligible Sun Life employees participate in various incentive plans, payment under which is discretionary and subject to individual and company performance. Certain sales focused roles have sales incentive plans based on individual or group sales results. 

 Diversity and inclusion have always been at the core of our values at Sun Life. A diverse workforce with wide perspectives and creative ideas benefits our Clients, the communities where we operate and all of us as colleagues. We welcome applications from qualified individuals from all backgrounds.

 Persons with disabilities who need accommodation in the application process, or those needing job postings in an alternative format, may e-mail a request to thebrightside@sunlife.com.

 We are proud to be a hybrid organization that offers our employees the choice and flexibility to work from both the office and virtually based on the needs of the business, our Clients and you.

 We may use artificial intelligence to support candidate sourcing, screening, interview scheduling.

jobs.title: Associate Director, Commercial Data Operations
jobs.description:
**Location** Mississauga, Ontario, Canada **Job ID** R\-262602 **Date posted** 22/10/2026
  
When we put unexpected teams in the same room, we unleash bold thinking with the power to inspire life\-changing medicines. In\-person working gives us the platform to connect, work at pace and challenge perceptions. That’s why we work, on average, a minimum of three days per week from the office. But that doesn’t mean we’re not flexible. We balance the expectation of being in the office while respecting individual flexibility. Join us in our unique and ambitious world.


The Associate Director, Commercial Data Operations leads the delivery and reliability of data that supports US Commercial decisions, operations, reporting and advanced analytics at Alexion, AstraZeneca Rare Disease. You will set priorities and operating standards across commercial data assets, partner with technology teams to deliver governed data products, and lead the response to material data issues. The role spans specialty pharmacy and distribution, patient services, claims, customer and product master data, customer engagement and performance data.


**Accountabilities:**


* Portfolio Leadership: Set and sequence priorities across new data sources, product launches, enhancements, and production support; translate business needs into a clear roadmap, delivery plans, and decisions on scope, timing, and dependencies.
* Data Product Ownership: Define business outcomes, common definitions, ownership, and acceptance criteria for reusable commercial data products; partner with engineering on models, lineage, access, testing, and transition from build to sustained operations.
* Source Onboarding and Integration: Assess internal and vendor data, contracts, and file specifications; coordinate design, historical loads, validation, and downstream readiness for reporting, Decision Science, CRM, and other consumers.
* Launch Readiness: Map the end\-to\-end flow—from source and master data through ingestion, data products, CRM alignment, reporting, and alerts; confirm dependencies, testing, and cutover plans; ensure downstream consumers are ready before launch.
* Production Reliability: Establish service expectations, monitoring, incident response, and escalation for critical feeds and pipelines; analyze recurring failures, drive corrective action with IT and vendors, and communicate business impact and recovery plans.
* Architecture, MDM, and Change Stewardship: Review designs and source\-to\-target mappings for scalability, maintainability, and downstream impact; partner on HCP, HCO, and product identity, affiliations, hierarchies, and cross\-system keys; align with enterprise standards while protecting US Commercial requirements.
* Leadership of Partners and Teams: Direct internal team members and external partners; clarify accountabilities, coach strong technical and business judgment, and hold vendors accountable for quality, schedules, and issue resolution.
* Stakeholder Engagement: Partner with Trade and Distribution, Patient Services, Market Access, Commercial Operations, Reporting and Insights, Decision Science, and IT; resolve competing priorities and provide concise updates on risks, decisions, and delivery status.
* Data Quality and Controls: Define critical data elements, thresholds, and controls across freshness, completeness, accuracy, consistency, and reconciliation; sponsor automated checks, dashboards, exception ownership, and alerting; require evidence for validation and regression testing; maintain lineage, documentation, and issue history so consumers understand data limits and changes.

**Essential Skills/Experience:**


* Education and experience: Bachelor’s degree in a relevant field or equivalent experience, with 8 or more years in pharmaceutical or healthcare commercial data management, operations or engineering, including leadership of complex initiatives.
* Commercial data and MDM expertise: Strong knowledge of pharmaceutical commercial data across specialty pharmacy or patient services, claims, CRM and performance. Understanding of HCP, HCO and product mastering, matching, affiliations and hierarchies, and their effect on downstream data products.
* Technical judgment: Advanced SQL and practical Snowflake experience for profiling, reconciliation and root cause analysis. Ability to review data models, pipeline designs, transformations and architecture with engineering teams; working knowledge of Python and orchestration or transformation tools.
* Data product and quality leadership: Experience defining reusable datasets, business rules, ownership, lineage, quality controls and release acceptance criteria across multiple data sources and consumers.
* Delivery leadership: Proven ability to run a portfolio of concurrent requests, incidents and launches; prioritize by business impact; lead testing, cutovers and operational handover; and manage vendors and delivery partners.
* Communication and influence: Ability to challenge ambiguous requirements, make tradeoffs clear, develop colleagues and influence senior business and technology stakeholders without relying on direct authority.

**Desirable Skills/Experience:**


* Rare disease and vendor knowledge: Experience with specialty pharmacy and distribution feeds, including patient status, dispense, inventory and shipment data; familiarity with Veeva, IQVIA, Komodo or similar sources.
* Modern data platform delivery: Experience with Snowflake, Airflow, dbt, S3, secure sharing, Git based releases and data product frameworks across raw, staging and curated layers.
* AI and Decision Science enablement: Experience applying AI or advanced analytics to data operations or quality monitoring, such as anomaly detection and investigation. Understanding of model inputs, scores and outputs used for field alerts, including validation, refresh timing and production support with Decision Science teams.
* People and change leadership: Experience coaching data teams, managing extern

jobs.title: Director, Strategic Deal Finance
jobs.description:
Liftoff is a leading AI\-powered performance marketing platform for the mobile app economy. Our end\-to\-end technology stack helps app marketers acquire and retain high\-value users, while enabling publishers to maximize revenue across programmatic and direct demand.



Liftoff's solutions, including Accelerate, Direct, Monetize, Intelligence, and Vungle Exchange, support over 6,600 mobile businesses across 74 countries in sectors such as gaming, social, finance, ecommerce, and entertainment. Founded in 2012 and headquartered in Redwood City, CA, Liftoff has a diverse, global presence.


We're seeking a Director to lead Deal Desk within Liftoff's Strategic Finance team that reports to the VP of Strategic Finance. This is a high\-ownership role at the center of how Liftoff structures, approves, and manages commercial agreements, from standard arrangements to complex, non\-standard deals with strategic advertising partners. As the ultimate DRI for revenue adjustments, deal economics, and the integrity of Liftoff's commercial commitments, you will partner closely with GTM, Finance, and senior leadership to set deal strategy, manage active deal performance, and ensure every commercial arrangement is entered into with a clear, defensible financial rationale. If you have deep comfort with ambiguity, strong independent judgment, exceptional attention to detail, and the ability to lead cross\-functional processes with confidence, we want to hear from you!


**Key Responsibilities:**
-------------------------


* Serve as DRI for all revenue adjustments in weekly reporting: own the underlying logic, file integrity, and formula soundness.
* Maintain active reconciliation checks and ensure adjustments are accurate, complete, and explainable at any point in the week.
* Work proactively with cross\-functional partners throughout the week to incorporate new intel before weekly close.
* Lead weekly alignment meetings with the FP\&A team; own WoW variance explanation and post summaries to relevant stakeholders.
* Own all deal types end\-to\-end ranging from standard structures to complex, unique, and customer\-specific arrangements.
* Maintain and enforce the Deal Desk approval matrix; lead a bi\-annual Deal Desk Strategy Review with SLT.
* Own the philosophy and commercial logic underlying how Liftoff approaches deal structures, including eligibility thresholds and deal parameters by customer segment.
* For non\-standard deals: lead upfront diligence including detailed financial modeling.
* Lead weekly cross\-functional reviews on active non\-standard deals; make budget and commercial adjustment recommendations as needed.
* Produce monthly performance updates on active deal programs for senior leadership, with clear variance analysis against original assumptions.
* Monitor cash flows and financial commitments on structured deals; update models as actuals come in and flag deviations proactively.
* Own and lead accrual review for all key Deal Desk items, including complex arrangements.
* Hold a well\-supported, defensible position on accrual levels, with the underlying data and logic ready to present in senior Finance forums.
* This role includes direct management of a Senior Analyst, with responsibility for mentorship, prioritization, and maintaining high analytical standards across Deal Desk operations

**Qualifications:**
-------------------


* Bachelor's degree in Finance, Accounting, Economics, or a related field.
* 10\+ years of experience in commercial finance, deal desk, revenue operations, or strategic finance; at least 5 years with direct ownership over deal structuring or commercial agreements.
* Demonstrated ability to evaluate complex deal economics independently, build defensible financial models, and present clear recommendations to senior leadership.
* Strong understanding of revenue recognition, accrual accounting, and the operational mechanics of commercial deal management.
* Exceptional judgment: able to hold a position under commercial pressure while remaining collaborative and solutions\-oriented.
* Track record of true DRI ownership, including proactively surfacing risks, driving process, and escalating only when genuinely warranted.
* Excellent communicator with experience presenting to CXO\-level audiences.


**Nice to have:**


* Ad tech, programmatic advertising, or mobile experience


If you're passionate about driving commercial excellence, managing complex deal structures, and partnering with leadership to ensure sound financial decision\-making, we want to hear from you! Working at Liftoff is fast\-paced, fun, and challenging, and we thrive on innovation. Come join the rocket ship and help shape the future of the mobile app ecosystem with us!



**Location:**
-------------



Liftoff follows a philosophy of "remote first, come together meaningfully" and allows employees to be based anywhere in Canada. We require that this role work during Pacific time zone; working from the Vancouver area is highly preferred.


**Travel Expectations:** We offer several opportunities for in\-person team gatherings, including but not limited to project meetings, regional meetups, and company\-wide events. We expect our employees to attend these gatherings at least once per quarter. These gatherings provide essential opportunities for collaboration, communication, and team building.


**Compensation:**
-----------------



Liftoff offers all employees a full compensation package that includes equity and health/vision/dental benefits associated with your country of residence. Base compensation will vary based on the candidate's location and experience.



The following is the OTE (base \+ bonus) salary range for Canada: CAD 185,000 \- 230,000

  

Liftoff offers a fast\-paced, collaborative, and innovative work environment where employees are empowered to grow and make an impact. We're shaping the future of the mobile app ecosystem—join us and help accelerate what's next.

jobs.title: Director of Finance
jobs.description:
Join the Digital Health Revolution!

About Pillway

Pillway is Canada’s premier digital pharmacy, redefining patient care through technology, innovation, and relentless operational excellence. We simplify medication management with intelligent adherence tools, personalized care, and seamless nationwide delivery empowering patients and caregivers with a modern, connected healthcare experience.

We aren't just a pharmacy, we are a fast-scaling healthcare technology company driving the future of the industry. By revolutionizing patient care
through proprietary digital solutions, we deliver an unmatched, patient-first model. Join our high-impact team to directly shape the future of Canadian pharmacy services
!

Role Overview

Pillway is seeking an experienced data-driven and strategic Growth Hacker. This role is critical for analyzing post-sign-up behavior, identifying funnel leakages, and implementing re-engagement strategies to increase conversions and customer loyalty on our platform.

Pillway is seeking an experienced Director of Finance that will lead Pillway’s finance, accounting, FP&A, and data analytics functions, serving as a key financial and analytical partner to executive leadership. In this role, you will oversee the finance and accounting team to ensure the accuracy, timeliness, and integrity of all organizational financial information while building scalable processes, reporting capabilities, and robust internal controls.

Core Responsibilities

Champion Financial & Accounting Operations

Drive core accounting functions including AP, AR, general ledger, and close cycles ensuring pristine financial accuracy and integrity.
Maintain impeccable financial records across multiple corporate entities and lead consolidated reporting with rigor.
Optimize liquidity, capital allocation, and internal controls to protect and scale the company's financial health.
Spearhead process automation and operational enhancements to build a modern, high-efficiency finance department.

Elevate Financial Reporting & Audit Governance

Deliver seamless monthly, quarterly, and annual reporting packages for executive leadership, board members, and investors.
Serve as the primary liaison for external auditors and tax advisors, fostering complete audit-readiness and compliance.

Shape Strategic FP&A & Growth Planning

Lead annual budgeting, continuous rolling forecasts, and dynamic financial models that guide strategic direction.
Analyze performance trends, cost structures, and variances to unlock actionable insights and maximize profitability.
Evaluate new investments, key commercial agreements, and expansion opportunities to accelerate business growth.

Lead Data & Analytics Innovation

Direct the Data & Analytics team to build robust, company-wide business intelligence tools and interactive KPI dashboards.
Empower cross-functional leaders with data transparency and metrics that inform key operational choices.

Inspire Leadership & Continuous Improvement

Mentor, develop, and empower a top-tier team across finance, accounting, and analytics.
Foster cross-functional collaboration across operations, sales, marketing, and customer service to drive organizational excellence.

Required Qualifications

CPA designation strongly preferred.
7–10+ years of progressive finance and accounting experience, including people leadership.
Strong technical accounting foundation, including financial statements, reconciliations, and audit preparation.
Demonstrated experience managing accounting teams and overseeing financial operations.
Strong FP&A capabilities, including budgeting, forecasting, and financial modeling.
Strong working knowledge of Canadian accounting standards (ASPE or IFRS), including financial statement preparation, consolidated reporting, and external audit requirements
Advanced Excel skills and experience with financial/accounting systems.
Ability to interpret business data and communicate financial insights to senior leadership.
Experience in multi-entity or multi-location organizations preferred.
Experience with Power BI, Tableau, or similar business intelligence tools is considered an asset.
Healthcare, pharmacy, technology, or transaction-intensive business experience considered an asset.

Why Join the Pillway Team?

At Pillway, we are transforming pharmacy care across Canada through technology, innovation, and an unwavering commitment to patient-centric healthcare. As our Director of Finance, you will play a pivotal role in shaping our strategic trajectory, driving operational excellence, and scaling a high-impact financial organization.

Strategic Financial Leadership: Directly influence executive decision-making, capital allocation, and long-term expansion in a high-growth health-tech environment.
Competitive Compensation & Equity: Receive a highly market-competitive salary, comprehensive health coverage, and opportunities for long-term equity participation through our Employee Stock Option Plan.
Flexible Work Environment: Enjoy a workplace culture that values flexibility, collaboration, and maintaining strong engagement across corporate teams.
Innovation & Ownership: Build and scale modern finance, FP&A, and analytics operations, supported by an inclusive, mission-driven team committed to excellence.

Join us at Pillway for a chance to shape the future of digital healthcare, where your work impacts lives daily, and innovation meets inclusivity.

Our Commitment to You

Pillway supports a workforce of diverse backgrounds and encompasses policies and initiatives designed to help all employees feel welcomed and well-equipped to succeed. We are an inclusive employer and provide accommodations for applicants with disabilities throughout the recruitment process. Please let us know if you require accommodation.

Note: We appreciate every application we receive, but due to our overwhelming response, we will only be able to contact those who are under consideration for the position.

Disclosure:
We use AI tools to assist with screening and evaluating application

jobs.title: Lead AI Security Automation Engineer, VP
jobs.description:
Who We Are Looking For

State Street's Cyber Data & Analytics (CyberDNA) team is seeking a Lead AI Security Automation Engineer to shape the next generation of cybersecurity data, analytics, and AI-powered platforms. Partnering closely with Global Cyber Security teams, Infrastructure Teams, and Enterprise Continuity Services, this team develops advanced data platforms, intelligent automation solutions, and engineering capabilities that enable cybersecurity teams to make faster, AI-driven decisions and strengthen the firm's ability to detect, prevent, and respond to evolving cyber threats.

Why this role is important to us

Through innovation in AI, analytics, and automation, CyberDNA team plays a critical role in protecting State Street, its clients, and its partners from increasingly sophisticated global threat actors. As cybersecurity operations increasingly rely on AI, automation, and data-driven decision-making, this role will lead the development of the foundational platforms and capabilities that enable intelligent security operations at enterprise scale. This role sits at the intersection of Artificial Intelligence, Cybersecurity, Data Engineering, and Full-Stack Software Development, with a primary focus on enabling secure, scalable, and governed AI adoption across the enterprise for supporting Cyber Security functions. The successful candidate will establish and lead a team of AI engineers focused on delivering next-generation AI platforms, autonomous agents, security automation solutions, and data-driven applications that strengthen cyber resilience, accelerate innovation, and transform cybersecurity operations through intelligent automation.

What You Will Be Responsible For

As the Lead AI Security Automation Engineer, you will

Build, lead, and mentor a high-performing team of AI Automation Engineers focused on advancing cybersecurity operations through automation and AI-driven innovation.
Lead the architecture and hands-on delivery of scalable, reliable agentic AI platforms for security workflows
Design and build production-grade AI systems including agents, skills, memory patterns, guardrails, and tool-use orchestration
Architect retrieval and context-engineering approaches including embeddings, semantic search, grounding, summarization, and prompt/version management
Engineer cloud-native AI solutions in AWS, Azure and GCP using containers and serverless patterns, event-driven messaging, and distributed data stores
Optimize platform performance across latency, throughput, scalability, caching, context efficiency, and cost controls
Build well-governed APIs and integrations that connect AI capabilities to security platforms, tools, and business processes
Establish evaluation, research, regression testing, and observability frameworks to continuously improve quality and agent behavior
Define engineering standards for reliability, security, and safe AI operation across the platform lifecycle
Mentor senior & junior engineers and influence engineering direction through code reviews, architecture forums, and cross-team technical leadership
Leverages enterprise-authorized AI coding assist tools within the work environment to improve code quality, delivery speed, and productivity across complex deliverables (e.g., code generation/refactoring, unit test creation, documentation), while validating outputs through peer review, automated testing, and secure coding standards; contributes learnings and reusable patterns to improve broader team effectiveness.
Applies knowledge of tools within the Software Development Life Cycle toolchain, including enterprise-authorized AI-assisted development and automation capabilities, to improve the value realized by automation.

What We Value

These skills will help you succeed in this role

Demonstrated experience architecting, developing, and deploying production-grade Generative AI and Large Language Model (LLM) based solutions, including agentic workflows, intelligent agents, and enterprise tool integration frameworks.
Strong software engineering fundamentals with expertise in designing and delivering cloud-native applications and services leveraging containers, serverless architectures, and modern public cloud platforms.
Proven experience building highly scalable distributed systems utilizing asynchronous processing, event-driven architectures, durable messaging, and high-performance data access patterns.
Hands-on expertise developing Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) solutions, including embeddings, semantic search, knowledge grounding, context engineering, prompt optimization, and prompt lifecycle management.
Experience implementing AI evaluation, testing, monitoring, and observability frameworks to measure model quality, reliability, performance, and safe operation in production environments.
Strong API design and integration experience, including the development of secure, reusable, and scalable platform services that enable enterprise-wide adoption of AI capabilities.
Demonstrated technical leadership skills with a track record of mentoring engineers, driving architectural decisions, influencing technology strategy, and collaborating effectively with cross-functional stakeholders.
Hands-on experience utilizing enterprise-approved AI-assisted software development tools to accelerate application delivery, improve code quality, streamline testing, and enhance documentation, while ensuring outputs are validated through secure coding practices, peer review, and automated testing.
Strong understanding of responsible AI principles, including data privacy, security, governance, resiliency, and risk management, with the ability to guide teams in the safe and effective use of AI technologies.
Deep understanding of cybersecurity functions to support threat detection engineering, threat hunting, offensive/defensive security, Threat intelligence and SOC operations.
Strong understanding of cybersecurity operations, including threat detection, incident response, threat hunting, security analytics, and security automation.
Proven ability to lead and influence geographically distributed teams through virtual collaboration, fostering strong partnerships, driving technical outcomes, and building effective relationships across engineering, security, and business organizations.
Deep understanding of CI/CD tools (Jenkins, Harness, Spinnaker, Argo CD, etc.) and methodology, production experience in designing and implementing CI/CD pipelines with a focus on helping teams release frequently to production while maintaining deployment reliability
Strong software development and automation skills with demonstrated experience in Python, JavaScript/TypeScript, Rust, Go (Golang), Bash, and PowerShell.
Proven ability to lead complex technical initiatives while remaining deeply hands-on.
LangGraph, Semantic Kernel, CrewAI, AutoGen, LangChain, or similar frameworks.
Databricks, Snowflake, Spark, Kafka, Delta Lake, Iceberg, and Airflow.
Experience with vector databases, semantic search, and enterprise RAG platforms.
Experience implementing MLOps, LLMOps, AI observability, and evaluation frameworks.
Knowledge of Responsible AI, data governance, and model risk management.

Education & Preferred Qualifications

Master's degree in Computer Science, Software Engineering, Artificial Intelligence, Data Science, Cybersecurity, or a related discipline.
10+ years of professional software engineering experience.
4+ years of experience developing AI, Machine Learning, or Generative AI solutions.
Demonstrated success designing and deploying enterprise-scale applications and platforms.
Experience developing cybersecurity, analytics, or operational intelligence solutions.

Work Requirement

Work shift is 8 AM – 5 PM local time with occasional Level 3 escalation resolution to support operational incidents
This hybrid role includes an in-office presence requirement of 2–4 days per week, consistent with the organization's hybrid work policy.

Salary Range

$120,000 - $217,500 Annual

We are committed to fostering an environment where every employee feels valued and empowered to reach their full potential. jobs.title: Responsable de l’expérience numérique / Digital Experience Leader, Customer Support
jobs.description:
At OneSpan, we specialize in digital identity and anti-fraud solutions that create exceptional and secure experiences.

Le ou la Responsable de l’expérience numérique
est chargé(e) de transformer le service de soutien à la clientèle de OneSpan en une expérience de soutien axée d’abord sur le numérique et propulsée par l’intelligence artificielle
. Ce rôle consiste à identifier et à mettre en œuvre des cas d’usage où les clients peuvent demander et obtenir de l’aide par l’intermédiaire de canaux numériques, notamment le portail de soutien client, les agents conversationnels (chatbots) et assistants virtuels, l’IA agentique, la recherche alimentée par l’IA, les formulaires structurés, l’automatisation des flux de travail, les capacités de libre-service ainsi que les améliorations apportées aux produits, avec peu ou pas d’intervention d’un agent du soutien à la clientèle de OneSpan.

La principale mesure de réussite consiste à atteindre un taux de résolution numérique de 60 % pour les demandes admissibles des clients non premium
, permettant ainsi à l’organisation du soutien à la clientèle de consacrer davantage de capacité aux interventions premium, complexes et à forte valeur ajoutée.

Un soutien à la clientèle de calibre mondial

Le soutien à la clientèle de OneSpan s’engage à contribuer au succès de ses clients grâce à un service rapide, compétent, courtois et réactif. Ce poste prolonge cette mission en modernisant la manière dont les clients reçoivent de l’assistance : en améliorant le libre-service, en réduisant les frictions, en accélérant la résolution des demandes et en assurant un transfert fluide vers un agent humain lorsque la résolution numérique n’est pas appropriée.

Principales responsabilités

Définir et piloter la feuille de route de la transformation numérique du soutien, couvrant le portail client, la recherche IA, les agents conversationnels et assistants virtuels, les formulaires structurés, l’automatisation des flux de travail, l’IA agentique, la gestion des connaissances, la documentation et les fonctionnalités de libre-service intégrées aux produits.
Identifier les types de demandes récurrentes et à fort volume pouvant être prévenus, automatisés, résolus en libre-service, améliorés grâce à la documentation ou éliminés par des améliorations produit.
Diriger la feuille de route nécessaire pour atteindre un taux de résolution numérique de 60 % des demandes admissibles non premium, tout en maintenant une expérience de soutien premium de grande qualité.
Collaborer étroitement avec les équipes de gestion de produit, d’ingénierie, des TI, les responsables de plateformes comme ServiceNow, les équipes de gestion des connaissances et de la documentation, les opérations de soutien, le succès client et les équipes de soutien de première ligne.
Assurer la coordination des initiatives selon les pratiques BPM et PMO, notamment la cartographie des processus, la planification des initiatives, l’élaboration de dossiers d’affaires, le suivi des dépendances, l’alignement des parties prenantes, la planification de l’adoption et la production de rapports destinés à la direction.
Améliorer les processus de collecte structurée des demandes, de triage, de classification, d’acheminement, de recommandations de résolution, de gestion des SLA et des escalades, ainsi que l’expérience des agents.
Mettre en place des tableaux de bord de performance pour suivre la résolution numérique, le taux de confinement, l’adoption du libre-service, la qualité de l’IA et de l’automatisation, la déviation des cas, l’expérience client et l’efficacité du soutien.
Veiller à ce que les solutions d’IA et d’automatisation soient déployées avec une gouvernance appropriée, des mécanismes de transfert vers l’humain, la protection des données clients, la transparence et une surveillance continue.
Transformer les apprentissages tirés du soutien à la clientèle en améliorations des produits, des processus, du portail, de la documentation et de la base de connaissances.

Objectifs et indicateurs de performance (KPI)

Atteindre un taux de résolution numérique de 60 % pour les demandes de soutien admissibles des clients non premium.
Accroître l’utilisation des canaux de soutien numériques, de la recherche alimentée par l’IA, du libre-service, des formulaires structurés et des flux de travail automatisés.
Réduire le volume de demandes répétitives non premium devant être traitées par les agents.
Améliorer l’effort client, la rapidité de résolution, l’efficacité opérationnelle et la cohérence du parcours de soutien.
Augmenter la capacité du soutien à la clientèle pour les interactions premium et les dossiers complexes.
Améliorer la qualité et l’actualité des connaissances, de la documentation et du contenu prêt pour l’IA.
Réaliser des améliorations mesurables aux processus, aux outils, aux produits et au portail client.

Exigences

Transformation numérique du soutien à la clientèle

Expérience démontrée dans la transformation des organisations de soutien à la clientèle grâce au libre-service, à l’automatisation, à l’intelligence artificielle et aux canaux numériques, avec des résultats mesurables en matière d’expérience client, d’efficacité opérationnelle et de capacité d’expansion du soutien.

Stratégie d’IA, d’automatisation et de libre-service

Expérience dans l’identification, la priorisation et la mise en œuvre de capacités de soutien alimentées par l’IA, de solutions d’automatisation des flux de travail, d’agents conversationnels et d’assistants virtuels, de libre-service fondé sur les connaissances et de parcours clients numériques.

Gestion des processus d’affaires (BPM) et livraison de programmes

Solides compétences en amélioration de processus et en gestion de programme (PMO), incluant la cartographie des processus, l’élaboration de dossiers d’affaires, la gestion de feuilles de route, l’alignement des parties prenantes, la gestion des dépendances et l’exécution d’initiatives de transformation interfonctionnelles.

Leadership transversal et influence

Capacité éprouvée à diriger des initiatives touchant le soutien à la clientèle, la gestion de produit, l’ingénierie, les TI, le succès client et les opérations, sans autorité hiérarchique directe, en favorisant l’alignement et l’atteinte des résultats d’affaires.

Prise de décision fondée sur les données

Excellentes compétences analytiques et expérience dans la définition et la gestion d’indicateurs de performance, ainsi que dans l’utilisation des données clients et opérationnelles pour identifier des occasions d’amélioration, mesurer l’adoption et favoriser l’optimisation continue.

Qualifications Souhaitées (atouts)

Expertise des plateformes de gestion des services

Expérience pratique avec ServiceNow, Salesforce Service Cloud, Zendesk, Jira, Confluence, Gainsight ou des plateformes comparables de soutien à la clientèle et d’automatisation des flux de travail.

Expérience dans les secteurs SaaS, cybersécurité ou fintech

Expérience dans des environnements technologiques réglementés tels que les logiciels SaaS B2B, la cybersécurité, l’identité numérique, l’authentification, les technologies financières (fintech) ou des domaines connexes.

Gestion des connaissances et recherche alimentée par l’IA

Expérience dans la mise en œuvre de programmes de gestion des connaissances, de solutions de recherche alimentées par l’IA, d’architectures basées sur la génération augmentée par récupération (RAG), de stratégies de documentation ou de méthodologies Knowledge-Centered Service (KCS).

Gouvernance de l’IA et IA responsable

Expérience dans l’établissement de cadres de gouvernance pour le soutien client assisté par l’IA, incluant le suivi de la qualité, les processus avec intervention humaine, la gestion des risques, la protection de la vie privée et la conformité.

Expérience en leadership

Expérience préalable dans la création, la direction ou le développement d’équipes hautement performantes au sein du soutien à la clientèle, de l’expérience client, de la transformation numérique, des opérations de soutien ou des opérations produit.

Certifications professionnelles

Certifications pertinentes telles que PMP, Agile/Scrum, Lean Six Sigma, ITIL, KCS, COPC, CCXP ou certifications liées à la gestion des processus d’affaires (BPM).

. Convert support insights into product, process, portal, documentation, and knowledgebase improvements.

Objectives / KPI’s

Increase use of digital support channels, AI search, self-service, structured intake, and automated workflows.
Reduce avoidable agent-handled volume for repeatable non-premium requests.
Improve customer effort, resolution speed, efficiency, and support journey consistency.
Increase Customer Support capacity for premium and complex customer engagements.
Improve quality and freshness of knowledge, documentation, and AI-ready content.
Deliver measurable process, tooling, product, and portal improvements.

Elections Manitoba (EM) is an integrity-driven organization dedicated to ensuring free, fair, and accessible elections for the people of Manitoba. As an independent office of the Manitoba Legislative Assembly, EM is steadfast in upholding the core values of democracy. The team at EM is committed to fairness, integrity, respect, excellence, participation, innovation, and accountability, striving to create an environment where every voice is heard and every vote counts.

The Opportunity

As Director, you will balance day-to-day operations with strategic oversight across the various administrative and corporate functions for Elections Manitoba as well as ensuring campaign finance is conducted as mandated in The Election Financing Act (EFA) . The position provides oversight of innovative and flexible solutions, processes, practices to manage and implement financial and administrative services, campaign review programs, information sharing, approval of and development of legislative requirements for different stakeholders, and internal controls for the cost-effective delivery of corporate and electoral events.

jobs.title: Director of Finance and Administration
jobs.description:
Lead financial and corporate stewardship for Curve Lake First Nation

Step into a senior leadership role offering a competitive $150,000 to $180,000 annual salary, negotiable based on qualifications, plus excellent benefits!

Build the systems, teams, and financial stability that will support the Nation for the next decade

About Curve Lake First Nation

Curve Lake First Nation is an Anishinaabe community with deep roots in this territory, grounded in relationships to land, water, and each other as Curve Lakers. Known historically as Mud Lake, Curve Lake continues as a living, resilient Nation of almost 3,000 members. As part of the Michi Saagiig Anishinaabeg and signatories to the Williams Treaties, the community carries forward its responsibilities, teachings, and governance systems. Curve Lake is a place of strong kinship, cultural continuity, and collective responsibility, where each member contributes to the wellbeing of the Nation. Our community is located just north of the City of Peterborough, Ontario.

Home to trailblazers like Elsie Knott, Canada's first Anishinaabe Kwe O'gimaa, and renowned artisans, our community blends rich history with vibrant culture. More than an employer, we're a community of choice. Join us in preserving traditions, fostering diversity, and contributing to a future where old ways merge seamlessly with progress. Shape the legacy of Curve Lake—a place where heritage meets opportunity.

To learn more about us, please visit: curvelakefirstnation.ca

About the Opportunity

Curve Lake First Nation has an exciting opportunity for a full-time, permanent Director of Finance and Administration
, based in Curve Lake, Ontario.
This role joins the organization during a period of organizational transition and growth.

Reporting to the Executive Director, you will provide strategic leadership across the Nation’s corporate functions. These are financial governance, human resources, policy and planning, communications, and information technology. Finance sits at the heart of the role. You will be accountable for sound financial oversight, audit readiness, and strong relationships with funders, auditors, and the First Nations Financial Management Board.

Where We Are Now

The Nation is strengthening its administrative foundations; you will provide interim oversight and stabilization across Finance, HR, IT, and Policy and Planning while building out your team. You will also lead the selection and implementation of a new Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP) system.

A key priority is moving the Nation from year-by-year funding to Indigenous Services Canada’s 10-year grant. This means completing the Financial Management Board certification process and putting the controls and reporting in place to qualify. Predictable, long-term funding will give the Nation far greater confidence in its forecasting and planning.

What Success Looks Like

In your first year, success will mean a fully staffed division with your managers in place, trusted relationships with Chief and Council, staff, and community, strengthened audit readiness and internal controls, and the ERP selection well underway.

By the end of year two, you will have led the Nation through FMB certification and embedded consistent financial, governance, and administrative practices. You will also have put systems in place that keep reporting and audits on schedule, giving the organization a solid foundation for the years ahead.

Your responsibilities include, but are not limited to:
Leading multi-year financial planning, forecasting, and annual operating and capital budgets
Serving as executive lead for external audits, including selecting the appropriate audit firm and working closely with auditors throughout the process
Ensuring compliance with funding agreements, Indigenous Services Canada reporting requirements, and the Nation’s Financial Administration Law
Leading the Nation through the FMB certification and 10-year grant process
Structuring and staffing the finance function so reporting deadlines are consistently met, working with bookkeepers, analysts, and account managers
Providing executive oversight of HR, IT, policy and planning, and communications through four direct-report managers
Overseeing the selection and implementation of an ERP system, along with cybersecurity, data governance, and digital modernization
Providing financial analysis, risk advice, and recommendations to the Executive Director and Chief and Council

Due to the role's significance, refer to the Director of Finance and Administration document for a comprehensive overview beyond the listed duties.

More About You

To qualify, you will need a post-secondary degree or diploma in finance, accounting, or a related financial field
, along with at least 5 years of senior-level experience in financial administration or corporate services,
including experience working within a First Nation organization.

The following are required:
A valid Class G Driver’s Licence
Ability to undergo a criminal background check and vulnerable sector check
Willingness and ability to travel as required

The following skills and experience will be strong assets:
Chartered Professional Accountant (CPA) designation
Certified Aboriginal Financial Manager (CAFM) or Certified Aboriginal Professional Administrator (CAPA) designation
A master’s degree in public administration, finance, or a related field
Direct experience with the First Nations Financial Management Board, FMB certification, or the 10-year grant process
Strong working knowledge of audit processes, GAAP, and funder reporting requirements
Experience working with Indigenous Services Canada and other funding agencies
Experience overseeing multiple functional areas such as Finance, HR, IT, and Planning

As our ideal candidate, you are a disciplined, systems-minded leader who keeps deadlines met and audits clean, and who knows how to build a finance team organized around its reporting obligations. Your understanding of First Nation finances runs from day-to-day funding agreements through to the path toward long-term grant funding. Just as importantly, you lead with integrity, calm, and a people-centred approach, bringing an awareness of intergenerational trauma and its impact on workplaces and governance, along with a genuine respect for Curve Lake First Nation’s history, culture, and traditions.

Note: Preference will be given to applicants who have First Nation or Indigenous ancestry.

About the Benefits

In exchange for your hard work and dedication, you will receive a highly competitive salary of $150,000 to $180,000
negotiable dependent on experience, along with a great host of benefits, including:
Relocation assistance
Comprehensive Benefits Plan: extended health care, dental, vision, life and long-term disability, etc.
Competitive Pension Plan with up to 7.5% employer matching
40 paid hours for Special/Personal Leave Bereavement Leave
Paid time off for 17 designated days, including National Indigenous Day, Christmas Day, etc.
Generous vacation accrual
Paid sick days
Regular community events such as Pow Wows, Harvesters' Gatherings, Christmas Craft Shows, and more!

Take on a senior leadership role that builds lasting financial stability and strong systems for the Curve Lake First Nation community. Apply now!

jobs.title: Director of Information Technology
jobs.description:
CarltonOne is a global B2B technology leader, and part of the Goldman Sachs portfolio, helping organizations around the world reward and inspire exceptional people. Our solutions empower employees to be more productive, sales teams to perform at their best, and customers to stay engaged and loyal.

Our platform powers the global engagement industry, enabling companies to deliver impactful employee recognition, customer loyalty, rewards, sales, and channel incentive programs. We partner with over 450 clients
, 500 vendors
, and serve 14 million members
across 185 countries
.

Beyond engagement, every CarltonOne solution drives our eco-action mission: funding tree planting to help restore the planet. To date, we’ve funded over 21 million trees
and are on track to plant millions more each year. Learn more at carltonone.com .

About the Opportunity:

CarltonOne is seeking a highly motivated Director, Information Technology to lead CarltonOne's global enterprise IT function, owning IT strategy, service management, governance, and employee technology experience.

This role is responsible for delivering a best-in-class employee technology experience across the organization, ensuring employees have the tools, systems, support, and infrastructure they need to be productive and successful. The Director, IT will lead internal IT support, service delivery, endpoint management, identity and access management, collaboration tools, workplace technology initiatives, and global hardware operations across CarltonOne's international workforce.

This is a strategic leadership role. The Director, IT is accountable for the outcomes of IT service delivery rather than working the support queue, leading through managers, team leads, and managed service partners who handle Level 1 and Level 2 support. The Director serves as the senior escalation point and leader during major IT and security incidents, and focuses on strengthening process, governance, and measurement to deliver an exceptional, proactive employee experience. The successful candidate will focus on improving service levels, modernizing IT processes, strengthening security practices, and scaling internal technology operations to support a growing global organization.

Responsibilities:

IT Service Management & Incident Leadership

Own CarltonOne's global IT operating model, including service desk structure, tiered support (L1/L2/L3), escalation paths, and the balance of in-house and managed service provider (MSP) coverage.
Hold the service desk and support partners accountable for timely, high-quality resolution of employee requests and issues, without personally working day-to-day L1/L2 tickets.
Define and publish SLAs, experience level agreements (XLAs), and an IT performance scorecard covering CSAT, first-contact resolution, mean time to resolve, SLA attainment, backlog age, and reopen rates, reported monthly to executive leadership.
Run a continuous improvement program driven by ticket trend analysis, employee feedback, and experience data, with the goal of reducing ticket volume per employee year over year.
Ensure consistent delivery of IT services across all regions and time zones.
Act as Major Incident Manager and senior escalation point for high-impact IT outages, leading coordinated response, stakeholder communications, and service restoration.
Partner with Information Security to support the response to security incidents, including containment of affected accounts and devices, evidence preservation, and executive communication, in line with the incident response plan.
Implement a problem management practice that uses root cause analysis and post-incident reviews to eliminate recurring issues, with tracked corrective actions.
Establish change, release, and configuration management processes that reduce change-related incidents and protect service stability.
Own Jira Service Management as the IT service management platform, driving workflow design, automation, SLA tracking, and reporting.
Partner with SaaS production, engineering, and DevOps teams to align IT processes such as access, change, and incident management with production operations, and provide the internal tools and access they need.
Own the IT service management (ITSM) platform roadmap, service catalogue, and knowledge base, aligned to ITIL 4 practices.

Employee Technology Experience

Develop and enhance the overall employee technology experience across the organization.
Ensure employees have access to reliable hardware, software, collaboration tools, and support resources regardless of location.
Partner with business leaders to understand technology needs and improve workplace productivity.
Evaluate and implement technologies that improve employee efficiency, collaboration, and engagement.
Champion self-service support resources, knowledge management programs, and technology adoption initiatives.
Shift IT from reactive to proactive by using monitoring, digital employee experience (DEX) tooling, and endpoint analytics to detect and resolve issues before employees are affected.
Measure employee technology sentiment through regular surveys and an IT Net Promoter Score, and act on the results with visible follow-through.
Promote a shift-left approach that moves common requests to self-service and automation, freeing the team for higher-value work.
Create seamless onboarding and offboarding experiences through standardized technology processes.

Global Hardware & Employee Technology Management

Own CarltonOne's global hardware procurement, deployment, lifecycle management, and asset governance strategy.
Develop and manage scalable processes for onboarding and offboarding employees across Canada, the United States, Brazil, the United Kingdom, Australia, and other international locations.
Partner with global vendors, distributors, and logistics providers to ensure timely delivery, replacement, retrieval, and support of employee equipment worldwide.
Establish global standards for laptops, peripherals, mobile devices, and collaboration technology to provide a consistent employee experience.
Oversee hardware inventory management, asset tracking, auditing, and recovery programs across all regions.
Manage relationships with international hardware partners and service providers to optimize cost, service levels, and operational efficiency.
Develop regional technology deployment strategies that account for customs requirements, shipping timelines, local regulations, and business needs.
Ensure all employee devices are properly configured, secured, encrypted, and compliant with company security standards prior to deployment.
Partner with Information Security teams to maintain endpoint management, device compliance, and security controls globally.
Lead technology refresh programs and lifecycle planning to ensure employees have access to modern and reliable equipment.
Establish reporting and KPIs related to deployment timelines, inventory accuracy, hardware utilization, asset recovery, and employee satisfaction.

IT Leadership & Talent

Build, lead, and develop a global IT organization, including people managers, team leads, and specialists, and manage MSP and outsourced support partners.
Establish team goals, performance expectations, and professional development plans.
Foster a customer-first service culture focused on responsiveness, accountability, and problem resolution.
Design staffing models, global coverage, escalation processes, and on-call rotations so that routine support across all time zones is delivered by the team and its partners.
Promote knowledge sharing, process consistency, and operational excellence across the team.
Build a high-performing IT organization capable of supporting a rapidly growing global workforce.

Infrastructure & Workplace Technology

Oversee the management of employee technology including laptops, mobile devices, conference room systems, printers, and collaboration tools.
Ensure reliable operation of corporate productivity platforms including Microsoft 365, communication platforms, and workplace technologies.
Support office technology infrastructure across multiple global locations.
Own software licensing and SaaS governance, including licence optimization, application rationalization, and shadow IT controls.
Identify opportunities to modernize and standardize workplace technology solutions.

Identity, Access Management & IT Security

Oversee user provisioning, deprovisioning, and identity and access management processes.
Partner closely with Information Security teams to maintain secure access controls and endpoint security standards.
Support security awareness initiatives and IT compliance requirements.
Ensure adherence to IT policies, security best practices, and governance standards.
Participate in internal and external audits related to IT operations and controls.
Help strengthen the company's security posture through proactive management of employee technology and access controls.

Vendor & Technology Management

Manage relationships with IT vendors, service providers, telecommunications partners, and technology suppliers.
Negotiate contracts, licensing agreements, and support arrangements.
Evaluate technology investments and recommend solutions that align with business requirements and budgets.
Monitor vendor performance and ensure service commitments are achieved.
Identify opportunities to consolidate vendors and improve operational efficiency.

Project & Program Leadership

Lead enterprise IT projects from planning through implementation and ongoing support.
Support technology rollouts, infrastructure upgrades, collaboration platform enhancements, and automation initiatives.
Partner with HR, Finance, Security, Operations, and Technology teams on cross-functional projects.
Develop project plans, budgets, timelines, resource requirements, and success metrics.
Drive automation and process improvement initiatives that increase productivity and reduce manual effort.

IT Strategy, Governance, Risk & Business Continuity

Develop and own a multi-year IT strategy and roadmap aligned to CarltonOne's business objectives and growth plans.
Own the IT operating and capital budget, with clear reporting on spend, cost per employee, and return on technology investments, including the cost, utilization, and value of software, SaaS, and AI tools.
Manage IT expenses through SAP Concur, ensuring policy compliance, accurate cost allocation, and timely financial reporting.
Establish and maintain IT operational policies, standards, and governance frameworks.
Chair IT governance forums, such as a change advisory board and a technology steering committee, to prioritize demand and investment.
Ensure compliance with corporate requirements, security policies, and audit standards, including ownership of IT general controls (ITGCs) and implementation and continuous compliance with the NIST Cybersecurity Framework, CIS Critical Security Controls, and SOC 2, including audit readiness, evidence collection, and remediation of findings.
Maintain accurate documentation of systems, assets, processes, and support procedures.
Own disaster recovery planning and regular testing for internal systems and employee technologies, and partner with the business on continuity planning.
Maintain an IT risk register, report key risks to leadership, and own mitigation plans through to closure.

Qualifications:

10+ years of progressive IT experience, including 5+ years in IT leadership, with experience managing managers and/or managed service partners.

Experience leading internal IT operations, service desk, workplace technology, or enterprise support teams.
Experience leading internal IT within a SaaS company, including supporting SaaS production, engineering, and DevOps teams with access management, tooling, change coordination, and incident collaboration.
Strong knowledge of Microsoft 365, Entra ID (Azure AD), endpoint management, collaboration platforms, and modern workplace tec

jobs.title: Canada Impact+ Emerging Leader in AI-integrated Biomedical Devices
jobs.description:
The Faculty of Engineering and Computer Science at the University of Victoria seeks to recruit a world-class junior faculty member for a Canada Impact+ Emerging Leader position in AI-integrated Biomedical Sensors, Diagnostics, and/or Medical Imaging. If awarded, this is a tenure-track position at the Assistant Professor level, to commence July 1, 2027. This position is for candidates working in alignment with the Federal Strategic Priority of “health and biotechnology.”

The Canada Impact+ Emerging Leaders program is a $120 million investment to help institutions bring more internationally based early career researchers (ECR) to Canada. This program is administered by the Tri-agency Institutional Programs Secretariat (TIPS). The Canada Impact+ Emerging Leader position is associated with an Eddie Goldenberg Research Chair and is valued at $100,000 per year over six years. A possible extension is available for six additional years at the same yearly amount and will be contingent on confirming that the recruited ECR has progressed in their academic career and demonstrates the research conducted since the recruitment has been transformational, translational and has garnered partners. 

Canada Impact+ Emerging Leaders awards are intended for exceptional early career researchers (ECR). Candidates must be within five years (minus eligible delays) of the start date of their first research-related appointment, defined as an appointment where the individual has the autonomy to conduct research independently. All eligible delays in research (e.g., maternity, parental, medical, bereavement) are credited as twice the amount of time taken. Professional leaves (e.g., training, sabbatical, administrative) are not credited as eligible leaves. Only candidates who are internationally based (both working and residing outside of Canada) as of July 28, 2026, are eligible. Applicants must state in their cover letter that they meet the criteria for an ECR and that they were based outside of Canada as of July 28, 2026.

The candidate’s qualifications, experience, overall market demand and rank will determine a final salary offer. Industry experience is an asset. The salary for this position includes a competitive salary range of $120,000 - $150,000. UVic is committed to offering an equitable and competitive salary, inclusive of a generous benefits package, eligible leaves and pension plan.

Requirements

The ideal applicant will have a strong foundation in next-generation devices or imaging methods that take advantage of recent advances in data science, machine learning, and artificial intelligence. This faculty member will join a vibrant, growing community of biomedical engineering researchers at the University of Victoria. This role offers the opportunity to move beyond traditional design and directly integrate cutting-edge artificial intelligence algorithms into complex real-world medical practice.
The successful candidate is expected to demonstrate deep expertise in one or more areas related to next-generation devices and approaches, with the expressed goal of improving patient outcomes at scale, improving equity of access to healthcare, and delivering cost savings to the public. Possible application areas include, but are not limited to the following:
AI-based sensors and wearable devices for remote, secure, and respectful monitoring of patient data and health in Indigenous and other underserved communities.
AI- and ML-based methods for image processing and medical imaging via X-ray, MRI, ultrasound, spectroscopy, or other modalities.

The successful applicant will:
be appointed to the Department of Mechanical Engineering and/or Electrical and Computer Engineering at the rank of Assistant Professor;
contribute to the design and delivery of course-based curricula for the Biomedical Engineering students at the undergraduate and graduate levels; and
interact with other relevant members of the scholarly community at UVic, within and outside the Faculty of Engineering and Computer Science.

The successful applicant will:
hold (or be on the verge of completing) a Ph.D. in biomedical engineering or a relevant engineering discipline;
be a registered professional engineer in Canada, or be eligible to apply for registration with the Engineers and Geoscientists of British Columbia (details available at www.egbc.ca);
have clear ideas and aspirations to contribute to the Biomedical Engineering Program’s drive to increase the diversity of our student population and foster a supportive and inclusive environment for all;
possess excellent communication skills with an ability to communicate research vision, methods, rationale and impacts across a diverse array of audiences; and
demonstrate a strong commitment to excellence in undergraduate and graduate engineering education as evidenced by:
potential for excellence in teaching courses related to the Biomedical Engineering discipline, and,
an inclusive approach to mentoring and supervising diverse students both in classroom and in research environments.

Please note that the requirement for the candidate to hold or be near completion of a Ph.D. is a requirement of the University of Victoria and not the Impact+ Program.

Additional information
The University acknowledges that career interruptions and slowdowns may affect a candidate’s record of research achievement and, when applicable, encourages applicants to describe these impacts in their application. Life circumstances such as illness, disability, family and community responsibilities (including parental leave, caregiving responsibilities, illness-related leave, chronic illness or disability, and COVID-19-related disruptions) are a normal part of life and may influence a nominee’s research record. These circumstances will be carefully considered during the assessment process. Overview

Overview

Are you curious and deeply passionate about technology and sales, and ready to tackle complex challenges in a dynamic environment in the era of AI? Are you passionate about empowering financial sector customers to achieve more with technology and help them succeed in their digital transformation?If so, we invite you to join our Canadian team as a Solution Sales Director for Cloud & AI
at Microsoft. In this role, you will be at the forefront of innovation, working on cutting‑edge projects that leverage the latest cloud and AI technologies to drive meaningful impact for citizens and a variety of industries. Join us and be part of a team that thrives on collaboration, creativity, and continuous learning. Microsoft believes that our Canadian organizations have a unique opportunity to transform society at scale. From central government and agencies to local authorities, healthcare institutions and education, these organizations are reinventing how they deliver secure, trusted and efficient services to citizens. With Microsoft Cloud, we aspire to empower every finance sector organization to innovate and modernize on our platform, while meeting the highest standards of security, compliance and digital sovereignty.

Responsibilities

Customer Engagement & Deal Execution

Lead the sales team responsible for driving Cloud & AI revenue across accounts, ensuring disciplined execution of the end‑to‑end sales cycle (prospection → qualification → deal shaping → closing).
Ensure teams adhere to Microsoft sales methodologies (including AI‑enhanced sales frameworks) to qualify opportunities, accelerate deal velocity and improve win rates.
Orchestrate complex deal cycles involving procurement, multi‑stakeholder governance, and compliance constraints typical of the French Financial Sector.
Coach sellers on how to engage, influence and secure executive alignment with C‑level decision makers (CEO, CIO, CTO/CDO, Business Line Leaders) to land Microsoft Cloud value propositions.
Drive competitive positioning, ensuring the team can clearly articulate differentiators against hyperscalers and specialized competitors.

Sales Leadership & People Management

Microsoft managers deliver success through empowerment and accountability by Modeling, Coaching and Caring
:

Model: Embody Microsoft leadership principles, customer obsession, integrity, and inclusiveness.
Coach: Set clear revenue targets and performance expectations, support deal strategy, help sellers adapt, learn and improve continuously.
Care: Attract, develop, and retain great sales talent; understand individual motivations; and support team members’ career growth.

Concrete Expectations

Build a strong, high‑performing sales culture: discipline in forecasting, usage of tools (MSX, CRM), robust pipeline management.
Establish a consistent coaching rhythm (1:1s, forecast reviews, opportunity strategy sessions, joint customer engagements).
Help sellers strengthen their executive communication skills—ensuring compelling, outcome‑focused conversations with Finance Sector leaders.

Sales Strategy & Pipeline Management

Own Cloud & AI revenue results for the territory: pipeline health, forecasting accuracy, bookings, consumption growth, and renewal performance.
Guide teams in building and maintaining high-quality pipelines with sufficient coverage, leveraging data (propensity, consumption trends, renewal risk, competitive signals) to prioritize and optimize effort.

Collaborate with Customer Success, Marketing, Partner teams and industry specialists to maximize impact, support strategic engagements, and ensure value realization for customers.
Foster strong collaboration with the partner ecosystem (GSIs, local integrators, software vendors, start‑ups) to drive differentiated, customer‑aligned solutions.
Ensure storytelling, customer references, and ecosystem success stories are captured and shared to fuel future wins.

Required Qualifications:

Bachelor's Degree in Computer Science, Information Technology, Business Administration, Information Security, or related field AND 8+ years experience in technology-related sales or account management OR equivalent experience.

Preferred Qualifications

Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Business, Economics, Management, Engineering, or any relevant field — OR equivalent practical experience.
Experience in complex enterprise sales, ideally in cloud, software, digital transformation, or technology markets.
Experience leading sales teams, including field sellers and/or virtual teams in competitive, high‑stakes environments.
Demonstrated experience selling to regulated industries, with strong understanding of procurement cycles, governance, and compliance requirements.
Proven ability to manage large opportunities and multi‑million‑euro deal cycles involving multiple stakeholders.
Executive presence and communication skills; ability to simplify complex value propositions and engage Finance Sector leadership.
Data‑driven mindset applied to forecasting, pipeline analysis, and revenue planning.

An established B2B and direct-to-consumer retail software provider is hiring a hands-on Chief Technology Officer. The company's mature point-of-sale and eCommerce platform, built on legacy Java and Swing, is central to how its customers run their businesses. Leadership is committed to modernizing it.

Remote

Technology strategy, architecture, infrastructure, DevOps, and software delivery

Think breakout DTC and omnichannel consumer brands, the ones already in your cart, your closet and your feed, whose growth story is still being written. You won't just be running campaigns for them. You'll be the strategic partner helping them figure out how paid media compounds into revenue, customer lifetime value and durable, profitable growth. That means owning the questions that actually move a business: how do we acquire new customers profitably, know which spend is truly incremental, and scale without giving up margin? The tactical craft matters (shopping feeds, creative testing, ROAS, CAC and MER performance), but here it's in service of something bigger: shaping how some of the most exciting consumer brands out there grow. Help shape the financial foundations of an organization dedicated to improving financial education and consumer awareness for children, parents, and teachers. As Chief Financial Officer, you will play a strategic role in building a sustainable financial structure that supports long-term growth and meaningful social impact. You will oversee financial planning, budgeting, liquidity management, and the responsible allocation of funds within a nonprofit framework. Beyond financial oversight, you will help develop fundraising strategies, attract financial supporters, and build lasting relationships with donors and institutional partners. This fully remote, voluntary leadership opportunity combines strategic influence with hands-on execution. It is ideal for a finance professional who wants to contribute their expertise to a purpose-driven mission.

Accountabilities

Take overall responsibility for the organization's financial structure, including financial planning, management, monitoring, and control.
