Lead budget planning, liquidity management, and the allocation of funds in accordance with nonprofit requirements.
Develop and implement strategies to attract supporting members, donors, and other financial contributors.
Actively contribute to fundraising by approaching potential supporters, structuring funding proposals, and supporting negotiations through to completion.
Establish and maintain strong relationships with donors, strategic partners, and institutional funding organizations.
Ensure transparent financial processes, reliable bookkeeping, and compliance with applicable accounting and tax requirements.
Work closely with the leadership team to assess financial priorities, guide resource allocation, and support strategic decision-making.
Identify opportunities to strengthen funding models and establish sustainable sources of financial support.

Requirements

You are a financially skilled and dependable professional who can combine strategic thinking with practical execution. You are comfortable working independently, managing financial priorities, and contributing to the development of a mission-driven organization. The key requirements include:

Professional experience in financial management, controlling, or a comparable business or finance function.
Understanding of financial structures within nonprofit organizations, or a strong willingness to develop expertise in this area.
Ability to translate financial strategies into practical plans, processes, and measurable outcomes.
Experience in fundraising, securing financial resources, building partnerships, or business development, or demonstrable strengths in these areas.
Strong numerical skills and a sound understanding of financial planning models and business economics.
A structured, reliable, and self-directed approach to work.
Ability to build relationships with external stakeholders and communicate financial matters clearly.
Strategic judgment and the ability to balance financial sustainability with the organization's social mission.

Benefits

100% remote work: Work from anywhere, with location-independent flexibility.
Meaningful social impact: Contribute to an initiative focused on financial education and consumer awareness.
Strategic influence: Directly shape the organization's financial development, resilience, and long-term sustainability.
Ownership and autonomy: Help build and refine effective financial and funding structures.

You will leverage your strong financial acumen to understand clients' complex needs and articulate the full breadth of our services. Furthermore, you will act as a key liaison, working seamlessly with internal partners to deliver comprehensive solutions, while leading the overall sales function, running key meetings, and reporting on pipeline metrics.

 About Fulfillment IQ 
 Fulfillment IQ (FIQ) is a supply chain technology and consulting company helping retailers, brands, and 3PLs solve complex fulfillment and logistics challenges.
 Our work spans three core practices: Supply Chain Consulting, Technology Delivery & Transformation, and Implementation. We help customers assess and design supply-chain strategies, select and implement technology, modernize fulfillment operations, and build technology solutions that solve complex operational challenges.

 The Opportunity  
 We are looking for a Director, Product & Strategy to lead our Tech Delivery practice across both sides of the house: the internal teams that build, and the client relationships that fund and shape the work. This is a hands-on leadership role for someone who is equally comfortable in a client boardroom shaping strategy and in a delivery stand-up unblocking a team.
 You will own the arc of a client engagement end to end: understanding the business problem, shaping the solution strategy, and directing the cross-functional team that delivers it, all while continuously deepening and expanding the client relationship. You will also help incubate Fulfillment IQ's own internal innovation products, applying the same product discipline to what we build for ourselves.

 What You’ll Do 
 Client & Relationship Leadership 
 Own the client relationship as the senior point of contact for assigned clients, building trust with stakeholders from operators to executives.
 Capture and translate client needs into clearly framed problems and solution strategies, translating business goals into delivery roadmaps.
 Grow and expand accounts by identifying new opportunities, shaping proposals and statements of work, and converting successful delivery into expanded scope and long-term partnership.
 Manage expectations, scope, risks, and escalations proactively, keeping engagements healthy commercially and operationally.
 Delivery & Team Leadership 
 Lead and mentor cross-functional delivery teams, product managers, business analysts, UX designers, DevOps engineers, developers (front-end, back-end, full-stack), and tech leads.
 Direct delivery across engagements, planning, resourcing, quality, timelines, and budgets, and holding teams accountable to outcomes.
 Establish delivery standards, ways of working, and reusable practices that raise quality and predictability across the practice.
 Attract and develop talent, coaching leads, growing capability, and building a team people want to be part of.
 Product & Solution Strategy 
 Shape solution architectures and product strategies that fit each client's operations, budget, and roadmap.
 Incubate Fulfillment IQ's internal innovation products, owning discovery, prioritization, and delivery of what we build for our own IP and platforms.
 Translate supply chain and fulfillment technology trends into practical recommendations and differentiated offerings.
 Partner closely with sales, partnerships, and leadership to align solutions with market opportunity.

 What You'll Bring 
 8+ years of relevant experience, including leadership of technology delivery, product, or professional-services teams (services, consulting, systems-integration, or product backgrounds all welcome).
 Proven ability to manage senior client relationships and grow accounts, turning delivery success into expanded scope and revenue.
 Strong command of software delivery: product management, requirements, UX, and engineering across the full stack, plus modern DevOps and agile practices.
 Experience shaping solution strategy and translating ambiguous business problems into clear, deliverable roadmaps.
 A track record of leading and developing cross-functional teams and setting delivery standards.
 Supply chain, fulfillment, logistics, WMS/OMS/TMS, or e-commerce technology experience strongly preferred.
 Product ownership instincts: comfortable driving internal innovation products from idea to launch.
 Excellent communication and executive presence; able to move fluidly between strategy conversations and hands-on delivery.
 Bachelor's degree in a related field, or equivalent experience; based in the US or Canada and able to work on a hybrid schedule.

Skills and Competencies 
 Required Skills 
 Client & stakeholder management: building and expanding senior relationships and negotiating scope.
 Delivery & program management: planning, resourcing, budgeting, risk management, and on-time execution across concurrent engagements.
 Solution & product strategy: framing ambiguous business problems and translating them into architectures and roadmaps.
 Cross-functional team leadership: directing product, BA, UX, engineering, and DevOps talent.
 Software delivery lifecycle fluency: agile/scrum, requirements, UX, and full-stack engineering across front-end, backend, and DevOps.
 Commercial acumen: proposals, statements of work, estimation, and account growth.
 Executive communication & presentation: clear, credible, and persuasive with technical and business audiences.
 Product ownership: prioritization, discovery, and driving products from concept to launch.
 Good-to-Have Skills

 Pre-sales & solutioning: shaping deals and demonstrating solutions to prospective clients.
 Modern cloud & DevOps tooling: CI/CD, containers, and cloud platforms (AWS, Azure, or GCP).
 Product & delivery tooling: Jira, roadmapping, and agile management platforms.
 Data & analytics literacy: using metrics to steer delivery and inform product decisions.
 Relevant certifications: PMP, SAFe, CSM/CSPO, or equivalent.
 Nice-to-Have Skills 
 Experience at a technology consultancy, systems integrator, or 3PL/retail technology organization.
 Pre-sales / solutioning experience and familiarity with SOW and commercial models.
 Hands-on background in one or more delivery disciplines (product, engineering, UX, or DevOps).

 Why Fulfillment IQ

 Work with experienced implementation leaders who understand the platforms and the operations they support.

The Director oversees the enterprise sales pipeline, manages strategic deal execution, and ensures alignment between customer business needs and the organization's products and services. Drive new business development and expansion opportunities across large, complex customer organizations.

**Headwaters Health Care Centre. One Community, Caring Together.**
------------------------------------------------------------------


At **Headwaters Health Care Centre,** we are proud to serve our community with compassion, accountability, and teamwork. We are seeking a **Director, Finance and Health Records** who is motivated by purpose, values collaboration, and wants to make a meaningful impact in a community hospital setting.


**About the Role**


Reporting to the Vice President, Corporate Services and Chief Financial Officer, this senior leadership role provides strategic and operational oversight for Finance, Health Records, Materials Management, and hospital‑owned medical office buildings. The Director plays a critical role in advancing financial sustainability, strengthening data‑informed decision‑making, and ensuring the integrity and accessibility of health information that supports high‑quality patient care.


As a trusted partner to clinical and corporate leaders, the Director leads core financial functions including budgeting, forecasting, financial reporting, audits, procurement, and internal controls, while also championing excellence in health information management, privacy, and digital health optimization. The role offers a unique opportunity to contribute to organizational strategy, quality improvement, and collaboration across the broader health system, while supporting the operational and financial performance of commercial rental facilities located on hospital property.


This is an ideal opportunity for a principled, forward‑thinking leader who enjoys working in a dynamic environment, values collaboration, and is passionate about using financial and information stewardship to enable excellent care.


**What You’ll Do**


* Provide strategic leadership for financial planning, budgeting, forecasting, reporting, and audits
* Champion excellence by leading and supporting high‑quality health records, privacy, data integrity, and digital health systems
* Oversee procurement and materials management in alignment with public‑sector best practices and with a focus on stewardship and transparency
* Manage the financial and operational performance of hospital‑owned medical office buildings
* Partner with leaders to assess risks, develop business cases, and drive continuous improvement
* Support Board, committee, and external reporting relationships with clarity and accountability
* Lead, mentor, and develop high‑performing teams, fostering engagement, growth and building strong succession and talent pipelines
  

**What You Bring**


You are a principled and collaborative leader who brings both professional expertise and a strong commitment to public service and patient‑centred care.


* A commitment to public service and patient‑centred care, grounded in integrity, accountability, and collaboration
* Progressive senior‑level financial leadership experience in a hospital or complex health‑care environment
* A CPA designation, with strong expertise in financial planning, reporting, audits, and stewardship of public resources
* The ability to translate financial, clinical, and operational data into meaningful insights that support decision‑making
* Experience leading or supporting large‑scale information system implementations and digital optimization initiatives
* A people‑centred leadership style, with a proven ability to engage, develop, and inspire high‑performing teams
* Strong judgment, analytical thinking, and comfort navigating complexity and change
* A collaborative mindset, with experience working in unionized environments and partnering across the health system
  

  

**Hours of Work:** 37\.5 hours per week, Monday to Friday
  

  

**Hiring Salary Range:** $160,602 \- $188,955  

  



We are currently hiring for an existing vacancy.


**Why Headwaters?**
  

  

At **Headwaters Health Care Centre**, you’ll be part of a purpose‑driven organization where your leadership directly supports patient care and community well‑being. We offer the opportunity to make a meaningful impact in a community hospital setting while working alongside dedicated, values‑driven professionals.
  

  

You’ll join a collaborative leadership team committed to accountability, continuous improvement, and thoughtful stewardship of public resources. At Headwaters, your expertise will be valued, your voice will matter, and your work will contribute to a trusted, high‑quality health system that serves today’s needs while planning responsibly for the future.  



We offer a wide range of employee perks, for information on our comprehensive benefits package, please visit **Headwaters Health Care Centre \- Careers at Headwaters** .
  

  

We thank all those who apply but only those individuals selected for further consideration will be contacted.
  

  

Headwaters Health Care Centre is an inclusive and equal opportunity employer and supports the compliance of the Accessibility for Ontarians with Disabilities Act (AODA). If you have a need for an accommodation, please contact Human Resources so that appropriate arrangements can be made.
  

  

Headwaters Health Care Centre is a smoke\-free facility. Smoking is not permitted on hospital properties. We thank everyone who works at or visits our hospitals for respecting this healthy initiative. We are also a scent\-free environment for all employees and visitors.

jobs.title: Chief Financial Officer
jobs.description:
Wag & Bright Supply Co.

Calgary, Alberta | Hybrid | Full-Time

Help us build what comes next.

Wag & Bright is a growing Canadian pet care company behind Puppy Polish and Mighty Marrows. We’re founder-led, ambitious, and looking for a financial leader who is excited to help build the business alongside us.

Our team is lean, our work is hands-on, and we’re building the systems and processes to support our next stage of growth.

We’re looking for a commercially minded CFO with an entrepreneurial mindset, strong technical accounting skills, and the resourcefulness to turn plans into action. Someone who sees a challenge, takes ownership, and helps find a way forward.

The opportunity

Working directly with the CEO and COO, you’ll lead financial planning, reporting, cash flow management and the development of our finance function.

This role combines strategy with execution. You should be equally comfortable discussing a growth opportunity, building a financial model, investigating a margin discrepancy, or helping the accounting team improve a process. You won’t need every system to be perfectly established before you can contribute. You’ll help us decide what needs building, what needs improving, and what can stay simple.

What you’ll own

Financial planning and cash flow. Lead budgets, rolling forecasts and financial modelling, giving leadership clear visibility into performance, working capital and future requirements.
Accounting and reporting. Take responsibility for accurate, timely financial reporting and strong controls, working with our accounting team and external advisors.
Costing and profitability. Improve visibility into product costs, inventory, margins and profitability across our sales channels. Help translate those insights into better pricing and operational decisions.
Systems and processes. Build practical reporting tools, improve workflows and introduce automation where it genuinely saves time or improves accuracy.
Commercial decision support. Help evaluate business opportunities, spending priorities, capital requirements and the financial implications of growth.
Financial leadership. Guide and develop the accounting function, coordinate with financial service providers, and oversee compliance and payroll processes.

Who will thrive here

We’re looking for someone who brings:
A strong finance foundation. Senior experience as a CFO, Finance Director, VP Finance or Controller, with hands-on expertise in accounting, forecasting and financial modelling. A CPA designation is strongly preferred.
Relevant business experience. An understanding of b2b, d2c, inventory, product costing and working capital, ideally gained in consumer products, manufacturing, wholesale, distribution or e-commerce.
An entrepreneurial mindset. You understand how to work with a lean team, prioritise limited resources and build practical solutions without unnecessary complexity.
Resilience and ownership. You’re comfortable with changing priorities, raise concerns early, and bring recommendations - not just a list of problems.
Clear communication and sound judgment. You can explain the numbers, challenge assumptions constructively, and work closely with founders and colleagues who aren’t finance specialists.
Strong Excel and financial modelling skills are essential. Experience with QuickBooks Online and improving financial systems is valuable.

You may already be a CFO, or you may be an accomplished Controller or Finance Director ready for broader responsibility. What matters most is your capability, your approach, and your enthusiasm for this stage of the business.

Why join us?

This is an opportunity to have a direct impact on how a growing company operates and what it becomes.

You’ll work closely with the founders, have a voice in important decisions, and help build a finance function that supports both day-to-day execution and long-term ambitions.

We’re looking for someone who is genuinely keen to take the journey with us- someone who cares about the business, takes pride in their work, and wants to help build something meaningful over time.

To apply

Please submit your résumé and a brief note about why joining a founder-led company at this stage appeals to you.

One last thing… 🐾

Tell us your pet’s name and what you love most about them! We’d love to get to know the person behind the résumé.

Work at CBC/Radio-Canada

At CBC/Radio-Canada, we create content that informs, entertains and connects Canadians on multiple platforms. Our successes and accomplishments are driven by embodying and upholding values, which include creativity, integrity, inclusiveness and relevance.

Do you think you have the ability and drive to keep up with this exciting, ever-changing industry? Whether it be in front of the camera, on air, online or behind the scenes, you would be joining a team that thrives on making connections and telling stories that are important to Canadians.

Job Overview:

This position is part of the Digital Media department, which oversees CBC and Radio-Canada’s flagship digital products.

In partnership with the Media Solutions division, the person in this role plays a key role in shaping the vision for CBC-RC monetization experience evolution. They leverage a deep understanding of digital, user behaviours, market trends, and technology to inform strategic thinking and guide product direction. They also will support the day to day audience segmentation activities and support and inform the monetization data strategy and roadmaps.

They lead the monetization products evolution — from testing to discovery to delivery — balancing user needs with business objectives. They work to enhance the overall experience and drive innovation to retain current clients, audiences and attract new ones. They also ensure the continuous evolution of tools and solutions that support Media Solutions and Marketing team operations as it relates to audience segmentation.

They collaborate with product managers to coordinate the work carried out by the product teams. They maintain strong ties with the sales, marketing, communications, and ad tech teams to ensure strategic and operational alignment.

This role also aims to create synergies across products to strengthen engagement within Radio-Canada’s broader digital ecosystem. The individual actively contributes to the organization’s digital transformation initiatives.

Why this role is important:

You are responsible for leading and evolving the organizations ability to drive revenue through the creation and maintenance of innovative ad products and services.
You are responsible for developing a strategic roadmap that aligns to the strategic priorities of the Media Solutions (Sales) team, by identifying and executing on the highest priorities.
You enable the evolution of ad formats, the integration of technologies within the ad tech stack, the evolution of the data strategy and the enablement of key features and improvements for our users.
You establish a testing practice that is continuously finding ways to improve the existing ad experience with new ad loads, scenarios by user type and ad formats to adopt.
You are in lock step with the strategy of the Media Solutions team. The products that your teams develop are relevant in the market and sellable.
You enable real collaboration between your stakeholders and the product teams focusing them on solving problems together.
You are the main point of accountability and escalation to Media Solutions as it relates to product development.
You coach and mentor a cross functional team of product managers, data analysts and data experts.

Core Competencies / Mindset:

This role requires a proactive and collaborative leader who acts as a crucial link between technical possibilities and business needs:

Problem Solver & Roadblock Remover: key to understanding what is possible, navigating the entire team around roadblocks, and creating options and alternatives to respond to business problems
Collaborative Leader: creates a positive and collaborative space that fosters deeper understanding between supported teams, often by facilitating meetings as forums for problem-solving
Clarity & Accountability: key to creating clarity on the roadmap, ensuring decisions are made, and escalating effectively to clear the path on execution
Efficiency Driver: focused on making things easier, faster, smoother, and better, including filling gaps personally with conversations and trackers, and coaching resources on performance
Client Service Mindset: sets high standards, seeks out feedback, acts on it, and ensures teams are serving stakeholders appropriately
Action-Oriented & Transparent: strongly biased towards action, pushing for ways forward with personal involvement over passing the buck. Works transparently, ensuring risks are appropriately distributed across all decision makers rather than made in silos
Product Leader: reinforces basic product principles, helps teams find effective ways forward, emphasizing the quest for value over increments of work

How you will make an impact:

You will work closely with your partners in Media Solutions - from Ad Tech, Ad Operations and Data Monetization to understand their needs to deepen the nature of the relationship. You will invest the time in understanding their strategic roadmaps and the most important problems to solve.
You will work closely with a team of product managers to ensure that roadmaps reflect the priorities and needs of the stakeholders and you will make sure the teams are focused on the right things. You will make sure that the product teams are delivering real value to your stakeholders.
You will enable the generation of revenue through the activation of audiences first party data.

Candidate Qualifications:

Minimum of five to seven (5 to 7) years of progressive leadership within the media or advertising industry
Deep expertise in advertising, digital transformation, and multi-platform consumer behaviour
Demonstrated adaptability in dynamic environments with the resilience to navigate ambiguity and lead organizational change
Exceptional communication and presentation skills; bilingual proficiency in French and English is highly desirable
Superior relationship management skills with a proven ability to influence senior executives through diplomacy and strategic negotiation
Ability to manage competing priorities and high-pressure deadlines with operational excellence

jobs.title: Sr Director, Business Strategy and Operations
jobs.description:
At Gilead, we’re creating a healthier world for all people. For more than 35 years, we’ve tackled diseases such as HIV, viral hepatitis, COVID-19 and cancer – working relentlessly to develop therapies that help improve lives and to ensure access to these therapies across the globe. We continue to fight against the world’s biggest health challenges, and our mission requires collaboration, determination and a relentless drive to make a difference.

Every member of Gilead’s team plays a critical role in the discovery and development of life-changing scientific innovations. Our employees are our greatest asset as we work to achieve our bold ambitions, and we’re looking for the next wave of passionate and ambitious people ready to make a direct impact.

We believe every employee deserves a great leader. People Leaders are the cornerstone to the employee experience at Gilead and Kite. As a people leader now or in the future, you are the key driver in evolving our culture and creating an environment where every employee feels included, developed and empowered to fulfil their aspirations. Join Gilead and help create possible, together.

Job Description

JOB RESPONSIBILITIES

Serves as a key strategic partner to the Vice President of Operations and the Site Leadership Team (SLT), enabling the Gilead Alberta site to achieve its short- and long-term business objectives through strong strategy deployment, operational discipline, organizational change management, communication, digital enablement, and operational excellence.
Accountable for translating site, Pharmaceutical Development and Manufacturing (PDM), and enterprise priorities into actionable plans, governance routines, performance management systems, and cross-functional execution mechanisms.
Provides leadership across multiple strategic and operational workstreams and ensures alignment between business priorities, resources, organizational capability, and site performance.
Responsible for multi-function strategic planning
Institutes key processes necessary to achieve long and short-term strategic goals.
Anticipates shifts in industry trends and regulatory environment that will impact Gilead’s business needs and positions the function to respond accordingly.
Works with the SLT to establish and publish Key Performance Indicators.

Strategy Development and Implementation

Acts as key strategic advisor, leading the development and execution of short- and long-range strategic plans in alignment with PDM and PDM Manufacturing strategy and ambition, company goals, market trends and in partnership with the SLT.
Provides insight in developing, prioritization and communicating site-wide priorities and initiatives. Creates buy-in for the business plans and vision for the future to ensure goals are aligned and achieved.
Develops plans to translate strategic objectives into tactical implementation of new technologies and processes to enhance production efficiency.
Monitors key performance indicators (KPIs) to track progress and identify areas for further optimization.
Builds strong relationships with internal and external stakeholders to facilitate collaboration and alignment on strategic and operational priorities.
Supports the development of a culture that aligns with the company values, encouraging growth and learning mindset while ensuring accountability and retaining key talent in a positive environment.

Organization Change Management & Communication

Leads the organizational change management strategy for major site initiatives, ensuring business changes are effectively planned, communicated, adopted, and sustained.
Communicates manufacturing site strategy and progress to the SLT, including regular updates on performance metrics.
Partners with the VP of Operations, SLT, HR and functional leaders to ensure messaging is aligned, timely, transparent, and connected to site values and strategic pillars.
Develops communication plans and ensures effective communication strategies are in place within the organization, including two-way communication channels.
Accountable for the success of formal organizational change management impacting all business units.
Strengthens site-wide change readiness by building leader capability in communication, stakeholder engagement, and change adoption.
Supports leaders in translating complex business changes into practical, audience-specific messages that promote understanding, engagement, and ownership.

Operational Excellence

Develops and leads the Alberta operational excellence strategy in alignment with site priorities, business needs, and enterprise goals.
Champions continuous improvement methodologies and establishes sustainable processes that improve productivity and effectiveness.
Manages multiple cross-functional projects.
Conducts process analysis, identifies bottlenecks and inefficiencies, and designs and implements process improvement solutions using methodologies like Lean Six Sigma, or other continuous improvement frameworks.
Utilizes data analytics to measure performance, identify trends, and track progress on improvement initiatives.
Supports a high-performing cross-functional team of operational excellence professionals, providing coaching and development opportunities.
Works closely with cross-functional teams across departments to identify and implement operational improvements.
Fosters a culture of continuous improvement, encouraging employee engagement and feedback on process improvement opportunities.
Ensures operational excellence initiatives are supported by appropriate change management, communication, training, adoption, and sustainment plans.

Experience Requirements

BS Degree and 14 years of experience

OR

Master's Degree and 12 years of experience

OR

PhD and 12 years of experience

People Leader Accountabilities

Create Inclusion - knowing the business value of diverse teams, modeling inclusion, and embedding the value of diversity in the way they manage their teams.
Develop Talent - understand the skills, experience, aspirations and potential of their employees and coach them on current performance and future potential. They ensure employees are receiving the feedback and insight needed to grow, develop and realize their purpose.
Empower Teams - connect the team to the organization by aligning goals, purpose, and organizational objectives, and holding them to account. They provide the support needed to remove barriers and connect their team to the broader ecosystem.

jobs.description:
**Description**
---------------


The Director/Senior Director Technology Audit and Advisory Services is accountable for the delivery of high quality, professional, cost\-effective, value\-added, and risk\-based internal audit services over Technology functions, across North America (Canada and US Segment), Global Wealth \& Asset Management, Group Functions, and the Global Data Technology Office. The role reports to the AVP of North America Segment Technology, Audit Services.

  

  

**Position Responsibilities:**


* Audit Delivery – Delivery of North America Segment Technology, Infrastructure and Cybersecurity (steady state/key risk, program and project, business integrated, issue assessments).
* Technology SOX – Delivery of application and infrastructure technology SOX audit work and to drive our approach and processes for this work forward through use of automation, data analytics, and shared services.
* Reporting and Planning – Execution and continuous improvement of reporting processes in support of the larger technology audit organization, as well as annual audit planning, resource management, and other process improvements for the immediate North America segment technology audit team.
* Other – Audit initiatives, engagements, and process improvements as assigned.
  

  

**Strategic Leadership**


* Understand the company’s strategy, operations, and regulatory environment to proactively identify areas of emerging and heightened risk related to technology that affects the company
* Support the development of an audit strategy that aligns to business, technology, and Audit Services strategies, provides sufficient coverage for key risks while meeting regulatory expectations
* Develop internal procedures and tools to drive consistency across all engagements and drive audit planning
* Help improve Technology SOX delivery and quality to improve efficiencies through increased use of data analytics, automation and shared services and other innovations
* Develop and produce meaningful reports for Senior Technology Management that identify trends and enable continuous improvement of risks and controls
* Contribute to the development of Audit Services procedures, strategy, and direction; continually improve audit and supporting processes leveraging technology to the fullest
  

  

**Audit Delivery and Oversight**


* Plan and direct audits and special audit projects to objectively evaluate the effectiveness of key controls and adequacy of risk management practices; collaborating with management to obtain a consensus on establishing the problem, risks exposure; produce meaningful audit reports that clearly articulate the position on risks and related issues, while meeting Audit Services operational targets related to budget, timeline and quality of execution
* Delivery of annual Technology Application and Infrastructure ITGC SOX work, in collaboration with Technology Management, SOX PMO, and external audit
* Perform integrated/cross\-functional audits in partnership with groups across Audit Services to provide comprehensive reporting on risks that could prevent the achievement of Management’s objectives
* Support the development of an annual audit plan using risk management processes, in collaboration with Management and Audit Services leadership
* Drive innovation and incorporate and develop industry best practices into forward thinking audit approach; manage Audit Services’ resources efficiently, economically, and effectively
* Provide management with timely recommendations that reduce risk, help them run their business better, make strategic and operational decisions, and oversee management of risks and controls
* Monitoring progress in implementing control recommendations and reporting thereon; assist with preparation of Audit Committee and senior leadership reports
  

**Leadership \& People Development**


* Lead and develop a high\-caliber audit team, attract, and retain top talent and provide appropriate development, coaching and training
* Foster creative culture that strives for continuous improvement and welcomes and offers feedback—enabling best\-in\-class audit practices
* Challenge, coach and enable the team members to develop to their fullest and maximize their contribution to the team
* Drive team skills development and engagement; manage talent across the team for development and succession and rotate change expertise
  

**Stakeholder Management**


* Managing Management’s expectations regarding assurance and advisory work deadlines and deliverables
* Providing relevant stakeholders with an overview of audit work and commentary on the control environment, including trends and emerging issues that could impact the Company
* Collaborate effectively with divisional and global stakeholders in Technology and Information Risk Management
* Establishing a high level of credibility and building professional relationships with key stakeholders responsible for technology and information risk across the Company
  

**Required Qualifications:**


* Exceptional communications judgement and the ability to communicate clearly and succinctly to effectively deliver key messages verbally and in writing and to listen and consider various perspectives; confident presentation and facilitation skills and strong interpersonal and leadership skills to facilitate working with senior management at all levels
* Ability to quickly understand business processes and risks, identify key controls, analyze complex situations, reach appropriate conclusions, make value\-added and practical recommendations and influence management to take appropriate actions on recommendations
* In\-depth knowledge of audit methodologies, project management and system development methodologies (including Agile), control frameworks and risk management practices, and regulatory requirements; Exceptional understanding of how technology supports business strategies, the latest technology and cyber security trends, best practices

jobs.title: Director, Enterprise Process & Business Readiness *** Directeur(ice), Processus d'entreprise et préparation opérationnelle
jobs.description:
At IPEX, the leader in thermoplastic piping systems, we are redefining the future of water management and clean energy. As part of the Aliaxis family, we combine global strength with local expertise to tackle the world's toughest challenges. Guided by our values – We Care, We Dare, We Deliver – we challenge the status quo to make a meaningful impact. If you're an innovative collaborator ready to make a difference, come join us in shaping a better tomorrow!  



  

**Job Summary**

The Director, Enterprise Process \& Business Readiness is accountable for leading the business transformation activities required to successfully deploy SAP across the enterprise’s manufacturing and distribution network.  



Reporting to the VP, ERP Business Transformation, this role serves as the senior business counterpart to the Director of ERP Delivery and is responsible for ensuring the organization is operationally prepared for the ERP deployment through process standardization, stakeholder alignment, organizational readiness, and deployment governance.  



The role partners closely with the Director, ERP Change \& Training, Director, Data Governance \& Management, Business Process Owners, Functional Leaders, Site Leadership Teams, and IT to drive adoption of standardized SAP\-enabled business processes across IPEX’s manufacturing plants and distribution centres.  



The Director leads the enterprise\-wide efforts to establish consistent operating practices, collaborate in the transformation of operational master data, mobilize business resources, and implement objective readiness measures that ensure successful deployment and business continuity during cutover and go\-live.  



**Key Responsibilities**

**Enterprise Process Transformation**

* Lead enterprise process transformation by establishing the future\-state business process model, leveraging SAP standard capabilities, leading practices and simplification opportunities
* Dotted line partner with the Business Process Owners (BPOs) to document, sustain, and deploy future\-state processes
* Establish governance mechanisms to ensure adherence to standardized processes and minimize local customization
* Drive alignment between enterprise process standards and site\-level operational requirements
* Resolve conflicts between local business practices and enterprise process design
* Facilitate process harmonization workshops with functional and operational leadership teams
* Ensure process design decisions support scalability, compliance, operational efficiency and SAP standard functionality
* Own business governance, quality, and stewardship of operational master data across assigned process domains.
* Approve and prioritize master data changes, ensuring compliance with data standards, controls, and business requirements.
* Partner with Data Governance, Data Stewards, and IT teams to define, maintain, and continuously improve master data processes and controls.

**Business Readiness**

* Develop and execute the enterprise business readiness strategy for ERP deployment
* Identify points of failure, risks, business contingency plans, and the metrics that trigger identified contingencies
* Develop key tactics to alter timing of typical business rhythms by advancing or deferring core activities or operations
* Plan daily operations to compensate for reduced staffing during training period
* Develop and deploy operational targets (KPIs), monitoring methods, and reporting cadence

Join a purpose driven winning team, committed to results, in an inclusive and high-performing culture.

Leads and oversees the Risk Advisory function within Risk Identification team, Canadian Banking Business Risk Management, providing proactive, practical and independent non-financial risk advice to Canadian Banking business units. The role partners with business leaders and Control and Support Functions to identify, assess, manage and escalate risk; strengthen control design and execution; support informed business decisions; and promote consistent application of the Bank's risk management frameworks, policies and risk appetite.

Lead a team of Risk Advisory professionals aligned to Canadian Banking business units, establishing clear coverage, service expectations, priorities and escalation protocols.

Guide business units in the effective use of risk management tools under the Bank's Operational Risk Management Framework and Compliance Risk Program, including risk and control self-assessments, key risk indicators, risk appetite activities, operational risk events and issue management.

Lead and drive a customer-focused culture across the team, leveraging broader Bank relationships, systems and knowledge to deliver consistent and effective advisory support.
Ensure the Bank's risk appetite and risk culture are considered in day-to-day activities and decisions.

Provides risk advisory coverage across Canadian Banking business units and products, in partnership with relevant Control and Support Functions.
Supports business decision-making and execution by providing timely, consistent and actionable non-financial risk advice.
Helps prevent financial loss, regulatory exposure, customer harm and reputational damage through early risk identification, effective challenge and sustainable control solutions.
Operates across key activities within the Operational Risk and Compliance Risk Programs and supports the continuous improvement of risk advisory practices.
Requires strong knowledge of Canadian Banking business processes, products, operations, systems, technology and change initiatives.
Engages stakeholders at all levels, from business and functional teams to Canadian Banking executives and enterprise risk partners.

MBA or University degree, with 10-15 years of relevant experience in financial services, risk management, business operations, controls, compliance or related field.
Strong understanding of Canadian Banking business units, products, services, customer journeys, operations, systems and practices.
Demonstrated experience providing risk advice and effective challenge to senior business leaders, including the ability to translate complex requirements into practical business actions.
In-depth knowledge of non-financial risk management, control design, risk and control assessment, key risk indicators, risk appetite, operational risk events and issue management.
Strong knowledge of applicable regulatory requirements and guidance impacting Canadian Banking, including relevant OSFI guidelines, the Bank Act and internal policies and frameworks.
Strong strategic thinking, judgement, influencing, facilitation and executive communication skills, with the ability to navigate ambiguity and balance risk, customer and business considerations.
Proven people leadership experience, including the ability to build advisory capability, establish accountability and lead through change.
Ability to identify cross-business themes and emerging risks and convert insights into clear recommendations for senior management and risk committees.

jobs.title: Director, Strategic Finance - Remote in Canada
jobs.description:
DIRECTOR, STRATEGIC FINANCE

Who is a Director, Strategic Finance?

The Director, Strategic Finance is a high-impact leader within the Office of the Chief Financial Officer (CFO) who brings an investment-oriented perspective to GoodLife Group’s most consequential strategic, financial and enterprise-value decisions. This role personally leads complex analysis and selected cross-functional workstreams under the delegated authority of the CFO.

Reporting directly to the Chief Financial Officer, the role expands the capacity and analytical depth of the Office of the CFO across executive decision support, capital allocation, enterprise performance, Value Creation Plan validation, Apollo and Board engagement, financing and merger and acquisition (M&A) execution.

Working with leadership from across Financial Planning & Analysis, Accounting, Data & Analytics and Operations departments, the role influences through expertise, credibility and delegated CFO authority, while functional leaders retain ownership of their teams, source information and recurring processes.

What will you be doing?

Enterprise strategic finance, corporate modelling and capital allocation

Build, enhance and apply integrated financial models, strategic scenarios and sensitivity analyses that connect operating performance, cash flow, leverage, capital requirements, and enterprise value.
Evaluate organic growth initiatives, capital projects, acquisitions, financing alternatives and other uses of capital through disciplined return, risk, liquidity and enterprise-value analysis; establish appropriate post investment performance reviews.
Translate complex financial, operational and market information into clear alternatives, trade-offs and recommendations for the CFO, CEO, and executive leadership.

Apollo, Board and lender performance insight

Lead the financial synthesis, analytical challenge and development of decision-useful performance narratives for selected Apollo, Board and lender discussions, while the CFO remains the primary relationship owner and existing teams retain responsibility for underlying financial information.
Integrate and constructively challenge inputs from Financial Planning & Analysis, Accounting, Data & Analytics and operating teams to identify key drivers, emerging risks, outlook implications and required decisions
Partner with the CFO and executive leadership to articulate clear financial narratives regarding business performance, strategic priorities, risks, and opportunities.
Lead selected follow-up analyses and coordinate timely resolution of material questions, commitments and decisions arising from Apollo, Board and lender discussions.

M&A, financing and strategic transaction execution

Lead core financial analysis and selected execution workstreams for acquisitions, dispositions, refinancing's and other strategic transactions, including screening, valuation, financial modelling, due diligence, scenario analysis and approval materials.
Support the CFO in evaluating capital structure, liquidity requirements, financing alternatives, and capital-allocation priorities.
Coordinate Finance workstreams, data-room requirements and financial analysis across internal teams, financing sources, counterparties and external advisors.
Evaluate transaction structures, synergies, risks, integration considerations and value-creation implications, and support post transaction performance tracking where appropriate.

Executive decision support and Office of the CFO effectiveness

Serve as a trusted thought partner to the CFO on high-priority strategic, financial and operational matters.
Lead selected cross-functional strategic workstreams and high-priority analyses, bringing investment discipline, structure, pace and clear accountability to complex or ambiguous issues.
Support the financial elements of the Value Creation Plan, including connecting initiative impacts to the long-range financial model, validating material financial assumptions and supporting the reporting cadence for key financial and operating KPIs, without assuming ownership of broader VCP governance or initiative execution.
Institutionalize rigorous decision and review processes for priority Office of the CFO mandates, including clear accountabilities, analytical standards and escalation protocols.
Build trusted relationships with long-tenured leaders and ensure that Strategic Finance complements, rather than cuts across, the responsibilities of existing functional teams.

Do you have what it takes?

Bachelor’s degree in business, finance, economics, accounting, mathematics, engineering or another quantitatively rigorous discipline
4 to 7 years of progressively responsible experience in private equity, investment banking, pension or infrastructure investing, strategic finance or another analytically rigorous transaction- or investment-oriented environment.
Demonstrated experience building and interpreting complex financial models, evaluating investments or transactions, and preparing concise decision materials for senior executives, investment committees, Boards or equivalent senior stakeholders
Advanced financial modelling, valuation, investment-return analysis, scenario analysis and business-case development skills, with expert-level proficiency in Microsoft Excel and the ability to create concise, executive-quality PowerPoint materials.
Deep understanding of the connections among income statement performance, balance sheet requirements, cash flow, liquidity, leverage, covenants and enterprise value.
Exceptional analytical judgment and attention to detail, with the ability to identify inconsistencies, test assumptions, distinguish material issues from noise and reconcile information from multiple sources.
Exceptional written, verbal and presentation communication skills, including the ability to produce concise, persuasive, executive- and Board-quality materials.
Credibility, judgment, and executive presence to work directly with senior leaders, investors, lenders and advisors while handling confidential information appropriately.
Highly self-directed, organized and action oriented; able to manage multiple workstreams, tight deadlines and ambiguity without requiring a large team or extensive direction.
A hands-on orientation and willingness to move between high-level strategic questions and detailed analysis and execution.
Strong collaboration and influencing skills, with the ability to lead cross-functional work through expertise, credibility and delegated authority rather than formal hierarchy.
Intellectual curiosity and a genuine interest in understanding GoodLife’s businesses at the club, member and operating-process levels.

What’s in it for you?

Ongoing training & development to ensure a long & successful career path
Career advancement opportunities
Competitive Total Rewards Package
FREE Performance Fitness membership
Fun & energetic atmosphere to come to every day!

jobs.title: Director of Finance / Controller
jobs.description:
THE OPPORTUNITY

We have an exciting opportunity for a Director of Finance / Controller to join LITCO LSO, a growing organization with multiple entities. Reporting to the Chief Operating Officer and partnering closely with the Fractional Chief Financial Officer, this role provides leadership to the Finance and Accounting team while overseeing accounting operations, financial reporting, budgeting, audit coordination and finance activities across multiple entities.

This role is responsible for strengthening the accounting function, improving financial reporting, and establishing consistent finance processes. The position also supports acquisition integration and the ongoing development of financial controls, reporting standards and accounting practices across the organization.

THE IDEAL CANDIDATE

The ideal candidate is an experienced finance leader with a strong technical accounting foundation and demonstrated success leading accounting and finance functions within complex, multi entity organizations. This individual combines strong financial management, budgeting, audit oversight, and financial reporting expertise with the ability to establish structure, improve processes, and strengthen financial controls.

Comfortable working with senior leaders and strong personalities, this individual provides objective advice, constructive challenge, and practical solutions. Success in the role requires confidence, resilience, sound judgment, executive presence, and the professional maturity to communicate candidly, uphold strong financial practices, and navigate complex situations with credibility.

THE ORGANIZATION

Litco LSO is North America’s leading Legal Support Organization, partnering with high-performing law firms that share our commitment to excellence, innovation, and client-first service. Backed by institutional investors and built on a foundation of operational rigor, we provide the resources, infrastructure, and strategic guidance firms need to scale—without sacrificing their values or autonomy. Our platform includes shared services in finance, HR, IT, marketing, and compliance, freeing our partner firms to focus on what they do best: serving clients.

We’re redefining what it means to run a modern law firm. Whether through M&A integration, advanced technology, or culture-driven leadership, Litco helps legal teams move beyond outdated business models and toward a sustainable, future-ready approach. Our growing network spans multiple jurisdictions across Canada and the U.S., uniting like-minded firms under a shared mission: to build the most respected and forward-thinking legal organization on the continent.

For more information, please visit their website: www.litcolso.com

RESPONSIBILITIES

Financial Reporting & Accounting

Lead the organization’s accounting and financial reporting functions across multiple entities.
Oversee the preparation of consolidated financial statements and ensure consistent accounting practices.
Ensure the timely and accurate preparation of monthly, quarterly and annual financial statements.
Maintain effective accounting policies, controls and reporting standards.
Provide financial analysis and recommendations that support business performance and operational decision making.

Budgeting & Financial Planning

Lead the annual budgeting process and ongoing forecasting activities.
Monitor financial performance, analyze variances, and identify emerging risks and opportunities.
Lead monthly operating reviews with each business unit, partnering with executive leaders to review financial performance, budget variances, forecasts, and operational results in support of effective decision making.
Develop financial models and analysis to support planning, resource allocation, and organizational objectives.

Audit & Financial Oversight

Oversee the annual external audit process and act as the primary liaison with external auditors.
Coordinate audit planning, documentation, and the resolution of audit related matters.
Ensure financial policies, procedures, and controls are maintained and consistently applied.
Ensure compliance with applicable financial reporting, regulatory, and internal control requirements.

Mergers, Acquisitions & Integration

Support finance related activities associated with acquisitions and integrations.
Support finance due diligence and post acquisition integration activities, as required.
Assist in evaluating and integrating financial processes across acquired entities.
Promote consistency in financial reporting, controls, and accounting practices across multiple entities.

Systems & Process Improvement

Lead or support the implementation, optimization, and enhancement of financial systems and reporting tools.
Identify and implement opportunities to improve efficiency, accuracy, and effectiveness within the finance function.
Support technology and process improvement initiatives that strengthen financial management and operational effectiveness.

Leadership & Stakeholder Collaboration

Provide leadership, direction, and mentorship to the Finance and Accounting team.
Build and strengthen the team through coaching, mentoring, and succession planning.
Foster a culture of accountability, collaboration, and continuous improvement.
Build effective working relationships with senior leaders and key stakeholders.
Communicate financial information clearly, confidently and effectively to a variety of audiences.

QUALIFICATIONS

Bachelor's degree in Accounting, Finance, Commerce, Business Administration, or a related discipline.
CPA designation required.
Strong technical accounting foundation with experience preparing consolidated financial statements.
Minimum of 10 years of progressive experience in finance and accounting, including experience leading finance and accounting functions within a complex organization.
Demonstrated experience overseeing budgeting, forecasting, financial reporting, and year end audit activities.
Experience working within organizations that operate across multiple entities, business units, or corporate structures.
Demonstrated experience supporting mergers, acquisitions, and integration activities.
Experience leading and developing finance and accounting teams.
Experience supporting financial systems implementations, technology-enabled process improvements, or organizational transformation initiatives is considered an asset.
Strong understanding of accounting principles, financial reporting, financial controls, and financial management practices.

KEY COMPETENCIES

Demonstrates strong financial and business acumen, using analysis and sound judgment to support effective organizational decision making.
Communicates with confidence, credibility, and executive presence, effectively presenting financial information, recommendations and business insights to senior leaders and C-suite executives.
Builds trusted relationships and provides objective advice and constructive challenge, demonstrating the confidence and professional maturity to work effectively with senior leaders, strong personalities, and diverse stakeholder groups.
Exercises professionalism, discretion, and sound judgment when managing sensitive issues and competing priorities.
Leads teams through accountability, mentorship, and clear expectations, fostering a culture of engagement and performance.
Identifies opportunities to improve processes, strengthen controls, and enhance operational effectiveness.
Comfortable establishing structure and adapting to changing priorities in a growing organization.
Adapts effectively to changing priorities and organizational needs while maintaining a practical, solutions focused approach.
Demonstrates integrity, accountability, and professionalism in all aspects of leadership and financial stewardship.

Director, Finance, Provident10

St. John’s, NL

Are you a strategic, forward thinking finance leader ready to drive financial excellence, strengthen organizational performance, and make a lasting impact on the retirement security of thousands of Newfoundlanders and Labradorians?

The Company

Some would say we’re in the pension business. We like to say we’re in the people business. One that focuses on creating an inclusive and diverse culture for everyone who comes through our doors. One that puts our 68,000 members at the heart of everything we do because they deserve nothing less than a secure, stable future to build upon. One that can include YOU.

Provident10 is the largest pension plan in Newfoundland and Labrador and one of the largest pension plans in Atlantic Canada - representing 1 in 8 Newfoundlanders and Labradorians. Our team proudly oversees the pension administration and investment management of the over $13 billion Public Service Pension Plan Fund. Future Focused. People Centric. The foundation for our vision. For us that means creating a
seamless experience for members and a positive culture for our employees; ensuring the organization remains efficient and agile, as we continue to make smart investments for growth – all while embracing technology and ensuring a consistent experience for our members.

The Role

The Director, Finance is accountable for the leadership, management, and integrity of the corporate and investment fund finance function, including financial reporting, planning, controls, investment accounting, and transaction processing. The role ensures the delivery of accurate and timely financial information, robust internal controls, and compliance with applicable standards and regulatory requirements., The Director, Finance supports organizational decision-making through financial analysis and planning and provides operational leadership across all finance activities. The role serves as the primary internal authority on financial management and stewardship, while contributing to enterprise planning and supporting Board and committee reporting.

Key Responsibilities:

Financial Management & Reporting:
Oversees corporate and fund financial reporting, including fund accounting requirements and related financial statement preparation. Leads the preparation of quarterly, and annual financial statements and reports. Ensures accuracy, completeness, and timeliness of all financial reporting in accordance with applicable accounting standards. Oversees the financial close process, including general ledger integrity and reconciliations. Provides financial analysis and insights to support organizational performance and decision-making.

Investment Fund Accounting & Oversight:
Leads the organization’s investment accounting and financial reporting activities for the pension fund. Oversees portfolio reconciliation, investment valuation, performance reporting controls, and the integrity of investment-related financial information. Maintains oversight of investment accounting systems, private market reporting, management and performance fee monitoring, and foreign tax recovery activities. Ensures investment accounting processes are completed accurately, timely, and in compliance with applicable accounting standards, regulatory requirements, and internal policies. Supports Board and committee reporting by providing analysis and insights on investment-related financial matters.

Planning, Budgeting & Forecasting:
Leads the annual budgeting process, including the development, consolidation, and monitoring of both corporate and investment fund budgets. Works collaboratively with department leaders. Oversees ongoing forecasting activities, monitors financial performance through variance analysis and provides recommendations to support long-term financial planning and sustainability analysis.

Controls, Compliance & Risk Management:
Establishes and maintains a strong internal control framework. Ensures compliance with legislative, regulatory, and accounting requirements. Maintains oversight of applicable tax compliance, reporting, and related advisory requirements. Leads external audit processes and coordinates responses to audit findings. Develops and maintains financial policies, procedures, and governance frameworks.

Operational Finance Leadership:
Provides day-to-day leadership and oversight of the finance function. Ensures efficient and effective financial processes and identifies opportunities for improvement and automation. Maintains oversight of cash management, financial transactions, and organizational financial resources. Ensures appropriate segregation of duties and transactional controls across all finance activities.

Stakeholder Support & Advisory:
Supports in the development of Board and committee materials, including Audit & Finance Committee reporting. Provides financial guidance and decision support to leaders across the organization. Acts as a key liaison with external auditors and other financial stakeholders.

People Leadership:
Leads, develops, and mentors the finance team. Establishes clear performance expectations and supports professional development. Ensures appropriate resourcing and capability to meet current and future organizational needs.

The Ideal Candidate

You are a collaborative, member-focused leader who excels at breaking down silos and building high-performing cross-functional partnerships. You bring a track record of engaging diverse stakeholders, aligning priorities, and making thoughtful decisions that support the broader goals of Provident10. As a trusted advisor, you develop innovative, practical solutions to complex challenges while maintaining an unwavering commitment to service excellence and member needs.

You bring a strong foundation in financial reporting, governance, and stewardship, complemented by experience leading complex finance functions and supporting sound organizational decision making. Ideally, you have exposure to pension plans, institutional investment operations, fund accounting, or other complex investment environments. You understand the importance of robust financial controls, accurate investment reporting, effective oversight of external service providers, and the financial stewardship required to support a large long-term investment fund.

You foster a culture of continuous improvement by encouraging new ideas, sharing leading practices, and empowering others to think differently. Highly accountable and results-driven, you set clear goals, adapt resources and priorities effectively, and persist through obstacles to achieve outcomes. You communicate progress transparently, remove barriers to success, and inspire teams to deliver sustainable results that create value for members, customers, stakeholders, and the organization.

Qualifications and Experience

While the Search Committee recognizes that no one candidate is likely to meet all qualifications in equal measure, those listed below are desirable and will be used to compare candidates.

Undergraduate degree in Business, Finance, or a related discipline.
CPA designation.
8–12 years of progressive experience in finance, accounting, or related roles.
Demonstrated experience in financial reporting, budgeting, compliance and controls, and audit management.
Experience with pension plans, institutional investment management, investment fund accounting and reporting, investment operations, custodial arrangements, private-market investments, or other large and complex investment portfolios is considered a strong asset.
Proven leadership experience managing teams and finance operations

Skills and Attributes

Strong analytical and financial modelling capabilities.
Ability to translate financial information into actionable insights.
Strong communication skills with experience supporting senior leadership and governance bodies.
Knowledge / Strong knowledge of accounting standards and financial reporting requirements.
Expertise in internal controls, audit processes, and financial governance.

Most financial reporting functions are measured by whether deadlines are met. That’s important, but this role gets to decide what excellence looks like while meeting deadlines.

With accountability for external reporting and technical accounting, the Senior Director, Financial Reporting will play a defining role in advancing the reporting function of a Canadian-headquartered public manufacturing company. Reporting to the VP, Finance, this leader will oversee the full reporting cycle and strengthen the processes, controls, technical expertise and team required to support its continued evolution.

This is a hands-on leadership role for someone who can deliver against current reporting requirements while strengthening the function for the future. The successful candidate will bring experience from a rigorous public company reporting environment and the judgment to apply that experience within a Finance organization that continues to evolve.

The Mandate

The Senior Director will have end-to-end responsibility for quarterly and annual public company reporting under IFRS, ensuring financial statements, disclosures and supporting documentation meet the standards required of a public company.

The role will also serve as a key technical accounting resource across Finance, providing guidance on complex and non-routine matters and ensuring accounting positions are well considered, documented and communicated.

Key responsibilities include:
Lead quarterly and annual public company reporting, including the preparation and review of external financial statements and disclosures under IFRS.
Own the reporting process from planning through review and completion, with clear accountability for quality, accuracy and timelines.
Provide technical accounting leadership across Finance, interpreting and applying IFRS to complex and judgmental matters.
Prepare and review technical accounting memos covering areas such as goodwill, impairment and significant accounting estimates.
Support potential US GAAP considerations and the requirements associated with a potential conversion.
Provide accounting support for M&A transactions, integrations and divestitures as they arise.
Lead reporting and technical accounting discussions with external auditors, ensuring issues are properly analyzed, documented and resolved.
Strengthen reporting processes, controls, documentation and review standards.
Identify opportunities to create greater consistency, efficiency and discipline across the reporting function.
Lead, coach and develop the team, including a planned Senior Manager, Technical Accounting hire.
Partner closely with Finance and Tax on accounting and reporting matters.
Build effective relationships with senior leaders and C-suite stakeholders, communicating complex issues clearly and credibly.

What You Bring

You are a CPA/CA with progressive public company financial reporting experience and strong technical accounting capability. You understand the discipline required in a public company environment and have experience taking ownership of a reporting process from beginning to end.

Your background includes:
CPA/CA designation, ideally with a foundation in public accounting.
Progressive public company financial reporting experience with direct ownership of quarterly and annual reporting.
Strong IFRS technical accounting expertise and experience applying guidance to complex accounting matters.
Experience preparing and reviewing technical accounting memos on significant, judgmental and non-routine issues.
The technical depth and judgment required to support potential US GAAP conversion requirements.
Experience working directly with external auditors and supporting accounting positions through clear analysis and documentation.

jobs.title: Vice President, Product Management, Platform & Innovation
jobs.description:
At Appfire, we believe that great work happens when people get to choose how they work. After 20 years of creating software that empowers teams to break silos and collaborate seamlessly, we've learned that one size does not fit all. We’re a team of 800+ employees, working remotely across 28 countries. Our flagship products include: JXL, Comala Document Management, 7Pace Time Tracker, Jira Misc Workflow Extensions, and BigPicture.

 Here you can read some of our customer stories: https://appfire.com/resources/resource-library/customer-stories 

 Appfire is seeking a Vice President, Product Management, Platform & Innovation to lead three connected areas central to the company’s next phase of growth: the Appfire Platform, the Innovation portfolio, and Appfire’s technical product relationship with Atlassian.

 You will define the vision, strategy, and roadmap for the Appfire Platform, the shared services and AI capabilities that power our products, accelerate delivery, and create leverage across the portfolio. You will also lead the Innovation team, responsible for discovering, validating, incubating, and launching the next generation of Appfire products.

 As Appfire’s senior product leader for the technical dimension of our Atlassian relationship, you will anticipate platform, API, Forge, and Marketplace changes; represent Appfire in technical and roadmap discussions; and translate ecosystem shifts into competitive advantage, product opportunity, and managed risk.

 As a member of the Product Leadership Team, you will help shape strategy across the broader portfolio, translate company priorities into focused product bets, and build a high-performing team of product leaders. You will partner closely with Engineering, Go-to-Market, Finance, Legal, Security, and executive leadership.

 Success will be measured by the adoption and business impact of platform capabilities, the quality and velocity of the innovation pipeline, and the revenue and strategic value created by new products launched through your team.

 Key Accountabilities 

 Strategy and Portfolio Leadership 

 Partner with executive leadership to establish a compelling vision for the Appfire Platform and new-product portfolio as part of the broader company strategy.

 Translate that vision into a clear investment thesis, product roadmap, measurable objectives, and operating plan.

 Make disciplined decisions about where to build, buy, partner, invest, scale, or stop.

 Maintain a clear view of progress, risks, dependencies, and tradeoffs, adjusting priorities as market and business conditions change.

 Communicate strategy, decisions, and outcomes clearly across executive, technical, and business audiences.

 Platform Product Leadership 

 Treat the Appfire Platform as a product, with defined customers, value propositions, roadmaps, adoption goals, and success measures.

 Define and deliver shared platform capabilities, including AI-enabled services, that increase customer value, enable revenue growth, accelerate product delivery, and reduce duplicated effort.

 Drive adoption across Appfire by reducing integration friction, establishing effective rollout and migration plans, and partnering closely with product and engineering teams.

 Establish metrics for platform adoption, reliability, cost efficiency, developer experience, time to market, and business impact.

 Build strong feedback loops with internal product teams and other platform users to ensure the roadmap addresses their highest-value needs.

 Communicate and demonstrate the value of the platform throughout the organization.

 Innovation and New Growth 

 Lead the Innovation team in identifying, validating, incubating, and launching net-new product opportunities.

 Build and actively manage a portfolio of product bets aligned with customer needs, market opportunity, and Appfire’s strategic advantages.

 Apply a disciplined 0-to-1 approach to customer discovery, market validation, experimentation, business-case development, and commercial launch.

 Establish clear stage gates and evidence-based criteria for advancing, changing, scaling, or stopping investments.

 Partner with Go-to-Market leaders on positioning, pricing, packaging, launch, and early commercial traction.

 Own the path from initial concept to measurable customer adoption and revenue.

 Transition validated products into the appropriate scaling organization when they are ready to move beyond incubation.

 Atlassian Technical Relationship 

 Serve as Appfire’s senior product owner for the technical dimension of the Atlassian relationship.

 Represent Appfire in technical, platform, and roadmap discussions with Atlassian.

 Maintain a forward-looking view of changes to Atlassian’s platform, APIs, Forge architecture, Marketplace, security requirements, and developer ecosystem.

 Translate ecosystem changes into product opportunities, competitive differentiation, internal readiness plans, and risk mitigation.

 Influence Atlassian’s technical direction where possible by clearly representing Appfire’s needs, customer use cases, and strategic priorities.

 Ensure relevant Product, Engineering, Security, Legal, and business teams understand upcoming changes and are prepared to respond.

 People and Organizational Leadership 

 Lead, develop, and grow a team of product managers and product leaders responsible for the Appfire Platform and Innovation portfolio.

 Set clear expectations for product strategy, customer insight, commercial thinking, execution quality, and accountability.

 Recruit and retain strong product talent while building a durable leadership bench and succession pipeline.

 Coach team members to take on broader and more complex product leadership responsibilities.

 Establish an effective operating cadence for planning, decision-making, performance management, and cross-functional alignment.

 Communicate progress, outcomes, risks, and decisions effectively at every level of the organization.

 About You
