The Alberta Public Service works to build a stronger province for current and future generations. We make a difference in the lives of Albertans through rewarding and diverse career opportunities.

Technology and Innovation is responsible for making innovation and technology the driving force behind Alberta’s economic growth and diversification. To learn more about us, please visit: https://www.alberta.ca/technology-and-innovation.aspx .

The passionate and solutions focused people that we hire help us to drive vital programs and services that affect Albertans. Whatever your position is here, you will be a part of something great. Join us!

Role Responsibilities

Lead The Cloud. Enable What’s Next.

As Director, Cloud Platform, you will provide strategic leadership for the Government of Alberta’s cloud and digital platform services, enabling secure, scalable, reliable, and modern technology solutions across government. You will set the vision, priorities, and outcomes for a portfolio spanning cloud platforms, identity and authentication, messaging, web hosting, and related foundational services.

Reporting to the Executive Director, Business Technology Operations, you will lead a diverse team and work closely with senior leaders across IMT, business partners, and technology vendors to align services with government priorities, client needs, security and risk requirements, and fiscal and contractual obligations. You will foster a collaborative, agile, and innovative culture while ensuring service availability, continuity, and operational excellence.

Responsibilities

Some of the responsibilities of this position include, but are not limited to:

Service/Platform Ownership

Lead the strategy, delivery, and lifecycle management of key technology services and platforms. Manage resources, budgets, contracts, vendors, and service agreements. Engage senior business leaders to align services with ministry priorities and client needs. Ensure services meet applicable security, privacy, legal, information management, and architectural standards. Oversee service performance, escalations, change management, and continuous improvement.

Leadership, Planning and Implementation

Lead workforce, financial, and operational planning to deliver effective technology services. Align priorities and resources across teams and stakeholders. Direct implementation of new solutions, projects, and services. Monitor performance, address issues, and report on progress and outcomes.

Service Level Management

Ensure services meet client and stakeholder needs and agreed service levels. Monitor service performance and drive improvements in service delivery. Contribute to GoA-wide service standards and practices.

Architecture and Standards

Provide direction on technology, architecture, standards, and processes across the portfolio. Ensure solutions align with GoA standards, approved environments, and business requirements. Advance modernization, innovation, and integration of technology services.

Risk Management

Identify, assess, and mitigate risks affecting services and initiatives. Provide leadership on risks related to cost, schedule, quality, security, and technical performance. Collaborate with Cybersecurity and other partners to address technology and security risks.

Unit Leadership and Operations

Develop and execute operational plans aligned with ministry and GoA priorities. Lead staffing, performance, workforce planning, and employee development. Oversee financial management, procurement, contracts, vendors, and service agreements. Foster a collaborative, inclusive, agile, and innovative workplace culture. Oversee executive briefings, correspondence, and other decision-support materials.

Branch and Division Leadership

Provide strategic advice and recommendations to executive leaders. Report on branch plans, performance, and outcomes to support division and ministry priorities. Collaborate across branches, divisions, and departments to advance shared priorities and service delivery. Drive collaboration, innovation, efficiency, and continuous improvement. Serve as Acting Executive Director, as required.

AI Stewardship

This role is designed with an AI-first mindset, requiring the successful candidate to leverage AI-powered tools and capabilities to strengthen stakeholder engagement through automated insights, personalized communications, and enhanced collaboration; create tailored, high-impact materials that align with stakeholder needs using AI-assisted content generation and feedback analysis; and develop, monitor, and refine key performance indicators.

To Be Successful In This Position You Will Demonstrate

Exceptional communication, consultation, and engagement skills, with the ability to adapt approaches for diverse audiences.
Strong political acumen and sensitivity, with the ability to navigate complex and sensitive situations effectively.
Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, including the ability to assess complex and competing issues and develop practical recommendations.
Expertise in building productive relationships across the ministry, Government of Alberta, partner organizations, and key stakeholders.
Experience in leading and managing a variety of projects and processes and delivering high quality results within established timelines.
Embraces technology and data by using AI-powered tools and performance metrics to inform strategy, measure success, and optimize delivery.

The Job Description is provided for further details on this position.

Systems Thinking: You will consider how work completed can impact various other groups/projects inside and outside the Alberta Public Service.
Agility: Proactively incorporates change into processes. Creates opportunities for improvement. Is aware of and adapts to changing priorities. Remains objective under pressure and supports others to manage their emotions. Proactively explains impact of change on roles and integrates change in existing work. Readily adapts plans and practices.
Develop self and others: A commitment to lifelong learning and the desire to invest in the development of the long-term capability of yourself and others.
Build Collaborative Environments: Collaborates across functional areas and proactively addresses conflict. Encourages broad thinking on projects and works to eliminate barriers to progress. Facilitates communication and collaboration. Anticipates and reduces conflict at the outset. Credits others and gets talent recognized. Promotes collaboration and commitment.
Develop Networks: Leverages relationships to build input and perspective. Looks broadly to engage stakeholders. Open to perspectives towards long-term goals. Actively seeks input into change initiatives. Maintains stakeholder relationships.

Head of Digital Marketing – Vanguard Canada

The Head of Digital Marketing for Canada will shape and lead the digital strategy that connects investors and advisors to Vanguard's products, insights, and thought leadership. This leader will play a critical role in advancing Vanguard's mission to give clients the best chance for investment success by creating meaningful, data-driven digital experiences that drive engagement, acquisition, and retention.

The ideal candidate will bring extensive experience leading digital marketing organizations within the financial services industry, with a strong understanding of investor and advisor audiences, financial products, regulatory considerations, and the unique dynamics of the wealth and asset management landscape. They will combine strategic vision with hands-on digital marketing expertise to deliver measurable business outcomes and elevate Vanguard's digital capabilities.

Responsibilities:

Develop and execute a comprehensive digital marketing strategy across paid, owned, and earned channels to support Vanguard Canada's growth objectives.
Establish leading digital marketing practices, optimize performance across the customer journey, and improve return on investment for key business partners.
Build and maintain a best-in-class digital marketing ecosystem that supports personalized, connected experiences for both advisor and investor audiences.
Lead the evolution of content and digital engagement strategies, ensuring communications are timely, relevant, compliant, and personalized across all channels.
Manage the paid media budget across campaign-based and always-on programs, maximizing efficiency and business impact.
Define analytics and measurement frameworks that provide clear attribution, actionable insights, and a comprehensive view of marketing performance.
Leverage customer, campaign, and market data to inform strategy, improve targeting, and deepen customer engagement.
Partner with Marketing Technology, Data, and IT teams to develop an integrated marketing technology architecture aligned with Vanguard's global design standards and future-state vision.
Evaluate emerging digital marketing and marketing technology solutions, including customer data platforms, artificial intelligence, and machine learning capabilities, to continuously enhance Vanguard's digital marketing effectiveness.
Lead, coach, and develop a high-performing team of digital marketing professionals while fostering a collaborative and inclusive team culture.
Manage agency and vendor partnerships to ensure strong performance, accountability, innovation, and alignment with business goals.

10+ years of progressive marketing leadership experience, including significant digital marketing leadership experience within financial services, asset management, wealth management, banking, insurance, or a related financial institution.
Demonstrated success developing and executing large-scale digital marketing strategies that drive measurable business outcomes, customer acquisition, engagement, and retention.
Deep expertise across digital marketing disciplines, including paid media, digital acquisition, customer journey optimization, marketing automation, personalization, analytics, and marketing technology.
Strong understanding of advisor and investor audiences, financial products, and the regulatory environment governing financial services marketing.
Proven experience managing substantial digital marketing budgets and external agency/vendor relationships.
Experience operating in complex, global, matrixed organizations and influencing senior stakeholders across functions and geographies.
Undergraduate degree required; MBA or other advanced degree preferred.
Proficiency in English required; French language skills are an asset.

Recognized digital marketing leader with a track record of transforming digital capabilities and driving growth within the financial services industry.
Strategic thinker with strong analytical, commercial, and execution skills.
Passion for leveraging data, technology, and innovation to enhance the customer experience and business outcomes.

The Director of Finance is a senior management position assigned to either the Department of Justice & Public Safety or the Departments of Economic Development, Trade & Artificial Intelligence/Workforce and Advanced Learning and is responsible to advise and support the Minister and Deputy Ministers. The Director provides senior management leadership in the financial administration of the Department, and provides oversight, direction and advice to maintain financial accountability for the Department.

The Director is responsible for all aspects of the Department’s financial and corporate management, including budgeting and financial planning, forecasting and financial reporting, internal controls, contracts and contribution agreements, compliance with Treasury Board Policies & Procedures, and Executive Council / Treasury Board Memoranda.

The Director provides advice to the Ministers, Deputy Ministers and Directors of the Department on all initiatives, programs and activities.

The Director and other staff assigned to the Department will provide financial support for capital projects and contract negotiations.

Duties will include but are not limited to:

Provide overall direction and leadership on the financial administration of the Department;
Direct the budget planning, forecasting and reporting processes, and provide leadership in setting financial objectives for the Department;
Advise and assist directors and managers in quarterly forecasting and annual budget preparations;
Develop annual departmental Operating and Capital Budgets;
Develop and monitor an appropriate system of internal controls to help safeguard the department and further its objectives. An effective system of internal controls function to minimize risks and protect assets, ensure accuracy of records, promote operational efficiency, and encourage adherence to policies, regulations, and legislation;
Provide high quality advice, assistance, and information to the Minister, Deputy Minister, and Department Divisions pertaining to the financial implications on strategic and operational planning;
Provide expert, contextualized advice on the financial implications for current policy and legislation and provide leadership and direction to planning, policy analysis and development, and legislative initiatives;
Provide overall direction and leadership to the financial administration of Capital projects;

Directing work plans and managing performance;
Other related duties.

jobs.title: Chief Technology Officer
jobs.description:
BE AT THE FOREFRONT OF CANADA'S CLEAN ENERGY TRANSFORMATION.

Salient Energy Inc. is advancing the next generation of safe, sustainable energy storage technology. Our zinc-ion batteries are designed to accelerate the global shift toward renewable power, providing a safer, more cost-effective, and scalable alternative to lithium-ion.

We're looking for a results-driven, technically savvy Chief Technology Officer who understands the pace, complexity, and challenges of a startup environment and brings a genuine passion for clean tech energy. As we move into the heart of commercialization, this leader will drive the continued advancement of our zinc-ion battery platform, aligning technology, execution, and team leadership to support scale, market readiness, and commercial success.

THE ROLE

Reporting to the CEO, the Chief Technology Officer will provide strategic and hands-on leadership across Salient Energy's technology function at a critical stage in the company's growth, balancing deep technical expertise with the operational and commercial oversight needed to advance through commercialization.

Leading the RCD, Cell Development, and Quality teams, the CTO will align technical direction, cross-functional execution, and team capability to support scale, certification, market readiness, and accelerated commercial success. As a member of the executive team, this leader will foster a strong, accountable, and collaborative culture while also serving as a trusted technical voice with the Board, investors, and external partners.

What You Will Do

Lead Salient's technology function by providing strategic and technical leadership across RCD, Cell Development, and Quality.
Define and deliver product specifications, technical priorities, and performance metrics aligned with Salient's technology roadmap and TRL targets.
Support the successful advancement of Salient's battery platform through commercialization, including readiness for scale, certification, and market adoption.
Ensure required product and process certifications, including UL and CSA standards, are achieved.
Represent Salient externally as a credible technical leader with the Board, investors, partners, and at relevant industry and technical forums.

Your Skills, Education & Experience

Education & Technical Depth

PhD in Chemistry, Chemical or Mechanical Engineering, or Materials Science/Engineering.
Deep expertise in battery chemistry, electrochemistry, and testing processes, supported by 10+ years in a chemistry lab environment.
Experience with advanced battery materials and ion transport mechanisms is considered an asset.

Product Development & Commercialization

8-10 years leading development projects, with demonstrated experience bringing new products to market.
Proven ability to align technical priorities with commercialization milestones, performance goals, and market needs.

Leadership Profile

Strategic & Commercial Acumen - able to connect technical direction to commercialization, scale, and business goals.
Technical & Operational Leadership - brings rigor, focus, and accountability across complex technical programs.
People & Stakeholder Influence - builds strong teams and communicates credibly with employees, executives, investors, and partners.

THE IDEAL CANDIDATE

The ideal candidate brings the technical depth and scientific credibility expected of a CTO, along with the leadership, operational oversight, and commercial mindset needed to advance Salient's technology through commercialization. While technical capability is essential, success in this role will depend on the ability to translate innovation into practical commercial application, aligning technical priorities with business objectives, supporting teams with clarity and accountability, and sustaining momentum toward scale, market readiness, and performance. This leader will understand how to balance thoughtful refinement and continuous innovation with the urgency required to meet business goals and move the product forward.

Excellent communication skills, with the ability to mentor teams and translate complex technical concepts into clear business value.

WHY SALIENT?

At Salient, you'll work alongside a team of scientists, engineers, and innovators who are deeply committed to building a safer, cleaner energy future. We believe the best ideas come from curiosity, collaboration, and continuous learning. As CTO, you will play a defining leadership role in shaping our technology strategy, strengthening our technical organization, and advancing our products toward market adoption. Your work will directly influence how Salient scales its zinc-ion platform and delivers meaningful impact in one of the world's most important sectors: clean energy storage.

We offer a competitive salary and a collegiate, supportive, and diverse team environment. Here, you'll have the opportunity to lead meaningful innovation, develop exceptional teams, and help build a technology company positioned to make a real difference.

TO APPLY

If you're ready to lead the advancement of future-defining battery technology, we'd love to hear from you. Please submit your resume and a compelling cover letter outlining your fit for this role for an initial review.

We embrace inclusion and diversity and welcome applicants to self-identify. Please feel free to indicate if you belong or self-identify. Please note this is an on-site position and requires the successful candidate be in, or relocate to HRM. All applications will be reviewed, but only those selected for an interview will be contacted.

jobs.description:
The Nova Scotia Nursing and Midwifery Regulator
(NSNMR) protects the public by regulating licensed practical nurses, registered nurses, registered psychiatric nurses, nurse practitioners, and registered midwives across Nova Scotia.

As the largest health profession regulator in Atlantic Canada, NSNMR is entering a pivotal stage in its evolution. Building on the transition to the Regulated Health Professions Act and the integration of nursing and midwifery regulation, the organization is focused on strengthening its operational foundations, modernizing systems and processes, advancing data-informed decision making, and positioning itself as a leading regulator within the region.

To support this important work, NSNMR is seeking a Director of Finance
.

This is an exceptional opportunity for a strategic and collaborative finance leader to contribute to an organization dedicated to public protection and regulatory excellence. The Director of Finance will help guide the organization's long-term financial sustainability while providing the financial insight, stewardship, and leadership required to support informed decision-making, effective governance, and organizational success.

The Role

Reporting to the Senior Director, Corporate Services, the Director of Finance provides leadership and oversight for NSNMR's financial operations, planning, reporting, audit, risk management, and internal controls. As a member of the leadership team, the Director serves as a trusted advisor to senior leadership and the Board, providing strategic financial guidance that supports effective decision-making, strong governance, and long-term organizational sustainability. Working closely with leaders across the organization, the Director helps ensure financial resources are aligned with strategic priorities and supports a culture of accountability, stewardship, and continuous improvement.

Key Responsibilities

Leading NSNMR's financial planning, budgeting, forecasting, and reporting processes to support organizational priorities and long-term sustainability.
Providing strategic financial advice and analysis to support executive and Board decision-making, governance, and resource allocation.
Overseeing all financial operations, including accounting, payroll, investments, cash management, audit, and financial reporting.
Ensuring effective financial controls, compliance practices, and risk management frameworks are in place to safeguard organizational resources.
Supporting organizational planning and performance by translating financial information into meaningful insights for leaders across the organization.
Building and maintaining productive relationships with the Board, auditors, financial institutions, and other external partners.
Leading and developing the finance team while fostering a culture of accountability, collaboration, and continuous improvement.

Ideal Candidate Profile

As the ideal candidate, you are a strategic and accomplished finance leader with a Chartered Professional Accountant (CPA) designation and progressive experience leading finance functions within complex organizations. You bring expertise in financial planning and analysis, budgeting, forecasting, reporting, audit, risk management, and internal controls, along with experience providing financial advice and insight to senior leaders and Boards.

You combine strong financial stewardship with sound business judgment and a collaborative leadership style. Comfortable navigating complexity and change, you use financial insight to support decision-making, long-term planning, and organizational sustainability.

An effective communicator and relationship builder, you excel at translating complex financial information into practical insights and building trusted partnerships with colleagues, executives, Board members, and external stakeholders. Experience in a regulated, healthcare, public sector, or not-for-profit environment would be considered an asset.

How to Apply

Technical Strategy & Architecture

Establish consistent technical practices, knowledge-sharing, and training opportunities across portfolio teams.

Position:
                   Director of Finance and Administration
Location:
                  Martin Luther University College, Waterloo, Ontario

1 - 2 roles

:                  December 2026

This is an existing vacancy.

Position Summary

Martin Luther University College (Luther) is a public university college federated with Wilfrid Laurier University. We are a faith-based academic community committed to excellence in teaching, research, and community engagement.

The Director of Finance and Administration provides strategic and operational leadership for Luther’s financial and administrative functions. Reporting to the Principal-Dean, the Director is responsible for financial reporting, compliance, planning and budgeting, internal controls, and administrative systems that support the long-term financial sustainability of the institution and its mission.

Responsibilities

Leadership of Financial Planning, Management, and Reporting

Ensure all necessary financial operations (including the operating budget), reporting, cash management, expenditure controls and other controls are in place and operating effectively to support Luther’s operations and the Board’s fiduciary obligations.
Prepare financial analysis and reports as needed including operating statements (revenues and expenditures), budget forecasts, and forecast of cash flow for use by the Principal-Dean, responsible managers or faculty, and the Finance Committee to support informed decision-making and organizational accountability for a $4 Million operating budget.
Manage the allocation of annual realized gains from endowment funds and reconcile investment manager’s reports for endowed and non-endowed investments, resolving discrepancies.
Take the initiative to manage investment transactions required as part of the annual budget or operations. Coordinate the flow of investment deposits and investment income with investment manager. Liaise with Luther’s investment manager and/or Finance Committee on investment issues for accounting purposes.
Prepare annual unaudited financial statements and all reconciliations, supporting schedules, background reporting, and year end entries and adjustments required for the annual audit; prepare an audit package and manage the annual audit with the external auditors once per year, including: Schedule the audit and associated activities, Negotiate the audit contract for recommendation to the Finance Committee, Manage Luther’s elements of the process, Ensure a clean audit
Assist Luther’s staff and faculty in understanding and using relevant financial information. Support them in budget development for their areas or projects.
Understand in detail and make recommendations to enhance the funding agreements between Luther and Wilfrid Laurier University and be able to advise the Principal-Dean on the implications to annual revenue of proposed revisions to these agreements.
Maximize the use of accounting software reporting capabilities where possible.
Manage the financial elements of grant projects, supporting the assigned project manager in planning and tracking financial commitments, and in financial reporting for the project.
Prepare and submit annual financial and statistical reporting required by external organizations such as Canada Revenue Agency (Registered Charity Information Return -- T3010, HST), Council of Ontario Universities (detailed analytical financial report), Association of Theological Schools, and others as required. Consult with these organizations regarding reporting requirements as necessary. 
Develop the annual capital budget (including equipment) for Board approval to maintain the Luther’s physical assets and avoid undue deferred maintenance.
Oversee the implementation of the capital budget.
Manage the financial elements of capital and construction projects.

General Administration

Act as the Chief Compliance Officer for reporting and legal requirements.

Policy Coordination and Board Support

Coordinate policy needs and improvements with the Principal-Dean to ensure all operational and board policies are consistently organized, reviewed, updated, and in compliance.

Support to the Principal-Dean

Support the activities of the Principal-Dean through research, high-level project/program development and implementation, implementation of confidential activities and other areas as they arise from time to time.

Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in Accounting, Finance, Business Administration, or a related field
CPA designation
A minimum of 5 years of progressive experience in finance or accounting
A minimum of 3 years of leadership or management experience
Ability to lead strategically while maintaining hands-on responsibility for day-to-day financial and administrative operations in a lean organizational environment
Ability to work effectively within a governance-based environment, supporting boards and collaborating with diverse interest holders
Experience in a post-secondary institution, public sector, or medium non-profit organization is preferred
Strong knowledge of public sector and/or fund accounting
Advanced financial planning, budgeting, and analytical skills
Ability to communicate complete financial information clearly to non-financial interest holders
Strong leadership, collaboration and relationship-management skills
High level of integrity, judgment, and professional discretion
Experience with enterprise resource planning and financial reporting systems

Working Conditions

This position is based primarily in an in-office environment and requires regular on-site presence during standard business hours. The role involves extended periods of computer work, frequent interaction with staff, leadership and external partners, and coordination of multiple operational priorities. Occasional evening or weekend work may be required to support meetings or organizational needs. The position requires the ability to manage competing deadlines, maintain confidentiality, and respond to evolving organizational priorities in a collaborative workplace setting.

This role requires extended periods of sitting and computer use, including keyboarding and screen work. The position may involve light physical activity such as moving between office spaces, attending meetings, and occasionally lifting or moving materials (up to approximately 10–20 lbs). The ability to communicate effectively in person and through digital platforms is required.

TO APPLY

To apply, please submit your resume and cover letter in one file
to search@luther.wlu.ca by November 4, 2026
. Please insert “Director of Finance and Administration”
in the subject line.

Candidates selected for an interview will be required to provide three professional references.

The organization is committed to providing an inclusive and accessible workplace. Reasonable accommodation will be provided throughout the recruitment process and employment in accordance with applicable accessibility and human rights legislation.

Martin Luther University College is committed to diversity and creating a culture of inclusion by increasing the diversity of faculty and staff and welcomes applications from qualified members of the equity-deserving groups. The College welcomes applications from all qualified candidates regardless of race nationality, gender-affiliation or sexual orientation.  All qualified candidates are encouraged to apply.

Candidate provided information is used for recruitment purposes only and will not be shared with outside agencies. Information will be retained for a minimum of two years for the sole purpose of applicant review and future recruitment.

Terms of Appointment:

This is a management position as an employee of Martin Luther University College. Luther employees are not employees of Wilfrid Laurier University.

ABOUT LUTHER

Martin Luther University College (formerly Waterloo Lutheran Seminary) is in Waterloo, Ontario and federated with Wilfrid Laurier University. As a federated college, Luther has its own Board of Governors which oversees the work of the institution, supporting its mission of education for a life of meaning and service through spiritually integrated education. Luther offers academic programming at the undergraduate, graduate, and graduate diploma levels. Our small class sizes and dedicated learning space help create a special sense of community where people connect closely with each other.

Students

Approximately 250 students are enrolled in Luther’s programs at any one time, and another 300 undergraduate students, registered at Wilfrid Laurier University, enroll in Luther courses as electives. Luther students come from a variety of different faith traditions while some have no faith tradition at all.

Faculty & Staff

Luther is comprised of thirteen full- and part-time faculty members, along with approximately 20 adjunct faculty who teach on a term-by-term basis. The school is supported by a team of eight full-time staff members working in communications, student services, and administration departments, and another 10 staff members working in part-time and program-related positions.

Centres at Martin Luther University College

The Centres of Luther offer programming at the intersection of scholarship and community engagement. Administratively, the Centres fall within Luther’s finance and administration portfolio, which supports their operations. Our largest centre is The Glebe Counselling Centre, a not-for-profit, multifaith counselling agency committed to strengthening emotional and spiritual well-being.

About Cortel Group

Cortel Group is an established real estate development company specializing in high-rise residential condominiums, commercial developments, and purpose-built rental communities throughout the Greater Toronto Area.

We are seeking an experienced, analytical, and proactive Director, Development Finance & Accounting
to lead the financial management of our development portfolio, oversee accounting operations, and provide strategic financial guidance directly to company leadership and partners.

This is a hands-on leadership position combining real estate development finance, project feasibility analysis, financial reporting, and team management. The successful candidate will play an important role in evaluating development opportunities, monitoring project performance, identifying financial risks, and improving the effectiveness of the Finance Department.

Development Finance & Feasibility Analysis

Develop, maintain, and evaluate detailed development pro formas, financial models, cash flow projections, and investment return analyses.
Conduct sensitivity and scenario analyses to assess the impact of changes in construction costs, development charges, financing rates, sales prices, rental rates, absorption, and project timelines.
Evaluate project profitability, financial viability, capital requirements, and investment risks.
Provide financial analysis, recommendations, and strategic insights directly to company leadership and partners to support acquisition, development, financing, and investment decisions.

Monitor project financial performance throughout the development lifecycle, from acquisition and construction through occupancy, stabilization, and final closing.
Oversee construction financing, lender reporting, and construction draw requirements.
Identify budget discrepancies, financial exposures, and opportunities for cost optimization.
Prepare and present timely, accurate financial reports and project performance updates to company leadership and partners.

Accounting & Team Leadership

Oversee financial reporting, reconciliations, intercompany transactions, and accounting across multiple corporate entities.
Maintain strong financial controls and ensure compliance with applicable accounting standards and regulatory requirements.
Coordinate with internal departments, financial institutions, auditors, legal advisors, and external consultants.
Establish clear reporting expectations, performance standards, and accountability within the accounting team.

Financial Reporting & Process Improvement

Evaluate existing financial reporting procedures, accounting systems, and project tracking processes.
Identify and implement opportunities to streamline workflows, improve accuracy, and increase departmental efficiency.
Develop consistent reporting frameworks that provide leadership with clear visibility into project budgets, cash flow, profitability, and financial risks.
Strengthen internal controls, reporting timelines, and financial accountability.
Proactively recommend improvements to financial management practices and operational processes.

Qualifications & Experience

8–12+ years of progressive accounting and finance experience, preferably within real estate development or construction.
Significant experience in high-rise residential development accounting and finance; exposure to commercial and purpose-built rental developments is an asset.
Demonstrated experience preparing development feasibility studies, financial models, sensitivity analyses, and project cash flow forecasts.
Strong understanding of real estate development economics, construction financing, development costs, and investment return metrics.
Proven experience managing multiple project budgets and overseeing financial reporting across multiple corporate entities.
Demonstrated leadership experience supervising and developing accounting personnel.
Strong financial modelling capabilities and advanced Microsoft Excel skills.
Experience implementing improvements to financial reporting, accounting systems, and internal processes.
Excellent analytical, organizational, communication, and problem-solving abilities.

We are looking for a commercially minded, hands-on financial leader who takes ownership, exercises sound judgment, and proactively identifies opportunities to improve financial performance and operational efficiency.

This is a full-time, in-person position. The CTO will play a central role in establishing and leading Martell Ventures' Waterloo technical hub.

Salary:
$150,000- $250,000 CAD base.

The opportunity also includes a proposed portfolio-level phantom equity component designed to align long-term incentives with the performance and success of the Ventures portfolio. Final terms are subject to confirmation.

About Martell Group

The Martell Group exists to build people, brands, and ventures that create meaningful impact. Across our four companies, we combine audience, operators, and execution to launch scalable products and empower ambitious leaders in Media, B2B SaaS, and AI.

Founded by serial entrepreneur and investor Dan Martell (investor in Udemy, Intercom, and Unbounce), we're building a company that values leadership, growth, and simplicity, and we're looking for people who live those values too.

Our goal is to attract world-class talent and align people where their impact is greatest. When you apply to Martell Group, you'll automatically be considered for all open roles across our companies, not just the one you applied for.

Position Responsibilities

Martell Ventures is looking for a highly technical builder and strategic thinker to lead engineering excellence across its growing portfolio of businesses.

This is not a traditional CTO role focused solely on executive oversight. We need someone who can think strategically, challenge assumptions, and get directly involved in the technical work when it matters most.

You will be the technical authority across the Ventures portfolio, helping companies build better products, solve complex engineering challenges, strengthen technical teams, and move faster with modern AI and agentic development.

You'll work closely with Dan Martell, portfolio business leaders, and experienced technology advisors to turn ambitious ideas into practical, scalable solutions.

A significant part of your mandate will be establishing Martell Ventures' technical presence in Waterloo, building a strong local engineering community, and creating the standards that enable our portfolio companies to scale.

This is an opportunity to shape how multiple businesses build, operate, and grow while remaining close to the technology itself.

What You'll Do

Technical Strategy & Architecture

Evaluate the technical infrastructure, architecture, codebases, and engineering practices across portfolio companies, identifying opportunities to improve quality, security, scalability, and performance.
Work directly with engineering teams to diagnose technical challenges, improve architecture, and implement practical solutions.
Establish consistent engineering standards, shared development practices, frameworks, and tooling across the portfolio.
Drive adoption of modern AI and agentic development practices to improve engineering speed, efficiency, and product delivery.
Ensure portfolio companies maintain appropriate technical infrastructure, security practices, backups, and operational resilience.
Help portfolio leaders understand technical risks, opportunities, and priorities so they can make informed business decisions.
Support technical readiness for future acquisitions, investment opportunities, and potential exits.

Building & Developing Technical Talent

Establish and grow Martell Ventures' technical presence in Kitchener-Waterloo.
Help recruit, assess, and develop exceptional engineering talent across the portfolio.
Partner with portfolio business leaders on technical hiring decisions, including engineering leads and senior technical positions.
Provide technical guidance and mentorship to portfolio engineering leaders while maintaining a dotted-line relationship with those leaders.
Establish consistent technical practices, knowledge-sharing, and training opportunities across portfolio teams.
Develop relationships with the University of Waterloo, Communitech, and the broader Waterloo technology ecosystem to build a sustainable talent pipeline.
Collaborate with Waterloo-based technology advisors Michael Litt and Marcelo Cortes to strengthen the group's engineering capabilities and local network.

Product Development & Execution

Translate ambitious business ideas into practical technical plans with clear priorities, realistic timelines, and measurable outcomes.
Provide hands-on technical support when portfolio companies face complex engineering challenges or execution bottlenecks.
Evaluate build-versus-buy decisions and help prioritize technical investments based on business value.
Support engineering teams in delivering reliable, scalable products that meet customer needs.
Identify opportunities to share technical capabilities, infrastructure, and resources across portfolio businesses.
Balance long-term technical architecture with the immediate needs of fast-moving businesses.

Strategic Partnership & Leadership

Serve as a trusted technical thought partner to Dan Martell and the Ventures leadership team.
Bring independent technical judgment, including the confidence to challenge ideas, push back on unrealistic commitments, and recommend alternative approaches.
Help establish a culture of technical excellence, accountability, and continuous improvement.
Work across multiple businesses and priorities while maintaining a clear focus on the highest-impact opportunities.
Communicate technical decisions, risks, and progress clearly to both technical and nontechnical stakeholders.
Lead by example through a combination of strategic thinking, practical execution, and strong technical credibility.

What You Bring

We are looking for someone with exceptional technical depth, strong product judgment, and the ability to build in fast-moving environments.

You may have held a CTO or VP of Engineering position, or you may be an exceptional Staff Engineer, Principal Engineer, or technical founder ready to take on broader responsibility.

What matters most is your ability to solve difficult technical problems, raise engineering standards, and build products that work.

Deep hands-on experience in software engineering, systems architecture, and building scalable production applications.
Recent, practical experience developing with modern AI technologies, LLMs, agents, and agentic development tools.
Demonstrated ability to evaluate existing software architecture, identify technical weaknesses, and implement effective solutions.
Strong technical credibility and the ability to work directly with experienced engineers on complex technical challenges.
Experience building and shipping software products in startup, scale-up, or similarly fast-moving environments.
Strong product and business judgment, with an understanding of how technical decisions affect customers, revenue, and growth.
Experience assessing engineering talent, making technical hiring decisions, and helping build high-performing teams.
Ability to balance technical quality with speed, pragmatism, and commercial priorities.
Confidence working with strong founder personalities and challenging ideas when necessary.
Strong communication skills, with the ability to translate complex technical concepts into clear business recommendations.
High ownership, adaptability, and comfort operating across multiple businesses with changing priorities.

Preferred:

Previous experience as a CTO, technical co-founder, VP of Engineering, or senior technical leader.
Experience supporting multiple products, portfolio companies, or venture-backed businesses.
Experience building or scaling an engineering function from an early stage.
Involvement in a successful company exit or technical due diligence process.
Existing connections within the Waterloo technology ecosystem, including the University of Waterloo or Communitech.
Experience establishing engineering standards and shared infrastructure across multiple teams.

Our Ideal Teammate Is Someone Who:

Is a builder at heart and genuinely enjoys getting into the technical details.
Is excited by the pace of change in AI and is actively experimenting with emerging tools and technologies.
Can move comfortably between high-level strategy and hands-on execution.

We’re a team of progressive thinkers and agile doers operating within a fast-paced culture of collaboration and respect. We believe in bringing smart and capable people together to create, solve, and grow with a clear shared vision and values of integrity, inclusivity, ingenuity, and impact.

We’ve Built And Nurtured a Culture That Is Intentionally Welcoming And Purposefully Rooted In Equity, Diversity, Inclusion, And Reconciliation (EDI&R). We Believe Diverse Teams, Perspectives, And Lived Experiences Contribute To Better Decisions And a Better Workplace. As UPP Celebrates Its Fifth Anniversary, We’re Proud To Be Recognized For Our Efforts

2026 Greater Toronto’s Top 100 Employers
2026 Canadian HR Award for Excellence in Diversity, Equity, Inclusion & Belonging

Join us in building a bright future for our members, our organization, and each other.

THE ROLE

This is an exciting opportunity for an exceptional individual to join a team of high performing professionals and make a significant impact.

As UPP builds its engagement model and implements a new Pension Administration Solution, the Associate Director, Pension Operations will play a dedicated role in engaging with the project team to build the go forward member and employer service experience and build out training strategy and artifacts. Once the project is complete, they will then transition to lead the teams accountable for service delivery.

Reporting to the Managing Director, Service Experience will build strong trusted relationships and communicate effectively with UPP’s members and employers in the support and development of UPP’s Pension services. This role will lead three lines of business: Member Transactions, pension payroll and Data, Reporting and Analytics. The role will provide leadership for pension data operations and governance, ensuring pension data is treated as a strategic asset with clear ownership, defined quality standards, effective controls, and transparent reporting across member, employer, payroll, actuarial, finance, technology, and regulatory processes.

In support of the Managing Director, Service Experience, this position will have a role in helping UPP meet our own strategic imperative to deliver world-class services to our members and employers.

This role is based in downtown Toronto under a hybrid work policy, allowing employees the flexibility to work remotely and in-office (approximately two days per week in-office).

This job is for an existing vacancy.

Specific Accountabilities

Pension Data Governance Leadership

Establish and operationalize a pension data governance framework with clear accountabilities, data standards, data definitions, business rules, lineage, and critical data elements required to support accurate member records, contributions, service, earnings, calculations, payroll, reporting, and regulatory obligations.
Lead pension data quality management across key dimensions including accuracy, completeness, consistency, timeliness, reliability, relevance, access, coherence, and interpretability, with measurable thresholds, monitoring routines, issue management, and escalation protocols.
Build and oversee data controls for inbound employer data, member events, pension calculations, payroll interfaces, system conversions, reconciliations, reporting extracts, and downstream data uses.
Lead root-cause analysis and remediation of pension data issues, ensuring defects are prioritized based on member impact, financial risk, regulatory exposure, operational risk, and employer experience.
Develop governance routines, dashboards, and reporting that provide senior leadership and Board-level visibility into data quality, data risks, remediation progress, unresolved exceptions, and emerging trends.
Partner with Pension Operations, Employer Experience, Member Experience, Technology, Finance, Actuarial, Legal, Privacy, and Risk teams to ensure data governance practices support plan administration, member outcomes, compliance, and service excellence.
Champion a culture of data accountability by creating practical guidance, training, issue resolution routines, and continuous improvement practices that strengthen trust in pension data across the organization.
Act as a subject-matter expert of UPP plan provisions and calculation rules
Instill a service mindset in team members
Develop an expert internal team to build UPP’s member service offering and intellectual capital base
Exhibit an ability to listen, negotiate and communicate goals; share knowledge, experience, and responsibility with the team to achieve the highest standards of professionalism
Contribute to UPP’s reputation as a respectful employer, partner, and participant in the financial sector
Other projects and activities, as required

Qualifications & Experience

Bachelor’s degree in Business Administration or other related disciplines
Possessing an MBA, C EBS, PPAC or any other relevant professional designation would be an asset
10+ years of progressive experience in pensions
Build strong cross-functional relationships
Demonstrated success working in a hands-on multi-faceted stakeholder environment
Ability to aspire confidence in a broad range of constituencies through a proactive, respectful, and accessible communication style
Demonstrated experience designing or operating data governance, data quality, data stewardship, or data management practices in a pension, financial services, insurance, benefits administration, or similarly regulated environment.
Strong understanding of how pension data supports contribution processing, service and earnings records, benefit calculations, payroll, actuarial valuations, financial controls, member communications, employer reporting, and regulatory filings.
Experience establishing data quality metrics, controls, reconciliations, issue logs, remediation plans, service-level expectations, and governance reporting for operational data sets.
Ability to translate complex data issues into clear business impacts, risk assessments, decision points, and executive-ready recommendations.

ATTRIBUTES

High degree of self-motivation and professionalism
Ability to prioritize and manage multiple client streams in a time sensitive manner
Excellent relationship building and conflict resolution skills
Demonstrated leadership abilities
Excellent interpersonal and verbal communication skills
A collaborative approach to understand and respond to organizational needs and partner with various organizational teams
High degree of professional ethics and integrity
Strong commercial and strategic judgment

Expected Compensation

The expected compensation for this role is a combination of base salary and variable incentive.

You may also be eligible for a variable incentive depending on organizational, divisional and personal performance. The final total compensation offered will vary depending on your skills, experience and other factors.

LIFE AT UPP

Do work that matters.
We are duty-bound to serve our members’ interests, and it’s a responsibility we don’t take lightly. That’s why we’ve ingrained sustainability in our work from day one—to ensure our members have a resilient future to retire into, both today and for generations to come.

Stronger together.
Collaboration is how UPP was born, and it’s how we work with each other and our partners day in, day out. No one at UPP is just a number (even if they are excellent at math) and every win is a shared win.

Grow every day.

jobs.title: Chief Financial Officer
jobs.description:
Lead the global capital strategy for a newly public, high-growth technology company at a pivotal stage of expansion. Bring your investor network and capital-markets expertise to drive transformational financing, strategic partnerships, and M&A opportunities. Partner directly with the Founder, Board, and Senior Executive team in a highly visible CFO role with significant influence, upside, and equity participation. Home base of either Toronto
is strongly preferred.

Who- the Company:

Swim Recruiting is conducting a confidential search on behalf of an AI and media technology company operating across Canada, the United States, and various countries in Europe.

The company delivers in an integrated solution with one connected platform. They are not selling new hardware, they are not pushing a major system change. They are taking data and intelligence that customers often already have, and strategically connecting the information to monetize real results. So far the company has over 50 clients in 4+ countries and their product is being used in thousands of locations. Following a recent reverse takeover and stock exchange listing, the organization has entered its next phase of growth: scaling their proven platform into new markets and verticals while continuing to build the capital markets profile of a public growth company.

What- the Role:

Swim Recruiting has been engaged on the search for a new Global Chief Financial Officer
whose first priority is capital markets: raising capital for a TSXV growth company and keeping the market informed and engaged once it is raised. It suits a capital markets professional who has led small-cap raises as a CFO, VP Finance, or corporate development lead and is ready to own the full mandate.

The CFO will run financings from term sheet to close, starting with private placements, bridge financing and working capital facilities, and growing into larger equity and debt rounds as the company scales. Working alongside the Founder & CEO and the Global COO, the CFO will be a primary face of the company to brokers, investors, and lenders and will play a key role in translating the growth story into funding.

This is not a back-office finance role. We are looking for an externally-facing CFO who already grown a public company and who arrives with an active network of institutional investors, private credit and structured finance providers, investment bankers, and strategic partners ready to engage with.

This is a rare opportunity to be the architect of the capital strategy for a newly public, fast-scaling technology company.

What- the Responsibilities:

Capital Markets & Fundraising
Lead brokered and non-brokered private placements, convertibles, and warrant structures from mandate through to close
Secure and manage bridge, working capital, and asset-based facilities, including LC and credit lines tied to inventory and deployment cycles
Build and work a pipeline of Canadian investment dealers, family offices, high-net-worth and institutional investors, and private lenders
Prepare the materials that win capital: investor decks, financial models, data rooms, and term sheet analysis
Run investor meetings, non-deal roadshows, and conferences in Canada and the US

Investor Relations & Disclosure
Own investor relations for a TSXV-listed company: shareholders, analysts, market makers, and IR firms
Prepare news releases, MD&A, and financing disclosure in coordination with securities counsel
Ensure every financing is structured, approved, and filed in compliance with TSXV policies and Canadian securities requirements

Capital Strategy
Build and maintain a 12 to 24 month funding roadmap that balances dilution, cost of capital, and growth speed
Advise the Founder & Chairman, Global COO, and Board on capital structure and on financing for strategic or M&A opportunities

Finance Oversight
Oversee reporting, treasury, and controls with country finance leads across Canada, the US, Europe, and Turkey, to public company standards
Present to the Board and Audit Committee on cash position, runway, and funding plans

Who- The Candidate:

10+ years in finance
, with at least 5 in Canadian capital markets as a public company CFO or VP Finance, in corporate development, or in investment banking or equity capital markets at a Canadian dealer
A track record of personally leading small-cap raises
on the TSXV, CSE, or TSX, typically C$2M to C$30M per round (we will ask about the amount, structure, and your role in each)
A current network
of Canadian investment dealers, family offices, high-net-worth investors, and private lenders you can put to work in your first 90 days. This network is a requirement of the role, not a nice-to-have.
Working knowledge of TSXV policies, NI 45-106 prospectus exemptions, continuous disclosure, and IFRS and current PIFF
CPA, CFA, or equivalent designation
Comfortable operating at both altitudes — the strategic capital-raising mandate and enough command of the underlying financials to be credible with investors, lenders, and the Board.
Experience in technology, AI/analytics, media, or adjacent sectors is highly preferred, almost required.. however we will consider CFOs with highly relevant work experience and networks who perhaps haven’t yet worked in this space.
Willingness to travel regularly across the company's markets in North America, UK, and Europe.

How Much:

The new CFO will receive a base salary commensurate with depth and breadth of work experience and relevant of investor networks, in the range of $240,000 to $300,000 Canadian
. The upside
for this role
is robust
. The CFO will be eligible for an annual bonus program and equity. The CEO/Founder will have their CFO’s total earnings increase in-step with the company’s growth. We are looking for a CFO who thrives on having “skin in the game”, and who is highly motivated by the potential rewards of their sweat equity, corporate finance savvy, and successful capital raising activities.

Where:

Home base of Greater Toronto Area, with frequent business travel across North America, as well occasional trips to the UK, Europe, and potentially Asia. Must have a valid passport and no travel restrictions.

When & How to Apply:

Swim Recruiting will be conducting initial screening and interviewing, and presenting the resumes and profiles of short-listed candidates directly to the hiring team. If you are interested in this opportunity so far and would like to hear more, please hit “ APPLY
” and a Recruitment Consultant at SWIM will reach out if there is a potential for a match. Thank you!

Position Overview

Autodesk is transforming how the AEC industry designs and builds through integration of Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Machine Learning (ML) across its products, including AutoCAD, Revit, and Forma.

As Head of Engineering, ML for Forma Generative AI, you will lead the ML Engineering organization responsible for computational design and data representations, applied ML model development, and ML infrastructure and operations. You will lead through three engineering managers, setting the ML strategy for the team, defining the technical and organizational standards across the discipline, and shaping how teams build, deploy, and operate production ML systems.

You will partner closely with Architecture, Software Engineering, Research, Product, and other senior leaders to define technical direction, resolve cross-organizational trade-offs, and ensure the organization can move from promising ML research to reliable product capabilities at scale.

Report:
You will report to the Director, Forma Generative AI.

Location:
We support hybrid work, and you work near our Toronto, Canada office. This role requires the ability to travel to team meetings, offsites, and conferences in the USA, Canada, and Europe.

Define and uphold ML engineering strategy, standards, and expectations across the organization, including how ML systems are designed, tested, reviewed, deployed, evaluated, and operated in production
Lead and develop the engineering managers responsible for Computational Design & Data Representations, Applied ML, and ML Infrastructure and Operations. Own the evolution of the ML engineering organization, including team structure, boundaries, hiring, succession, and organizational design
Partner with Architecture and peer engineering leaders to establish shared ML architectures, reusable components, and engineering practices that enable teams to move quickly without compromising quality or consistency
Partner with Research, Product, and Engineering leaders to balance long-term ML research and platform investments with iterative product delivery; align priorities, staffing, and capacity across the ML organization; surface constraints early and resolve cross-team trade-offs to keep critical work moving
Represent ML engineering in organizational planning, resourcing, escalations, and major technical decisions, serving as the discipline’s leadership voice across Forma Generative AI
Build a high-trust engineering culture that develops strong technical leaders, encourages knowledge sharing, and raises the quality of engineering judgement across the organization

Minimum Qualifications

BS or MS in Computer Science, Machine Learning, or a related field, or equivalent experience
8+ years of software/ML engineering experience, including 4+ years of engineering management experience and demonstrated experience managing engineering managers or leading multiple engineering teams
Track record building and operating production ML systems at scale across training, deployment, inference, monitoring, and evaluation
Experience establishing engineering standards and technical direction across multiple teams without centralizing every decision
Demonstrated success hiring, developing, and retaining engineering managers and senior technical leads, with strong communication and influence across senior stakeholders

Experience leading engineering organizations responsible for large-scale ML or foundation-model systems
Deep technical familiarity with modern ML engineering and production infrastructure, including ML frameworks (e.g. PyTorch), distributed training and inference, cloud infrastructure, observability, CI/CD, Infrastructure-as-Code, and production automation
Experience designing or leading development of foundation-model and agentic systems, including evaluation harnesses, tool-use/orchestration patterns, and other production scaffolding around models
Experience partnering with peer engineering, architecture, research, and product leaders in a matrixed organization
Experience in the AEC industry, Autodesk products, or another technically complex design/engineering domain
Experience applying rapidly evolving foundation-model and agentic-system technologies in production environments

The Ideal Candidate

You know the difference between managing a team and leading an organization; you develop strong managers, create clear ownership, and scale through others
You can establish a technical bar and make it stick through standards, coaching, and strong engineering judgement rather than personal gatekeeping
You build trust with senior peers across architecture, research, product, and engineering, and can navigate disagreement and ambiguity while keeping the organization moving
You communicate effectively across disciplines and levels, adapting your approach to build shared understanding with technical, product, research, and executive audiences

Being part of Air Canada is to become part of an iconic Canadian symbol, recently ranked the best Airline in North America. Let your career take flight by joining our diverse and vibrant team at the leading edge of passenger aviation.

The Director of Application Development will lead the design, development, and delivery of some of our most critical customer digital applications and all our in-house cargo applications. Its customer application portfolio consists of aircanada.com’s content related applications (Content Management System (CMS) platform, Homepage), marketing digital assets (Offer Management, DNA) as well as Customer Identity and Access Management (CIAM). Its cargo portfolio includes the cargo website (informational and transactional), the cargo distribution API, the cargo digital backend and all the cargo integrations, a portfolio that keeps growing with the new Cargo Management System implementation through the end of 2028.

This role will also be responsible for the Delivery COE and the Innovation COE for all the customer and cargo portfolios. The Delivery COE aims at harmonizing the delivery practice, KPIs, continuous improvements within the portfolio. The Innovation COE aims at improving our digital technology platforms, through continuous improvements (i.e., progressive AI adoption, Continuous Integration /Continuous Development (CI/CD) pipeline enhancements, etc) as well as disruptive innovations through POCs and partnership with Air Canada’s key technology vendors (i.e., transition to Mono Repo, introduction of a new Model Context Protocol (MCP) stack, etc.). This role is key to our digital transformation journey and will be pivotal in empowering the IDD organization to achieve its cost transformation and innovation goals.

This role will also focus on people leadership, including talent acquisition, training, performance management, and fostering a high-performing team culture.

Provide strategic and hands-on leadership for teams building the future marketing and content technology landscape for Air Canada
Lead the cargo deliver teams towards a successful implementation of the new Cargo Management System.
Deliver disruptive technology driven innovations that dramatically increase revenue or reduce cost.
Drive the insourcing strategy by recruiting, developing, and retaining top engineering talent, reducing reliance on vendor-driven delivery models.
Collaborate with Product Owners, UX/UI Designers, and Architects to define the product vision, architecture, and development roadmap.

Champion the use and integration of Generative AI tooling and AI Agents within the development lifecycle to increase developer productivity and enable rapid iteration.
Stay ahead of emerging technologies and assess their relevance and value for digital product development.
Foster a culture of engineering excellence through code quality, design standards, peer reviews, and continuous learning.

Own end-to-end product delivery, from development through production deployment and support.
Collaborate closely with internal product managers, designers, architects, and quality assurance teams to ensure timely and high-quality product releases.
Monitor team performance, manage risks, remove delivery blockers, and drive accountability for outcomes.
Ensure proper technical documentation and knowledge-sharing across teams.

Collaboration & Communication
Partner cross-functionally with other IT and Digital leaders, including Architecture, Security, Data, and Infrastructure teams.
Engage with key business stakeholders across Digital, Marketing, Loyalty, and HR to ensure alignment between product features and business priorities.
Present technical strategies and delivery progress to senior leadership, contributing to enterprise-wide technology planning.

Manage operational and capital budgets, ensuring efficient resource allocation and delivery within financial targets.
Develop and maintain staffing plans, forecast resource needs, and align capacity to strategic priorities.
Support training and professional development programs to grow technical capabilities within the team.
Establish performance metrics and continuous improvement practices for team delivery and application performance.

Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Software Engineering, or related field; equivalent experience may be considered in lieu of formal education.

Proven success in leading digital transformations, including insourcing and adoption of modern development frameworks and practices.
Deep technical expertise in web and mobile application development, microservices, cloud-native architecture, and API ecosystems.

At General Dynamics Mission Systems–Canada, we’re not just engineering technology — we’re shaping the future of defence and security. Our teams design and deliver advanced, mission-critical solutions that enhance national security, strengthen communities, and protect the people we serve.

Job Description

Reporting to the Chief Digital and Information Officer (CDIO), the Director, Enterprise Data & Integration is responsible for establishing and maturing the organization's enterprise data capability. This includes developing the enterprise data strategy, architecture, governance framework, integration standards, and technology roadmap required to support operational excellence, analytics, reporting, artificial intelligence, and digital transformation.

The Director will help build and lead a small Data Engineering team and work across business and technology functions to transform fragmented, project-based data initiatives into a scalable, governed, and sustainable enterprise capability. This role is accountable for ensuring enterprise data is managed, integrated, and leveraged as a strategic asset across the organization.

Key Responsibilities

Enterprise Data Strategy & Capability Development

Develop and maintain the enterprise data strategy, roadmap, operating model, and target-state architecture aligned with business priorities.
Establish and mature enterprise data capabilities spanning architecture, governance, integration, engineering standards, and information management practices.
Partner with business and technology leaders to enable data-driven decision-making, analytics, automation, and AI readiness.

Data Architecture, Governance & Integration

Define and govern enterprise data architecture, integration architecture, information management standards, and reference models.
Establish scalable approaches for APIs, MuleSoft integration services, event-driven architecture, data pipelines, metadata, lineage, master/reference data, and data quality.
Ensure enterprise data solutions are secure, compliant, resilient, and aligned with enterprise architecture principles.

Platforms, Technology & Innovation

Provide strategic leadership for enterprise data platforms, integration technologies, analytics environments, and AI-enabling capabilities.
Evaluate technologies, vendors, and strategic investments to ensure alignment with business objectives, architecture standards, and long-term sustainability.
Drive modernization, simplification, and standardization across the enterprise data and integration landscape.

Support the planning, prioritization, and successful delivery of enterprise data and integration initiatives.
Build strong partnerships across business units, cybersecurity, infrastructure, applications, enterprise architecture, and external partners.

Governance & Continuous Improvement

Establish governance processes, architecture reviews, standards, and decision-making frameworks for enterprise data and integration solutions.
Identify and reduce technical debt, platform fragmentation, unmanaged data movement, and point-to-point integrations.
Promote reuse, consistency, and continuous improvement across enterprise data platforms, services, and integration capabilities.

10+ years of experience in enterprise data architecture, integration architecture, data engineering, enterprise architecture, or related disciplines.
Demonstrated experience developing enterprise data strategies, governance frameworks, architecture standards, and technology roadmaps.
Experience leading technical teams and influencing senior business and technology stakeholders.
Strong understanding of enterprise data management, integration, governance, analytics, cloud platforms, security, and information management principles.
Experience working with or familiarity with AI/ML models

Experience designing and governing enterprise integration capabilities using MuleSoft Anypoint Platform
, including API-led connectivity, reusable integration services, event-driven architectures, and integration governance.
Experience with modern enterprise data platforms including Snowflake
, Microsoft Fabric, Azure Data Factory, Synapse, Databricks, Purview, AWS data services, or comparable technologies.

Position Summary

The Vice President, Head of Data Management, is primarily responsible for Omnicom’s data architecture, governance, integrity, and movement of data.
This role oversees data architecture, such as cloud-based platforms for storage and analytics, as well as the composer layer that allows for bespoke workflow and data pipelines to be designed/provisioned, and the orchestration layer to automate workflows/tasks that are durable, reliable and scalable. In general, this role focuses on upstream solution design and management (including how data is collected, structured, stored, and made accessible), and works closely with stakeholders in global engineering, local IT, and data solutions teams to maintain data quality, privacy compliance (e.g. PIPEDA, Law 25), and scalability of the data ecosystem.

This role requires a strong familiarity with common media analytics and technology tools, both syndicated and proprietary. The ideal candidate must be able to proactively communicate ideas and opportunities, build strong relationships with internal and external partners, and evolve the data management practice across the Canadian offices. The candidate must have a mindset towards fostering processes through automation, as well as establishing data as the backbone of other OM media disciplines.

Primary Responsibilities

Administrative & Departmental Development

Work with OM Global Central Team, and local Data and Solutions and Business Operations teams to establish agency-level standard Data Management practices and thought leadership. Oversee application of such standards across all OM accounts.
Act as subject matter expert on data operations and business intelligence solutions; prescriptively advise how they should be applied to deliver against client needs.
Contribute to client statements of work (SOWs) and/or service-line agreements (SLAs) during contract negotiations, re-negotiations and renewals
Work with team leadership, finance and data solutions resourcing, both onshore and offshore, to establish resource rate cards, platform and staffing costs and various business engagement requirements

Serve as the escalation point to address critical business issues; have direct conversations with internal teams and clients, as needed. Support the development of short-term plans to prioritize needs and to resolve urgent issues.
Analyze employee time utilization to ensure employee hours are properly scoped to the right projects

Data Management & Strategy

Collaborate with the Chief Data & Solutions Officier on both overall OM, and individual client, data strategy

Act as the subject matter expert for projects relating to data quality and business rules
Demand best practices are being followed by onshore and offshore data teams across all engagements
Lead and manage cross-functional and cross-organizational teams to understand complex data issues involving multiple systems
Establish priorities, develop improvement plans, allocate resources, and implement solutions
Keep up to date on digital operations - buy changes, creative specifications, etc

Data Governance & Documentation

Lead the development of a comprehensive departmental data management and integrity program, including being accountable on cross-account adoption of a coordinated governance process
Drive cross-discipline documentation process and create standardization for validating the implementation, optimization, and reconciliation of all campaign data
Oversee the documentation of processes, workflows, and technical implementations of any project. Proactively identify, propose, and generate targeted solutions for data quality issues and operational inefficiencies.

People & Project Management

Socialize OM and projects tasks staging/RACIs - ensuring clarity on roles, responsibilities and expectations across teams
Supervise Directors and Managers to perform data management, data operations, data quality assurance and client project tasks. Provide guidance to team members and promote a team environment.
Accountable for growth of direct reports. Tailor OM, client and personal goals to develop and emphasize strengths of each direct report.

Experience, Skill and Technical Requirements

10+ years’ experience in data operations and/or business intelligence, including 8+ years in a management role, 2+ years in a senior management role
8+ years’ experience (media agency, in-house media team or retail media network), working directly with media data (ad server, display & video, search, social, offline, etc)
8+ years’ experience in an agile development environment
Minimum 8 years’ experience in client facing work
Experience managing teams that are onshore and offshore
Strong verbal and written communication skills
Strong organizational and project management skills (scoping, task staging, resource and change management)
Advanced proficiency with one or more of: Salesforce Marketing Cloud Intelligence (fka Datorama), Power BI, Alteryx, Tableau. Experience with Google BigQuery and Cloud Composer 3 a plus.
Intermediate proficiency with Amazon Web Services (S3, Redshift)
3+ years’ experience with project management platforms such as Hive, Asana or Smartsheet
Intermediate proficiency with Excel and PowerPoint
