jobs.title: Performance Planning Director
jobs.description:
Role Overview

We’re looking for a Performance Planning Director
that can bridge the gap between strategy and activation, combining deep platform knowledge with strong tactical planning expertise. The role turns business and media objectives into clear, actionable performance plans, grounded in an understanding of how campaigns are activated, optimized, measured, and evolved in-market.
The ideal candidate is a confident, self-sufficient planner that sees beyond platform execution. They understand the full campaign lifecycle and how upper- and lower-funnel media work together to drive business outcomes. They are naturally curious about what drives performance, bringing together audience, channel, budget, bidding, creative, measurement, and optimization considerations to develop smarter tactical recommendations.

What You’ll Do

Tactical Planning

Translate media strategies and business objectives into clear, actionable performance plans across paid social, programmatic, search, and other digital channels.
Develop channel and platform recommendations across audience, budget, bidding, targeting, placements, creative, and optimization tactics.
Identify opportunities to improve campaign efficiency and performance through thoughtful tactical planning.
Build full-funnel campaign approaches that balance short-term performance objectives with longer-term brand, customer, and business outcomes.
Build connected, full-funnel approaches that define the role of upper- and lower-funnel media and how they work together against shared business objectives.
Translate broader brand and customer objectives into performance strategies, ensuring lower-funnel activity builds on the audiences, signals, and momentum created by upper-funnel investment.
Stay curious about new platform capabilities, betas, formats, audience solutions, and emerging performance tactics.
Demonstrate strong working knowledge of relevant advertising platforms and their tactical capabilities.
Manage planned budgets, roll over and communicate changes based on performance requirements.

Performance Analysis & Optimization

Turn performance data into clear insights and actionable recommendations.
Make clear recommendations to test and refine targeting, budget allocation, creative, and platform tactics.
Evaluate performance within the context of the broader media plan, considering how upper-funnel activity may influence lower-funnel outcomes and optimization decisions.
Connect platform metrics to broader campaign and business KPIs, helping teams understand how activity across the funnel contributes to overall performance.
Understand the relationship between platform-level performance and broader campaign/business outcomes.

Collaboration & Communication

As a part of the Activation team, partner closely with Strategic Planning and Client Experience teams to ensure tactical plans align with the overall media strategy.
Clearly articulate the rationale behind tactical recommendations and campaign decisions.
Bring a proactive, solutions-oriented mindset to campaign challenges.
Share platform knowledge and best practices with the broader Activation team.

What We’re Looking For

Strong end-to-end knowledge of performance media platforms across Paid Search, Social, Programmatic and other digital channels, with hands-on experience across key platforms.
A solid understanding of platform capabilities - audiences, budgets, placements, creative, measurement, and optimization - work together.
A strong passion for tactical planning and curiosity about how campaigns can be built and optimized to perform better.
Strong analytical skills and the ability to move beyond reporting numbers to identify meaningful actions.
Highly organized, detail-oriented, and comfortable managing multiple campaigns and priorities.
Strong communication skills, with the ability to explain technical and tactical concepts clearly to both internal and client-facing audiences.
Strong storytelling skills, with the ability to connect upper- and lower-funnel media, clearly articulating how each contributes to performance and broader business outcomes.
Proactive and self-sufficient, with the ability to identify opportunities, solve problems and confidently manage multiple priorities with limited direction.

What Success Looks Like

Success in this role means being a trusted bridge between client strategy and tactical execution, connecting upper- and lower-funnel objectives into a cohesive media approach and clearly articulating the role of each channel, the rationale behind recommendations, and the outcomes we expect to drive.
You bring a strong understanding of media platforms and a strategic mindset that goes beyond building plans. You proactively challenge assumptions, identify opportunities, and continuously refine the media approach, understanding how investment across the funnel works together, to ensure every investment is purposeful, connected to client objectives, and positioned to deliver measurable results.

Interim Vice President, Finance, Technology & Business Operations
jobs.description:
IMMEDIATE INTERIM OPPORTUNITY

Interim Vice President, Finance, Technology & Business Operations

Reports To: Chief Executive Officer

Duration: 3 to 6 months

Location: Greater Toronto Area

Hybrid Working

Our client is a respected national not-for-profit organization with a complex operating model, multiple stakeholders and a strong mission-driven culture. The organization works collaboratively with regional partners and relies on effective financial stewardship, technology, data, risk management and business operations to deliver on its mandate.

The Opportunity

The organization is seeking an experienced interim executive to provide transitional leadership following an unexpected leave. This is a three-to-six-month assignment combining hands-on operational oversight with strategic advice and support to the CEO.

The Interim Vice President will inherit a capable, well-performing team across finance and technology. The priority is not to initiate unnecessary change, but to provide stability, sound judgment and thoughtful leadership through a delicate period of transition. The successful interim will maintain operational continuity, coach and support the team, and ensure that the CEO and executive leadership have the financial information, analytics and technology advice required for effective decision-making.

The portfolio includes responsibility for finance and technology/information services, with broader involvement in business operations, risk and organizational planning.

Transitional and Operational Leadership

Provide steady, visible and reassuring leadership during a sensitive period of transition.
Assume day-to-day executive accountability for finance, technology and related business operations.
Maintain momentum on existing priorities while ensuring continuity of critical services, reporting and controls.
Quickly assess emerging issues and determine which matters require immediate attention, which should continue as planned and which should be deferred.
Establish an effective working relationship with the CEO and serve as a trusted, pragmatic strategic adviser.
Support clear communication and collaboration across the executive team and broader organization.

Finance, Analytics and Executive Decision Support

Oversee budgeting, forecasting, cash management, financial reporting, audit readiness and core financial operations.
Ensure the continued integrity of financial systems, internal controls and risk-management practices.
Provide the CEO, executive team and Board committees with timely, relevant and decision-oriented financial analysis.
Strengthen the quality of management information by moving reporting beyond historical results toward clearer analysis of trends, risks, opportunities and forward-looking implications.
Improve the use of data, dashboards and analytics to support program, operational and resource-allocation decisions.
Ensure leaders receive appropriate support in developing and monitoring departmental and program budgets.
Maintain oversight of funder reporting, donor and partnership funds, charitable reporting requirements and other sector-specific financial obligations.

The underlying role is responsible for budgeting, financial analysis, monthly reporting, accounts payable and receivable, payroll, cash management, donor receipting, audit coordination and charitable-sector reporting.

Technology, AI and Cybersecurity

Provide executive oversight of the technology function and ensure that systems and services remain reliable, secure and aligned with organizational priorities.
Review the organization’s technology roadmap and identify immediate risks, dependencies and opportunities.
Help the CEO and executive team evaluate the responsible use of artificial intelligence, including where AI can improve productivity, analysis and service delivery while appropriately managing privacy, security and reputational risk.
Assess the organization’s cybersecurity and data-privacy posture, ensuring that material vulnerabilities and required actions are clearly understood by leadership.
Support the organization in prioritizing technology investments based on operational value, risk and available resources.
Ensure major technology initiatives are appropriately governed and positioned to deliver reliable performance and a positive user experience.
Strengthen the connection between finance, technology and organizational data so that leadership receives more integrated and actionable insights.

Team Leadership and Coaching

Lead a small, established team across finance and technology with empathy, clarity and consistency.
Preserve the strengths of a well-performing team while providing the direction and executive access needed during the transition.
Coach team members, clarify priorities and reinforce accountability without creating disruption or unnecessary organizational change.
Identify opportunities to strengthen capability, cross-functional collaboration and succession coverage.
Create an environment in which team members feel supported, informed and confident in raising concerns or escalating risks.
Provide the CEO with an objective assessment of team capacity, operating pressures and longer-term organizational needs.

Risk, Governance and Business Operations

Maintain effective financial, technology, privacy, legal and operational risk-management practices.
Ensure that material risks are identified, evaluated, documented and communicated to the CEO and the appropriate Board committee.
Support risk-register updates, insurance considerations, crisis-management readiness and business-continuity planning.
Ensure contracts and material commitments receive appropriate financial, operational and legal review.
Contribute to operational planning and help align organizational priorities, resources and budgets.
Prepare clear transition documentation and recommendations to support the eventual return or onboarding of permanent leadership.

Ideal Candidate Profile

The successful candidate will be an accomplished finance and business operations executive who has previously led both finance and technology portfolios. They will bring the maturity and judgment required to enter a stable team, establish credibility quickly and lead through a sensitive transition without overstepping the interim mandate.

Ideally, the candidate will offer:

Senior executive experience as a CFO, Vice President of Finance, Vice President of Corporate Services, or Vice President of Finance and Operations.
Demonstrated responsibility for both finance and information technology, either through direct leadership or an integrated corporate-services portfolio.
Experience working in a not-for-profit, charitable, membership-based, sport, healthcare, education or similar mission-driven environment.
Strong financial leadership capabilities encompassing budgeting, forecasting, financial reporting, audit, internal controls, cash management and executive decision support.
Experience improving management reporting, data analytics, business intelligence and organizational performance insights.
Meaningful exposure to cybersecurity, data privacy, technology governance and digital transformation.
A practical understanding of artificial intelligence and the governance considerations associated with its responsible organizational use.
Experience advising a CEO and presenting complex financial, operational and technology matters to executive teams and Board committees.
A collaborative, low-ego leadership style and demonstrated success coaching capable teams through periods of uncertainty or transition.
Discretion, diplomacy and emotional steadiness are required for a confidential leadership assignment.
A professional accounting designation would be strongly preferred.
Bilingualism would be considered an asset.

Leadership Style

This assignment will suit an interim executive who is:

Calm grounded and comfortable operating in ambiguity.
Strategic while remaining willing to engage directly in operational matters.
Respectful of the organization’s culture, history and existing team.
Able to distinguish between urgent stabilization needs and longer-term transformation opportunities.
Skilled at translating financial and technology complexity into clear executive-level advice.
Comfortable challenging constructively while remaining supportive of the CEO and leadership team.
Focused on leaving the organization, its systems and its people stronger at the conclusion of the mandate.

Measures of Success

Success over the three-to-six-month assignment will include:

Uninterrupted delivery of critical finance, technology and business operations.
A supported, engaged and well-directed finance and technology team.
Reliable financial reporting, forecasting, controls and audit readiness.
More decision-useful data, analytics and insights for the CEO and executive team.
Clearer prioritization of technology, AI, cybersecurity and data-privacy risks.
Sound and timely strategic advice to the CEO.
Effective management and escalation of organizational risks.
A disciplined transition plan, including documentation of key decisions, open issues and recommendations for longer-term leadership.

Position Description

ROLE:
MANAGING DIRECTOR , MEDIA STRATEGY(Financial Institution Experience)

TEAM:
ACCOUNTS, SALT MEDIA

LOCATION
: TORONTO (HYBRID)

Company Overview

Salt is a North American marketing agency that creates connected experiences through creative, digital & media innovation. Our mission is to “Earn The World’s Attention” and Salt is built to find, develop, execute, and amplify the ideas that are worthy of our clients’ audiences. We’ve structured our agency to do what’s right for our clients – to connect different perspectives, to work across mediums, and to focus on delivering meaningful, effective results.

We’re committed to living up to the values in our name. “Salt of The Earth” means we value collaborative, humble, hard-working people here. We’re looking for people who are as smart as they are kind because we believe the right talent and the right culture help us do what’s right for our clients.

Role Overview

As a Managing Director, Media, you will lead Salt’s media practice by driving strategic excellence, operational performance, and commercial growth across a portfolio of clients and media investments. You are responsible for shaping media strategy, guiding investment decisions, and ensuring best-in-class planning, buying, measurement, and optimization across all channels.

You oversee multidisciplinary teams, foster senior client relationships, and champion innovation in media technology, audience strategy, and performance marketing. As a senior agency leader, you balance long-term vision with hands-on leadership—stepping in to solve complex business challenges, elevate client outcomes, and create scalable systems that drive growth.

This role is about building a high-performing media practice that delivers measurable business impact. You will be accountable for portfolio performance, media investment stewardship, team development, operational excellence, and expanding Salt’s media capabilities in a rapidly evolving landscape

Core Responsibilities

Media Strategy & Planning Leadership

Lead integrated, full-funnel media strategies across a portfolio of clients, ensuring alignment with business objectives, customer journeys, and brand goals.
Establish strategic planning frameworks and media approaches that drive consistency, innovation, and measurable outcomes across teams.
Guide senior media leaders in developing channel strategies, investment allocations, and audience approaches that maximize effectiveness and efficiency.
Partner with Strategy, Creative, Digital, and Account teams to deliver connected marketing solutions that drive business growth.
Represent Salt as a media thought leader through client presentations, industry events, and marketplace engagement.

Media Buying & Investment Management

Oversee media investment across client portfolios, ensuring budgets are optimized to deliver maximum performance and value.
Lead media investment philosophy, governance, and buying practices across all channels and platforms.
Build and maintain executive-level relationships with media partners, publishers, and technology vendors to unlock innovation, preferential pricing, and strategic opportunities.
Negotiate high-value media agreements and partnerships that improve agency leverage and client outcomes.
Ensure media plans and investments remain aligned to business objectives, market conditions, and evolving consumer behaviors.

Measurement, Analytics & Insight Development

Champion data-driven decision-making across the media practice through robust measurement frameworks and reporting standards.
Oversee dashboard strategy, data integration, and performance reporting processes that provide actionable insights to clients and teams.
Guide teams in translating media performance data into strategic recommendations that improve future planning and business results.
Ensure consistent measurement methodologies are applied across client portfolios to support optimization, accountability, and learning.
Promote a culture of testing, learning, and continuous improvement through data and analytics.

Media Technology & Innovation

Lead the adoption and evolution of media tools, platforms, and technologies that improve operational efficiency and campaign effectiveness.
Oversee vendor relationships and platform partnerships to ensure optimal utilization, innovation, and return on investment.
Identify emerging technologies, automation opportunities, and industry trends that can strengthen Salt’s media capabilities.
Collaborate with leadership to establish long-term technology roadmaps that support agency growth and competitive advantage.
Drive innovation initiatives that improve workflow efficiency, scalability, and campaign performance.

Performance Optimization & Audience Strategy

Champion advanced optimization frameworks, automation solutions, and testing methodologies across client portfolios.
Guide teams in developing audience-first strategies that leverage data, segmentation, and behavioral insights to improve effectiveness.
Establish best practices for audience targeting, channel selection, and performance measurement across all media programs.
Lead innovation in automation, optimization, and performance systems that improve efficiency and business outcomes.
Ensure media strategies evolve continuously through audience insights, testing results, and market intelligence.

Financial Leadership

Own portfolio-level financial performance, including media investment oversight, forecasting, profitability, and growth targets.

jobs.description:
Corporate Audit is looking for an experienced Assistant Vice President (AVP) to lead and execute complex audits and validation work across Global Treasury. The role will primarily cover liquidity risk, interest rate risk in the banking book, investment portfolio, governance, and related regulatory reporting.

The successful candidate will combine strong audit execution and leadership skills with practical knowledge of Treasury risk management. The individual will lead assigned audit teams through planning, testing, issue development, and reporting. They will also review work for quality and evidentiary support and communicate conclusions to senior management.

The role is for an experienced auditor who must be able to thrive in a fast-paced environment, communicate clearly, and already possess strong auditing capabilities.

Why this role is important to us

The audit team plays an important role in the overall success of the organization. Across the globe, the firm, relies on us to help them manage risk, respond to challenges, and drive performance and profitability; regulators rely upon us to provide assurance that the bank operates in a manner that is compliant with key banking regulations to properly manage risks to the company and the global financial systems.

What You Will Be Responsible For

As Global Treasury Audit, AVP you will

Lead complex audits across Global Treasury, from planning, through testing, issue development, and final reporting.
Direct audit teams assigned to individual engagements, establish clear expectations, monitor delivery, review workpapers, and coach team members throughout the engagement.
Plan and perform controls testing, including walkthroughs, sample selection, inspection of evidence, reperformance and evaluation of operating effectiveness.
Evaluate Treasury processes against applicable regulatory requirements, supervisory guidance, internal policies, and established risk limits.
Apply professional skepticism to assess the quality, completeness and reliability of evidence, and challenge unsupported or inconsistent explanations.
Use data analytics to support testing, identify anomalies and enable continuous monitoring where appropriate.
Communicate testing status, emerging concerns, scope changes and delivery risks promptly to audit management, together with fact-based analysis and proposed solutions.
Build constructive relationships across the lines of defense while maintaining audit independence and objectivity.
Maintain current knowledge of Global Treasury risks, regulatory expectations and industry practices, particularly in liquidity risk, asset-liability management and interest rate risk.

What We Value

These skills will help you succeed in this role

Practical knowledge of Treasury risk management, with experience in liquidity risk, interest rate risk in the banking book, asset and liability management, or a related discipline.
Strong analytical and professional judgment, including the ability to identify the risks that matter and develop well-supported conclusions.
Ability to independently manage multiple priorities, meet commitments and escalate obstacles early in a fast-paced environment.
Clear, factual and concise written and verbal communication, including communication with senior management and regulators.
Ability to research, interpret and apply regulatory requirements and supervisory expectations relevant to Treasury and liquidity requirements and supervisory guidance.
Collaborative approach and ability to provide clear direction and review feedback to audit team members.

Education And Required Qualifications

The following are required:

Bachelor’s degree in Finance, Accounting, Business, Risk Management or a related field.
At least 5 years of relevant experience in internal audit, Global Treasury, public accounting, or another first- or second-line risk management role.
Experience leading significant workstreams and audit engagements.
Advanced degree or certification, Certified Public Accountant (CPA), Certified Internal Auditor (CIA), or Chartered Financial Analyst (CFA) designation or its equivalent preferred.

jobs.description:
Job Description:

Our mission is to Drive Business Performance. We use data to create personalized and connected experiences that deliver transformative business outcomes. Our role is to ensure our clients meet their quantifiable business goals every day, consistently, in every market. We are entirely focused on delivering better business results through optimization, creation and analysis across all digital platforms. Our scope ranges from recommending how to use content more effectively to optimizing daily media channel performance and maximizing visibility in eCommerce platforms.

The Director, Digital Strategy is the senior strategic digital lead for the client account. The role defines how digital channels work together across the customer journey to support the client’s brand and business goals, and ensures digital thinking is embedded from the brief onward rather than added once activation begins.This is a client-facing leadership role focused on vision, integration and decision-making. The Director turns audience, cultural, platform, business and measurement signals into a focused digital strategy, clear priorities and practical roadmaps. The role brings choiceful recommendations, constructive challenge and a future-facing point of view.

The Director will work alongside Client Leadership and Planning, while partnering closely with the Digital Manager, channel specialists and Media Effectiveness. The Digital Manager and specialists remain responsible for in-platform strategy, buying, account structure, bidding, pacing, optimization, trafficking and quality assurance. The Director sets the strategic direction and ensures the work adds up to one connected digital proposition.

What Success Looks Like

The client can clearly articulate the digital channel strategy, the role of each channel and how the ecosystem supports business growth.
Digital strategy develops at the same pace as the broader media strategy and shapes investment, audience and measurement decisions from the outset.
The client receives concise, decisive recommendations that clarify what matters now, what comes next and why.
Testing, measurement and learning lead to visible changes in strategy, investment and activation.
First-party data, audience and innovation opportunities progress through practical, phased roadmaps with clear ownership and dependencies.
The account operates as one integrated client leadership, planning, digital activation and measurement team.

Key Accountabilities

Digital channel strategy and integration

Own the account’s digital channel strategy and roadmap, connecting business objectives, audience needs, customer journey, channel roles, investment priorities and measurement
Partner with Client Leadership and Planning from the brief onward so digital strategy is developed as part of the core media response, not as a downstream activation layer.
Define how paid Search, Social, Programmatic, Display, Video and other relevant digital channels work together across the funnel, while channel specialists determine the detailed in-platform approach.
Translate complex inputs into a focused set of priorities, choices and actions the client and team can understand and deliver.

Audience, innovation and growth agenda

Develop audience and segmentation strategies that connect broad media audiences, platform signals, app and loyalty opportunities, and first-party data ambitions.
Identify opportunities to improve brand impact, acquisition, engagement, loyalty and media effectiveness, and convert them into sequenced recommendations with clear expected value.
Bring a forward-looking point of view on changing consumer behaviour, platform evolution, AI-enabled media and emerging digital opportunities, distinguishing useful innovation from novelty.
Create a visible innovation agenda for the client that links new opportunities to real business questions, readiness and measurable outcomes.

Measurement, testing and learnin g

With Media Effectiveness and channel leads, define the learning agenda and ensure each priority has a clear business question, hypothesis, success measure and decision rule.
Connect reach, attention, engagement, conversion, efficiency and incrementality evidence to the business question being answered.
Turn reporting and specialist input into concise recommendations on what to continue, change, stop, scale or test next.
Ensure learning is applied back into audience, channel, investment and creative decisions, creating a continuous strategy-to-learning cycle.

First-party data and connected capabilities

Lead the media strategy and use-case components of the first-party data and audience maturity roadmap, in partnership with Media Effectiveness, CRM, loyalty, app, privacy, data and technology stakeholders.
Break complex ambitions into practical phases with explicit ownership, dependencies, decision points and realistic timelines.
First party data connecting to business strategy

Present the digital strategy and roadmap in senior meetings, annual planning, business reviews and critical transformation workstreams.
Coach the Digital Manager, planners and specialists to connect platform recommendations to the wider strategy and communicate with greater clarity and confidence.
Establish clear ways of working and decision rights across Client Leadership, Planning, Digital Activation, Media Effectiveness and specialist partners.

Post-secondary degree or diploma in Media, Advertising, Marketing, Business, Strategy, Analytics or a related field

Experience translating audience, platform, analytics, research and business signals into a clear strategic point of view and actionable roadmap.
Practical understanding of first-party data, CRM, app and loyalty use cases, including the organizational and measurement dependencies required to activate them.
Experience shaping learning agendas and working with measurement specialists to turn evidence into decisions.

jobs.title: Director of Business Technology
jobs.description:
Liteline Corporation is a privately held Canadian commercial lighting manufacturer with more than 160 employees, selling across Canada and the United States. We are adding a Director of Business Technology to our leadership team, a senior, hands-on role with ownership of technology across the business.

The role has two halves. The first is the job every growing company needs: keep our technology running, secure and recoverable across roughly 130 computers, Microsoft 365, our server cluster and our network. The second is newer. Our own people, from the three Co-Presidents to staff in Finance, Product Development, Engineering and Customer Service, now build software tools with AI assistants. The Director of Business Technology will give that work a professional backbone: version control, permissions, backups and fast recovery.

This is an enabling role as much as a technical one. We want our people to keep building quickly. The person in this position will make sure what they build is safe, recoverable and well looked after, without slowing anyone down.

This is a build role. Liteline’s people are already creating their own tools with AI. We are looking for a leader who can keep the core IT environment solid, put the right platforms and guardrails under home-built software, and teach non-programmers to work safely.

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

Keep Things Running

Own day-to-day IT across the business: computers, email, servers, networking, security and backups.
Run Microsoft 365, including sign-in, multi-factor authentication (MFA), user access and licensing.
Look after our on-premises server cluster, storage and network infrastructure.
Oversee security monitoring and incident response together with our security monitoring partner.
Maintain tested backups and the ability to restore systems and data quickly.
Lead the help desk and set the service standards the business is held to.

Own the Platforms

Set up and run, hands-on, the platforms our home-built tools live on.
Own Liteline’s company GitHub organization, where code is saved with full history, including structure, permissions, single sign-on (SSO) and branch protection.
Administer hosted databases (Supabase / Postgres), including access control, backups and recovery.
Manage website and application hosting (Netlify), including deployments, domains and environments.
Maintain a clear inventory of the tools in use, who owns each one and where it runs.

Govern and Teach

Decide what AI assistants can access and set sensible guardrails for company data and credentials.
Set light, practical rules that protect the business without getting in the way of the people building.
Decide which home-built tools are business-critical and what level of protection each one needs.
Run and rehearse restores so that recovery is proven, not assumed.
Teach staff who are not programmers to work safely, for example explaining version control to someone in purchasing.
Run training, enablement and “lunch and learn” sessions across the business.

Team and Partners

Lead two on-site IT staff.
Manage our outside partners for managed services, security monitoring and backup.
Own the technology budget, licensing and vendor relationships, and bring forward stronger options as the market moves.

WHAT WE ARE LOOKING FOR

We are looking for a hands-on technology leader who is equally comfortable running core IT and building platforms that sit under modern, AI-assisted development.

The successful candidate will understand infrastructure, identity and security, and will also understand how software is built, saved, deployed and recovered. Just as importantly, you will be able to explain those ideas in plain language to people who have never written code and help them adopt habits that last.

Strong candidates will bring:

Hands-on experience setting up or administering a GitHub organization, including SSO and branch protection.
Experience running a Microsoft Power Platform Centre of Excellence, citizen-developer or low-code programme.
Hands-on experience running Supabase, Postgres, Netlify, Vercel or similar platforms.
Solid Microsoft 365, identity, MFA, endpoint and security fundamentals.
A track record of training and enabling non-technical staff, such as “lunch and learn” or enablement programmes.
Experience building a function or process from scratch at a growing company.
Clear communication and sound judgment about when rules help and when they get in the way.

There is no single path to this role. You might be:
An IT lead at a 100-to-500-person manufacturer or distributor who personally ran a Power Platform governance programme, a low-code programme or the company’s GitHub organization.
A developer or DevOps engineer who moved into an IT management role at a small or mid-sized company.
A solutions architect or senior consultant at a managed services provider (MSP) serving small and mid-sized businesses, ready to go in-house.
The “first IT hire” at a startup who set up sign-in, devices and GitHub from scratch, then moved to a mid-sized company.
Experience in mid-sized manufacturing, distribution or wholesale is helpful but not required.

REPORTING AND WORKING RELATIONSHIPS

This position reports to the VP of Operations.

You will work closely with Liteline’s three Co-Presidents, who are technically capable and build their own tools, and with Finance, Product Development, Engineering and Customer Service. You will be a partner to the people building, not a gatekeeper.

LOCATION AND WORKING ARRANGEMENT

This position is based at Liteline's Richmond Hill head office and is on-site five days per week with regular presence at our distribution facilities.

The successful candidate should expect to be highly engaged with the business and to spend real time understanding how departments and facilities actually operate.

THE OPPORTUNITY

This is a rare chance to shape how an established Canadian manufacturer builds and runs its technology at a moment when AI is changing who can create software.

Liteline is privately held, decisions are made without layers of approval, and good ideas get backed. Our leaders build with technology themselves and value this work. The Director of Business Technology will define the platforms, guardrails and habits that let the whole company build with confidence.

WHAT WE OFFER

Liteline offers a comprehensive benefits package including medical, dental and life insurance following three months of service, and a group RRSP with partial company match.

TO APPLY

Qualified candidates are invited to apply directly through this posting.

Liteline Corporation is an equal opportunity employer that values the unique skills and experiences of every candidate. We are committed to accommodating people with disabilities throughout the recruitment and hiring process. To request accommodation, please contact Human Resources with the position title in the subject line.

jobs.title: Director of Financial Planning and Analysis
jobs.description:
About Allied

Allied is a leading owner-operator of distinctive urban workspace in Canada’s major cities. Our work is grounded in a clear purpose: to provide knowledge-based organizations with distinctive urban environments that support creativity, connectivity and human wellness.

Our vision is more expansive. We seek to make a continuous contribution to cities and culture that elevates and inspires the humanity in all of us. This vision informs how we operate, how we design and how we lead.

Real estate, for us, is not a passive investment. It is a profoundly human endeavour, one that must promote wellness, sustainability, diversity and creativity—today and for generations to come.

Allied is also a place to build a career of consequence. If you are looking for work that is thoughtful, tangible and enduring—work that contributes meaningfully to cities and the people who inhabit them—you will find purpose here.

For more information on Allied’s approach to city-building, visit our Insights page.

Purpose

Lead Allied’s financial planning, forecasting, performance analysis and management reporting activities.
As Director, Financial Planning & Analysis (FP&A), you will lead budgeting and forecasting processes, develop long-term financial plans and provide analysis of financial and operating performance across Allied’s portfolio and corporate functions.

As a key member of the Finance leadership team, you will serve as a strategic business partner to senior leaders and help strengthen financial planning, analytical capabilities and financial discipline across the organization. This role is well suited to a collaborative and forward-looking finance leader with strong financial modelling and analytical capabilities and a commitment to developing people and building high-performing teams.

Responsibilities

Financial Planning, Budgeting and Forecasting
Lead budgeting and forecasting processes across the organization, establishing timelines, assumptions and requirements in partnership with key stakeholders.
Develop and own consolidated financial forecasts and multi-year financial plans.
Establish and track key performance indicators related to occupancy, leasing, operating performance, capital expenditures, financing and other business drivers.
Develop scenario and sensitivity analyses to assess the financial implications of changing business and market conditions.
Continuously enhance planning and forecasting processes to improve accuracy, efficiency and business insight.

Performance Analysis and Management Reporting
Lead the preparation of monthly and quarterly management reporting for senior leadership.
Analyze actual financial performance relative to budget, forecast and prior periods, identifying key drivers of variances.
Analyze key performance indicators, including funds from operations (FFO), adjusted funds from operations (AFFO) and related financial and operating metrics.
Identify emerging trends, risks and opportunities and communicate their potential financial impact to senior leadership.
Develop and maintain dashboards, scorecards and other reporting tools that provide clear visibility into organizational performance.
Lead the development of financial and performance reporting for the Board of Trustees and its committees.

Long-Term Financial Planning and Strategic Analysis
Lead the development and maintenance of Allied’s long-term financial model.
Assess the impact of changes in occupancy, leasing activity, rental rates, interest rates, capital expenditures, development activity and other key business assumptions.
Model the financial implications of potential acquisitions, dispositions, developments and other strategic initiatives in partnership with Investments and other business functions.
Evaluate alternative financial scenarios and provide recommendations to support strategic planning and capital allocation decisions.
Provide financial analysis and recommendations to the Chief Financial Officer and senior leadership to support business and strategic decisions.
Assess the impact of business plans and strategic initiatives on liquidity, leverage, FFO, AFFO and other key financial measures.

Capital Planning
Coordinate Allied’s annual and long-term capital planning processes.
Consolidate forecasts for property capital expenditures, leasing capital, tenant improvements and development expenditures.
Monitor capital spending against approved plans and identify material variances, risks and emerging requirements.
Integrate capital plans into corporate forecasts and long-term financial models.
Provide analysis of the impact of capital investments on financial performance, liquidity and key REIT metrics.

FP&A Systems, Data and Continuous Improvement
Lead the development and enhancement of financial planning, forecasting and management reporting tools and processes.
Identify opportunities to automate and streamline financial planning and reporting activities.
Establish consistent financial models, reporting methodologies and performance measures across the organization.
Promote effective use of financial and operational data to improve business insight and decision-making.
Partner with Corporate Accounting and technology teams to support the effective integration of financial systems, data and reporting tools.
Champion continuous improvement and best practices across the FP&A function.

Leadership and Team Development
Lead, mentor and develop the FP&A team, fostering strong analytical, financial and business-partnering capabilities.
Establish clear priorities and expectations and promote a high standard of quality, accountability and collaboration.
Build strong relationships across Finance and the broader organization.
Develop organizational capability through coaching, knowledge sharing and succession planning.
Foster a culture of curiosity, continuous improvement and informed decision-making.

Qualifications

CPA designation required.
7+ years of progressive experience in accounting and finance within commercial real estate or property accounting.
Strong technical accounting and financial reporting experience, including full-cycle accounting processes.
Experience leading and developing high-performing teams.
Experience supporting budgeting and reforecasting processes in partnership with FP&A and operational teams.
Strong interpersonal and relationship-building skills, with the ability to collaborate effectively across functions and levels of the organization.
Strong analytical, problem-solving and organizational skills, with a high level of attention to detail.
Experience with Yardi or similar property accounting systems is considered an asset.

Total Rewards and the Employee Experience

At Allied, total rewards are designed with the same perspective that shapes our operations. They are intended to support sustained contribution, creativity and a genuine sense of ownership in the work we do.

In practice, this includes:

Shared financial success and an ownership mindset

Eligible employees participate in performance-based bonus programs and a retirement savings program, with the option to invest in traditional funds or Allied units. This approach aligns individual effort with Allied’s long-term performance and reinforces a sense of ownership at every level of the organization.

Intentional presence and time off

In addition to vacation, employees receive six personal days and half-days before statutory holidays. Allied supports flexibility while maintaining a strong, in-person culture. This reflects how we collaborate most effectively and how we operate as a business.

Health, wellbeing and support

Comprehensive, company-paid health benefits include vision and dental coverage, along with a healthcare spending account. An employee assistance program is available to provide confidential support when it is needed.

Growth through leadership and exposure

Allied believes in leadership at every level. Employees are encouraged to contribute beyond the boundaries of their role, collaborate across disciplines and develop a broad understanding of the business. For those drawn to real estate, this includes uncommon exposure to how buildings, organizations and cities evolve through hands-on experience and shared responsibility.

Professional development grounded in practice

Learning at Allied is both formal and experiential. Ongoing professional development and a mentorship program support growth through structured learning and day-to-day engagement with experienced colleagues across the organization.

Purpose and connection beyond work

Each year, employees are provided with a paid volunteer day to contribute time and effort to a cause that is personally meaningful to them, reflecting our belief that contribution extends beyond the workplace.

If you are motivated by the role real estate plays in shaping cities and culture, and want your work to contribute to that effort, we encourage you to apply.

More insight into life at Allied, including our ESG and EDI initiatives, can be found in our annual ESG report.

Additional Information

We value human connection and experience. While Allied uses technology, including AI-enabled tools, to support administrative efficiency, all screening, assessment and hiring decisions are made by people.

We are committed to hiring the most qualified candidates with a dedication towards supporting diversity, equity and inclusion across our organization. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to gender, ethnicity, origin, sexual orientation, disability and socioeconomic background. Diverse perspectives strengthen our organization and help us deliver better outcomes for our tenants, partners and communities. All qualified candidates are encouraged to apply.

We strive to provide an accessible recruitment experience and welcome reasonable accommodation requests at any stage of the recruitment process. Please reach out to talent@alliedreit.com if support is needed.

We look forward to receiving your application.

jobs.title: Director, Engineering, AI
jobs.description:
Job Description

Are you passionate about transforming how legal professionals find trusted answers with AI? Join our Global Westlaw Engineering organization and help shape the future of AI-driven legal research.

Westlaw helps legal professionals around the world research, analyze, and act with confidence. We are building the next generation of fiduciary-level, AI-powered legal research and workflow capabilities, and we are changing how we build software.

As Director, you will lead a global organization of engineering managers, senior engineers, and vendor partners. You will own the multi-year AI engineering strategy and its alignment with the product delivery roadmap. You will move the organization to mission-based teams with clear ownership and accountability. You will also drive the shift to AI-assisted, agent-driven development and use engineering data to guide decisions and show results.

We want a technical leader with a track record of leading AI transformation, who leads by example, stays hands-on, keeps up with AI and engineering best practices, uses data to find what needs to change, and empowers teams to innovate across the organization.

Key Responsibilities

Lead

Lead a high-performing global organization. Set clear expectations, coach managers and engineers, and lead by example, using AI tools and engineering data in your own work.
Stay close to the technical work. Work directly with senior engineers on architecture, technical direction, and hard problems to raise the technical bar across the organization.
Own Engineering strategy implementation and its alignment with the product delivery roadmap. Run it as a living plan with clear milestones and owners, adapt quickly as priorities evolve, and recommend measures that keep engineering objectives aligned to business strategy.
Lead the transformation to a mission-based operating model. Replace project-by-project handoffs with long-lived teams that own a product area, service, or customer outcome from design through production support. Define each team's mission, scope, decision rights, and the skills and authority it needs.
Set measures for each mission. Define measures such as reliability, quality, delivery speed, adoption, and cost. Review them regularly and use them to guide priorities, resourcing, and accountability.
Manage the vendor relationship. Help the vendor keep pace with business needs. Integrate vendor-managed teams into the organization, with clear scope, outcomes, service levels, and governance. Hold them to the same standards as internal teams for architecture, quality, security, and delivery, and measure their performance with the same data. Make sure they document their work and transfer knowledge, so the organization does not depend on a single vendor.
Decide what to do in-house, with partners, or through vendors. Balance cost, speed, capability, risk, and long-term knowledge retention.
Communicate proactively. Show how your organization's work delivers business value and supports strategy, and work directly with stakeholders and peers to shape the future of our products.

Deliver

Deliver strategic projects with urgency. Partner with Product Management, UX Design, and other Technology teams. Remove blockers, make timely decisions, and enable your teams to solve complex business problems with clearly defined outcomes.
Drive the end-to-end AI lifecycle. Own the work from retrieval and model integration through evaluation, deployment, and monitoring.
Set the standard for operational excellence. Hold AI and non-AI services to high standards for reliability, security, performance, and cost. Champion a DevOps-first model supported by automation, CI/CD, and infrastructure as code on AWS.
Manage the project portfolio. Own budget, priorities, and staff allocation.

Operate: Run a Data-Driven, AI-Enabled Organization:

Provide guardrails and empower teams to use AI. Equip managers, engineers, and teams to apply AI in daily engineering work, including coding assistants, agents, code review, test automation, and quality evaluation. Provide clear guardrails for responsible use, covering security, data handling, and human review of AI-generated code and outputs. Within those guardrails, encourage teams to experiment and adopt AI, and remove the barriers that slow them down.
Make decisions with data. Analyze GitHub data, such as pull request cycle time, review latency, build and deployment frequency, and AI tool usage, to find bottlenecks and show where change is working.
Track ownership and accountability. Use incident response, change failure rate, and cycle time by team to show whether ownership and accountability are improving. Share results openly, use them to coach rather than blame, and turn them into practical changes in how teams work.
Measure the impact of AI. Track its effect on delivery speed, code quality, defect rates, and reliability. Use those measures to adjust strategy and investment.
Own the economics of AI usage. Set AI budgets, and track and optimize token consumption, inference cost, and tooling spend. Guide model selection and cost-versus-quality trade-offs, balancing them against productivity, quality, and speed.

Innovate

Stay on top of the AI landscape. Follow new models, agent frameworks, tool protocols such as MCP, and retrieval patterns. Judge what is production-ready, bring it into your teams' practices, and grow adoption of AI/ML engineering practices and frameworks across the enterprise.
Try new approaches. Take informed risks. Encourage your managers and teams to do the same, and recognize those who do.

Required Qualifications

Education. A bachelor's degree in computer science, information technology, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience.
Experience. 10+ years in software development, including 3+ years leading AI solution development, and 10+ years managing managers and building high-performing engineering teams in an agile environment.
Organizational leadership. Experience leading managers, individual contributors, and vendor-managed teams, including scope, performance, cost, and quality. You can coach managers on people leadership and engage credibly with Staff and Principal engineers.
Strategy and execution. Experience turning a multi-year vision into programs, roadmaps, and measurable results across multiple teams, including large-scale rollouts and infrastructure initiatives.
Shipping AI in production. A track record of shipping LLM-based applications, RAG, or agent workflows in production-grade software. You can speak credibly about prompt and context design, retrieval, evaluation, and production trade-offs.
Cloud, DevOps, and reliability. Strong depth in cloud-native architecture on AWS, CI/CD, and infrastructure as code, and experience running mission-critical, high-availability systems.
Hands-on AI tool use. Daily use of AI coding tools (e.g., GitHub Copilot, Cursor, Claude Code). You lead by example and have empowered managers and teams to adopt AI-assisted development, with strong practices for review, quality, and security.

jobs.title: Director, Enterprise Financial Performance
jobs.description:
SaskEnergy is seeking a qualified and motivated individual to join our team. Director, Enterprise Financial Performance directs and provides strategic leadership for a focused enterprise function that improves the Corporation’s financial performance through sustainable cost control, productivity improvement, revenue assurance, revenue optimization and stronger financial discipline. The Director identifies and prioritizes material opportunities, leads targeted financial and operational analysis, and works collaboratively with business and functional leaders to develop and advance practical solutions. This position leads complex and cross-functional reviews where issues require dedicated capacity, independent challenge and integrated financial and operational judgment. Business and functional leaders retain accountability for operational decisions, execution, ongoing process ownership and sustainment.

Position Details

Non-union. This position is permanent full time.

Key Accountabilities

Direct the development and management of a prioritized pipeline of material cost, productivity, revenue and financial-performance opportunities aligned with Corporate priorities and financial objectives.
Lead targeted reviews of material, recurring or cross-functional cost and performance issues to identify underlying operational, process, resource, technology and accountability drivers; quantify opportunities and recommend practical actions.
Lead or coordinate initiatives to strengthen revenue integrity and optimize revenue, including revenue leakage, billing and collection process gaps, non-tariffed service fees, cost recovery, missed billable activity and other opportunities.
Provide strategic financial analysis and independent decision support for complex or emerging matters of enterprise significance, including financial modelling, options and scenario analysis, investigations and fact finding.
Assess end-to-end accountabilities, hand-offs and operating models where financial performance issues cross organizational boundaries; facilitate decisions and support accountable leaders in implementing agreed changes.
Mobilize and coordinate the business, financial, process-improvement, technology and other expertise required to evaluate opportunities, design practical solutions and support implementation.
Work with accountable leaders to establish implementation plans, milestones, ownership and expected outcomes; identify barriers and support corrective action through to transition and sustainment.
Work with Finance and business leaders to ensure financial impacts are appropriately validated and sustainable improvements are reflected in Corporate forecasts, budgets and financial plans.
Provide concise, evidence-based recommendations, portfolio updates, risks and decisions required to the CFO, Executive and other governance bodies.
Strengthen financial acumen by helping leaders understand cost and revenue drivers and apply financial and operational information to material decisions and improvement opportunities.
Direct and develop the Enterprise Financial Performance function, establish effective operating practices and resource requirements, lead assigned employees, and oversee the effective use of matrixed and contracted resources.
Monitor relevant utility, cost-management, revenue-assurance and enterprise-performance practices and recommend approaches that can improve sustainable Corporate financial outcomes.
Other related duties as assigned.

Knowledge/Skills/Abilities

Degree in Business Administration, Commerce, Finance, Accounting, Economics, Engineering or a related discipline.
A professional accounting designation or other relevant professional credential is an asset. Process-improvement, project or change-management training is also beneficial.
Ten (10) years of progressively responsible experience in financial management, business performance, financial analysis, operational improvement, commercial analysis, transformation or related work in a complex organization, including leadership of significant cross-functional initiatives.
Strong knowledge of regulated utility, energy or similarly asset-intensive operations and the relationship among safety, reliability, customer service, cost structures, revenues, capital investment, regulation and financial performance.
Demonstrated financial and commercial acumen, including interpretation of financial statements, cost and revenue drivers, business cases, complex financial modelling, scenario analysis and translation of operational issues into financial implications.
Demonstrated ability to identify and prioritize material opportunities, move from analysis to practical action, and influence accountable leaders without assuming operational authority.
Knowledge of revenue assurance, cost management, end-to-end process analysis, operating-model design, performance improvement, implementation and benefit-realization practices.
Exceptional judgment, facilitation, negotiation and executive communication skills, with the ability to constructively challenge established practices and work effectively across organizational boundaries.
Ability to lead and develop employees and coordinate multidisciplinary resources through ambiguity, competing priorities and sensitive organizational issues.
Must have a continuing record of professional development and continuous learning.

A suitable combination of relevant education and experience may also be considered.

Additional Information

Travel, including overnight stays away from headquarters, is required on occasion.
A Class 5 Driver’s License is required.

Application Instructions

Please apply online with your cover letter and resume outlining your qualifications.
For more information on this position, please contact Human Resources at 306-777-9091.

October 29, 2026

$135,237 - $193,956

jobs.description:
We’re building a relationship-oriented bank for the modern world. We need talented, passionate professionals who are dedicated to doing what’s right for our clients. 

 At CIBC, we embrace your strengths and your ambitions, so you are empowered at work. Our team members have what they need to make a meaningful impact and are truly valued for who they are and what they contribute. 

 To learn more about CIBC, please visit CIBC.com 

 What you'll be doing 

 As part of CIBC’s technology team, you’ll lead our AI Applications Development function and guide a high-performing team of AI engineers, developers, and quality assurance specialists who build and support enterprise-grade AI solutions. As Director, you’ll provide technical and people leadership to drive the design, development, deployment, and ongoing evolution of advanced AI applications across the bank. You’ll work closely with technology and business partners to shape solution architecture, define integration requirements, and deliver solutions that align to strategic priorities and enterprise standards. You’ll help ensure our AI-driven applications are secure, scalable, reliable, and well monitored, with a strong focus on cloud-native delivery, observability, and compliance. You’ll also foster a culture of innovation, collaboration, continuous improvement, and strong documentation practices while supporting your leaders and teams in delivering high-quality solutions that enhance the client experience.

 At CIBC we enable the work environment most optimal for you to thrive in your role. Details on your work arrangement (proportion of on-site and remote work) will be discussed at the time of your interview. 

 How you'll succeed  
 People leadership - Lead and develop a team of leaders, AI engineers, developers, and quality assurance specialists by setting clear direction, providing meaningful coaching, and creating opportunities for growth. Build an inclusive, high-performing environment where team members are supported, accountable, and connected to CIBC’s priorities.
 Strategic partnership - Build trusted relationships with technology and business partners, vendors, and senior stakeholders to understand business needs, translate them into practical AI solutions, and influence decisions through clear, business-focused communication.
 Technical leadership - Guide architecture and engineering decisions for enterprise AI applications, with a focus on security, scalability, performance, and reliability. Support the development and deployment of modern AI solutions using tools and technologies such as Python, FastAPI, JavaScript frameworks, Azure AI services, retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), large language models (LLMs), and agentic AI frameworks.
 Quality and platform excellence - Champion strong engineering practices across cloud infrastructure, continuous integration and continuous delivery, observability, documentation, and test automation to help ensure solutions are resilient, maintainable, and ready for enterprise scale.
 Delivery leadership - Work with internal partners to prioritize, plan, and deliver initiatives on agreed timelines and budgets. Identify opportunities to improve efficiency, encourage reuse across teams, and help shape a shared AI strategy that scales across the enterprise.

 Who you are  
 You are a hands-on builder first. You have recently designed, built, and shipped production AI applications yourself, and you still enjoy writing code, reviewing pull requests, and solving production issues alongside the team.
 You bring strong technical depth. You have hands-on experience with Python, FastAPI, JavaScript (Vue.js or React.js), SQL, Redis, and Azure Cloud services, including Azure OpenAI / AI Foundry and API Management. You are comfortable with CI/CD tools such as GitHub Actions and QA automation frameworks such as Playwright, Cypress, or Selenium.
 You know modern AI engineering. You have built solutions using large language models (LLMs), retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), prompt and context engineering, tool calling, and agentic frameworks such as LangGraph, LangChain, LangSmith, or equivalent. It’s an asset if you have experience with Databricks, LLM evaluation, and observability for AI agents in production (e.g., Splunk, OpenTelemetry).
 You build for the enterprise. You design for security, scalability, reliability, and compliance, and you understand what it takes to run AI safely in a regulated environment.
 You are ready to grow as a people leader. You mentor engineers, set technical direction, and raise the engineering bar. You are excited to grow into leading a team of engineers and QA specialists as the function scales.
 Your influence makes a difference. You build trusted relationships with business and technology partners, translate business needs into practical AI solutions, and explain complex ideas clearly to non-technical audiences.
 You're digitally savvy. You are curious, adapt quickly to new tools and trends, and take ownership of outcomes in a fast-moving space.
 You live your values. You bring high standards, genuine care to your relationships, and want to grow with an employer that shares your values and brings out your best.

 What CIBC Offers 

 At CIBC, your goals are a priority. We start with your strengths and ambitions as an employee and strive to create opportunities to tap into your potential. We aspire to give you a career, rather than just a paycheck.
 We work to recognize you in meaningful, personalized ways including a competitive salary, incentive pay, banking benefits, a benefits program*, defined benefit pension plan*, an employee share purchase plan, a vacation offering, wellbeing support, and MomentMakers, our social, points-based recognition program.

 Our spaces and technological toolkit will make it simple to bring together great minds to create innovative solutions that make a difference for our clients.

 We cultivate a culture where you can express your ambition through initiatives like Purpose Day; a paid day off dedicated for you to use to invest in your growth and development.

Exceptional organizational and project oversight skills, including resource allocation, and timeline control across large, multi-stakeholder initiatives.

jobs.title: Senior Director of Finance & Operations
jobs.description:
BoomerangFX

Location:
Mississauga, Ontario — on-site, five days per week
Reports to:
Chief Executive Officer

Mandatory Experience

A Canadian CPA designation and hands-on experience leading finance and operations for a PE-backed SaaS company scaling ARR from $5 million to $50 million are mandatory. Only applicants meeting these requirements will be considered for the role.

Why Join BoomerangFX?

BoomerangFX is a global healthcare technology company bringing SaaS, artificial intelligence and digital marketing together to help private-pay healthcare practices operate and grow. Recognized through Deloitte’s Technology Fast 500 program, we are building technology that simplifies practice management, strengthens patient engagement and helps healthcare businesses reach more people.
With operations in the United States, Canada, the United Kingdom, Australia and India
, we are scaling internationally and working at the forefront of AI in healthcare. Our teams collaborate across countries and disciplines to turn new ideas into products and services that make a practical difference for customers.

Joining BoomerangFX is an opportunity to build your career alongside a growing global business. You will have meaningful responsibility, exposure to international markets and the opportunity to contribute ideas, develop your skills and see the impact of your work. We welcome people who take ownership, move quickly and want to help build what comes next.

The Role

Reporting to the CEO, you will lead financial management and general operations with strong financial acumen, commercial judgment and a practical approach to execution
.

You will oversee the Controller and Accountant
while taking responsibility for talent acquisition, human resources, vendor negotiations and corporate infrastructure
. You must be comfortable reviewing the detail, challenging assumptions and resolving issues personally while building an accountable team.

Financial Leadership and Accounting Oversight

Directly oversee the Controller and Accountant, setting clear expectations for accuracy, reporting deadlines, financial controls and accountability. Review their work and provide hands-on guidance on complex issues.
Own the quality and timeliness of monthly, quarterly and annual financial reporting. Review financial statements, balance-sheet reconciliations, management reports and material accounting judgments.
Oversee billing, subscription revenue recognition, deferred revenue, collections, accounts payable, payroll and intercompany reporting. Maintain clear controls over approvals, payments and financial records.
Coordinate external accountants, auditors and tax advisers, and strengthen accounting policies and controls as the company scales.

Financial Performance and Cash Management

Lead annual budgeting, rolling forecasts, financial modelling and variance analysis. Challenge assumptions and translate financial results into clear recommendations for the CEO and department leaders.
Own a rolling 13-week cash-flow forecast and longer-term liquidity projections. Improve collections, working capital, spending discipline and visibility into financial commitments.
Analyze profitability by product, service and market. Use SaaS metrics, including ARR, retention, churn, gross margin, customer acquisition cost and payback, to evaluate performance and investment decisions.
Assess hiring plans, pricing, operating costs and major expenditures against expected returns. Drive measurable improvements in margins, productivity and progress toward sustainable profitability.

Talent Acquisition and Human Resources

Oversee talent acquisition and human resources, including internal staff and external providers. Align recruitment priorities and headcount plans with approved budgets and business needs.
Oversee recruitment execution, agency relationships, hiring timelines, onboarding and workforce planning. Hold hiring managers accountable for clear requirements, timely decisions and hiring outcomes.
Oversee HR administration, employee records, compensation and benefits coordination, performance-review processes, employee relations and offboarding, working with qualified advisers where required.

Vendor Negotiations and Corporate Infrastructure

Lead vendor negotiations and oversee procurement, contracts and renewals. Secure commercially sound pricing, payment terms and service commitments, and hold providers accountable for delivery.
Oversee corporate infrastructure, including offices, facilities, equipment, business systems and outsourced services. Ensure these resources support reliable daily operations and future growth.
Work with technology leaders on corporate IT providers, software licences, infrastructure spending and business continuity arrangements. Improve utilization and eliminate unnecessary or duplicate costs.

Operating Performance and Team Leadership

Establish operating KPIs, management dashboards and regular performance reviews across finance and the functions under your oversight.
Improve workflows, approval processes and reporting through practical automation and stronger data quality. Ensure corrective actions have accountable owners and deadlines.
Lead and develop the finance team and collaborate with Sales, Marketing, Customer Success, Product and Technology leaders to improve execution and resource allocation.

Mandatory Qualifications

CPA designation in good standing in Canada.

At least 10 years of progressive finance experience, including hands-on leadership across financial reporting, controllership, budgeting, forecasting, cash management and operating performance.
At least three years of hands-on experience in a fast-paced SaaS business, including leadership of finance and operations for a PE-backed SaaS company scaling ARR from $5 million to $50 million.

Strong financial acumen and commercial judgment: the ability to interrogate financial results, build credible forecasts, evaluate SaaS unit economics and make sound decisions on costs, headcount and investment.
Proven experience directly supervising a Controller and accounting staff, reviewing their work and maintaining high standards for financial accuracy, control and delivery.
Direct experience overseeing talent acquisition, human resources, vendor negotiations and corporate infrastructure, with accountability for operational results.
Advanced financial modelling and Excel or Google Sheets skills, proficiency with accounting and reporting systems, and the ability to explain financial issues clearly to business leaders.
A record of personal ownership and effective execution in an environment with rapidly changing priorities, tight deadlines and limited resources. You must be willing to work on-site in Mississauga five days per week.

Additional Experience We Value

Measurable success improving profitability, cash generation or progress toward break-even.
Experience managing multiple entities, currencies or international operations.
Experience in healthcare technology or a business combining SaaS subscriptions and services.
Experience implementing finance systems, automating reporting or supporting transaction readiness.

Compensation and Benefits

Base salary:
CAD $135,000–$150,000 annually.
Annual target performance bonus:
50% of base salary, based on achievement of agreed performance objectives.
Total target compensation:
CAD $202,500–$225,000 annually.
Performance objectives will reflect measurable outcomes in profitability, cash management, financial reporting and operational execution.
Comprehensive health, dental and vision coverage.
Paid vacation and free on-site parking.
An opportunity to work closely with the CEO and senior leadership and make a measurable contribution to a growing global healthcare technology business.

How to Apply

Submit your résumé with a brief summary of your experience in high-growth software or technology-enabled companies, including two or three measurable financial or operational results you personally delivered.
Shortlisted candidates should be prepared to discuss their experience with financial oversight, operational leadership, strategic planning, and board reporting. CPA credentials, employment experience, and professional references will be verified.

Accessibility Statement

BoomerangFX is an equal opportunity employer committed to diversity and inclusion. We welcome applications from all qualified individuals and are dedicated to accommodating people with disabilities. If you require accommodation at any stage of the application process, please contact recruitment@boomerangfx.com.

Ontario Brain Institute (OBI) is a provincially funded, not-for-profit research organization driving discovery and innovation to improve brain health.
