The Aga Khan Museum connects cultures and communities through the arts. The Museum’s mission is to spark wonder, curiosity, and understanding of Muslim cultures and their connection with other cultures through the arts.

The Toronto-based Museum promotes pluralism through art, storytelling, and enlightened encounters across cultures. Using traditional and contemporary art as well as performing arts as a force for positive change, the Museum’s vision is to impact lives and contribute to more inclusive and peaceful societies. The Museum acts as a global learning hub, playing a unique and pivotal role in building connections between people and communities locally, nationally, and internationally.

Purpose of Position

Reporting to the Director & Chief Executive Officer, the Chief Financial Officer (CFO) is a key member of the Senior Leadership Team (SLT) responsible for the financial sustainability, stewardship, risk management and financial governance of the organization, while serving as a strategic advisor to the Director & CEO, Board of Directors, and SLT. The CFO also provides financial and strategic oversight of the Museum’s commercial activities.

Leadership Profile

The ideal candidate is a strategic and financially sophisticated executive who combines disciplined stewardship with sound commercial judgment. They are collaborative, analytical and results-oriented, with exceptional integrity, sound judgement and the ability to communicate complex financial matters clearly. They build strong relationships with the internal senior leaders and external partners and are capable of leading through change and complexity while advancing the Museum’s mission.

Ultimately, the CFO is responsible for safeguarding the organization's financial health and long-term sustainability.

Key Responsibilities

Strategic Leadership

Serve as a strategic advisor to the Director & CEO, SLT, and Board of Directors.
Serve as the principal management liaison with the Board, Finance & Audit Committee, and the Investment Committee by preparing and presenting financial information and recommendations, supporting Committee mandates, agendas and decision-making, advising the Board on significant financial risks and ensuring appropriate follow-up on Board and Committee decisions.
Foster collaboration, accountability, innovation, and continuous improvement.
Build, develop and lead high-performing finance, procurement, and commercial teams with appropriate capabilities, succession, accountability and service orientation.

Financial Stewardship

Develop and maintain a long-term financial sustainability framework, including scenarios focused on funding, operating costs, reserves, liquidity and capital requirements aligned with the organizational strategy of the Museum.
Lead the annual budgeting, multi-year financial planning, forecasting, management reporting and financial performance analysis processes, ensuring that financial resources are aligned with the Museum’s strategic priorities.
Lead the Museum’s preparation for and coordination of the annual external financial statement audit, serving as the senior management liaison with the external auditors and ensuring the timely resolution and communication of significant audit matters, findings and recommendations.
Partner with the Development team to support fundraising and grant objectives through sound financial planning, proposal development and reporting, and ensure appropriate accounting and stewardship of restricted funds, grants, funding agreements and donor-designated resources.
Identify opportunities to enhance revenue, control costs, and improve Museum performance.

Risk, Compliance & Governance

Accountable for the integrity and timeliness of the Museum’s financial statements, management and Board reporting, accounting practices, internal controls, external audit and statutory and regulatory reporting.
Oversee treasury, liquidity, banking and financing arrangements, reserve strategy, investment governance and performance, and the financial planning and oversight of major capital requirements and projects.
Ensures the Museum maintains its tax-exempt charitable status and meets all related tax compliance requirements, including tax reporting, disbursement quotas, and dealings with the CRA.
Lead the Museum’s enterprise risk management framework and consolidated risk reporting, ensuring that significant financial, operational, insurance, legal, contractual, technology and other organizational risks have appropriate ownership, assessment and mitigation plans.
Coordinate the integration of enterprise risk management with business continuity planning and reporting to the Board and relevant Committees.
Provide executive oversight of procurement, ensuring appropriate policies, competitive practices, delegated authorities, contract controls and value for money.

Commercial Activities

Provide financial and strategic oversight of the Museum’s commercial activities.
Work with the responsible operational leaders to establish and monitor appropriate revenue, margin and performance targets and ensure effective financial controls and reporting.
Evaluate significant new commercial opportunities for financial viability, organizational capacity, risk and alignment with the Museum’s mission and strategic priorities.
Establish and monitor commercial performance targets.

CPA designation.
MBA or graduate degree in business, finance, or a related field is an asset.
Minimum 10 years of progressive leadership experience, including at least five years in a senior financial leadership or executive role.
Proven expertise in financial leadership, strategic planning, organizational performance, risk management, and governance.
Experience providing financial and strategic oversight of commercial activities.
Experience presenting to Boards and leading multidisciplinary teams.
Nonprofit and/or charitable sector experience in arts, culture, hospitality, tourism, entertainment, education, or other mission-driven organizations preferred.

High energy and driven.

Accurate and timely reporting

Strong controls and reconciliations
Improved collections and working capital
Reliable budgets and forecasts
Efficient accounting processes
A capable and accountable finance team

This is more than a CFO role. It's an opportunity to step into a key leadership position, partner directly with the CEO, and help shape the future of a growing healthcare organization. If you're ready to build, lead, influence, and make a lasting impact, we encourage you to apply.

The position is responsible for the financial stewardship and accountability of public funds administered by Health. At the core of their duties is the oversight of the department’s capital and operations and maintenance budget, ensuring that financial resources are allocated efficiently and in accordance with government policies and regulations. The Director of Finance is also accountable for compliance with financial regulations and standards. They must ensure that all financial transactions and operations within the department adhere to the Financial Administrative Manual (FAM) as well as legal and ethical guidelines.

The main responsibilities of the Director are, but are not limited to:

Leading the process of developing the department's annual budget, working with program managers and finance staff to gather input, projections, and cost estimates;
Facilitating the budget approval process, working closely with government agencies, legislative bodies, and stakeholders to address questions, concerns, and revisions;
Overseeing the allocation and execution of budgeted funds, ensuring that expenditures are in line with approved allocations and regulatory guidelines;
Managing the process for budget amendments or revisions as necessary, providing clear justifications and seeking necessary approvals for changes;
Ensuring that all financial reports meet regulatory requirements and government accounting principles, providing transparency and accountability in financial disclosures;
Establishing and maintaining robust internal controls to safeguard financial assets, prevent fraud, and ensure the accuracy and integrity of financial data;
Overseeing and leading a team of financial professionals, providing guidance, mentorship, and support to promote their professional growth and ensure effective departmental operations;
Fostering a culture of collaboration and cross-functional teamwork, working closely with other department heads to ensure financial considerations are integrated into broader strategic planning.

The knowledge, skills, and abilities required for this job are usually obtained through a recognized:

Undergraduate degree in accounting, finance, business administration, economics, commerce, or related field;
Completion of a professional accounting designation CPA (CMA, CGA or CA);
Eight (8) years of related experience;
Five (5) years of progressive managerial experience in assigning priorities and managing performance of professional teams.

This is a Position of Trust and a satisfactory Criminal Record Check is required.

Come shape the future of brand experience.

At Jack Morton, we design and build
head-turning, smile-inducing, impact-driving brand experiences that redefine what experiential marketing can achieve. We help our clients unlock the full value of experiences

Experience without limits—in your work, your growth, and your impact.

The Opportunity

We're looking for a commercially minded and operationally focused Finance Director, Fabrication Operations
to serve as the finance lead and strategic business partner for our North American fabrication network.

Partnering directly with the Head of Fabrication, you will help build the financial and operational foundation for a growing multi-site production organization. This role is ideal for someone who thrives at the intersection of finance and operations, can connect financial performance to what is happening on the production floor, and enjoys transforming data into actionable business decisions.

You will play a critical role in improving profitability, building reporting and forecasting capabilities, optimizing capacity utilization, and supporting the integration and standardization of fabrication operations across the network.

What You'll Do

Financial Performance & Cost Management

Build and maintain consistent individual and consolidated P&Ls across four fabrication facilities, along with separate P&Ls for storage, rental inventory, and fleet operations.
Conduct a comprehensive assessment of facility cost structures, labor models, capacity utilization, and current reporting practices.
Develop budgeting, forecasting, and scenario-planning models covering labor, overtime, freelance resources, subcontracting, storage, fleet, and facility expenses.
Establish project profitability reviews to compare estimated versus actual margins and create feedback loops that improve future estimating and pricing decisions.
Analyze labor productivity, utilization, overhead absorption, and operational drivers of profitability.
Partner with operational leaders to identify opportunities to improve margins, reduce waste, optimize labor deployment, and increase financial discipline.
Lead monthly performance reviews with fabrication leadership teams.

Capacity Planning & Network Optimization

Map capacity against demand across the fabrication network and develop reporting that supports more effective planning and resource allocation.
Improve pipeline visibility to provide a reliable view of future fabrication demand and workload requirements.
Separate fabrication, non-fabrication, and insourced work streams to support accurate capacity planning and decision-making.
Support long-term network planning, including facility footprint decisions, capability investments, and capital expenditure evaluations.
Build financial models that support insource versus outsource decisions, staffing strategies, overtime management, and facility investments.
Support vendor consolidation initiatives, rebate tracking, and procurement savings opportunities.

Reporting, KPIs & Integration

Develop and implement a standardized KPI framework across all fabrication locations, including utilization, throughput, overtime, on-time delivery, rework, and profitability metrics.
Launch and maintain executive dashboards covering network performance, financial performance, pipeline, capacity utilization, storage, rental inventory, and fleet operations.
Establish standardized reporting and performance management processes across all locations.
Support the integration of Jack Morton and Impact XM fabrication operations through common definitions, metrics, and processes for job costing, work orders, change orders, and markup structures.
Support D365 adoption and help reduce reliance on manual processes and offline workarounds.
Partner across Fabrication, Finance, Commercial, Estimating, Creative, Account, and Project Management teams to improve planning, visibility, profitability, and operational execution.

What We're Looking For

8-12+ years of progressive finance experience, including significant experience supporting manufacturing, fabrication, production, logistics, or other operational environments.
Strong understanding of cost accounting, job costing, labor utilization, overhead allocation, margin analysis, and operational performance management.
Experience supporting multiple facilities, locations, or operating units.
Demonstrated ability to build financial models, forecasting processes, dashboards, and KPI frameworks from the ground up.
Experience driving finance process improvements, operational standardization, and systems adoption within growing or transforming organizations.
Strong analytical skills with the ability to translate complex financial information into actionable operational recommendations.
Experience evaluating capital investments and developing ROI-based business cases.
Strong business partnering and stakeholder management skills with the ability to influence leaders across functions.
Comfortable working in fast-paced, project-based environments where priorities can shift quickly.
Advanced Excel and financial modeling skills; experience with ERP systems and business intelligence tools preferred.
Bachelor's degree in Finance, Accounting, Economics, or a related field. CPA, CMA, or MBA is a plus.

What Success Looks Like

Assessed the financial and operational performance of all fabrication facilities and support operations.
Established consistent facility, storage, rental, and fleet P&Ls.
Implemented a standardized KPI and reporting framework across the network.
Launched fabrication performance dashboards that provide clear visibility into profitability, utilization, capacity, and demand.
Built forecasting and scenario-planning tools that support operational decision-making.
Established a regular performance review cadence with facility leaders.
Improved visibility into project profitability and manufacturing economics.
Helped advance the integration and standardization of production operations across Jack Morton.

jobs.title: Chief Financial Officer
jobs.description:
Venor is proud to partner with Commissionaires Nova Scotia in the recruitment of a Chief Financial Officer.

Based in Bedford, Nova Scotia, Commissionaires Nova Scotia (CNS) is the province’s leading not-for-profit security provider, delivering guarding, monitoring, investigative, and specialized security services to more than 200 sites across the province. With roughly 1,300 employees, a large share of them veterans of the Canadian Armed Forces and RCMP, CNS is the largest private-sector employer of veterans in Nova Scotia. As part of the national Commissionaires federation of over 22,000 security professionals across Canada, CNS reinvests more than 90% of its annual revenue directly into employee wages, training, and benefits.

On their behalf, we are seeking a strategic and hands-on Chief Financial Officer to join the executive team. Reporting to the CEO, you will lead the organization’s financial strategy, reporting, planning and analysis, budgeting, forecasting, capital allocation, risk management, regulatory compliance, and governance. As a trusted advisor to the CEO, Executive Team, and Board of Governors, you’ll bring financial insight to strategic decision-making while leading a team of finance, IT, and procurement professionals and ensuring the organization’s long-term financial sustainability.

What You’ll Be Doing

In this role, you’ll lead the organization’s financial strategy and provide executive-level financial advice across all business lines. You’ll develop, implement, and maintain financial policies, internal controls, and governance frameworks, and oversee financial planning, budgeting, forecasting, controllership, treasury management, and audit activities. You’ll also manage the enterprise financial systems and reporting platforms that keep the organization’s financial information timely and accurate, preparing and presenting financial reports to the CEO, Executive Team, Finance and Audit Committee, and Board of Governors, and developing the annual operating and capital budgets, including required submissions to Public Services and Procurement Canada (PSPC).

You’ll provide strategic pricing guidance, including contract billing and labour rates, and ensure compliance with financial, regulatory, tax, and not-for-profit reporting requirements, including CRA obligations. Externally, you’ll manage relationships with financial institutions, auditors, insurers, the national Commissionaires federation, and government partners, and contribute to organizational strategy through financial analysis, business cases, and recommendations that support sustainable growth. Internally, you’ll provide executive oversight of payroll, compensation, benefits, and related financial administration, and lead, mentor, and develop a finance team spanning budgeting, payroll and accounts, IT/cyber, and procurement.

What You’ll Bring

You bring a Bachelor’s degree in Commerce, Business Administration, Finance, Accounting, or a related field (or an equivalent combination of education and executive experience), along with a Chartered Professional Accountant (CPA) designation in good standing. You have 10+ years of progressive senior financial leadership experience, including strategic planning, budgeting, forecasting, reporting, and governance within a complex organization, and a track record of advising executive teams, Boards of Directors or Governors, and senior stakeholders. Your knowledge of financial management, accounting standards, regulatory compliance, risk management, and corporate governance is strong, and you’ve demonstrated the ability to translate strategic priorities into measurable financial plans and business cases. You’ve led and developed high-performing finance teams, and you communicate complex financial information clearly to both financial and non-financial audiences.

The ideal candidate is a thoughtful, collaborative leader with strong business acumen and a genuine commitment to integrity, innovation, and service excellence. You’re as comfortable in the details of financial reporting as you are advising the boardroom, and you bring the judgment to manage competing priorities during budgeting, audit, and Board reporting cycles.

Kraken Customer

From optimizing resources to delivering cost-effective, exceptional customer experiences through advanced Customer Information Systems (CIS), billing, meter data management, CRM, and AI-driven communications, Kraken is powering the next wave of innovation in the energy industry.

Why we do it: future energy will not look like energy as we know it today. We need to not just think about our future, but build for it. Now.

Why it matters: There are singular moments in every industry where a tectonic shift reshapes the entire sector and unlocks previously unheard of possibilities. There are few industries remaining that are ripe for disruption. Those moments need leaders and the energy sector is in that moment. The disruption is happening now.

Our Kraken software and operating model enable our energy clients to lead this shift while enhancing their operational effectiveness. The accelerated adoption of Kraken means we need someone to lead a major North America client implementation to deliver world-changing results. Are you that leader?

The Company

The Kraken platform is effectively the operating system for utilities, at the core of how they run their business.

Kraken is growing rapidly, disrupting the incumbent tech landscape, with over 64 million end-customer accounts contracted across 11 markets globally and managing the optimisation of over 65GW. Kraken has secured licensing deals with large international energy clients to replace their core technology stack and re-image their operations with an unblemished track record of transformation success.

Excellent communication and facilitation skills. You are well respected with a natural gravitas

. The successful executive will be strategic when the situation requires it, but willing to roll up their sleeves, challenge assumptions, solve problems and help the team execute.

Providing strong financial stewardship

Leading and supporting a strong finance team, creating clarity, engagement and momentum through a period of change.
Acting as a trusted financial advisor to senior leadership, bringing insight to organizational performance, longer-term planning and decision-making.
Reviewing existing financial processes, controls and practices and identifying opportunities to modernize, streamline and elevate the sophistication of the function.
Providing leadership across facilities management and procurement, ensuring strong governance, commercial discipline and effective execution.
Strengthening budgeting, forecasting, cash-flow planning, risk management and performance reporting.
Working effectively with external advisors, auditors and other key stakeholders.
Supporting senior leadership and the organization's governance bodies with credible, thoughtful financial insight. The underlying position specifically supports Audit and Finance Committee and Board activities.
Looking beyond business-as-usual to identify opportunities to drive change, improve effectiveness and leave the organization stronger at the conclusion of the mandate.

The Ideal Interim Executive

We are looking for a seasoned financial executive who knows how to enter an established organization, quickly understand the environment and add value without unnecessary disruption
.

Ideally, this individual will bring a combination of not-for-profit and commercial experience
, pairing an understanding of stewardship, governance and stakeholder accountability with the commercial instincts and operational discipline of the private sector.

The ideal candidate will bring:

Significant senior financial leadership experience within a complex organization.
A professional accounting designation, with strong technical grounding across accounting, financial reporting, budgeting, forecasting and internal controls. The underlying profile calls for a CPA/CA-preferred designation and experience with IFRS, ASPE and ASNPO.
Experience leading strong teams through periods of transition, change or transformation
.
A genuinely hands-on style. Someone prepared to get into the numbers and issues rather than lead exclusively from 30,000 feet.
The ability to move comfortably between strategy and execution
.
Exposure to facilities, procurement and broader corporate services would be highly valuable.
Strong executive presence and the ability to establish credibility quickly with senior executives, employees, external advisors and governance stakeholders.
A pragmatic, collaborative leadership style with the confidence to respectfully challenge the status quo.
Experience operating across both mission-driven/not-for-profit and commercially oriented environments
would be particularly attractive.

Why This Assignment?

For the right interim executive, this offers the opportunity to do what great interims do best: step into an important organization at an important moment and make a measurable difference.

You will be joining a high-performing team rather than rebuilding a broken function. The opportunity is to provide leadership through transition, bring an objective external lens, elevate financial and operational practices, and create sustainable improvements that remain long after the assignment has concluded.

This is an assignment for someone who enjoys being more than a caretaker. It requires an executive who can protect what is working, challenge what can be better, and create momentum for what comes next.

This includes overseeing strategic financial planning, accounting, revenue collection, and cash management, ensuring alignment with the Town’s adopted plans, policies, bylaws, regulations, and standards. In addition to fostering interdepartmental collaboration and ensuring compliance with all financial obligations as outlined in the Municipal Government Act (MGA), the Director supervises a team of four (4): a Financial Analyst, Accounts Payable and Receivable Clerk, Utilities and Tax Clerk, and Support Services Clerk.

THE ORGANIZATION

The Town of High Level is a vibrant northern community of approximately 4,000 residents, serving as the regional service and trading centre for a surrounding population of more than 30,000 people. Located in the northwest corner of Alberta, High Level is strategically positioned at the intersection of Highways 35 and 58, providing critical access to northern industries and communities.

High Level is recognized as a hub for healthcare, education, retail, construction, transportation, and resource development, offering a unique blend of professional challenge and community connection. Known for its breathtaking Northern Lights, endless summer days and access to pristine lakes, rivers and outdoor adventures, the Town is a gateway to exceptional northern living. Residents also enjoy a strong sense of community and rich Indigenous culture, with local festivals, rodeos, and family-oriented activities year-round.

Vision

High Level, an inclusive and vibrant community, with a strong and resilient economy that offers an active and healthy lifestyle.

Mission

We foster a thriving community that enhances our quality of life through sustainable planning, economic prosperity, and inclusion.

For more information, please visit their website: www.highlevel.ca

RESPONSIBILITIES

Plans, directs and coordinates the functions and workload within the Department and ensures that schedules, procedures and performance standards are developed and met.
Utilizes significant judgement, initiative and conceptual thinking in the planning, development and implementation of programs and policies affecting matters related to the scope of duties of this position.
Plans, directs and coordinates the preparation of annual and long-term operational and capital budgets. Provides direct oversight, control and implementation of approved budgets.
Responsible for the preparation of statements and reports on municipal financial affairs for CAO, Directors, Council and the public; includes financial reports on the status and variance of all operating and capital budgets.
Responsible for compiling and supplying information relating to the financial affairs of the municipality as required by Municipal Affairs.
Prepares all financial bylaws, resolutions and subsequent amendments relating to the revenues, expenditures, tax levies and other fiscal and operating matters within the scope of duties of this position. This includes, but is not limited to, bylaws related to the Financial Plan, fees & charges, user rates, tax rates, loan authorization and others.
Administers the provision and management of property insurance policies, claims and related activities.
Oversees the delivery of the Town’s support services, including audit, accounting, taxation, treasury functions, and the management of financial software systems.
Prepares year-end financial working papers, internal statements and municipal reporting forms for audit review and liaises with the Town auditors in connection with the financial audit.
Supports procurement and contract management processes to ensure fiscal responsibility.
Oversees the development and maintenance of the Town’s asset management plan, including strategies, policies and procedures.
Oversees the development of policies for Financial Services. Provides input to policies of other departments.
Provides advice to Town staff, including explanation and interpretation of bylaws, procedures and legislative requirements affecting the Financial Administration department related to the scope of duties of this position.
Responsible for the supervision and mentoring of finance staff including hiring, training, dismissal, appraisals and evaluations of Financial Services employees within approved personnel policies.
Directs, coordinates, and supervises subordinate staff activities and contract staff. Monitors their work performance and delegates work appropriately.
Prepares, or directs the preparation, of reports and makes recommendations to the Chief Administrative Officer on financial matters related to the scope of duties of the position.
Attends all Council meetings, Committee meetings, public hearings and public meetings as required and as directed by the Chief Administrative Officer.
Prepares reports and statistical summaries as necessary for review by the Chief Administrative Officer, Council or other bodies.
As a member of the Senior Management Team, supports and assists other senior managers and is respectful of colleagues' roles, responsibilities and perspectives.
May be required to assist the Town in providing emergency services. Duties assigned during an emergency may differ from regular duties.
Follows and ensures compliance with all policies, procedures, regulations and standards of the Town of High Level.

QUALIFICATIONS

Degree from a recognized post-secondary institution in Accounting, Finance, Business or Public Administration.
Chartered Professional Accountant (CPA) designation.
Minimum of five (5) years of increasingly responsible, relevant experience in public sector finance (including supervisory experience), preferably in a local government setting, or an equivalent combination of education and experience.
Thorough and demonstrated knowledge of the principles and practices of public sector accounting standards (PSAS), internal control procedures, computerized financial applications, finance and fiscal planning, and budgetary, accounting and reporting systems.
Thorough and demonstrated knowledge of municipal legislation including the Municipal Government Act and other related regulations, policies and procedures.

KEY COMPETENCIES

Demonstrated knowledge of GAAP, Public Sector Accounting and Budget processes.
Demonstrated leadership skills.
Exceptional interpersonal, communication, presentation, public relations, problem-solving, investigative, decision-making, leadership and general management skills.
Effective written and verbal communication skills including the ability to prepare comprehensive, concise and clear reports and deliver oral presentations.
Ability to multi-task with strong attention to detail.
Results-oriented in a multi-faceted, fast-paced environment with changing priorities.
Knowledge of and demonstrated fiscal responsibility in support of budget preparation and control.
Ability to work effectively, independently and cooperatively in a team atmosphere.
Ability to exercise courtesy, tact, and diplomacy in the exchange of non-routine information with other employees, employees of private companies and members of the general public.
Exceptionally well organized and able to work effectively with minimal guidelines and supervision.
Ability to exercise sound judgement regarding confidential and sensitive information.
Proficiency in the use of Microsoft Office applications and extensive knowledge in computer systems relevant to municipal operations. Experience with Questica Budget and Diamond ERP Accounting Software is desired.

jobs.description:
We shape, build, and connect the North.

Position: Chief Financial Officer

Status: Permanent, full time
Salary Range: From $250,000 + incentive pay
Location:
Whitehorse, Yukon or remote with monthly onsite presence

The opportunity

Northern Vision Development is growing. For more than two decades, NVD has built and operated hotels, restaurants, commercial and residential real estate, seniors living, and development assets across Yukon and British Columbia.

As Chief Financial Officer, you will shape how NVD grows, allocates capital, manages risk, and creates long-term value for its unitholders and communities. The decisions ahead about where to invest, how to finance it and how much risk to carry will shape the company for decades to come. This is an opportunity to bring Drive to an ambitious growth agenda, Rigour to complex financial decisions, and Kindness to the relationships and leadership required to move the organization forward.

What does your success look like?

The CEO and Board rely on your advice for major investment, development and financing decisions, and those decisions rest on tested assumptions and clear expectations for return and risk.
NVD can see ahead on liquidity, capital capacity, and covenant headroom, and grow without putting its financial resilience or lender relationships at risk.
The Board, Audit Committee, unitholders, and lenders trust NVD’s financial reporting because it is timely, dependable, and useful for decisions.
Operating leaders use forecasts and performance information to make decisions and are accountable for their results.
NVD has a clear, well-reasoned decision on the direction of its financial systems.
Partnership and ownership structures with First Nation partners are financially sound and clearly understood by all parties.
The finance function has leadership, structure, and capability the business needs, and its people grow under your leadership.

What you bring to the role

CFO-level leadership of a full finance function in a multi-entity, asset-intensive organization, including consolidated reporting.
Leadership of capital planning and forecasting, with direct personal accountability for a syndicated or multi-lender credit facility, including covenant management and lender reporting.
Experience advising a CEO, Board and Audit Committee on major decisions, and reporting to investors, unitholders, and owners.
Oversight of corporate and partnership tax planning with external advisors, including the tax implications of transactions and financing.
A hands-on approach - you are comfortable doing the work yourself in a lean team as well as leading it.

Assets:
Experience in real estate development, hospitality, and/or multi-property operations.
Experiencing leading the improvement or implementation of finance and accounting systems.
Experience reporting under ASPE (the private-company accounting standards).

Why build your career with us?

This is an opportunity to influence the future of a growing, majority First Nations-owned company with meaningful assets, strong community partnerships, and ambitious plans for the North. We offer:

4-weeks’ vacation pay, increasing at defined service milestones
1-week managers’ leave
Health coverage including extended health, dental, vision, life, and short-term disability
4% RRSP matching to support your long-term financial security
Professional development
Paid professional fees
Short term and long-term incentive pay programs
Preferred staff and friends and family rates across our hotel portfolio
Employee assistance and wellness program for you and your dependents
Relocation assistance

Job requirements:
CPA or CFA designation in good standing

About NVD

NVD is a majority First Nations-owned company based in the Yukon with a growing regional footprint. For more than two decades, we have built and operated hotels, restaurants, residential and commercial properties, seniors living communities, and mixed-use developments across the North. We are operators and entrepreneurs at heart, locally present and performance focused. We build strong businesses and lasting partnerships that strengthen our communities.

We are committed to building a diverse workforce that reflects the communities we serve. Joining NVD means becoming part of a team that takes ownership, works collaboratively, and helps shape how northern communities live, work, and gather.

jobs.description:
Are you ready to embark on a career that truly affects people around the world? Trulioo invites you to be a catalyst for change in the dynamic realm of digital identity verification. As the global front-runner in our industry, we are redefining how businesses grow, innovate and comply online.

Picture yourself at the forefront of innovation, contributing to our award-winning platform that enables organizations worldwide to quickly onboard customers, optimize costs and combat fraud. Fueled by Silicon Valley support, Trulioo stands as the trusted platform that can verify more than 5 billion people and 700 million business entities spanning 195 countries.

But Trulioo is more than a tech company. We are a united force of dedicated experts committed to establishing trust online - and we’re proud to be recognized as a BC Top Employer for the second consecutive year
, reflecting our commitment to an inclusive, collaborative, and people-first workplace.

Headquartered in Vancouver and with strategic hubs in San Diego and Dublin, we foster a culture of collaboration and open communication. Our offices support a hybrid model and staff typically work three days per week at a hub location. Join us where excitement meets innovation and contribute to a world where trust and technology unite.

What We Offer

Comprehensive Benefits: We provide a robust benefits package for full-time, permanent employees, including health, dental, and vision coverage, retirement plans with company match, paid time off, parental leave, and an annual education & training stipend (equivalent to $1,000 in local currency). Specific benefits may vary by location and will be discussed further during the interview process.
Flexible Hybrid Working Environment: Our offices are designed to support both collaboration and flexibility. Enjoy weekly lunches, quality coffee, and regular social events. Many locations also feature parent rooms, on-site gyms, comfortable lounges, and adaptable workstations to support your comfort and productivity.
Wellness: We care about your well-being. Team members have access to wellness workshops and events, as well as a complimentary Headspace subscription to help you stay focused, grounded, and energized.
Employee Resource Groups: Belonging is an important part of doing your best work. Our ERGs provide an inclusive space, support and community for employees of diverse backgrounds and allies. We host informative, fun sessions and celebrations that are often open to the entire organization.

Position Summary

Trulioo is seeking a commercially minded and execution-oriented Senior Director, Global Privacy & Data Protection to lead our global privacy strategy, data protection program, and designated Data Protection Officer.

Reporting to the Chief Risk and Strategy Officer, this role will actively lead how privacy, data protection, AI governance, and responsible data use are embedded across Trulioo’s products, operations, commercial motions, and governed by leading practices. This is a senior leadership role for a privacy executive who can operate in scaling, agile environments and partnering with Product, Engineering, Legal, Security, Enterprise Risk, Sales, Marketing, and Customer Success.

The ideal candidate brings extensive expertise in GDPR, U.S. state privacy laws, and Canadian privacy laws, with experience in emerging areas including, but not limited to, biometrics, AI, age verification, data retention, data classification, and emerging identity technologies.

This role is expected to leverage AI and emerging technologies to improve productivity, enhance decision-making, and continuously optimize how work is performed.

This will be a full-time, permanent position working on a hybrid model from one of our North American offices or fully remote.

What You’ll Be Doing

Global Privacy Strategy & DPO

Build and lead Trulioo’s global privacy and data protection strategy across priority markets, products, customers, and operating environments.
Serve as Trulioo’s designated Data Protection Officer for Europe, providing independent, credible, and commercially practical advice on GDPR and related obligations.
Advise executive leadership, as needed, on privacy risk, regulatory change, customer expectations, and strategic trade-offs tied to product innovation and market expansion.
Represent Trulioo in privacy-related engagements with regulators, enterprise customers, industry groups, and other external stakeholders.
Act as a strategic advisor on privacy and data protection implications as Trulioo expands into new operating regions, verticals, and expands the product catalog.
Monitor global privacy developments and translate implications into practical guidance for products, operations, market expansion, and customer commitments.

Privacy Program Operations & Governance

Mature Trulioo’s privacy program, including PIAs, DPIAs, records of processing, data subject rights, vendor privacy reviews, and cross-border transfer mechanisms. Integrate privacy by design into product development, commercial contracting, customer onboarding, third-party management, enterprise risk management, and agile operating rhythms.
Own and evolve key privacy and data governance policies, including data retention, data classification, information classification and protection, data handling, and responsible data use.
Lead privacy incident readiness and response, including investigation support, breach assessment, regulatory notification analysis, remediation, and post-incident improvement.
Develop practical reporting, metrics, and executive-level insights that create visibility into privacy risks, regulatory readiness, and program maturity.

Commercial Enablement, Product, & Engineering Advisor

Partner with Product and Engineering to embed privacy by design into agile product development, architecture decisions, data flows, and release processes.
Provide guidance on privacy risks tied to identity verification, fraud prevention, biometrics, document verification, data enrichment, AI, machine learning, and emerging identity technologies.
Serve as a senior privacy advisor to Sales, Customer Success, Marketing, Solutions, and Legal in support of enterprise due diligence, RFPs, audits, and strategic customer engagements.
Help shape responsible AI governance, including privacy impact analysis, consumer data use, automated processing, transparency, and controls for responsible product deployment.
Lead or support negotiation of DPAs, SCCs, data transfer terms, privacy schedules, customer commitments, vendor terms, and partner arrangements.
Support commercialization by validating privacy positioning, customer-facing claims, contractual commitments, and market- specific privacy requirements.
Build privacy thought leadership that strengthens Trulioo’s credibility with customers, regulators, partners, and industry stakeholders.

Team Leadership & Cross-Functional Influence

Lead, coach, and develop a high-performing privacy team with strong judgment, business orientation, and operational discipline.
Create clear decision-making frameworks that allow teams to move quickly while managing privacy and data protection risk effectively.
Foster a culture of responsible innovation, practical risk management, and accountable data use across the organization.

What You’ll Bring

15+ years of experience in privacy, data protection, technology law, regulatory advisory, or related legal and risk leadership roles, including significant in-house experience.
Extensive expertise in GDPR, European data protection expectations, U.S. state privacy laws, and Canadian privacy laws.
Demonstrated ability to serve as a senior privacy leader or Data Protection Officer in a complex, global technology environment.
Experience advising Product, Engineering, Security, Legal, and go-to-market teams on privacy by design, data protection risk, product launches, and customer-facing commitments.
Practical experience with PIAs, DPIAs, data mapping, transfer mechanisms, DPAs, SCCs, vendor risk, data subject rights, retention, and privacy incident response.
Strong understanding of privacy issues tied to emerging identity technology and use cases including biometrics, identity, AI, behavior analysis, automated processing, fraud prevention, and device intelligence.
Track record building or maturing privacy program operations in agile, high-growth, regulated, or enterprise SaaS environments.
Executive presence, sound judgment, and the ability to translate regulatory complexity into clear business decisions.
Strong people leadership skills, with the ability to build capability, set direction, and raise the operating maturity of a privacy function.
Law degree or equivalent legal/privacy qualification; membership in good standing with a relevant law society or bar is strongly preferred.

Nice To Have

Experience in RegTech, FinTech, identity verification, fraud prevention, payments, financial services, or enterprise SaaS.
Working knowledge of privacy and data protection frameworks in Asia-Pacific, India, China, and Latin America.
Experience supporting AI governance, responsible AI programs, model governance, or data ethics frameworks.
Familiarity with information security, data governance, cybersecurity, enterprise risk, or public-company readiness programs.
Privacy certifications such as CIPP/E, CIPP/US, CIPP/C, CIPM, CIPT, or equivalent credentials.
Experience speaking externally, publishing privacy insights, or representing a company in industry forums.

Interview Process

At Trulioo, we strive to create an interview experience that is transparent, engaging, and respectful of your time. Our process is designed to help us learn more about your skills and experience while giving you insight into our team, culture, and the impact of the work we do.

Here's What You Can Expect Throughout The Interview Process

Recruiter Interview: 30 minutes
Hiring Manager Interview: 45 minutes
Panel Interview: 60 minutes
Chief People Officer Interview: 45 minutes
Final Executive Interview: 30 minutes

Thriving at Trulioo

At Trulioo, you’re not just an employee. You’re a valued member of our Trulicrew on a journey of professional and personal growth with a world-class organization. With Trulioo, you have the power to revolutionize the intersection of technology, digital trust and online identity to open the global economy to everyone. Together, we can shape the digital future.

We’re on the lookout for exceptional people to empower with trust, autonomy and the freedom to cultivate their potential. Your curiosity, meticulous attention to detail and passion to contribute are highly valued. If that resonates with you, apply today to become a part of our team. Join us in shaping a future where your career isn’t just a journey but also a boundless exploration into the possibilities of technology and digital identity verification.

Get an inside look at life at Trulioo by following us on LinkedIn, or learn more about us at www.trulioo.com

jobs.title: Senior Vice President – Water, Automation & Manufacturing
jobs.description:
Aplin has partnered with Delco Water Group, an established Canadian provider of integrated water and wastewater treatment solutions, to recruit a Senior Vice President
. This executive will provide strategic, operational and commercial leadership across the organization’s Water, Automation and Manufacturing businesses.

Reporting to the Executive Vice President, Operations, the Senior Vice President will serve as the senior business-unit leader, with full P&L accountability for revenue, profitability, cash flow and overall business performance.

This is an exceptional succession opportunity for an accomplished water-industry executive to lead an established, mid-sized business, strengthen operational performance and accountability, develop the management team, and position the organization for continued growth and long-term success.

The Opportunity

The Senior Vice President will provide end-to-end leadership across business development, engineering, project delivery, manufacturing, supply chain, quality and customer service. Working within the strategic direction established by executive leadership, this individual will translate organizational priorities into executable business plans, budgets and performance objectives.

A central part of the mandate will be establishing clear accountability throughout the business. The successful candidate will mentor and develop internal talent, clarify responsibilities and decision-making authority, address operational inefficiencies, and ensure the management team is aligned around common business objectives.

The successful candidate must bring sufficient water or wastewater industry knowledge to understand the market and become effective quickly. This requires an experienced business leader who can take ownership of the complete operation while remaining personally involved when circumstances require.

Key Responsibilities

Facilitate the development and execution of business strategy, annual operating plans and budgets.
Assume full P&L accountability for revenue, profitability, cash flow and overall business performance.
Translate executive direction into clear commercial, operational and financial priorities.
Strengthen operational alignment and identify efficiencies across the Water, Automation and Manufacturing businesses.
Lead commercial and operational performance across business development, engineering, project management, manufacturing, supply chain, quality and customer service.
Strengthen relationships with customers, engineering consultants, Indigenous partners, technology providers, government representatives and industry stakeholders.
Identify opportunities for organic growth, national expansion, recurring revenue, strategic partnerships and acquisitions.
Ensure engineered-to-order projects are delivered safely, on schedule, within budget and to customer expectations.
Improve financial and operational discipline through effective forecasting, performance measurement, risk management and continuous improvement.
Establish clear responsibilities, decision-making authority and accountability throughout the organization.
Build, mentor and develop a high-performing management team.
Introduce appropriate systems, processes and controls while maintaining the organization’s entrepreneurial and responsive culture.
Represent the business with key customers, consultants, partners, industry organizations and community stakeholders.
Report to the board on business performance, operational results and strategic priorities.

Candidate Profile

The ideal candidate will be an accomplished executive with direct experience in the water or wastewater industry. Relevant experience may include water or wastewater treatment, engineered systems, project delivery, equipment manufacturing, product distribution or related industrial solutions.

Most importantly, the successful candidate will bring both water-industry credibility and experience leading a complete business with end-to-end responsibility.

The successful candidate will bring:

Senior executive or business-unit leadership experience within the water or wastewater industry.
End-to-end leadership responsibility across the commercial, operational and financial functions of a business.
Full P&L accountability for a complex division, business unit or organization generating at least $30 million in annual revenue.
Experience leading a project-based, engineered-to-order, manufacturing or industrial solutions business.
Sufficient technical knowledge of water-treatment processes and engineered systems to evaluate recommendations, challenge assumptions and support technical leaders.
Experience leading across sales, engineering, project delivery, automation, manufacturing and customer service.
A record of growing revenue, improving profitability and strengthening operational performance.
Commercial leadership experience within a long-cycle, relationship-driven sales environment.
Established credibility with major customers, engineering consultants and strategic partners.
Strong financial-management, budgeting, forecasting and business-planning capabilities.
Experience establishing accountability and addressing complex organizational and performance issues.
Experience building, mentoring and developing high-performing management teams.
The independence, maturity and executive presence required to lead the complete business.

Delco Water Group is open to candidates whose experience is weighted more heavily toward commercial growth or operational leadership, provided they possess full-business leadership capability and can build complementary strengths within the management team.

A relevant post-secondary degree in engineering, business, operations or a related discipline is preferred. An MBA or comparable advanced qualification would be an asset. Demonstrated leadership accomplishments and business results will be given significant consideration.

Leadership Style

The successful candidate will be a self-directed and accountable leader who is comfortable operating in an entrepreneurial, mid-sized organization. This individual must be prepared to become personally involved when required, influence across functional boundaries and balance increased structure with organizational agility.

This is a hands-on leadership opportunity. Candidates accustomed to relying on extensive large-company infrastructure or narrowly defined responsibilities may find the environment challenging. The successful executive will be comfortable wearing multiple hats, making difficult decisions and taking ownership of issues across the complete business.

Location

The Senior Vice President will be based in Saskatoon, where Delco Water Group’s primary operations and approximately 175 employees are located. A consistent on-site leadership presence is required.

Qualified candidates from across Canada will be considered, and relocation assistance is available. Reasonable transitional arrangements may be considered to support relocation. Travel will be required to develop customer and consultant relationships and support partnerships and growth initiatives.

All inquiries and applications will be treated with the highest degree of confidentiality.

To be considered, applicants must be legally entitled to work in Canada, including holding any required permits. jobs.description:
La version française suit

Company Description

Headquartered in Montreal, Detroit and Munich, Vention helps manufacturers automate their operations in record time with the only hardware and software AI-powered platform built for the factory floor. Our technology powers over 25,000 machines across 4,000 factories across 5 continents and we have the privilege to work with a significant proportion of Fortune 500 manufacturers, from space rockets, to electrical cars, to robotics.

At Vention, you’ll work alongside driven and talented people who care deeply about their craft and the impact they create. We’re a team of high achievers who grow through meaningful work, solving complex challenges, learning fast, and seeing the results of our efforts every day.

We move quickly and aim high, but we do it together with care, collaboration, and respect. Our culture celebrates diverse perspectives and supports your growth through intentional development, strong leadership, and opportunities to make a real difference.

What You’ll Do

This is not a traditional SaaS product leadership role.

Vention's software platform sits at the intersection of industrial automation, robotics, developer tools, cloud software, embedded systems and Physical AI. Our products are tightly interconnected, with decisions in one part of the stack often creating significant implications elsewhere.

The VP Product will lead a team of Product Managers and UI/UX Designers across a broad portfolio including:

MachineBuilder — 3D machine design and configuration
MachineLogic — Robot programming and automation development
Simulation — machine and robot simulation
Robot Control — real-time control and orchestration
Physical AI — AI-powered automation capabilities
Web & eCommerce — digital purchasing and configuration experience
RemoteSupport & RemoteView — remote machine support and operation
MachineAnalytics — machine data, monitoring and intelligence

The mandate is simple: make Vention's software dramatically better while dramatically increasing the velocity at which we ship it.

You will bring product rigor and leadership to an organization where the CEO and CTO remain deeply involved in product direction. Your role is therefore not to simply "own the roadmap." It is to become the operating engine that translates strategic direction into an exceptional product vision, clear priorities and fast execution.

Set the Product Vision & Experience
Define the long-term product vision across Vention's entire software platform.
Establish a coherent product strategy spanning design, programming, simulation, robotics, AI, eCommerce and machine operations.
Raise the bar for simplicity, usability and design quality across the platform, with an Apple-like obsession for product excellence.
Establish product principles and UX standards that make a highly sophisticated technology stack feel simple and intuitive.
Translate company-level strategic direction into a clear, differentiated product vision and roadmap.
Drive Product Velocity & Execution
Dramatically accelerate the pace at which Vention turns ideas into shipped products.
Establish a high-performance product operating cadence focused on fast decisions, clear accountability and measurable outcomes.
Ruthlessly prioritize initiatives based on customer impact, strategic value and business outcomes.
Remove organizational and process bottlenecks that slow product development.
Build a culture where Product, Engineering and Design are accountable for shipping—not simply planning.
Orchestrate the Platform Roadmap
Own prioritization across a highly integrated portfolio of software, firmware, robotics and Physical AI products.
Manage dependencies and sequencing across MachineBuilder, MachineLogic, simulation, robot control, firmware, analytics, RemoteView, RemoteSupport and eCommerce.
Balance customer-facing features, foundational technology investments, technical debt and emerging opportunities.
Resolve competing priorities across product teams and make difficult trade-offs quickly.
Ensure individual product roadmaps collectively move the Vention platform forward as one integrated system.
Lead Product, Design & Technical Product Management
Lead, develop and scale a high-performing organization of Product Managers and UI/UX Designers.
Raise the technical depth, product judgment and execution standards of the product organization.
Partner closely with Engineering to make sound architectural and product trade-offs.

Develop product leaders who can operate independently while maintaining alignment with Vention's overall product strategy.

What You Bring To The Table

Exceptional product leader with 12+ years of experience in product, software or technology leadership, including significant experience managing multiple product teams.
Deep technical credibility with the ability to understand software architecture, APIs, distributed systems, embedded systems and technical trade-offs—and to go into the code when necessary.
Broad platform experience managing complex, highly integrated products where decisions and dependencies span multiple teams and technology layers.
Outstanding product taste with an instinct for simplicity, elegance, consistency and intuitive user experiences; a genuine obsession with design quality and product perfection.
Proven execution track record with a bias toward action, demonstrated ability to accelerate roadmaps, make decisions quickly and consistently turn strategy into shipped products.
Exceptional prioritization skills with the ability to make difficult trade-offs across competing customer needs, technical investments, product opportunities and business priorities.
Strong systems thinker who can understand how individual products, technologies and teams fit together into a coherent platform and architecture.
Customer- and business-oriented with the ability to balance customer value, strategic differentiation, revenue impact and long-term platform investments.

Description De L’entreprise

Basée à Montréal, Detroit et Munich, Vention aide les fabricants à automatiser leurs opérations en un temps record grâce à la seule plateforme matérielle et logicielle alimentée par l’IA conçue pour l’usine. Notre technologie alimente plus de 25 000 machines dans 4 000 usines réparties sur 5 continents, et nous avons le privilège de collaborer avec une grande proportion des fabricants du Fortune 500, allant de la construction de fusées à l’automobile électrique, en passant par la robotique.

Chez Vention, vous travaillerez aux côtés de personnes passionnées et talentueuses qui ont à cœur leur métier et l’impact qu’elles créent. Nous formons une équipe de personnes ambitieuses qui évoluent grâce à un travail porteur de sens, en relevant des défis complexes, en apprenant rapidement et en constatant chaque jour les résultats de leurs efforts.

Nous avançons vite et visons haut, mais nous le faisons ensemble, avec soin, collaboration et respect. Notre culture valorise la diversité des perspectives et soutient votre développement grâce à un encadrement intentionnel, un leadership fort et des occasions concrètes de faire une réelle différence.

Ce Que Vous Ferez

Il ne s'agit pas d'un rôle de leadership de produit SaaS traditionnel.

La plateforme logicielle de Vention se situe à l'intersection de l'automatisation industrielle, de la robotique, des outils pour développeurs, des logiciels infonuagiques, des systèmes embarqués et de l'IA physique (Physical AI). Nos produits sont étroitement interconnectés, et les décisions prises dans une partie de l'architecture technologique (stack) ont souvent des implications importantes ailleurs.

Le Ou La VP Produit Dirigera Une Équipe De Gestionnaires De Produits Et De Designers UI/UX à Travers Un Vaste Portefeuille Comprenant

MachineBuilder — Conception de machines en 3D et configuration

Simulation — Simulation de machines et de robots

Physical AI (IA Physique) — Capacités d'automatisation propulsées par l'IA
Web & eCommerce (Commerce électronique) — Expérience numérique d'achat et de configuration
RemoteSupport & RemoteView — Soutien et exploitation de machines à distance
MachineAnalytics — Données de machines, surveillance et intelligence

Le mandat est simple : rendre les logiciels de Vention considérablement meilleurs, tout en augmentant de façon draconienne la vitesse à laquelle nous les livrons (ship).

Vous apporterez de la rigueur et du leadership en matière de produit au sein d'une organisation où le PDG (CEO) et le Chef de la technologie (CTO) restent profondément impliqués dans l'orientation du produit. Votre rôle ne consistera donc pas simplement à « posséder la feuille de route » (roadmap). Il s'agira de devenir le moteur opérationnel qui traduit l'orientation stratégique en une vision de produit exceptionnelle, avec des priorités claires et une exécution rapide.

Établir une stratégie de produit cohérente couvrant la conception, la programmation, la simulation, la robotique, l'IA, le commerce électronique et les opérations des machines.
Rehausser la barre en matière de simplicité, de convivialité et de qualité de conception sur l'ensemble de la plateforme, avec une obsession de l'excellence produit digne d'Apple.
Établir des principes de produit et des normes d'expérience utilisateur (UX) qui rendent une architecture technologique haut

jobs.title: Senior Director, AI Transformation
jobs.description:
About Powerfleet

Powerfleet (Nasdaq: AIOT; JSE: PWR) is a global leader in the artificial intelligence of things (AIoT) software-as-a-service (SaaS) mobile asset industry. With more than 30 years of experience, Powerfleet unifies business operations through the ingestion, harmonization, and integration of data—regardless of source—and delivers actionable insights to help companies meet their strategic objectives around Safety, Compliance, Efficiency and Sustainability. Our people-first culture and relentless innovation empower customers to achieve measurable, sustainable business improvements. Powerfleet serves over 2.6 million subscribers across more than 48,000 customers in 120 countries, with commercial operations across every major continent.

About The Role

Powerfleet is seeking a Senior Director, AI Transformation to help drive the adoption and business impact of AI across the enterprise. This role will work across functions including Sales, Marketing, Finance, HR, Product, Operations, Customer Success, and Technology to identify, prioritize, and advance high-value AI opportunities.

The Senior Director will serve as a key partner to the AI Transformation leadership, helping establish and execute the enterprise AI transformation roadmap, AI governance, and AI Center of Excellence (CoE). The role will connect business priorities with emerging AI capabilities, helping teams move from ideas and use cases to practical adoption and measurable outcomes.

This is a highly cross-functional, individual contributor role requiring strong business judgment, program leadership, communication, and the ability to influence stakeholders across the organization.

Key Responsibilities

Enterprise AI Transformation

Partner with business and functional leaders to identify, evaluate, and prioritize AI opportunities across Sales, Marketing, Finance, HR, Product, Operations, Customer Success, and Technology based on business value, feasibility, readiness, risk, and potential impact.
Build and maintain an enterprise portfolio of AI use cases and support the prioritization, sequencing, and execution of initiatives as part of Powerfleet’s broader AI transformation roadmap.
Help business teams move AI initiatives from ideas and experimentation toward adoption, scale, and measurable business outcomes, including opportunities leveraging AI, GenAI, agents, and intelligent automation.

AI Center of Excellence & Governance

Partner with AI Transformation leadership to establish and evolve Powerfleet’s AI Center of Excellence, including practical frameworks, playbooks, best practices, and knowledge-sharing mechanisms that accelerate responsible AI adoption.
Help develop and operationalize AI governance frameworks, standards, and processes, working with Technology, Security, Legal, Privacy, Risk, and business stakeholders to support responsible and scalable AI adoption.

AI Portfolio & Program Leadership

Lead coordination of major cross-functional AI transformation initiatives, establishing clear objectives, milestones, owners, dependencies, and outcomes while helping teams maintain execution momentum.
Establish metrics to track AI adoption, productivity, business impact, and value realization, and support executive reviews of AI initiatives, progress, risks, opportunities, and outcomes.
Help evaluate build-versus-buy opportunities and identify technologies, platforms, and strategic partners that can accelerate AI adoption.

Executive & Stakeholder Engagement

Prepare and present AI transformation strategies, roadmaps, use cases, recommendations, progress, and business outcomes to executive leadership and translate complex AI concepts and emerging technologies into practical business opportunities and facilitate decision-making across business, product, technology, and executive stakeholders. Act as a trusted advisor to leaders across the organization on AI opportunities, adoption, transformation, and value realization.

AI Adoption & Change

Help establish an enterprise culture of responsible AI adoption and experimentation through communication, education, and enablement. Identify and scale successful AI use cases, patterns, and best practices across functions and geographies.

Qualifications

10+ years of experience in technology, digital transformation, strategy, consulting, product, operations, or related disciplines, with meaningful experience working with AI or emerging technologies.
Strong understanding of AI, GenAI, automation, and emerging AI capabilities and their practical business applications.
Experience identifying, evaluating, prioritizing, and executing technology or AI use cases based on business value and feasibility.
Experience developing executive-level presentations, recommendations, roadmaps, and business cases.
Familiarity with AI governance, responsible AI, data privacy, security, and enterprise technology considerations.
Bachelor’s degree in business, Computer Science, Engineering, Data Science, or a related field; advanced degree preferred.

The base salary range for this full-time position is [CAD $185,000-215,000]
, with eligibility for additional variable compensation. Final compensation will be determined based on experience, skills, and location.

Our VP, FP&A is a strategic partner and a critical enterprise leader who shapes how the business plans, allocates capital, measures performance, and makes decisions. This role combines deep financial expertise with strong executive presence, business acumen, and the ability to influence across a complex, franchise system.

As we shift toward a Product Operating Model, this leader will modernize FP&A into a proactive, insight-driven, technology-enabled function. They will help guide the business through this evolution, bringing structure, clarity, challenge, and strategic framing to elevate financial maturity across the organization.

The VP, FP&A must be both a relationship-builder and a systems thinker — equally comfortable diving into models, simplifying complexity, coaching a tactical FP&A team, and advising senior leaders with confidence and credibility.

A DAY IN THE LIFE

CFO Partnership & Executive Influence

Serve as trusted advisor to the CFO, providing structure, insight, guidance, and challenge on key decisions.
Strengthen the CFO’s influence by preparing high-quality narratives, decision frameworks, and financial storytelling for the Executive.
Bring clarity to ambiguity — shaping options, risks, and trade-offs in a way that enables confident decision-making.
Uplift FP&A capability and bring discipline to planning, forecasting, scenario thinking, and enterprise prioritization.

Modernize FP&A for a Product Operating Model

Translate traditional FP&A into a future-state model aligned with product planning, value streams, capacity-based resourcing, and multi-quarter bets.
Align financial rhythms with product cycles, investment governance, and product portfolio management.
Build FP&A frameworks that support experimentation, iterative planning, and benefit realization.

Enterprise Planning & Forecasting Leadership

Lead the company’s planning cycles: annual plan, rolling forecast, and long-term model.
Ensure assumptions, targets, and resource allocations align with strategy and enterprise priorities.
Elevate forecasting accuracy and enforce strong financial discipline across functions and brands.

Performance Management & Decision Support

Build standardized KPIs, dashboards, and reporting that unify financial and operational performance.
Run monthly and quarterly business reviews with a focus on insight, action, and accountability.
Provide functional and brand leaders with high-quality decision support, scenario analysis, and commercial insight.
Connect franchisor, brand, and franchise partner economics into a clear view of system-wide value creation.

Investment Governance & Capital Allocation

Operate the investment governance framework: ROI, payback, prioritization, and benefit realization.
Support the CFO in modeling and communicating enterprise value, including key drivers and risk factors.
Ensure investment decisions are aligned with strategic priorities and supported by clear financial logic.

FP&A Technology, Systems & Data Modernization

Modernize FP&A processes through improved systems, automation, and real-time insight (Cube, NetSuite, Tableau).
Strengthen data flows to eliminate manual overhead and improve the accuracy and speed of business insights.
Ensure the Finance team remains effective during the transition by supporting Excel- and Sheets-based processes while building toward a more automated future state.

Lead, coach, and elevate a high-performing FP&A team
Build a culture of clarity, curiosity, accountability, and cross-functional partnership.
Increase the commercial, analytical, and business-partnering capability of FP&A professionals.
Model behaviors aligned with the Product Operating Model: transparency, collaboration, system thinking, and customer obsession.

What You Bring To The Table

Proven experience leading FP&A in complex, multi-stakeholder, or high-growth environments, with accountability for forecasting, planning, analysis, and decision support.
Demonstrated success as a strategic partner to a CFO or senior executive, providing backbone support, structured thinking, and trusted challenge.

Executive presence and relationship strength — able to build trust quickly, influence without friction, and communicate with clarity.
Technical and process depth, including financial modeling, scenario planning, and the ability to build, audit, and simplify models in Excel/Sheets.
Experience modernizing FP&A systems and data flows (Cube, Adaptive, Anaplan, Power BI, Tableau).
High EQ, sound judgment, and the ability to navigate ambiguity and competing priorities.
