jobs.description:
Job Title: Finance Director
Job Description

The Finance Director leads core financial reporting, regulatory reporting, and FP&A activities while playing a key role in ongoing finance transformation initiatives. This role oversees month-end close, prepares and reviews financial statements and management reporting, and ensures audit-ready documentation and regulatory compliance. The Finance Director also supports IFRS 17 implementation, systems and process improvements, and provides strategic financial analysis and executive reporting in a collaborative, highly visible finance environment.

Responsibilities

Lead and support monthly, quarterly, and annual financial close processes, ensuring timely and accurate completion.
Prepare and review journal entries, account reconciliations, and supporting schedules for balance sheet and income statement accounts.
Analyze balance sheet and income statement fluctuations to identify trends, risks, and opportunities, and communicate findings to leadership.
Prepare financial statements and comprehensive management reporting packages for senior leadership and key stakeholders.
Maintain audit-ready supporting documentation for all financial reporting activities and ensure strong internal controls.
Support internal and external audit requirements, including preparation of audit materials and responding to audit inquiries.
Oversee and support regulatory reporting activities, including OSFI and other regulatory filings.
Prepare reporting schedules, reconciliations, and supporting documentation for regulatory submissions.
Review regulatory filings to ensure reporting accuracy, completeness, and compliance with applicable regulations.
Support finance transformation initiatives, with a particular focus on IFRS 17-related process enhancements and implementation activities.
Participate in testing, controls validation, data verification, and user acceptance testing for new and enhanced finance processes and systems.
Contribute to finance systems and process improvement initiatives, including ERP, reporting, and finance system implementations and integrations.
Lead or support FP&A activities, including budgeting, forecasting, and financial planning processes.
Develop financial models and analytical reporting to support decision-making and strategic planning.
Perform variance analysis on financial results and provide clear, insightful explanations for executive reporting.
Prepare and deliver executive reporting and presentations that summarize financial performance, forecasts, and key insights.
Provide technical accounting guidance, including gap analysis and interpretation of complex accounting standards such as IFRS 17.
Collaborate closely with accounting, reporting, FP&A, and project teams to drive results and support enterprise-wide initiatives.
Demonstrate leadership within a small, highly visible finance team, contributing across multiple areas of finance as needed.
Adapt to changing priorities and work independently while maintaining strong communication and collaboration across the organization.

Essential Skills

Proven experience in financial reporting, including preparation and review of financial statements and management reporting packages.
Strong background in month-end close processes, journal entries, reconciliations, and supporting schedules.
Expertise in forecasting, budgeting, and financial planning and analysis (FP&A).
Demonstrated ability to perform detailed variance analysis and provide clear, actionable insights.
Experience with regulatory reporting, particularly OSFI reporting requirements.
Hands-on experience with IFRS 17 and related technical accounting and process implications.
Strong technical accounting skills, including closing and reporting and gap analysis.
Experience supporting finance transformation and process improvement initiatives.
Proficiency with ERP and finance systems, including SAP, Oracle, and Sun Accounting.
Leadership experience in a finance function, with the ability to work in a small, highly visible team.
Knowledge of Property & Casualty (P&C) insurance financial and regulatory requirements.
Audit experience, including supporting internal and external audits.
Excellent analytical, reporting, and problem-solving skills.
Strong communication skills, with the ability to present complex financial information clearly to executives and stakeholders.

Additional Skills & Qualifications

CPA designation.
Bachelors degree in Accounting, Finance, Commerce, or a related field.
Experience working within Property & Casualty (P&C) insurance organizations.
Hands-on experience with SAP, Oracle, and Sun Accounting systems.
background in audit, either in public accounting or corporate audit functions.
Experience with integration projects and enterprise-wide system implementations.
Proven ability to support finance transformation initiatives and process improvements.
Comfort operating in a hands-on environment and contributing across accounting, reporting, FP&A, and strategic projects.
Ability to navigate changing priorities and work independently while maintaining strong collaboration.
Track record of partnering with senior finance leadership, including CFO-level stakeholders.

Work Environment

This role operates within a small, collaborative, and highly visible finance team where professionals work closely with the CFO and finance leadership. The culture is hands-on, with a strong emphasis on adaptability, clear communication, and a willingness to roll up your sleeves wherever support is needed. The position follows a hybrid work model, with a company policy of three days per week in the office and a standard 37.5-hour workweek. The office is located in Toronto and provides exposure to major finance transformation initiatives, including IFRS 17 implementation, ERP and reporting system enhancements, and enterprise-wide process improvements. Team members partner across accounting, reporting, FP&A, and project teams, gaining broad experience in financial reporting, accounting, FP&A, and strategic projects within a dynamic, transformation-focused environment.

Job Type & Location

This is a Contract position based out of Toronto, ON.

Pay And Benefits

The pay range for this position is $70.00 - $75.00/hr.

Individual compensation offered for this position within this range will depend on many factors, including qualifications, skills, relevant experience, job knowledge, geographic location, internal equity, and other pertinent job-related factors.

jobs.title: Cloud Architecture & Engineering, Director
jobs.description:
At PwC, our people in infrastructure focus on designing and implementing robust, secure IT systems that support business operations. They enable the smooth functioning of networks, servers, and data centres to optimise performance and minimise downtime. Those in site reliability engineering at PwC will focus on enabling the reliability, scalability, and performance of organisational technology infrastructure. This will include working to automate processes, monitor systems, and resolve incidents to maintain a seamless user experience.**Meaningful work you’ll be part of**

  

As a Director, Cloud Architecture \& Engineering, you’ll work as part of a team of problem solvers, helping to solve business issues, deliver high\-quality client service and operational efficiency. Responsibilities include but are not limited to:

  

* You will play a pivotal leadership role at the intersection of cloud strategy, architecture, engineering, and client engagement.
* This role combines deep technical cloud expertise with strategic leadership, practice development, and team coaching.
* You will shape and scale cloud capabilities, guide clients through complex transformation journeys, and help drive PwC’s cloud first vision.
* You will be responsible for designing and governing enterprise grade cloud architectures while also driving advisory engagements, leading teams, strengthening client relationships, and contributing to the innovation pipeline for cloud\-based solutions and assets.
* This role requires a seasoned cloud leader who can operate fluently across business strategy, modern cloud architectures, and hands\-on technical depth—while mentoring teams and influencing both internal and client executives.

 **Cloud Architecture \& Engineering Leadership**

* Lead the design, governance, and implementation of end\-to\-end cloud architectures aligned to business goals and industry best practices.
* Architect scalable, secure, and cost optimized cloud solutions across AWS, Azure, and GCP.
* Develop cloud foundation blueprints, reference architectures, and reusable patterns.
* Oversee the design and optimization of Kubernetes platforms (EKS, AKS, GKE) and containerized environments.
* Guide the development and automation of cloud infrastructure using Infrastructure\-as\-Code (Terraform, CloudFormation, AWS CDK, ARM, etc.).
* Provide technical guidance on compute, storage, networking, security, identity, data services, and DevOps tooling.

 **Cloud Advisory \& Client Engagement**

* Serve as a trusted advisor to executive\-level stakeholders, helping them define and execute cloud strategies and operating models.
* Assess existing environments, develop modernization roadmaps, and oversee cloud migration programs.
* Lead proposal creation, solutioning activities, statements of work, and client presentations.
* Communicate complex technical concepts to nontechnical audiences clearly and effectively.
* Identify and prioritize client use cases and translate business requirements into architectural approaches and execution plans.

 **Practice \& Team Leadership**

* Build, lead, and mentor teams of cloud architects, engineers, and technical specialists.
* Foster a culture of continuous learning, experimentation, and cloud innovation.
* Recruit and grow diverse technical talent, ensuring strong career development and retention.
* Collaborate with practice leadership to define strategic direction, emerging offerings, and go\-to\-market assets.
* Lead initiatives that strengthen practice foundations: capability models, delivery frameworks, accelerators, patterns, and reusable assets.

 **Innovation, Delivery \& Thought Leadership**

* Lead technical innovation cycles to evaluate, test, and showcase new cloud technologies, tools, and architectures.
* Drive and participate in hands\-on cloud prototyping, labbing, and solution validation.
* Develop technical demos, asset\-driven solutions, and market\-aligned accelerators.
* Present at internal and external events, contributing to PwC’s thought leadership presence.
* Maintain active engagement with cloud provider alliances and product engineering teams to share early insights and influence product evolution.

**Experiences and skills you’ll use to solve**

 **Technical Expertise**

* Extensive experience in cloud architecture and engineering across AWS (primary), Azure, and/or GCP.
* Deep knowledge of Kubernetes, containers, microservices, serverless architectures, and modern DevOps practices.
* Hands\-on experience with IaC tools (Terraform strongly preferred), CI/CD pipelines (GitHub Actions, Jenkins, GitLab CI, Argo, etc.), and automated deployment patterns.
* Strong understanding of cloud security, IAM, network segmentation, encryption, monitoring, cost optimization, and governance frameworks.
* Experience supporting modernization programs such as application migration, refactoring, API strategies, and technical debt remediation.
* AI\-assisted development and prior experience deploying agentic workloads and MLOps pipelines is an asset.

 **Leadership \& Consulting Skills**

* Demonstrated experience leading cloud\-focused teams and initiatives in a complex, multistakeholder environment.
* Strong executive communication skills suitable for client\-facing consulting environments.
* Ability to bridge business and technical perspectives and articulate value propositions, architecture decisions, and tradeoffs.
* Strategic mindset with a bias toward execution, innovation, and measurable impact.

 **Qualifications**

* Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or a related field (or equivalent experience).
* Significant cloud architecture and engineering leadership experience.
* Preferred: AWS Solutions Architect (Professional); Azure or GCP Architect certifications; Certified Kubernetes Administrator (CKA) or CKAD; Terraform Associate Certification.
* Ability to obtain Government of Canada **Security Clearance; Level 2 security clearance is an asset**.
*

jobs.title: Director, Data Foundations, Automation & Infrastructure
jobs.description:
Application Deadline: 

10/30/2026 

 Address: 
250 Yonge Street 

 Job Family Group:

Data Analytics & Reporting 

 About the Opportunity: 
 This is an exciting leadership opportunity within Commercial Banking to shape the future of how data powers business decisions across Canada and the U.S. 
 As Director, Data Foundations, Automation & Information Infrastructure, you will lead a highly technical team responsible for delivering trusted, curated, and scalable data assets that support reporting, analytics, AI, and strategic decision-making across Commercial Banking. You will oversee data engineering, data operations, information infrastructure, and business-managed applications while influencing the broader Commercial Banking data strategy. 
 The role combines banking knowledge, technical leadership, people management, and strategic thinking. As the organization continues its journey toward cloud modernization, AI-enabled automation, Client 360 capabilities, and near real-time data delivery, this leader will play a critical role in shaping the future state of Commercial Banking's data ecosystem. 
 This opportunity is ideal for a banking-savvy technology leader who enjoys building high-performing teams, solving complex data challenges, driving modernization initiatives, and translating business needs into scalable technical solutions. 

 About This Role 
 The Director, Data Foundations leads the team responsible for building, managing and continuously improving the curated data that powers Commercial Banking. This includes client, financial, client activity and master data, along with the other key business data sets that reporting, analytics and AI teams across the organization rely on to make decisions.
 The Director owns the end-to-end data lifecycle, from requirements, data modeling and architecture, through ETL and pipeline development, to the reliable production of trusted data within established service levels. The role partners with business, analytics, AI, Technology and Data Governance partners to ensure data is accurate, well documented and easy to use, and leads the ongoing modernization of data platforms and practices. 
 The ideal candidate combines deep data management expertise with strong people leadership and a high standard for quality. 
 Why This Role Matters 
 Trusted, well-managed data is the foundation for sound decisions, effective and trusted reporting, and the responsible use of AI. This role directly contributes to: 
 ·        Consistent, reliable data that supports executive reporting and business decision-making 
 ·        Curated data assets that allow reporting, analytics and AI teams to focus on insights 
 ·        A scalable, modern data ecosystem that keeps pace with evolving business needs 
 ·        Strong data quality and control practices aligned to BMO’s data governance standards 
 Key Responsibilities 
 Data Strategy and Architecture 
 ·        Define and deliver the Data Foundations strategy and roadmap, aligned to business, CDAO and enterprise data priorities 
 ·        Design and maintain the data architecture and models for curated data assets, including master and reference data, with long-term usability and scalability in mind 
 ·        Establish and uphold standards for data modeling, naming, metadata, integration and data sharing 
 Data Development and Operations 
 ·        Lead the design, development and operation of ETL processes and data pipelines 
 ·        Ensure recurring data production is accurate, timely and reconciled to authoritative sources, within published service levels 
 ·        Monitor data flows, resolve issues promptly and drive root-cause remediation 
 ·        Embed data quality checks, validation and controls throughout the data lifecycle 
 ·        Ensure data is handled securely and protected from loss or unauthorized access, in line with legal and company standards 
 Modernization and Innovation 
 ·        Continuously evaluate and adopt technologies, tools and practices that improve the scalability, efficiency and resilience of the data ecosystem 
 ·        Partner with Technology on platform strategy, infrastructure and the path to production 
 ·        Prepare and structure data to support advanced analytics and AI use cases 
 Data Enablement and Partnership 
 ·        Manage the intake and prioritization of data requests transparently, with clear service levels 
 ·        Promote data literacy and self-service through documentation, data dictionaries and a community of practice 
 ·        Serve as a trusted partner to business, analytics, AI and Technology teams on data definitions, changes and their downstream impacts 
 ·        Partner with Data Governance to meet data quality, metadata, lineage and data risk requirements 
 Business-Managed Applications 
 ·        Oversee a portfolio of business-managed applications that support key business processes, from intake and design through delivery, enhancement and ongoing support 
 ·        Ensure these applications are well controlled and supported, and aligned to BMO technology, data and risk standards 
 People Leadership 
 ·        Build, develop and lead a high-performing team of data professionals, working effectively with vendor partners 
 ·        Set clear goals and accountability, coach for growth, and foster a culture of ownership, quality and continuous improvement 
 ·        Attract, retain and develop top talent, recognizing strong performance and addressing gaps 
 ·        Role model BMO values and foster an inclusive culture connected to our purpose 
 ·        Take measured risks while protecting the bank by applying our Risk Management Framework in the execution of your role, in line with our Risk Culture and within our approved Risk Appetite, making sound and risk informed decisions that align to business strategy, protect assets, and adhere to applicable policy documents (Frameworks, Policies, Standards, Procedures and Supporting documents), laws and regulations. 
 Who You Are 
 ·        Treats data as a product: curated, documented, reconciled and reusable 
 ·        Holds a high standard for accuracy and builds processes that make quality repeatable 
 ·        Balances stability with progress, modernizing while keeping production dependable 
 ·        Understands Commercial Banking and how data flows across clients, products and channels 
 ·        Communicates clearly and builds trust through transparency 
 ·        Influences without authority and aligns diverse stakeholders around shared definitions 
 ·        Thrives in ambiguity and brings creative solutions to complex, interdependent problems 
 Qualifications 
 ·        9+ years of experience in data management, data engineering or a related field, including leadership of data teams 
 ·        Deep expertise in ETL and data pipeline development, data modeling and data quality management 
 ·        Strong proficiency in SQL and modern data programming languages such as Python 
 ·        Experience with cloud and modern data platforms 
 ·        Working knowledge of master data, metadata, semantic layer and data governance practices, including data privacy and integrity 
 ·        Experience operating in a highly regulated environment; Commercial Banking or financial services experience is an asset 
 ·        Excellent communication and stakeholder management skills 
 ·        Post-secondary degree in a related field of study, or an equivalent combination of education and experience 
 Why This Role 
 ·        Lead the Data Foundation that underpins reporting, analytics and AI across Commercial Banking 
 ·        Shape how data is built, managed and used at scale 
 Join a culture that values ownership, collaboration, trust and measurable outcomes

 Salary: 

$120,000.00 - $215,000.00 
 Pay Type: 

Salaried 
 The above represents BMO Financial Group’s pay range and type.

 Salaries will vary based on factors such as location, skills, experience, education, and qualifications for the role, and may include a commission structure. Salaries for part-time roles will be pro-rated based on number of hours regularly worked. For commission roles, the salary listed above represents BMO Financial Group’s expected target for the first year in this position.

 BMO Financial Group’s total compensation package will vary based on the pay type of the position and may include performance-based incentives, discretionary bonuses, as well as other perks and rewards. BMO also offers health insurance, tuition reimbursement, accident and life insurance, and retirement savings plans. To view more details of our benefits, please visit:  https://jobs.bmo.com/global/en/Total-Rewards 

 About Us 

 At BMO we are driven by a shared Purpose: Boldly Grow the Good in business and life. It calls on us to create lasting, positive change for our customers, our communities and our people. By working together, innovating and pushing boundaries, we transform lives and businesses, and power economic growth around the world.

 As a member of the BMO team you are valued, respected and heard, and you have more ways to grow and make an impact. We strive to help you make an impact from day one – for yourself and our customers. We’ll support you with the tools and resources you need to reach new milestones, as you help our customers reach theirs. From in-depth training and coaching, to manager support and network-building opportunities, we’ll help you gain valuable experience, and broaden your skillset.

 To find out more visit us at https://jobs.bmo.com/ca/en.

 BMO is committed to an inclusive, equitable and accessible workplace. By learning from each other’s differences, we gain strength through our people and our perspectives. Accommodations are available on request for candidates taking part in all aspects of the selection process. To request accommodation, please contact your recruiter.

 Note to Recruiters: BMO does not accept unsolicited resumes from any source other than directly from a candidate. Any unsolicited resumes sent to BMO, directly or indirectly, will be considered BMO property. BMO will not pay a fee for any placement resulting from the receipt of an unsolicited resume. A recruiting agency must first have a valid, written and fully executed agency agreement contract for service to submit resumes.

**This is a hybrid position based out of our 243 Consumers Rd location in North York, with 4 days per week in office and 1 day remote.**

  

Lifemark Health Group (LHG) is a market leader in customized healthcare solutions. With over 20 years of service excellence, LHG is one of the largest, most trusted, and most comprehensive providers in Canada. As a national healthcare company, LHG employs over 5,000 highly trained clinicians, medical experts and team members in almost 400 locations coast\-to\-coast and continues to grow both organically as well as through acquisitions. Lifemark was acquired by Loblaw Companies on May 10, 2022\.

This role requires a combination of advanced financial analysis, strong credit analysis and relationship management abilities.  Associate Directors contribute to client decisioning, credit structuring, and portfolio oversight, while also supporting new business development and delivering a superior client experience.  Work is performed in close partnership with Managing Director and/or Director.  The deal team is responsible for marketing, managing, and monitoring large commercial loan portfolios, and also supporting credit requirements and cross selling efforts for other businesses including subordinated debt, equipment leasing, derivatives, cash management, and trade finance.  The team assesses financing opportunities of $10,000,000 or more, both on a syndicated and bilateral basis.

 Analyzes credit information to support lending decisions and processes for new and existing Commercial banking loans and credit solutions in an assigned portfolio of clients. Makes credit decisions and recommendations in compliance with bank policies and procedures while maintaining an exceptional client service environment.
 Negotiates loan structures and terms and conditions that align client requirements with the bank risk appetite and policies.

 Signs off on new, renewal and extension loans within delegated authority.
 Monitors portfolio to identify deteriorating credit conditions and compliance, analyses metrics, and assesses broader industry trends to spot risks and opportunities.
 Evaluates portfolio performance and recommends capital allocation strategies that optimize returns with investment objectives.
 Leads proposal development and delivers presentations to capture new business and expand client relationships.
 Networks with industry contacts to gather competitive insights and best practices.
 Develops and executes business development plans focused on enhancing client relationships and growth opportunities within the portfolio.
 Builds and maintains client relationships to ensure long-term financial performance in collaboration with Relationship Manager and business partners.
 Structures and supports new, renewal and extension loans aligned with client needs and bank & risk policies
 Conducts financial analysis and risk assessments of clients’ credit information, for an assigned portfolio, to provide insights and make informed decisions
 Monitors the portfolio performance for assigned portfolio of Commercial Banking clients on an ongoing basis, taking corrective action when required. 
 Minimizes BMO’s risk exposure by adhering to credit policies, regulatory standards, and operational guidelines.
 Serves as a point of contact for service requests, ensuring expectations are consistently met or exceeded.  Escalates issues when needed.
 Supports and implements initiatives to enhance service quality, acquire new business and expand client relationships.
 Identifies revenue and cross-selling opportunities to enhance portfolio growth.
 Identifies share of wallet opportunities.
 Leverages analysis tools to nurture and grow a portfolio that exceeds ROE thresholds and evaluates client returns on a proactive basis.
 Manages timely and accurate data entry into BMO's systems and leverages the data to support decision-making.
 Focus is primarily on business/group within BMO; may have broader, enterprise-wide focus.
 Provides specialized consulting, analytical and technical support.
 Exercises judgment to identify, diagnose, and solve problems within given rules.
 Works independently and regularly handles non-routine situations.

 Take measured risks while protecting the bank by applying our Risk Management Framework in the execution of your role, in line with our Risk Culture and within our approved Risk Appetite, making sound and risk informed decisions that align to business strategy, protect assets, and adhere to applicable policy documents (Frameworks, Policies, Standards, Procedures and Supporting documents), laws and regulations.

Job Title: Director, People Strategy and HR Portfolio (Project) Management 
Location: Mississauga, ON - Hybrid
 
**Travel to Office expectations**
For Hybrid Roles: If this role is Hybrid, there will be an expectation to reside within commutable distance to the office/location specified in the job listing. This will include, but not limited to, weekly/bi-weekly/monthly events in the office with your specific team. This is a requirement for this role.
 
At PointClickCare our mission is simple: to help providers deliver exceptional care. And that starts with our people. As a leading health tech company that’s founder-led and privately held, we empower our employees to push boundaries, innovate, and shape the future of healthcare.
 
With the largest long-term and post-acute care dataset and a Marketplace of 400+ integrated partners, our platform serves over 30,000 provider organizations, making a real difference in millions of lives. We also reinvest a significant percentage of our revenue back into research and development, ensuring our employees have the resources to innovate and make a lasting impact. Recognized by Forbes as a top private cloud company and honored as one of Canada’s Most Admired Corporate Cultures, we offer flexibility, growth opportunities, and meaningful work. 
 
At PointClickCare, we empower our people to be the architects of a smarter healthcare future; one that is human-first and accelerated by AI to create meaningful and lasting change. Employees harness AI as a catalyst for creativity, productivity, and thoughtful decision-making. By integrating AI tools into our daily workflows, collaboration is enhanced, outcomes are improved, and every team member has the proficiency to maximize their impact. It all starts with our hiring practices where we uncover AI expertise that complements our mission, and we continue to invest in training and development to nurture innovation throughout the employee journey.
 
Join us in redefining healthcare — so it doesn’t just survive, it thrives. To learn more about PointClickCare, check out Life at PointClickCare and connect with us on Glassdoor and LinkedIn.
 
About the Team
The People Strategy & Transformation (PST) is PointClickCare's HR strategy, organizational design, and portfolio management pillar. The team includes HR Business Partners, Organizational Design & Effectiveness, People Experience, and the HR Strategy & Enablement function, with a dotted-line partnership to Internal Communications. PST is responsible for ensuring HR's work across every Center of Excellence is planned, resourced, sequenced, and tracked against business outcomes — spanning a portfolio of Pillar Initiatives, Cross-Pillar Projects, and Program Roll-Ups delivered across all four HR solution groups.
 
Position Summary:
The Director, People Strategy and HR Portfolio (Project) Management s is the VP, People Strategy & Transformation's strategic thought partner in building and running PointClickCare's HR Portfolio Management Office (HR PMO) — co-designing the strategy, governance model, capacity methodology, and dashboard reporting that let HR plan, resource, and track its work against business outcomes. This is a net-new function: no HR PMO currently exists at PointClickCare, and this role will design these mechanics in partnership with the VP rather than operate a system someone else has already built.

Operating with significant design authority but without direct reports or final decision rights on cross-functional trade-offs, this role earns influence through the credibility of the mechanics it builds and runs. It operates across all four HR solution groups without formal authority over any of them, serves as the VP's thought partner on HR strategy and the HR SLT prioritization process, and convenes HR initiative stakeholders and Internal Communications to coordinate how HR's work reaches the business.
 
Key Responsibilities:
Design and run the HR Portfolio Management Office’s core operating mechanics
Design and maintain the capacity management methodology, including the heat map model and the oversubscription thresholds used to flag resourcing conflicts across HR COEs
Own and run the Portfolio Council governance cadence end to end — intake, capacity check, tier assignment, publish, mid-quarter check, and close-out
Build and maintain the integrated HR initiative dashboard, ensuring data currency and accuracy across every active Pillar Initiative, Cross-Pillar Project, and Program Roll-Up
Example deliverable: a quarterly Portfolio Council capacity heat map showing every HR COE’s current initiative load, used to approve or defer new initiative intake
Serve as strategic thought partner to the VP, People Strategy & Transformation
Co-design the HR SLT prioritization process and criteria used to evaluate and sequence HR initiatives each planning cycle
Co-design the OKR and scorecard measurement architecture — what gets measured, how it rolls up, and the cadence it runs on
Co-author and stress-test the HR Strategy on a Page, contributing independent analysis before it is finalized by the VP
Example deliverable: a documented HR SLT prioritization framework — criteria, weighting, and process — adopted for the FY28 planning cycle
Own capacity management and project plan oversight across the full HR initiative portfolio
Track progress against committed business outcomes, not activity completion alone, across every active HR initiative
Maintain consistent project plan structure, milestone tracking, and dependency mapping in partnership with each initiative’s named Delivery Lead
Proactively surface cross-COE capacity collisions and resourcing conflicts before they reach Portfolio Council
Example deliverable: a consolidated project plan view across all active Program Roll-Ups, flagging dependency risk before it affects a committed milestone
Convene HR initiative stakeholders and Internal Communications on a recurring cadence
Establish and run a recurring go-to-market coordination cadence bringing together initiative Delivery Leads and Internal Communications
Sequence the timing and stakeholder readiness of HR initiative rollouts to the business, avoiding duplicate or conflicting messages landing in the same window
Maintain a shared go-to-market calendar visible to HR SLT, showing what is launching, when, and to whom
Example deliverable: a quarterly HR go-to-market calendar sequencing every planned initiative rollout to the business, reviewed and approved by HR SLT before the quarter begins
Represent HR in enterprise planning and governance forums
Serve as the primary operational liaison to the Strategic Delivery Office, aligning HR’s initiative classification and intake practices to enterprise taxonomy
Represent HR’s initiative portfolio and capacity picture in the Corporate Strategy Group’s quarterly planning cadence
Flag enterprise-level dependencies or conflicts affecting HR’s ability to deliver against committed priorities
Example deliverable: HR’s consolidated initiative and capacity submission into the Corporate Strategy Group’s quarterly planning sprint, reflecting current Portfolio Council status
 
Required Skills & Qualifications:
10–15 years of experience in program/portfolio management, management consulting, or a PMO leadership capacity, including demonstrated experience designing — not only operating — portfolio governance, capacity management, or OKR measurement systems
A track record serving as a strategic thought partner to a senior leader, with evidence of shaping that leader's thinking rather than only executing direction
Demonstrated experience operating in matrixed, cross-functional environments without formal authority over the teams being coordinated
Strong data and dashboard fluency — comfortable architecting reporting tools and the metrics model behind them, not just maintaining an existing build
Executive-level communication skills — this role prepares materials for and interacts directly with VP-level stakeholders across every HR pillar
Experience convening cross-functional stakeholder groups to coordinate sequencing and alignment on complex, multi-team initiatives
 
Preferred Experience:
Experience building a PMO or governance function from scratch, in a design capacity, rather than operating within an already-mature one
HR domain experience, including familiarity with COE structures and business-outcome-linked workforce initiatives
Experience partnering with internal communications or marketing functions on coordinated, multi-stakeholder rollouts
 
At PointClickCare, base salary is one of the many components that make up our total rewards package. The Canada base salary range for this position is $127,000 - $158,700 + bonus + benefits. Within the range, individual compensation is determined by job-related skills and knowledge, relevant experience including professional and lived experience, and/or work location. jobs.title: Regional Director, Digital Assets Sales & Commercialization, North America
jobs.description:
Our Purpose 

 Mastercard powers economies and empowers people in 200+ countries and territories worldwide. Together with our customers, we’re helping build a sustainable economy where everyone can prosper. We support a wide range of digital payments choices, making transactions secure, simple, smart and accessible. Our technology and innovation, partnerships and networks combine to deliver a unique set of products and services that help people, businesses and governments realize their greatest potential. 

 Title and Summary 

Regional Director, Digital Assets Sales & Commercialization, North America 

Overview

Mastercard is seeking a highly strategic, commercially focused, and externally oriented Director, Regional Commercialization, Digital Assets to lead the growth, market expansion, and commercialization of Mastercard's BVNK solution across NAM Region. This sales executive will play a critical role in establishing Mastercard's leadership position in next-generation payments by driving adoption of Mastercard's stablecoin capabilities and BVNK-powered solutions.

He/she will define and execute the regional go-to-market strategy, shape ecosystem partnerships, and drive revenue growth across financial institutions, fintechs, payment service providers, marketplaces, digital merchants, and emerging payment innovators.

The successful candidate will serve as Mastercard's expert sales leader for accelerating the adoption and usage of MA’s BVNK solution opportunities, working closely with BVNK Senior Sales leadership, MA Regional Sales and Product leadership and account management teams, market development and MA Move teams to originate, structure, and accelerate strategic opportunities. The role requires balancing commercialization execution with long-term ecosystem development and strategic market expansion.

This is a highly visible expert sales role requiring deep expertise in payments, digital assets, cross-border flows, stablecoins, fintech ecosystems, and platform commercialization.

Role

The Director, Regional Commercialization, Digital Assets will be accountable for driving market adoption, revenue growth, and ecosystem expansion for BVNK and MA’s digital asset solutions across NAM Region.

The role serves as the BVNK expert sales leader connecting BVNK’s solutions, Mastercard's capabilities, and regional customer opportunities.

Key Responsibilities 

Strategic Leadership & Commercialization 

• Define and execute the regional commercialization strategy for Mastercard's BVNK- powered solutions and stablecoin offerings 

• Collaborate with MA account teams to advance pipeline generation, strategic partnerships, client acquisition, and revenue realization. 

• Establish regional priorities, target segments, and market expansion strategies 

Revenue Growth & Market Expansion 

• Lead targeted regional sales efforts focused on MA customer segments including financial institutions, fintechs, PSPs, remittance providers, marketplaces, merchants, and digital economy participants. 

• Develop and govern a robust pipeline of high-value opportunities while supporting deal progression from origination through contract execution, retention and growth. 

• Sponsor strategic pursuits and executive-level client engagements for priority opportunities. 

• Drive achievement of revenue, transaction volume, and market adoption goals across the region. 

• Identify new market opportunities, geographic expansion priorities, and emerging use cases that create sustainable growth. 

Executive Client Engagement 

• Evangelize BVNK and MA’s digital assets and stablecoin-based payment solutions. 

• Build and maintain executive relationships with key Account Managers, clients, and ecosystem partners. 

• Provide stablecoin expert sales for strategic client discussions, executive briefings, workshops, and solution design engagements. 

• Support regional sales teams in navigating complex opportunities and executive-level negotiations. 

Strategic Partnerships & Ecosystem Development 

• Identify emerging partnership opportunities that accelerate adoption of Mastercard and BVNK’s digital asset capabilities. 

• Monitor competitive, regulatory, and market developments and translate insights into commercialization strategies. 

Product & Market Development 

• Partner with BVNKs product teams to inform client insights, competitive analysis, product strategy, roadmap prioritization, market readiness decisions, and future product investments. 

• Develop regional growth strategies around key digital asset use cases, including: 

 • Stablecoin-enabled cross-border payments 

 • Remittances 

 • Merchant payouts and settlement 

 • Treasury and liquidity management 

 • B2B payments 

 • Disbursements 

 • Marketplace payouts 

 • Wallet funding and cash-out solutions 

• Assess market readiness and prioritize opportunities by country, client segment, use case, and revenue potential. 

All About You 

Required Qualifications 

• Significant experience leading commercialization, business development, product, or growth initiatives within payments, digital assets, fintech, cross-border payments, or financial technology. 

• Demonstrated ability to originate, negotiate, and close complex strategic partnerships and enterprise opportunities. 

• Deep understanding of the payments and financial services landscape across NAM Region. 

• Experience engaging and influencing C-level executives and senior decision-makers. 

• Ability to lead through influence across highly matrixed global organizations. 

• Strong executive presence with exceptional communication, negotiation, and stakeholder management skills. 

• Demonstrated success operating within rapidly evolving and ambiguous market environments. 

• Ability to translate emerging technologies and market trends into commercial business opportunities. 

• Willingness to travel across the region. 

Preferred Qualifications 

• Experience in digital assets, stablecoins, blockchain-based payment infrastructure, or crypto-financial services. 

• Experience commercializing emerging or nascent payment technologies at scale. 

• Strong network across the banking, fintech, digital commerce, and payments ecosystem within the region. 

• Experience developing market-entry strategies and scaling new business lines globally or regionally. 

• Background in consultative sales, strategic partnerships, product leadership, or general management. 

Success Measures 

Success in this role will be measured by: 

• Achievement of regional digital asset revenue and business growth objectives. 

• Strategic pipeline creation, conversion, and closed revenue. 

• Expansion of Mastercard's stablecoin and BVNK-powered solution adoption. 

Mastercard is a merit-based, inclusive, equal opportunity employer that considers applicants without regard to gender, gender identity, sexual orientation, race, ethnicity, disabled or veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by law. We hire the most qualified candidate for the role. In the US or Canada, if you require accommodations or assistance to complete the online application process or during the recruitment process, please contact reasonable_accommodation@mastercard.com and identify the type of accommodation or assistance you are requesting. Do not include any medical or health information in this email. The Reasonable Accommodations team will respond to your email promptly. 

 Corporate Security Responsibility 

All activities involving access to Mastercard assets, information, and networks comes with an inherent risk to the organization and, therefore, it is expected that every person working for, or on behalf of, Mastercard is responsible for information security and must:
 Abide by Mastercard’s security policies and practices;

 Ensure the confidentiality and integrity of the information being accessed;

 Report any suspected information security violation or breach, and

 Complete all periodic mandatory security trainings in accordance with Mastercard’s guidelines.

In line with Mastercard’s total compensation philosophy and assuming that the job will be performed in Canada, the successful candidate will be offered a competitive pay based on location, experience and other qualifications for the role and may be eligible to participate in a discretionary annual incentive program. This posting reflects one or more current openings on our team.

Toronto, Canada: $138,000 - $221,000 CAD

jobs.title: VP, Business Group Chief Information Security Officer, Canada
jobs.description:
You are as unique as your background, experience and point of view. Here, you’ll be encouraged, empowered and challenged to be your best self. You'll work with dynamic colleagues - experts in their fields - who are eager to share their knowledge with you. Your leaders will inspire and help you reach your potential and soar to new heights. Every day, you'll have new and exciting opportunities to make life brighter for our Clients - who are at the heart of everything we do. 

 At Sun Life, we're driven by our Purpose: helping our Clients achieve lifetime financial security and live healthier lives. Our values shape how we work: caring, authentic, bold, inspiring, and impactful.

 When you join Sun Life, you'll work with passionate colleagues and empowering leaders who support your growth and celebrate your contributions, so you can make a meaningful difference in our Clients' lives.

 Discover how you can make a difference in the lives of individuals, families and communities around the world.

 Job Description: 
 VP, Business Group Information Security Officer, Sun Life Canada 

 Job Purpose  

 The Vice-President, Business Group Information Security Officer, Canada (BG CISO) serves as a senior security leader and partner to the Business Group leadership team and Business Group President.  Acting as the senior security executive for the Business Group and the primary bridge between the business and enterprise Security function, the BG CISO provides independent oversight and challenge of cyber risk, resilience and security outcomes across the business group. 

 The BG CISO, Sun Life Canada is accountable for cyber risk, resilience, and security outcomes for Sun Life Canada, one of the company’s core markets and a leader in health, wealth and protection, serving Clients across Canada through group benefits, individual insurance, wealth, advice and distribution channels.  

The Canadian business is made up of complex ecosystems, requiring strong alignment with Canadian regulatory expectations, enterprise risk practices and digital/client-service priorities.  Reporting directly to the global Chief Security Officer this position will have direct and indirect reports including a team of ~ 10 security leads and advisors aligned to the Canada business and subsidiary priorities including oversight of Dialogue security, product/platform risk, incident readiness, and stakeholder engagement. 

 The BG CISO partners closely with executives, technology leaders, risk partners, and the enterprise security team to protect critical assets, enable innovation, strengthen resilience, and ensure risks are understood and managed within the organization's risk appetite. The BG CISO is accountable for providing independent business-aligned security oversight while enabling growth, innovation and transformation across the Business Group. The role translates complex cyber and security risks into business impacts and shapes strategy, investments, priorities, and operating decisions across the Business Group.  

 Scope, Decision Authority and Key Interfaces  

 The Vice-President, Business Group Information Security Officer serves as the senior security executive and trusted advisor to the Business Group President and leadership team. The role is accountable for cyber risk oversight, executive advisory services, security governance, resilience alignment, regulatory engagement, and independent challenge across the assigned business group. The Vice-President translates enterprise security strategy into business-relevant actions while ensuring cyber risk, resilience, regulatory obligations, and security priorities are appropriately considered within business decisions and transformation initiatives.  

 The Vice-President has delegated authority to establish business-group security governance routines, direct security assessments, challenge risk decisions, require remediation planning, recommend security investment priorities, and escalate material cyber and resilience concerns through appropriate governance channels. Within approved authorities, the role provides independent advice and challenge regarding cyber risk, resilience, technology transformation, regulatory obligations, third-party risk, and risk acceptance decisions. Where management disagreement exists regarding material cyber risk acceptance, the matter will be escalated to the Global Chief Information Security Officer for review and discussion with the applicable Business Group President before a final decision is made. 

 The role is accountable for business-group security oversight, executive advisory services, risk escalation, independent challenge, alignment of enterprise security services to business priorities, and operational ownership of Business Group Customer Identity and Access Management (CIAM) platforms and associated security outcomes. The role does not own enterprise cyber defence operations, enterprise security platform engineering, vulnerability remediation, incident response operations, or second-line risk oversight except where responsibilities are expressly assigned. The Vice-President works closely with Enterprise Security leaders to ensure Business Group CIAM capabilities remain aligned with enterprise architecture, security standards, resilience requirements, and regulatory obligations. 

 Matters escalated to the Chief Information Security Officer would typically include significant cyber or operational resilience concerns, material breaches of risk appetite, major regulatory matters, unresolved management actions, significant third-party security issues, material client commitments, or disagreements regarding risk acceptance, prioritization, or investment decisions. 

 Major Accountabilities   

 Strategic Security Leadership and Vision  
 Serve as the primary Security advisor to the Business Group executive team and Business Group President. 
 Accountable for defining and driving the Business Group security strategy, aligned to enterprise security priorities and business objectives. 
 Ensure security considerations are integrated into business strategy, transformation initiatives, digital strategies, and operational decision-making. 
 Report significant changes in risk to appropriate levels of leadership on a periodic and event-driven basis.  
 Exercise independent challenge and escalate material cyber, technology, resilience and security risks through appropriate governance forums when risk exposure exceeds established risk appetite or remediation commitments are not achieved.  
 Deliver timely insights and data to enable informed executive decision-making, prioritization, and risk-based trade-offs.  
 Influence and shape multi-year security, resilience, and technology risk investment strategies, ensuring resource allocation aligns with business priorities, regulatory expectations and evolving threat landscapes.  
 Identify emerging threats, trends, and regulatory developments that may impact the Business Group and proactively develop mitigation strategies. 

 Business Partnership & Influence  
 Build trusted relationships with business and technology executives. 
 Act as the voice of the Business Group within the CISO organization and as the voice of the CISO organization within the Business Group. 
 Facilitate effective collaboration between business stakeholders and enterprise security teams. 
 Influence business group investment priorities and strategic trade-offs related to cyber risk, resilience, regulatory obligations, and secure technology adoption 

 Cyber Risk Management  
 Accountable for the Business Group’s cyber risk posture, control effectiveness and security outcomes, ensuring material risks are identified, assessed, escalated, remediated, or formally accepted through appropriate governance and in alignment with enterprise risk appetite. 
 Facilitate cyber risk assessments across application/platform/system levels to identify vulnerabilities and potential threats, analyze impacts, and recommend protection required based on threat modeling. 
 Support business leaders in making informed risk decisions consistent with enterprise policies and risk appetite. 
 Work with the Global Cyber threat intelligence team and monitor evolving threat landscapes and advise leaders on risk implications and required actions. 
 Provide oversight of BG specific third-party cyber risk related to critical vendors, strategic partners, outsourced services, and technology providers, ensuring security risks are appropriately identified, assessed, governed, monitored and escalated as appropriate.  
 Provide independent security advice on material risk acceptance decisions and ensure risks exceeding approved appetite or delegated authority are escalated to the appropriate enterprise and business governance forums.  

 Governance, Regulatory & Compliance  
 Lead security governance activities within the Business Group. 
 Oversee regular reporting and ensure alignment to global functional teams 
 Represent Security on business governance forums, executive committees, and risk councils. 
 Ensure effective management of applicable cybersecurity, technology risk, operational resilience, regulatory, legal, and policy requirements within the Business Group. 
 Represent the Business Group during regulatory examinations, supervisory reviews, external assessments and cybersecurity-related audits.  
 Hold leaders accountable to effective remediation of audit findings, regulatory issues, and control deficiencies. 

 Security Integration & Transformation  
 Partner with the enterprise security team to ensure security services and controls meet the needs of the Business Group. 
 Provide security leadership for major initiatives, acquisitions, client commitments, strategic partnerships, and technology transformations, including cyber due diligence, risk assessment, integration planning, and oversight of material remediation commitments. 
 Enable secure adoption of emerging technologies, including cloud, AI, automation, and digital solutions, ensuring appropriate cybersecurity, data protection, privacy, and governance controls are embedded throughout the lifecycle. 
 Provide oversight of information protection, data security, AI security and emerging technology risks ensuring critical information assets are protected and used responsibly and in compliance with regulatory and enterprise requirements.  
 Champion a secure-by-design approach across technology and business initiatives. 

 Incident Preparedness & Resilience  
 Serve as the senior security executive for the Business Group during significant cyber incidents, operational disruptions, and crisis events, coordinating with enterprise incident response, business continuity, legal, privacy, risk, communications, and business leadership to support timely decisions, escalation, recovery and reporting. 
 Oversee the Business Group’s cyber and operational resilience preparedness, including alignment with business continuity and crisis management, scenario testing, crisis simulations, recovery planning and oversight of resulting remediation actions.  
 Oversee the Business Group’s cyber risk assessment program across critical applications, platforms, systems, business processes, and transformation initiatives, ensuring material vulnerabilities, and threats are evaluated, prioritized, and addressed based on business impact and threat-informed analysis. 

 Security Culture & Awareness  
 Foster a strong security culture across the Business Group. 
 Promote accountability for risk management among leaders and employees. 
 Drive awareness and adoption of security best practices. 

 Leadership & Talent Development  
 Lead a network of business-aligned security leaders and professionals from across the Business Group and affiliate entities, providing strategic direction, oversight, and coordination of security priorities within a complex global matrix environment.  
 Present cyber risk, resilience, security posture, and emerging threats to executive committees, governance forums, and board-level audiences as required.  
 Lead through influence across complex matrixed environments. 
 Represent both the enterprise security function and business group with senior executives, regulators, auditors, and within industry forums.  
 Demonstrate executive presence and credibility with senior leaders. 
 Balance risk management with commercial and strategic objectives. 
 Drive informed decision-making under ambiguity and changing conditions. 
 Act as a trusted advisor capable of challenging constructively when risks warrant escalation. 

 Qualifications  

 Education  
 University degree in Information Security, Computer Science, Technology, Risk Management, Business, or a related discipline. 
 Relevant security certifications preferred (CISSP, CISM, CRISC, CGEIT, or equivalent). 

 Experience  
 15+ years of progressive experience in cybersecurity, information security, technology risk, risk management, or related disciplines. 
 Experience advising senior global executives on technology and cyber risk matters. 
 Experience operating in highly regulated environments. 
 Proven ability to influence strategic and investment decisions at an executive level.

 Job Description: 
 VP, Business Group Information Security Officer, SLAM (BG CISO)  

 Job Purpose  

 The Vice-President, Business Group Information Security Officer, SLAM (BG CISO) serves as a senior security leader and partner to the Business Group leadership team and Business Group President.  Acting as the senior security executive for the Business Group and the primary bridge between the business and enterprise Security function, the BG CISO provides independent oversight and challenge of cyber risk, resilience and security outcomes across the business group. 

 The BG CISO is accountable for cyber risk, resilience, and security outcomes for Sun Life Asset Management, a global asset management platform with approximately $1.6 trillion in AUM, established to strengthen collaboration across MFS Investment Management, SLC Management, Sun Life’s stake in Aditya Birla Sun Life Asset Management, the pension risk transfer business and the broader company.  

 Reporting directly to the global Chief Security Officer, this role is responsible for ongoing emphasis on ensuring full capabilities across Sun Life Asset Management are consistently leveraged to deliver value and innovation.  Direct and indirect reports include a team of ~ 10 security leads and advisors aligned to Asset Management business priorities, product/platform risk, incident readiness, and stakeholder engagement.  

 The BG CISO partners closely with executives, technology leaders, risk partners, and the enterprise security team to protect critical assets, enable innovation, strengthen resilience, and ensure risks are understood and managed within the organization's risk appetite. The BG CISO is accountable for providing independent business-aligned security oversight while enabling growth, innovation and transformation across the Business Group. The role translates complex cyber and security risks into business impacts and shapes strategy, investments, priorities, and operating decisions across the Business Group.  

 Scope, Decision Authority and Key Interfaces  

 The Vice-President, Business Group Information Security Officer serves as the senior security executive and trusted advisor to the Business Group President and leadership team. The role is accountable for cyber risk oversight, executive advisory services, security governance, resilience alignment, regulatory engagement, and independent challenge across the assigned business group. The Vice-President translates enterprise security strategy into business-relevant actions while ensuring cyber risk, resilience, regulatory obligations, and security priorities are appropriately considered within business decisions and transformation initiatives.  

 The Vice-President has delegated authority to establish business-group security governance routines, direct security assessments, challenge risk decisions, require remediation planning, recommend security investment priorities, and escalate material cyber and resilience concerns through appropriate governance channels. Within approved authorities, the role provides independent advice and challenge regarding cyber risk, resilience, technology transformation, regulatory obligations, third-party risk, and risk acceptance decisions. Where management disagreement exists regarding material cyber risk acceptance, the matter will be escalated to the Global Chief Information Security Officer for review and discussion with the applicable Business Group President before a final decision is made. 

 The role is accountable for business-group security oversight, executive advisory services, risk escalation, independent challenge, alignment of enterprise security services to business priorities, and operational ownership of Business Group Customer Identity and Access Management (CIAM) platforms and associated security outcomes. The role does not own enterprise cyber defence operations, enterprise security platform engineering, vulnerability remediation, incident response operations, or second-line risk oversight except where responsibilities are expressly assigned. The Vice-President works closely with Enterprise Security leaders to ensure Business Group CIAM capabilities remain aligned with enterprise architecture, security standards, resilience requirements, and regulatory obligations. 

 Matters escalated to the Chief Information Security Officer would typically include significant cyber or operational resilience concerns, material breaches of risk appetite, major regulatory matters, unresolved management actions, significant third-party security issues, material client commitments, or disagreements regarding risk acceptance, prioritization, or investment decisions. 

 Major Accountabilities   
 Strategic Security Leadership and Vision  

 Serve as the primary Security advisor to the Business Group executive team and Business Group President. 
 Accountable for defining and driving the Business Group security strategy, aligned to enterprise security priorities and business objectives. 
 Ensure security considerations are integrated into business strategy, transformation initiatives, digital strategies, and operational decision-making. 
 Report significant changes in risk to appropriate levels of leadership on a periodic and event-driven basis.  
 Exercise independent challenge and escalate material cyber, technology, resilience and security risks through appropriate governance forums when risk exposure exceeds established risk appetite or remediation commitments are not achieved.  
 Deliver timely insights and data to enable informed executive decision-making, prioritization, and risk-based trade-offs.  
 Influence and shape multi-year security, resilience, and technology risk investment strategies, ensuring resource allocation aligns with business priorities, regulatory expectations and evolving threat landscapes.  
 Identify emerging threats, trends, and regulatory developments that may impact the Business Group and proactively develop mitigation strategies. 

 Business Partnership & Influence  
 Build trusted relationships with business and technology executives. 
 Act as the voice of the Business Group within the CISO organization and as the voice of the CISO organization within the Business Group. 
 Facilitate effective collaboration between business stakeholders and enterprise security teams. 
 Influence business group investment priorities and strategic trade-offs related to cyber risk, resilience, regulatory obligations, and secure technology adoption 

 Cyber Risk Management  
 Accountable for the Business Group’s cyber risk posture, control effectiveness and security outcomes, ensuring material risks are identified, assessed, escalated, remediated, or formally accepted through appropriate governance and in alignment with enterprise risk appetite. 
 Facilitate cyber risk assessments across application/platform/system levels to identify vulnerabilities and potential threats, analyze impacts, and recommend protection required based on threat modeling. 
 Support business leaders in making informed risk decisions consistent with enterprise policies and risk appetite. 
 Work with the Global Cyber threat intelligence team and monitor evolving threat landscapes and advise leaders on risk implications and required actions. 
 Provide oversight of BG specific third-party cyber risk related to critical vendors, strategic partners, outsourced services, and technology providers, ensuring security risks are appropriately identified, assessed, governed, monitored and escalated as appropriate.  
 Provide independent security advice on material risk acceptance decisions and ensure risks exceeding approved appetite or delegated authority are escalated to the appropriate enterprise and business governance forums.  

 Governance, Regulatory & Compliance  
 Lead security governance activities within the Business Group. 
 Oversee regular reporting and ensure alignment to global functional teams 
 Represent Security on business governance forums, executive committees, and risk councils. 
 Ensure effective management of applicable cybersecurity, technology risk, operational resilience, regulatory, legal, and policy requirements within the Business Group. 
 Represent the Business Group during regulatory examinations, supervisory reviews, external assessments and cybersecurity-related audits.  
 Hold leaders accountable to effective remediation of audit findings, regulatory issues, and control deficiencies. 

   Security Integration & Transformation  
 Partner with the enterprise security team to ensure security services and controls meet the needs of the Business Group. 
 Provide security leadership for major initiatives, acquisitions, client commitments, strategic partnerships, and technology transformations, including cyber due diligence, risk assessment, integration planning, and oversight of material remediation commitments. 
 Enable secure adoption of emerging technologies, including cloud, AI, automation, and digital solutions, ensuring appropriate cybersecurity, data protection, privacy, and governance controls are embedded throughout the lifecycle. 
 Provide oversight of information protection, data security, AI security and emerging technology risks ensuring critical information assets are protected and used responsibly and in compliance with regulatory and enterprise requirements.  
 Champion a secure-by-design approach across technology and business initiatives. 
 Incident Preparedness & Resilience  
 Serve as the senior security executive for the Business Group during significant cyber incidents, operational disruptions, and crisis events, coordinating with enterprise incident response, business continuity, legal, privacy, risk, communications, and business leadership to support timely decisions, escalation, recovery and reporting. 
 Oversee the Business Group’s cyber and operational resilience preparedness, including alignment with business continuity and crisis management, scenario testing, crisis simulations, recovery planning and oversight of resulting remediation actions.  
 Oversee the Business Group’s cyber risk assessment program across critical applications, platforms, systems, business processes, and transformation initiatives, ensuring material vulnerabilities, and threats are evaluated, prioritized, and addressed based on business impact and threat-informed analysis. 

 Security Culture & Awareness  
 Foster a strong security culture across the Business Group. 
 Promote accountability for risk management among leaders and employees. 
 Drive awareness and adoption of security best practices. 

 Leadership & Talent Development  
 Lead a network of business-aligned security leaders and professionals from across the Business Group and affiliate entities, providing strategic direction, oversight, and coordination of security priorities within a complex global matrix environment.  
 Present cyber risk, resilience, security posture, and emerging threats to executive committees, governance forums, and board-level audiences as required.  
 Lead through influence across complex matrixed environments. 
 Represent both the enterprise security function and business group with senior executives, regulators, auditors, and within industry forums.  
 Demonstrate executive presence and credibility with senior leaders. 
 Balance risk management with commercial and strategic objectives. 
 Drive informed decision-making under ambiguity and changing conditions. 
 Act as a trusted advisor capable of challenging constructively when risks warrant escalation. 

 Qualifications  

 Education  
 University degree in Information Security, Computer Science, Technology, Risk Management, Business, or a related discipline. 
 Relevant security certifications preferred (CISSP, CISM, CRISC, CGEIT, or equivalent). 

 Experience  
 15+ years of progressive experience in cybersecurity, information security, technology risk, risk management, or related disciplines. 
 Experience advising senior global executives on technology and cyber risk matters. 
 Experience operating in highly regulated environments. 
 Proven ability to influence strategic and investment decisions at an executive level. 
 Experience leading large-scale transformation, risk, or security initiatives. 

 Key Knowledge & Skills

 Strong business acumen and ability to translate technical risks into business impacts. 
 Exceptional stakeholder management and executive communication skills.

 Strategic leader with the ability to anticipate and address emerging risks and opportunities.

Make an impact at all\-North American precious metals producer. New Gold is now part of Coeur Mining. Visit www.coeur.com to learn more.

  



Coeur Mining attracts and hires highly skilled individuals. By joining our team, you can look forward to:


* A stimulating values\-based work environment
* A culture of collaboration and inclusion
* Inspiring colleagues and approachable leaders
* Career development opportunities
* A deeply rooted commitment to responsible mining, health and safety and community engagement
* A competitive total compensation program
* A comprehensive benefits package including a retirement savings plan

  


**About Coeur Mining:**



Coeur Mining is a growing, all\-North American precious metals producer with seven operations: the Las Chispas silver\-gold mine and Palmarejo gold\-silver complex in Mexico, the Rochester silver gold mine in Nevada, the Kensington gold mine in Alaska, the Wharf gold mine in South Dakota, the Rainy River gold mine in Ontario, Canada, and the New Afton copper\-gold mine in British Columbia, Canada. In addition, Coeur owns the Silvertip silver\-zinc\-lead exploration project in British Columbia.


Coeur offers a flexible, hybrid work model and a culture built on safety, collaboration, and real opportunities to develop your career for those who want to grow alongside a company that is doing the same.

  

**Location**: Remote US with travel required

  


**Position Overview**


Reporting to the Senior Director, Site Finance \& Consolidations, the Director, Accounting Operations – US Site Finance is responsible for overseeing Coeur’s site\-level finance and accounting functions across its US mining operations. This role ensures the timely and accurate completion of operational financial close processes, provides strong leadership to site controllers, supports SEC reporting and internal controls, and performance reporting to support operational decision\-making and strategic initiatives.

  


**Key Responsibilities**


* Oversee the operations of the site accounting departments, including consolidated accounting, financial reporting, and tax functions at the site level
* Lead the monthly financial close process for Coeur’s mining operations, ensuring accuracy, completeness, and conformity with GAAP
* Direct, oversee, and provide leadership to site controllers across all US operations, including performance management, development, and standardization of processes
* Oversee the execution of site\-level financial planning processes, including life\-of\-mine modeling, annual budgets, forecasts, and strategic plans
* Develop, improve, and standardize site\-level financial reporting, financial planning, supply chain, and accounting systems/processes
* Analyze key performance indicators for operations and project groups and communicate results across management levels to support decision\-making
* Prepare and review financial analysis, variance explanations, and materials for site General Managers, Executive Leadership Team, and Board of Directors
* Support the integration of key processes, systems, and data across sites and corporate to enable high\-quality information flow and informed strategic planning
* Ensure transactions are accurately and timely recorded in accordance with GAAP; review journal entries, reconciliations, cash disbursements, and other accounting entries for propriety
* Prepare and/or review audit schedules and work directly with external auditors (GT) to resolve questions and issues.
* Assist with the preparation of 10\-Ks, 10\-Qs, and other regulatory reports, including coordination of site\-level inputs.
* Support AP and supply chain functions to maintain optimal working capital levels
* Coordinates production and compilation of various reports and statements for management review and for accounting purposes.
* Provide ongoing assistance to internal stakeholders on accounting and Oracle related matters
* Lead and participate in special projects, including process improvements, system implementations, and value\-added financial analysis.
* Champion data management, model governance, controls, and documentation as a single source of truth
* Identify and implement continuous improvement opportunities across site and corporate accounting practices

  


**Qualifications**


* Bachelor’s degree in Accounting or Finance required; CPA designation strongly preferred
* Minimum of 10 years of progressive finance and accounting experience, with significant time in operations finance or controller roles within the mining industry
* Minimum of 5 years of experience managing and leading accounting/finance teams
* Strong understanding of GAAP, SEC reporting, internal controls (SOX), and mining\-specific accounting (e.g., inventory, reclamation, revenue recognition)
* Proven ability to advise senior stakeholders, build relationships with site/operational teams, communicate complex financial information, and influence decision\-making
* Experience with ERP systems (Oracle preferred), Blackline, and other financial reporting tools

  


**Other Requirements**


* Excellent analytical, organizational, and problem\-solving skills
* Strong oral and written communication skills with the ability to interact effectively at all levels of the organization
* Ability to manage multiple priorities, conflicting stakeholder interests, and tight deadlines in a fast\-paced environment
* Strong operational mining knowledge is highly desirable
* Demonstrated commitment to confidentiality and ethical standards
